load_notes.vectors: plot_256, plot_512 and plot_1024 are not included: the import always generates them from plot with the Elasticsearch inference service.
load_notes.nested: belongs_to_collection and keywords are nested objects.
load_notes.csv: Arrays and nested objects are JSON-encoded inside each cell. The file is UTF-8 with BOM.
load_notes.part: Part 6 of 7, sorted by id. Each part is a complete catalog on its own: load it in bulk to replace the catalog or in append to add to it.

documents.title: The Hate U Give
documents.tagline: Two worlds. One voice. No going back.
documents.overview: Raised in a poverty-stricken slum, a 16-year-old girl named Starr now attends a suburban prep school. After she witnesses a police officer shoot her unarmed best friend, she's torn between her two very different worlds as she tries to speak her truth.
documents.plot:
The Hate U Give is a powerful and thought-provoking film that explores themes of racism, police brutality, activism, and identity. Directed by George Tillman Jr., the movie is based on the young adult novel of the same name by Angie Thomas.

The story follows 16-year-old Starr Carter (played by Amandla Stenberg), a black teenager who lives in the predominantly white and affluent neighborhood of Williamson, Georgia. However, her life takes a drastic turn when she transfers to a low-income black school in Garden Heights, where she is surrounded by poverty, violence, and police brutality.

Starr's dual identity becomes a central theme of the film. She navigates between two worlds: the privileged world of Williamson, where she has grown up with her middle-class family, and the harsh realities of Garden Heights, where she finds herself among friends who are struggling to survive.

The plot thickens when Starr witnesses the fatal shooting of her friend Khalil (played by Algee Smith) by a white police officer, Chris Breaux (played by Brian Tyree Henry). The incident sparks widespread outrage and protests in Garden Heights, while the Williamson community is largely oblivious to the event.

As news of Khalil's death spreads, Starr becomes an unlikely activist and voice for her community. She uses social media to share her story and raise awareness about police brutality and systemic racism. However, this newfound attention also puts her at odds with her family, particularly her mother, Lisa (played by Regina Hall), who wants to keep a low profile.

Throughout the film, Starr grapples with the complexities of activism, identity, and community. She must confront the harsh realities of police brutality and systemic racism, while also navigating her relationships with her friends, family, and romantic partner, Chris (played by KJ Apa).

The Hate U Give is a powerful exploration of the Black Lives Matter movement and the struggles faced by young black people in America. The film's portrayal of police brutality, racial profiling, and systemic inequality is unflinching and thought-provoking.

Ultimately, the film builds towards a climactic confrontation between Starr and Chris Breaux, as well as a dramatic showdown between the Garden Heights community and the Williamson police department. The ending is both heart-wrenching and hopeful, leaving audiences with a sense of urgency and a renewed commitment to fighting for justice and equality.

Overall, The Hate U Give is a powerful and timely film that sheds light on the struggles faced by young black people in America. With its talented cast, thought-provoking themes, and unflinching portrayal of police brutality, it's a movie that will leave you thinking long after the credits roll.

documents.title: 24 Hours to Live
documents.tagline: Contracted to kill. Fighting to survive.
documents.overview: An assassin seeks redemption after being given a second chance at life.
documents.plot:
"24 Hours to Kill" is a 2017 action thriller film directed by Renny Harlin and starring Bruce Willis.

The main theme of "24 Hours to Kill" revolves around the concept of time and its value. The movie follows James Wheeler, an assassin who wakes up with only 24 hours to live after being poisoned. With this newfound knowledge, he sets out to complete his last job and make amends for past mistakes before his time runs out.

Throughout the film, the theme of time is explored through James' actions and decisions. He must navigate a complex web of double-crosses and betrayals while trying to stay one step ahead of his enemies. The clock ticking away serves as a constant reminder of his mortality, driving him to make the most of the limited time he has.

Another significant theme present in the movie is redemption. James' character arc revolves around finding forgiveness for past wrongdoings and making amends with those he has hurt. As he navigates his final 24 hours, he must confront his own demons and face the consequences of his actions.

The film also touches on the idea of mortality and the value of human life. The protagonist's situation forces him to reevaluate his priorities and consider what truly matters in life. This theme is explored through James' interactions with those around him, particularly his daughter, who serves as a catalyst for his redemption arc.

Overall, "24 Hours to Kill" explores themes of time, redemption, mortality, and the value of human life, all woven together by Bruce Willis's gripping performance as the protagonist.

documents.title: Summer of 84
documents.tagline: Every serial killer lives next door to someone
documents.overview: After suspecting that their police officer neighbor is a serial killer, a group of teenage friends spend their summer spying on him and gathering evidence, but as they get closer to discovering the truth, things get dangerous
documents.plot:
Summer of 84 is a 2018 teen horror film directed by the Canadian filmmaking trio François Simard, Anouk Whissell and Yoann-Karl Whissell, known collectively as RKSS, from a screenplay by Matt Leslie and Stephen J. Smith. It stars Graham Verchere, Judah Lewis, Caleb Emery, Cory Grüter-Andrew, Tiera Skovbye and Rich Sommer. After a Sundance premiere in January 2018, it reached US cinemas in a limited release from Gunpowder & Sky on August 10, 2018.

Over the previous decade, thirteen teenage boys have vanished in the region around the Oregon suburb of Ipswich, victims of an unidentified killer the press calls the Cape May Slayer. In the summer of 1984, fifteen-year-old paperboy Davey Armstrong spends his days with his friends Woody, Farraday and Eats, and daydreams about Nikki, his former babysitter.

Davey, a lover of conspiracy theories and urban legends, becomes convinced that his neighbour Wayne Mackey, a popular local police officer, is the killer. His friends laugh at the idea until a boy whom Davey glimpsed in Mackey's window is reported missing, and they agree to spy on him. They log suspicious habits: Mackey buys digging tools and bags of soil, carries a duffel bag to work and jogs late at night. Searching his property while he is away, they find a bloodstained shirt, but Davey's parents are furious at the intrusion and make the boys apologise to Mackey, who later visits the Armstrongs with a plausible explanation that only deepens Davey's suspicions.

When another man is arrested for the murders, with Mackey making the arrest, Davey plans to search his house during the town festival. Farraday and Eats drop out after learning that the soil was for a civic project, but Davey, Woody and Nikki get inside with a video camera. In a locked basement room they find a missing boy's corpse, a living captive and a wall of photographs of victims, including one of Davey's family. Their footage leads the police to issue a warrant for Mackey, and Davey's parents apologise.

Mackey, however, has been hiding in the Armstrongs' attic. He abducts Davey and Woody, takes them to a wooded island and hunts them, killing Woody and wounding Davey, whom he deliberately leaves alive to live in fear. The film ends with a traumatised Davey resuming his paper route, his friendships broken, as the headlines report that the killer remains at large.

It received positive reviews, with 72% approval on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: Abducted in Plain Sight
documents.overview: In 1974, 12-year-old Jan Broberg is abducted from a small church-going community in Idaho by a trusted neighbour and close family friend.
documents.plot:
Abducted in Plain Sight is a 2017 documentary film directed by Skye Borgman, not 2018, and produced by Top Knot Films. The movie revolves around the Broberg family, whose daughter Jan was kidnapped multiple times by a close family friend, Robert Berchtold.

The main theme of Abducted in Plain Sight is the disturbing and complex relationship between trust, loyalty, and manipulation within families. It explores how a seemingly ordinary and loving family can be infiltrated by a charismatic individual who uses their charm to gain the trust of the parents and exploit it for his own sinister purposes.

Throughout the film, the audience witnesses the gradual erosion of Jan's sense of security and autonomy as she is repeatedly kidnapped and manipulated by Berchtold. The documentary sheds light on how the family's dynamics are warped by a toxic mix of codependency, enabling behavior, and a lack of boundaries, ultimately leading to devastating consequences.

The film also delves into the theme of gaslighting, where Berchtold skillfully manipulates Jan and her parents, making them question their own perceptions and sanity. This creates a sense of unease and tension, as the audience is left wondering how such a situation could unfold in real life.

Ultimately, Abducted in Plain Sight serves as a cautionary tale about the dangers of blind trust and the importance of setting boundaries within families. It raises questions about the nature of relationships, the power dynamics at play, and the devastating consequences that can result when these dynamics are exploited for personal gain.

documents.title: I Can Only Imagine
documents.tagline: The Song You Know. The Story You Don't.
documents.overview: 10-year-old Bart Millard lives with his mother and abusive father Arthur in Texas. One day his mother drops him off at a Christian camp where he meets Shannon. Upon his return from camp, Bart finds his mother has left and movers are removing her belongings. He angrily confronts his father, who denies that his abusiveness was the reason she left. Years later, in high school, Bart and Shannon are dating. Bart plays football to please his father but is injured, breaking both ankles and ending his career. The only elective with openings is music class, so he reluctantly signs up.
documents.plot:
I Can Only Imagine is a 2018 American biographical drama film directed by the Erwin Brothers and written by Alex Cramer, Jon Erwin, and Brent McCorkle. The movie is based on the life of Christian music star Bart Millard and his journey to write the song "I Can Only Imagine," which has become one of the most popular Christian songs of all time.

The film begins with a young Bart Millard (played by J. Michael Finley) growing up in a troubled home with an abusive father, Robert Millard (played by Dennis Quaid). Despite his difficult childhood, Bart finds solace in music and becomes a talented singer-songwriter. As he grows older, Bart's relationship with his father deteriorates, leading to a rift between them.

Bart's mother, Karen (played by Margo Martindale), tries to keep the family together, but ultimately passes away when Bart is just 15 years old. This event sets Bart on a path of self-discovery and spiritual exploration. He begins to question his faith and struggles with feelings of anger and resentment towards God.

As Bart navigates his teenage years, he meets a girl named Samantha (played by Cloris Leachman), who becomes a source of comfort and support in his life. However, their relationship is complicated, and they eventually part ways.

Bart's journey takes a dramatic turn when he discovers that his father has been diagnosed with terminal cancer. This event forces Bart to confront his feelings towards God and seek answers about the nature of suffering and pain. In a moment of profound insight, Bart writes "I Can Only Imagine," which becomes a powerful expression of his faith and emotions.

The film's climax features Bart performing the song live for the first time, with his father in attendance. The performance is met with an outpouring of emotion from the audience, including Robert Millard, who is visibly moved by the song's message.

Throughout the movie, the Erwin Brothers weave together themes of faith, family, and redemption, creating a powerful narrative that explores the complexities of human experience. The film features a talented cast, including Finley, Quaid, Martindale, and Leachman, who deliver nuanced performances that bring depth and emotion to their characters.

Ultimately, I Can Only Imagine is a movie about the transformative power of music and faith. It's a story about how one person's song can touch the lives of countless others and inspire them to seek answers about the nature of God and the human experience. The film's message is both uplifting and thought-provoking, making it a must-see for fans of Christian music and drama.

documents.title: At First Light
documents.tagline: We called, they answered,  she's the proof
documents.overview: A high school senior, Alex Lainey, has an encounter with mysterious lights that appear over her small town. She soon develops dangerous, supernatural abilities and turns to her childhood friend Sean Terrel. The authorities target them and a chase ensues as officials try to discover the truth behind Alex's transformation.
documents.plot:
At First Light, also titled First Light, is a 2018 Canadian science fiction thriller drama film written and directed by Jason Stone. It stars Stefanie Scott as Alex and Théodore Pellerin as Sean, with Saïd Taghmaoui as Cal, Kate Burton, James Wotherspoon and Percy Hynes White. The film premiered at South by Southwest in 2018, and after Gravitas Ventures acquired its distribution rights for the United States, Australia and New Zealand, it was released in theaters and on demand on September 28, 2018.

Seventeen-year-old Sean looks after his catatonic grandmother and his little brother. At a party he reconnects with Alex, an old friend he has long had a crush on, and writes his number on her arm. Later that night Alex goes swimming with her boyfriend and drowns, but as she sinks, mysterious lights fill the sky and the water around her. She is next seen wandering along a road, confused and unable to remember anything, and calls Sean, who takes her home, assuming she is on drugs. The next day, strange things begin to happen around her: lights flicker, knives float in the air and Sean's grandmother suddenly becomes lively and lucid again. When Sean tries to take Alex home, where her stepmother has reported her missing, she pushes him out of a second-story window and then halts their fall with her new powers. On the run together, they meet Cal, a former scientist who has tracked Alex through the electromagnetic energy she gives off. He tells them that the organization he once worked for has been sending messages into space for years and that someone, or something, has finally answered. He also warns Sean that staying close to Alex is exposing him to radiation that will eventually kill him. Torn between her feelings for Sean and the harm she is causing him, Alex sets off alone toward a vast circle of solar panels in the desert, while agents from Cal's former organization, who have discovered that she has survived far longer than anyone like her before, close in on both of them.

The film received mixed reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes, 50% of 14 critics' reviews are positive, and Metacritic gave it a score of 49 out of 100. Chris Knight of the National Post felt that the drab screenplay did the capable actors no favors, while Kevin Crust of the Los Angeles Times gave it a positive review, praising Pellerin and Scott.

documents.title: Wheelman
documents.overview: A getaway driver for a bank robbery realizes he has been double crossed and races to find out who betrayed him.
documents.plot:
Wheelman is a 2017 action thriller film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of one's actions. The movie follows the story of Ben, a former getaway driver who is forced back into his old life after being double-crossed by his associates.

At its core, Wheelman explores the theme of loyalty and betrayal. Ben's world is turned upside down when he discovers that those he trusted have abandoned him, leaving him to pick up the pieces of his shattered life. This sense of betrayal serves as a catalyst for Ben's downward spiral, as he becomes increasingly consumed by anger and a desire for revenge.

The film also touches on the theme of identity and redemption. As Ben navigates the treacherous underworld of organized crime, he is forced to confront the choices he made in the past and the person he has become. Through his journey, Ben grapples with the idea of finding redemption and making amends for past mistakes.

Furthermore, Wheelman critiques the notion of toxic masculinity and the dangers of unchecked aggression. Ben's character embodies a toxic form of masculinity that is rooted in violence and control, but as the story progresses, it becomes clear that this persona is both a product of his environment and a destructive force that threatens to consume him.

Ultimately, Wheelman presents a complex and thought-provoking exploration of human nature, one that raises questions about the consequences of our actions and the fragility of the human psyche.

documents.title: Batman: Gotham by Gaslight
documents.tagline: As the Ripper stalks Gotham City, the Dark Knight reveals the face of terror.
documents.overview: In an alternative Victorian Age Gotham City, Batman begins his war on crime while he investigates a new series of murders by Jack the Ripper.
documents.plot:
Batman: Gotham by Gaslight is an animated adaptation of the classic Sherlock Holmes story "The Hound of the Baskervilles," set in a dark and gothic version of 19th-century Gotham City, where Batman is portrayed as a character inspired by the iconic detective.

At its core, the movie explores the theme of obsession and the blurred lines between good and evil. The main antagonist, Professor James Gordon, has become consumed by his own darkness, driven by a desire for revenge against the villainous Jack the Ripper, who has come to Gotham City from London. As Batman delves deeper into the mystery, he finds himself entangled in a web of corruption and deceit that threatens to destroy the very fabric of Gotham.

The film also touches on the idea of identity and the masks we wear to hide our true selves. Both Batman and Professor Gordon are characters who have taken on personas that serve as a shield against the world, but as the story unfolds, their facades begin to crack, revealing the complexities and vulnerabilities beneath.

Furthermore, the movie critiques the notion of heroism and the morality of vigilantism. Batman's actions are driven by a desire to protect Gotham, but his methods often walk a fine line between justice and revenge. The film raises questions about the nature of heroism and whether it is ever truly justified, especially when the ends justify the means.

Overall, Batman: Gotham by Gaslight is a thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, delving into the darker aspects of human nature and the complexities of morality in a world where right and wrong are often gray.

documents.title: Oxygen
documents.tagline: No escape. No memory. 90 min to live.
documents.overview: A woman wakes in a cryogenic chamber with no recollection of how she got there, and must find a way out before running out of air.
documents.plot:
Oxygen is a 2021 French thriller film directed by Alexandre Moors and written by Juliette Grandet. The movie follows the story of Hana, a pregnant woman who wakes up in a sealed room with no memory of how she got there.

The main themes of Oxygen include:

1. **Survival and Resilience**: Hana's primary goal is to survive and find a way out of the room, which serves as a metaphor for the human spirit's ability to persevere in the face of adversity.
2. **Motherhood and Protection**: As Hana navigates her confinement, she becomes increasingly desperate to protect herself and her unborn child from the unknown forces that are holding her captive.
3. **Psychological Trauma and Memory Loss**: The film explores the psychological effects of trauma on Hana's memory and identity, leaving the audience questioning what is real and what is just a product of her imagination.
4. **Isolation and Confinement**: The sealed room serves as a symbol of isolation, highlighting the themes of confinement and the loss of freedom that can occur in life.

Throughout the film, these themes are expertly woven together to create a tense and suspenseful narrative that keeps the audience on the edge of their seats until the very end.

documents.title: Greta
documents.overview: A young woman befriends a lonely widow who's harboring a dark and deadly agenda toward her.
documents.plot:
Greta (2018) is a psychological thriller film directed by Neil Jordan, produced by Sidney Kimmel Entertainment, and written by David Koepp.

The main themes of Greta include:

1. Obsession: The film explores the theme of obsession, as the protagonist, Maren (Chloë Grace Moretz), becomes increasingly fixated on her deceased great aunt, Greta (Helen Mirren). This fixation leads to a downward spiral of events that puts Maren's life in danger.

2. Family Secrets: The movie delves into the complexities of family relationships and the secrets that can be hidden within them. As Maren digs deeper into her aunt's past, she uncovers dark secrets that threaten to destroy her own sense of identity.

3. Identity Crisis: Greta is also a film about identity crisis, as Maren struggles to come to terms with her own sense of self and purpose. Her fixation on her aunt serves as a distraction from her own feelings of emptiness and disconnection.

4. The Power of the Past: The movie highlights the idea that the past can be both a source of comfort and a burden. Greta's obsession with her aunt is, in part, driven by a desire to connect with her past and find meaning in her life.

5. Mental Health: The film touches on themes of mental health, particularly anxiety and depression. Maren's fixation on her aunt serves as a coping mechanism for her own emotional pain, but ultimately exacerbates the situation.

Overall, Greta is a complex and thought-provoking thriller that explores the darker aspects of human nature and the complexities of family relationships.

documents.title: Destroyer
documents.tagline: There's nothing to lose when you've already lost everything
documents.overview: When Erin Bell was a young cop, she was given an undercover assignment that ended badly and destroyed her life. Years later, she must face her demons in order to make peace with her past.
documents.plot:
Destroyer is a 2018 American neo-noir crime drama film directed by Karyn Kusama and written by Phil Hay and Matt Manfredi. Nicole Kidman stars as a haunted Los Angeles police detective confronting her past, with Toby Kebbell, Tatiana Maslany, Scoot McNairy, Bradley Whitford and Sebastian Stan. The film premiered at the Telluride Film Festival on August 31, 2018, and was released in the United States by Annapurna Pictures on December 25, 2018.

Erin Bell, a worn-out, hard-drinking LAPD detective, arrives at the scene of an unidentified man's murder and hints that she knows who is responsible. Soon after, she receives an anonymous envelope containing a dye-stained hundred-dollar bill, which she recognizes as coming from a bank robbery sixteen years earlier. At that time, she and her partner, the FBI agent Chris, had gone undercover in a desert gang led by the charismatic and violent Silas. Convinced that Silas has resurfaced, Erin sets out to find him, tracking down the surviving gang members one by one.

She begins with Toby, a dying former member released from prison, who points her to Arturo, now a lawyer. Arturo leads her to DiFranco, a corrupt attorney who launders the gang's money, and after she beats him she learns where Silas's girlfriend, Petra, will next collect cash. Erin follows Petra into a bank robbery staged by Silas's new crew, survives the shootout and captures Petra after a vicious fight. She also tries to reconnect with her teenage daughter, Shelby, who was raised by an adoptive father.

Flashbacks reveal what went wrong. While undercover, Erin and Chris fell in love and she became pregnant. At her urging, they decided to take part in the gang's robbery and keep their share before quitting the force. But a dye pack exploded, Silas killed a teller, and Chris was shot dead trying to intervene. Erin hid her share of the money and returned to police work, consumed by guilt. In the present, she retrieves the cash from a storage unit and finds most of it ruined by dye. When she meets Silas, she kills him, revealing that he was the dead man in the opening scene. Erin hands her partner evidence of her own guilt. Bleeding internally, she sits alone in her car, remembering a happier moment with her young daughter.

Destroyer received generally positive reviews, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 74% approval; critics singled out Kidman's transformative performance, which earned a Golden Globe nomination, though the film grossed only $5.6 million.

documents.title: The Last Warrior
documents.overview: Ivan is an ordinary guy who is transferred from modern Moscow to the fantasy world Belogorye. In this parallel universe where characters of Russian fairy tales live, magic is an integral part of daily life, and arguments are settled with the help of sword . Unexpectedly, Ivan finds himself in the middle of a battle between good and evil, and he must discover why everyone thinks that he must play the main role in upcoming events...
documents.plot:
The Last Warrior, also known as The Last Knight (Poslyedniy bogatyr), is a 2017 Russian fantasy comedy directed by Dmitriy Dyachenko. It was produced by The Walt Disney Company CIS with Yellow, Black and White and Kinoslovo. Viktor Khorinyak stars as Ivan, with Mila Sivatskaya as Vasilisa the Wise, Elena Yakovleva as Baba Yaga, Konstantin Lavronenko as Koschei, Ekaterina Vilkova as Princess Varvara and Yevgeny Dyatlov as Dobrynya Nikitich.

In Belogorie, a magical parallel ancient Russia, the sorceress Varvara petrifies the hero Alyosha Popovich and casts him into the sea. In Moscow, the orphan Ivan Naydenov is a con artist posing as a "white mage" on rigged psychic shows. He begins to doubt his life when he is asked to cure a boy in a coma. Fleeing a client's husband, he lands in Belogorie, a world of Russian fairy-tale characters. A volkhv tells him he is the lost son of the hero Ilya Muromets. He is brought to the friendly Prince Dobrynya, but Dobrynya's wife Varvara secretly imprisons him. There, the disembodied Koschei tells him only the sword Kladenets can send him home. Baba Yaga and Vasilisa, cursed to live mostly as a frog, free the prisoners, and the unlikely group sets out to find the sword with help from Vodyanoy the merman.

Ivan learns that the jealous Varvara turned Vasilisa's village into frogs, and grows fond of her, though he still wants to go home. Varvara captures his friends and forces Ivan to retrieve the sword. Koschei turns out to be in league with her, and Dobrynya is the real mastermind, planning to use the sword to become immortal. Dobrynya betrays Koschei, and Ivan escapes to Moscow. Unable to abandon Vasilisa, Ivan returns, frees the dragon Zmey Gorynych and fights his way to Dobrynya with a handgun. As he duels the now-immortal prince, Koschei is moved by Ivan's selflessness and destroys the magic stone, killing both himself and Dobrynya. Varvara flees, her petrified victims return to life, and Ivan reunites with his father Ilya. He marries Vasilisa and returns to Earth only briefly to heal the boy. A mid-credits scene reveals that Ivan's housekeeper, Galina, is Varvara's mother.

The film was released in October 2017. By late November it was Russia's highest-grossing local-language release, earning more than 1.7 billion rubles in total and recovering its budget in 11 days; Going Vertical soon topped it. Critical reviews were mixed, with praise for its humor but criticism of its clichés. Sequels followed in 2021.

documents.title: Victor Crowley
documents.overview: Ten years ago, over forty people were brutally torn to pieces in Louisiana’s Honey Island Swamp. Over the past decade, lone survivor Andrew’s claims that local legend Victor Crowley was responsible for the horrific massacre have been met with great controversy. But when a twist of fate puts him back at the scene of the tragedy, Crowley is mistakenly resurrected and Andrew must face the bloodthirsty ghost from his past.
documents.plot:
Victor Crowley, also known as Hatchet IV, is a 2017 American supernatural slasher film written and directed by Adam Green, the sequel to Hatchet III and the fourth installment in the Hatchet series. Kane Hodder returns as the title killer, alongside Parry Shen, Laura Ortiz, Dave Sheridan, Katie Booth and Brian Quinn. Green had become reluctant to continue the franchise until George A. Romero persuaded him to make the film. He wrote the script under the title Arwen's Fancy Dinner, and the film was shot in secret over eleven days under the working title Arwen's Revenge, with a full day lost when a set collapsed.

Ten years after the Honey Island Swamp massacre, its survivor Andrew Yong is offered an interview for a true crime television series on the condition that it be filmed in the swamp itself. Haunted by his ordeal, Andrew refuses until his publicist Kathleen secures him a million-dollar fee. On the chartered flight, he discovers that the interview will be conducted by his ex-wife Sabrina and her crew. Meanwhile, in the swamp, aspiring filmmaker Chloe, her boyfriend Alex and her best friend Rose are shooting a trailer for a movie based on the Crowley massacre with the help of Dillon, an eccentric local tour guide and actor. While researching online, Rose looks up videos of people attempting to recite the voodoo curse that originally brought Crowley back to life. When the plane suffers an engine explosion and crashes into the swamp, killing several on board, Rose and Dillon go to help the survivors, finding one of the crew trapped in the partially submerged wreckage as the water rises. At that moment, Rose's phone automatically plays a video of the curse being read aloud, inadvertently resurrecting Victor Crowley. Crowley begins slaughtering everyone in his path, and the trapped survivors, including Andrew, must find a way to escape the wreckage and outlast Crowley before he claims them all.

Victor Crowley premiered by surprise in Los Angeles on August 22, 2017, at an event billed as a tenth-anniversary screening of the original Hatchet, and was then shown at one-night "Victor Crowley Road Show" events across the United States from October 5, 2017, before its home release in February 2018. Reviews were generally mixed, though it holds a 67% rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: Ayla: The Daughter of War
documents.overview: In 1950, amidst the ravages of the Korean War, Sergeant Süleyman stumbles upon a a half-frozen little girl, with no parents and no help in sight. Frantic, scared and on the verge of death, this little girl captures the heart of Süleyman, who risks his own life to save her, smuggling her into his Army base and out of harms way. Not knowing her name and unable to communicate with her, Süleyman names her Ayla, in reminiscence of the moon on the fateful night during which they met. The two form an instantaneous and inseparable bond, and Ayla, almost effortlessly, brings an uncanny joy to the Turkish brigade in the grip of war. As the war comes to a close however, Süleyman's brigade is told that they will be returning home. Süleyman cannot bear abandoning Ayla, and does everything within his power to take her with him. After repeated failure, he is forced to give Ayla to an orphanage, but doesn't give up on the hope of one day reuniting with her. Will the two ever get back together?
documents.plot:
Ayla: The Daughter of War is a 2017 Turkish historical drama film directed by Mehmet Ergen. The movie tells the story of Ayla, a young girl who is kidnapped from her tribe and taken to the Ottoman Empire as a slave. As she navigates this new world, she faces numerous challenges and struggles to maintain her identity.

The main theme of Ayla: The Daughter of War revolves around the struggle for self-discovery and cultural preservation in the face of oppression and assimilation. Ayla's journey is a powerful metaphor for the resilience of indigenous cultures and the importance of preserving traditional ways of life in the face of colonialism and imperialism.

Throughout the film, Ayla grapples with her own identity, caught between her nomadic heritage and her new surroundings in the Ottoman Empire. She must confront the harsh realities of slavery, cultural erasure, and the loss of her family and community. Despite these challenges, Ayla remains determined to hold on to her roots and traditions, even as she is forced to adapt to a new and unfamiliar world.

The film also explores themes of love, sacrifice, and redemption, as Ayla forms connections with those around her and finds ways to cope with the trauma she has experienced. Ultimately, Ayla's story is one of hope and resilience, a testament to the human spirit's ability to persevere in the face of adversity.

Overall, Ayla: The Daughter of War is a powerful and moving film that sheds light on the experiences of indigenous people and the importance of preserving cultural heritage.

documents.title: The Moment You Fall in Love
documents.original_title: 好きになるその瞬間を。～告白実行委員会～
documents.overview: Following Natsuki Enomoto's confession rehearsals with Yuu Setoguchi, their younger siblings Kotarou and Hina struggle to confess their own love. Despite a disastrous first meeting in middle school with her upperclassman Koyuki Ayase, Hina’s heart is captured by his warm smile. Initially confused by these newfound feelings, Hina soon realizes that she has fallen in love for the very first time.  Chasing after her brother Yuu and her crush Koyuki, Hina also enrolls in Sakuragaoka High School; but the threads of love are far-reaching, and they entangle Hina and her friends. Boisterous but sensitive, Hina hopes to confess her feelings to the tender-hearted Koyuki. Meanwhile, Kotarou, oblivious to his own feelings for her, is determined to always keep Hina smiling.  This movie follows Hina, Kotarou, and Koyuki in high school. Their youthful love forges new relationships, but also threatens to break others.
documents.plot:
The Moment You Fall in Love is a 2016 animated short film produced by Qualia Animation. 

The story revolves around two young rabbits, who are initially portrayed as rivals, but eventually develop feelings for each other. As they navigate their blossoming romance, the film explores themes of love, vulnerability, and acceptance.

One of the main themes of The Moment You Fall in Love is the power of vulnerability and openness in relationships. The two rabbit characters must confront their own fears and insecurities in order to truly connect with each other. This theme is beautifully conveyed through the film's gentle animation and soothing music.

Another significant theme present in the film is the importance of acceptance and understanding. As the rabbits navigate their differences, they learn to appreciate and celebrate their unique qualities, rather than trying to change or hide them. This message promotes a positive and inclusive attitude towards diversity and individuality.

The film also touches on the idea that love can be a transformative experience, allowing individuals to grow and evolve as people. The rabbit characters' relationship serves as a catalyst for personal growth, as they learn to let go of their past fears and insecurities in order to move forward together.

Overall, The Moment You Fall in Love is a heartwarming and poignant film that explores the complexities and beauty of love and relationships through its gentle and charming storytelling.

documents.title: Zoo
documents.tagline: The true story of a larger than life friendship
documents.overview: Young Tom and his misfit friends fight to save 'Buster' the baby elephant during the German air raid bombings of Belfast in 1941.
documents.plot:
Zoo is a 2017 Irish-British historical family drama written and directed by Colin McIvor, a Belfast native making his third feature. Loosely based on the true story of Denise Austin, the Belfast woman remembered as the zoo's "elephant angel", it stars Penelope Wilton as Denise Austin, Art Parkinson as Tom Hall, Toby Jones as the security guard Charlie, Emily Flain as Jane, Ian O'Reilly as Pete, James Stockdale as Pete's brother Mickey, Stephen Hagan as the veterinarian Jake, Damian O'Hare and Amy Huberman as Tom's parents, and Ian McElhinney.

In 1941, twelve-year-old Tom dreams of following his father George, who works at the slightly shabby Bellevue Zoo in Belfast, into a life with animals. The highlight of the year is the arrival of a young Asian elephant, whom Tom names Buster. Soon afterwards George is called up to serve in the British Army, leaving Tom and his mother to cope as the war closes in. Worried about Buster, Tom keeps sneaking past the grumpy guard Charlie, only to find the elephant in the care of the hostile Jake.

When German bombers strike the city in the Belfast Blitz, the authorities order the destruction of the zoo's potentially dangerous animals in case they escape during another raid. Realizing that Buster could be next, Tom devises an audacious plan to rescue him. He recruits Jane, a neglected classmate with an alcoholic father, Pete, a former bully who proves softer than he seems, and Pete's brother Mickey, a boy with a disability whose family has kept him hidden from view. Their unlikely ally is Mrs. Austin, a reclusive, eccentric woman who shares her cluttered home with a menagerie of animals and gradually reveals the losses she suffered in an earlier war. Together they spirit the elephant out of the zoo and hide him in her back yard, trying to keep him secret amid the air raids, in what Tom calls the most unforgettable year of his life.

Principal photography began in Belfast in September 2016, combining trained animals with computer-generated stand-ins. Samuel Goldwyn Films released Zoo in the United States on June 8, 2018. Reviews were positive, with about 88 percent of critics on Rotten Tomatoes rating it favourably. The Hollywood Reporter called it a lovingly crafted, big-hearted adventure for all ages, while Variety enjoyed its child heroes and air-raid set pieces but noted that it takes considerable liberties with the real story, sidelining Austin, a zoo employee who sheltered the elephant in her yard each night.

documents.title: The Goldfinch
documents.tagline: The story of a stolen life
documents.overview: A boy in New York is taken in by a wealthy family after his mother is killed in a bombing at the Metropolitan Museum of Art. In a rush of panic, he steals 'The Goldfinch', a painting that eventually draws him into a world of crime.
documents.plot:
The Goldfinch is a 2019 American drama film directed by John Cameron Mitchell, based on the 2013 novel of the same name by Donna Tartt.

The main themes of The Goldfinch include:

1. **Trauma and Recovery**: The film explores the long-term effects of trauma on the protagonist, Theo Decker, who witnesses a terrorist attack at an art museum in New York City. The story delves into his struggles to cope with grief, guilt, and anxiety.
2. **Grief and Loss**: The Goldfinch is a poignant exploration of the complexities of human emotions, particularly in the face of loss. Theo's relationship with his mother, who dies in the attack, serves as a catalyst for his emotional journey.
3. **Identity and Belonging**: As Theo navigates his way through life, he grapples with finding his place in the world. The film examines his relationships with others, including his friends, family, and mentors, to understand what it means to belong and find one's identity.
4. **Art and Creativity**: The Goldfinch highlights the significance of art as a means of expression, healing, and connection. Theo's love for art serves as a source of comfort and inspiration throughout his journey.
5. **Mortality and Impermanence**: The film confronts the reality of mortality, reminding viewers that life is fleeting and that we must cherish every moment. This theme is particularly evident in Theo's relationships with those who have passed away.

The story unfolds over several decades, following Theo as he grows from a vulnerable child to a young adult struggling to find his place in the world. The film features stunning cinematography, memorable performances, and a richly detailed narrative that explores the complexities of human emotions.

Overall, The Goldfinch is a powerful exploration of the human experience, tackling themes that are both universally relatable and deeply personal.

documents.title: The Last Man
documents.overview: Tov Matheson is a war veteran with PTSD who perceives that the apocalypse is coming. After starting a relationship with a dubious Messiah, he leaves his normal life and begins the construction of a shelter underground, training himself, in an extreme way, at the cost of losing everything and making people believe he is insane. When he also believes it, something extraordinary happens.
documents.plot:
The Last Man (Spanish: El último hombre) is a 2019 Argentine-Canadian science fiction film co-written and directed by Rodrigo H. Vila. Set in a bleak, storm-ravaged future, it stars Hayden Christensen as Kurt, a war veteran suffering from post-traumatic stress disorder, Harvey Keitel as Noe, a street prophet who predicts an imminent catastrophe, and Liz Solari as Jessica, a woman who shares his belief, with Marco Leonardi and Rafael Spregelburd.

Kurt lives in an unnamed city plagued by constant storms, a world that collapsed during a 30-day crisis known as "the Black Month." Haunted by nightmares of a wounded soldier begging to be killed, he sleeps under his bed clutching a weapon. At a black market he crosses paths with a neo-Nazi gang extorting money from shopkeepers, and he hears Noe preach that a devastating electrical storm is coming. When Kurt returns a faulty gas mask to a shop run by Noe's followers, the prophet gives him a survival book, and Kurt is beaten by the gang. He takes a job at a security company run by Jessica's father, who values his combat experience, and is warned by the boss's enforcer, Gomez, to stay away from Jessica. He also sees the ghost of his friend Johnny, the soldier from his nightmare, whom Kurt shot, and a strange boy who calls him a ghost.

Kurt prepares for the apocalypse by building a secret bunker and grows close to Jessica, who wants to join him. When the gang returns to rob Noe's departing followers, Kurt kills several of them and lets the group escape. Gomez, who has been stealing money from the company and framing Kurt, uses Jessica as bait to capture him, and Kurt is locked in an asylum, where he is told that Noe is a convicted fraudster and that the world is not ending. Noe, disguised as Kurt's lawyer, arranges his escape. Before confronting Gomez, Kurt realizes the mysterious boy is his own younger self. At the security office, he plays a recording proving Gomez's guilt; Gomez shoots Kurt, who survives thanks to a protective vest, and kills Jessica's father before Kurt kills him. As the storms return worse than ever, Kurt fights his way back to his bunker and finds Jessica waiting for him.

The film was released in theaters and on video on demand on January 18, 2019, grossing only about $12,000. Reviews were negative, criticizing the plot and Christensen's performance; Christy Lemire of RogerEbert.com called it thoroughly unpleasant, though Noel Murray of the Los Angeles Times praised its gloomy atmosphere.

documents.title: The Souvenir
documents.tagline: The past never stays in focus.
documents.overview: A shy but ambitious film student falls into an intense, emotionally fraught relationship with a charismatic but untrustworthy older man.
documents.plot:
The Souvenir is a 2019 British drama film directed by Joanna Hogg, not BBC Film. 

The Souvenir explores the complex and often fraught relationship between nostalgia and reality, as well as the blurred lines between past and present. The film delves into themes of youthful disillusionment, the fragility of relationships, and the struggle to find one's identity.

Through its protagonist, Jodie, the film masterfully weaves a narrative that is both deeply personal and universally relatable. As Jodie navigates her way through a tumultuous romance with Anthony, she finds herself caught in a web of nostalgia, where memories are distorted and reality becomes increasingly uncertain.

The Souvenir also touches on the theme of female identity, particularly in the context of women's experiences during the 1980s. The film offers a poignant portrayal of the struggles faced by women at that time, including the constraints placed upon them by societal expectations and the limited opportunities available to them.

Ultimately, The Souvenir is a nuanced exploration of the human experience, one that probes the complexities of love, loss, and identity with sensitivity and depth.

documents.title: Uncut Gems
documents.overview: A charismatic New York City jeweler always on the lookout for the next big score makes a series of high-stakes bets that could lead to the windfall of a lifetime. Howard must perform a precarious high-wire act, balancing business, family, and encroaching adversaries on all sides in his relentless pursuit of the ultimate win.
documents.plot:
Uncut Gems is a 2019 American crime thriller film directed by Josh and Benny Safdie, written by Josh and Benny Safdie, and produced by Scott Rudin Productions. The film stars Adam Sandler as Howard Ratner, a diamond dealer who becomes embroiled in a world of crime and deception.

The film begins with Howard Ratner (Adam Sandler), a successful but troubled diamond dealer, who is struggling to make ends meet. He is married to Dinah (Lauren Lapkus) and has two children, but his personal life is on the rocks. Howard's business partner, Arno (Eric Bogosian), is pushing him to take more risks and expand his operations.

One day, while at a poker game in Las Vegas, Howard meets Julia De Fiore (Julia Stiles), a beautiful and charming woman who becomes infatuated with him. However, their relationship is complicated by the fact that Julia's husband, Kevin (Paddy Considine), is a ruthless and violent man.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Howard is deeply in debt to various individuals, including Arno, who is threatening to cut him out of his business unless he pays up. Meanwhile, Howard becomes obsessed with a rare and valuable diamond called the "Black Mamba," which he believes will be the key to saving his business.

However, things take a dark turn when Kevin De Fiore discovers that Julia has been having an affair with Howard, leading to a violent confrontation between the two men. As tensions escalate, Howard becomes increasingly desperate and reckless, making a series of poor decisions that put him in grave danger.

As the plot thickens, it becomes clear that Howard's world is on the verge of collapse. He is pursued by a group of ruthless thugs, including Kevin De Fiore, who will stop at nothing to get what they want from him. In a desperate bid to save himself and his family, Howard turns to an unlikely ally: a young man named Julius (Idris Elba), who becomes embroiled in his web of deceit.

The film builds towards a shocking and violent climax, as Howard's world comes crashing down around him. In the end, it is unclear whether Howard will emerge from this ordeal alive or dead, but one thing is certain: he has lost everything that truly mattered to him.

Throughout the film, the Safdie brothers use their unique visual style and editing techniques to create a sense of tension and unease, drawing the viewer into Howard's world of crime and deception. Adam Sandler delivers a tour-de-force performance as the troubled and complex Howard Ratner, bringing depth and nuance to a character that could have easily been reduced to caricature.

Overall, Uncut Gems is a gripping and intense thriller that explores the darker side of human nature. With its talented cast, clever script, and masterful direction, it is a must-see for fans of crime dramas and thrillers.

documents.title: 2036: Nexus Dawn
documents.overview: This in-world short film takes place in the year 2036 and revolves around Jared Leto’s character, Niander Wallace. In this short, Wallace introduces a new line of “perfected” replicants called the Nexus 9, seeking to get the prohibition on replicants repealed. This no doubt has serious ramifications that will be crucial to the plot of Blade Runner 2049.
documents.plot:
2036: Nexus Dawn is a 2017 American science fiction short film that serves as a prequel to the feature Blade Runner 2049. Directed by Luke Scott, son of the original Blade Runner director Ridley Scott, and written by Hampton Fancher and Michael Green, who also wrote the feature, it stars Jared Leto as the industrialist Niander Wallace, with Benedict Wong, Ned Dennehy, Ade Sapara and Ania Marson as lawmakers and Set Sjöstrand as a replicant. It is one of three shorts made to bridge the decades between the two feature films, alongside 2048: Nowhere to Run and the animated Blade Runner Black Out 2022.

The film is set in Los Angeles in 2036, thirteen years before the events of Blade Runner 2049. Following a catastrophic event known as the Blackout, the manufacture of replicants, the bioengineered humans used as labor, has been banned, and the Tyrell Corporation has gone bankrupt. Earth's ecosystem is on the verge of collapse. Niander Wallace, the blind head of the Wallace Corporation, which has acquired Tyrell's assets, is summoned before a panel of lawmakers to discuss his ambition to produce a new generation of replicants.

The lawmakers warn Wallace that what he proposes is illegal and not open to debate, but Wallace argues that humanity cannot survive without the cheap labor that replicants provide. He insists that his new models are perfectly obedient and pose no danger to humans. When the officials remain unconvinced, Wallace offers a chilling demonstration with his replicant assistant, a newly designed Nexus-9, ordering him to harm himself and to choose between his own life and that of his maker. The replicant's response shocks the room, and Wallace once again asks the lawmakers whether they are prepared to authorize production.

The short establishes Wallace's cold vision and the circumstances that allow replicants to return in Blade Runner 2049, while expanding the world of the franchise between its two films.

The short was announced on August 29, 2017, as part of a series of films chosen by Blade Runner 2049 director Denis Villeneuve, and was released online the following day, about five weeks before the feature reached cinemas. Its Chinese version adds a text prologue explaining the backstory of the replicant ban and the Wallace Corporation.

documents.title: Traffik
documents.overview: A couple off for a romantic weekend in the mountains are accosted by a biker gang. Alone in the mountains, Brea and John must defend themselves against the gang, who will stop at nothing to protect their secrets.
documents.plot:
Traffik is a 2018 American crime thriller film directed by Deon Taylor. The movie follows the story of Brea Kelly (played by Paula Patton), a mother whose life is turned upside down when her son is kidnapped and she discovers that he was involved in human trafficking.

The main themes of Traffik include:

1. **Human Trafficking**: The film sheds light on the dark reality of human trafficking, highlighting its devastating effects on victims and their families.
2. **Motherly Love and Sacrifice**: Brea's journey is driven by her unwavering love for her son, which motivates her to risk everything to rescue him and bring the perpetrators to justice.
3. **Corruption and Injustice**: The movie exposes the corruption and complicity of law enforcement officials and other authorities in enabling human trafficking, highlighting the need for accountability and reform.
4. **Trauma and Recovery**: Brea's experiences leave her with physical and emotional scars, forcing her to confront her own trauma and find a way to heal and move forward.
5. **Redemption and Justice**: Throughout the film, Brea seeks redemption by taking down those responsible for her son's kidnapping and exploitation, ultimately finding a sense of justice and closure.

Overall, Traffik is a powerful and thought-provoking film that tackles tough subjects with sensitivity and nuance, offering a hopeful message about the resilience of the human spirit.

documents.title: Calibre
documents.overview: Two lifelong friends head up to an isolated Scottish Highlands village for a weekend hunting trip that descends into a never-ending nightmare as they attempt to cover up a horrific hunting accident.
documents.plot:
Calibre is a 2018 British psychological thriller film written and directed by Matt Palmer in his feature debut. Jack Lowden and Martin McCann star as two lifelong friends whose hunting trip in the Scottish Highlands turns into a nightmare, with Tony Curran in support. After premiering at the Edinburgh International Film Festival, it was released on Netflix in June 2018.

Vaughn, a quiet Edinburgh man whose fiancée is expecting their first child, joins his confident, wealthy childhood friend Marcus for a weekend of deer hunting in a remote Highland village. On their first night, they drink at the local pub, where they meet the community's leader, Logan, and two young women, Kara and Iona. Marcus goes home with Kara despite being warned off. The next morning, a hungover Vaughn realizes he has forgotten his ammunition, so Marcus illegally lends him one of his rifles. When Vaughn fires at a stag, it moves at the last moment and his bullet kills a young boy who was hidden behind it. The boy's grief-stricken father seizes the rifle and turns it on Vaughn, and Marcus shoots him dead.

Vaughn wants to go to the police, but Marcus persuades him that they will be treated as murderers. They hide the bodies, and that night return to bury them after Marcus cuts the bullets out of them. Back in the village, Logan invites them to dinner and asks Marcus to help find investors for the struggling community, while one of Logan's brothers slashes their tires as revenge for Marcus's night with Kara, trapping them in the village while repairs are made. Vaughn learns that the victims were Logan's relatives, and suspicion grows when Marcus mentions the missing pair before word of the father's disappearance has spread.

The two men are drawn into the search party, and a dog leads the villagers to the grave. Marcus and Vaughn attempt to flee, but their car is disabled and they are hunted down. Captured, Vaughn confesses. Logan gives him a terrible ultimatum: kill Marcus, or both will die. After resisting, Vaughn shoots his friend, and Logan coaches him in a cover story for the police. Months later, Vaughn, now a father, sits awake in the dark at home, haunted by what he has done, before going to comfort his crying baby.

Calibre received critical acclaim, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 100% approval and Metacritic a score of 76. Critics praised its tension and its lead performances.

documents.title: Uncle Drew
documents.overview: Uncle Drew recruits a squad of older basketball players to return to the court to compete in a tournament.
documents.plot:
"Uncle Drew" is a 2018 American sports comedy film directed by Charles Stone III. The movie follows the story of Uncle Drew, a 75-year-old former basketball player who comes out of retirement to lead his old team, the Harlem Globetrotters, in a bid to save their home from being demolished.

The main themes of "Uncle Drew" include:

1. **Redemption and Second Chances**: The film explores the idea that it's never too late to pursue your dreams or make amends for past mistakes. Uncle Drew, who had retired from basketball years ago, gets a second chance to prove himself and lead his team to victory.
2. **Ageism and Stereotypes**: The movie challenges ageist stereotypes by showcasing an older man who is still capable of performing at a high level. This theme is also reflected in the character of Uncle Drew's rival, Darnell Lewis, who underestimates him due to his age.
3. **Community and Family**: The Harlem Globetrotters are more than just a basketball team; they're a family. The film highlights the importance of community and family ties, as the players come together to support each other and their home.
4. **Self-Discovery and Empowerment**: Through his journey, Uncle Drew discovers new aspects of himself and finds a sense of purpose. He also empowers the younger generation, particularly Darnell's son, to believe in themselves and pursue their passions.

Overall, "Uncle Drew" is a heartwarming film that celebrates the power of redemption, community, and self-discovery, while also showcasing the importance of ageism awareness and challenging stereotypes.

documents.title: It Chapter Two
documents.overview: 27 years after overcoming the malevolent supernatural entity Pennywise, the former members of the Losers' Club, who have grown up and moved away from Derry, are brought back together by a devastating phone call.
documents.plot:
It Chapter Two is a 2019 American horror film directed by Andy Muschietti, based on the novel of the same name by Stephen King. The film serves as a sequel to the 2017 film It and concludes the story of the Losers' Club.

The movie takes place 27 years after the events of the first film. The Losers' Club, now in their mid-40s, has been reunited for Pennywise's (Bill Skarsgård) return to Derry, Maine. The group consists of Bill Denbrough (James McAvoy), Beverly Marsh (Jessica Chastain), Ben Hanscom (Jay Ryan), Richie Tozier (Bill Hader), Mike Hanlon (Isaiah Mustafa), and Eddie Kaspbrak (James Ransone).

As Pennywise returns, the Losers' Club must face their personal demons and confront the evil entity once again. The group is forced to return to Derry, where they are met with a mixture of nostalgia and terror. They soon realize that Pennywise has been awakened by a mysterious ritual performed by a group of children who have been possessed by his spirit.

The Losers' Club must work together to stop Pennywise's return and save the town of Derry from destruction. Along the way, they are forced to confront their own personal traumas and the consequences of their past actions. The film features a mix of horror, drama, and coming-of-age themes, as the characters navigate their complex relationships with each other.

One of the standout aspects of It Chapter Two is its exploration of the Losers' Club's adult lives. The film delves into the personal struggles and triumphs of each character, adding depth to the story and making it more relatable to audiences. The film also features a number of memorable performances, including Jessica Chastain's portrayal of Beverly Marsh, which earned her an Academy Award nomination.

Overall, It Chapter Two is a satisfying conclusion to the Losers' Club's story, offering a mix of horror, drama, and emotional depth. While it may not be as tightly wound as its predecessor, the film delivers on its promise of a thrilling and emotionally resonant conclusion to the series.

documents.title: Teen Titans Go! To the Movies
documents.original_title: Teen Titans Go! To the Movies
documents.tagline: The superhero movie to end all superhero movies. Hopefully.
documents.overview: All the major DC superheroes are starring in their own films, all but the Teen Titans, so Robin is determined to remedy this situation by getting over his role as a sidekick and becoming a movie star. Thus, with a few madcap ideas and an inspirational song in their hearts, the Teen Titans head to Hollywood to fulfill their dreams.
documents.plot:
Teen Titans Go! To the Movies is a 2018 American animated superhero comedy film based on the Cartoon Network series Teen Titans Go!, produced by Warner Bros. Animation and DC Entertainment. Directed by Peter Rida Michail and Aaron Horvath from a script by Horvath and Michael Jelenic, it features the series' voice cast, including Scott Menville as Robin, Khary Payton, Tara Strong, Greg Cipes and Hynden Walch, joined by Will Arnett as Slade and Kristen Bell as the filmmaker Jade Wilson, with Nicolas Cage as Superman and Halsey as Wonder Woman.

In Jump City, the Teen Titans get distracted by their own rap song while fighting the Balloon Man, forcing the Justice League to step in. The League mocks them for their childishness and points out that they do not even have a movie of their own. At the premiere of Batman Again, Robin is humiliated when he mistakenly believes a film about him is being shown. After the supervillain Slade breaks into S.T.A.R. Labs to steal a crystal and mocks the Titans, Robin resolves that they will go to Hollywood. At Warner Bros. Studios, director Jade Wilson, responsible for every superhero film, rejects them because they lack an archnemesis. A misguided trip back in time to prevent other heroes' origins leaves the world overrun by villains, and the Titans have to set things right.

Battling Slade at Wayne Tech to recover the crystal earns them a movie deal, but after the team's antics, Jade decides to make the film about Robin alone, and he breaks up the team, believing they hold each other back. On the last day of filming, Jade reveals herself to be Slade in disguise: her superhero movies were a ploy to keep the heroes busy while he stole technology to build D.O.O.M.S.D.A.Y., a streaming service that will let him control minds, and he deliberately split Robin from his friends. Slade destroys Titans Tower; Robin apologizes and the team reunites. At the premiere of Robin: The Movie, Slade uses the crystal to hypnotize the Justice League and then Robin, but the Titans snap him out of it by showing him the homemade movie they made for him. Using their rap song, they defeat Slade, freeing the world, and the Justice League finally acknowledges them as heroes.

Released by Warner Bros. Pictures on July 27, 2018, the film grossed about $52 million worldwide on a $10 million budget and was well received, earning 92% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 69 for its light-hearted, intelligent humor.

documents.title: Mariah Carey's All I Want for Christmas Is You
documents.original_title: Mariah Carey's All I Want for Christmas Is You
documents.overview: When young Mariah sees a darling little puppy named "Princess" at the pet store, she suddenly knows exactly what she wants for Christmas. But before her Christmas wish can come true, she must prove that she can dog-sit her uncle's dog, Jack, a scraggly rascal; in fact, the worst dog in the county!
documents.plot:
Mariah Carey's All I Want for Christmas Is You is a 2017 American animated Christmas musical comedy based on Mariah Carey's 1994 hit song and her children's book of the same name. Directed by Guy Vasilovich and released direct-to-video by Universal Pictures Home Entertainment, it features Breanna Yde as the voice of the young Mariah, Henry Winkler, Lacey Chabert, Phil Morris, and Carey herself as the narrator.

Young Mariah has always wanted a dog but has never been allowed one, because of her father's allergies and her mother's love of tidiness. A few days before Christmas, her grandmother takes her to a pet store, where she falls in love with Princess, a hypoallergenic toy poodle. She begs her father to give her the dog for Christmas, and he agrees on one condition: she must first prove that she is responsible enough to care for a pet. He brings home Jack, a scruffy Jack Russell terrier belonging to his brother, for Mariah to look after over the holidays.

Jack turns out to be a handful. He runs out of the house and refuses to come back until Mariah lures him with a steak, has accidents indoors, slips his leash in the park and knocks over Mariah's school principal, and barks so loudly at her choir concert that snow falls from the roof onto the singers. When Mariah tries to deliver toys to a donation box, Jack refuses to give them up. As one disaster follows another, Mariah fears she will never get Princess. As Christmas approaches, Mariah gradually realizes how attached she has become to the mischievous dog, and through her misadventures she learns about responsibility and the true meaning of Christmas, discovering that what she really wants may not be the perfect puppy she imagined, and she performs the film's title song in a holiday finale.

Released on home video and digital platforms for the 2017 holiday season, the film was positioned as a family holiday feature tied to the enduring popularity of Carey's song, which has become one of the best-selling Christmas singles of all time, and it includes several musical numbers alongside the title track.

documents.title: The Lodge
documents.overview: When a father is forced to abruptly depart for work, he leaves his children, Aidan and Mia, at their holiday home in the care of his new girlfriend, Grace. Isolated and alone, a blizzard traps them inside the lodge as terrifying events summon specters from Grace's dark past.
documents.plot:
The Lodge is a 2019 psychological horror film directed by Veronika Franz and Severin Fiala, the filmmaking duo behind Goodnight Mommy, from a screenplay they wrote with Sergio Casci. It stars Riley Keough as Grace Marshall, Jaeden Martell and Lia McHugh as the siblings Aiden and Mia Hall, Richard Armitage as their father Richard and Alicia Silverstone as their mother Laura. Casci's original script had been sold to Hammer Films, and the directors rewrote much of it, including the ending.

When Richard tells his estranged wife Laura that he intends to marry Grace, a younger woman he met while researching a book on an extremist cult, Laura takes her own life. Grace was raised in that cult and was the only survivor of a mass suicide led by her father. Six months later, Richard decides that his grieving children should spend Christmas with Grace at the family's remote lodge in Massachusetts so they can get to know her. Aiden and Mia, who blame Grace for their mother's death, have found footage of the cult's dead followers and treat her with open hostility.

When Richard returns to the city for work, Grace is left alone with the children in the snowbound lodge, surrounded by Catholic imagery that stirs nightmares about her father. One morning she wakes to find her clothes, her psychiatric medication, her dog, the food and the Christmas decorations gone, the generator dead and the clocks showing a later date. Aiden suggests that they may all have died and be trapped in some kind of afterlife. As days pass in cold and hunger, Grace, deprived of her pills, begins to sleepwalk and hear her father's sermons, and her grip on reality slips. The children's cruel deception, intended to drive her away, spirals into something far more dangerous than they anticipated.

The film draws on themes of grief, religious trauma and guilt, building its dread through the claustrophobic setting and the cold, isolating winter landscape.

The Lodge premiered at the Sundance Film Festival on 25 January 2019 and was released by Neon in a limited release on 7 February 2020, later expanding. It received generally positive reviews, holding 75 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus singled out Keough's performance, and a Metacritic score of 64.

documents.title: The Sweetest Christmas
documents.overview: After breaking up with her long-term boyfriend just before the holidays, passionate baker Kylie reconnects with her high school sweetheart, Nick. Thanks to their newly rekindled friendship, Kylie uses Nick’s restaurant to prepare for a gingerbread baking competition with a large cash prize that would help her open her own bakery.
documents.plot:
The Sweetest Christmas is a 2017 American Christmas romance television film directed by Terry Ingram from a screenplay by Erinne Dobson, made for Hallmark Channel. It stars Lacey Chabert as the aspiring pastry chef Kylie Watson and Lea Coco as Nick Mazzanti, with Jonathan Adams as Nick's chef and friend Ralphie, Brenden Sunderland as his young son Bobby, Lane Edwards as Kylie's boyfriend Alex, and Lara Gilchrist, Jill Morrison and Brenda Crichlow in supporting roles.

Kylie, a talented baker working as a temporary receptionist for her boyfriend, the real estate developer Alex Hawkey, learns that she has finally become a semifinalist in the American Gingerbread Competition, whose $25,000 prize could help her open a bakery of her own. Expecting a marriage proposal at their anniversary dinner at a local pizzeria, she is instead offered a promotion to office manager, and realizing that Alex does not support her dreams, she breaks up with him. The pizzeria turns out to belong to Nick, her old boyfriend, whom she has not seen in years; he gave up his ambition of becoming a pastry chef to run the family restaurant and is raising Bobby on his own. When Kylie's oven breaks down, Nick lets her use his industrial pizza oven at night, and as she bakes, helps Bobby make cupcakes for a school party and reminisces with Nick about their youthful dreams, their romance is rekindled. Alex, meanwhile, tries to win her back by sponsoring the celebrated "Godmother of Gingerbread", Ina Bruckner, to compete in the same contest. When he stages a grand gesture at the competition, presenting a gingerbread jewelry store containing an engagement ring, Nick assumes Kylie has accepted and pulls away. Realizing she has lost her creative spark trying to imitate Ina, Kylie spends a twelve-hour marathon building a new entry, a moving gingerbread carousel commemorating her first kiss with Nick, wins the prize and reconciles with him at their old carousel.

The film premiered on Hallmark Channel on 11 November 2017. Matt Mueller of OnMilwaukee found it merely "fine", calling Chabert pleasant but given little to work with, Coco nice but bland and Edwards almost too dopey as the ex-boyfriend, while singling out Adams as the most enjoyable character; he likened the film to a Chips Ahoy cookie, sweet enough but not particularly good.

documents.title: Christmas in Evergreen
documents.overview: Allie, a veterinarian in Evergreen, reluctantly will spend Christmas with her long-distance boyfriend. Bound for the airport, she has engine trouble, and Ryan, headed to Florida with his daughter Zoe, stops to help. Sure they won’t meet again, they ignore their attraction, and part ways. At the diner, Zoe wishes on a snow globe, and a storm seems to grant her wish.
documents.plot:
Christmas in Evergreen is a heartwarming holiday film that explores the themes of love, family, and second chances. The movie follows Samantha, a successful businesswoman who returns to her small hometown of Evergreen after a painful loss, only to find herself rekindling old flames with a childhood sweetheart, Jake.

As Samantha navigates her complicated past and present, she must confront the choices that led her away from her roots and the people she loves. The film masterfully weaves together themes of nostalgia, forgiveness, and the power of community, highlighting the importance of embracing one's heritage and finding comfort in the familiar.

Through Samantha's journey, Christmas in Evergreen also touches on the idea of letting go of past regrets and embracing new beginnings. As she rediscovers the joys of small-town life and reconnects with Jake, she begins to see that sometimes, it's never too late to rediscover what truly matters in life.

Ultimately, the film presents a poignant exploration of the human experience during the holiday season, reminding viewers that love, family, and community are the greatest gifts of all.

documents.title: The Christmas Train
documents.overview: Forced to take the intercontinental trip to Los Angeles by train, and determined to chronicle his adventure, disillusioned journalist Tom Langdon finds himself westbound with a variety of characters. While all passengers on the Christmas train appear to be headed for the same destination, Tom has no idea that the rugged locomotives taking him across America will instead detour straight into his heart.
documents.plot:
The Christmas Train is a 2017 American Christmas romantic drama television film directed by Ron Oliver and written by Neal H. Dobrofsky and Tippi Dobrofsky, adapted from the 2003 novel of the same name by the thriller writer David Baldacci. Produced by Front Street Pictures as an instalment of the Hallmark Hall of Fame anthology, with music by Peter Allen and cinematography by Adam Sliwinski, it stars Dermot Mulroney, Kimberly Williams-Paisley, Danny Glover and Joan Cusack. It premiered on the Hallmark Channel and Hallmark Movies & Mysteries on 25 November 2017, drawing 4.87 million viewers.

Mulroney plays Tom Langdon, a disillusioned journalist and former globe-trotting war correspondent, who sets out from Washington, D.C., to spend Christmas in Los Angeles with Lelia, the woman he is seeing. Travelling across the country by train, he resolves to chronicle the journey, both to find fresh inspiration and to fulfil a last wish of his late father, although he regards the assignment of writing about a holiday train as a puff piece. On board he meets a colourful assortment of fellow passengers, among them the famous film producer Max Powers (Glover); Agnes (Cusack), a seemingly nosy and somewhat mysterious woman who always seems to be on the train and whose sleeping compartment is next to his; a man trying to find himself after the death of his wife; and a young couple eager to marry.

To Tom's surprise, the passengers also include Eleanor Carter (Williams-Paisley), a fellow journalist and his former love. The two had worked together as war correspondents and fallen deeply in love, but the pressures of deadlines and schedules drove them apart, and they had parted painfully years earlier. Their reunion has been arranged through their mutual connection, Max. As the train rolls west through the snow, the journey becomes a mix of romance, light adventure and mystery, with each passenger gradually revealing hidden secrets, and Tom and Eleanor begin to realise that all is not yet lost between them. The story builds to a final plot twist that Mulroney described as completely unexpected.

Mulroney said the production was shot on real trains, with snow added later, and he also wrote and sang a song, "Christmas Train", that is heard in the film. Mulroney described the film as an exemplar of Hallmark's heartwarming holiday entertainment and promised that fans of Baldacci's novel would be thrilled.

documents.title: Finding Santa
documents.overview: Christmas is a busy, busy time for the residents of Green River, particularly for Grace Long, the third generation of her family to steward the New England town’s signature Christmas Eve parade. This year’s audience for the parade promises to be in the millions, thanks to a national morning show that has chosen Green River as the site of its Christmas Eve day program.
documents.plot:
Finding Santa is a heartwarming Christmas film that explores the theme of self-discovery and redemption. The story follows a woman who has lost touch with her own sense of purpose and meaning, feeling unfulfilled in her life. When she meets a mysterious man claiming to be Santa Claus, she begins to see the world through his eyes and is inspired to re-examine her own values and priorities.

As the narrative unfolds, the film delves into the idea that it's never too late to rediscover one's passions and pursue new dreams. The protagonist's journey is a metaphor for the human experience of seeking purpose and finding happiness in unexpected places. Through her interactions with Santa, she learns to let go of her fears and doubts, embracing the magic of the holiday season and the possibility of a second chance.

The film also touches on the theme of kindness and generosity, highlighting the transformative power of small acts of compassion and empathy towards others. As the protagonist navigates her newfound connection with Santa, she begins to see the world as a place where everyone deserves love, care, and understanding – a message that resonates deeply during the holiday season.

Ultimately, Finding Santa is a feel-good film that celebrates the human spirit's capacity for growth, renewal, and redemption.

documents.title: A Private War
documents.tagline: The Most Powerful Weapon Is The Truth
documents.overview: One of the most celebrated war correspondents of our time, Marie Colvin is an utterly fearless and rebellious spirit, driven to the frontlines of conflicts across the globe to give voice to the voiceless.
documents.plot:
A Private War is a 2018 biographical war drama film directed by Matthew Heineman. The movie revolves around Marie Colvin, a renowned American war correspondent who risked her life to report on conflicts in various parts of the world.

The main theme of A Private War is the cost of war and the human toll it takes on those who cover it. The film delves into the complexities of war journalism, highlighting the moral dilemmas faced by correspondents like Marie Colvin, who often find themselves caught between their duty to report the truth and the danger posed by their work.

The movie also explores the theme of female empowerment and the struggles women face in a male-dominated field. Marie Colvin's character is portrayed as a strong-willed and determined individual who refuses to back down from her assignments, despite the risks involved.

Furthermore, A Private War touches on the theme of sacrifice and the personal cost of one's profession. The film shows how Marie Colvin's work takes a toll on her personal life, relationships, and ultimately, her own life.

The movie also raises questions about the responsibility of journalists in war zones and the impact of their reporting on the public's perception of conflict. Through Marie Colvin's character, the film highlights the importance of accurate and nuanced reporting in shaping our understanding of complex issues.

Overall, A Private War is a powerful exploration of the human cost of war journalism, female empowerment, and the personal sacrifices made by those who risk everything to tell the stories that need to be told.

keywords.name: based on magazine, newspaper or article

documents.title: How It Ends
documents.overview: A desperate father tries to return home to his pregnant wife after a mysterious apocalyptic event turns everything to chaos.
documents.plot:
How It Ends is a 2018 American apocalyptic action thriller directed by David M. Rosenthal and written by Brooks McLaren.
