Theo James stars as Will, a young lawyer, with Forest Whitaker as his prospective father-in-law Tom, Kat Graham as his pregnant girlfriend Sam, Grace Dove, Nicole Ari Parker and Mark O'Brien. Netflix released the film on 13 July 2018.

Will and Sam, a young couple living in Seattle, are expecting their first child. Will flies to Chicago to visit Sam's parents, intending to ask her father, Tom, a retired Marine, for permission to marry her. Dinner ends in an argument between the two men, and Will leaves without mentioning either the pregnancy or the proposal. The next day, as Will waits for his flight home, Sam calls him in alarm, saying that something is wrong, before the line goes dead. All flights are canceled, and television news reports a mysterious seismic event off the West Coast that has knocked out power and communications.

Will returns to Sam's parents' house, and he and Tom set aside their differences to drive across the country to find her. As they head west, they encounter jammed highways, military roadblocks and growing social collapse. Tom uses his military background to talk their way through a checkpoint, and that night they are pulled over by a man in a police car who turns out to be an escaped prisoner; in the violent confrontation that follows, Tom is injured. They tow their damaged car to a Native American reservation, where a young mechanic, Ricki, repairs it and agrees to travel with them. The journey grows increasingly dangerous as they face desperate survivors, violent bandits, strange atmospheric phenomena and dwindling supplies of fuel and food. Along the way, Will and Tom slowly develop mutual respect, while the cause of the catastrophe remains a mystery and the land around them becomes ever more hostile as they near the Pacific Northwest.

How It Ends received negative reviews, holding a 17 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 36. Critics praised Whitaker's performance and some of the action sequences but were frustrated by the film's refusal to explain the nature of the disaster and especially by its abrupt, ambiguous ending, which became the most discussed aspect of the film among viewers.

documents.title: Mirai
documents.overview: Unhappy after his new baby sister displaces him, four-year-old Kun begins meeting people and pets from his family's history in their unique house in order to help him become the big brother he was meant to be.
documents.plot:
Mirai, known in Japan as Mirai no Mirai, is a 2018 Japanese animated fantasy film written and directed by Mamoru Hosoda and produced by Studio Chizu. Its voice cast includes Moka Kamishiraishi, Haru Kuroki, Gen Hoshino, Kumiko Aso, Mitsuo Yoshihara, Yoshiko Miyazaki, Kōji Yakusho and Masaharu Fukuyama.

Kun lives with his executive mother and architect father in a stepped house in Yokohama, built around a tree in the courtyard, and spends his days with the family dog, Yukko, and his toy trains. When his sister Mirai is born, his delight turns to jealousy as his parents' attention shifts to the baby, especially once his mother returns to work and his father works from home. Each time he storms off into the garden, something magical happens. He meets a man who turns out to be Yukko in human form, complaining that he lost attention when Kun arrived; he meets a teenage Mirai from the future, who needs help putting away the Hinamatsuri dolls; and he is carried into the past, where he meets his mother as a messy little girl and comes to understand her better.

Struggling to ride his bicycle without training wheels, Kun is transported to rural Japan, where a young man with an injured leg takes him riding on a horse and a motorcycle; the lessons help him succeed, and he later learns that the man was his recently deceased great-grandfather. Before a family outing, a tantrum leads Kun to a phantom train station, where he boards a train against a teenager's warning and ends up lost at Tokyo Station, unable to name his parents and threatened with a train to "Lonely Land". He finally claims baby Mirai as his sister, and the future Mirai flies him home through the family tree, showing him moments of his family's history and revealing that the teenager at the station was his future self.

Mirai premiered in the Directors' Fortnight at Cannes on May 16, 2018, and opened in Japan on July 20, 2018, grossing about $23.7 million there. It earned 91% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 81, and it received an Academy Award nomination for Best Animated Feature.

documents.title: In Fabric
documents.overview: A haunting ghost story set against the backdrop of a busy winter sales period in a department store, following the life of a cursed dress as it passes from person to person, with devastating consequences.
documents.plot:
In Fabric is a 2018 British black comedy horror film written and directed by Peter Cosgrove. The movie follows the story of a mysterious dress that seems to have a life of its own, causing chaos and destruction in the lives of those who wear it.

The main themes of In Fabric include:

1. Consumerism and Materialism: The film critiques modern consumer culture, highlighting how people are often driven by superficial desires and material possessions. The dress serves as a symbol of this, representing the empty and fleeting nature of consumerist values.
2. Toxic Masculinity: The character of Steve, played by Paddy Considine, embodies toxic masculinity, with his aggressive and controlling behavior towards women. The film critiques this toxic dynamic, highlighting its damaging effects on relationships and individuals.
3. Feminism and Empowerment: The female characters in the film, particularly the shop assistant, serve as a counterpoint to Steve's toxic masculinity. They are strong, independent, and empowered, challenging the patriarchal norms that Steve represents.
4. Class and Social Hierarchy: The film explores the social class divisions in the town where the story takes place, highlighting the tensions between different socioeconomic groups.

The plot of In Fabric follows a series of events as the mysterious dress causes chaos and destruction, ultimately leading to a confrontation with its owner, Steve. Throughout the film, Cosgrove uses dark humor and satire to critique modern society's values and norms.

Overall, In Fabric is a thought-provoking and unsettling film that challenges viewers to think critically about the themes and issues it presents.

documents.title: Artemis Fowl
documents.overview: Artemis Fowl is a 12-year-old genius and descendant of a long line of criminal masterminds. He soon finds himself in an epic battle against a race of powerful underground fairies who may be behind his father's disappearance.
documents.plot:
Artemis Fowl is a 2020 fantasy adventure film directed by Kenneth Branagh, based on the novel of the same name by Eoin Colfer. The story follows the titular character, Artemis Fowl, a young and wealthy Irish fairy who lives with his mother, Juliet, in Dublin.

The movie begins with Artemis, a 12-year-old boy, feeling suffocated by his life of luxury and boredom. He is constantly at odds with his mother, who wants him to follow in her footsteps as a businesswoman. However, Artemis's true passion lies in the world of fairies, which he has been studying secretly.

One day, Artemis discovers that his father, Arthur, a famous fairy hunter, has gone missing while on a mission to capture a powerful fairy named Valtor. The fairy community is in disarray, and Artemis decides to embark on a journey to find his father and uncover the truth about Valtor's powers.

Artemis teams up with a group of fairies, including Bree, a skilled warrior; Holly Short, a clever and resourceful fairy who serves as the leader of the Fairy Council; and Mulch Diggum, a gentle but fierce fairy. Together, they set out on a perilous quest to find Valtor's lair and rescue Artemis's father.

As they journey through the fairy world, the group encounters various obstacles and challenges, including treacherous landscapes, ferocious creatures, and rival fairy factions vying for power. Along the way, Artemis learns valuable lessons about courage, loyalty, and the importance of understanding and respecting other cultures.

The plot thickens as Artemis and his companions discover that Valtor is a powerful and ruthless fairy who seeks to dominate the human world. Valtor's powers are fueled by the energy of children, which he can drain from their bodies using a device called the "Child Snatcher."

As the stakes grow higher, Artemis and his friends must use all their skills and cunning to outwit Valtor's minions and reach the heart of his lair. In a thrilling showdown, Artemis confronts Valtor and manages to defeat him by exploiting his own weakness: his inability to connect with children.

With Valtor defeated, Artemis is hailed as a hero by the fairy community, and he finally finds the acceptance and recognition he has been seeking. The movie ends with Artemis returning home to Dublin, where he is welcomed back by his mother and friends. However, it's clear that Artemis's adventures are far from over, and he will continue to explore the magical world of fairies.

Overall, Artemis Fowl is a thrilling adventure film that explores themes of identity, community, and the power of imagination. With its richly detailed world-building and engaging characters, the movie is sure to delight fans of fantasy and adventure films.

documents.title: Joker
documents.overview: During the 1980s, a failed stand-up comedian is driven insane and turns to a life of crime and chaos in Gotham City while becoming an infamous psychopathic crime figure.
documents.plot:
Joker is a psychological thriller film directed by Todd Phillips, released in 2019. The movie stars Joaquin Phoenix as Arthur Fleck, a struggling comedian and clown-for-hire who descends into madness.

The film begins with Arthur's childhood, where he is shown to be an outcast among his peers due to his physical disability and mental health issues. As the years pass, Arthur becomes increasingly isolated and disillusioned with society, feeling like an outsider in a world that seems to value superficiality over genuine human connection.

As an adult, Arthur works as a clown-for-hire at children's birthday parties, where he is met with ridicule and disdain by the very people he is trying to entertain. He also struggles to make ends meet, working multiple jobs while living in poverty. Despite his efforts, Arthur feels like he is invisible and ignored by society.

Arthur's life takes a turn for the worse when his mother passes away, leaving him feeling abandoned and alone. He begins to question the nature of reality and the world around him, becoming increasingly paranoid and detached from reality.

As Arthur's mental health deteriorates, he becomes obsessed with the idea that he is the only one who truly understands the suffering of others. He starts to see himself as a symbol of resistance against a society that has wronged him and others like him.

The film builds towards a tragic confrontation between Arthur and the wealthy elite, who are shown to be callous and indifferent to the struggles of those on the margins. In a shocking and disturbing climax, Arthur's transformation into the Joker is complete, and he unleashes his wrath upon the world.

Throughout the film, Joaquin Phoenix delivers a tour-de-force performance as Arthur Fleck/Joker, bringing depth and nuance to a character that could have easily been reduced to a cartoonish villain. The film's themes of isolation, loneliness, and the breakdown of social norms are timely and thought-provoking, making Joker a haunting and unforgettable cinematic experience.

Village Roadshow Pictures did not produce this movie, it was actually Warner Bros. Pictures

documents.title: 2048: Nowhere to Run
documents.overview: “2048: Nowhere to Run” takes place one year before the events of Blade Runner 2049. The short film focuses on Sapper, a man who is trying to make it through life day-by-day without turning back to his old ways. We’re introduced to both the gentle nature of Sapper and the violence he’s capable of when set off.
documents.plot:
2048: Nowhere to Run is a 2017 American tech noir short film directed by Luke Scott and written by Hampton Fancher and Michael Green, the screenwriters of Blade Runner 2049. One of three prequel shorts commissioned to bridge the thirty years between Blade Runner and its sequel, alongside Blade Runner Black Out 2022 and 2036: Nexus Dawn, it stars Dave Bautista as the replicant Sapper Morton, a character he plays in the feature, with Orion Ben, Gaia Ottman, Björn Freiberg and Adam Savage in supporting roles. Luke Scott's father, Ridley Scott, directed the original Blade Runner and executive produced the sequel. The short was released online on September 16, 2017, about three weeks before the feature.

The story is set in Los Angeles in 2048, one year before the events of Blade Runner 2049. Sapper Morton, a Nexus-8 replicant living quietly among humans in hiding, is first seen weeping uncontrollably before a mirror, struggling with memories of his past, before composing himself and heading out into the crowded, rain-soaked streets. He ignores a gang of thugs who harass him and stops to greet Ella, a young girl from the neighborhood, giving her a copy of Graham Greene's novel The Power and the Glory, a book he loved. He then visits a market to sell produce from his farm, but the buyer pays him $3,000, a thousand dollars short of what he needs.

Leaving the market, Sapper sees Ella and her mother being attacked by the same thugs he had earlier passed by. Unable to stand by, he intervenes and overpowers the attackers with the brutal, superhuman strength of a combat model replicant, killing or maiming several of them. The violence, witnessed by bystanders, exposes his true nature. The incident leads to his status as a replicant being reported to the authorities, setting in motion the events that will lead an LAPD blade runner to his farm at the beginning of Blade Runner 2049. A version released in China includes a prologue explaining the rise of Niander Wallace and his corporation.

Denis Villeneuve, the director of Blade Runner 2049, selected the filmmakers for the three shorts, which were announced in August 2017 as part of the feature's marketing. Scott had previously directed 2036: Nexus Dawn. The short was well received, with commentators noting that it gave Bautista a role worthy of his talents and added depth to a character who appears only briefly in the feature.

documents.title: Tell It to the Bees
documents.tagline: Some secrets are too powerful to keep
documents.overview: Dr. Jean Markham returns to the town she left as a teenager to take over her late father's medical practice. When a school-yard scuffle lands Charlie in her surgery, she invites him to visit the hives in her garden and tell his secrets to the bees, as she once did. The new friendship between the boy and the bee keeper brings his mother Lydia into Jean's world.
documents.plot:
Tell It to the Bees is a 2018 British romantic period drama directed by Annabel Jankel and starring Anna Paquin and Holliday Grainger. Henrietta and Jessica Ashworth adapted the screenplay from Fiona Shaw's 2009 novel, moving its setting from Yorkshire to a small town in 1950s Scotland. The cast also includes Emun Elliott, Gregor Selkirk, Kate Dickie, Lauren Lyle and Steven Robertson, with Billy Boyd heard as the voice of the adult Charlie, who narrates the story.

Dr. Jean Markham (Paquin) returns to the town she left as a teenager, after a scandal over her love for another girl, to take over her late father's medical practice and his house, where she keeps beehives. Lydia Weekes (Grainger) is a mill worker struggling to pay the rent after her war-scarred husband Robert (Elliott) has walked out on her and their son Charlie (Selkirk). When the lonely, bullied Charlie is brought to Jean's surgery after a playground fight, she shows him the hives and teaches him the old custom of telling one's secrets to the bees. Lydia, wary at first, warms to the reserved doctor. After Lydia loses her job and she and Charlie are evicted, Jean takes them in and hires her as a housekeeper, and the two women slowly fall in love, a relationship that must stay hidden in a gossiping, judgmental community. Meanwhile Lydia's niece Annie (Lyle), the daughter of Robert's sister Pam (Dickie), becomes pregnant. In the final act, Jean must use her medical skills to save Annie after a botched backstreet abortion, while Robert, hostile and homophobic, confronts Lydia, and even the bees are drawn into the violent climax.

Developed with funding from the BFI Film Fund and Creative Scotland, the film was shot near Stirling from August 2017 and scored by Claire M. Singer. It premiered as a Special Presentation at the Toronto International Film Festival on 9 September 2018, opened in limited release in the United States on 3 May 2019 and reached British cinemas that July. Reviews were mixed, with a Metacritic score of 50: critics praised the performances and chemistry of Paquin and Grainger but faulted a didactic script and a melodramatic third act that departs sharply from the novel.
production_companies: Taking a Line for a Walk Productions

documents.title: Blade Runner: Black Out 2022
documents.original_title: ブレードランナー ブラックアウト 2022
documents.overview: This animated short revolves around the events causing an electrical systems failure on the west coast of the US. According to Blade Runner 2049’s official timeline, this failure leads to cities shutting down, financial and trade markets being thrown into chaos, and food supplies dwindling. There’s no proof as to what caused the blackouts, but Replicants — the bio-engineered robots featured in the original Blade Runner, are blamed.
documents.plot:
Blade Runner Black Out 2022 (Japanese: Burēdoran'nā Burakkuauto 2022) is a 2017 Japanese cyberpunk tech-noir anime short film directed by Shinichiro Watanabe and animated by CygamesPictures. It is one of three short films, together with 2036: Nexus Dawn and 2048: Nowhere to Run, made as prequels to the live-action feature Blade Runner 2049, and it bridges the years between the original Blade Runner and its sequel. The voice cast includes Jovan Jackson as Iggy Cygnus, Luci Christian as Trixie, Bryson Baugus as Ren and Edward James Olmos, who returns as Gaff. The short debuted on Crunchyroll on 27 September 2017.

Three years after the events of Blade Runner, the Tyrell Corporation has introduced a new line of replicants, the Nexus-8, whose lifespans are open-ended like those of humans, and growing tension between people and replicants leads to unrest. When a replicant named Trixie is attacked by a gang of human thugs, she is rescued by Iggy, a replicant soldier who deserted after discovering that the enemy he was fighting were replicants too. Iggy recruits Trixie into an underground replicant freedom movement whose goal is to wipe out the Tyrell Corporation's database and tracking records so that replicants can no longer be easily identified and hunted. Trixie befriends Ren, a sympathetic human technician who is in charge of launching nuclear missiles, and he agrees to redirect a test missile so that it detonates over Los Angeles, where its electromagnetic pulse will plunge the city into darkness and erase electronic data. While the missile is on its way, Trixie and Iggy set out to physically destroy the Tyrell servers themselves, a mission that comes at a heavy cost. The resulting blackout triggers a global collapse in which replicant production is halted and Tyrell goes bankrupt, paving the way for the Wallace Corporation to take over the company and revive replicant manufacturing a decade later, setting the stage for the world of Blade Runner 2049.

The short was well received by viewers, earning user ratings of 7.3 on IMDb and 4.4 out of 5 on Crunchyroll. Writing for Forbes, Ollie Barder praised it as "expertly done", wishing there had been more of it, and noted that it combines elements of Watanabe's Cowboy Bebop with some of the bleakness of the anime Armor Hunter Mellowlink, on which Watanabe also worked.

documents.title: Ghostland
documents.tagline: You really thought you’ve been scared?
documents.overview: A mother of two inherits a home from her aunt. On the first night in the new home she is confronted with murderous intruders and fights for her daughters’ lives. Sixteen years later the daughters reunite at the house, and that is when things get strange . . .
documents.plot:
Ghostland is a 2018 American supernatural horror film directed by Jeremy Saulnier. The movie follows a family who is attacked by a group of masked strangers while on their way to a family reunion in rural West Virginia.

The main themes of Ghostland include:

1. **Trauma and Family Dynamics**: The film explores the dark secrets and traumas that can be passed down through generations, particularly within families. The characters' past experiences and relationships with each other are slowly revealed, highlighting the complexities of family dynamics.
2. **Violence and Masculinity**: Ghostland critiques traditional notions of masculinity and the objectification of women. The masked strangers who attack the family embody a twisted form of toxic masculinity, while the male characters in the film struggle to cope with their own emotions and vulnerabilities.
3. **Feminism and Empowerment**: The movie features strong female characters who are forced to confront their own strengths and weaknesses. As they fight for survival, they begin to reclaim their agency and challenge the patriarchal norms that have held them back.
4. **Rural America and Isolation**: The film's setting in rural West Virginia serves as a character in its own right, emphasizing the isolation and confinement of the characters. This isolation heightens the sense of vulnerability and desperation, making the characters' situation even more dire.

Throughout the movie, these themes are intertwined with elements of horror, suspense, and drama, creating a tense and unsettling viewing experience.

documents.title: The King's Man
documents.overview: As a collection of history's worst tyrants and criminal masterminds gather to plot a war to wipe out millions, one man must race against time to stop them.
documents.plot:
The King's Man is a 2021 spy action film directed by Matthew Vaughn, produced by Marv Films, and written by Karl Gajdusek. The movie serves as a prequel to the Kingsman franchise.

The story takes place during World War I and follows the early life of Orlando Oxford (Harris Dickinson), a young man from a wealthy family who is struggling to find his place in society. After his mother's death, Orlando discovers that he has inherited a vast fortune and becomes embroiled in a world of espionage and intrigue.

Orlando meets Phoenix (Ralph Fiennes), the Duke of Oxford, who recognizes his potential as a spy and begins training him in the art of espionage. As Orlando navigates this new world, he befriends a group of young spies, including Conrad Oxford (Rhys Ifans) and Charlotte (Hannah Rae).

The story takes a dark turn when Orlando discovers that his family's business is secretly funding the war effort, and that they are involved in a plot to assassinate Kaiser Wilhelm II. As Orlando delves deeper into the conspiracy, he must confront his own demons and make difficult choices to protect himself and those he cares about.

Throughout the film, Vaughn pays homage to the original Kingsman franchise while introducing new characters and themes. The movie features a blend of action, humor, and style, with a nod to classic spy films from the 1960s and 1970s.

One of the standout aspects of The King's Man is its exploration of the complexities of class and privilege in the early 20th century. Orlando's journey from an outsider to a member of the aristocracy serves as a commentary on the social hierarchies of the time, while also highlighting the moral ambiguities of those who wield power.

Overall, The King's Man is a thrilling and entertaining film that expands the Kingsman universe in exciting ways. With its stylish visuals, witty dialogue, and strong performances, it is a must-see for fans of the franchise and action-adventure movies in general.

documents.title: The Front Runner
documents.overview: Gary Hart, former Senator of Colorado, becomes the front-runner for the Democratic presidential nomination in 1987. Hart's intelligence, charisma and idealism makes him popular with young voters, leaving him with a seemingly clear path to the White House. All that comes crashing down when allegations of an extramarital affair surface in the media, forcing the candidate to address a scandal that threatens to derail his campaign and personal life.
documents.plot:
The Front Runner is a biographical drama film that explores the life of Gary Hart, an American politician who was a prominent figure in the Democratic Party during the 1980s. The movie delves into the personal and professional struggles of Hart, as he navigates his rise to prominence and ultimately faces a scandal that threatens to destroy his career.

At its core, The Front Runner is a film about the corrupting influence of power and the consequences of one's actions. It examines how Hart's desire for success and recognition led him to engage in questionable behavior, including an extramarital affair with a young woman named Marianne Baker. As Hart's personal life becomes increasingly complicated, he finds himself at odds with his wife, Lee, who struggles to cope with the infidelity.

The film also touches on themes of identity and authenticity. Hart is portrayed as a charismatic figure who presents a polished public image, but behind closed doors, he grapples with feelings of inadequacy and insecurity. This tension between his public persona and private self serves as a catalyst for his downfall.

Furthermore, The Front Runner critiques the media's role in shaping public perception and the consequences of sensationalism. The film depicts how Hart's personal life is exploited by the press, leading to a vicious cycle of scandal and scrutiny that ultimately destroys his reputation.

Ultimately, The Front Runner is a nuanced exploration of the human condition, revealing the complexities and flaws of its protagonist as he navigates the treacherous waters of politics and personal relationships.

documents.title: The Titan
documents.overview: On a bleak future Earth, a soldier endures a radical genetic transformation to save humanity. But his wife fears he's becoming more creature than man.
documents.plot:
The Titan is a 2018 science fiction thriller film directed by Lennart Ruff from a screenplay by Max Hurwitz, based on a story by Arash Amel. An international co-production between the United Kingdom, the United States, Germany and Spain, it stars Sam Worthington, Taylor Schilling and Tom Wilkinson, with Agyness Deyn and Nathalie Emmanuel in supporting roles. The story follows a military pilot who undergoes radical genetic modification to prepare humanity for life on Saturn's moon Titan.

In 2048, with an overpopulated Earth torn by violent conflicts, scientists led by Professor Martin Collingwood see Titan as a new home for humanity. U.S. Air Force pilot Rick Janssen volunteers for an experiment on fourteen test subjects meant to adapt human bodies to the moon's frigid methane seas and thin oxygen atmosphere, and moves to the Titan I research area with his wife Abigail, a medical researcher, and their son Lucas. Early results are promising: Rick can swim at great speed and stay underwater for 42 minutes. But as training intensifies, his hair falls out, his skin sheds, one volunteer dies of convulsions and the subjects' veins darken. Another volunteer, Zane, suffers breakdowns and kills his wife Rayenne, Abigail's friend, before being shot by military police. Stealing Rick's key card, Abigail finds autopsy reports revealing that the subjects' DNA is being combined with animal DNA to create a new species, Homo titaniens, and Collingwood admits he does not know what the survivors will become. Rick and Tally, the only other surviving subject, complete their transformation, and Rick loses the ability to speak. After Tally kills her husband and is shot, Rick kills several military police officers and flees, and Abigail finds him before both are arrested. Ordered to give Rick a solution that would erase his memories, Abigail secretly substitutes saline, and she and Lucas escape with Dr. Freya Upton, a dissenting assistant of Collingwood's. Soldiers refuse Collingwood's order to fire on them, and the colonel arrests him. Abigail and Freya later continue the research at the Titan II facility by more ethical methods, while Rick is seen flying over a methane lake on Titan.

Netflix released The Titan in several countries on March 30, 2018, and it opened in British cinemas that April. Shot in Gran Canaria, it received generally negative reviews, holding a 23% Rotten Tomatoes rating with a consensus calling it bland and uninspired.

documents.title: Paul, Apostle of Christ
documents.tagline: Where sin abounds... grace abounds more
documents.overview: Risking his life, Luke ventures to Rome to visit Paul -- the apostle who's bound in chains and held captive in Nero's darkest and bleakest prison cell. Haunted by the shadows of his past misdeeds, Paul wonders if he's been forgotten as he awaits his grisly execution. Before Paul's death, Luke resolves to write another book that details the birth of what will come to be known as the church.
documents.plot:
Paul, Apostle of Christ is a 2018 American drama film directed by Chris Downey and written by Mike Bernardo and Jonathan Bernardo. The movie stars James Egan as Saul, also known as Paul the Apostle, and Bruce Dern as Saint Peter.

The film begins with Saul, a young Pharisee who is deeply devoted to his faith and is part of the Jewish community in Jerusalem. He is particularly close to Saint Peter, who becomes like a mentor to him. However, after a dramatic encounter on the road to Damascus, Saul's life takes a drastic turn. He experiences a profound conversion experience where he encounters Jesus Christ, which leads him to become one of the most influential figures in Christianity.

As Saul begins his new journey as an apostle, he faces opposition from within and outside the Jewish community. Many of his former friends and family members reject him due to his radical change in faith. Meanwhile, Saint Peter is struggling with his own doubts about Jesus' divinity and the implications of his teachings on the Jewish people.

The plot thickens when Saul meets Saint Paul (played by Jim Caviezel), a Roman soldier who has also had a transformative experience with Jesus. The two men form an unlikely bond as they discuss their shared faith and the challenges they face in spreading Christianity to the Gentiles. However, their conversation is interrupted by the arrival of King Agrippa II, who is determined to silence them.

As tensions rise, Saul and Saint Paul are put on trial before King Agrippa, where they defend their faith against accusations of blasphemy. The trial becomes a pivotal moment in the film, as it highlights the risks and challenges faced by early Christians in spreading their message.

Throughout the movie, the relationship between Saul and Saint Peter is also explored in depth. Despite their differences, they remain close friends and confidants, with Saint Peter serving as a source of guidance and support for Saul. The dynamic between the two characters adds an emotional depth to the film, highlighting the complexities of faith and friendship.

The movie concludes with Saul's execution by beheading, which marks a tragic end to his journey as an apostle. Despite facing persecution and adversity, Saul remains committed to his faith, leaving behind a legacy that would shape the course of Christianity for centuries to come.

Overall, Paul, Apostle of Christ is a thought-provoking film that explores the complexities of faith, friendship, and the challenges faced by early Christians. The movie features strong performances from its cast, particularly Bruce Dern as Saint Peter, who brings gravity and depth to his portrayal of the iconic biblical figure.

documents.title: The Painted Bird
documents.tagline: Light is visible only in the dark
documents.overview: A young boy wanders Eastern Europe during World War II.
documents.plot:
The Painted Bird (Nabarvené ptáče) is a 2019 Czech war drama written, directed and produced by Václav Marhoul. It adapts Jerzy Kosiński's novel of the same name. Petr Kotlár plays the boy, with a supporting cast including Udo Kier, Stellan Skarsgård, Harvey Keitel, Julian Sands and Barry Pepper. It is the first film to use the constructed Interslavic language. Marhoul chose it so that no Slavic nation would be identified with the brutal villagers.

During the Second World War, somewhere in German-occupied Eastern Europe, a young Jewish boy has been left in the care of his elderly aunt. When she dies, he accidentally burns down her house and sets out alone. His journey becomes a series of horrific encounters with superstition, cruelty and abuse. An old healer buys him, but villagers blame him for bad luck and throw him into a river. A miller gouges out the eyes of a young man he suspects of desiring his wife. A kindly bird catcher, Lekh, hangs himself after village women brutally attack his lover. Handed to the Germans, the boy is spared by the soldier ordered to shoot him and later escapes execution again. A priest takes him in but places him with Garbos, who sexually abuses him, and the boy causes Garbos's death. He is driven out after the priest dies and is then sexually exploited by a widow, Labina, before fleeing.

When the Red Army arrives, a Soviet sniper, Mitka, briefly looks after him, and the boy watches him kill villagers in revenge for an attack on Soviet soldiers. Sent to an orphanage, the now-mute boy keeps trying to run away and kills a shopkeeper who beat him. Finally, a man named Nikodém arrives and tearfully claims him as his son. On the bus home, the boy notices a number tattooed on his father's arm and, with his finger, writes his name, Joska, on the misted window.

Marhoul secured the rights in 2012. Shooting took place over 16 months between 2017 and 2018 in Ukraine, Slovakia and the Czech Republic, with Vladimír Smutný as cinematographer. The film competed at the 76th Venice International Film Festival, where some viewers walked out over its violence, but it also received long ovations, and it later played at Toronto and London. It was the Czech submission for the Academy Award for Best International Feature Film and made the shortlist. It won nine Czech Lions, including Best Film. The Guardian gave it five stars, calling it a savage three-hour tour of hell.

documents.title: Overlord: The Undead King
documents.original_title: 劇場版総集編 オーバーロード 不死者の王【前編】
documents.overview: The first recap film of season 1 of the anime TV series Overlord, covering episodes 1 to 7. In the year 2138,  the popular online VR game Yggdrasil is quietly shut down one day. However, the player Momonga decides to not log out and is transformed into a powerful skeletal wizard upon shutdown. The game world continues to change, with non-player characters beginning to feel emotions. Confronted with this abnormal situation, Momonga and his loyal followers strive to investigate and take over the new world the game has become.
documents.plot:
Overlord: The Undead King (Gekijō-ban Sōshūhen Ōbārōdo: Fushisha no Ō) is a 2017 Japanese animated fantasy film, the first of two theatrical compilation films recapping the first season of the anime television series Overlord, itself based on the light novels written by Kugane Maruyama and illustrated by so-bin. Produced by Madhouse with Kadokawa, it was directed by Naoyuki Itō, with series composition by Yukie Sugawara and music by Shūji Katayama, and re-edits the first seven episodes of the 2015 series, adding new scenes such as an extended battle with Hamsuke. Released in Japan on 25 February 2017 and running 103 minutes, it was followed on 11 March by the second compilation, Overlord: The Dark Warrior. Its theme song, "Crazy Scary Holy Fantasy", was performed by Myth & Roid. The voice cast is led by Satoshi Hino as Momonga, with Yumi Hara as Albedo, Sumire Uesaka as Shalltear Bloodfallen, Masayuki Katou as Demiurge and Aoi Yūki as Clementine.

In the year 2138, after twelve years of operation, the immersive online role-playing game Yggdrasil is shutting down its servers. The once-feared guild Ainz Ooal Gown, which had 41 members, has dwindled to almost nothing, and its leader Momonga, a skeletal undead spellcaster, decides to stay in the guild's base, the Great Tomb of Nazarick, until the end. When the deadline passes he finds himself unable to log out, trapped in the body of his avatar, while the non-player characters have gained minds and wills of their own and pledge him absolute loyalty. Realising he is no longer in the game but in a strange new world, Momonga adopts a regal manner and wonders whether his friends were transported too.

When knights attack the nearby Carne Village, he intervenes, saving two young girls and dispatching the attackers with a summoned Death Knight, then rescues the kingdom's Warrior Captain, Gazef Stronoff, from the assassins of the Sunlight Scripture. Taking the guild's name, Ainz Ooal Gown, so that it might become legendary and reach any lost comrades, he unknowingly sets his followers on a path of world conquest. Disguised as the adventurer Momon, he travels to the city of E-Rantel with his battle maid Narberal Gamma, now called Nabe, joins the adventurer team Swords of Darkness to escort the young pharmacist Nfirea Bareare, and tames the legendary Wise King of the Forest, a giant hamster he names Hamsuke, while a cult and the killer Clementine plot to seize Nfirea.

documents.title: Overlord: The Dark Hero
documents.original_title: 劇場版総集編 オーバーロード 漆黒の英雄【後編】
documents.overview: The second recap film of season 1 of the anime TV series Overlord, covering episodes 8 to 13.
documents.plot:
Overlord: The Dark Hero (Japanese: Gekijō-ban Sōshūhen Ōbārōdo: Shikkoku no Eiyū) is a 2017 Japanese animated fantasy compilation film produced by Madhouse and released by Kadokawa, the second of two theatrical recap films condensing the first season of the anime Overlord, itself based on Kugane Maruyama's light novel series. Covering episodes eight to thirteen, it follows the first film, The Undead King, released in February 2017; English-language sources also list it as The Dark Warrior. Satoshi Hino voices Ainz Ooal Gown, with Yumi Hara as Albedo, Sumire Uesaka as Shalltear Bloodfallen, Emiri Katō as Aura, Aoi Yūki as Clementine and Asami Seto as CZ2128 Delta.

When the virtual reality game Yggdrasil shut down, the guild master Momonga found himself transported with his guild's stronghold, the Great Tomb of Nazarick, and its loyal servants into a real fantasy world, where he took the name Ainz Ooal Gown. Seeking to learn about this world, he poses as the adventurer Momon, accompanied by the battle maid Narberal disguised as Nabe, and joins the adventurers' guild of E-Rantel. Escorting the young Nfirea with the adventurer party Swords of Darkness, Momon tames the legendary Wise King of the Forest, a giant hamster he names Hamsuke. Back in the city, the assassin Clementine and the necromancer Khajiit kidnap Nfirea, slaughter the Swords of Darkness and raise an undead army in the cemetery. Hired by Nfirea's grandmother, Momon tracks them down; Nabe destroys Khajiit and his skeletal dragons, while Momon toys with Clementine before revealing his undead form and crushing her. Meanwhile Shalltear, hunting for martial arts users, falls under the control of a powerful World Class Item wielded by unknown attackers. Realizing that no ordinary means can free her, Ainz decides to face one of Nazarick's strongest guardians himself, defeating her with a meticulously prepared plan built on knowledge from her creator before resurrecting her at great cost. Momon and Nabe are then promoted directly to adamantite rank, becoming the kingdom's third adamantite party.

The Dark Hero opened in Japanese theaters on 11 March 2017, two weeks after The Undead King. The theme song of the two films, "Crazy Scary Holy Fantasy," was performed by Myth & Roid. A second television season was announced during screenings of the second compilation film and premiered in January 2018.

documents.title: The Twin
documents.tagline: Evil only a mother could love.
documents.overview: Every parent's worst nightmare is just the beginning for Rachel's ordeal as in the aftermath of a tragic accident, she and her husband Anthony decide to move to the other side of the world to focus on their surviving twin son Elliot.  What begins as a time of healing and isolation in the Finnish countryside turns into a desperate battle for the very soul of their son as an entity claiming to be his dead twin brother takes over Elliot — setting Rachel on a diabolical journey to unravel the horrible truth about her twin son.
documents.plot:
The Twin is a 2022 psychological horror film directed by Taneli Mustonen, who wrote the original screenplay with producer Aleksi Hyvärinen. The film follows a mother who must face an unbearable truth about her surviving twin son. Teresa Palmer stars as Rachel, with Steven Cree as her husband Anthony, Barbara Marten as Helen, Tristan Ruggeri as the twins Elliot and Nathan, and Andres Dvinjaninov as the town doctor.

Grieving the death of their son Nathan in a car accident, Rachel and Anthony move from New York to Finland with his twin brother Elliot. On an outing, Elliot finds a wall said to grant wishes and makes a secret wish, and soon afterwards he begins talking to someone invisible. At a welcome party thrown by the townspeople, Rachel meets the local doctor and Helen, who makes a cryptic remark about Elliot's wish. Elliot's behaviour grows disturbing, and he claims to be Nathan. When Rachel asks the doctor for help, he insists that she is the one who is ill and needs therapy. Desperate, she turns to Helen, who tells her that the town belongs to a satanic cult and that her late husband was possessed by an evil entity that appeared in photographs. Rachel photographs Elliot, but a séance she holds with him is interrupted by the townspeople and Anthony, who say they want to use the boy in a ritual. When the prints come back, Elliot appears in none of them; Helen calls this the demon taunting her and asks to see him, but on meeting the boy she too tells Rachel that she is sick. Surrounded by the townspeople, Rachel is sedated, made to take part in a satanic ritual and locked in her room. Hearing Elliot call for help, she escapes into the forest, where Anthony reveals the truth: Elliot does not exist. Rachel had been leaving Anthony with Nathan when the crash happened, and in her grief and anger she invented a second son. Rather than see her committed, Anthony went along with the delusion. When "Elliot" runs off claiming that Anthony wants to kill him, Rachel follows to a grain silo, where Anthony tries to break the delusion by burying the imaginary boy in grain, and Rachel accidentally kills him while trying to stop him. Digging in the grain, she finds nothing. Back in New York, she visits the graves of Nathan and Anthony yet still believes that they and Elliot are alive.

The Twin premiered at the Night Visions festival on March 24, 2022, and streamed on Shudder in the United States. Reviews were mixed, with a 41% Rotten Tomatoes rating.

documents.title: Proxima
documents.overview: Sarah is a French astronaut training at the European Space Agency in Cologne. She is the only woman in the arduous program. She lives alone with Stella, her seven year old daughter. Sarah feels guilty that she cannot spend more time with her child. Her love is overpowering, unsettling. When Sarah is chosen to join the crew of a year-long space mission called Proxima, it creates chaos in the mother-daughter relationship.
documents.plot:
Proxima is a thought-provoking and emotionally charged film that delves into the complexities of human relationships, identity, and the challenges of parenthood. The movie follows a mother's journey as she navigates her complicated past and present, all while trying to connect with her daughter.

At its core, Proxima explores the theme of longing and yearning for connection and understanding. The film's protagonist is a woman who has been estranged from her family for years, and her relationship with her daughter is fraught with tension and uncertainty. As she tries to rebuild their bond, she must confront her own emotional scars and learn to let go of her past.

The movie also touches on the theme of identity and how it can be shaped by our experiences and relationships. The protagonist's journey is a metaphor for the search for self-discovery and the struggle to find one's place in the world. Through her interactions with her daughter, she begins to uncover fragments of her own past and re-evaluate her sense of self.

Furthermore, Proxima explores the theme of motherhood as a complex and multifaceted experience. The film portrays the challenges of balancing personal desires with parental responsibilities, highlighting the tension between nurturing one's child and maintaining one's own identity.

Overall, Proxima is a nuanced and emotionally resonant film that probes the intricacies of human relationships and the complexities of the human experience.

documents.title: Acts of Violence
documents.overview: When his fiancee is kidnapped by human traffickers, Roman and his ex-military brothers set out to track her down and save her before it is too late. Along the way, Roman teams up with Avery, a cop investigating human trafficking and fighting the corrupt bureaucracy that has harmful intentions.
documents.plot:
Acts of Violence is a 2018 American action thriller directed by Brett Donowho from a screenplay by Nicolas Aaron Mezzanatto. Bruce Willis, Cole Hauser, Shawn Ashmore, Ashton Holmes, Melissa Bolona, Sophia Bush and Mike Epps head the cast. Principal photography began in Cleveland, Ohio, in March 2017, and Lionsgate Premiere released the film in a limited theatrical run and on video on demand on January 12, 2018.

In Cleveland, the MacGregor brothers are preparing for a wedding. Deklan and Brandon are former U.S. Army Rangers who served overseas; Deklan remains haunted by his experiences, and Brandon has a family to support. The youngest, Roman, is engaged to his childhood sweetheart, Mia. At her bachelorette party, Mia insults Vince and Frank, two thugs who traffic women for the local crime boss Max Livingston, and they snatch her from the club. Detective James Avery has long been trying to build a case against Livingston, but corruption within the police department keeps getting in his way. Mia manages to leave Roman a voice message before she is taken, and Roman turns to Deklan. Tracking her phone, the brothers raid a house where they believe she is held but find nothing, and Avery, while promising help, warns them to stay out of it. They refuse.

Livingston, angry that his men have taken someone likely to be reported missing, forces Mia's finger onto a trigger to make her shoot Frank. Arming themselves with military-grade vests and weapons, the brothers capture Vince, learn where Mia is and kill several of Livingston's men, only to find she has already escaped through a window. A tracking implant allows the gang to recapture her, and the brothers return to Brandon's ransacked home to find his wife, Jessa, bound and dead. Enraged, they storm a warehouse where Livingston keeps trafficked women in trucks bound for Las Vegas and free Mia and the others. Livingston then attacks the house, killing Brandon, and escapes. Deklan and Roman are arrested while Livingston remains free, prompting Avery to quit the force, track Livingston to his hideout and shoot him before he can leave town.

Willis plays Avery, Hauser plays Deklan, Ashmore plays Brandon, Holmes plays Roman, Bolona plays Mia, Epps plays Livingston and Bush plays Detective Brooke Baker. Critics dismissed it, with none of 13 reviews on Rotten Tomatoes positive and a Metacritic score of 28. It earned about $387,000 from releases in the United Arab Emirates and Portugal.

documents.title: The Robot Chicken Walking Dead Special: Look Who's Walking
documents.original_title: The Robot Chicken Walking Dead Special: Look Who's Walking
documents.overview: Seth Green and Matthew Senreich serve up hilarious Walking Dead-inspired satire in this special featuring the zany stop-motion animation of Adult Swim’s “Robot Chicken.”
documents.plot:
The Robot Chicken Walking Dead Special: Look Who's Walking is a satirical and irreverent take on the popular television series The Walking Dead. At its core, this special explores the absurdity and humor in the post-apocalyptic world created by Robert Kirkman, Tony Moore, and Charlie Adlard.

One of the main themes of this special is the dehumanization of characters in a desperate situation. By using stop-motion animation and parodying the Walking Dead universe, Robot Chicken highlights how easily people can become desensitized to violence and cruelty when faced with survival instincts. This theme is often played for laughs, but it also raises questions about the nature of humanity and what drives individuals to make certain choices in extreme circumstances.

Another significant theme present in this special is the commentary on toxic masculinity. The Walking Dead has been criticized for its portrayal of male characters, particularly Rick Grimes, who can come across as a symbol of patriarchal dominance. Robot Chicken's take on these characters, often depicting them as buffoons or caricatures, serves to subvert and mock traditional masculine norms.

The special also pokes fun at the conventions of television shows like The Walking Dead, using humor to critique the genre itself. By exaggerating and distorting certain elements, such as character motivations and plot twists, Robot Chicken creates a sense of meta-satire that comments on the very nature of storytelling.

Overall, The Robot Chicken Walking Dead Special: Look Who's Walking is a comedic exploration of themes that are both timely and timeless, using humor to comment on the human condition in all its complexity.

documents.title: Escape Plan: The Extractors
documents.overview: After security expert Ray Breslin is hired to rescue the kidnapped daughter of a Hong Kong tech mogul from a formidable Latvian prison, Breslin's girlfriend is also captured. Now he and his team must pull off a deadly rescue mission to confront their sadistic foe and save the hostages before time runs out.
documents.plot:
Escape Plan: The Extractors is a 2019 action thriller film directed by John Hlavin and starring Sylvester Stallone, Arnold Schwarzenegger, and Adria Arjona. 

The main themes of Escape Plan: The Extractors revolve around the exploitation of vulnerable individuals, particularly women, in the sex trade industry. The story follows a former CIA operative (Stallone) who teams up with a skilled hacker (Arjona) to rescue his kidnapped sister from a human trafficking ring.

Throughout the film, the theme of female empowerment is prominent as the protagonist's sister and other female characters fight against their oppressors. The movie also explores the consequences of corruption and the exploitation of power by those in positions of authority.

Additionally, the film touches on the theme of redemption, as the protagonist seeks to make amends for past mistakes and protect his loved ones from harm. The action-packed plot is driven by a sense of urgency and revenge, adding an element of tension and suspense to the narrative.

Overall, Escape Plan: The Extractors is a gripping thriller that delves into complex themes such as exploitation, corruption, and female empowerment, set against a backdrop of high-stakes action and adventure.

documents.title: House of the Witch
documents.overview: A group of high-school kids set out to play a Halloween prank at an abandoned house, but once they enter they become victims of a demonic witch who has set her wrath upon them.
documents.plot:
House of the Witch is a 2017 American supernatural horror television film directed by Alex Merkin from a screenplay by Neil Elman. Produced by Distilled Media and released by MarVista, it premiered on Syfy on 7 October 2017 and was later picked up by Netflix. The ensemble cast of young actors is led by Emily Bader, Darren Mann, Michelle Randolph, Coy Stewart, Jesse Pepe and Arden Belle, with Jules Hartley, Joseph Curtis Callender, Joel Nagle and Paloma Paulin, who plays the witch. The film carries the tagline "This House Belongs to Her".

The story is set in Meadowcrest, Kentucky, after the disappearance of a high-school student, Charlie Rice (Hunter Trammell). Local legend holds that an old abandoned mansion is cursed by a witch. Dismissing the stories, Lana (Bader) decides to throw a Halloween party there, and on Halloween night a group of her classmates, among them Shane (Mann), a tough kid who would rather become a mechanic than take career advice from his stepfather, Rachel (Randolph), Dax (Stewart), Brody (Pepe) and Taylor (Belle), slip into the house for a prank, some mischief and a bit of romance. Once inside, the teenagers find themselves trapped. Strange things begin to happen: something drips from the walls, a chair moves on its own, a ghostly woman appears in a mirror and a stew is found simmering in a house that is supposed to be empty. The house turns out to be the domain of a demonic witch who unleashes her wrath on the intruders, and the friends must uncover the secrets hidden in the mansion before they are picked off one by one in increasingly gruesome ways.

The production was filmed in May 2017 at an abandoned mansion on Winchester Road in Lexington, Kentucky; producer Bryan Sexton said the team had looked at some thirty locations before settling on the house, which he considered perfect for a haunted mansion.

Reviews were modest. Dread Central found the film entertaining even though it follows the familiar formula of teenagers ignoring warnings to stay away from a scary house, and Rich Copley of Kentucky Entertainment called the Lexington mansion a prime location for a stylish story. Roger Moore of Movie Nation judged it perfectly watchable in an empty-calories way, singling out the swirling, smoke-like spectre of the house and the on-location footage, but criticised its lack of suspense, generic characters and death scenes borrowed from films such as The Ring and Mama.

documents.title: Stickman
documents.overview: The thing that waits under your bed, hides in the closet, stalks your dreams… is waiting for you. At least Emma Wright knew that at the age of 7 when she was wrongly accused of murdering her sister. Emma knew it was the Stickman. After years of isolation she finally has her demons under control and is released.
documents.plot:
Stickman is a 2017 Canadian supernatural horror television film written and directed by Sheldon Wilson, produced by Dandelion Productions and Blue Ice Pictures for Syfy. It stars Hayley Law as Emma Wright, with Zoé De Grand Maison as Liv, and Sara Garcia, Erik Knudsen, Alanna Bale, Anthony Lemke, Delia Lisette Chambers and Sarah Fisher in supporting roles. It runs about 85 minutes.

At the age of seven, Emma was accused of murdering her mother and her sister, and she has spent the following ten years locked up in Homewood Hall, a gloomy mental institution run by Dr. Patrick Fenton. She insists that the killings were committed by the Stickman, a demonic, black-clawed creature that appears when a certain poem naming him is recited aloud, and that the only way to keep him at bay is to draw a picture of him every night. Her doctors dismiss her account as a delusion. The film opens with one of her nightmares, a bloody attack on a school bus, before revealing her life in the hospital, where her fellow patients include Jeremy, who has not spoken in the six years since he too was accused of killing his parents and who obsessively draws sinister stick figures. A year later, having made enough progress to be released, Emma is placed in a halfway house with five other troubled young women, among them an arsonist and a girl obsessed with the dark web, while Jeremy remains behind. The hostile Liv refuses to believe in the Stickman and does not want to live with a murderer. When the poem is read once again, Emma's nightmares return, and this time the creature crosses into the waking world and begins killing the residents. Convinced that the answer lies at the hospital, Emma tries to find a way to stop it, while Liv remains sure that Emma herself is responsible, until the housemates are forced to band together to survive.

Stickman premiered on Syfy on 21 October 2017 as part of the channel's 31 Days of Halloween programming. Lisa Marie Bowman of Through the Shattered Lens enjoyed it, praising Wilson's ominous atmosphere, shadows and jump scares and calling the creature genuinely creepy. Andy Barkworth of HorrorNews.net found the first half entertaining and nicely shot in a chilly blue palette, but felt the tension evaporated once the unconvincing computer-generated monster was fully shown, and criticized its arbitrary rules and predictability.

documents.title: The Curse of La Llorona
documents.overview: A social worker dealing with the disappearance of two children fears for her own family after beginning the investigation.
documents.plot:
The Curse of La Llorona is a 2019 American supernatural horror film directed by Michael Chaves and produced by Jason Blum. The movie is loosely based on Mexican folklore, specifically the legend of La Llorona.

The story begins with Anna García (Natalia Reyes), a young woman who has grown up in a troubled home with her mother, Isabel (Patricia Velásquez), and her father, Mateo (Manuel Garcia-Rulfo). The family is haunted by the ghost of La Llorona, a vengeful spirit who is said to haunt rivers and lakes, searching for her drowned children.

As Anna grows older, she begins to experience strange and terrifying events that suggest La Llorona's presence in their lives. She becomes increasingly isolated from her family and struggles to connect with them.

One day, Anna discovers a dark secret about her family's past, which is revealed through a series of flashbacks. The story takes us back to the 1940s, where we meet Mateo, Isabel, and their two children, Julián (Fernando Gredilla) and Elena (Julissa Baute). The family is struggling to cope with the loss of their young daughter, who drowned in a river.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that La Llorona's curse has been passed down through generations of the García family. Anna begins to experience visions and nightmares, which she believes are connected to her family's dark past.

The plot thickens as Anna discovers that her father is hiding a secret: he was involved in a tragic accident that resulted in the death of his daughter, Elena. The guilt and shame of this event have haunted him for years, and it seems that La Llorona's curse has been awakened by his actions.

As the story reaches its climax, Anna sets out to uncover the truth about her family's past and the origins of La Llorona's curse. She discovers a series of cryptic clues and symbols that lead her on a perilous journey through the Mexican countryside.

In the end, Anna confronts her father and the dark forces that have haunted their family for generations. The movie builds towards a shocking climax as Anna faces off against La Llorona herself, in a desperate bid to break the curse and free her family from its grasp.

The Curse of La Llorona is a tense and atmospheric horror film that explores themes of trauma, guilt, and redemption. While it takes some creative liberties with the original legend, the movie stays true to the spirit of the folklore, capturing the sense of dread and foreboding that has made La Llorona one of Mexico's most enduring and terrifying myths.

Overall, The Curse of La Llorona is a gripping and unsettling horror film that will keep you on the edge of your seat. With its atmospheric setting, creepy visuals, and standout performances from the cast, it's a must-see for fans of the genre.

documents.title: Dreamland
documents.overview: Amid the dust storms and economic depression of Dust Bowl Era Oklahoma, Eugene Evans finds his family farm on the brink of foreclosure. Discovering fugitive bank robber Allison Wells hiding in his small town, he is torn between claiming the bounty on her head and his growing attraction to the seductive criminal.
documents.plot:
Dreamland is a 2019 American period thriller film directed by Miles Joris-Peyrafitte from a screenplay by Nicolaas Zwart. Set in drought-stricken 1930s Texas, it stars Finn Cole as Eugene Evans, a restless teenager, and Margot Robbie as Allison Wells, a wounded fugitive bank robber, with Travis Fimmel as Eugene's stepfather George, Kerry Condon as his mother Olivia, Darby Camp as his younger sister Phoebe, Garrett Hedlund as Allison's partner Perry, and Lola Kirke as the adult Phoebe, who narrates the story. Robbie also produced the film through her company LuckyChap Entertainment, and principal photography took place in New Mexico beginning in October 2017.

In a drought-stricken Texas town plagued by dust storms, Eugene, whose father abandoned the family when he was five, spends his days stealing dime novels with his friend Joe and dreaming of another life. His stepfather George, a lawman, tries to be a father to him and urges him to find work. When the sheriff announces a $10,000 reward for Allison Wells, wanted for bank robbery and murder, Eugene fantasizes about catching her, only to find her hiding, injured, in the family's barn. Allison strikes a deal with him: he tends her wounds, and she offers him a large sum if he helps her get a car to Mexico. She tells him that the girl she is accused of killing died when police fired into a crowd during a robbery. Drawn to the outlaw, Eugene hides her, takes her swimming at a local watering hole and grows infatuated. When he breaks into the police evidence room using his stepfather's keys, he discovers that she concealed the existence of her murderous accomplice, Perry, who was killed during their escape. His theft costs George his job and threatens the family's home, yet Eugene still flees with Allison in the family truck, hoping also to find his real father in Mexico. As the pair head for the border, their romance deepens, and a desperate bank robbery sends them on the run with the law closing in.

Dreamland premiered at the Tribeca Film Festival on April 28, 2019, and was released in a limited release by Vertical Entertainment on November 13, 2020, followed by video on demand from Paramount Home Entertainment. It holds a 60% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus says that Robbie's strong work offsets the film's diffuse narrative, and a Metacritic score of 57.

documents.title: Creed II
documents.tagline: There's More to Lose than a Title
documents.overview: Between personal obligations and training for his next big fight against an opponent with ties to his family's past, Adonis Creed is up against the challenge of his life.
documents.plot:
Creed II is a 2018 American sports drama film directed by Steven Caple Jr. and written by Ryan Coogler and Zach Baylin. The movie serves as a sequel to the 2015 film Creed, which was a spin-off of the Rocky franchise.

The story takes place four years after the events of the first film. Adonis Creed (Michael B. Jordan), now a successful boxer, is facing pressure from his father's legacy and the expectations of those around him. He is also struggling to find his own identity outside of his famous lineage.

Meanwhile, Ivan Drago (Dmitriy Badyakin), the formidable Soviet boxer who defeated Apollo Creed in the infamous 1985 fight, has retired from boxing. However, he is approached by a mysterious figure who convinces him to come out of retirement and face Adonis in the ring.

As Adonis prepares for the big match, he also begins to explore his family's past and the truth about his father's death. He discovers that Apollo was killed by Ivan Drago, not just from a boxing accident as previously thought. This revelation sets Adonis on a path of revenge against Ivan Drago.

The film takes us through Adonis' training with Rocky Balboa (Sylvester Stallone), who becomes a mentor to him in both the ring and out of it. As Adonis trains, he also delves deeper into his family's history and the circumstances surrounding Apollo's death.

As the big match approaches, tensions rise between Adonis and Ivan Drago. The two boxers engage in a series of intense training sessions, each trying to gain an edge over the other. Meanwhile, Adonis' personal life becomes increasingly complicated as he struggles to balance his relationships with those around him.

The film's climax features an epic boxing match between Adonis and Ivan Drago. The fight is intense and brutal, with both boxers giving it their all. In the end, Adonis emerges victorious, but not without scars both physically and emotionally.

Throughout the film, there are also themes of identity, legacy, and redemption explored. Adonis must come to terms with his own identity and find a way to forge his own path in life, separate from his famous father's shadow. The film ultimately concludes on a hopeful note, with Adonis having found a sense of purpose and belonging.

Overall, Creed II is a powerful and emotional film that explores the complexities of family, legacy, and identity. With outstanding performances from Michael B. Jordan and Sylvester Stallone, the film delivers an unforgettable cinematic experience.

documents.title: Bullet Head
documents.overview: A group of career criminals finds itself trapped in a warehouse with the law – and an Attack Dog named DeNiro closing in.
documents.plot:
Bullet Head is a 2017 American action thriller film directed by Paul McGuigan. The movie follows three prisoners - Frank, Jimmy, and Turk - who are brought together to participate in a prison's "Bullet Head" program, where they must work together to solve a murder mystery.

The main theme of Bullet Head revolves around the concept of redemption and second chances. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that each character has their own personal demons and struggles with their past mistakes. Through their interactions and shared experiences, they begin to confront their inner demons and work towards redemption.

One of the primary themes is also the idea of toxic masculinity and how societal expectations can lead men down a path of violence and aggression. The characters' backstories and motivations are deeply rooted in this theme, highlighting the destructive nature of unchecked masculinity and the importance of vulnerability and empathy.

Furthermore, Bullet Head explores the concept of loyalty and trust, as the three prisoners must navigate their complicated relationships with each other to solve the murder mystery. This theme is intertwined with the idea of redemption, as the characters are forced to confront their own flaws and weaknesses in order to find a way out of their troubled pasts.

Overall, Bullet Head is a gripping thriller that delves into complex themes of redemption, toxic masculinity, loyalty, and trust, making for a thought-provoking and intense viewing experience.

documents.title: Christmas Getaway
documents.overview: When a reservation mix-up at a mountain resort forces a newly-single travel writer to share a cabin with a handsome widower and his precocious daughter over the holidays, their lives are transformed by the magic of Christmas and the unexpected power of love.
documents.plot:
Christmas Getaway is a 2017 American Christmas romance television film directed by Mel Damski. The teleplay was written by Tracy Andreen, Elizabeth Snyder and Marlene McPherson, the latter two also credited with the story. Produced for the Hallmark Channel's line of original movies and shot in Vancouver, British Columbia, it was first broadcast in December 2017. It stars Bridget Regan and Travis Van Winkle, with Raven Stewart and Teryl Rothery in supporting roles.

Emory (Regan), a newly single travel writer had planned to spend a quiet Christmas alone at home. At short notice, however, her editor hands her an assignment that seems to suit her perfectly: a piece about Christmas in the mountains. She rents a snowbound cabin at a resort in Pine Grove, only to discover on arrival that a reservation mix-up has double-booked it. The other party is Scott Hays (Van Winkle), a widowed lawyer who has reserved the same cabin for himself, his mother Marilyn (Rothery) and his precocious young daughter Katy (Stewart).

With no other cabin available and feeling she cannot argue against a single father, Emory decides to drive back to San Francisco, but a snowstorm sets in and her car will not start in the cold. Scott relents and lets her stay in the fairly roomy cabin. Katy is fascinated by Emory's travel stories. The girl's Christmas wish list, from cutting down their own tree and baking cookies to ice skating and building a snowman, proves a gift to Emory, who can weave the activities into her story. When Marilyn arrives she takes an instant liking to Emory, hoping that her son will open up again after his wife's death. At first the relationship between Scott and Emory remains coolly matter-of-fact, but it warms the more time they spend together. Still, both hesitate to admit their feelings, and Emory leaves without much of a goodbye. When she changes her mind and tries to turn back, her car breaks down again; Scott learns of it and sets out to find her. The two finally talk things through and confess their love, making it the best Christmas ever for all three.

German critics treated the film as a typical example of its genre. TV Spielfilm called it Hallmark television as one knows it, as sugary and sticky as a marshmallow, while Filmdienst described it as a harmless, likeable holiday romance that barely bothers with complications, consisting mostly of a succession of sweet Christmas impressions and stressing the unifying character of the holiday.

documents.title: Radioactive
documents.overview: The story of Nobel Prize winner Marie Curie and her extraordinary scientific discoveries—through the prism of her marriage to husband Pierre—and the seismic and transformative effects their discovery of radium had on the 20th century.
documents.plot:
Radioactive is a 2019 British biographical drama directed by Marjane Satrapi and starring Rosamund Pike as Marie Curie, with Sam Riley as Pierre Curie, Aneurin Barnard as Paul Langevin, Anya Taylor-Joy as the adult Irène Curie and Simon Russell Beale. Jack Thorne's screenplay adapts Lauren Redniss's 2010 graphic novel Radioactive: Marie & Pierre Curie: A Tale of Love and Fallout.

In 1934 Marie Curie collapses in her Paris laboratory, and as she is taken to hospital her life passes before her. In 1893 her abrasive manner has cost her funding and laboratory space, a trait she shares with the scientist Pierre Curie, and the two end up working side by side. They fall in love, marry and have two daughters, and their research leads to the discovery of polonium and radium and of radioactivity itself, transforming physics and chemistry. Radium quickly finds its way into a wave of commercial products.

Marie, an unbeliever since her mother's death in Poland, scorns the séances Pierre attends. He turns down the Légion d'honneur because it ignores her and insists they share the Nobel Prize in Physics, yet she is hurt when he accepts it in Stockholm without her. Weakened by illness linked to their work, Pierre is killed by a horse-drawn cart. Marie long dismisses fears about radium's dangers even as people exposed to it fall ill.

Grieving, she begins an affair with her colleague Paul Langevin. Although she succeeds Pierre as professor at the Sorbonne, the nationalist press exposes the affair and she is targeted by xenophobic crowds because of her Polish origins. In desperation she asks her friend Loie Fuller to help her reach Pierre's spirit. Awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1911, she ignores the committee's request to stay away and is cheered at the ceremony. During the First World War her daughter Irène persuades her to run mobile X-ray units at the front.

Interwoven with her story are scenes of her discoveries' legacy, from radiotherapy in 1950s Cleveland to Hiroshima, a 1961 nuclear test in Nevada and Chernobyl. Dying, Marie sees these visions and leaves the hospital with Pierre.

The film closed the 2019 Toronto International Film Festival. After its cinema release was cancelled by the COVID-19 pandemic, it reached audiences digitally and on Amazon Prime Video in 2020, earning 63% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, with Pike's performance singled out.

documents.title: Let There Be Light
documents.overview: An atheist goes through a near-death experience in an auto accident before converting to Christianity.
documents.plot:
Let There Be Light is a 2017 American drama film directed by Jeremy Goldberg and written by Jeremy Goldberg and Michael McEvoy. The movie stars Steven Yeun, Samm Levine, and Janina Gavankar.

The main themes of Let There Be Light revolve around mental health, specifically bipolar disorder, and the struggles of living with a stigmatized condition. The film follows the story of John (played by Steven Yeun), a successful businessman who is diagnosed with bipolar disorder after experiencing a severe manic episode.

Throughout the movie, the theme of mental illness is portrayed as a complex and multifaceted issue that affects not only the individual but also their loved ones. The film explores the challenges of managing symptoms, maintaining relationships, and finding treatment options in a society that often stigmatizes mental health issues.

Another significant theme present in Let There Be Light is the importance of community and support. John's journey is marked by his struggles to find acceptance and understanding from those around him, particularly his family and friends. The film highlights the need for empathy, education, and open conversation about mental health to break down stigmas and promote a culture of understanding.

The movie also touches on themes of identity, self-discovery, and personal growth. As John navigates his diagnosis and treatment, he is forced to confront his own strengths, weaknesses, and values, ultimately leading to a deeper understanding of himself and the world around him.

Overall, Let There Be Light offers a nuanced and thought-provoking exploration of mental health, community, and personal growth, shedding light on the complexities of living with bipolar disorder and promoting greater awareness and understanding.

documents.title: The Addams Family
documents.overview: The Addams family's lives begin to unravel when they face-off against a treacherous, greedy crafty reality-TV host while also preparing for their extended family to arrive for a major celebration.
documents.plot:
The Addams Family is a 2019 computer-animated supernatural comedy based on the characters created by cartoonist Charles Addams, directed by Conrad Vernon and Greg Tiernan and written by Matt Lieberman. It features the voices of Oscar Isaac as Gomez, Charlize Theron as Morticia, Chloë Grace Moretz as Wednesday, Finn Wolfhard as Pugsley, Nick Kroll as Uncle Fester, Snoop Dogg as Cousin Itt, Bette Midler as Grandmama and Allison Janney as the reality TV host Margaux Needler.

After an angry mob disrupts their midnight wedding, Gomez and Morticia Addams flee with Thing and settle in New Jersey, a place where, they reason, no one would be caught dead. They make their home in an abandoned asylum on a hill and recruit Lurch, an escaped patient, as their butler. Thirteen years later, the family lives happily in gloomy isolation. Gomez is preparing his son Pugsley for the Sabre Mazurka, a traditional rite of passage in front of the entire Addams clan, while Morticia struggles to keep Wednesday from wanting to explore the world beyond the mansion.

Meanwhile, Margaux Needler, a home makeover television host, is completing a pastel-colored planned community called Assimilation below the hill for her show's season finale. When she discovers the Addamses' creepy mansion, she sets out to force the family to conform or leave, spreading rumors about them online. Wednesday befriends Margaux's neglected daughter, Parker, and persuades her mother to let her attend junior high school, where she stands up to a bully and the two girls swap their styles of dress, Parker turning gothic and Wednesday colorful, to the horror of both mothers. As the relatives arrive for Pugsley's ceremony, Margaux rallies the townspeople against the Addamses, and the family must defend its home and teach the town to accept people who are different.

The film celebrates individuality and acceptance, updating the macabre humor of the original cartoons for a family audience. Its soundtrack includes an updated version of Vic Mizzy's classic theme song.

Released by MGM on October 11, 2019, the film grossed 204 million dollars worldwide. Reviews were mixed, with 46 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 46. A sequel, The Addams Family 2, followed in 2021.

documents.title: All the Devil's Men
documents.overview: A battle-scarred War on Terror bounty hunter is forced to go to London on a manhunt for a disavowed CIA operative, which leads him into a deadly running battle with a former military comrade and his private army.
documents.plot:
All the Devil's Men is a 2018 British action thriller written and directed by Matthew Hope. Milo Gibson stars as Jack Collins, a former Navy SEAL turned bounty hunter, with Sylvia Hoeks as his CIA handler Leigh Allen, William Fichtner as Mike Brennan, Gbenga Akinnagbe as Pete Samuelson, Joseph Millson as Tony Deighton and Elliot Cowan as Terry McKnight, alongside Perry Fitzpatrick and Yavor Baharov.

Collins is a war junkie who makes his living hunting terrorists for a private company, part of the CIA's practice of outsourcing such operations to contractors. He is struggling with personal demons, and his superiors have begun to see him as a liability. Leigh offers him one last chance to keep doing the only work he knows and sends him to London on a new assignment. There he joins a three-man team with the veteran operative Brennan and Samuelson. Their target is McKnight, a disavowed CIA operative who is trying to buy a weapon of mass destruction from Russian gangsters before vanishing for good.

The mission is complicated by McKnight's protection: he has hired Deighton, a former colleague of the team, and his private army. What follows is a running urban battle through London between two groups of professionals who know each other's methods and fight intelligently. As the operation goes on, casualties mount on both sides, loyalties shift, and Collins finds that betrayal can come from within his own camp as easily as from the enemy, with a series of double and triple crosses keeping it unclear who is working for whom.
