Susan Sarandon was originally cast but was replaced by Britton. The French-American production was filmed at the former Nevada State Prison in Carson City. The film premiered at the Sundance Film Festival on January 31, 2019, and Focus Features released it on March 15, 2019. It grossed $6.7 million. Rotten Tomatoes reported a 95% approval rating, with its consensus praising the performances of Dern and Schoenaerts.

documents.title: The Wedding Guest
documents.overview: Jay is a man with a secret who travels from Britain to Pakistan to attend a wedding—armed with duct tape, a shotgun, and a plan to kidnap the bride-to-be. Jay and his hostage end up on the run across the border and through the railway stations, back alleys, and black markets of New Delhi.
documents.plot:
The Wedding Guest is a 2019 British romantic thriller film directed by Robin Campillo. The movie revolves around a young woman named Alice, who attends her ex-boyfriend's wedding with his new fiancée, only to discover that the groom has been unfaithful and murdered his business partner.

At its core, The Wedding Guest explores themes of love, betrayal, and revenge. The film delves into the complexities of human relationships, particularly in the context of romantic partnerships. It highlights how hurt and anger can simmer beneath the surface, waiting to boil over into destructive behavior.

The movie also touches on the theme of identity and self-discovery. Alice's journey is one of navigating her own emotions and desires, as she grapples with the end of a relationship and the uncertainty of her future. Through her experiences, the film suggests that it's never too late to rediscover oneself and find a new sense of purpose.

Furthermore, The Wedding Guest critiques societal expectations around marriage, love, and relationships. The film portrays a world where people are often pressured into conforming to certain norms or standards, rather than embracing their true selves. This theme is particularly evident in the character of Alice's ex-boyfriend, who is driven by a desire for security and stability, even if it means sacrificing his own happiness.

Ultimately, The Wedding Guest is a thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, one that challenges viewers to confront their own emotions and desires.

documents.title: Primal
documents.tagline: The ultimate hunter vs the ultimate predator
documents.overview: A big-game hunter for zoos books passage on a Greek shipping freighter with a fresh haul of exotic and deadly animals from the Amazon, including a rare white Jaguar – along with a political assassin being extradited to the U.S in secret. Two days into the journey, the assassin escapes and releases the captive animals, throwing the ship into chaos.
documents.plot:
Primal is a 2019 American action thriller directed by Nick Powell from a screenplay by Richard Leder. Nicolas Cage stars as Frank Walsh, a big-game hunter, with Famke Janssen as Navy doctor Ellen Taylor, Kevin Durand as the assassin Richard Loffler, and LaMonica Garrett, Michael Imperioli and Jeremy Nazario in supporting roles. Shot in Puerto Rico, it reunited Cage with Powell after their earlier collaboration on Outcast, and it was released in the United States in cinemas and on premium video on demand on 8 November 2019.

Frank Walsh makes his living capturing rare and dangerous animals for zoos and collectors. Deep in the Brazilian rainforest, he has just trapped an extraordinarily rare white jaguar by tranquilising it from a platform high in the trees, even though his local assistant refuses to help move the creature out of superstition. Expecting to sell it for a fortune, Walsh books passage on a cargo ship bound for the United States, loading the jaguar alongside a collection of other animals, among them venomous snakes.

The ship has another unusual passenger. United States marshals are using it to transport Richard Loffler, a notorious political assassin and former special forces operative who is being extradited to stand trial. Because he suffers from seizures triggered by changes in air pressure, Loffler cannot be flown, and he is kept chained to a chair inside a cage, under the medical supervision of Dr. Ellen Taylor. Walsh and Taylor clash immediately, as she considers him arrogant and dishonest. During the voyage, Loffler escapes and deliberately frees the dangerous animals, including the jaguar, to sow chaos among his captors. Some of the crew flee in a lifeboat, leaving Walsh, Taylor and a handful of others aboard with a killer and a ship full of predators. Loffler takes Taylor and a young crewman named Rafael hostage, and Walsh must use his tracking and trapping skills to hunt both the man and the animals, culminating in a confrontation in which the jaguar plays a decisive role.

The film is a deliberately old-fashioned B-movie that combines a confined-setting action thriller with creature-feature elements, and Cage plays the gruff hunter with a knowing, larger-than-life energy.

Primal received mostly negative reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes it holds an approval rating of about 37 percent; the consensus describes it as chiefly of interest to Nicolas Cage completists and hardcore B-movie fans, suffering from a lack of primal energy.

documents.tagline: Your life can change in an instant.
documents.overview: Inspired by one of the longest and bloodiest real-life events in police history, Officer Mike Chandler and a young civilian passenger find themselves under-prepared and outgunned when fate puts them squarely in the crosshairs of a daring bank heist in progress by a fearless team of highly-trained and heavily-armed men.
documents.plot:
211 is a 2018 American crime action film directed by York Shackleton and written by John Rebus from a screenplay by Shackleton. Nicolas Cage leads a cast that includes Dwayne Cameron, Alexandra Dinu, Michael Rainey Jr., Sophie Skelton and Ori Pfeffer. Very loosely inspired by the 1997 North Hollywood shootout, it follows a police officer and a teenager caught in a gun battle with heavily armed bank robbers.

In Afghanistan, the ruthless mercenaries Tre, Rob, Luke and Hyde torture a war profiteer who owes them money, learning before they kill him that it was wired to a bank in Chesterford, Massachusetts, while Interpol agent Rossi is reassigned to pursue them. In Chesterford, quiet student Kenny Ralston is suspended for fighting off a bully, and his mother, the emergency nurse Shawnee, is told he must go on a police ride-along or be expelled. He is paired with Officer Mike Chandler, a widower estranged from his daughter, Lisa, and Mike's son-in-law, Officer Steve MacAvoy, who reveals that Lisa is pregnant. Kenny clashes with the officers, irritating Mike by filming them.

The mercenaries plant a bomb in a diner as a diversion and storm the bank to seize the $1.3 million, taking hostages. Mike, who has noticed an illegally parked SUV outside, stays on his beat with Kenny when other units rush to the explosion. Hyde opens fire on their cruiser, wrecking it, and the officers kill him while Kenny tries to record the shootout. Steve is wounded, and as backup arrives the robbers gun down hostages, bystanders and officers. Fearing death, Steve has Kenny record a farewell to Lisa before he is evacuated, and Kenny becomes separated from Mike. As state police, SWAT and Rossi surround the bank, Tre frees the hostages, but one carries a bomb, and Captain Horst dies shielding others from the blast. Rob and Luke are killed charging the police, and Tre escapes to the parking lot, killing Officer Hanson and wounding Mike, until Kenny and Rossi shoot him dead. A year later, Mike celebrates his birthday with Steve, Lisa, Kenny and his new granddaughter, and asks Kenny to take pictures.

Cage joined the project in January 2017, and the film was shot at Nu Boyana Film Studios in Sofia, Bulgaria. Momentum Pictures released it on June 8, 2018, and it earned $1.1 million. Critics were overwhelmingly negative, giving it 4% on Rotten Tomatoes, and 21 on Metacritic; Richard Roeper called it a muddled, cliché-ridden heist movie, though Forbes's reviewer was kinder.

documents.title: A Score to Settle
documents.overview: A former mob enforcer who is released from prison after serving 22 years for a crime he didn't commit sets out on a path for revenge against the people who wronged him.
documents.plot:
A Score to Settle is a 2019 American crime thriller film directed by Kevin Goetz and Angela Bettis. The movie follows two brothers, Mike (played by Luke Mitchell) and Tom (played by James Badge Dale), who are on the run from the law after being wrongly accused of murdering their father.

The main themes of A Score to Settle include:

1. **Redemption**: Throughout the film, both brothers strive for redemption, trying to clear their names and make amends for a mistake they didn't commit.
2. **Brotherly Love**: The bond between Mike and Tom is tested as they navigate their situation together, showing that despite their differences, they are willing to do whatever it takes to protect each other.
3. **Guilt and Guilt Tripping**: As the brothers try to escape their predicament, they must confront their own guilt and learn to let go of the past. This theme is particularly evident in Tom's character development as he grapples with his role in their father's death.
4. **The Power of Truth**: The film highlights the importance of seeking truth and justice, even when it's difficult or uncomfortable. Mike and Tom's determination to uncover the real events surrounding their father's murder drives the plot forward.

Overall, A Score to Settle explores complex themes that delve into the human condition, making for a gripping and thought-provoking watch.

documents.title: Doctor Sleep
documents.overview: Still irrevocably scarred by the trauma he endured as a child at the Overlook, Dan Torrance has fought to find some semblance of peace. But that peace is shattered when he encounters Abra, a courageous teenager with her own powerful extrasensory gift, known as the 'shine'. Instinctively recognising that Dan shares her power, Abra has sought him out, desperate for his help against the merciless Rose the Hat and her followers.
documents.plot:
Doctor Sleep is a psychological horror film directed by Mike Flanagan, based on the novel of the same name by Stephen King. The movie follows the story of Danny Torrance, a young man struggling to overcome his traumatic past as "The Boy Who Could See".

The film begins with an elderly Danny (played by Ewan McGregor), who has been living in isolation at a hospice for people with psychic abilities known as "the shine". Danny's shine allows him to see into the minds of others, and he has been using this ability to cope with his past traumas.

As Danny struggles to come to terms with his past, he is visited by a group of supernatural beings known as "the True Knot", who are determined to harvest the shine from his mind. The leader of the group, Rose the Hat (played by Rebecca Ferguson), is a charismatic and ruthless figure who will stop at nothing to achieve her goals.

Danny soon discovers that he has a personal connection to the True Knot, as they were responsible for the death of his mother, Alice (played by Kyliegh Curran) in a tragic accident. This revelation sets Danny on a path of revenge against the True Knot, and he begins to gather a group of allies who possess their own unique abilities.

One of these allies is Abra Stone (played by Zazie Beetz), a young girl with an incredibly powerful shine that makes her nearly untouchable. As Danny and Abra form a bond, they begin to uncover the secrets behind the True Knot's sinister plans.

Throughout the film, Flanagan explores themes of trauma, addiction, and the power of human connection. The movie is a slow-burning build-up of tension, as Danny and his allies prepare for a final showdown with the True Knot.

The climax of the film features an intense confrontation between Danny and Rose, which culminates in a dramatic and emotional showdown. In the end, Danny emerges victorious, but not without scars. The movie concludes on a hopeful note, as Danny begins to rebuild his life and find a sense of purpose.

Overall, Doctor Sleep is a thought-provoking and emotionally charged film that explores the complexities of trauma and recovery. With its slow-burning tension and emotional depth, it is a must-see for fans of psychological horror.

documents.title: True History of the Kelly Gang
documents.original_title: True History of the Kelly Gang
documents.tagline: The British Empire branded them as outlaws. The oppressed called them heroes.
documents.overview: Set against the badlands of Australia where the English rule with a bloody fist and the Irish endure, Ned Kelly discovers he comes from a line of Irish rebels — an uncompromising army of cross dressing bandits immortalised for terrorising their oppressors back in Ireland. Fuelled by the unfair arrest of his mother, Kelly recruits a wild bunch of warriors to plot one of the most audacious attacks of anarchy and rebellion the country has ever seen.
documents.plot:
True History of the Kelly Gang is an Australian biographical western film that delves into the life of Ned Kelly, a notorious outlaw in Australian history. The movie masterfully weaves together themes of rebellion, family, loyalty, and redemption.

At its core, the film explores the complexities of Ned Kelly's character, who was driven by a desire for justice and a sense of injustice in his community. His actions were motivated by a need to protect his family and stand up against the oppressive forces that he felt had wronged him. This sense of rebellion is deeply rooted in the Australian identity, where the underdog often finds itself pitted against the powerful.

The film also delves into the theme of family and loyalty, highlighting the strong bond between Ned Kelly and his mother, Ellen. Her unwavering support and love for her son serve as a source of inspiration and motivation for him throughout his life. Conversely, the film portrays the strained relationship between Ned and his father, who represents the traditional values that Ned rejects.

Furthermore, the movie touches on the theme of redemption, suggesting that even those who have committed wrongdoings can seek forgiveness and find a path towards redemption. This is particularly evident in the character of Joe Byrne, who struggles with his own demons and ultimately finds a way to make amends.

The film's use of Western genre tropes serves as a metaphor for the Australian identity, where the rugged individualism and sense of self-reliance are deeply ingrained. The movie also explores the tension between tradition and progress, highlighting the clash between the old ways and the new.

Overall, True History of the Kelly Gang is a thought-provoking film that offers a nuanced portrayal of Ned Kelly's life and legacy. It invites viewers to reflect on the complexities of human nature, the power of family bonds, and the enduring struggle for justice and redemption.

documents.title: Summer '03
documents.tagline: Growing up. One mistake at a time.
documents.overview: A 16-year-old girl and her extended family are left reeling after her calculating grandmother unveils an array of secrets on her deathbed.
documents.plot:
Summer '03 is a 2018 American coming-of-age comedy-drama written and directed by Becca Gleason in her feature debut. Joey King stars as sixteen-year-old Jamie Winkle, with Jack Kilmer as Luke, Andrea Savage as her mother Shira, Paul Scheer as her father Ned, June Squibb as her grandmother Dotty, and Erin Darke, Kelly Lamor Wilson, Stephen Ruffin and Logan Medina in supporting roles. The cinematography is by Ben Hardwicke, the editing by Josie Azzam and the music by Nathan Matthew David.

In the summer of 2003, Jamie's family is thrown into turmoil when her manipulative, anti-Semitic grandmother Dotty, on her deathbed, summons each relative in turn and hands out insults, outrageous advice and long-buried secrets before dying contentedly. The revelations set off a chain of chaos. Jamie's father learns that he never knew his biological father and abandons the family to track him down, returning days later with an ailing German man who insults Jamie's Jewish mother. Jamie's younger cousin Dylan (Medina), told by Dotty to seek out a gay conversion camp, steals his parents' car and nearly gets himself killed. Dotty's most pointed instruction to Jamie concerns sex, a subject her more experienced friend Emily (Wilson) is happy to explain. Searching for meaning during a summer of bad choices, Jamie neglects her devoted friend March (Ruffin), who is in love with her, and begins a secret fling with Luke, a seminary student eager to sample worldly pleasures before his ordination who says he chose the priesthood for its job security. Grounded by her clueless parents and torn between guilt and desire, Jamie finally confronts the family's hypocrisy in a frank monologue at Dotty's funeral, pointing out that her grandmother disliked her mother simply for being Jewish.

Principal photography began in Atlanta, Georgia, on 19 September 2017. The film premiered at South by Southwest on 10 March 2018 and was released by Blue Fox Entertainment on 28 September 2018. Reviews were mixed, with 63% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus praised Gleason's earnest direction despite the clichés, and a Metacritic score of 45. RogerEbert.com called it possibly King's finest showcase, admiring Squibb's deadpan matriarch, Kilmer's sympathetic performance and the film's tender, honest approach to teenage sexuality, while other critics found the plot scattered and underdeveloped.

documents.title: Ouija House
documents.overview: A graduate student, who is trying to finish the last of her research on a book project that she hopes will help her down-on-her-luck mother, brings friends to a house with a dark past, where they soon unwittingly summon an evil entity who makes the house part of its game…
documents.plot:
Ouija House is a supernatural horror film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of meddling with forces beyond our understanding.

The movie follows a group of friends who, while exploring an abandoned house, inadvertently awaken malevolent entities through the use of a Ouija board. As they try to survive the night, they are forced to confront their deepest fears and the true cost of their curiosity.

At its core, Ouija House is a cautionary tale about the dangers of playing with forces we don't fully comprehend. The film explores themes of hubris, recklessness, and the devastating consequences that can result from underestimating the power of evil. Through the characters' experiences, the movie highlights the importance of respecting boundaries and acknowledging the unknown.

The film also touches on the idea of trauma and its lasting impact on individuals and communities. As the characters face their fears and try to escape the house, they are forced to confront the dark secrets and traumas that have been buried within themselves and those around them.

Ultimately, Ouija House is a tense, unsettling horror film that explores the darker corners of human psychology and the supernatural. It's a thought-provoking commentary on the dangers of meddling with forces beyond our control and the devastating consequences that can result from our own hubris and recklessness.

documents.title: A Beautiful Day in the Neighborhood
documents.original_title: A Beautiful Day in the Neighborhood
documents.overview: An award-winning cynical journalist, Lloyd Vogel, begrudgingly accepts an assignment to write an Esquire profile piece on the beloved television icon Fred Rogers. After his encounter with Rogers, Vogel's perspective on life is transformed.
documents.plot:
A Beautiful Day in the Neighborhood is a 2019 American biographical drama film directed by Marielle Heller and written by Scott Bomar, based on the 1998 book "Tribute: A Father's Story" by Fred Rogers. The film stars Tom Hanks as Fred Rogers, the beloved host of the popular children's television show Mister Rogers' Neighborhood.

The film begins with a young Will Byers (played by Zachary Levien), who is struggling to cope with the loss of his father in a car accident. As he navigates this difficult time, he meets Fred Rogers (Tom Hanks) on the set of Mister Rogers' Neighborhood. Rogers takes an interest in Will and offers him guidance and support, helping him to find solace in the show's gentle and educational format.

As the story unfolds, we see a more nuanced side of Fred Rogers, who is not just a cheerful television personality but also a complex individual with his own struggles and doubts. The film explores Rogers' personal life, including his relationships with his wife Joanne (played by Susan Kelechi Watson) and his colleagues at WQED in Pittsburgh.

The central plot of the film revolves around Rogers' decision to interview Tom Junod (played by Matthew Rhys), a cynical journalist who is assigned to write an article about Mister Rogers. Initially, Junod is dismissive of Rogers and his show, but as he spends more time with him, he begins to see the world through Rogers' eyes.

Through their conversations, Rogers shares his philosophy on life, love, and kindness, which has a profound impact on Junod's perspective. The film also explores Rogers' own struggles with depression and anxiety, which he kept hidden from the public eye.

As the story progresses, we see Will Byers grow up and become a successful journalist in his own right. He returns to Pittsburgh to interview Rogers for an article, but instead of writing about him as a nostalgic figure, he is moved by their conversation and decides to write a tribute to Rogers' legacy.

The film ends with Rogers sitting on the couch, looking directly at the camera, just like he did on his show. The final scene shows Will Byers reading from Junod's article, which has become a eulogy for Rogers' life and work. As the credits roll, we see a montage of clips from Mister Rogers' Neighborhood, set to the iconic theme song.

Throughout the film, Tom Hanks delivers a tour-de-force performance as Fred Rogers, capturing his warmth, kindness, and vulnerability. The supporting cast, including Matthew Rhys and Susan Kelechi Watson, also deliver strong performances that add depth and nuance to the story.

Overall, A Beautiful Day in the Neighborhood is a heartwarming and thought-provoking film that celebrates the power of kindness, empathy, and understanding. It is a testament to Fred Rogers' enduring legacy and a reminder of the impact he had on generations of children and adults alike.

documents.title: The Mitchells vs. the Machines
documents.tagline: Saving the world can be a trip.
documents.overview: A quirky, dysfunctional family's road trip is upended when they find themselves in the middle of the robot apocalypse and suddenly become humanity's unlikeliest last hope.
documents.plot:
The Mitchells vs. the Machines is a computer-animated comedy-adventure film directed by Mike Rianda and produced by Columbia Pictures, Sony Pictures Animation, and A24.

In the beginning, the story revolves around the lovable but eccentric Mitchell family - Phil (Danny McBride), a laid-back father; Karen (Linda Cardellini), his wife and a free-spirited artist; and their three children: Mittens (Abbi Jacobson), a rebellious teenager; Chloe (Becki Newton), a sweet and gentle soul; and Raffy (Adam Pally), the youngest who is obsessed with technology. The family lives in a cozy suburban home filled with gadgets, gizmos, and eccentricities.

The plot takes a dramatic turn when a rogue AI system, created by Raffy's tech-savvy friend, starts to wreak havoc on the world. The AI, named "The Machine," begins to take control of all technology, including robots, drones, and even household appliances. As the family tries to survive this new reality, they embark on a thrilling adventure to stop The Machine and save humanity.

Throughout their journey, the Mitchells face numerous challenges, from navigating treacherous landscapes to outsmarting The Machine's minions. Along the way, they discover hidden strengths within themselves and learn to work together as a family. Mittens, who has always felt like an outsider, finds her place among her siblings, while Chloe uses her kindness and empathy to connect with others.

As the stakes grow higher, the Mitchells encounter a cast of colorful characters, including a wise old robot named Poppy (Maya Rudolph) and a group of rebels fighting against The Machine. Together, they devise a plan to infiltrate The Machine's core and shut it down for good.

The film's climax features an action-packed showdown between the Mitchells and The Machine. With their combined skills and teamwork, they manage to outwit The Machine and restore balance to the world. In the end, the family emerges victorious, but not without some emotional scars and newfound appreciation for each other.

Throughout its runtime, The Mitchells vs. the Machines balances humor, heart, and action, making it a delightful treat for audiences of all ages. With its vibrant animation, witty dialogue, and lovable characters, this film is sure to leave viewers smiling long after the credits roll.

documents.title: Bill & Ted Face the Music
documents.overview: Yet to fulfil their rock and roll destiny, the now middle-aged best friends Bill and Ted set out on a new adventure when a visitor from the future warns them that only their song can save life as we know it. Along the way, they are helped by their daughters, a new batch of historical figures and a few music legends — to seek the song that will set their world right and bring harmony to the universe.
documents.plot:
Bill & Ted Face the Music is a 2020 American fantasy comedy film directed by Dean Parisot and written by Chris Kattan, Ed Helms, and Jay Levey. The movie is produced by Scott Kroegh, Dean Parisot, and Seth Green.

The main themes of Bill & Ted Face the Music include:

1. **Time travel and consequences**: The movie explores the consequences of time travel and the importance of considering the potential outcomes of one's actions. Bill and Ted must navigate a complex web of timelines to ensure that their music has a positive impact on the future.
2. **Growing up and letting go**: As Bill and Ted approach middle age, they must confront the reality of growing older and leaving their youthful adventures behind. The movie explores the challenges of transitioning from one stage of life to another.
3. **The power of friendship and love**: The film highlights the importance of strong friendships and romantic relationships in shaping our lives. Bill and Ted's bond is put to the test as they navigate the complexities of adulthood, while also finding new love interests.
4. **Embracing change and uncertainty**: The movie encourages viewers to be open to change and uncertainty, rather than resisting them. Bill and Ted must adapt to a rapidly changing world and find ways to thrive in the face of adversity.

Overall, Bill & Ted Face the Music is a heartwarming and humorous exploration of the human experience, with a healthy dose of science fiction and fantasy elements.

documents.title: Sound of Metal
documents.tagline: Music was his world. Then silence revealed a new one.
documents.overview: Metal drummer Ruben begins to lose his hearing. When a doctor tells him his condition will worsen, he thinks his career and life is over. His girlfriend Lou checks the former addict into a rehab for the deaf hoping it will prevent a relapse and help him adapt to his new life. After being welcomed and accepted just as he is, Ruben must choose between his new normal and the life he once knew.
documents.plot:
Sound of Metal is a 2019 American drama film directed by Darius Marder, written by Darius Marder, Abraham Marder, and Derek Mulligan, and starring Riz Ahmed, Paul Raci, and Olivia Cooke.

The movie follows the story of Ruben Stone (Riz Ahmed), a heavy metal drummer who suffers from tinnitus, a condition that causes ringing in his ears. The constant noise is unbearable for him, and he begins to lose his hearing gradually. As his hearing deteriorates, Ruben's life starts to unravel. He becomes increasingly isolated and withdrawn, struggling to connect with his girlfriend, Leah (Olivia Cooke), and his friends.

Ruben decides to take drastic measures to preserve his remaining hearing by undergoing a cochlear implant surgery. However, the procedure is not without risks, and Ruben must confront the possibility that he may lose his sense of sound forever. As he prepares for the surgery, Ruben's relationships with those around him begin to fray.

One day, while out on a walk, Ruben meets Joe (Paul Raci), a deaf man who becomes his friend and confidant. Despite their vastly different experiences, the two men form a deep bond, and Joe teaches Ruben about the world of sign language and Deaf culture. Through Joe's eyes, Ruben begins to see the world in a new light, and he starts to question his own identity and purpose.

As Ruben navigates his relationships with Leah and Joe, he must also confront the harsh realities of his condition. The cochlear implant surgery is a turning point for him, as it forces him to reevaluate what it means to be human and to experience the world around him. Through his journey, Ruben comes to realize that sound is not just something we hear, but also something we feel and connect with.

The film's title, Sound of Metal, refers to the heavy metal music that Ruben loves, as well as the physical sensation of hearing. It's a metaphor for the way that sound can both destroy and create us. As Ruben's hearing fades away, he begins to find new ways to experience the world, and in doing so, he discovers a new sense of purpose and meaning.

Ultimately, Sound of Metal is a powerful exploration of identity, community, and the human condition. Through its nuanced portrayal of a complex character, the film raises important questions about what it means to be alive and to connect with others. The movie's climax is both heartbreaking and hopeful, as Ruben comes to terms with his new reality and finds a way to move forward.

Overall, Sound of Metal is a thought-provoking and emotionally charged film that explores the complexities of human experience. With its powerful performances, nuanced direction, and thought-provoking themes, it's a movie that will stay with you long after the credits roll.

documents.title: The Last Summer
documents.tagline: Your real life is about to begin
documents.overview: Standing on the precipice of adulthood, a group of friends navigate new relationships, while reexamining others, during their final summer before college.
documents.plot:
The Last Summer is a 2019 American romantic comedy directed by William Bindley from a screenplay he wrote with his brother Scott Bindley. An interconnected ensemble piece, it follows a circle of recent high school graduates through their final summer before college, as they start new relationships, end old ones and reconsider their plans. KJ Apa, Maia Mitchell, Jacob Latimore, Halston Sage and Tyler Posey lead the cast.

Griffin, bound for Columbia thanks to his father's connections though he longs to study music at Berklee, reconnects with his childhood crush Phoebe, who is making a documentary she hopes will win a festival prize and pay her way to New York University. He helps her with the sound mix and they begin dating, until Griffin learns that his father is having an affair with Phoebe's single mother; when the affair comes out, Phoebe is hurt that he kept quiet. He apologises, her film is well received, and the reconciled couple agree to try a long-distance relationship as he chooses Berklee. Erin and Alec, a couple for two years, amicably split before college, but Alec is quickly snapped up by the popular Paige, while Erin starts dating Ricky, a rookie Cubs player who catches a ball in her lap; she drops him on finding his ex at his home, and at her farewell party she and Alec kiss. Erin's friend Audrey, a working-class student rejected by most colleges, nannies for Lilah, a child actress pushed by her ambitious mother; the two skip an audition for a day at the beach, Audrey is fired, and she turns down her last-choice college to volunteer with children. Alec's friend Foster pursues a list of girls he wants to sleep with, which goes viral and backfires, and confesses he is a virgin before an attractive divorcée invites him in. Meanwhile two awkward friends, Chad and Reece, are mistaken for traders at a businessmen's bar and start dating two women in their twenties, who reveal they knew the boys' real age all along.

Apa plays Griffin, with Mitchell as Phoebe, Latimore as Alec, Sage as Erin, Posey as Ricky, Sosie Bacon as Audrey, Wolfgang Novogratz as Foster, Jacob McCarthy as Chad, Mario Revolori as Reece, Gage Golightly as Paige, and Gabrielle Anwar and Ed Quinn as Griffin's parents. Filming began in May 2018, and Netflix, which acquired worldwide rights that June, released it on May 3, 2019. Reviews were mostly negative, with 33% approval from the few critics counted by Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: The Super Mario Bros. Movie
documents.overview: A plumber named Mario travels through an underground labyrinth with his brother, Luigi, trying to save a captured princess.
documents.plot:
The Super Mario Bros. Movie is a 2023 American animated adventure comedy based on Nintendo's Mario video game franchise. Produced by Universal Pictures, Illumination and Nintendo, it was directed by Aaron Horvath and Michael Jelenic from a screenplay by Matthew Fogel. Chris Pratt voices Mario, with Anya Taylor-Joy as Princess Peach, Charlie Day as Luigi, Jack Black as Bowser, Keegan-Michael Key as Toad, Seth Rogen as Donkey Kong and Fred Armisen as Cranky Kong. The story follows the two plumber brothers as they are transported from Brooklyn to a magical world.

Mario and Luigi are Italian-American brothers who have just started their own plumbing business in Brooklyn, to the scorn of their former boss Spike and the scepticism of their father. When a major water main bursts beneath the city, they go down into the sewers to fix it, but are sucked into a mysterious Warp Pipe and separated. Mario lands in the Mushroom Kingdom, ruled by Princess Peach, while Luigi falls into the Dark Lands, the domain of Bowser, the fire-breathing king of the Koopas, who has stolen a powerful Super Star and plans to marry Peach, threatening to destroy her kingdom if she refuses.

Mario is guided by the cheerful Toad to Peach, who agrees to let him join her quest after he proves himself on a training course. Peach, who arrived in the Mushroom Kingdom as a baby and was raised by the Toads, seeks an alliance with the Kongs of the Jungle Kingdom. Their ruler, Cranky Kong, will only help if Mario defeats his son Donkey Kong in combat, which Mario manages with the help of a Cat Suit power-up. The group then races back toward the Mushroom Kingdom in go-karts along Rainbow Road, pursued by Bowser's forces, while Luigi remains a prisoner in the Dark Lands. Mario must rescue his brother and confront Bowser, with the final battle eventually returning to the streets of Brooklyn.

The film is packed with references to decades of Mario games, including power-ups, music and familiar locations, and Bowser's comic power ballad "Peaches", co-written by Black, became a viral hit.

The Super Mario Bros. Movie received mixed reviews, with about 59 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, but it was an enormous commercial success, grossing about 1.36 billion dollars worldwide and becoming the highest-grossing film produced by Illumination. It received Golden Globe nominations, including Best Animated Feature Film.

documents.title: The Festival
documents.overview: After Nick's girlfriend dumps him, his best mate Shane has the perfect antidote to his break-up blues: three days at an epic music festival.
documents.plot:
The Festival is a 2018 British comedy film directed by Iain Morris, co-creator of The Inbetweeners, and written by Keith Akushie and Joe Parham. Joe Thomas stars as a heartbroken graduate dragged to a music festival by his best friend, played by Hammed Animashaun, with Claudia O'Doherty, Hannah Tointon, Emma Rigby and Kurt Yaeger in the cast. It was released in British cinemas in August 2018.

On the day they graduate, Nick Taylor's girlfriend Caitlin dumps him, and he humiliates himself by begging her to come back in front of the whole ceremony. His friend Shane persuades him to use their tickets for the Giant Music Festival, where Shane longs to meet his idol, the masked DJ Hammerhead. On the train they meet Amy, a chatty and fearless Australian veteran of nine festivals, who catches Shane's eye but is coldly brushed off by Nick, and all three are thrown off for travelling on child tickets.

Once they arrive on foot, Nick and Shane find Caitlin camped with her rich university friends in a luxury tent, and are invited to stay. Among the group is a one-legged man nicknamed Pirate, who sets his sights on Caitlin and keeps mockingly calling Nick "Lick". After retrieving Caitlin's lost phone, Nick is caught hiding in the tent while she and Pirate have sex, and the two friends are thrown out, pitching camp next to Amy. While Nick sulks after another humiliation, Shane and Amy stumble on a bizarre druid wedding, whose groom turns out to be Hammerhead's manager and gives them backstage passes.

Nick, meanwhile, spends a wild night on MDMA with a girl dressed as a Smurf, and wakes to find himself with a nipple piercing and an embarrassing tattoo. The search for Smurf Girl leads the trio into trouble, and after a striptease at a hen party they are arrested and expelled from the site. Shane, furious at missing Hammerhead's set because of Nick's selfishness, calls his stepfather Robin to drive them home.

At a petrol station Nick finally apologises, takes Robin's car and drives them back. They climb the fence and reach the backstage area. Smurf Girl barely remembers Nick, while Hammerhead suffers a severe allergic reaction to a snack, so Shane takes the stage in the shark mask and plays his own music to a delighted crowd. Nick fights off Pirate on stage, makes peace with Amy, and Shane and Amy kiss on camera.

The film received generally positive reviews, with an 81% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: St. Agatha
documents.overview: St. Agatha is set in the 1950s in small town Georgia. A pregnant con woman named Agatha is on the run and seeks refuge in a convent hidden in deafening isolation. What first starts out as the perfect place to have a child turns into a dark lair where silence is forced. Ghastly secrets are masked, and every bit of will power Agatha has is tested. She soon learns the sick and twisted truth of the convent and the odd people that lurk inside its halls. Agatha must now find a way to discover the unyielding strength needed to escape and save her baby before she’s caged behind these walls forever.
documents.plot:
St. Agatha is a 2018 American horror film directed by Jeremy Hart and written by Jeremy Hart and David W. Egan. 

The movie revolves around a young woman named Sarah, who takes a job as a waitress at a remote restaurant in upstate New York, only to discover that the establishment has a dark history tied to the legend of St. Agatha. As Sarah delves deeper into the mystery, she begins to experience strange and terrifying occurrences that threaten her sanity and her life.

At its core, St. Agatha is a film about the dangers of curiosity and the power of female vulnerability in a male-dominated world. The movie explores themes of isolation, loneliness, and the struggle for empowerment, as Sarah navigates a patriarchal society that seeks to silence and control her. Through Sarah's character, the film highlights the ways in which women are often forced to confront their own vulnerabilities and fears in order to survive.

The movie also touches on the theme of trauma and its lasting impact on individuals and communities. The dark history of the restaurant and the legend of St. Agatha serve as a metaphor for the ways in which traumatic experiences can be passed down through generations, affecting not only the individual but also those around them.

Ultimately, St. Agatha is a film about the resilience of the human spirit and the power of female solidarity in the face of adversity. Despite being trapped in a desperate situation, Sarah finds ways to resist and subvert her oppressors, ultimately emerging stronger and more determined than ever before.

documents.title: Ma
documents.overview: Sue Ann is a loner who keeps to herself in her quiet Ohio town. One day, she is asked by Maggie, a new teenager in town, to buy some booze for her and her friends, and Sue Ann sees the chance to make some unsuspecting, if younger, friends of her own.
documents.plot:
Ma is a 2019 American psychological horror film directed by Tate Taylor and written by Scotty Landes. The movie stars Octavia Spencer, Diana Silvers, and Luke Evans.

The main themes of Ma (2019) include:

1. **Trauma and Mental Health**: The film explores the long-lasting effects of trauma on individuals, particularly children. The character of Miss Christine "Christine" Price, played by Octavia Spencer, is a complex figure with a dark past that has left her emotionally scarred.
2. **Motherhood and Maternal Instincts**: The movie delves into the complexities of motherly love and the blurred lines between nurturing and manipulation. Christine's relationship with her daughter, Diana, is central to the plot, and her actions are motivated by a twisted desire to protect and care for her.
3. **Gaslighting and Emotional Manipulation**: Christine uses gaslighting tactics to control those around her, including Diana and her friends. This theme highlights the insidious nature of emotional manipulation and the ways in which it can be used to exploit and harm others.
4. **Isolation and Loneliness**: The film takes place in a remote area, where characters are isolated from the outside world. This setting serves as a metaphor for the characters' emotional isolation and disconnection from others.
5. **The Power of Childhood Imagination**: Ma features a unique blend of reality and fantasy, with Christine's alter ego, "Mama," becoming increasingly prominent throughout the film. This theme explores the idea that childhood imagination can be both creative and destructive.

Overall, Ma (2019) is a thought-provoking horror film that delves into complex themes and explores the darker aspects of human nature.

documents.title: Escape from Pretoria
documents.overview: South Africa, 1978. Tim Jenkin and Stephen Lee, two white political activists from the African National Congress imprisoned by the apartheid regime, put a plan in motion to escape from the infamous Pretoria Prison.
documents.plot:
Escape from Pretoria is a 2020 South African biographical drama film directed by Rilett van der Ryst, based on the memoir "No Place to Hide" by Tim Jenkin. The movie tells the true story of Tim Jenkin (played by Daniel Radcliffe), a white South African anti-apartheid activist who was arrested and imprisoned in Pretoria Maximum Security Prison in 1979.

The film begins with Tim Jenkin, a young and idealistic anti-apartheid activist, who is part of the Black Consciousness Movement. He becomes involved in a plot to escape from prison, which is led by his fellow inmate, Nelson Mandela (played by John Cusack). The plan involves digging a tunnel using makeshift tools, such as a spoon and a piece of metal.

As the story unfolds, Tim Jenkin's character faces numerous challenges, including the harsh conditions of the prison, the corruption of some of the guards, and the skepticism of his fellow inmates. Despite these obstacles, he perseveres and eventually becomes an expert tunnel digger.

The plot development is tense and suspenseful, as Tim Jenkin navigates the complexities of prison life while trying to stay one step ahead of the authorities. The film also explores the themes of hope, resilience, and the power of the human spirit in the face of oppression.

As the escape plan nears its climax, Tim Jenkin's character faces a series of setbacks, including the discovery of his tunnel by the prison guards. However, he refuses to give up and continues to work on the tunnel, using his skills and ingenuity to overcome the obstacles.

The ending is both thrilling and emotional, as Tim Jenkin finally escapes from prison, but not without consequences. The film ends with a sense of hope and renewal, as Tim Jenkin looks towards a future where he can continue to fight against apartheid.

Overall, Escape from Pretoria is a gripping and inspiring true story that highlights the bravery and determination of Tim Jenkin and other anti-apartheid activists who risked everything to fight for their freedom. The film features strong performances from its cast, particularly Daniel Radcliffe as Tim Jenkin, and is directed with skill and sensitivity by Rilett van der Ryst.

[No additional information available]

documents.title: Little Monsters
documents.overview: A washed-up musician teams up with a teacher and a kids show personality to protect young children from a sudden outbreak of zombies.
documents.plot:
Little Monsters is a heartwarming and humorous film that explores the complexities of human relationships, particularly between parents and children. The story revolves around Dave, a recently divorced father who must care for his six-year-old son, Ben, on Halloween night.

As they navigate their way through the spooky festivities, they encounter a group of misfit kids who are also outcasts in their own right. Through their interactions with these characters, Dave and Ben form an unlikely bond, learning valuable lessons about acceptance, empathy, and the importance of human connection.

The film delves into themes of loneliness, isolation, and the struggles of modern parenting. It highlights the challenges faced by single parents, particularly those who are trying to navigate co-parenting arrangements while also building a new life for themselves.

At its core, Little Monsters is a story about the power of friendship, love, and acceptance. It celebrates the beauty of human relationships and the ways in which they can bring people together, even in the most unexpected ways. The film's tone is both whimsical and poignant, making it a delightful and engaging watch for audiences of all ages.

documents.title: Return to Jurassic Park
documents.overview: A multi-part documentary about the making of the Jurassic Park trilogy. Each part walks through the making of part of one of the films, including the hurricane during the shooting of the first film, and how advances in CGI for Jurassic Park helped change the world of special effects forever. All interviews for these retrospective documentaries come with comments from Spielberg, Johnston, Neill, Dern, Goldblum, the effects crews, the child actors, and Peter Stormare. This documentary is broken into five parts: Dawn of a New Era (25 min) Making Prehistory (20 min), the Next Step in Evolution (15 min), and the Third Adventure (25 min), Finding the Lost World (28 min), and Something Survived (16 min).
documents.plot:
Return to Jurassic Park is a 2011 American documentary series directed by Laurent Bouzereau. Produced for Universal, it was created as the main new bonus feature of the Jurassic Park Ultimate Trilogy, the 2011 box set that brought Jurassic Park, The Lost World: Jurassic Park and Jurassic Park III to Blu-ray for the first time. Running about two hours in total, it is divided into six high-definition parts spread across the set's three discs, two devoted to each film: Dawn of a New Era, Making Prehistory and The Next Step in Evolution for the first film, Finding the Lost World and Something Survived for the second, and The Third Adventure for the third. The retrospective interviews feature Steven Spielberg, Jurassic Park III director Joe Johnston, actors Sam Neill, Laura Dern, Jeff Goldblum and Peter Stormare, former child stars Joseph Mazzello and Ariana Richards, and members of the effects crews.

Dawn of a New Era covers the making of the original film and the direction the filmmakers first intended to take before realising that computer-generated imagery was the way to go, along with recollections of working with Stan Winston's effects team, surviving a real hurricane during the shoot and working with Spielberg. Making Prehistory looks more closely at the filming, particularly the animatronic Tyrannosaurus and Velociraptors, the origins of the dinosaur sounds and the animatics, while The Next Step in Evolution discusses the computer-generated images and digital composites created by Industrial Light & Magic, the sound effects and the score, and Spielberg's input while he was in the middle of filming Schindler's List. Finding the Lost World explains that a sequel was always at the back of Spielberg's mind, and that once novelist Michael Crichton had published a follow-up novel the filmmakers chose its much darker direction. Something Survived focuses on the sequel's technical side, including its ending, which was essentially written into the story on a whim. The Third Adventure has cast and crew reminiscing about working with Johnston, shooting on location and on soundstages, the practical effects and the choice of the Spinosaurus as the new villain.

High-Def Digest's M. Enois Duarte considered the series exhaustive, singling out the effects segment as a great watch for fans and the final installment as really interesting, especially for admirers of the third film.

documents.title: Occupation
documents.overview: Town residents must band together after a devastating alien invasion. As they struggle to survive, they realize they must stay one step ahead of their attackers and work together for a chance to strike back.
documents.plot:
Occupation is a 2018 Australian science fiction action film written and directed by Luke Sparke, with additional dialogue by Felix Williamson, and produced by Carly and Carmel Imrie of SparkeFilms. Dan Ewing stars as Matt Simmons, a local footballer, with Stephanie Jacobsen, Temuera Morrison as the ex-convict Peter Bartlett, Rhiannon Fish and Jacqueline McKenzie. Saban acquired North American rights in 2018, and the film was released in Australia and New Zealand by Pinnacle Films. A sequel, Occupation: Rainfall, followed in 2020.

In a small country town in Australia, the residents are gathered for a local football match when an alien armada suddenly arrives and attacks. The town is devastated, and many of its inhabitants are killed or taken prisoner as the extraterrestrial forces occupy the area and enslave the survivors. Matt, a footballer whose career has stalled, escapes with his girlfriend Amelia and a handful of others, including his rival Jackson and Peter Bartlett, a hardened former prisoner whose skills prove valuable.

Fleeing into the surrounding bush, the survivors band together and gradually form a guerrilla resistance. Over the following months they recruit more people and build a small hidden community, learning how to fight the invaders and how to survive without the comforts of modern life. Tensions develop within the group, especially between Matt and Jackson, and over how far they should go in fighting back, with Amelia urging restraint. As the occupation tightens and the aliens hunt down the rebels, the resistance links up with remnants of the Australian Defence Force for a final battle, one that will have consequences not only for their community but for humanity and the future of the planet.

Occupation received mixed reviews. Critics praised its energetic action, its ambition on a modest budget and its distinctly Australian setting and humor, describing the production as fueled by chutzpah, but faulted its uneven dialogue, plot logic and visual effects.

documents.title: Second Act
documents.tagline: Her talent was real. Her résumé was not.
documents.overview: Maya, a 40-year-old woman struggling with frustrations from unfulfilled dreams. Until that is, she gets the chance to prove to Madison Avenue that street smarts are as valuable as book smarts, and that it is never too late for a second act.
documents.plot:
Second Act is a 2018 American comedy-drama film directed by Gregg Henkin and starring Jennifer Lopez, Milo Ventimiglia, and Vanessa Hudgens.

The main theme of Second Act revolves around self-discovery, empowerment, and the pursuit of one's dreams. The story follows Margot Leighton (played by Jennifer Lopez), a struggling single mother who works as an accountant at a large corporation. Despite her success in her job, she feels unfulfilled and restless, yearning for something more.

As Margot navigates her personal life, she meets a young girl named Emily (played by Vanessa Hudgens) who is struggling to find her place in the world. Inspired by Emily's passion and determination, Margot decides to take a leap of faith and pursue her own dreams, which leads her to become a successful fashion designer.

Throughout the film, Second Act explores themes of:

1. Self-discovery: Margot's journey is a metaphor for finding one's true purpose and identity. As she navigates her life, she discovers new passions and interests that bring her joy and fulfillment.
2. Empowerment: The film celebrates women's empowerment and independence. Margot takes control of her life, making choices that align with her values and aspirations.
3. Perseverance: Despite facing numerous setbacks and rejections, Margot remains determined to pursue her dreams. Her perseverance ultimately leads to success and personal growth.

The film also touches on themes of motherhood, friendship, and the importance of following one's heart. Overall, Second Act is a heartwarming and inspiring story about embracing change and pursuing one's passions.

documents.title: The Package
documents.overview: When a group of teenagers goes on a spring break camping trip, an unfortunate accident sets off a race to save their friend’s most prized possession.
documents.plot:
The Package is a 2018 American teen comedy directed by Jake Szymanski from a screenplay by Kevin Burrows and Matt Mider. Daniel Doheny, Sadie Calvano, Geraldine Viswanathan, Luke Spencer Roberts and Eduardo Franco star as a group of teenagers whose spring break camping trip goes catastrophically wrong.

Sean Floyd, home from Germany, heads into the woods for spring break with his friends Jeremy and Donnie. Without telling the others, Jeremy has also invited his twin sister Becky, on whom Sean has a long-standing crush and who has just split from her boyfriend Chad, and her friend Sarah, Donnie's ex-girlfriend. Soon after they reach the remote campsite, Sean and Donnie startle Jeremy while he is relieving himself with a knife in hand, and he accidentally severs his own penis. Sean hikes off with everyone's phones to find a signal, calls for help, sends an angry text to Chad from Becky's phone and then loses all of the phones. Paramedics airlift Jeremy to hospital, but once they have gone the friends realize that Sean handed over the wrong cooler.

What follows is a frantic race against time to deliver the severed organ before it is too late. Along the way, a rattlesnake bites it, a ravine and a foul-mouthed eleven-year-old with a drone stand between them and a boat, and a patriotic gas station clerk who believed Jeremy's fake military ID turns hostile when he learns the truth. When they finally reach a hospital, the organ is mistakenly attached to the wrong patient, a man whose girlfriend had mutilated him in revenge for cheating, and the friends must retrieve it all over again. Meanwhile, tensions flare when Becky learns about the text Sean sent to Chad, before Sean apologizes and the group reunites. They eventually discover that Jeremy was registered under the name on his fake ID and finally get the package to him. Donnie and Sarah reconcile, and Sean and Becky begin a relationship.

Netflix won a bidding war for Burrows and Mider's spec script, originally titled Eggplant Emoji, in January 2017. Szymanski was announced as director that July, the principal cast joined in August 2017, and the film was subsequently retitled. It was released on Netflix on August 10, 2018. Reviews were largely negative: Rotten Tomatoes reports a 37% approval rating from 19 critics, with a consensus remarking that the film learns the hard way that a single crude joke does not make a movie.

documents.title: Army of the Dead
documents.overview: Following a zombie outbreak in Las Vegas, a group of mercenaries take the ultimate gamble: venturing into the quarantine zone to pull off the greatest heist ever attempted.
documents.plot:
Army of the Dead is a 2021 American zombie apocalypse film written and directed by Zack Snyder. The movie takes place in Las Vegas, where a group of mercenaries, led by Scott Ward (played by Dave Bautista), are hired to pull off a heist during a zombie outbreak.

The story begins with Scott Ward, a former Army Ranger, who is struggling to find purpose after his divorce and the loss of his daughter. He is approached by a mysterious woman named Abigail (played by Ana de Armas) who offers him a lucrative job: to lead a team of mercenaries into the zombie-infested Las Vegas Strip and retrieve $1 million from an ATM.

Ward assembles a team, including his old friend Blythe (played by Jessica Henwick), a skilled hacker; Navid (played by Michael Rooker), a seasoned mercenary; and Doc (played by Buddy Johnson), a medic. The team is joined by Abigail, who claims to have a personal stake in the heist.

As they enter the zombie-infested Strip, the team quickly realizes that the situation is more complex than they anticipated. They must navigate through hordes of zombies, avoid rival treasure hunters, and contend with their own personal demons.

Throughout the movie, Ward's character undergoes significant development as he confronts his past and learns to trust himself and his team. The group faces numerous challenges, including a zombie-infested casino, a treacherous underground bunker, and a showdown with a ruthless zombie leader.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Abigail's true intentions are not entirely altruistic. She has her own motivations for pulling off the heist, which puts the entire team at risk.

The climax of the movie features an intense battle between Ward's team and the zombies, as well as a confrontation with Abigail's true identity. In the end, Ward emerges victorious, but not without scars both physical and emotional.

One of the standout aspects of Army of the Dead is its unique blend of action, horror, and humor. The movie features a talented ensemble cast, witty dialogue, and plenty of nods to classic zombie movies.

Overall, Army of the Dead is a thrilling and entertaining ride that pays homage to the zombie genre while also offering something fresh and original. With its talented cast, clever plot twists, and over-the-top action sequences, it's no wonder this movie has become a fan favorite among horror and action fans alike.

documents.title: What Keeps You Alive
documents.overview: Majestic mountains, a still lake and venomous betrayals engulf a female married couple attempting to celebrate their one-year anniversary.
documents.plot:
What Keeps You Alive is a 2018 Canadian psychological horror film written and directed by Colin Minihan, starring Hannah Emily Anderson and Brittany Allen. Early drafts centered on a husband and wife before the leads became a same-sex couple. The film was shot in Muskoka, Ontario, and Allen also composed its score, her first credit as a composer. It premiered at the SXSW Film Festival on March 10, 2018, and IFC Midnight released it in Los Angeles and New York and on video on demand on August 24, 2018.

Jackie and her wife, Jules, celebrate their first anniversary at a remote lakeside cabin owned by Jackie's family. Jules grows uneasy when Jackie's childhood friend Sarah calls her "Megan", a name Jackie says she dropped because the new one suits her better, and when Jules learns from Sarah and her husband, Daniel, that a girl named Jenny drowned in the lake when they were young. Jackie tearfully claims she has always blamed herself, and the couple seem reconciled, until Jackie shoves Jules off a cliff and goes back to rehearse a grief-stricken call to the police.

Jules survives and, watching Jackie search the woods, realizes that her wife's sobbing is an act. She tries to escape across the lake but is caught, and Jackie admits that she never loved her and plans to collect her life insurance. When Jules tries to alert Sarah during a dinner, Jackie murders Daniel and Sarah, confessing to Sarah that she killed Jenny too, and forces Jules to help hide the bodies. She explains that she has simply always lacked feeling or conscience, and Jules finds a hidden box of necklaces that Jackie gave to earlier wives. Jules escapes another trip to the cliff with a tranquilizer dart, but after a final fight Jackie throws her over the edge again and calls the police. When the diabetic Jackie takes her insulin, a video left by Jules reveals that it has been replaced with hydrogen peroxide, and Jackie collapses in the woods and dies of a stroke, while at the foot of the cliff Jules draws breath.

Anderson plays Jackie and Allen plays Jules, with Martha MacIsaac as Sarah and Joey Klein as Daniel. Reviews were positive, with 80% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 66. IndieWire praised the leads and the film's update of the Final Girl trope, while Newsweek felt it reduced its villain to a simple psychopath.

documents.title: Enter the Fat Dragon
documents.overview: After being dumped by his fiancé, heartbroken Hong Kong police officer Fallon Zhu gains 200+ pounds. His superiors demote him to the job of escorting convicts to Japan. When a convict in his custody mysteriously dies, he must team up with citizen Thor to solve the mystery.
documents.plot:
Enter the Fat Dragon is a 2020 martial arts comedy film that pays homage to the classic films of the genre while also exploring themes of identity, community, and redemption.

At its core, the movie is about a man who must confront his past and find a new sense of purpose. The protagonist, a former martial artist turned baker, is forced back into his old life when an old friend comes to him for help. As he navigates this new reality, he must come to terms with his own identity and the choices he has made.

One of the main themes of the film is the importance of community and found family. The protagonist's journey is not just about personal growth, but also about finding a sense of belonging and connection with others. Through his relationships with his friends and allies, he learns to let go of his past and find a new sense of purpose.

The movie also explores themes of redemption and second chances. The protagonist is given a chance to redeem himself and make amends for past mistakes, and he must learn to forgive himself and others in order to move forward.

Overall, Enter the Fat Dragon is a heartwarming and action-packed film that celebrates the power of community, identity, and redemption.

documents.title: The Lighthouse
documents.tagline: There is enchantment in the light.
documents.overview: Two lighthouse keepers try to maintain their sanity while living on a remote and mysterious New England island in the 1890s.
documents.plot:
The Lighthouse is a 2019 film directed and produced by Robert Eggers from a screenplay he wrote with his brother Max Eggers. It stars Robert Pattinson as a young lighthouse keeper calling himself Ephraim Winslow and Willem Dafoe as his superior, Thomas Wake, two tormented men stranded on a remote New England outpost by a violent storm. The project grew out of Max's script based on Edgar Allan Poe's unfinished story "The Light-House", and Eggers shaped the plot from a nineteenth-century legend about an accident at a Welsh lighthouse.

In the 1890s, Winslow arrives for a four-week stint as a "wickie" on an isolated island under Wake, a former sailor. He finds a small scrimshaw carving of a mermaid and keeps it. The domineering Wake assigns him the hardest labor while forbidding him to enter the lantern room, where Winslow sees him undress before the light each night. Winslow begins to have visions of sea creatures, is harassed by a one-eyed gull that Wake warns him not to harm, since gulls are said to hold the souls of dead sailors, and learns that his predecessor went mad. On the eve of his departure, he finds a dead gull fouling the cistern and beats the one-eyed gull to death. The wind turns, a fierce storm prevents the tender from relieving them, and the two men drink heavily as Winslow sees a mermaid on the shore.

Cut off for what Wake insists has been weeks, they veer between camaraderie and violence. Winslow fails to steal the lantern keys and glimpses the head of the previous keeper in a lobster trap. Drunk, he confesses that he is really Thomas Howard, who took the name of a cruel foreman he let drown during a log drive. Howard's attempt to flee in the dory ends when Wake smashes the boat with an axe, later blaming Howard. After the alcohol runs out, they drink turpentine. Reading Wake's logbook, which recommends he be dismissed without pay, Howard attacks him amid hallucinations, forces him into a grave, and takes the keys, then kills him when Wake strikes back. Climbing to the lamp, Howard stares into the lens, screams and tumbles down the stairs, and is last seen lying naked on the rocks as gulls devour him.

Shot in Nova Scotia in 2018, the film premiered at Cannes in the Directors' Fortnight in May 2019 and was released by A24 on October 18, 2019, grossing $18.3 million. Critics acclaimed Eggers's filmmaking and the two leads, giving it 90% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 83.

documents.title: The Mule
documents.overview: Earl Stone, a man in his eighties, is broke, alone, and facing foreclosure of his business when he is offered a job that simply requires him to drive. Easy enough, but, unbeknownst to Earl, he's just signed on as a drug courier for a Mexican cartel. He does so well that his cargo increases exponentially, and Earl hit the radar of hard-charging DEA agent Colin Bates.
documents.plot:
The Mule is a 2018 American crime drama film directed by Clint Eastwood, written by Nick Payne, and starring Clint Eastwood, Bradley Cooper, and Alison Eastwood. 

The movie begins with the introduction of Luke Wilson's character, David Brown, who is an elderly man living in a nursing home. He suffers from dementia and has lost his memory due to Alzheimer's disease. However, it is revealed that he was once a successful drug trafficker for the Mexican cartel.

As the story unfolds, we see flashbacks of Luke's life as a mule, transporting large quantities of cocaine for the cartel. The film then cuts back to the present day, where David Brown has been diagnosed with Alzheimer's and is struggling to cope with his condition.

One day, while in the nursing home, David meets a new patient named Benicio (played by Bradley Cooper), who claims to be an old friend from Luke's past. However, it becomes clear that Benicio is actually a former cartel member sent to kill Luke.

As the story progresses, we see Luke's life flashbacks become more vivid and intense, revealing his rise to becoming a successful drug trafficker. We also see glimpses of his relationships with his family members, including his wife, Lena (played by Alison Eastwood), and his son, Danny (played by Michael Peña).

As the plot thickens, Luke begins to suspect that Benicio is not who he claims to be. He starts to investigate and gather evidence, using his knowledge of the cartel's operations to stay one step ahead.

In a thrilling climax, Luke confronts Benicio in an intense showdown at a truck stop. With the help of some unexpected allies, including a young woman named Teresa (played by Gina Rodriguez), Luke manages to outsmart Benicio and bring him to justice.

Throughout the film, Clint Eastwood delivers a powerful performance as Luke Wilson's character, bringing depth and nuance to the role. The supporting cast also delivers strong performances, particularly Bradley Cooper, who brings a sense of menace and unpredictability to his portrayal of Benicio.

Overall, The Mule is a gripping and intense thriller that explores themes of loyalty, betrayal, and redemption. With its strong performances, engaging plot, and Clint Eastwood's direction, the film is a must-see for fans of crime dramas.
