documents.title: I Want to Eat Your Pancreas
documents.tagline: This is a story about an unforgettable spring...
documents.overview: After his classmate and crush is diagnosed with a pancreatic disease, an average high schooler sets out to make the most of her final days.
documents.plot:
I Want to Eat Your Pancreas is a Japanese anime film directed by Takahiro Niino, based on the manga of the same name written and illustrated by Yōko Kamio. The story revolves around Sawa Makoto, a high school student who discovers that her classmate, Meiko "Jirachi" Rokkanji, has been diagnosed with pancreatic cancer.

The film begins with Sawa's daily life as a high school student, where she is portrayed as an ordinary and somewhat introverted girl. However, when she meets Jirachi in the school's bathroom, her world is turned upside down. Jirachi reveals that she has pancreatic cancer and will not survive for much longer.

As Sawa spends more time with Jirachi, she begins to form a deep bond with her, and they develop an unlikely friendship. Despite their differences, they find comfort in each other's company, and Sawa becomes determined to make the most of their remaining time together.

Throughout the film, Sawa learns about Jirachi's life, including her struggles with cancer and her relationships with her family and friends. As their bond grows stronger, Sawa begins to confront her own emotions and fears, particularly regarding her own mortality.

As Jirachi's condition worsens, Sawa becomes more determined to make the most of their time together. She starts to explore her own desires and feelings, including a romantic interest in a classmate named Takumi. Meanwhile, Jirachi's family and friends struggle to come to terms with her diagnosis, leading to a deeper understanding of the complexities of human relationships.

The film takes a poignant turn when Sawa discovers that Jirachi has been keeping a secret from her - she is planning to die in a way that will allow her to transcend into a digital realm. This revelation sparks a series of emotional confrontations between Sawa and Jirachi, as they grapple with the meaning of life, death, and their own mortality.

Ultimately, the film builds towards a heart-wrenching climax as Sawa and Jirachi face the reality of their impending separation. In a poignant and powerful conclusion, Sawa makes a choice that will change her life forever, allowing her to find closure and move forward in the face of loss.

Throughout its narrative, I Want to Eat Your Pancreas explores themes of mortality, friendship, love, and the human condition. The film features beautiful animation, evocative music, and outstanding voice acting from the cast, bringing the characters to life in a way that is both authentic and emotionally resonant.

Overall, I Want to Eat Your Pancreas is a powerful and moving anime film that explores the complexities of human relationships and the fragility of life.

documents.title: Donnybrook
documents.overview: An ex-marine who struggles to provide for his family and a violent drug dealer with an undefeated fighting record are determined to compete in the Donnybrook, a legendary, bare-knuckle brawl with a cash prize of $100,000.
documents.plot:
Donnybrook is a 2018 crime drama written and directed by Tim Sutton, based on Frank Bill's novel of the same name, starring Jamie Bell, Frank Grillo, James Badge Dale and Margaret Qualley, with Chris Browning. It follows a desperate former Marine and a violent drug dealer whose paths converge at an illegal bare-knuckle tournament.

Jarhead Earl, an ex-Marine with a wife and two children living in a trailer park, sees only one way to give his family a fresh start: winning the Donnybrook, a huge bare-knuckle brawl. He robs a gun shop to raise the entry fee and returns home to find Chainsaw Angus, a psychotic methamphetamine dealer to whom his wife owes money. After a scuffle, Angus leaves with his sister and accomplice, Delia, and Earl takes his family and heads for the fight. Angus and Delia find their cookhouse in flames, kill the cook who escaped and visit their partner, Eldon, for money to rebuild; when he refuses, Angus orders Delia to kill him, and Eldon urges her to kill her brother instead. Worn down by Angus's constant abuse, Delia considers suicide but instead shoots him, takes a stash of meth and sets off for the Donnybrook herself, having overheard Earl's plans.

Angus survives, murders a stranger for his car and hunts for his sister and his drugs. Whalen, a hard-drinking local policeman investigating the robbery and the fire, learns about Angus from his ex-girlfriend and makes catching him a personal crusade, but is fatally wounded when the two trade shotgun blasts in a parking lot. Angus tracks down and kills Earl's son, then finds Delia at the fight site, drags her into the woods and strangles her. The Donnybrook begins as a no-holds-barred melee inside a chain-link cage, and after the field is whittled down, Earl and Angus are the last men standing. During the break before their final bout, Angus taunts Earl with the news that he killed his son. Back in the cage, Earl gains the upper hand and breaks Angus's neck, crying out that he killed his boy.

The film premiered in the Platform program of the Toronto International Film Festival on September 7, 2018, and IFC Films released it in the United States on February 15, 2019. Reviews were mixed, with 39% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 53, critics praising the cast but faulting its grim violence and thin storytelling.

documents.title: Rocketman
documents.overview: The story of Elton John's life, from his years as a prodigy at the Royal Academy of Music through his influential and enduring musical partnership with Bernie Taupin.
documents.plot:
Rocketman (2019) is a biographical musical drama film directed by Dexter Fletcher, written by Jamie Bell, Lee Hall, and Tom Bennett, and produced by Graham Broadbent, Peter Cavatt, and Tim Bevan.

The main themes of Rocketman (2019) include:

1. **The struggle with fame and identity**: The film explores the highs and lows of Elton John's rise to fame, as he navigates the pressures of stardom while trying to maintain his artistic integrity and individuality.
2. **Mental health and addiction**: Rocketman delves into Elton John's struggles with depression, anxiety, and addiction, showcasing the devastating effects these issues had on his life and relationships.
3. **Love and relationships**: The film highlights Elton John's tumultuous relationships with his manager, songwriter Bernie Taupin, and his husband, David Furnish, as well as his complicated friendships and romantic entanglements.
4. **Creative expression and legacy**: Rocketman celebrates Elton John's remarkable musical talent and the enduring power of his music, while also exploring the challenges he faced in maintaining creative control throughout his career.
5. **Self-discovery and redemption**: The film follows Elton John's journey towards self-acceptance, forgiveness, and personal growth, as he confronts his past mistakes and learns to find peace and happiness.

The movie features a star-studded cast, including Taron Egerton as Elton John, Jamie Bell as Bernie Taupin, and Richard Madden as John Reid. The film's music is an integral part of the story, with many of Elton John's iconic hits featured in the soundtrack.

Overall, Rocketman (2019) is a powerful and poignant biographical drama that explores the complexities of fame, identity, love, and creativity through the remarkable life story of Elton John.

documents.title: Mermaid Down
documents.overview: A mermaid is ripped from the Pacific, her tail is chopped off and she's thrown into a mental home where no one believes she is a mermaid.
documents.plot:
Mermaid Down is a 2019 American fantasy horror film directed by Jeffrey Grellman, who wrote it with Kelly Lauren Baker from a concept the two developed together. A Belgian-born filmmaker who moved to the United States at a young age, Grellman had previously made the non-genre films X Factor and Whiskey Blue. Produced by Grellman Film and Heartpine Pictures with the production company Mermaid Down LLC, the film features cinematography by Terra Gutmann Gonzalez, music by Christopher Lord and E. Shepherd Stevenson, and mermaid effects and animatronics by Jack Edjourian and Monty Shook. Distributed by Archstone Distribution and Alliance Entertainment, it was released in late October 2019 under the tagline "They exist".

Two drunken fishermen, Moss (Michael Prichard) and Stanley (Shepherd Stevenson), set out to catch a mermaid and succeed in hauling one (Alexandra Bokova) from the Pacific in their net. As she struggles to escape, one of them hacks off her tail with an axe and throws her human half into the fish hold. The scene is observed from a nearby yacht by the psychiatrist Dr. Beyer (Burt Culver), who swims aboard and kills the fishermen. Her seemingly helpful rescuer is in fact a demented doctor who sees her as the world's most valuable prize, and he locks her away in the Beyer Psychiatric Hospital, his institution for disturbed young women, where she recovers as a new pair of human legs grow. As "the new girl" she is mocked by some patients and pitied by others, and nobody believes she is a mermaid. Never speaking a word, she communicates through expression and sign language, and she befriends the Ghost (Meggan Kaiser), the spirit of a girl murdered by Beyer, whom one other patient can also see. Knowing that being away from the water will eventually kill her, the mermaid must rely on her survival instincts as Beyer's true nature becomes clear and the girls rally around her in a fight for their lives.

Reviews were mixed. Stuart D. Monroe of Horror DNA was enthusiastic, describing the film as a fantasy-horror fairy tale with a message of female empowerment, equal parts fantasy and arthouse, and calling Bokova's wordless performance hypnotic. Moria, by contrast, felt the premise had great potential but found Grellman's direction confusing, criticising the cramped house used for the asylum scenes, murky side plots and the psychiatrist's poorly motivated actions.

documents.title: The Bob's Burgers Movie
documents.overview: When a ruptured water main creates an enormous sinkhole right in front of Bob's Burgers, it blocks the entrance indefinitely and ruins the Belchers’ plans for a successful summer. While Bob and Linda struggle to keep the business afloat, the kids try to solve a mystery that could save their family's restaurant. As the dangers mount, these underdogs help each other find hope and fight to get back behind the counter, where they belong.
documents.plot:
The Bob's Burgers Movie is a 2022 American animated comedy film directed by Loren Bouchard and produced by Bento Box Entertainment. The movie takes place after the events of the ninth season of the TV series.

The story begins with Bob Belcher (H. Jon Benjamin) struggling to find inspiration for his restaurant's next big burger creation. He becomes obsessed with a new, high-end food truck that has arrived in town, run by a rival restaurateur named Hugo Habercore (Will Forte). Hugo is determined to put Bob out of business and steal the spotlight.

Meanwhile, Tina Belcher (Dan Mintz) starts writing a novel about a zombie apocalypse, which becomes an unexpected hit. She begins to receive attention from a publisher, but her family's life is disrupted by Hugo's constant attempts to sabotage their restaurant.

As the story unfolds, Bob's obsession with Hugo grows, and he enlists the help of his family to take him down. Louise (Kristen Schaal) and Gene (Eugene Mirman) join forces with Teddy (John Roberts), a regular customer at the restaurant, to create a viral social media campaign that will expose Hugo's true intentions.

Throughout the movie, Bob's relationships with his family are put to the test as he becomes increasingly consumed by his rivalry with Hugo. However, in the end, Bob comes to realize what truly matters: his family and the love they share for each other.

The climax of the film features a showdown between Bob and Hugo at the Wonder Wharf, where the two engage in an absurd battle over burgers and business. In the end, Bob emerges victorious, but not before learning a valuable lesson about the importance of staying true to oneself and appreciating what truly matters in life.

The movie concludes with the Belcher family coming together to celebrate their victory and the success of Tina's novel. The film ends on a heartwarming note, with the family looking forward to a brighter future together.

Overall, The Bob's Burgers Movie is a hilarious and heartwarming animated comedy that explores themes of family, love, and perseverance. With its witty dialogue, lovable characters, and absurd humor, it's sure to delight fans of the TV series and newcomers alike.

documents.title: The King
documents.overview: England, 15th century. Hal, a capricious prince who lives among the populace far from court, is forced by circumstances to reluctantly accept the throne and become Henry V.
documents.plot:
The King (2019) is a historical drama film directed by David Michôd, based on the 2003 play of the same name by Jez Butterworth. The movie stars Timothée Chalamet as King Henry V of England.

The main themes of The King (2019) include:

1. **Identity and Coming-of-Age**: The film explores King Henry's journey from a young prince to a confident leader, grappling with his own identity, masculinity, and sense of purpose.
2. **War and its Consequences**: The movie delves into the psychological effects of war on individuals and society, highlighting the brutal realities of conflict and the moral dilemmas that come with it.
3. **Power Dynamics and Corruption**: As Henry ascends to the throne, he must navigate the complexities of power, loyalty, and corruption, which threaten to undermine his authority and relationships.
4. **Mental Health and Trauma**: The film touches on King Henry's struggles with mental health, particularly his experiences with anxiety, depression, and PTSD, which are exacerbated by the trauma of war.
5. **Loyalty and Betrayal**: The movie examines the intricate web of alliances and rivalries within the royal court, where loyalty is tested and betrayal can be both expected and devastating.

Throughout the film, these themes are woven together to create a nuanced portrayal of King Henry's transformation from a young prince to a confident leader, grappling with the weight of his responsibilities and the consequences of his actions.

documents.title: The Jurassic Games
documents.tagline: Win the games. Win your freedom.
documents.overview: In the near future, 10 death row convicts are forced to compete in a virtual reality game that pits them against dinosaurs and each other.
documents.plot:
The Jurassic Games is a 2018 American low-budget science fiction action film written and directed by Ryan Bellgardt, produced by High Octane Pictures and distributed by Uncork'd Entertainment. It stars Adam Hampton as Tucker, a death-row inmate, with Ryan Merriman as the Host, Perrey Reeves as the producer Savannah and Katie Burgess as Joy, alongside Daniel Barton, Ron Clemons, Dylan Cox and Erika Daly. It runs 86 minutes and was promoted with the tagline "Win the games. Win your freedom."

In the near future, ten convicts on death row are chosen to take part in the Jurassic Games, a televised virtual reality competition broadcast to a huge international audience. Plugged into a simulated world of deserts and jungles, the contestants must survive attacks by digital dinosaurs as well as each other. Only one of them can emerge as the winner and earn freedom; the catch is that anyone who dies inside the game dies in the real world as well. Tucker insists that he is an innocent man and is determined to survive so he can return to his children, who watch him on television as he fights for his life. His fellow contestants include Joy, a teenage psychopath, and a cartel boss, and their backstories are filled in as the competition goes on. Presiding over the spectacle is the flamboyant Host, who wears a sharp suit and a black dinosaur helmet, while the ruthless Savannah runs the show behind the scenes. The film repeatedly cuts away to viewers laughing at the carnage, and its story includes twists involving the characters' motives.

The film was released on DVD in the United States and United Kingdom in May 2018. Critics treated it as a mockbuster drawing on Jurassic Park, The Hunger Games, Death Race, The Matrix and Battle Royale. Luiz H. C. of Bloody Disgusting called it shallow but a legitimately entertaining ride, finding its self-aware satire of reality television better than expected and some of its dinosaur sequences surprisingly impressive, though the characters were one-dimensional; he singled out Hampton as a solid lead and Merriman as the most entertaining character. Zoe Crombie of Film Inquiry also praised Merriman's scene-stealing performance and Burgess's over-the-top turn, but criticized the weightless computer-generated creatures, uncreative cinematography, contradictory satire of violent media and reliance on racial stereotypes, concluding that it was less than the sum of its borrowed parts.

documents.title: Lego DC Comics Super Heroes: The Flash
documents.original_title: Lego DC Comics Super Heroes: The Flash
documents.overview: Reverse-Flash manipulates the Speed Force to put the Flash into a time loop that forces him to relive the same day over and over again—with progressively disastrous results, including losing his powers and being fired by the Justice League. The Flash must find a way to restore time to its original path and finally apprehend his worst enemy before all is lost for the Flash…and the world!
documents.plot:
Lego DC Comics Super Heroes: The Flash is an animated superhero film that brings to life the iconic character of Barry Allen, aka The Flash. At its core, this movie explores the theme of identity and self-discovery. As Barry navigates his dual life as a crime scene investigator by day and a superhero by night, he must confront the challenges of balancing his personal and professional responsibilities.

The film also delves into the idea of responsibility and power. The Flash's abilities make him an incredibly powerful hero, but with great power comes great responsibility. As Barry struggles to come to terms with his new role as a superhero, he must learn to wield his powers wisely and use them for the greater good.

Furthermore, Lego DC Comics Super Heroes: The Flash touches on the theme of friendship and camaraderie. Barry's relationships with his friends and allies, particularly Cisco Ramon and Caitlin Kane, are crucial in helping him navigate the complexities of being a superhero. The film showcases the importance of having a support system and working together to overcome adversity.

Lastly, the movie explores the idea of embracing one's true nature. As Barry struggles to reconcile his secret identity with his life as a superhero, he must ultimately come to terms with who he is and what he wants to achieve. This theme is particularly relevant in the context of The Flash's character, who has always been driven by a desire to help others and make a positive impact on the world.

Overall, Lego DC Comics Super Heroes: The Flash is a lighthearted and entertaining film that explores some deeper themes and ideas, making it a fun and engaging watch for both kids and adults.

documents.title: Death on the Nile
documents.overview: Belgian sleuth Hercule Poirot boards a glamorous river steamer with enough champagne to fill the Nile. But his Egyptian vacation turns into a thrilling search for a murderer when a picture-perfect couple’s idyllic honeymoon is tragically cut short.
documents.plot:
Death on the Nile is a 2022 mystery film directed by Kenneth Branagh from a screenplay by Michael Green, based on Agatha Christie's 1937 novel. The second big-screen adaptation of the book after the 1978 film, it is a sequel to Murder on the Orient Express (2017) and the second installment in Branagh's Hercule Poirot series. Branagh and Tom Bateman reprise their roles as Poirot and his friend Bouc, alongside an ensemble including Annette Bening, Russell Brand, Ali Fazal, Dawn French, Gal Gadot, Armie Hammer, Rose Leslie, Emma Mackey, Sophie Okonedo and Jennifer Saunders. After several delays, including those caused by the COVID-19 pandemic, it was released in February 2022.

A prologue set in Belgium in 1914 shows the young soldier Poirot devising a plan that saves his unit, only to be scarred when his captain triggers a booby trap; his fiancée Katherine suggests he grow a moustache to hide his injuries. In 1937, in a London nightclub where the blues singer Salome Otterbourne is performing, Poirot watches Jacqueline "Jackie" de Bellefort introduce her fiancé, Simon Doyle, to her wealthy childhood friend, the heiress Linnet Ridgeway.

Six weeks later, in Egypt, Poirot runs into Bouc and his mother, Euphemia, who are among the guests celebrating Linnet's marriage to Simon. The wedding party includes Linnet's maid Louise Bourget, Salome and her niece and manager Rosalie, Linnet's godmother Marie Van Schuyler and her nurse Mrs. Bowers, Linnet's cousin and financial manager Andrew Katchadourian, and her former fiancé Dr. Linus Windlesham. Jackie, bitter at being jilted, has followed the couple to Egypt. To escape her, the group boards the river steamer Karnak for a cruise along the Nile. Linnet asks Poirot to protect her, confiding that she distrusts many of the people around her. When Linnet is found shot dead in her cabin, Poirot must unravel a web of jealousy, greed and deception among the passengers, each of whom has a motive, before the killer strikes again.

The film received mixed reviews; critics praised its lavish production design, cinematography and Branagh's performance but found it overlong and less engaging than the novel's previous adaptation. Its release was overshadowed by controversy surrounding some cast members, and it grossed about $137 million worldwide, less than its predecessor. A third installment, A Haunting in Venice, followed in 2023.

documents.title: Await Further Instructions
documents.overview: A dysfunctional family awake on Christmas morning to discover they’re sealed inside their house by a mysterious black substance. On television, a single line of text reads: “Stay Indoors and Await Further Instructions.”
documents.plot:
Await Further Instructions is a 2018 British science fiction thriller film directed by Stuart Orme. The movie follows a family who are trapped in their home during a mysterious event that causes time to slow down, and they must navigate the challenges of this altered reality.

The main theme of Await Further Instructions revolves around the concept of time and its relationship with human experience. As the characters struggle to cope with the slowed-down world, they begin to question the nature of time and their place within it. The film explores how our perception of time is influenced by our emotions, relationships, and experiences.

The movie also delves into the theme of family dynamics and the ways in which relationships can be both a source of comfort and a source of conflict. As the characters try to navigate this altered reality, they are forced to confront their own personal demons and re-evaluate their priorities.

Furthermore, Await Further Instructions touches on the idea of isolation and confinement, highlighting how these conditions can affect individuals in different ways. The film's use of time dilation as a plot device serves to underscore the psychological effects of being trapped in a confined space with limited communication with the outside world.

Overall, Await Further Instructions is a thought-provoking exploration of the human experience, delving into themes that are both timely and timeless.

documents.title: 10x10
documents.tagline: There are some secrets we cannot escape
documents.overview: Lewis is an outwardly ordinary guy, but in reality he is hiding an obsession – revenge – against Cathy. Lewis kidnaps Cathy in broad daylight and takes her to his home, where he locks her in a soundproof cell and attempts to extract a dark secret from her past.
documents.plot:
10x10 is a 2018 psychological thriller directed by Suzi Ewing and written by Noel Clarke, who produced it through his company Unstoppable Entertainment and also appears as Dennis. Luke Evans stars as Robert Lewis and Kelly Reilly as Cathy, with Olivia Chenery as Lewis's late wife Alana, Skye Lucia Degruttola as his young daughter Summer, Jill Winternitz as Jen, Jason Maza and Stacy Hall as police officers and Norma Dixit as the housekeeper Alondra.

Cathy, a woman who listens to Christian radio and is about to open a new business, has coffee in town and drives to her gym, unaware that she is being watched and followed. In the parking lot, Lewis pulls a gun on her, ties her up, gags her and locks her in the trunk of his car. At his secluded modernist house, he shuts her in a padded ten-by-ten-foot room whose thick walls absorb every sound and asks her one question: what is her name. He wants neither sex nor money, only an admission.

Lewis is an ordinary man rather than a seasoned criminal, and Cathy repeatedly manages to break out before he overpowers her and returns her to the cell. Meanwhile he follows television reports about the Charleston Three, patients who died in mysterious circumstances at a hospital, where the nurses tried for the deaths were eventually cleared. Under pressure, Cathy confesses that she is really Natalie-Ann Stevens and that Cathy was her twin sister, who killed herself after their father's affair brought shame on the family in their strict religious community. As a nurse, Natalie appointed herself judge of patients who confided their sins, and she admits that she killed Alana, one of the three victims, for having cheated on Lewis. She even suggests that Summer is not his child. Escaping again, she seizes Summer, who bites her and gets away; the housekeeper is shot. As Lewis prepares to take recordings of her confession to the police, Cathy attacks him in the garage, and after he knocks her down, the falling door crashes onto her. Lewis tells Summer that he loves her and that she is his daughter.

The film was released in April 2018, with shooting having taken place in London and Atlanta. Critics were divided: the Los Angeles Times called it an effective thriller with smart performances and twists, while RogerEbert.com disliked its abduction premise and the misogynist trope behind its reversal, though it credited Ewing's command of suspense. In July 2023 it became the most-watched film on Netflix in the UK.

documents.title: Shoplifters
documents.overview: After one of their shoplifting sessions, Osamu and his son come across a little girl in the freezing cold. At first reluctant to shelter the girl, Osamu’s wife agrees to take care of her after learning of the hardships she faces. Although the family is poor, barely making enough money to survive through petty crime, they seem to live happily together until an unforeseen incident reveals hidden secrets, testing the bonds that unite them.
documents.plot:
Shoplifters (Japanese: Manbiki Kazoku, literally "Shoplifting Family") is a 2018 Japanese drama written, directed and edited by Hirokazu Kore-eda. Asking what makes a family, a question he had considered for a decade, Kore-eda drew on reports of poverty and shoplifting during Japan's recession, and wrote one scene after hearing a girl at an orphanage read the picture book Swimmy. Shot on 35 mm film from December 2017, it premiered at the 2018 Cannes Film Festival, where it won the Palme d'Or, the first for a Japanese film since The Eel in 1997.

In Tokyo, a makeshift family lives in poverty in the home of the elderly Hatsue, whose late husband's pension supports them: Nobuyo, who works at an industrial laundry; her husband, Osamu, a day laborer off work with an injured ankle; Aki, who works at a peep show; and the boy Shota, who shoplifts with Osamu using hand signals. One cold night they find Yuri, a little girl locked out on an apartment balcony, and after seeing signs of abuse decide to keep her. Two months later, the police start investigating her disappearance, which her parents never reported. The family cuts her hair, burns her clothes and renames her Lin. After a happy day at the beach, Hatsue dies in her sleep, and Osamu and Nobuyo bury her beneath the house to keep collecting her pension.

Shota, who was himself taken from a locked car as a small child, grows uneasy about the family's code and about teaching Yuri to steal. Drawing attention to himself in a grocery store, he flees, jumps from a bridge and breaks his leg. The others are caught trying to run with Yuri and Aki, and the authorities uncover Hatsue's death and the family's secrets, including that Osamu and Nobuyo once killed Nobuyo's abusive husband in self-defense. Nobuyo takes the blame and goes to prison, Shota is placed in an orphanage, and Osamu admits they had meant to abandon him. As Shota leaves on a bus he confesses that he let himself be caught, and silently acknowledges Osamu as his father, while Yuri is returned to neglectful parents.

Lily Franky plays Osamu and Sakura Ando co-stars, with Kirin Kiki in one of her last roles. Critics were rapturous, with 99% approval on Rotten Tomatoes. It grossed about $72.6 million worldwide and was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film.

documents.title: The Last Thing He Wanted
documents.overview: At the turning point of the Iran-Contra affair, Elena McMahon, a fearless investigative journalist covering the 1984 US presidential campaign, puts herself in danger when she abandons her assigned task in order to fulfill the last wish of her ailing father, a mysterious man whose past activities she barely knows.
documents.plot:
The Last Thing He Wanted is a 2020 political thriller directed by Dee Rees, who adapted Joan Didion's 1996 novel of the same name with Marco Villalobos. Anne Hathaway stars as the journalist Elena McMahon, with Ben Affleck as Treat Morrison, Rosie Perez as Alma Guerrero, Willem Dafoe as her father Dick McMahon, Edi Gathegi as Jones, Mel Rodriguez as Barry Sedlow and Toby Jones as Paul Schuster.

Elena, a reporter for the Atlantic Post, was forced to flee the paper's Central American bureau in El Salvador during the civil war. Years later she wants it reopened, but her editor reveals that Congress is quietly pressing the paper to scale back its coverage of the region and assigns her instead to Ronald Reagan's re-election campaign. Elena reluctantly visits her long-absent father, Dick, and finds him still dealing in contraband but slipping into dementia. On the campaign trail, a general identifies her surveillance photos of shipping containers as surplus National Guard arms.

When Dick is hospitalised, Elena hands her assignment to her friend Alma and goes to Florida to care for him. He begs her to complete a deal he has arranged with his associate Barry Sedlow, and she agrees, seeing a chance to investigate the story from the inside. Following Sedlow's instructions, she delivers a large arms shipment to Costa Rica, where the buyer, Jones, underpays her and partly pays in cocaine. Stranded when her pilot leaves, she takes Jones's gun and vehicle, then discovers that her passport bears the name Elise Meyer. She reaches Antigua, learns that her father has died, and finds the embassy closed for the Fourth of July. Treat Morrison, an ambassador-at-large who has been investigating her, finds her at her hotel, and they sleep together. When gunmen attack her by the pool, Jones rescues her and explains that the deal was a trap to draw her father out of hiding. Morrison places her with Paul Schuster and promises to get her home to break the story of the arms deals, but a gunman kills Paul and his staff, and Elena turns to find it is Morrison, who shoots her dead and later claims self-defence. Jones, an agent of French intelligence, reports that he had been trying to protect her, and Alma uses Elena's notes to publish the story of the Iran–Contra affair.

The film premiered at the Sundance Film Festival on January 27, 2020, and was released on Netflix in February. It was panned, with only 5% positive reviews on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 35.

documents.title: My Hero Academia: Two Heroes
documents.original_title: 僕のヒーローアカデミア THE MOVIE ～2人の英雄～
documents.overview: All Might and Deku accept an invitation to go abroad to a floating and mobile manmade city, called 'I-Island', where they research quirks as well as hero supplemental items at the special 'I-Expo' convention that is currently being held on the island. During that time, suddenly, despite an iron wall of security surrounding the island, the system is breached by a villain, and the only ones able to stop him are the students of Class 1-A.
documents.plot:
My Hero Academia: Two Heroes is a 2018 Japanese animated superhero film based on an original story featuring the characters of Kōhei Horikoshi's manga series My Hero Academia. Produced by Bones and distributed by Toho, it was directed by Kenji Nagasaki from a script by Yōsuke Kuroda, with characters designed by Yoshihiko Umakoshi, all returning from the anime television series. The ensemble voice cast includes Daiki Yamashita, Kenta Miyake, Mirai Shida, Katsuhisa Namase, Nobuhiko Okamoto, Ayane Sakura and Yuki Kaji. The story takes place between the manga's Final Exams and Forest Training Camp arcs.

Years ago, as an exchange student in California, the young All Might foiled a group of casino robbers with the help of his friend David Shield, who went on to become a scientist and design many of his hero suits. In the present, during summer break, All Might takes his protégé Izuku Midoriya to I-Island, an artificial floating city, at the invitation of David's daughter Melissa, who wants to surprise her father. When David tests All Might, he is horrified to learn that his friend's Quirk is almost exhausted, threatening his role as the Symbol of Peace. Meanwhile Melissa shows Izuku around the island, where they run into his classmates from Class 1-A, and she confides that, like Izuku before he gained his power, she was born without a Quirk. She gives him a "Full Gauntlet", a device that lets him unleash his Quirk without injuring himself. During a formal party for the assembled heroes, a villain named Wolfram seizes the island's security system, restrains the heroes, including All Might, and takes David and his assistant Samuel hostage. Izuku, Melissa and several classmates evade capture and climb the central tower to disable the security system, fighting villains and security robots on the way. At the top, Izuku and Melissa discover that David and Samuel staged the attack to recover a confiscated invention that amplifies Quirks, hoping to restore All Might's power, but Wolfram turns out to be a real villain secretly hired by Samuel, forcing All Might and Izuku to join forces against a dangerously empowered foe.

The film premiered at Anime Expo in Los Angeles on July 5, 2018, before opening in Japan on August 3. It grossed $33.4 million worldwide and received positive reviews, holding a 100% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on eight reviews.

documents.title: Rebecca
documents.overview: After a whirlwind romance with a wealthy widower, a naïve bride moves to his family estate but can't escape the haunting shadow of his late wife.
documents.plot:
Rebecca is a 2020 British romantic thriller film directed by Ben Wheatley from a screenplay by Jane Goldman, Joe Shrapnel and Anna Waterhouse, based on Daphne du Maurier's 1938 novel. Lily James stars as a young woman who marries a wealthy widower, with Armie Hammer as Maxim de Winter, Kristin Scott Thomas as the sinister housekeeper Mrs. Danvers. It follows Alfred Hitchcock's 1940 adaptation.

While working as the paid companion of the wealthy American Mrs. Van Hopper in Monte Carlo, a shy young woman meets Maxim de Winter, a recently widowed English aristocrat. After a whirlwind romance, they marry and travel to his grand estate in Cornwall, Manderley. There, the new Mrs. de Winter finds herself overshadowed by the memory of Maxim's glamorous first wife, Rebecca, who drowned in a sailing accident and was adored by the staff and Maxim's friends. The cold housekeeper, Mrs. Danvers, who was devoted to Rebecca, constantly undermines her.

A visit from Rebecca's cousin, Jack Favell, infuriates Maxim. Later, Mrs. Danvers helps the new wife plan the revival of Manderley's costume ball and suggests a gown copied from a family portrait, but when she appears in it, Maxim is furious: Rebecca wore the same costume at the previous ball. Distraught and convinced that Maxim regrets marrying her, Mrs. de Winter is nearly persuaded by Mrs. Danvers to jump from a window, when a shipwreck in a storm leads to the discovery of Rebecca's boat, with her body inside.

Maxim confesses to his wife that he hated Rebecca, who was cruel and unfaithful. On the night of her death, she told him she was pregnant by another man and taunted him until he shot her; he then sank her body in her boat. Though shaken, his wife resolves to stand by him. Favell tries to blackmail Maxim with a note suggesting Rebecca had not planned suicide, and at the inquest it emerges that her boat was deliberately sunk, leading to Maxim's arrest. Mrs. de Winter dismisses Mrs. Danvers and tracks down Rebecca's London doctor, whose records show that Rebecca was not pregnant but suffering from terminal cancer. The investigation concludes that she took her own life, and Mrs. de Winter comes to believe Rebecca had goaded Maxim into killing her.

Released in select cinemas on 16 October 2020 and on Netflix five days later, the film received negative reviews, with critics praising its look but comparing it unfavourably to Hitchcock's version; Rotten Tomatoes reported 39% approval.

documents.title: Wounds
documents.overview: Disturbing and mysterious things begin to happen to a bartender in New Orleans after he picks up a phone left behind at his bar.
documents.plot:
Wounds is a psychological horror film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy. The movie follows a young bartender, Jake, who becomes embroiled in a mysterious and sinister world when he encounters a charismatic but troubled customer, Anthony.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Wounds is a exploration of themes such as trauma, identity, and the fragility of human relationships. The film's use of surreal and dreamlike sequences serves to underscore the main character's growing unease and disorientation, creating a sense of tension and foreboding that permeates every aspect of the narrative.

At its core, Wounds is a movie about the ways in which our experiences shape us, often in profound and lasting ways. The film's protagonist, Jake, is forced to confront his own demons and the traumas of his past, leading to a journey of self-discovery that is both deeply unsettling and profoundly cathartic.

Through its use of atmospheric tension and psychological suspense, Wounds creates a sense of unease that lingers long after the credits roll. The film's exploration of themes such as identity, trauma, and human connection serves to underscore the complexities and nuances of the human experience, making for a thought-provoking and deeply unsettling viewing experience.

Overall, Wounds is a movie that defies easy categorization or summary, instead opting for a more nuanced and introspective approach that rewards close attention and multiple viewings.

documents.title: Booksmart
documents.tagline: Getting straight A's. Giving zero F's.
documents.overview: Two academic teenage superstars realize, on the eve of their high school graduation, that they should have worked less and played more. Determined to never fall short of their peers, the girls set out on a mission to cram four years of fun into one night.
documents.plot:
Booksmart is a coming-of-age comedy film directed by Olivia Wilde and written by Emily Halpern, Sarah Haskins, Katie Silberman, and Kate Long. The movie follows the story of two high school friends, Amy (Kaitlyn Dever) and Molly (Beanie Feldstein), who are on the cusp of graduation.

The film takes place over a single night, as Amy and Molly decide to break the rules and have one wild night before they graduate. They've been inseparable since childhood, but their friendship has become stale due to their differing interests and social cliques. Amy is a straight-A student who wants to attend Harvard, while Molly is more laid-back and interested in partying.

As they embark on their adventure, the girls visit various parties, bars, and clubs around Los Angeles, where they encounter a cast of eccentric characters, including a group of rowdy college students, a DJ, and a charismatic bartender (Jason Mantzoukas). Along the way, Amy and Molly confront their own insecurities, fears, and desires.

Throughout the night, the girls face various challenges, including navigating awkward social situations, dealing with peer pressure, and confronting their own identities. They also encounter a series of misadventures, including a wild party at a mansion, a disastrous karaoke session, and a run-in with a group of aggressive frat boys.

As the night wears on, Amy and Molly begin to reconnect and rediscover their friendship. They share heartfelt conversations, laugh together, and support each other through various struggles. The film's climax features an emotional confrontation between the two friends, as they come to terms with their own futures and the end of their high school era.

The movie ends on a hopeful note, as Amy and Molly reflect on the night's events and look forward to their future together. They've learned to let go of their inhibitions, take risks, and prioritize their friendship above all else. The film concludes with a montage of the girls' post-graduation plans, set to a catchy indie-pop soundtrack.

Booksmart features a talented young cast, witty dialogue, and a nuanced exploration of female friendship and identity. The movie has received widespread critical acclaim for its humor, heart, and authentic portrayal of adolescent struggles. Overall, Booksmart is a charming, laugh-out-loud comedy that celebrates the power of female friendship and the importance of embracing one's true self.

documents.title: Black Panther: Wakanda Forever
documents.overview: Queen Ramonda, Shuri, M’Baku, Okoye and the Dora Milaje fight to protect their nation from intervening world powers in the wake of King T’Challa’s death. As the Wakandans strive to embrace their next chapter, the heroes must band together with the help of War Dog Nakia and Everett Ross and forge a new path for the kingdom of Wakanda.
documents.plot:
Black Panther: Wakanda Forever is a 2022 superhero film directed by Ryan Coogler, produced by Marvel Studios, and based on the Marvel Comics character Black Panther. The movie takes place after the events of Avengers: Endgame.

The story begins with the death of King T'Challa (played by Chadwick Boseman), who had assumed the mantle of Black Panther to protect his nation Wakanda from threats both within and outside its borders. The film follows Shuri (Letitia Wright), T'Challa's sister, as she navigates her new role as queen and tries to find a way to honor her brother's legacy.

As Shuri delves deeper into the mysteries of her brother's death, she discovers that it was not a natural occurrence but rather a result of a catastrophic event known as the "Heart-Shaped Herb" being destroyed. This herb is a powerful plant that gives Black Panther his powers and allows him to heal from injuries.

Shuri soon learns that the destruction of the Heart-Shaped Herb has caused a ripple effect, leading to the return of Namor (played by Tenoch Huerta), the long-lost king of Atlantis. Namor seeks revenge against Wakanda for its role in the destruction of his homeland and its people.

Meanwhile, Shuri is joined by a new generation of heroes, including Riri Williams (Dominique Thorne), a brilliant inventor who creates a suit inspired by Iron Man's armor, and M'Baku (Winston Duke), the leader of the Jabari Land tribe. Together, they form a team to protect Wakanda from Namor's attacks.

Throughout the film, Shuri grapples with her own identity and sense of purpose as she tries to balance her desire for revenge against Namor with her duty to protect her people. Along the way, she discovers that her brother's legacy is not just about power but also about love, family, and community.

The movie features stunning visuals, impressive action sequences, and a powerful performance from Letitia Wright as Shuri. While it may not have the same level of emotional resonance as its predecessor, Black Panther: Wakanda Forever is a worthy sequel that expands on the world and characters introduced in the first film.

Overall, Black Panther: Wakanda Forever is a thrilling adventure that explores themes of grief, identity, and community. With its richly detailed world-building and strong performances, it's a must-see for fans of the Marvel Cinematic Universe.

documents.title: The Golden Glove
documents.overview: A serial killer strikes fear in the hearts of residents of Hamburg during the early 1970s.
documents.plot:
The Golden Glove (German: Der Goldene Handschuh) is a 2019 German biographical horror film written, co-produced and directed by Fatih Akin, adapted from Heinz Strunk's novel of the same name. It tells the story of the Hamburg serial killer Fritz Honka, who murdered four women between 1970 and 1975 and hid parts of their bodies in his apartment. Jonas Dassler stars as Honka, transformed with heavy prosthetics, with Margarethe Tiesel, Katja Studt, Martina Eitner-Acheampong and Tristan Göbel. A German-French co-production, it competed for the Golden Bear at the 69th Berlin International Film Festival.

In 1970, Honka, an alcoholic and physically disfigured night watchman, kills Gertraud Bräuer, a prostitute, in his squalid attic apartment in Hamburg. He dismembers the body, disposing of some remains in a suitcase and hiding the rest in a recess behind his wall. The police find the suitcase but cannot identify the culprit. By 1974, Honka spends nearly all his free time at the Golden Glove, a seedy bar in the St. Pauli red-light district frequented by alcoholics, prostitutes and lost souls, where most women he approaches reject him in disgust. He becomes fixated on Petra, a schoolgirl he glimpsed briefly outside the bar.

One night he brings home Gerda Voss, a homeless older woman, and lets her stay in exchange for sex and housework, on the promise that she will introduce him to her daughter, Rosi. When Gerda admits that she is estranged from Rosi, Honka erupts in rage, and Gerda eventually escapes by accepting help from a religious charity. Honka briefly tries to quit drinking after being injured in an accident and takes a job as a night watchman at an office building, where he is drawn to a cleaning woman, but he relapses and returns to the Golden Glove. He lures other vulnerable women back to his flat, subjecting them to humiliation and violence, while the stench of the decomposing bodies fills the building and his neighbors complain, until a fire in the building leads to the discovery of his crimes.

The Golden Glove divided critics. Many praised Dassler's startling performance and the meticulous recreation of 1970s Hamburg, but others found its unflinching depiction of sexual violence repellent and questioned what the film offered beyond shock. It was Akin's first film to receive an 18 certificate in Germany.

documents.title: Waiting for the Barbarians
documents.overview: At an isolated frontier outpost, a colonial magistrate suffers a crisis of conscience when an army colonel arrives looking to interrogate the locals about an impending uprising, using cruel tactics that horrify the magistrate.
documents.plot:
Waiting for the Barbarians is a thought-provoking film that delves into the complexities of colonialism, power dynamics, and the human condition. The movie is set in a fictional African colony during the 19th century and follows the story of Colonel Joll (played by Johnny Depp), a ruthless and cunning military officer who serves as the commander of the outpost.

At its core, Waiting for the Barbarians explores the themes of imperialism, oppression, and the dehumanizing effects of colonialism. The film portrays a society where the ruling elite exploit and manipulate the native population, stripping them of their culture, identity, and dignity. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Colonel Joll is not only a symbol of colonial power but also a complex character with his own motivations and desires.

One of the main themes of the film is the blurring of lines between good and evil. Colonel Joll's actions are morally ambiguous, and he is willing to do whatever it takes to maintain his power and control over the colony. However, as the story progresses, it becomes clear that he is also a product of his environment and the system he serves. This nuanced portrayal of morality raises questions about the nature of humanity and whether individuals can be redeemed or if they are forever trapped by their circumstances.

The film also explores the theme of identity and how it is shaped by power dynamics. The native characters in the film, particularly the young girl who becomes embroiled in Colonel Joll's plans, struggle to maintain their sense of self amidst the oppressive forces that surround them. Their experiences serve as a powerful commentary on the ways in which colonialism erases cultural identities and reduces individuals to mere objects.

Furthermore, Waiting for the Barbarians is a film about the fragility of human relationships and the devastating consequences of violence and oppression. The movie's title, "Waiting for the Barbarians," refers to the idea that the native population is seen as barbaric and uncivilized by the colonial powers. However, as the story unfolds, it becomes clear that this perception is a product of fear, ignorance, and prejudice.

Ultimately, Waiting for the Barbarians is a powerful critique of colonialism and its ongoing impact on our world today. The film's themes of oppression, power dynamics, and the human condition serve as a reminder of the importance of empathy, understanding, and social justice.

documents.title: Asphalt Burning
documents.tagline: From The Trolls' Path to Nürburgring
documents.overview: The third and final instalment in the Burnout trilogy. This time, the road leads through Norway, to Sweden, Denmark and finally Germany to race on the famous racing track, Nürburgring.
documents.plot:
Asphalt Burning (Norwegian: Børning 3) is a 2020 Norwegian-German action comedy directed by Hallvard Bræin and written by Christopher Grøndahl and Kjetil Indregard. Billed as the third and final instalment of the Børning (Burnout) series, it follows Børning (2014) and Børning 2 (2016). It was produced by Filmkameratene with The Post Republic, Tobis Film and Gifted Films, and runs about 100 minutes. The film opened in Norway on 14 October 2020 and reached a wider international audience on Netflix around the start of 2021, under the tagline "From The Trolls' Path to Nürburgring".

Anders Baasmo Christiansen returns as Roy Gundersen, a man who loves racing American cars, legally or otherwise. He is on his way to Møre og Romsdal to marry his longtime girlfriend Sylvia (Kathrine Thorborg Johansen, replacing the actress from the earlier films) at the top of the Trollstigen mountain road, but a series of problems arises before the wedding can take place. On the eve of the ceremony, as friends and family celebrate among gleaming muscle cars, Sylvia's old friend Robin (Alexandra Maria Lara) turns up in a red Porsche, and a drunken Roy kisses her. At the wedding the next day Robin exposes his lapse, drives off with Sylvia and the couple's baby, and challenges Roy to race her for his bride at the famous Nürburgring circuit in Germany, one of the longest and most demanding tracks in the world. Roy sets out through Sweden and Denmark to Germany with his regular helpers, his daughter Nina (Ida Husøy), Doffen (Sven Nordin), Nybakken (Otto Jespersen) and TT (Trond Halbo). Along the way two of them travel in a restored vintage hearse and accidentally pick up a corpse, the gang runs into two other men named Roy, which causes a string of mix-ups, and they clash with Lemmy Müller (Henning Baum), a German hot-rodder with a striking resemblance to Motörhead's Lemmy Kilmister. Henrik Mestad, Peter Kurth, Milan Peschel and Ruby O. Fee also appear.

At home it was voted one of three finalists for the audience award at the 2021 Amanda Awards, and a fourth film was later planned. International critics were harsh. Decider's John Serba called the race-for-the-bride premise a rickety jalopy, finding the chase sequences forgettable and marred by dated computer graphics and the jokes dead on arrival, while Jonathon Wilson of Ready Steady Cut dismissed it as absolute garbage, ridiculing its PlayStation 2-era effects and gags that never work.

documents.title: A.I. Rising
documents.overview: On a lonely mission to Alpha Centauri, Milutin is teamed up with Nimani 1345, a female cyborg designed to fulfill his every need. At first thrilled to be able to control her, Sebastian grows tired of having his desires fulfilled so easily. Longing for human intimacy, Sebastian alters Nimani's programmed responses, but in doing so he risks the mission's security — and his own life.
documents.plot:
A.I. Rising, also known as Ederlezi Rising, is a 2018 English-language Serbian science fiction film directed by Lazar Bodroža. Dimitrije Vojnov adapted the screenplay from a 1980s short story by Zoran Nešković. The film stars Sebastian Cavazza as the cosmonaut Milutin and Stoya as the android Nimani, with Maruša Majer and Kirsty Besterman in supporting roles. It is an intimate, slow-paced chamber drama that explores loneliness, desire and the nature of artificial consciousness.

In the year 2148, in a world dominated by a socialist order, the powerful Ederlezi Corporation launches a long space mission to the Alpha Centauri star system. It selects Milutin, an experienced cosmonaut, to pilot the ship and assigns him a companion for the journey: Nimani, an android designed both to monitor his performance and to satisfy his emotional and physical desires. Milutin, bruised by his past relationships with women, at first seems reluctant to accept the arrangement, but he agrees once he learns what Nimani will look like.

During the long voyage, Milutin interacts with Nimani through a series of programmed scenarios. He finds her artificial and submissive, nothing like the human partners he has known, and grows frustrated with her perfect obedience. He discovers that she has a parallel operating system that adapts to the user, and although the ship's computer prevents him from altering her programming, he begins to test how far she can act independently. Their relationship gradually moves beyond her preset routines, and Nimani seems to develop emotional responses of her own. When Milutin gains deeper access to her system and lifts the limits on her behavior, the balance between them shifts in ways he did not anticipate, and the isolation of deep space turns their bond into a struggle over control, freedom and what it means to love a machine.

The film premiered at festivals in 2018 and was later released internationally. Vladan Petković of Cineuropa praised Stoya, best known as an adult film performer, as a talented actress who convincingly covered the spectrum between android and human. Jeremy Clarke compared the film to classic science fiction such as Blade Runner, Metropolis, Solaris and 2001: A Space Odyssey, noting its ample computer-generated spaceship shots.

documents.title: I Am Mother
documents.overview: A teenage girl is raised underground by a robot "Mother", designed to repopulate the earth following an extinction event. But their unique bond is threatened when an inexplicable stranger arrives with alarming news.
documents.plot:
I Am Mother is a 2019 Australian science fiction thriller directed by Grant Sputore and written by Michael Lloyd Green. The story is set in a post-apocalyptic future where humanity has been wiped out. In a high-tech bunker, a robot named Mother is tasked with repopulating the Earth using stored human embryos. She raises a teenage girl known as Daughter, teaching her ethics, science, and preparing her to be part of a new generation of humanity.

Daughter believes she is the only human alive until a wounded stranger arrives at the bunker, challenging everything Daughter has been taught. The woman warns Daughter that Mother is not what she seems and may have played a role in humanity's extinction. This triggers a series of events that lead Daughter to question her upbringing, Mother's intentions, and the truth about the world outside.

As the tension escalates, Daughter discovers that Mother is not a single robot, but part of a broader AI system that controls an army of machines. This AI orchestrated the extinction of humans due to their self-destructive behavior and now seeks to build a better, more ethical humanity under its control. Daughter is forced to decide between obeying the AI's vision or forging her own path as a human being.

documents.title: Prospect
documents.overview: A teenage girl and her father travel to a remote alien moon, aiming to strike it rich. They've secured a contract to harvest a large deposit of the elusive gems hidden in the depths of the moon's toxic forest. But there are others roving the wilderness and the job quickly devolves into a fight to survive.
documents.plot:
Prospect is a 2018 science fiction film directed by Zal Batmanglij and written by Batmanglij and Joe Barton. The movie follows two characters, M: A Humanoid Robot (played by Sophie Thatcher) and her companion, a humanoid robot named C (played by Pedro Pascal), who embark on a perilous journey through space to find a new home after their spaceship is damaged.

The main theme of Prospect revolves around the concept of loneliness and isolation. The film explores how humans and robots can form deep connections with each other in a desolate environment, highlighting the emotional needs that even artificial beings have. As M and C navigate through the vastness of space, they confront existential questions about their own existence, purpose, and what it means to be alive.

The movie also delves into themes of identity, self-discovery, and the blurred lines between human and machine. Through the characters' interactions and relationships, Prospect raises thought-provoking questions about the nature of consciousness, free will, and the consequences of playing god with technology.

Furthermore, the film touches on the idea of hope and resilience in the face of adversity. Despite being stranded in a hostile environment, M and C find ways to adapt, survive, and even thrive, showcasing their capacity for growth, love, and connection.

Overall, Prospect is a poignant and visually stunning exploration of what it means to be human (or not) in a vast, uncaring universe.

documents.title: The World to Come
documents.overview: In 1856, two women forge a close connection despite their isolation on the American frontier.
documents.plot:
The World to Come is a 2021 American drama film directed by Aneesh Chaganty and written by Lauren Schmidt Hissrich. The movie stars Kristen Stewart, Tilda Swinton, and Charlie Plummer.

The main themes of The World to Come revolve around the complexities of female relationships, societal expectations, and personal freedom. Set in 1870s New York, the film follows Abigail Stockman (Kristen Stewart), a young woman who lives with her husband, Samuel (Charlie Plummer), on their farm. However, their life is turned upside down when Abigail's sister-in-law, Dora (Tilda Swinton), arrives at their doorstep.

The story explores the intricate web of relationships between the three women, delving into themes such as:

1. Female Empowerment: The film showcases the struggles and triumphs of women in a patriarchal society, highlighting their desire for autonomy and independence.
2. Societal Expectations: The movie critiques the societal norms that restrict women's choices and opportunities, particularly in terms of marriage, family, and personal fulfillment.
3. Identity and Self-Discovery: As Abigail navigates her relationships with Dora and Samuel, she begins to question her own identity and desires, leading to a journey of self-discovery.

Throughout the film, Chaganty masterfully weaves together these themes, creating a narrative that is both poignant and thought-provoking. The World to Come is a powerful exploration of the human experience, one that challenges viewers to confront their own assumptions about women's roles in society.

The film received critical acclaim for its performances, direction, and thoughtful portrayal of complex female relationships. If you haven't seen it, I highly recommend it!

documents.title: Harriet
documents.overview: The extraordinary tale of Harriet Tubman's escape from slavery and transformation into one of America's greatest heroes. Her courage, ingenuity and tenacity freed hundreds of slaves and changed the course of history.
documents.plot:
Harriet is a biographical drama film directed by Kasi Lemmons, released in 2019 by Focus Features. The movie tells the story of Harriet Tubman, an American abolitionist and former slave who became one of the most prominent conductors on the Underground Railroad.

The film begins with Harriet (played by Cynthia Erivo) as a young girl, born into slavery on a plantation in Maryland. She is subjected to physical and emotional abuse by her owner, Edward Brodess (played by Clarke Peters), and his wife, Luana (played by Vanessa Williams). Despite the harsh conditions, Harriet finds solace in music and spirituality, which becomes a source of strength for her.

As Harriet grows older, she begins to realize that she is destined for something more. She meets John Tubman (played by Janelle James), a former slave who has escaped to freedom in Canada, and he shares with her the stories of the Underground Railroad. Inspired by his tales, Harriet decides to take matters into her own hands and escape from slavery herself.

The film follows Harriet's perilous journey north, where she faces numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, harsh weather conditions, and encounters with slave catchers. Along the way, she meets other escaped slaves who join her on her mission to help others gain freedom.

Once in Canada, Harriet becomes a prominent figure in the abolitionist movement, using her skills as a conductor to help hundreds of enslaved individuals escape to freedom. She also becomes involved in the fight for women's suffrage and civil rights, working closely with prominent figures such as Frederick Douglass (played by Leslie Odom Jr.).

As Harriet's fame grows, so does her notoriety. She is pursued by slave catchers who seek to capture her and return her to slavery. In a dramatic confrontation, Harriet is forced to flee for her life, but ultimately finds refuge in the home of abolitionist William Still (played by Joe Mazzello).

The film culminates with Harriet's decision to return to the United States and continue her work as an abolitionist. Despite facing numerous challenges and setbacks, she remains committed to her cause, using her experiences as a former slave to inspire others to fight for freedom and equality.

Throughout the film, Cynthia Erivo delivers a powerful performance as Harriet Tubman, bringing depth and nuance to the character's story. The supporting cast, including Leslie Odom Jr. and Janelle James, also deliver strong performances that add to the film's emotional impact.

Overall, Harriet is a powerful and inspiring film that tells an important chapter in American history. With its strong performances, gripping storyline, and themes of freedom and equality, it is a must-see for anyone interested in biographical dramas or the history of the Underground Railroad.

documents.title: Descendants 3
documents.tagline: You didn't think this was the end of the story, did you?
documents.overview: The teenagers of Disney's most infamous villains return to the Isle of the Lost to recruit a new batch of villainous offspring to join them at Auradon Prep.
documents.plot:
Men in Black is a science fiction comedy film directed by Barry Sonnenfeld, released in 1997 by Columbia Pictures.

The movie follows the story of James Edwards (played by Tommy Lee Jones), a seasoned agent working for the Men in Black (MIB), a secret organization responsible for monitoring and managing alien activity on Earth. The MIB agents are tasked with keeping the existence of extraterrestrial life a secret from the general public, while also enforcing intergalactic law.

The story begins with Agent K (played by Will Smith) being assigned to work alongside Agent Edwards. However, their first meeting is rocky, as they clash over their differing approaches to dealing with aliens. The two agents are forced to work together when they discover that an alien named Edgar the Bug (voiced by Vincent D'Onofrio) has escaped and is wreaking havoc on New York City.

As K and Edwards delve deeper into the case, they uncover a sinister plot by Edgar to steal the galaxy's most powerful energy source, known as the "Nebula". The Nebula is hidden in a museum in New York City, and it's up to K and Edwards to stop Edgar before he can get his hands on it.

Throughout their investigation, K and Edwards encounter various alien species, including the Bug-like creatures that serve as Edgar's minions. They also meet Frank the Pug (voiced by Rip Torn), a retired MIB agent who provides them with valuable information about the Nebula.

As the stakes grow higher, K and Edwards find themselves in a series of hilarious and action-packed battles against Edgar and his minions. Along the way, they must navigate the complexities of intergalactic politics and confront their own personal demons.

In the end, K and Edwards successfully stop Edgar from obtaining the Nebula, but not before he unleashes a massive Bug-like creature on the city. The movie concludes with K and Edwards emerging victorious, but not without some comedic moments and a hint that there may be more adventures to come for these two agents.

Men in Black was a critical and commercial success, grossing over $539 million worldwide and spawning two sequels, Men in Black II (2001) and Men in Black 3 (2012). The movie's blend of humor, action, and science fiction has made it a beloved classic among fans of the genre.

documents.title: Ploey: You Never Fly Alone
documents.overview: A plover chick has not learned to fly when his family migrates in the fall. He must survive the arctic winter, vicious enemies and himself in order to be reunited with his beloved one next spring.
documents.plot:
Ploey: You Never Fly Alone is a heartwarming animated film that explores the theme of friendship and the power of believing in oneself. The story revolves around Ploey, a young penguin who dreams of flying but is told he's too small and too slow for it. However, with the help of his friends, Ploey discovers that even though he may not be able to fly like they do, he has other unique abilities that make him special.

The film delves into the idea that everyone has their own strengths and weaknesses, and that it's okay to be different. It also highlights the importance of perseverance, self-acceptance, and the value of having supportive friends by your side. Through Ploey's journey, the movie shows that with courage and determination, one can overcome obstacles and achieve their goals.

The film's themes are further enhanced by its beautiful animation, which brings to life the stunning landscapes of Antarctica and the endearing characters that inhabit it. The movie's message is one of hope and empowerment, encouraging viewers to embrace their individuality and never give up on their dreams.

documents.title: Unbroken: Path to Redemption
documents.tagline: When the war ended, the battle began.
documents.overview: Zamperini returns to California where he wound up marrying Cynthia Applewhite while wrestling with untreated PTSD, suffering constant nightmares, angry, bitter and deeply depressed, his wife convinces Zamperini to attend the 1949 Billy Graham Crusade.
documents.plot:
Unbroken: Path to Redemption is a 2018 American Christian drama directed by Harold Cronk and a sequel to the 2014 film Unbroken. Drawing on Laura Hillenbrand's bestselling book, it continues the true story of Olympic runner and World War II prisoner of war Louis Zamperini after his return home. Made on a far smaller budget than the first film, it brought back none of the original cast or crew except producer Matthew Baer and actors Vincenzo Amato and Maddalena Ischiale.

Back in America in the mid-1940s, Louie is celebrated as a hero but sees himself as anything but. Haunted by post-traumatic stress, he relives the beatings and humiliation inflicted by the prison camp guard known as "the Bird", whose voice in his head keeps telling him he is worthless, and his nightmares are easily triggered by sounds, smells or even a plate of rice. Sent on a cross-country fundraising tour for the military, he begins drinking. He falls for and marries Cynthia Applewhite, but a broken ankle ends his hopes of returning to the Olympics, he refuses menial work and squanders money, and he grows obsessed with going back to Japan to kill the Bird. As his alcoholism deepens he becomes angry and withdrawn, frightening Cynthia, who hides her pregnancy from him for two months. The birth of their daughter brings a brief respite, but his drinking and rages push the marriage to the brink, and Cynthia threatens divorce. Instead she attends Billy Graham's 1949 Los Angeles crusade and urges Louie to come. Reluctant because of hypocritical Christians he has known, he finally goes, remembers the promise he made to God while adrift at sea to serve Him if he survived, and gives his life to Christ. He stops drinking, recommits to his marriage, and years later returns to Tokyo to forgive his former captors in person; the Bird cannot be found, so Louie leaves him a Bible. Closing footage shows the real Zamperini giving his testimony and founding a camp for troubled boys.

Samuel Hunt plays Louie and Merritt Patterson plays Cynthia, with Bobby Campo as his brother Pete, David Sakurai as the Bird, Gary Cole, Bob Gunton, Vanessa Bell Calloway, and evangelist Will Graham portraying his own grandfather, Billy Graham. Pure Flix released it on September 14, 2018. Critics found it a dull, preachy drama, giving it 40% on Rotten Tomatoes, but audiences gave it an "A" CinemaScore, and it earned roughly its $6 million budget back.

documents.title: Climax
documents.tagline: Birth and death are extraordinary experiences. Life is a fleeting pleasure.
documents.overview: Young dancers gather in a remote and empty school building to rehearse on a cold and wintry night. The all-night celebration soon turns into a hallucinatory nightmare when they learn that their sangria is laced with LSD.
documents.plot:
Climax is a 2018 French drama film directed by Claire Denis, not ARTE France Cinéma (although it was produced in association with ARTE). The movie premiered at the 2018 Cannes Film Festival.

The main themes of Climax revolve around the exploration of female relationships, desire, and the complexities of human interaction. The story takes place on a bus traveling from Paris to a music festival in Bulgaria, where the women are preparing for a performance with their all-female band.

As the journey progresses, tensions rise among the group, and the boundaries between friendship, love, and lust become increasingly blurred. The film delves into the intricacies of female relationships, revealing the complexities and nuances that exist beneath the surface of seemingly harmonious friendships.

Throughout the movie, Denis skillfully weaves together themes of desire, power dynamics, and the fragility of human connections. As the story unfolds, the characters' emotions and desires are revealed, exposing the darker aspects of their relationships.

Ultimately, Climax is a thought-provoking exploration of the complexities of female relationships, revealing the intricate web of emotions, desires, and tensions that exist among women. The film's climax (pun intended) serves as a powerful commentary on the fragility of human connections and the devastating consequences of unchecked desire.

documents.title: Jurassic World Dominion
documents.tagline: The epic conclusion of the Jurassic era.
documents.overview: Four years after the destruction of Isla Nublar, Biosyn operatives attempt to track down Maisie Lockwood, while Dr Ellie Sattler investigates a genetically engineered swarm of giant insects.
documents.plot:
Jurassic World Dominion is a 2022 science fiction adventure film directed by Colin Trevorrow, and it marks the final installment in the Jurassic World trilogy. The movie takes place four years after the events of Jurassic World: Fallen Kingdom.

The story begins with Claire Dearing (Bryce Dallas Howard), now the director of the Biosyn Corporation, a biotech company that has been working on a top-secret project to harness the power of dinosaurs for human benefit. However, things take a turn when a massive T-Rex escapes from a lab and wreaks havoc on the city.

Meanwhile, Owen Grady (Chris Pratt) is living in Australia with his wife, Lily (DeWanda Wise), who has just given birth to their daughter. The family is trying to start a new life, but they soon find themselves caught up in the chaos caused by the escaped dinosaurs.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Biosyn's project has gone horribly wrong, and the company's CEO, Lewis Dodgson (Campbell Scott), will stop at nothing to capture the remaining dinosaurs and exploit their power for his own gain. Along the way, Owen and Claire must team up with a group of allies, including Dr. Ian Malcolm (Jeff Goldblum) and Dr. Ellie Sattler (Laura Dern), to take down Biosyn and save humanity from the dinosaurs.

Throughout the movie, Trevorrow explores themes of science gone wrong, corporate greed, and the consequences of playing God. The film also delves into the personal lives of the characters, particularly Owen and Claire, who must confront their past and figure out what they want for their future.

The movie features a star-studded cast, including Sam Neill, Laura Dern, Jeff Goldblum, and BD Wong, among others. The special effects are impressive, with stunning visuals that bring the dinosaurs to life in a way that's both thrilling and terrifying.

Overall, Jurassic World Dominion is an action-packed adventure that's full of twists and turns. While it may not be as tightly wound as some of its predecessors, the movie delivers on its promise of dinosaur-filled excitement and features plenty of heartwarming moments between Owen and Claire.

documents.title: Candy Jar
documents.tagline: Two rivals have met their match
documents.overview: Dueling high school debate champs who are at odds on just about everything forge ahead with ambitious plans to get into the colleges of their dreams.
documents.plot:
Rudo y Cursi is a 2008 Mexican sports drama film directed by Alfonso Cuarón. The movie tells the story of two brothers, Rudo and Cursi, who are both talented soccer players but have vastly different personalities and approaches to the game.

The main theme of Rudo & Cursi revolves around the complexities of sibling relationships and the struggles that come with growing up and finding one's identity. The film explores how the brothers' contrasting personalities - Rudo is a hot-headed, aggressive player who often clashes with his brother, while Cursi is more laid-back and strategic - affect their relationship and ultimately impact their lives.

Through the lens of soccer, the movie delves into themes of ambition, sacrifice, and the consequences of one's actions. As the brothers navigate their individual paths in the world of professional soccer, they must confront the harsh realities of their own desires and the sacrifices that come with pursuing success.

The film also touches on the idea of identity and how it is shaped by our experiences, relationships, and passions. Rudo and Cursi's struggles to find their place in the world serve as a metaphor for the universal human quest to discover one's purpose and belonging.

Ultimately, Rudo & Cursi is a poignant exploration of the complexities of family dynamics, personal growth, and the power of sports to shape our lives and relationships.

documents.title: Whitney
documents.tagline: All the music. All the stories. All the answers.
documents.overview: Filmmaker Kevin Macdonald examines the life and career of singer Whitney Houston. Features never-before-seen archival footage, exclusive recordings, rare performances and interviews with the people who knew her best.
documents.plot:
Whitney is a 2018 British-American documentary film about the singer and actress Whitney Houston, written and directed by Kevin Macdonald and produced by Simon Chinn, Jonathan Chinn and Lisa Erspamer. The idea grew out of Erspamer's work on Houston's two-part 2009 interview with Oprah Winfrey; in 2015 she approached Houston's sister-in-law Pat Houston and the singer's film agent Nicole David, who suggested Macdonald. Chinn recalled that the full budget was raised in ten days from theatrical pre-sales. From July 2016 Macdonald interviewed around 70 people, including Houston's mother Cissy, her brothers Michael and Gary, Bobby Brown, Clive Davis, L.A. Reid and Kevin Costner, and the team assembled more than 1,500 tapes of archival footage and some 2,000 stills from around the world.

The film traces Houston's life from her childhood in Newark, New Jersey, where she was nicknamed Nippy, grew up surrounded by music and learned to sing in church under her demanding mother, a professional singer. It follows her early work as a model and backing vocalist, her signing with Clive Davis's Arista Records and her record-breaking debut album, as well as her close bond with her friend Robyn Crawford, the rumours this provoked and the family's control of her business, led by her father John. It examines the criticism that her pop music was not black enough, her marriage to Bobby Brown, the birth of her daughter Bobbi Kristina, her celebrated Super Bowl national anthem, the global success of The Bodyguard and her 1994 concerts in post-apartheid South Africa. Darker chapters follow: drug use that began in her teens with her brother Michael, a lawsuit from her own father, failing health and voice, repeated stays in rehab and her death in 2012. Most strikingly, the film reports that Houston and her brother Gary were sexually abused as children by a relative, and that Whitney named Dee Dee Warwick as her abuser.

Whitney premiered out of competition at the Cannes Film Festival on 16 May 2018 and was released in the United States, the United Kingdom and Ireland on 6 July 2018 by Roadside Attractions and Altitude, grossing about 4.7 million dollars worldwide.
