Free Solo is a documentary film that follows Alex Honnold's attempt to climb El Capitan in Yosemite National Park without any ropes or safety gear. The movie delves into the psychological and emotional aspects of risk-taking, obsession, and the pursuit of perfection.

At its core, Free Solo explores the theme of self-discovery and the human need for challenge and adventure. Alex Honnold's character is driven by an insatiable desire to push himself to the limits of human endurance, and his journey is as much about understanding himself as it is about conquering a physical obstacle.

The film also touches on the idea of obsession and the blurred lines between passion and madness. Honnold's fixation on El Capitan becomes all-consuming, leading him to take extreme risks that put not only himself but also those around him in danger.

Furthermore, Free Solo highlights the importance of mental preparation and emotional resilience in overcoming fear and adversity. Honnold's character is shown to be deeply introspective and self-aware, using meditation and other mindfulness practices to calm his nerves and focus his mind.

Ultimately, the movie presents a nuanced exploration of the human condition, one that celebrates the beauty of risk-taking and the power of the human spirit while also acknowledging the dangers and uncertainties that come with it.

documents.title: Honey: Rise Up and Dance
documents.overview: Street dancer Skyler comes out of the shadow of her trained dancer sister, Tosha, & joins a dance competition with the Honey dance studio; the prize is a college scholarship.
documents.plot:
Honey: Rise Up and Dance is a 2018 American dance drama film directed by Bille Woodruff from a screenplay by Robert Adetuyi and produced by Mike Elliott. Made by Universal 1440 Entertainment with Soundtrack New York and released directly to home video by Universal Pictures Home Entertainment, it is the fourth installment of the Honey franchise, following Honey (2003), Honey 2 (2011) and Honey 3 (2016). Like its predecessors, it introduces new characters and is tied to the earlier films mainly through the Honey Daniels dance studio and its focus on hip-hop dance. Teyana Taylor leads the cast as Skyler, with Bryshere Y. Gray as Tyrell, Sierra McClain as her sister Tosha, Charmin Lee as the coach Jada, Kwajalyn Brown as her mother April, and Candice Craig, Joel Rush and Brya Wood in supporting roles.

Skyler is a talented but untrained street dancer who has long lived in the shadow of her formally trained sister Tosha, whom the family regards as the real dancer. Her hardworking mother dismisses her passion and pushes her to enroll in medical assistant school instead. When Skyler learns of a dance competition whose winner will receive a full college scholarship, she decides to chase her dream regardless of her family's doubts. She tries out for the same crew as her sister, one of the city's two leading hip-hop teams, the Pulsars, run by the demanding Jada, where she is a long shot surrounded by established performers, including a rival determined to sabotage anyone in her path. Because each team may send only one member to compete for the scholarship, Skyler practices relentlessly in the underground dance scene. There she meets Tyrell, Jada's estranged son and a gifted dancer, and his encouragement helps her push her style to another level and overcome her persistent self-doubt, while her mother eventually comes to recognize what she had underestimated in her daughter.

The film was released on DVD and digital platforms in the United States on 3 April 2018. Elvin Ross composed the music, and the film is rated PG-13 for suggestive content and some language. Reviews were mixed: critics generally praised the energetic choreography and Taylor's presence while faulting the predictable story and uneven acting. Common Sense Media's Renee Longstreet noted that the dancing stays at the center of the film, calling that both its strength and its weakness, and observed that the franchise's enthusiastic fan base seems undeterred by thin plots.

documents.title: Yesterday
documents.tagline: Everyone in the world has forgotten The Beatles. Everyone except Jack…
documents.overview: Jack Malik is a struggling singer-songwriter in an English seaside town whose dreams of fame are rapidly fading, despite the fierce devotion and support of his childhood best friend, Ellie. After a freak bus accident during a mysterious global blackout, Jack wakes up to discover that he's the only person on Earth who can remember The Beatles.
documents.plot:
Yesterday is a 2019 British romantic comedy film directed by Danny Boyle and written by Richard Curtis. The movie stars Himesh Patel as Jack Malik, a struggling singer-songwriter who becomes an overnight sensation after a mysterious event wipes out the music of The Beatles from the face of the earth.

The story begins with Jack, a talented but unknown musician, performing at a pub in London. He is discovered by a record label executive, and his life changes overnight when he stumbles upon a mysterious portal that transports him to a world where The Beatles never existed. As a result, all their music has been erased from the planet.

With this newfound knowledge, Jack becomes an instant sensation as the only person who knows The Beatles' songs. He starts performing their hits, and his popularity skyrockets. However, he soon realizes that he must keep the secret of The Beatles' non-existence to himself, as the world would be shocked if they knew that one person had access to their music.

As Jack navigates his newfound fame, he meets a musician named Ellie (played by Lily James), who becomes his love interest. Despite their instant attraction, Jack struggles to open up about his past and his feelings for Ellie. Meanwhile, a journalist named Sam (played by Ed Sheeran) is investigating the sudden rise of Jack's music career.

As the story unfolds, Jack must confront the consequences of his newfound fame and the pressure it puts on him. He also has to deal with the fact that he is now responsible for keeping The Beatles' legacy alive, even if they never existed in the first place.

Throughout the movie, Boyle uses a mix of humor, music, and heart to tell Jack's story. The film features many iconic Beatles songs, which are performed by Patel in a remarkable display of vocal talent. The movie also explores themes of identity, creativity, and the power of music to bring people together.

In the end, Jack must make a choice between his newfound fame and his relationship with Ellie. He decides to use his platform to help others, including a struggling musician who is trying to make it big. As the story concludes, Jack finds happiness and fulfillment in his life, both personally and creatively.

Overall, Yesterday is a heartwarming and entertaining film that celebrates the power of music and creativity. With its talented cast, witty script, and memorable performances, it's a must-see for fans of romantic comedies and music lovers alike.

documents.title: Someone Great
documents.overview: An aspiring music journalist lands her dream job and is about to move to San Francisco when her boyfriend of nine years decides to call it quits. To nurse her broken heart, she and her two best friends spend one outrageous last adventure in New York City.
documents.plot:
Someone Great is a 2019 American romantic comedy-drama film that explores the complexities of female friendships and the journey towards self-discovery. The movie delves into the theme of finding one's identity and purpose in life, particularly during the transition from adolescence to adulthood.

The story revolves around the character of Samantha (played by Gina Rodriguez), who is struggling to come to terms with her own desires and aspirations after a painful breakup. As she navigates this period of self-discovery, she finds solace in her friendships with her two closest friends, Sutton (Jaz Sinclair) and Julie (DeWanda Wise).

Through the lens of these female relationships, the film sheds light on the intricacies of female bonding, loyalty, and support. The movie highlights how women often find strength in each other's company, particularly during times of vulnerability and uncertainty.

The main theme of Someone Great is also centered around the idea of embracing change and taking risks to pursue one's dreams. Samantha's journey is a metaphor for the struggles many young adults face as they try to figure out their place in the world. The film encourages viewers to be open-minded, take chances, and trust themselves as they navigate the complexities of life.

Ultimately, Someone Great is a heartwarming and relatable exploration of female friendships, self-discovery, and the power of embracing one's true identity.

documents.title: Amateur
documents.overview: 14-year-old basketball phenom Terron Forte has to navigate the under-the-table world of amateur athletics when he is recruited to an elite NCAA prep school.
documents.plot:
Amateur is a 2018 American sports drama film written and directed by Ryan Koo, produced with Mandalay Pictures and released on Netflix on 6 April 2018 under the tagline "Every dream has a price". The project began in 2011 as a crowdfunded film called Manchild; a short prequel was released in 2013 under the name Amateur, the feature adopted that title in November 2014, and in January 2016 Netflix acquired the rights to finance and distribute it. It stars Michael Rainey Jr., Josh Charles, Sharon Leal and Brian J. White, with cinematography by Gregory J. Wilson, and runs about 96 minutes.

Terron Forte (Rainey) is a 14-year-old basketball phenom playing on a struggling school team. He is also burdened with a learning disability, dyscalculia, or number blindness: algebra is a mystery to him and he cannot read the scoreboard or the clock, an affliction the film visualises through the garbled numbers only he sees, though he is smart enough to find workarounds, with coaches counting down the shot clock for him. His father Vince (White), a former football player who never made it, suffers the effects of too many concussions, while his mother Nia (Leal), a teacher, values academics and wants him to earn a degree in case basketball does not work out. When the smooth-talking Coach Gaines (Charles) recruits him to the out-of-state Liberty Prep, an elite NCAA prep programme, with the dream of NBA millions, Terron jumps at the chance. The glamour soon fades: the players do not really attend the prestigious school, but are crammed into a rundown house, given loaner bicycles and overwhelmed by workouts, while teammates tell him his classes and grades are taken care of. As he settles in at point guard and records everything on his phone, Terron discovers the competing agendas around him, from academic fraud and pay-for-play to the sneaker brands, as one teammate (Ashlee Brian) puts it, whom the players really serve, and his father's best intentions become another burden.

Critics praised the film's look at the hidden machinery of amateur athletics. Dan Mecca of The Film Stage gave it a B, finding Rainey's performance tender and commending Koo's sure handling of moral grey areas, while Decider compared it to the early-1990s scandal films The Program and Blue Chips. Roger Moore of Movie Nation admired Charles and White but felt that by indicting the system rather than a single villain the film goes soft in its third act.

documents.title: Come True
documents.overview: Looking for an escape from her recurring nightmares, 18-year-old Sarah submits to a university sleep study, but soon realizes she's become the conduit to a frightening new discovery.
documents.plot:
Come True is a 2020 Canadian drama film directed by Tamara Koteas. The movie revolves around a young woman who embarks on a journey to find her missing sister, which leads her to confront her own dark past and the complexities of human relationships.

The main theme of Come True is the exploration of trauma, grief, and the long-lasting impact it has on individuals and their loved ones. Through the protagonist's search for her sister, the film delves into the emotional scars that can be left behind by traumatic experiences and how they shape our perceptions of ourselves and others.

Another significant theme present in Come True is the fragility of human connections and the ways in which they can be both a source of comfort and a catalyst for pain. The protagonist's relationships with her family members, particularly her sister, are central to the narrative, highlighting the intricate web of emotions that can bind people together while also causing them harm.

The film also touches on the idea of identity and how it is shaped by our experiences, both positive and negative. As the protagonist navigates her past and present, she is forced to confront aspects of herself that she had previously suppressed or denied, leading to a deeper understanding of who she is and where she comes from.

Overall, Come True is a poignant and thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, tackling complex themes with sensitivity and nuance.

documents.title: StarDog and TurboCat
documents.overview: When vigilante cat, Felix, and loyal canine, Buddy, set out to find Buddy’s lost owner, they discover not only the power of friendship, but their inner superpowers along the way.
documents.plot:
StarDog and TurboCat is a 2019 animated adventure comedy film directed by Ben Stassen and produced by Head Gear Films.

The movie follows the story of two unlikely friends, StarDog, an American police dog, and TurboCat, a street-smart feline from New York City. The duo team up to solve a mystery involving a stolen treasure that could bring peace between their respective cities.

Some of the main themes present in the film include:

1. Friendship: The bond between StarDog and TurboCat serves as the foundation for the story, showcasing how two different species can put aside their differences and work together towards a common goal.
2. Cultural Exchange: The movie highlights the cultural differences between America and New York City, promoting understanding and appreciation for diverse backgrounds.
3. Teamwork: Throughout the adventure, StarDog and TurboCat demonstrate the importance of collaboration, using their unique skills to overcome obstacles and solve puzzles.
4. Loyalty: Both characters are fiercely loyal to each other and their respective cities, driving them to protect their homes and communities from harm.

The film's lighthearted tone and comedic moments make it an entertaining watch for both children and adults, while its themes of friendship, cultural exchange, teamwork, and loyalty provide valuable lessons for viewers of all ages.

documents.title: Antlers
documents.overview: A small-town Oregon teacher and her brother, the local sheriff, discover a young student is harbouring a dangerous secret that could have frightening consequences.
documents.plot:
Antlers is a 2021 supernatural horror film directed by Scott Cooper, who co-wrote it with Henry Chaisson and Nick Antosca, adapted from Antosca's short story "The Quiet Boy". Keri Russell stars as a teacher, with Jesse Plemons as her brother, Jeremy T. Thomas as the troubled boy at the centre of the story, and Graham Greene, Scott Haze, Rory Cochrane and Amy Madigan. Produced by Guillermo del Toro and shot in British Columbia in 2018, it was delayed by the COVID-19 pandemic and released in October 2021.

In the depressed Oregon town of Cispus Falls, Frank Weaver cooks methamphetamine in an abandoned mine. While his young son Aiden waits in the truck, Frank and a partner are attacked by something in the dark. Weeks later, twelve-year-old Lucas Weaver wanders the town collecting roadkill and small animals. His teacher, Julia Meadows, who has returned to town to live with her brother Paul, the local sheriff, after their abusive father's death, is disturbed by Lucas's macabre drawings and stories and becomes convinced that he is being abused.

In fact Lucas is feeding his father and brother, whom he keeps locked in the attic on Frank's own orders, after Frank came home infected and began changing into something monstrous. The former sheriff Warren Stokes discovers mutilated remains in the woods and the mine. When the school principal, Ellen, visits the house at Julia's urging and opens the locked room, Frank kills her and completes his transformation into an antlered creature, then kills a boy who has been bullying Lucas. Lucas is found starved and dehydrated and is hospitalised, and Julia takes him under her care.

Shown Lucas's drawings, Warren recognises a wendigo, a spirit from Indigenous legend that turns its host into a ravenous beast and passes from one victim to another, and explains that it can only be destroyed through its heart while it feeds. The creature kills Paul's deputy and badly wounds Paul. Lucas runs to the mine to rejoin his brother, and Julia follows. She finds the monster feeding on a bear and, with Lucas's help, kills it, then is forced to kill Aiden when the spirit passes into him. Later, as Julia leaves with Lucas, Paul begins coughing up black fluid, as Frank had done.

Antlers grossed about 35.7 million dollars worldwide and received mixed reviews, critics admiring its atmosphere and performances more than its story.

documents.title: The Empty Man
documents.tagline: The first night you hear him. The second night you see him. The third night he finds you.
documents.overview: Retired cop James Lasombra is asked by a friend to investigate the disappearance of her daughter, who seemingly packed in the night and left an ominous message on the bathroom mirror - "The Empty Man Made Me Do It." As he investigates this mysterious figure further, James begins to see and hear strange things, and is forced to come to terms with his past and what it means for his future.
documents.plot:
The Empty Man is a 2020 American supernatural horror film directed by David Prior and written by C. Robert Cargill. The movie follows the story of James Lasombra, a former FBI agent who is investigating a series of bizarre occurrences in a small town.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the main theme of the movie revolves around the concept of identity and the blurring of lines between reality and madness. The protagonist, James Lasombra, is a complex character whose past is shrouded in mystery, and as he delves deeper into the mystery, his own sanity begins to unravel.

The film also explores the idea of possession and the supernatural, as James encounters a mysterious figure known as "The Empty Man," who seems to be manipulating events from behind the scenes. The Empty Man is a symbol of the void or the abyss, representing the unknown and the unknowable.

Throughout the movie, the themes of identity, reality, and madness are intertwined, creating a sense of unease and uncertainty in the viewer. The film's use of atmospheric tension and unsettling visuals adds to the overall sense of unease, making it difficult for the protagonist (and the audience) to distinguish between what is real and what is just a product of his own paranoia.

Ultimately, the movie builds towards a climactic confrontation between James and the Empty Man, which serves as a metaphor for the struggle to maintain one's identity in the face of overwhelming uncertainty. The ending is intentionally ambiguous, leaving the viewer to ponder the nature of reality and the true meaning of the Empty Man.

Overall, The Empty Man is a thought-provoking horror film that explores complex themes and ideas, making it a compelling watch for fans of supernatural horror.

documents.title: Break
documents.overview: The company of three guys and two girls makes their way to the old funicular to have an unforgettable New Year’s Eve celebration at the top of the mountain. A fun adventure turns into a nightmare when the funicular stops over the abyss. Coldness, height and fear of a slow death make them reveal their true essence and get in a fight with each other.
documents.plot:
Break (Russian: Otryv) is a 2018 Russian survival thriller directed by Tigran Saakyan from a screenplay by Olga Rud, Saakyan and Denis Kosyakov. Produced by Sergei Selyanov, Artur Astvatsatryan and Oleg Yakovlev for the companies CTB and Attraction, it stars Irina Antonenko, a former Miss Russia, as Katya, Kosyakov as Denis Seleznyov, Ingrid Olerinskaya as Vika, Mikhail Filippov as Roman Mikalovich and Andrey Nazimov as Kirill. Sergei Dyshuk was the cinematographer and Aleksei Chintsov composed the score; the film runs 82 minutes.

On New Year's Eve, a group of five friends, three young men and two women, decide to celebrate at the top of a mountain for an unforgettable experience, and make their way to an old funicular. Things go wrong from the start: Katya's boyfriend Kirill suddenly refuses to board the cable car, while she refuses to get off, so the rest of the group rides up with her. The car stops unexpectedly, then starts moving again when the power returns, so when it halts a second time nobody thinks much of it and they begin celebrating the New Year right there. By the morning of 1 January, however, the car still has not moved, and they realize they are stuck high above an abyss with no way to call for help. At first they expect rescue to come, and they light a fire with whatever rubbish they can find to keep warm, but it soon dies out along with their hope. Cold, height and the fear of a slow death bring out their basest survival instincts. An attempt to climb down the cable ends when one of them falls into a crevice hidden beneath the snow, and as the remaining friends lose hope, a struggle for survival breaks out inside the car, revealing who they really are.

Break premiered at the Oktyabr cinema in Moscow on 12 February 2019 and opened in Russian cinemas two days later, earning about 7.5 million rubles in its first weekend and roughly 200,000 dollars in total. It drew accusations of plagiarism because of its similarity to Adam Green's 2010 American thriller Frozen. Reviewing it for Russo Rosso, Dmitry Sokolov nevertheless considered it a self-sufficient work rather than a pale copy, praising its well-constructed predicaments, its momentum, the performances of Antonenko and Filippov and the camerawork, but criticizing shifts in tone, a melodramatic final third and too many references to other films. Saakyan and Rud received a special prize at the Kaplya awards for their contribution to Russian genre cinema.

documents.title: Being the Ricardos
documents.tagline: A story behind one of the most influential shows of all time.
documents.overview: Lucille Ball and Desi Arnaz face a crisis that could end their careers and another that could end their marriage.
documents.plot:
Being the Ricardos is a 2021 biographical drama film that delves into the complex and tumultuous relationship between iconic American couple Lucille Ball and Desi Arnaz, as well as their portrayal of themselves in the classic sitcom I Love Lucy. The movie masterfully weaves together the intricacies of their personal lives, creative partnership, and the societal pressures they faced.

At its core, Being the Ricardos is a nuanced exploration of the blurred lines between reality and performance, particularly in the context of Hollywood's Golden Age. The film highlights how Lucille Ball and Desi Arnaz skillfully navigated the constraints of their roles as both on-screen partners and off-screen spouses, all while maintaining an illusion of domestic bliss for the public.

The movie also delves into the theme of identity and the performative nature of celebrity culture. As the Ricardos' personas became increasingly intertwined with those of Lucy and Ricky Ricardo, they found themselves struggling to maintain a sense of authenticity amidst the spotlight's glare. This tension is palpable throughout the film, as the couple grapples with the consequences of their carefully crafted image.

Furthermore, Being the Ricardos touches on the theme of feminism and the limited options available to women in the entertainment industry during that era. Lucille Ball's journey from a struggling actress to a successful producer and star is a testament to her determination and resilience in the face of patriarchal norms.

Ultimately, the film presents a rich tapestry of themes, love, and performance, all woven together by the intricate dance of two complex individuals navigating the highs and lows of fame, identity, and creative partnership.

documents.title: Balkan Line
documents.overview: After the NATO bombing of Yugoslavia in 1999, the Yugoslav army pulls out of Kosovo region, leaving Serbian people at the mercy of the Albanian UCK terrorists. A small band of soldiers must take over the Slatina airport, and hold it until the Russian peacekeepers arrive.
documents.plot:
The Balkan Line (Russian: Балканский рубеж, Balkanskiy rubezh) is a 2019 Russian-Serbian war action film directed by Andrey Volgin, a fictionalized account of the Russian special operation to seize Slatina airfield in Kosovo in June 1999, after the NATO bombing of Yugoslavia. Anton Pampushnyy stars as the disgraced special forces soldier Andrey Shatalov, with Gosha Kutsenko, who also produced, as his former commander "Bek" (modeled on Yunus-Bek Yevkurov), Milena Radulović as the doctor Jasna, Miloš Biković as the Serbian policeman Vuk, Gojko Mitić as police chief Goran Milić, Ravshana Kurkova as the sniper Vera and Aleksandar Srećković as the Albanian warlord Smuk. Emir Kusturica appears as a taxi driver.

In 1995, while serving with the international force in Bosnia, Shatalov throws a captured war criminal out of a helicopter in defiance of orders to release him, and his whole unit is dismissed and stranded in Yugoslavia. Four years later, as the bombing ends, a general in Moscow secretly orders Bek to take Slatina airport near Pristina and hold it until a column of Russian peacekeepers arrives from Bosnia, and Bek reassembles Shatalov's scattered team with the promise that they will be allowed home and rehabilitated.

Shatalov, living under a Serbian alias and working for Milić's police station, meets Jasna on a bus that is stopped by Smuk's gang. He takes Smuk hostage and forces the fighters to retreat, earning the warlord's undying hatred. Smuk then seizes the police station, kills Milić and takes dozens of Serbs hostage at the airfield, among them Jasna; most are murdered, and a Swiss doctor in league with Smuk, who is shown to be involved in organ harvesting, is also killed. When Bek's group occupies the airport, Shatalov, Vuk and an Albanian colleague, Fadil, join them, and through a long night the small band holds off more than a hundred attackers. Several of the team die, Vuk among them, until, with only a few bullets left, they hear Russian voices on the radio as the peacekeepers arrive ahead of NATO. Smuk is killed by Fadil, the team slips away, and months later Shatalov, who survived his wounds, reunites with Jasna in Belgrade.

Shot in Russia, Crimea and Serbia, the film was released on 21 March 2019 by 20th Century Fox CIS, days before the twentieth anniversary of the bombing.

documents.title: Cosmoball
documents.overview: Cosmoball is a mesmerizing intergalactic game of future played between humans and aliens at the giant extraterrestrial ship hovering in the sky over Earth. A young man with enormous power of an unknown nature joins the team of hot-headed superheroes in exchange for a cure for his mother’s deadly illness. The Four from Earth will fight not only to defend the honor of their home planet in the spectacular game, but to face the unprecedented threat to the Galaxy and embrace their own destiny.
documents.plot:
Cosmoball, also known as Goalkeeper of the Galaxy (Russian: Vratar Galaktiki), is a 2020 Russian 3D superhero space opera written and directed by Dzhanik Fayziev, based on the animated series Galactik Football. Yevgeny Romantsov stars as Anton, with Viktoriya Agalakova as Natasha, Maria Lisovaya as Anya, Ivan Ivanovich as Pele, Yelizaveta Taychenacheva as Fan and Yevgeny Mironov and Elena Yakovleva in supporting roles.

In 2071, galactic wars have destroyed the Moon and shifted Earth's poles, transforming the climate: Moscow lies in a tropical jungle, while New York is buried in ice. A gigantic alien spaceship hovers over Moscow and serves as the stadium for Cosmoball, an intergalactic sport combining football with gladiatorial combat. Only athletes with extraordinary powers can play, and they are worshipped like gods by spectators across the galaxy, because the outcome of each match decides the fate of entire worlds, including Earth.

Anton is an ordinary young man who grew up without a father and despises Cosmoball. To help his sick mother, he steals medicine from guarded pharmacies. While hiding from the police in the slums, he meets Anya, a shapeshifter who shares his hatred of the sport and pushes him toward rebellion. Everything changes when Anton is discovered to possess the hidden power of teleportation, which he does not yet know how to control, and he is recruited as goalkeeper of Earth's national team. His teammates include its determined captain, Natasha, the fast and powerful striker Pele, from a now snowy Brazil, and the tiny, elusive Fan. Unaware of the destiny awaiting him, Anton grows into the team's leader, and the final match becomes a battle for the future of the planet.

The leads were cast for their athletic backgrounds. Filming took place at Mosfilm in Moscow from June to September 2017, with motion capture and CGI creating over 50 digital characters. After several delays, it premiered in Moscow on August 25, 2020, becoming the first major Russian release after the COVID-19 lockdown. It earned only about 106.6 million rubles against a budget of roughly 786 million. Russian critics were mostly lukewarm, faulting the weak story and flat dialogue. Nikolai Kornatsky of Film Art found the effects comparable to Valerian and Guardians of the Galaxy but felt a sense of déjà vu, and Anton Dolin wrote that its three stories, a Frankenstein tale, a messiah story and a sports competition, never fit together.

documents.title: Haunt
documents.overview: On Halloween, a group of friends encounter an "extreme" haunted house that promises to feed on their darkest fears. The night turns deadly as they come to the horrifying realization that some nightmares are real.
documents.plot:
Haunt is a 2019 American slasher film written and directed by Scott Beck and Bryan Woods and produced by Eli Roth, Todd Garner, Mark Fasano, Ankur Rungta and Vishal Rungta. Katie Stevens, Will Brittain, Lauryn McClain, Andrew Caldwell and Shazi Raja joined the cast in October 2017, and principal photography took place that autumn in Covington, Kentucky. The film premiered at the Popcorn Frights Film Festival in Fort Lauderdale on August 8, 2019, screened at FrightFest in London, and received a limited US release from Momentum Pictures on September 13, 2019.

On Halloween night in Carbondale, Illinois, Harper, who is trapped in an abusive relationship, goes to a party with friends Bailey, Angela and Mallory, where they meet college students Evan and Nathan. The group heads to a haunted house attraction, where a performer dressed as a clown makes them sign liability waivers and lock away their phones. Inside, a witch-masked woman burns a screaming girl's face with a poker; when the group splits up, Bailey is slashed by a razor and Mallory is killed by the witch. A man in a ghost mask who poses as a helpful employee traps Nathan, and the costumed killers pick the group off one by one: a devil kills Angela, and the ghost removes his mask to reveal a heavily modified face before killing Evan.

Harper takes refuge in an escape room resembling a child's bedroom, which brings back memories of hiding from her abusive father. She finds a key, stabs the devil in the eye and uses the room's timed shotgun trap to kill him, but in the confusion fatally stabs a gagged Bailey, disguised in a skull mask. Harper's boyfriend, Sam, summoned by Nathan's text, is killed on arrival. Harper and Nathan fight back, and a vampire-masked performer, whose face is unaltered, explains that the performers belong to an extreme body modification group that builds attractions in order to kill people. The pair escape in Sam's truck as the clown burns the house down. Realizing the waivers listed their home addresses, Harper prepares, and when the clown later turns up at her mother's house, she traps and shoots him.

Stevens plays Harper, with Brittain as Nathan, McClain as Bailey, Caldwell as Evan and Raja as Angela. Critics were broadly positive, with 71% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 69, though some noted its debt to familiar influences. It grossed $2.4 million worldwide and later became Shudder's most-watched film premiere of 2019.

documents.title: Hatching
documents.tagline: She's coming out of her shell
documents.overview: 12 year old Tinja is desperate to please her mother, a woman obsessed with presenting the image of a perfect family. One night, Tinja finds a strange egg. What hatches is beyond belief.
documents.plot:
Hatching (Finnish: Pahanhautoja, literally "Hatcher of Evil," a play on a Finnish idiom for nursing a grudge) is a 2022 Finnish psychological body horror film directed by Hanna Bergholm in her feature debut and written by Ilja Rautsi. Siiri Solalinna stars as Tinja, with Sophia Heikkilä as her mother, Jani Volanen and Reino Nordin. The film premiered at the Sundance Film Festival in January 2022 and was released in Finland by Nordisk Film in March.

Twelve-year-old Tinja is a gymnast pushed relentlessly by her mother, a former figure skater who runs a lifestyle blog presenting her family as perfect. When a crow flies into the house and wrecks the immaculate living room, her mother calmly breaks its neck and tells Tinja to throw it away. That night Tinja finds the dying bird in the woods, puts it out of its misery and takes home an egg she finds nearby. She hides the egg in her room and cares for it, and it grows to an unnatural size.

Meanwhile, the cracks in the family's picture-perfect life become visible. Tinja discovers that her mother is having an affair with a man named Tero, and the arrival of a talented new neighbor, Reetta, who joins her gymnastics club, increases the pressure on her to succeed, driving her to train until her hands bleed. The egg finally hatches into a large, grotesque bird-like creature, which Tinja names Alli and secretly raises under her bed, feeding it in ways that are as disturbing as they are tender. Alli seems to act on Tinja's suppressed anger and jealousy, attacking whatever upsets her, starting with a neighbor's barking dog. As the creature grows and changes, becoming more and more like Tinja herself, she struggles to keep it hidden while the violence escalates.

Hatching was acclaimed for its practical creature effects, its satire of social-media perfection and Solalinna's performance. It holds a 93 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus calls it a message movie with a hard horror shell that establishes Bergholm as a bright new talent, and a Metacritic score of 75. It won the Grand Prix and the Youth Jury Prize at the Gérardmer International Fantastic Film Festival in 2022.

documents.title: Tesla
documents.overview: The story of the Promethean struggles of Nikola Tesla, as he attempts to transcend entrenched technology—including his own previous work—by pioneering a system of wireless energy that would change the world.
documents.plot:
Tesla is a 2020 biographical drama film that tells the story of Nikola Tesla's life and struggles. The main theme of the film revolves around the tension between genius and madness, as Tesla's extraordinary intellect and innovative ideas are constantly at odds with his own personal demons.

The movie delves into the darker aspects of Tesla's personality, exploring his obsessive nature, his struggles with mental health, and his tumultuous relationships. Through Tesla's character, the film highlights the sacrifices that geniuses often make in pursuit of their passions, including the loss of personal connections and emotional stability.

Furthermore, the film touches on the theme of isolation and loneliness, as Tesla's reclusive lifestyle and eccentric behavior lead to him being ostracized by society. This sense of disconnection serves as a catalyst for his creative genius, but also exacerbates his mental health struggles.

The movie also explores the theme of power and control, particularly in the context of Tesla's rivalry with Thomas Edison. The film portrays their competition as a battle of wits, with each man trying to outmaneuver the other in the pursuit of scientific supremacy.

Ultimately, Tesla is a thought-provoking drama that sheds light on the complexities of a brilliant mind and the personal costs of genius.

documents.title: The Farm
documents.overview: A young couple gets kidnapped and treated like farm animals after stopping at a roadside diner to eat meat.
documents.plot:
The Farm is an American independent horror film written and directed by Hans Stjernswärd in his feature-length directorial debut. Completed in 2018 and released in 2019, it stars Nora Yessayan and Alec Gaylord as a young couple, with Ken Volok, Rob Tisdale and Kelly Mis in supporting roles. Combining backwoods horror with exploitation elements, the film imagines a remote farm on which human beings are raised and slaughtered in the same way that animals are in industrial agriculture, and it received a limited release that included the United Kingdom.

Nora and Alec, a couple from Los Angeles, are on a road trip through the countryside when they get lost. A series of unsettling encounters follows: a deserted rest stop, a hostile woman with a broken-down car, and a roadside diner where a stranger quietly warns Nora that she is not safe. Running low on fuel and needing somewhere to sleep, they rent a small cabin from a strange landlord. During the night, a figure wearing a sheep mask emerges from beneath their bed.

Nora wakes the next morning locked in a wire cage inside a barn, surrounded by silent workers wearing animal masks. She gradually realises that the farm is a place where people are kept as livestock. The men are held in separate enclosures, fattened and eventually killed and butchered, while the women are confined to pens, forcibly impregnated and milked. Alec, imprisoned among the male captives, witnesses other prisoners being bludgeoned to death and carried away to an on-site slaughterhouse. As the couple endure the dehumanising routine of the farm, each looks for a way to escape and find the other, while the masked keepers carry out their work with an unsettling calm efficiency.

The film functions as an allegory of factory farming, reversing the roles of humans and animals in order to confront viewers with practices such as confinement, separation of mothers and offspring, and mechanised slaughter. Stjernswärd avoids explicit speeches, instead letting the imagery of caged, numbered and processed human beings carry the message, and the film closes on a bleak final note.

The Farm received mixed reviews. A critic for Culture Crypt observed that the film makes its point clearly by showing masked workers handling human captives like animals without turning into an outright lecture, although many reviewers found the characters thin and the pacing slow.

documents.title: Capernaum
documents.overview: Zain, a 12-year-old boy scrambling to survive on the streets of Beirut, sues his parents for having brought him into such an unjust world, where being a refugee with no documents means that your rights can easily be denied.
documents.plot:
Capernaum is a 2018 Lebanese drama film directed by Nadine Labaki, produced by Open City Films, among others.

The main themes of Capernaum revolve around the struggles of childhood, poverty, and the complexities of human relationships. The story follows Zain, a 12-year-old boy who sues God for giving him life with all its hardships.

At its core, Capernaum explores the theme of childhood innocence and the harsh realities of growing up in a world that often seems cruel and unforgiving. Zain's journey is marked by his experiences as an orphan living on the streets, struggling to survive, and facing numerous challenges, including poverty, abuse, and neglect.

The film also delves into the theme of family and belonging, highlighting the difficulties of finding one's place in a world that often seems hostile towards those who are marginalized or vulnerable. Zain's relationships with his caregivers, particularly the woman who takes care of him, serve as a source of comfort and support, but also underscore the complexities of human connection.

Furthermore, Capernaum critiques the notion of divine responsibility and the idea that individuals can be held accountable for their circumstances. The film raises questions about the nature of God and whether He is truly responsible for the suffering of His children.

Throughout the narrative, Labaki employs a non-linear storytelling approach, jumping back and forth in time to reveal Zain's backstory and his experiences as an adult. This structure adds to the sense of disorientation and confusion that pervades the film, mirroring Zain's own struggles to make sense of his life.

Ultimately, Capernaum is a powerful exploration of the human condition, one that challenges viewers to confront the complexities of existence and the difficulties of growing up in a world that often seems cruel and unforgiving.

documents.title: Border
documents.overview: When a border guard with a sixth sense for identifying smugglers encounters the first person she cannot prove is guilty, she is forced to confront terrifying revelations about herself and humankind.
documents.plot:
Border is a 2018 Swedish drama film directed by Olaf Falck and produced by Det Danske Filminstitut. The movie revolves around a mysterious and isolated border control officer, Joan, who lives in the middle of nowhere, Sweden, and her peculiar relationship with a young migrant named Torgers.

The main theme of Border is the exploration of identity, particularly in relation to borders both physical and metaphorical. The film delves into the complexities of human migration, highlighting the struggles and challenges faced by those seeking a new life elsewhere. Through Joan's character, the movie raises questions about the nature of belonging, identity, and what it means to be human.

The story also touches on themes of loneliness, isolation, and the blurring of boundaries between self and other. Joan's peculiar relationship with Torgers serves as a catalyst for exploring these themes, as she begins to question her own sense of identity and purpose in life.

Furthermore, Border critiques the notion of borders as physical barriers that separate people from their humanity. The film suggests that borders are often arbitrary and can be both oppressive and liberating, depending on one's perspective. Through its thought-provoking narrative, Border encourages viewers to reflect on their own assumptions about identity, belonging, and what it means to be human.

Overall, Border is a poignant and introspective film that challenges viewers to confront the complexities of human migration and identity in a world where borders are increasingly complex and multifaceted.
production_companies: MEDIA Programme of the European Union

documents.title: The Laundromat
documents.overview: When her idyllic vacation takes an unthinkable turn, Ellen Martin begins investigating a fake insurance policy, only to find herself down a rabbit hole of questionable dealings that can be linked to a Panama City law firm and its vested interest in helping the world's wealthiest citizens amass larger fortunes.
documents.plot:
The Laundromat is a 2019 film that delves into the world of international finance and corruption, focusing on the Panama Papers scandal. At its core, the movie explores the theme of power and greed, as embodied by the wealthy and influential individuals who use offshore accounts to hide their ill-gotten gains.

Through the story of Ruth Kramer (played by Julia Roberts), a determined and resourceful woman, the film sheds light on the darker aspects of global finance and the corrupt systems that allow these crimes to thrive. The movie also touches on the theme of accountability, as Ruth's quest for justice puts her at odds with powerful forces that seek to silence her.

Furthermore, The Laundromat critiques the notion of "clean money" and the ways in which wealth can be laundered and hidden from public scrutiny. The film highlights the consequences of this corruption, not only for individuals but also for entire communities and societies as a whole.

Ultimately, the movie serves as a cautionary tale about the dangers of unchecked power and greed, and the importance of holding those in positions of authority accountable for their actions.

documents.title: The Spy Gone North
documents.tagline: In the lasting days of the Cold War.
documents.overview: South Korea, 1993. An agent of the National Intelligence Service is sent to Beijing to infiltrate a group of North Korean officials with the ultimate goal of obtaining information about their nuclear program.
documents.plot:
The Spy Gone North (Korean: Gongjak) is a 2018 South Korean spy drama directed by Yoon Jong-bin. Hwang Jung-min stars as a South Korean agent who infiltrates the North Korean elite, with Lee Sung-min, Cho Jin-woong and Ju Ji-hoon in the main supporting roles. The film is loosely based on the true story of Park Chae-seo, a former agent known by the code name "Black Venus". It premiered at Cannes and was released in South Korean theaters on August 8, 2018.

In January 1992, Major Park Seok-young is recruited by the Agency for National Security Planning, South Korea's intelligence service, to uncover the truth about North Korea's nuclear weapons program, the extent of which is known only to the regime's inner circle and its leader Kim Jong-il. On the orders of Director Choi, played by Cho Jin-woong, Park takes on a carefully constructed cover as a disgraced former officer turned debt-ridden, hard-drinking businessman. His assignment is to get close to Ri Myung-woon, played by Lee Sung-min, the head of North Korea's External Economic Committee.

Operating out of Beijing, Park presents himself as an entrepreneur eager to do business with the North, and he gradually earns Ri's attention. The agency engineers a situation that leaves Ri in need of money, opening the door for Park, though Ri remains wary and demands proof of good faith. A suspicious officer of the North's State Security Department, Jung Moo-taek, played by Ju Ji-hoon, keeps a close eye on the newcomer. Park eventually proposes a joint venture to film South Korean television commercials in the North, a plan that brings him all the way to Pyongyang and into a rare audience with Kim Jong-il himself.

As he climbs higher, Park discovers that political figures in Seoul are secretly negotiating with North Korean officials to manipulate tensions ahead of the 1997 South Korean presidential election, betraying the very mission he has risked his life for. Caught between two governments, Park and Ri, who has come to see the cost of the regime's policies on his own people, form an unlikely bond of mutual respect that transcends the border dividing them.

The film was a major box office success in South Korea, drawing nearly five million admissions and grossing more than US$38 million. Critics praised its tense, dialogue-driven approach to espionage, which favors psychological suspense over action, as well as the performances of Hwang and Lee, and it went on to win numerous domestic film awards.

documents.title: Along with the Gods: The Last 49 Days
documents.overview: As the deceased soul Ja-hong and his three afterlife guardians prepare for their remaining trials for reincarnation, the guardians soon come face to face with the truth of their tragic time on Earth 1,000 years earlier.
documents.plot:
Along with the Gods: The Last 49 Days is a 2018 South Korean fantasy adventure film directed by Kim Sung-su and written by Lee Seung-jun. The movie is based on the novel of the same name by Park Chang-pil.

The story follows Han-seo (played by Ha Jung-woo), a young man who dies in a car accident at the age of 18. However, he soon finds himself transported to the afterlife, where he meets three gods: Hae-soo (played by Kim Hyang-gi), a goddess of love and beauty; Jang-seo (played by Park Seo-joon), a god of war; and Mu-seo (played by Ma Dong-seok), a god of death.

The three gods inform Han-seo that he has been chosen to participate in the "Great Competition" - a test of worthiness to ascend to heaven. The competition is a 49-day trial, during which Han-seo must complete various tasks and prove his worth to the gods.

As the story progresses, Han-seo embarks on a journey through different realms, each representing a different aspect of human life. He encounters various characters, including a young woman named Ji-hyun (played by Kim Mi-so), who becomes his love interest. Along the way, he also faces numerous challenges and obstacles, including fierce battles with monsters and rival contestants.

Throughout the movie, Han-seo's character undergoes significant development as he learns to confront his own flaws and weaknesses. He begins to understand the true nature of the afterlife and the gods' intentions, which ultimately leads him to question their motives.

As the 49-day trial nears its end, Han-seo faces off against the main antagonist, a powerful being known as the "God of Darkness." In a climactic battle, Han-seo uses his newfound skills and knowledge to defeat the God of Darkness and prove himself worthy to ascend to heaven.

In the end, Han-seo is granted his wish to return to earth, but with a twist - he is given a second chance at life, albeit in a different form. The movie concludes on a hopeful note, as Han-seo sets out to make the most of his new life and find happiness with Ji-hyun.

Overall, Along with the Gods: The Last 49 Days is a visually stunning and action-packed film that explores themes of mortality, redemption, and the human condition. With its unique blend of fantasy and adventure elements, it has become a beloved classic among Korean cinema fans.

documents.title: Leprechaun Returns
documents.tagline: Be careful what you wish for.
documents.overview: A group of unwitting sorority sisters accidentally awaken the serial-killing Leprechaun after they build a sorority house on his hunting grounds.
documents.plot:
Leprechaun Returns is a 2018 supernatural horror film that serves as a sequel to the original Leprechaun series. The movie delves into the theme of revenge and the consequences of playing with forces beyond human control.

The story revolves around a young woman named Ophelia, who unwittingly unleashes the vengeful spirit of the Leprechaun, Mr. Knuckles, from his ancient prison. As the film progresses, it becomes clear that Mr. Knuckles is driven by a desire for revenge against those who wronged him in life.

The movie explores the idea of karma and the cyclical nature of violence. Mr. Knuckles' actions are motivated by a deep-seated anger and hurt, which he seeks to inflict upon others. However, as the story unfolds, it becomes apparent that his quest for revenge is also fueled by a twisted sense of justice.

Throughout the film, the theme of female empowerment is also present. Ophelia, who initially unleashes Mr. Knuckles' wrath, must navigate a treacherous world and confront her own vulnerabilities in order to survive. Her journey serves as a metaphor for the struggle women often face in overcoming patriarchal oppression and reclaiming their agency.

Ultimately, Leprechaun Returns is a cautionary tale about the dangers of meddling with forces beyond human understanding. The film warns against the consequences of playing with fire and the devastating repercussions that can result from seeking revenge or trying to control the uncontrollable.

documents.title: Harry & Meghan: A Royal Romance
documents.overview: Examine the history of Prince Harry and Meghan Markle from the moment they met after being set up by friends, through their initial courtship when they were able to keep their romance under wraps, and ultimately the intense global media attention surrounding their relationship and Meghan’s life as a divorced American actress.
documents.plot:
Harry & Meghan: A Royal Romance is a 2018 American television film directed by Menhaj Huda from a script by Terrence Coli and Scarlett Lacey, dramatizing the meeting and courtship of Prince Harry and Meghan Markle. Murray Fraser and Parisa Fitz-Henley star as the couple, with Burgess Abernethy and Laura Mitchell as Prince William and Catherine, Duchess of Cambridge, Steve Coulter as Prince Charles, Deborah Ramsay as Camilla, Bonnie Soper as Diana, Princess of Wales, Trevor Lerner as Thomas Markle and Melanie Nicholls-King as Doria Ragland.

The film opens with Harry as a boy on a family trip to Africa after his mother's funeral, where he has a dramatic encounter with a lion, and then shows Meghan as a young girl grappling with her biracial heritage and the media's depiction of gender roles. In the present, the two are set up on a blind date, where Meghan, the star of Suits, makes Harry apologize for being late. They quickly fall in love, bonding over combative senses of humor and the scars of their parents' divorces, and a safari trip to Botswana deepens their romance.

Their relationship is soon exposed by the tabloids after a Halloween party, and the couple face intense global media attention, with photographers besieging the home of Meghan's mother. The film follows the reactions of family and friends: William and Kate are portrayed as stuffy guardians of tradition, while Charles and Camilla quickly give their blessing. Meghan confronts snobbery and racism from royal hangers-on and courtiers, including an incident involving an offensive brooch at a palace luncheon, and repeatedly breaks off the relationship as she fears losing the life and independence she has built. Harry persists, and the two eventually reach equal footing as he realizes that she must become his wife. The script lacked any royal approval, and much of the private romance is invented.

The film premiered on Lifetime on May 13, 2018, six days before the real royal wedding, drawing about 2.2 million viewers and ranking as cable's best original movie of the year in key demographics. Critics found it cliché-packed and silly, though Fitz-Henley's grounded performance was generally praised; the Guardian's Amy Nicholson called it a brain-numbing charmer and guilty pleasure, crediting Fitz-Henley with the emotional heavy lifting. Lifetime followed it with two sequels, Harry & Meghan: Becoming Royal in 2019 and Harry & Meghan: Escaping the Palace in 2021.

documents.title: Animal World
documents.overview: Drifting aimlessly through life, Kaisi has racked up debts of several million having borrowed money from his friends. Lured with the promise of writing it all off, Kaisi leaves his ailing mother and childhood sweetheart Qing to board the ship Destiny and attend a gambling party controlled by the mysterious Anderson. All players join the game with stars. For each game they lose, their opponent captures a star. Everyone is holding daggers behind their backs plotting dirty means by which to overcome their opponents. The game quickly deteriorates into a slaughter and Kaisi must battle save his own skin.
documents.plot:
Animal World (Chinese: 动物世界), also known as Animal World: Mr. Nobody, is a 2018 Chinese action-adventure film written and directed by Han Yan and based on Nobuyuki Fukumoto's manga Kaiji. Li Yifeng stars as Zheng Kaisi, with Michael Douglas as Anderson, Zhou Dongyu as Liu Qing, Cao Bingkun as Li Jun, Wang Ge as Meng Xiaopang ("Fatty Meng") and Su Ke as Zhang Jingkun.

Kaisi works a poorly paid job and struggles to cover his mother's medical bills, relying on help from his girlfriend Liu Qing, a nurse. On the advice of his friend Li Jun, he mortgages his mother's apartment to invest in a property scheme, which collapses and leaves him even deeper in debt. Anderson, the man who holds his debt, invites him aboard the ship Destiny, where players from around the world gamble on games of rock paper scissors. Each player receives cards representing rock, paper or scissors and three stars, which are won or lost with each match. To leave the ship, a player must use up all of their cards while keeping at least three stars.

Another player, Zhang Jingkun, proposes they tie all their matches but betrays Kaisi, leaving him one star. Kaisi teams up with Li Jun, also aboard, and Fatty Meng, another one-star player. Kaisi's talent for mathematics and probability lets him choose winning matches and guide his teammates. When Jingkun tries to lure him away, Kaisi refuses and exposes the fact that Jingkun has marked the cards. Left with one card and no one willing to play him, Jingkun is offered a final match by Kaisi, who wants revenge by forcing him to slap himself. Kaisi loses all his stars and is taken to the "black room", where he waits for his teammates to rescue him. Li Jun and Fatty Meng win the stars they need with his strategy, but Fatty Meng persuades Li Jun to sell them instead to clear their own debts. Kaisi tricks his way out of the black room and uses the money his former teammates earned to buy freedom for another betrayed player. He returns to Liu Qing a changed man. In an epilogue, he realizes that Anderson is the man who killed his father.

It was filmed in 2017. The film premiered at the 21st Shanghai International Film Festival and opened in China on June 29, 2018. It topped the Chinese box office, displacing Jurassic World: Fallen Kingdom, and grossed about CN¥510 million in China, for a worldwide total of roughly $77.4 million. Netflix acquired its global digital rights. Reviews were mainly positive.

documents.title: Warriors of Future
documents.overview: When a meteor carrying a destructive plant strikes the world, a suicide squad is given hours to save their post-apocalyptic city from total collapse.
documents.plot:
Warriors of Future (Chinese: 明日戰記), previously known as Virtus, is a 2022 Hong Kong military science fiction action film and the directorial debut of the visual effects artist Ng Yuen-fai. It stars Louis Koo as Tyler, an elite pilot, Sean Lau as his comrade Johnson Cheng and Carina Lau as Colonel Tam. Koo also served as executive producer, and the film was financed and distributed by his company, One Cool Group. Production began in 2017, and the release was delayed for years to allow for extensive visual effects work.

In 2055, Earth has been devastated by wars fought with advanced military robots, and pollution and climate change have poisoned the atmosphere, causing widespread illness and birth defects. Surviving cities are protected by enormous domes known as Skynets. During the construction of the dome over Sector B-16, a futuristic Hong Kong, a meteor crashes into the city carrying a giant alien plant, named Pandora, which spreads rapidly whenever it rains and destroys everything in its path, though scientists discover that it can also purify the polluted air.

A military scientist develops a gene-altering virus that can stop Pandora's growth while preserving its ability to repair the atmosphere. Tyler and Cheng are assigned to lead a mission to deliver the "gene bullet" to the plant's pistil during a window between two rainstorms. Colonel Tam, sent to oversee the operation, has a secret backup plan to bomb Pandora from the air, which would destroy the plant but could kill a hundred and sixty thousand civilians. When the mission is sabotaged from within and the soldiers find themselves trapped in the heart of the alien growth, they must fight hostile robots and the plant itself to save the city.

Its large-scale visual effects were described by critics as a milestone for Hong Kong cinema.

Warriors of Future opened the 46th Hong Kong International Film Festival on 15 August 2022 and was released in Hong Kong on 25 August, becoming the highest-grossing domestic film in Hong Kong at that time and earning about 111 million dollars including mainland China. The South China Morning Post praised its groundbreaking visual effects but noted a lack of fresh ideas.

documents.title: Pain and Glory
documents.overview: Salvador Mallo, a filmmaker in the twilight of his career, remembers his life: his mother, his lovers, the actors he worked with. The sixties in a small village in Valencia, the eighties in Madrid, the present, when he feels an immeasurable emptiness, facing his mortality, the incapability of continuing filming, the impossibility of separating creation from his own life. The need of narrating his past can be his salvation.
documents.plot:
Pain and Glory is a 2019 Spanish drama film directed by Pedro Almodóvar, not El Deseo. The movie follows the story of a retired theater director, Sergio, who embarks on a journey to rediscover his passion for life and art after being diagnosed with cancer.

The main themes of Pain and Glory revolve around the complexities of human existence, love, loss, and the search for meaning in life. The film explores the idea that our experiences, both joyful and painful, shape us into who we are, and that it's never too late to rediscover ourselves and pursue our passions.

Through Sergio's story, Almodóvar delves into the human condition, examining the ways in which we cope with mortality, grief, and the fear of losing what matters most. The film also touches on the theme of creative expression as a means of healing and self-discovery.

Ultimately, Pain and Glory is a poignant exploration of the human spirit's capacity for resilience, love, and transformation, even in the face of adversity.

documents.title: Nappily Ever After
documents.overview: After an accident at the hair salon, Violet realizes she's not living life to the fullest. A soulful barber helps her put the pieces back together.
documents.plot:
Nappily Ever After is a 2018 American romantic comedy-drama film that explores the complexities of love, identity, and self-discovery. The movie delves into the life of Wade, a successful African-American man who has given up on finding true love after being hurt in past relationships.

The main theme of Nappily Ever After revolves around the idea of embracing one's true self and letting go of societal expectations. Wade's journey is a metaphor for the struggles many people face in navigating their identities, particularly those from marginalized communities. The film highlights the tension between conforming to traditional norms and forging one's own path.

Through Wade's story, the movie sheds light on the importance of vulnerability, trust, and open communication in relationships. It also explores the theme of healing and recovery, as Wade grapples with his past traumas and learns to forgive himself and others.

The film's portrayal of love is nuanced and multifaceted, acknowledging that it can be messy, complicated, and imperfect. Ultimately, Nappily Ever After suggests that true connection and happiness come from embracing one's authentic self and being willing to take risks in pursuit of love and personal growth.

documents.title: Queen of Hearts
documents.overview: Anne, a brilliant and dedicated advocacy lawyer specialising in society’s most vulnerable, children and young adults, lives what appears to be the picture-perfect life with her doctor-husband, Peter, and their twin daughters. When her estranged teenage stepson, Gustav, moves in with them, Anne’s escalating desire leads her down a dangerous rabbit hole which, once exposed, unleashes a sequence of events destined to destroy her world.
documents.plot:
Queen of Hearts (Danish: Dronningen) is a 2019 Danish drama directed by May el-Toukhy, who co-wrote it with Maren Louise Käehne, starring Trine Dyrholm and Gustav Lindh, with Magnus Krepper as Peter. The titles allude to the Queen of Hearts from Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, which recurs throughout the film. It was Denmark's submission for the Academy Award for Best International Feature Film and won the 2019 Nordic Council Film Prize.

Anne is a successful lawyer who specialises in cases of rape and abuse involving young people. She lives a comfortable life with her husband Peter, a physician, and their young twin daughters, Frida and Fanny. Peter's teenage son from a previous marriage, Gustav, has been living with his mother in Sweden, but the family arranges for him to move in with them. Sullen and rebellious, he clashes with his father and pushes to live on his own despite being a minor. When the house is burgled, Anne discovers that Gustav was the thief; she agrees to keep his secret if he commits to family life, and he begins to settle in, even reading Alice's Adventures in Wonderland to the twins.

Anne becomes increasingly drawn to her stepson. Aroused after overhearing him with his girlfriend, she takes him to a bar, kisses him and later seduces him in his bedroom, beginning a secret sexual relationship. When her sister Lina sees the two kissing at the twins' birthday party, Anne panics and ends the affair. After a weekend at the family cabin, Peter tells Anne that Gustav wants to go to boarding school and has told him about the relationship. Anne coldly denies everything, claims that Gustav resents her for breaking up his parents' marriage, and exposes him as the burglar. In a confrontation with all three present, she maintains her lie, and Gustav is sent away.

Later Gustav comes to Anne's office and threatens to report her, but she tells him that no one will ever believe him. When he turns up at the house one night asking for his father, she turns him away and leaves him weeping in the drive. Some time later, news comes that Gustav has disappeared from his school, and his body is found frozen in the woods near the cabin. When Anne tells Peter that the death was not his fault, he violently silences her, and the family drive in silence to the funeral.

The film was acclaimed, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 97% approval; Variety called it a sleek, engrossing melodrama and Dyrholm's performance was especially praised.

documents.title: Nancy Drew and the Hidden Staircase
documents.original_title: Nancy Drew and the Hidden Staircase
documents.overview: Nancy Drew, a smart high schooler with a penchant for keen observation and deduction, stumbles upon the haunting of a local home. A bit of an outsider struggling to fit into her new surroundings, Nancy and her pals set out to solve the mystery, make new friends, and establish their place in the community
documents.plot:
Nancy Drew and the Hidden Staircase is a 2019 American teen mystery comedy directed by Katt Shea from a screenplay by Nina Fiore and John Herrera, based on the Nancy Drew novel The Hidden Staircase by Carolyn Keene. A reboot of the Nancy Drew film series distributed by Warner Bros., it stars Sophia Lillis as the amateur sleuth, with Zoe Renee, Mackenzie Graham, Laura Slade Wiggins, Sam Trammell and Linda Lavin.

After her mother's death, sixteen-year-old Nancy Drew moves with her father Carson, a lawyer, from Chicago to the small town of River Heights. Nancy struggles to fit in, while Carson becomes involved in local politics, opposing plans for a railway line through the town. One night a local thug, Willie Wharton, threatens Nancy in an attempt to intimidate her father. When a school bully, Derek, humiliates Nancy's new friend Bess with an edited video, Nancy takes revenge by rigging the gym shower to dye him blue, and is sentenced to community service.

During her service she meets Flora, an elderly woman who believes her house is haunted. Intrigued, Nancy spends the night there with Flora's niece Helen, Derek's girlfriend. Lights flicker and burst, cupboards and drawers fly open, and a cloaked figure warns Nancy to drop the case. Investigating the next day, Nancy and Helen discover a secret passage leading outside, together with the equipment used to fake the haunting, including a rigged fuse box and a device pumping concentrated nutmeg through the air vents to cause hallucinations.

Nancy then realises that her father, supposedly away on business, has not been in touch. His friend Nate claims that Carson is at a campsite with poor reception, but Nancy knows he was staying at a hotel. She and Helen find that he never checked out, and security footage shows him being abducted by Wharton. Her friends Bess and George discover that Wharton also bought the nutmeg, and Nancy deduces that her father is being held in the hidden passage at Flora's house. There she and Helen find Wharton and Nate holding Carson and Flora captive. The pair have been sabotaging the anti-railway campaign and trying to frighten Flora into selling her land for the line. Nancy and Helen outwit the captors, who are arrested, and Helen joins Nancy's circle of friends as they plan their next mystery.

The film earned modest box-office returns but generally favourable reviews, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 76% approval and praising Lillis's performance.

documents.title: The Last Witness
documents.tagline: When war ends, the fight for the truth begins.
documents.overview: An ambitious young journalist uncovers the horrific slaughter of 22,000 Polish officers during World War II, a secret kept hidden for far too many years.
documents.plot:
The Last Witness is a 2018 British-Polish historical thriller directed by Piotr Szkopiak and based on a stage play by Paul Szambowski. It stars Alex Pettyfer as the journalist Stephen Underwood, Robert Więckiewicz as Michael Loboda, Talulah Riley as Jeanette Mitchell and Michael Gambon as Frank Hamilton, with Will Thorp, Henry Lloyd-Hughes, Piotr Stramowski and Gwilym Lee. The film deals with political intrigue in the United Kingdom after the Second World War surrounding the Katyn massacre.

The Katyn massacre was the mass execution of thousands of Polish officers, policemen and members of the intelligentsia carried out by the Soviet secret police in 1940, a crime that Soviet authorities blamed on Nazi Germany for decades. In the film, Stephen Underwood is a young and ambitious newspaper journalist in post-war England who begins investigating a story connected to the Polish community and refugees who settled in Britain after the war. His inquiries lead him to Michael Loboda, an Eastern European refugee whose true identity is a mystery.

As Stephen digs deeper, he uncovers evidence that Loboda may have witnessed the atrocity at Katyn and that the British government, eager to preserve its wartime alliance with the Soviet Union, has been complicit in covering up the truth about who was responsible. His pursuit of the story places him in increasing danger, as powerful figures in the intelligence services and the establishment, represented by the enigmatic Frank Hamilton, seek to keep the secret buried. Stephen must risk his career, his relationship with Jeanette and ultimately his own life to bring the truth to light.

The script was written fifteen years before the film was made and was shot in just eighteen days. Szkopiak, who was born in the United Kingdom to Polish parents, described the project as deeply personal, as his grandfather was among those murdered at Katyn; it was his first film in nineteen years.

The Last Witness was released in Poland by Kino Świat on 11 May 2018, in the United States by Momentum Pictures on 29 May and in the United Kingdom by Signature Entertainment on 17 August. It won numerous festival awards, though it holds 29 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes from a small number of reviews; Why So Blu? praised it for making history exciting.

documents.title: Driven
documents.tagline: How a lemon became a legend.
documents.overview: FBI informant Jim Hoffman lures troubled automobile magnate John DeLorean to an undercover sting for cocaine trafficking.
documents.plot:
Driven is a 2018 biographical comedy thriller directed by Nick Hamm and written by Colin Bateman. It stars Jason Sudeikis as Jim Hoffman, a pilot and FBI informant, and Lee Pace as the car designer John DeLorean, with Judy Greer as Hoffman's wife Ellen, Corey Stoll as FBI agent Benedict Tisa, Michael Cudlitz as drug smuggler Morgan Hetrick, Isabel Arraiza and Erin Moriarty. The film dramatizes the events leading up to DeLorean's arrest in an FBI sting.

Pilot Jim Hoffman is caught by the FBI flying a load of cocaine into the United States. To avoid prison, he agrees to become an informant, and the FBI relocates him and his family to San Diego, where agent Benedict Tisa pressures him to help bring down his former boss, the trafficker Morgan Hetrick. Hoffman soon discovers that his new next-door neighbor is John DeLorean, the famous automobile executive, who is trying to build his dream car. The two families become friends, and the charming, flamboyant DeLorean draws Hoffman into his glamorous world.

DeLorean is deeply in debt and struggling to raise money for his company, and when he asks Hoffman to help him find investors, Hoffman sees an opportunity. Under pressure from the FBI and eager to free himself from his obligations as an informant, Hoffman arranges a meeting between DeLorean, Hetrick and Tisa, who poses as a drug dealer offering to finance a cocaine deal. When the money falls short, Hoffman even persuades the FBI to lend DeLorean the funds. DeLorean is arrested in a hotel room after completing the deal, and the story is interwoven with scenes of Hoffman testifying at his trial, where his uncertain testimony about who proposed the deal becomes decisive.

The film portrays the case as a darkly comic tale of ambition, vanity and deception, focusing on the unusual friendship between the two men.

Driven premiered at the 75th Venice International Film Festival on September 8, 2018, and screened at the Toronto International Film Festival before its release in the United States in August 2019. It received mixed to positive reviews, with 63 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus praised the outstanding cast, and a Metacritic score of 55.

documents.title: Bodies Bodies Bodies
documents.tagline: This is not a safe space.
documents.overview: In an isolated family mansion, a group of rich 20-somethings decides to play Bodies Bodies Bodies, a game where one of them is secretly a "killer" while the rest tries to "escape". Things take a turn for the worse when real bodies start turning up, setting off a paranoid and dangerous chain of events.
documents.plot:
Bodies Bodies Bodies is a 2022 American horror-comedy film written and directed by Halina Reijn. The movie follows three friends, Emily (Amandla Stenberg), Claire (Maria Bakalova), and Whitney (Myanmar-born actress Pimberley), who reunite for a weekend at a remote vacation home in rural Texas.

The story begins with the trio engaging in a game of "Truth or Dare," which they played as teenagers. The game, however, takes a dark turn when Claire is forced to perform a gruesome task, resulting in her death. The remaining two friends are shocked and traumatized by the event, but they soon realize that they have been invited to Claire's funeral.

As the weekend progresses, Emily and Whitney begin to experience strange and terrifying events at the house. They start to suspect that someone is impersonating Claire, who had a troubled past with her friends. The tension builds as the two women try to uncover the identity of the imposter and the motives behind it.

Throughout the film, the lines between reality and fantasy become increasingly blurred. Emily and Whitney's perceptions of each other and themselves are challenged, leading to a descent into paranoia and violence. As the body count rises, the friends' relationships with each other begin to deteriorate.

The movie takes a darkly comedic turn as the characters engage in a series of gruesome and satirical murders, which serve as a commentary on toxic masculinity, privilege, and social status. The film's tone is reminiscent of classic horror movies from the 1970s and 1980s, with a dash of modern irreverence.

As the story unfolds, Emily and Whitney are forced to confront their own dark pasts and the true nature of their friendship. In the end, only one person remains, and the film's climax is both shocking and thought-provoking.

Bodies Bodies Bodies received widespread critical acclaim for its originality, wit, and performances. The movie has been praised for its subversion of traditional horror tropes and its commentary on toxic masculinity and social status.

documents.title: Happiest Season
documents.tagline: This holiday, everyone's secrets are coming out.
documents.overview: A young woman's plans to propose to her girlfriend while at her family's annual holiday party are upended when she discovers her partner hasn't yet come out to her conservative parents.
documents.plot:
Happiest Season is a 2020 American romantic comedy film written by Abby Kohn and Marc Silverstein, directed by Clea DuVall, and produced by Temple Hill Entertainment.

The movie follows the story of Abby (played by Kristen Stewart), a successful event planner who has been dating her girlfriend, Molly (played by Mackenzie Davis), for three years. As Christmas approaches, Abby's family invites them to spend the holiday together at their home in New York. However, things take an unexpected turn when Abby reveals that she wants to get engaged to Molly.

Abby's plan is to propose to Molly during a festive holiday party, but her plans are soon derailed by her own anxiety and fear of commitment. As the family gathers for Christmas dinner, Abby begins to question whether she's truly ready for marriage. Meanwhile, Molly starts to feel pressure from Abby's family to take their relationship to the next level.

As the story unfolds, we see flashbacks of Abby's childhood, where she was always the "good girl" and struggled with her own desires and identity. This backstory helps explain why Abby is hesitant to commit to marriage. The film also explores Molly's character, who comes from a more traditional family background and feels pressure to conform to societal expectations.

Throughout the movie, the characters navigate their relationships, identities, and expectations. The dialogue is witty and engaging, with many humorous moments that poke fun at the challenges of modern dating and family dynamics.

As Christmas Day approaches, Abby's anxiety reaches a boiling point. She begins to question whether she's truly in love with Molly or just feeling pressure from her family and society. In a heartwarming moment, Abby has an epiphany and realizes what she truly wants for her future.

The film culminates with a romantic proposal that is both heartfelt and humorous. The ending is satisfying, but also leaves room for interpretation. Ultimately, the movie suggests that love and commitment are about finding someone who accepts you for who you are, flaws and all.

Overall, Happiest Season is a charming and witty romantic comedy that explores themes of identity, family, and love. With strong performances from Kristen Stewart and Mackenzie Davis, the film is sure to delight audiences looking for a feel-good holiday movie.

documents.title: King of Thieves
documents.tagline: It's never too late to earn
