As Michael tries to rescue Dina, he discovers that she is not what she seems. She has a hidden past and is actually a skilled assassin in her own right. The two form an unlikely alliance as they work together to take down Marcus and his henchmen.

Throughout the film, Michael and Dina's banter-filled relationship evolves from one of adversaries to something more. They develop a strong bond, with Michael learning to trust Dina and appreciate her skills. Meanwhile, Marcus becomes increasingly unhinged, leading to a series of intense confrontations between the three leads.

As the story unfolds, it is revealed that Dina has a personal vendetta against Marcus, who had betrayed her in the past. The two engage in a cat-and-mouse game, with Michael caught in the middle. Along the way, they encounter a range of colorful characters, including a bumbling CIA agent (Frank Grillo) and a group of skilled assassins.

The film's action sequences are fast-paced and entertaining, with plenty of twists and turns to keep viewers on the edge of their seats. The chemistry between Reynolds and Jackson is undeniable, making their rivalry both humorous and intense.

In the end, Michael and Dina successfully take down Marcus and his henchmen, but not before a thrilling showdown in which they use all their skills to outwit and overpower their foes. As the dust settles, Michael and Dina share a romantic moment, hinting at a possible future together.

Overall, Hitman's Wife's Bodyguard is a fun, action-packed romp with plenty of laughs and excitement. The film's cast delivers strong performances, and the chemistry between Reynolds and Jackson is undeniable. With its witty banter, over-the-top action sequences, and heartwarming romance, this movie is sure to delight fans of the genre.

documents.title: Rambo: Last Blood
documents.tagline: Everyone has one more fight in them
documents.overview: After fighting his demons for decades, John Rambo now lives in peace on his family ranch in Arizona, but his rest is interrupted when Gabriela, the granddaughter of his housekeeper María, disappears after crossing the border into Mexico to meet her biological father. Rambo, who has become a true father figure for Gabriela over the years, undertakes a desperate and dangerous journey to find her.
documents.plot:
Rambo: Last Blood is a 2019 action-thriller film directed by Patrick Hughes and starring Sylvester Stallone as John Rambo, the iconic protagonist from the previous films. The movie marks the fifth installment in the Rambo series.

The story begins with an elderly John Rambo living on his farm in Arizona, where he spends most of his days tending to his animals and enjoying the peace and quiet. However, his life is disrupted when a young Mexican girl, Ángela (Natalia Cordova-Buckley), arrives at his doorstep seeking help. She claims that her mother was kidnapped by human traffickers, and Rambo agrees to help her.

As Rambo delves deeper into the case, he discovers that the kidnappers are being led by a ruthless and cunning leader named Camacho (Yul Vazquez). Camacho is responsible for the kidnapping of many young girls from Mexico, who are then forced into prostitution. Rambo becomes determined to track down Camacho and rescue Ángela.

Rambo's investigation takes him back to his past, where he encounters a group of former soldiers who were also involved in the war against the Guatemalan rebels. They reveal that Camacho was once a member of their unit, but turned rogue after being disillusioned with the US government's handling of the conflict.

As Rambo gets closer to Camacho, he faces numerous challenges and obstacles, including treacherous terrain, hostile locals, and his own personal demons. Along the way, he also encounters a young woman named Sarah (Mia Sara), who becomes his ally in the fight against Camacho.

The climax of the film takes place at a human trafficking ring in Mexico, where Rambo confronts Camacho and his henchmen. In a intense and bloody battle, Rambo fights to rescue Ángela and bring justice to those responsible for her kidnapping.

In the end, Rambo emerges victorious, but not without scars. He returns to his farm, where he reflects on the sacrifices he has made and the toll that his actions have taken on him. The film ends with Rambo sitting alone in his rocking chair, lost in thought as the camera pans out to reveal the vast expanse of the Arizona desert.

Throughout the film, Stallone delivers a powerful performance as Rambo, bringing depth and nuance to the character's iconic persona. The action sequences are intense and well-choreographed, with plenty of nods to the previous films in the series. While some critics have argued that the film is overly reliant on familiar tropes and plot devices, it remains a satisfying conclusion to the Rambo saga.

Overall, Rambo: Last Blood is a gripping and emotionally resonant action-thriller that explores themes of trauma, redemption, and the human cost of war. With its stunning cinematography, pulse-pounding action sequences, and Stallone's iconic performance, it is a must-see for fans of the franchise.

documents.title: Running with the Devil
documents.overview: A leader of a drug cartel sends his two toughest henchmen to investigate why a shipment was botched.
documents.plot:
Running with the Devil is a 2019 American crime drama film directed by Tim Sutton. The movie follows the story of a young man who gets caught up in a life of crime and must navigate the dark world of gangsters, corrupt cops, and loyalty.

The main theme of Running with the Devil revolves around the destructive nature of loyalty and the blurred lines between right and wrong. The film explores how easily one can become entangled in a web of deceit and violence, and how difficult it is to escape once you're in too deep. As the protagonist navigates this treacherous world, he must confront the consequences of his actions and decide where his true loyalties lie.

The movie also delves into the theme of identity and self-discovery, as the protagonist struggles to find his place within the gangster culture and define himself outside of it. This internal conflict is mirrored in the external struggle between good and evil, highlighting the gray areas that often exist in real life.

Furthermore, Running with the Devil touches on the theme of redemption, suggesting that even those who have made mistakes or poor choices can seek forgiveness and start anew. However, this path to redemption is fraught with danger, and the film raises questions about whether it's possible to truly change one's ways or if we're forever bound by our past actions.

Overall, Running with the Devil presents a gritty and unflinching portrayal of life on the wrong side of the law, exploring themes that are both timely and timeless.

documents.title: In the Tall Grass
documents.tagline: Some places have a mind of their own.
documents.overview: After hearing a child screaming for help from the green depths of a vast field of tall grass, Becky, a pregnant woman, and Cal, her brother, park their car near a mysterious abandoned church and recklessly enter the field, discovering that they are not alone and because of some reason they are unable of escaping a completely inextricable vegetable labyrinth.
documents.plot:
In the Tall Grass is a psychological horror film directed by Vincenzo Natali, based on the novella of the same name by Stephen King and Joe Hill. The movie follows two siblings, Becky and Cal, who embark on a journey to find their missing sister in a field of tall grass that seems to have a life of its own.

The main themes of In the Tall Grass include:

1. **Family dynamics**: The film explores the complex relationships within families, particularly the bond between siblings. Becky and Cal's relationship is put to the test as they navigate the treacherous terrain in search of their sister.
2. **Trauma and grief**: The movie delves into the emotional scars left by traumatic events, such as the disappearance of their sister. The characters' experiences are intertwined with the eerie atmosphere of the tall grass, which serves as a metaphor for the overwhelming nature of grief.
3. **The power of nature**: The film highlights the awe-inspiring and intimidating aspects of nature, particularly the tall grass itself. The environment seems to have a malevolent presence, manipulating the characters' perceptions and actions.
4. **Perception vs. reality**: As the story unfolds, it becomes increasingly difficult for Becky and Cal to distinguish between what's real and what's just their imagination or the product of the tall grass's influence. This theme adds to the sense of unease and uncertainty.
5. **The fragility of human existence**: In the Tall Grass ultimately reveals that some secrets are better left unspoken, and the truth can be more terrifying than fiction. The film suggests that our understanding of reality is fragile and can be shattered by the unknown.

Overall, In the Tall Grass is a thought-provoking horror film that explores the darker aspects of human nature, family dynamics, and the power of nature to shape our perceptions.

documents.title: Late Night
documents.overview: A legendary late-night talk show host's world is turned upside down when she hires her only female staff writer. Originally intended to smooth over diversity concerns, her decision has unexpectedly hilarious consequences as the two women separated by culture and generation are united by their love of a biting punchline.
documents.plot:
Late Night is a 2019 American comedy-drama film that explores the complexities of female identity, ambition, and the struggles of women in male-dominated industries.

The movie delves into the life of Kate McKinnon's character, Devi, a young comedian who lands a late-night talk show host gig after the sudden departure of her predecessor. As she navigates this new role, Devi must confront her own insecurities, biases, and privilege, all while trying to find her voice and connect with her audience.

Throughout the film, the main theme of female empowerment is woven throughout, as Devi struggles to balance her creative ambitions with the pressures of being a woman in a male-dominated industry. The movie also touches on themes of identity, particularly for women who are navigating their 30s and trying to find their place in the world.

The film's portrayal of the late-night talk show host's inner workings serves as a metaphor for the ways in which societal expectations can constrain individuals, particularly women. As Devi navigates her new role, she must confront the biases and stereotypes that have been ingrained in the industry, all while trying to find her own unique voice.

Ultimately, Late Night is a heartwarming and humorous exploration of what it means to be a woman in today's society, and the ways in which we can support and uplift each other as we navigate our careers and personal lives.

documents.title: Prisoners of the Ghostland
documents.overview: In the treacherous frontier city of Samurai Town, a ruthless bank robber is sprung from jail by wealthy warlord The Governor, whose adopted granddaughter Bernice has gone missing. The Governor offers the prisoner his freedom in exchange for retrieving the runaway. Strapped into a leather suit that will self-destruct within five days, the bandit sets off on a journey to find the young woman—and his own path to redemption.
documents.plot:
Prisoners of the Ghostland is a 2021 American-Japanese dystopian Western film directed by Sion Sono from a script by Aaron Hendry and Reza Sixo Safai. Blending the Western with horror and the Japanese swordplay genre known as chanbara, it stars Nicolas Cage, Sofia Boutella, Bill Moseley and Nick Cassavetes, with Tak Sakaguchi as the samurai Yasujiro. It premiered at the 2021 Sundance Film Festival on January 31, 2021, and was released in theaters and on video on demand by RLJE Films on September 17, 2021.

Years after a crash between a prison bus and a truck carrying nuclear waste devastated a region of Japan, a frontier settlement called Samurai Town is ruled by a corrupt Governor who has mixed traditional Japanese culture with the trappings of the American Old West and keeps a harem of adopted "granddaughters". Beyond the town lies the Ghostland, a wasteland inhabited by half-mad outcasts and victims of the contamination. When one of the granddaughters, Bernice, flees the Governor's house and disappears into the Ghostland, the Governor releases Hero, a notorious bank robber imprisoned after a heist in which his partner Psycho murdered innocent bystanders. Hero is sent to bring Bernice back within five days, locked into a bodysuit fitted with explosive charges that will detonate if he harms her, tampers with the suit or runs out of time. As he leaves, a parting gesture of defiance impresses Yasujiro, the Governor's bodyguard, whose own sister is one of the granddaughters. In the Ghostland, Hero is taken to a cult-like enclave of outcasts led by a man named Enoch, and finds Bernice among them, catatonic from trauma. As the clock runs down, an accidental detonation, haunting memories of the robbery and the realization of his own part in the original catastrophe force Hero to reckon with his past, and he must rally the Ghostlanders against the Governor before returning to Samurai Town for a final confrontation.

Critics gave the film mixed reviews. It has a 61% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on 160 reviews, with a consensus that, while far from Sono's most distinctive work, it offers viewers a deliriously gonzo genre mash-up with an explosive performance from Cage, and Metacritic gives it a weighted average score of 53 out of 100.

documents.title: Little Italy
documents.overview: Former childhood pals Leo and Nikki are attracted to each other as adults—but will their feuding parents' rival pizzerias put a chill on their sizzling romance?
documents.plot:
Little Italy is a 2018 Canadian romantic comedy-drama film directed by Donald Petrie. The movie follows the story of Max, a young man who returns to his hometown of Toronto's Little Italy after being away for several years.

The main theme of Little Italy revolves around the idea of identity and belonging. Max struggles to find his place in the world outside of his family's expectations, but ultimately discovers that home is where the heart is. The film explores the complexities of cultural heritage and the importance of embracing one's roots.

Throughout the movie, themes of love, family, and community are also woven together, highlighting the significance of human connections in our lives. Max's relationships with those around him, particularly his mother and a local business owner, help shape his understanding of himself and where he belongs.

The film also touches on the idea of nostalgia and the passing of time, as Max navigates his way through adulthood while still holding onto memories of his childhood. Overall, Little Italy is a heartwarming story about finding one's place in the world and embracing the people and places that make life meaningful.

documents.title: Next Gen
documents.overview: A friendship with a top-secret robot turns a lonely girl's life into a thrilling adventure as they take on bullies, evil bots and a scheming madman.
documents.plot:
Next Gen is an animated science fiction film that revolves around a young girl named Mae, who forms a bond with a robot dog named Beep Boop. The movie explores the theme of acceptance and understanding between humans and artificial intelligence.

The story delves into the idea of what it means to be alive and whether a machine can truly experience emotions. Through Mae's relationship with Beep Boop, the film highlights the importance of empathy and compassion in breaking down barriers between different species.

Moreover, Next Gen touches upon the theme of family and belonging. Mae finds a sense of home and connection with Beep Boop, which challenges traditional notions of what it means to be part of a family. The movie suggests that love and acceptance can transcend boundaries, whether they are human or artificial.

The film also explores the consequences of playing god with technology and the ethics of creating life-like robots. As Mae and Beep Boop navigate their relationship, they must confront the implications of their existence and the responsibilities that come with it.

Overall, Next Gen is a heartwarming and thought-provoking film that encourages viewers to think critically about the intersection of humanity and technology.

documents.title: Words on Bathroom Walls
documents.tagline: If you can't trust your mind, trust your heart.
documents.overview: Diagnosed with a mental illness halfway through his senior year of high school, a witty, introspective teen struggles to keep it a secret while falling in love with a brilliant classmate who inspires him to open his heart and not be defined by his condition.
documents.plot:
Words on Bathroom Walls is a poignant and thought-provoking film that delves into the complexities of mental health, identity, and the struggles of growing up. The movie follows the story of Jamie Sullivan, a charismatic and creative teenager who navigates his way through high school while living with schizophrenia.

At its core, Words on Bathroom Walls explores the theme of finding one's voice in the face of adversity. Jamie's experiences with mental illness serve as a catalyst for self-discovery, forcing him to confront his emotions, challenge societal expectations, and forge his own path. The film beautifully captures the tension between conformity and individuality, highlighting the importance of embracing one's uniqueness.

The movie also touches on the theme of social isolation and the struggle to form meaningful connections with others. Jamie's relationships with his family and peers are fraught with challenges, as he grapples with feelings of loneliness and disconnection. Through Jamie's journey, the film sheds light on the devastating consequences of neglecting mental health and the importance of empathy and understanding in building strong relationships.

Furthermore, Words on Bathroom Walls tackles the theme of identity and self-acceptance. As Jamie navigates his way through adolescence, he must confront the expectations placed upon him by others and forge a sense of self that is authentic and true to who he is. The film's portrayal of Jamie's inner world is both haunting and beautiful, offering a powerful exploration of the human experience.

Ultimately, Words on Bathroom Walls is a heart-wrenching and ultimately uplifting film that celebrates the resilience of the human spirit. Through its thoughtful and nuanced portrayal of mental health, identity, and relationships, the movie offers a powerful message of hope and acceptance.

documents.title: The Last Sharknado: It's About Time
documents.original_title: The Last Sharknado: It's About Time
documents.tagline: History's biggest disaster comes to an end.
documents.overview: With much of America lying in ruins, the rest of the world braces for a global sharknado, Fin and his family must travel around the world to stop them.
documents.plot:
The Last Sharknado: It's About Time is a campy, over-the-top disaster film that serves as the eighth installment in The Sharknado franchise. Directed by Anthony C. Ferrante and written by S.S. Wilson, Markward DiChiro, and Anthony C. Ferrante, the movie was released on July 26, 2018.

The story begins with Fin Shepard (Ian Ziering), the main protagonist of the series, who has finally found a way to defeat the sharknadoes that have plagued his life for years. With the help of his family and friends, including Tara (Tara Reid), Hugo (Cody Alston), and Nick (John Heffernan), Fin creates a time machine that allows them to travel back in time to prevent the sharknados from ever occurring.

However, things quickly go awry as they realize that their actions in the past are having unintended consequences on the present. They soon discover that every decision they make in the past is creating a new timeline, and they must navigate through multiple parallel universes to find a way to restore the original timeline.

As Fin and his team travel through time, they encounter alternate versions of themselves and other characters from previous Sharknado films. Along the way, they also meet a young version of Fin's father, George (Richard Herd), who becomes a key player in their quest.

The plot thickens as Fin and his team realize that they are not alone in their time-traveling adventures. A rival group, led by a sinister figure known only as "The Timekeeper" (Mark McGrath), is also traveling through time to alter the course of history for their own gain.

As the stakes grow higher, Fin and his team must use all their wits and cunning to outsmart The Timekeeper and restore the original timeline. Along the way, they encounter a range of wacky characters, including a time-traveling version of Tara (played by Tara Reid) who becomes a key ally in their quest.

The movie culminates in an epic showdown between Fin and The Timekeeper, with the fate of the universe hanging in the balance. In the end, Fin emerges victorious, but not before realizing that his actions have created a new reality where sharknados are still a threat.

Throughout the film, Ferrante pokes fun at time travel tropes and the absurdity of the Sharknado franchise. The movie is full of humorous references to previous films in the series, as well as nods to classic disaster movies like Independence Day and Armageddon.

Overall, The Last Sharknado: It's About Time is a lighthearted, entertaining romp that is sure to delight fans of the franchise. While it may not be the most sophisticated or nuanced film, its campy charm and over-the-top antics make it a must-see for anyone who loves B-movies and disaster films.

documents.title: Megalodon
documents.overview: A military vessel on the search for an unidentified submersible finds themselves face to face with a giant shark, forced to use only what they have on board to defend themselves from the monstrous beast.
documents.plot:
Megalodon is a 2018 American creature-feature television film directed by James Thomas, who also worked on the script, and produced by The Asylum, the studio known for low-budget "mockbusters" released alongside major studio films. Made to capitalize on Jon Turteltaub's The Meg, which opened in theaters three days earlier, it premiered on the Syfy channel on 13 August 2018. Michael Madsen leads the cast as Admiral King, with Caroline Harris as Commander Lynch, Dominic Pace as Captain Streeper, Ego Mikitas as the Russian captain Ivanov, Aimee Stolte as Yana Popov, Paulina Nguyen as Cheng and Scott C. Roe as Jameson.

A few hundred miles west of Hawaii, a Russian submarine is secretly tapping an American communications cable when the noise of its drilling awakens a gigantic prehistoric shark, which tears the vessel apart. Ivanov escapes into the bow with three crew members, abandoning the others. The US Navy destroyer Shaw finds the wreck, and Lynch dives in the submersible she designed, rescuing the Russians, who claim to be whale researchers, before the shark swallows the submersible whole. Admiral King wants to cut the crew loose to protect the ship, but Streeper insists on a rescue, and the loyal crew locks the admiral in his cabin. Cheng rigs an anchor with high-voltage current as bait; when the shark opens its mouth, the submersible escapes, and the jolt appears to stop the creature, though one sailor dies in the electrified water.

Under questioning, Popov admits the Russians were on an intelligence mission. Ivanov breaks free, arms a comrade and kills the tactical adviser Jameson, while the shark resurfaces and devours a yacht. Cheng turns the submersible into a bomb, but Ivanov forces her to throw the detonator overboard, and the backup remote she builds only works at close range. Streeper orders the crew into the lifeboats and prepares to go down with his ship, and Lynch swims back to help him. King, freed from his cabin, kills Ivanov in a shootout but is mortally wounded, and when the shark crashes through the hull, he detonates the explosives, destroying the beast and the destroyer as the survivors salute him.

The exterior shipboard scenes were filmed aboard the SS Lane Victory, a World War II vessel now serving as a museum ship in San Pedro, California. A sequel, Megalodon Rising, followed in 2021.

documents.title: Meander
documents.tagline: You have just woken up stuck in a pipe full of deadly traps. How far will you go?
documents.overview: After getting a car ride from an unknown man, Lisa wakes up in a tube. On her arm is strapped a bracelet with a countdown. She quickly understands that every 8 minutes, fire burns an occupied section. She has no choice but to crawl into safe sections to survive. To know why she’s there and how to get out, Lisa will have to face the memories of her dead daughter…
documents.plot:
Meander (French: Méandre) is a 2020 French science fiction film written and directed by Mathieu Turi, starring Gaia Weiss as Lisa and Peter Franzén as Adam. It premiered online at the Sitges Film Festival on 11 October 2020, opened in French cinemas on 26 May 2021 and was released in the United States and on video on demand by Gravitas Ventures on 9 July 2021.

On an empty road somewhere in America, Lisa, a Frenchwoman, accepts a ride from a man named Adam who has a cross tattooed on his right hand. She tells him that her daughter, Nina, died young and would have turned nine that day. When a radio bulletin describes a serial-killer suspect with the same tattoo, Adam brakes hard and Lisa is knocked unconscious. She wakes in a maze of narrow metal tunnels, wearing a catsuit and a strange glowing bracelet, and must crawl past crushers, flamethrowers, flooded passages and acid, finding the decayed bodies of others dressed as she is. She meets a filthy, raving prisoner who dies in a burst of flame after they struggle over a single safe space; his surviving hand bears the cross tattoo, revealing that he is Adam and that she has been there far longer than she realized. Beneath his bracelet are tattooed symbols she cannot decipher.

A mechanical tentacle tipped with a skull tends her wounds and triggers memories of Adam stabbing her and a strange light in the sky. Pursued by a burned, one-handed creature that seems to be Adam's revived corpse, she relives Nina's fatal fall from a window, and when she becomes snared in razor wire, a trapdoor drops her back to where she started. Copying Adam's symbols on the wall in her own blood, she realizes they are directions through the labyrinth, burns off her own bracelet in acid and finds a fresh set tattooed on her wrist. She passes a womb-like chamber with alien shapes moving beyond its walls, crushes the creature in a compactor and loses a foot to a blade, only to find that the daylight ahead is a screen. As she weeps, she is lifted into a light and wakes, whole, on a sunlit rock beside Nina, who explains that her body died many times, the corpses being her earlier selves, and tells her to live. The camera reveals an alien world.

Critics often compared the film to Cube, and Screen Daily singled out its sound design. It holds 86% approval on Rotten Tomatoes from 14 reviews and grossed about $698,000 worldwide.

documents.title: Greenland
documents.overview: John Garrity, his estranged wife and their young son embark on a perilous journey to find sanctuary as a planet-killing comet hurtles toward Earth. Amid terrifying accounts of cities getting levelled, the Garritys experience the best and worst in humanity. As the countdown to the global apocalypse approaches zero, their incredible trek culminates in a desperate and last-minute flight to a possible safe haven.
documents.plot:
Greenland is a 2020 American post-apocalyptic disaster film directed by Ric Roman Waugh and written by Chris Bremner. The movie stars Gerard Butler, Morena Baccarin, Roger Dale Floyd, and Sienna Campbell.

The story begins with a family - John (Gerard Butler), his wife Allison (Morena Baccarin), and their 11-year-old son Caleb (Sienna Campbell) - living in Greenland with their young daughter. The family is preparing for the annual summer solstice celebration when they receive an alert from NASA about a massive asteroid hurtling towards Earth.

The asteroid, which is approximately 5 miles in diameter, is predicted to impact Earth and cause catastrophic destruction. The government has only 6 months to prepare for the impending disaster, but it's clear that this will not be enough time.

As the family tries to come to terms with their situation, they realize that they are one of the few families who have managed to escape the initial blast of the asteroid. They soon discover that the impact has caused widespread destruction and chaos around the world, with many cities being reduced to rubble.

The family sets out on a perilous journey across Greenland in search of safety and hope. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, harsh weather conditions, and other survivors who are not as trustworthy as they seem.

As the days turn into weeks, the family faces numerous challenges, including finding food and shelter, navigating through the treacherous landscape, and dealing with the emotional toll of their situation. They also encounter a group of survivors who are determined to take control of the remaining resources in Greenland.

Throughout the movie, the family's relationship is put to the test as they struggle to work together and make difficult decisions that will determine their survival. John, who has been struggling with feelings of guilt and inadequacy, must come to terms with his role as a father and leader.

As the asteroid hurtles towards Earth, the family faces an impossible decision: stay in Greenland and risk being crushed by the impact, or try to find a way to escape the planet. In the end, they make a desperate bid for survival, using their skills and ingenuity to launch themselves into space on a makeshift rocket.

The movie ends with John and Caleb floating above the Earth, watching as the asteroid impacts the planet below them. The family's fate is left uncertain, leaving the audience to wonder if they will survive or succumb to the harsh conditions of space.

Overall, Greenland is a tense and suspenseful thriller that explores themes of survival, hope, and redemption in the face of catastrophic disaster.

documents.title: The Mortuary Collection
documents.overview: In the phantasmagorical town of Raven's End, a misguided young girl takes refuge in a decrepit old mortuary. The eccentric undertaker chronicles the strange history of the town through a series of twisted tales, each more terrifying than the last, but the young girl's world is unhinged when she discovers that the final story... is her own.
documents.plot:
The Mortuary Collection is a 2020 American anthology horror film directed by Ryan Spindell and written by Ryan Spindell and Josh Stolberg. The movie consists of five segments, each with its own unique story and characters.

One of the main themes of The Mortuary Collection is the exploration of grief and loss. Each segment deals with a different character's experience of dealing with death, whether it be a personal loss or a traumatic event. The film shows how people cope with their emotions in different ways, ranging from denial to acceptance.

Another theme present in the movie is the idea of trauma and its lasting impact on individuals. Many characters in the film have experienced traumatic events in the past, which continue to haunt them in various ways throughout the story.

The Mortuary Collection also touches on the concept of mortality and the fear of death. The title itself suggests a sense of foreboding and dread, which is reflected in the film's atmosphere and tone. The characters' experiences are often marked by a sense of unease and discomfort, highlighting their deep-seated fears about dying.

The film also explores the idea of mental health and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy. Many characters struggle with their own sanity, questioning what is real and what is just a product of their imagination.

Finally, The Mortuary Collection can be seen as a commentary on the human condition, highlighting our universal experiences and emotions. Despite the different stories and characters, there are common threads that run throughout the film, making it relatable to audiences.

Overall, The Mortuary Collection is a thought-provoking horror film that explores complex themes and emotions, making it more than just a typical fright-fest.

documents.title: The Intruder
documents.overview: A psychological thriller about a young married couple who buys a beautiful Napa Valley house on several acres of land only to find that the man they bought it from refuses to let go of the property.
documents.plot:
The Intruder is a 2019 American psychological thriller directed by Deon Taylor and written by David Loughery. Michael Ealy and Meagan Good star as Scott and Annie Howard, a couple who buy a house in the country, and Dennis Quaid plays Charlie Peck, its previous owner, who cannot let it go; Joseph Sikora co-stars.

Scott and Annie buy "Foxglove", a Napa Valley house, from Charlie, who says his wife, Ellen, died of cancer two years earlier and that he is moving to Florida to live with his daughter, Cassidy. Soon after, their friend Mike senses he is being watched during an overnight visit and finds a cigarette burn on his car seat. Annie catches Charlie mowing their lawn yet invites him to Thanksgiving, and after Scott spots someone in the woods, he installs security cameras, a job Charlie tries to stop. Charlie keeps turning up uninvited, claiming he is staying at a hotel in town, and the couple quarrel over Scott's coldness toward him and Annie's sympathy. A neighbor tells Scott that Charlie's wife actually shot herself with one of his shotguns, and Charlie, increasingly obsessed with Annie, visits her whenever Scott is away.

While jogging, Scott is run down by a truck driven by Charlie, and Mike learns that Charlie sold the house only because of debts and legal trouble. With Scott in the hospital, Charlie dines with Annie, and when Mike comes to check on her, Charlie kills him with an axe. Scott discovers that Charlie never stayed at the hotel, and Cassidy, who has changed her name, tells him that her father is a pathological liar who murdered her mother when she threatened divorce. Meanwhile Annie finds a hidden door behind a linen closet leading to the cellar where Charlie has been living since the sale. Charlie knocks her out and attacks her, throws the returning Scott over a balcony and tries to strangle Annie, until she stabs him in the back. Wounded, he hunts them with a shotgun, but Scott knocks him down with a baseball bat and takes the gun, and as Annie tells a 911 dispatcher that her husband has shot an intruder, Scott kills Charlie.

Moved back a week from its planned date to avoid Avengers: Endgame, the film was released by Sony Pictures on May 3, 2019. Critics were negative, with 35% on Rotten Tomatoes and 39 on Metacritic, but it grossed $40.6 million worldwide on an $8 million budget.

documents.title: I See You
documents.overview: When a 12-year-old boy goes missing, lead investigator Greg Harper struggles to balance the pressure of the investigation and troubles with his wife, Jackie. Facing a recent affair, great strain is put on the family that slowly gnaws away at Jackie's grip on reality. But after a malicious presence manifests itself in their home and puts their son, Connor, in mortal danger, the cold, hard truth about evil in the Harper household is finally uncovered.
documents.plot:
I See You is a 2019 American horror thriller directed by Adam Randall from a screenplay by Devon Graye. It stars Helen Hunt, Jon Tenney and Judah Lewis, with Owen Teague and Libe Barer, in a story about a detective's family whose suburban home becomes the scene of increasingly unsettling events.

When ten-year-old Justin Whitter vanishes while riding his bike, detective Greg Harper leads the case with his partner, Spitzky. A green pocket knife left at the scene links the abduction to a series of crimes from fifteen years earlier, committed by a man who is now in prison. At home, Connor resents his mother for a recent affair, and strange things keep happening: objects disappear, a repairman says a daughter the Harpers do not have let him in, and Greg is locked inside a closet. When Jackie's former lover, Todd, shows up, he is struck on the head and later found dead, and Jackie, believing Connor killed him, persuades Greg to help bury the body. Soon afterward the couple find Connor tied up in the bathtub with a green knife beside him.

Flashbacks then reveal that two drifters, Mindy and Alec, have been secretly living in the house. Alec caused the disturbances to torment the family, but Mindy witnessed the true killer of Todd: Greg. Hidden in Greg's car, Mindy finds green knives and Justin's shirt, follows him into the forest and discovers the missing boys locked in a trailer, making a broken 911 call before Greg captures her and kills her at home, staging it as self-defense. Alec confronts Greg, who claims he was once a victim himself, and shoots him dead. Spitzky arrives and wounds Alec, the evidence in Greg's car exposes the truth, and the boys are rescued by tracing Mindy's call.

The film premiered in the Midnighters section of SXSW on March 13, 2019, and Saban Films released it in theaters on December 6, 2019. It grossed about $1.2 million worldwide on a $5 million budget. Reviews were favorable, with 73% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 65; critics found the twisting plot convoluted but praised the cast and its slow-building suspense.

documents.title: The Report
documents.overview: The story of Daniel Jones, lead investigator for the US Senate’s sweeping study into the CIA's Detention and Interrogation Program, which was found to be brutal, immoral and ineffective. With the truth at stake, Jones battled tirelessly to make public what many in power sought to keep hidden.
documents.plot:
The Report is a 2019 American thriller film directed by Scott Z. Burns, starring Adam Driver as Daniel J. Jones, a Senate staffer who uncovers the CIA's use of torture during the George W. Bush administration.

The main themes of The Report include:

1. **Government Accountability and Transparency**: The film highlights the importance of holding those in power accountable for their actions. Daniel J. Jones' investigation into the CIA's torture program exposes the agency's wrongdoing, leading to a re-evaluation of its policies.
2. **Torture and Its Consequences**: The movie delves into the moral implications of torture, both on individuals and society as a whole. It raises questions about the nature of truth, the limits of human endurance, and the long-term effects of trauma on those who have been subjected to it.
3. **The Power of Investigative Journalism**: The Report showcases the crucial role that investigative journalists play in uncovering and exposing government wrongdoing. Daniel J. Jones' work serves as a testament to the importance of a free press in holding those in power accountable.
4. **The Complexity of Morality**: Throughout the film, characters grapple with complex moral dilemmas, often finding themselves torn between their personal values and the demands of their profession. This theme adds depth to the narrative, encouraging viewers to consider the nuances of right and wrong.
5. **The Legacy of 9/11 and the War on Terror**: The Report is set against the backdrop of the post-9/11 era, exploring the consequences of the War on Terror and the subsequent erosion of civil liberties. The film serves as a commentary on the ongoing debate about national security, individual freedoms, and the role of government in times of crisis.

Overall, The Report is a thought-provoking thriller that challenges viewers to confront the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of unchecked power.

documents.title: Eternals
documents.overview: The Eternals are a team of ancient aliens who have been living on Earth in secret for thousands of years. When an unexpected tragedy forces them out of the shadows, they are forced to reunite against mankind’s most ancient enemy, the Deviants.
documents.plot:
Eternals is a 2021 superhero film directed by Chloé Zhao, produced by Marvel Studios, and based on the Marvel Comics series of the same name. The movie follows an ancient group of immortal beings known as the Eternals, who have been living among humans for thousands of years.

The story begins with the introduction of Ikaris (Richard Madden), a powerful Eternal who has been hiding in plain sight on Earth. He is joined by his sister Sersi (Gemma Chan), who was once a mortal but gained immortality after being transformed by her brother's powers. The two Eternals are part of a larger group, including Kingo (Kit Harington), Ajak (Salma Hayek), Makkari (Lauren Ridloff), Phastos (Brian Tyree Henry), and Sprite (Lia McHugh).

The Eternals have been watching over humanity for centuries, protecting them from the Deviants, monstrous creatures that threaten to destroy the world. However, a new threat emerges in the form of Gilgamesh (Don Lee), a powerful Deviant who seeks to destroy humanity.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the Eternals' past is shrouded in mystery and tragedy. The group's leader, Ajak, has been keeping secrets about their history, which are slowly revealed throughout the film. It is also revealed that the Eternals have a complex relationship with humans, often walking a fine line between helping and harming them.

The movie takes a dramatic turn when Sersi discovers her true identity as an Eternal and begins to question her place in the world. Ikaris's actions become increasingly erratic, leading to a confrontation with his sister that puts the entire group at risk.

Throughout the film, Zhao explores themes of identity, community, and the weight of secrets. The Eternals are a complex and flawed group, struggling to come to terms with their own mortality (or lack thereof). The movie's climax features an epic battle between the Eternals and the Deviants, which serves as a turning point for the characters.

Ultimately, Eternals is a film about finding one's place in the world and embracing one's true identity. It is a visually stunning and action-packed adventure that explores the complexities of the Marvel Cinematic Universe.

documents.title: Blindsided: The Game
documents.overview: After blind man Walter Cooke (Eric Jacobus) prevents a local gang from shaking down his local grocer Gordon (Roger Yuan), Walter must reckon with the gang's boss Sal (Joe Bucaro). The stakes are high, but Walter's got an ace up his sleeve.
documents.plot:
Blindsided: The Game is a 2018 American action comedy short film directed by Clayton J. Barber, who wrote it with its star, the martial artist and stunt performer Eric Jacobus. Running about 46 minutes, it expands the twelve-minute short Blindsided, released the previous year, into a longer story after Jacobus's production company secured funding to continue it. The cast includes Roger Yuan, Joe Bucaro III, David William No, Michelle Lee, Pete Antico, Khalid Ghajji, Nicholas Verdi, Justin Hall and the veteran stuntman and fight choreographer Luke LaFontaine. Jacobus oversaw the action, with Yuan, LaFontaine and No, who also served as a producer, contributing to the fight choreography, and the score is by Steffan Schmidt and Raymond Lane. The film was released free to stream on YouTube on 17 May 2018.

Walter Cooke (Jacobus) is a blind man living in a modern American city, an apple pie enthusiast with a knack for sensing danger. Underestimated and brushed aside by a local gang while shopping at his neighbourhood grocery, he comes to the aid of its owner Gordon (Yuan), his friend, who is deep in debt to the gangsters. Surprising both Gordon and the thugs with his physical abilities, Walter sends them packing in an alley fight in which he puts his white cane to good use. This is where the original short ended and where The Game picks up. Following the gangsters back to their boss, Sal (Bucaro), Walter and Gordon get further into trouble, and elements of Gordon's own past come to light in connection with the villains. The stakes rise, but Walter has an ace up his sleeve, and the confrontation eventually leads the pair to take on the toughs in their own warehouse, where Gordon must fight alongside Walter against an array of opponents armed with guns and blades. Walter himself remains something of an enigma, with hints of a deeper history left for possible future stories.

Reviewers from action-focused outlets welcomed it as a homage to the blind swordsman genre, especially Zatoichi and Blind Fury. Cinapse called it enjoyable, praising the basic character work that adds heart and comedy between the set pieces and Jacobus's physical and comedic talents, and recommended it to action devotees and fans of the sub-genre. Film Combat Syndicate praised its blend of slapstick and intense fight scenes and its warm portrayal of Walter and Gordon's friendship, while noting that the short format leaves Walter's background largely unexplored.

documents.title: May the Devil Take You
documents.overview: Hoping to find answers to her estranged father's mysterious illness, a young woman visits his old villa and uncovers a horrifying truth from the past.
documents.plot:
May the Devil Take You is a 2018 Thai horror film directed by Pong Jitjira and produced by Legacy Pictures.

The movie revolves around a young woman named Nai, who returns to her hometown after being away for several years. She reunites with her childhood friends, including her best friend, Poo, but their reunion is short-lived as they soon discover that the town has been plagued by supernatural events and mysterious disappearances.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the town's dark past and a series of tragic events have awakened an ancient evil force. The film explores themes of trauma, grief, and the consequences of unresolved emotions. Nai's character is particularly affected by her own traumatic experiences, which are slowly revealed throughout the movie.

The film also touches on the idea of guilt and responsibility, as the characters grapple with their past mistakes and try to make amends. The supernatural elements serve as a metaphor for the destructive power of unchecked emotions and the devastating consequences of ignoring one's inner demons.

Throughout the movie, the atmosphere is tense and foreboding, building towards a shocking climax that explores the true nature of evil and its ability to consume even the strongest individuals. Overall, May the Devil Take You is a thought-provoking horror film that delves into the darker aspects of human psychology and the devastating consequences of unresolved trauma.

documents.title: A Christmas Prince: The Royal Wedding
documents.original_title: A Christmas Prince: The Royal Wedding
documents.overview: A year after Amber helped Richard secure the crown. The two are set to tie the knot in a royal Christmas wedding — but their plans are jeopardized when Amber finds herself second-guessing whether or not she's cut out to be queen, and Richard is faced with a political crisis that threatens to tarnish not only the holiday season but the future of the kingdom.
documents.plot:
A Christmas Prince: The Royal Wedding is a heartwarming and romantic film that explores the theme of self-discovery and growth, particularly for its protagonist, Amber. As she navigates her new role as a princess, Amber must confront her own identity and values, learning to balance her royal duties with her personal aspirations.

The movie also delves into the theme of love and relationships, showcasing the blossoming romance between Amber and Simon, the prince. Their relationship serves as a catalyst for growth and change in both characters, highlighting the importance of communication, trust, and mutual respect in any partnership.

Furthermore, the film touches on the theme of family and tradition, particularly in the context of royal families. The movie pokes fun at the conventions and expectations that come with royal life, while also celebrating the importance of heritage and legacy.

Ultimately, A Christmas Prince: The Royal Wedding is a feel-good film that celebrates the power of love, self-discovery, and personal growth, making it a delightful watch for audiences during the holiday season.

documents.title: Welcome Home
documents.overview: A couple try to repair their damaged union in an Italian vacation paradise. Then they discover the owner's intentions.
documents.plot:
Welcome Home is a 2018 thriller film directed by George Ratliff from a screenplay by David Levinson, produced by Allan Mandelbaum, Tim White and Trevor White for Voltage Pictures. Aaron Paul and Emily Ratajkowski, cast in April 2017, play a troubled couple who hope a romantic getaway to Italy will save their relationship, with Riccardo Scamarcio in a supporting role as Federico. The first trailer appeared in October 2018, and the film went to video on demand in November 2018 without a North American theatrical run.

Bryan and Cassie rent a house in Umbria in an effort to repair their relationship after Cassie was caught having drunken sex with a co-worker, an episode that has left Bryan impotent. While out running, Cassie hurts her ankle and is helped by Federico, a handsome stranger who drives her back and offers them a ride into town the next day. After a tense trip, Bryan accuses Cassie of failing to notice how Federico leers at her, and she storms off. Federico joins Bryan at a bar, secretly drugs his drink and arranges for two women to take him to a hotel, where Bryan has sex with them but later remembers nothing. Federico, it emerges, has hidden cameras throughout the house and watches the couple constantly.

Bryan discovers that Federico is not their neighbor, as he claimed, and when he threatens to expose him, Federico threatens to tell Cassie about the hotel. Cassie warms to Federico until an unsettling dinner of rabbit stew. Enraged after watching the couple reconcile, Federico locks Bryan in the cellar, tricks a blindfolded Cassie into letting him kiss and grope her while filming it, then leaves Bryan's phone playing the hotel video for her to find. The couple's furious argument ends when a thrown phone shatters a mirror and reveals a hidden camera. Federico arrives and attacks Bryan with a knife, and Cassie beats him to death with a cane. Eduardo, the owner of the house, then arrives and reveals himself as Federico's accomplice, but Cassie stabs him and Bryan shoots him. Bryan finds recordings of many other couples, and the pair burn the tapes, bury the bodies and vow silence, unaware that a camera hidden in a garden gnome is streaming them to viewers worldwide, part of a global network of similarly wired rentals.

Francesco Acquaroli plays Eduardo. Critics were unenthusiastic, with 10% approval on Rotten Tomatoes from ten reviews and a Metacritic score of 38. The film earned about $332,000 from foreign release.

documents.title: The Bouncer
documents.overview: A tough nightclub bouncer struggling to raise his 8-year-old daughter is forced to go undercover after an unfortunate event.
documents.plot:
The Bouncer (original title: Lukas) is a 2018 French-Belgian action thriller film directed by Julien Leclercq and starring Jean-Claude Van Damme, Sveva Alviti, Sami Bouajila, Alice Verset and Sam Louwyck. Set in Belgium, it follows a nightclub bouncer who is coerced into helping the authorities bring down a crime boss. The original European version, released as Lukas, is mostly in French with some Flemish and English, while the version released a year later in the United States as The Bouncer had some scenes cut and was dubbed into English.

Lukas fled South Africa after the death of his wife and now lives quietly in his native Belgium with his eight-year-old daughter, Sarah, working as a bouncer at a nightclub. One night he restrains an aggressive patron who then badly injures himself while trying to attack him. Because the injured man is the son of a member of the European Parliament, Lukas loses his job and comes under investigation by a mysterious officer named Maxim, who gives him a choice: go to prison, or go undercover at a strip club owned by Jan Dekkers, an organized crime figure, and spy on him. Lukas reluctantly agrees and soon finds himself drawn into Jan's world. His first job is to drive Lisa, an Italian woman once indicted for forgery, and he gradually learns that Jan is planning a large counterfeiting operation. Meanwhile his daughter is taken into the care of social services, and Lukas realizes that cooperating may be the only way to get her back. He is sent on increasingly dangerous assignments, including the kidnapping of a drug cook to be traded to Dutch gangsters for the special watermarked paper needed to print banknotes, a deal that turns violent. When Lukas tries to quit, Maxim threatens to send him back to South Africa, to face punishment for what he did after his wife's killers went unpunished by the police. Caught between the police and the criminals, and forming a cautious bond with Lisa, who has her own reasons to escape her past, Lukas must stay alive long enough to see the operation through and protect his daughter.

The film received generally positive reviews from critics, and on Rotten Tomatoes it holds a 100% approval rating based on five reviews. The cast also includes Kevin Janssens, with Van Damme in the title role of Lukas.

documents.title: Daughter of the Wolf
documents.tagline: In the Wild, Only the Strong Survive
documents.overview: Ex-military specialist Clair Hamilton returns home from her tour in the Middle East due to her father's passing and to claim her inheritance. Her son is then kidnapped and held for ransom by a gang led by a mysterious figure known only as “Father”.
documents.plot:
Daughter of the Wolf is a 2019 Canadian action thriller directed by David Hackl and written by Nika Agiashvili. Gina Carano stars as Clair Hamilton, a military veteran fighting to rescue her kidnapped son, with Richard Dreyfuss as the kidnappers' leader, known only as Father, Brendan Fehr as Larsen, Sydelle Noel as Hobbs and Anton Gillis-Adelman as the boy, Charlie. It was shot in the spring of 2019 around West Kelowna, British Columbia.

Clair arrives at a remote exchange with a bag of ransom money, only to be double-crossed. In the shootout she kills two of the gang, and while chasing the third, Larsen, she falls through the ice of a frozen lake. Larsen, who never meant for anyone to die, pulls her out. Recovering, Clair has a calm encounter with a black wolf, then catches Larsen and forces him to lead her to her son. Father, it emerges, holds a grudge against Clair's father for shutting down a mill and leaving with money owed to him. Along the way a gunman ambushes them but is killed by wolves, and Larsen confesses that Father murdered his own father and abducted him and his mother when he was a child.

The gang has moved Charlie to a lodge across the mountain to sell him. When Clair tries to trade the money and Larsen for the boy, Father fires at Charlie, and Larsen takes the bullet. Clair escapes on a snowmobile but is chased by Hobbs, loses a knife fight and goes over a waterfall, while Charlie is recaptured. Guided by wolves through the forest, she returns to the lodge, where Father is torturing Larsen. She kills Hobbs and the remaining gang, and in a final struggle pushes Father through a window. Larsen dies, Clair flees with Charlie, and wolves descend on Father in the snow. Months later, hiking in spring, Clair sees the black wolf again.

The film was released in the United States on 14 June 2019 and in Canada that August, and screened at the Taormina Film Fest. Reviews were largely negative, with a 25% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 36. The Hollywood Reporter called it a subpar vehicle for its star, though Variety praised it as a capably crafted, female-led action film.

documents.title: Bombshell
documents.overview: Bombshell is a revealing look inside the most powerful and controversial media empire of all time; and the explosive story of the women who brought down the infamous man who created it.
documents.plot:
Bombshell is a 2019 American biographical drama film directed by Jay Roach, written by Charles Randolph, and produced by Charlize Theron, Aaron Ryder, and Teri Segal. The film is based on the book "Fire and Reckoning: Inside the World of Fox News" by Byron York.

The film takes place in 1996-1997 and focuses on the lives of three women who worked at Fox News Channel during its early years: Megyn Kelly (played by Charlize Theron), Gretchen Carlson (played by Nicole Kidman), and Kayla Pospisil (played by Allison Janney).

The film begins with a dramatic sequence showing the 1996 presidential election, where Republican candidate Bob Dole loses to Democratic candidate Bill Clinton. The scene then shifts to Fox News Channel's launch in October 1996, where Megyn Kelly is hired as a news anchor.

As the story unfolds, we see how Megyn Kelly navigates her way through the male-dominated world of Fox News, facing sexism and misogyny from her colleagues, including Roger Ailes (played by Jodie Foster), the channel's CEO. Despite these challenges, Kelly proves herself to be a talented journalist and becomes one of the network's top anchors.

Meanwhile, Gretchen Carlson is introduced as a rising star at Fox News, where she works alongside Megyn Kelly. However, her career is soon derailed when she accuses Roger Ailes of sexual harassment. The film depicts the intense pressure and fear that Carlson faces as she decides to take on Ailes, who has significant power over her career.

As the story progresses, we see how Kayla Pospisil, a young producer at Fox News, becomes embroiled in the scandal surrounding Roger Ailes' behavior. She is one of the few women who speak out against him, and her bravery inspires others to do the same.

The film's climax features a dramatic confrontation between Gretchen Carlson and Roger Ailes, where she accuses him of sexual harassment and demands that he resign from his position as CEO of Fox News. The scene is intense and emotional, with both characters delivering powerful performances.

In the aftermath of Ailes' resignation, the film shows how the women at Fox News Channel come together to support each other and rebuild their careers. Megyn Kelly becomes a leading voice for women's rights and feminism, while Gretchen Carlson finds new success as a lawyer and advocate.

The film ends with a sense of hope and renewal, as the women at Fox News Channel look towards a brighter future. The final scene shows Kayla Pospisil, now a successful journalist in her own right, reflecting on the lessons she learned from her experience at Fox News.

Overall, Bombshell is a powerful and timely film that sheds light on the struggles faced by women in the male-dominated world of journalism. With outstanding performances from its cast, including Charlize Theron, Nicole Kidman, and Allison Janney, the film is a must-see for anyone interested in politics, media, or feminism.

documents.title: The Night Clerk
documents.overview: Hotel night clerk Bart Bromley is a highly intelligent young man on the Autism spectrum. When a woman is murdered during his shift, Bart becomes the prime suspect. As the police investigation closes in, Bart makes a personal connection with a beautiful guest named Andrea, but soon realises he must stop the real murderer before she becomes the next victim.
documents.plot:
The Night Clerk is a 2020 American crime drama film written and directed by Michael Cristofer. It stars Tye Sheridan as Bart Bromley, a hotel night clerk who becomes the center of a murder investigation, with Ana de Armas as Andrea Rivera, John Leguizamo as Detective Espada, Helen Hunt as Bart's mother Ethel and Johnathon Schaech as Detective Nick Perretti.

Bart, a young man with Asperger syndrome who lives with his mother, works the night shift at a hotel, where he secretly places cameras in a guest room and studies the recordings to imitate the speech and mannerisms of the guests and overcome his social awkwardness. One night, after his shift, he watches from home as a new guest, Karen, lets a man into her room, argues with him and is beaten. Seeing a gun fall from her purse, Bart races back to the hotel. Soon after, his co-worker Jack hears a gunshot and finds Karen dead with Bart sitting on the bed. While Jack calls 911, Bart removes his cameras but leaves behind a storage card. Questioned by Detective Espada, Bart claims he returned to the hotel for his forgotten wallet, a lie Espada sees through because Bart had just bought ice cream. Reviewing his recording, Bart notices that the killer had a bird tattoo on his arm.

Reassigned to another hotel, Bart meets Andrea Rivera, a guest who recognizes his condition and flirts with him. He hides cameras in her room, and they share a kiss by the pool. Smitten, he gets a haircut, a new suit and a new car, but then sees Andrea in bed with the man with the bird tattoo. The police seize his equipment, though Bart has kept a hidden copy of the recording of Karen's room. The man is Karen's husband, Nick, a detective having an affair with Andrea, who wants her to get rid of Bart. When Bart sees Nick beating Andrea on camera, he rushes to help and shows her the recording proving that Nick killed Karen. She weeps and falls asleep in his bed, but the next morning she is gone with the hard drive, leaving behind Karen's gun. As Andrea and Nick drive out of town, the police find that Bart has left the gun, the camera storage cards and a note for Espada, and the couple are pulled over. Bart walks through a mall, practising the conversational skills he has learned from his recordings.

Saban Films released The Night Clerk on February 21, 2020, and it reached Netflix's Top Ten after arriving on the service in June. Reviews were unfavorable, with 34% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 44.

documents.title: Like a Boss
documents.tagline: The world of beauty is about to get ugly.
documents.overview: Two female friends with very different ideals decide to start a beauty company together. One is more practical, while the other wants to earn her fortune and live a lavish lifestyle.
documents.plot:
Like a Boss is a 2020 American comedy film directed by Miguel Arteta and written by Susanna Fogel and Kay Cannon. The movie stars Tiffany Haddish, Rose Byrne, and Salma Hayek as three friends who start a beauty company together.

The main themes of Like a Boss revolve around female friendship, entrepreneurship, and the challenges faced by women in male-dominated industries. The film explores the complexities of female relationships, particularly those between close friends, as they navigate their personal and professional lives.

Throughout the movie, the characters face various obstacles, including sexism, competition, and self-doubt. However, they ultimately learn to support each other and work together to achieve their goals. The film celebrates the power of female friendship and the importance of women lifting each other up in a world that often tries to tear them down.

The movie also touches on themes of identity, ambition, and the struggle for balance between personal and professional life. As the characters navigate their careers and relationships, they must confront their own desires, values, and priorities.

Overall, Like a Boss is a heartwarming and humorous film that explores the complexities of female friendship and entrepreneurship in a way that is both relatable and entertaining.

documents.title: Little
documents.overview: Jordan Sanders, a take-no-prisoners tech mogul, wakes up one morning in the body of her 13-year-old self right before a do-or-die presentation. Her beleaguered assistant April is the only one in on the secret that her daily tormentor is now trapped in an awkward tween body, just as everything is on the line.
documents.plot:
Little (2019) is a fantasy comedy film directed by Tina Gordon, written by Tracy Oliver, and produced by Will Packer and Marc E. Platt.

The movie takes place on March 8th, which is International Women's Day, and follows the story of Maureen "Ma" Johnson (played by Regina Hall), a successful businesswoman who has just been passed over for a promotion at her company. Feeling frustrated and underappreciated, Ma decides to take revenge on her sexist boss, James King (played by Dan Aykroyd).

As she walks out of the office building, Ma is suddenly transported back in time to March 8th, 1982, when she was just a teenager. She finds herself reliving memories from her past, including her high school days and her relationships with her friends and family.

In this alternate timeline, Ma discovers that she has the ability to see and interact with the inner thoughts of women throughout history, including Frida Kahlo (played by Patricia Arquette), Rosa Parks (played by Regina King), and Susan B. Anthony (played by Danielle Brooks). These powerful women become her allies and mentors, guiding her on a journey of self-discovery and empowerment.

As Ma navigates this new reality, she also meets a young version of herself, played by Storm Reid, who is struggling to find her place in the world. Through her interactions with her past and present selves, Ma learns valuable lessons about feminism, identity, and the importance of supporting women.

Throughout the movie, Little features a talented ensemble cast, including Lyriq Bent, Marsai Martin, and Brian Tyree Henry. The film's humor is witty and relatable, making it an enjoyable watch for audiences of all ages.

As Ma continues to explore her past and present selves, she begins to realize that her experiences are not just about personal growth but also about the collective progress of women throughout history. In the end, Ma returns to her own time, armed with a newfound sense of confidence and purpose.

The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Ma embracing her inner strength and using it to inspire others. The final shot is of Ma walking out of the office building, ready to take on the world as a powerful and empowered woman.

Overall, Little (2019) is a heartwarming and entertaining film that celebrates women's empowerment and the importance of female friendships. With its talented cast, witty humor, and inspiring message, it's a must-watch for anyone looking for a feel-good movie experience.

documents.title: Look Away
documents.overview: A timid and socially alienated 17-year-old high school student's life is turned upside down when she switches places with her sinister mirror image.
documents.plot:
Look Away is a 2018 American drama film directed by Michael McDonald. The movie revolves around a young woman named Rachel, who becomes involved with a charismatic but troubled man named Darryl. As their relationship deepens, Rachel finds herself drawn into Darryl's world of crime and deception.

The main theme of Look Away is the destructive nature of toxic relationships and the ways in which they can consume and destroy individuals. The film explores how Rachel's desire for love and connection leads her to overlook the warning signs of Darryl's problematic behavior, ultimately putting herself in harm's way.

Through Rachel's character, the movie also touches on themes of vulnerability, naivety, and the struggle to break free from patterns of self-destructive behavior. The film raises questions about the complexities of human relationships and the ways in which we can both hurt and help each other.

The movie also delves into the darker aspects of human nature, revealing a world where crime and deception are often intertwined with charm and charisma. This dichotomy serves as a commentary on the societal pressures that can lead individuals to engage in destructive behavior, and the ways in which these behaviors can be normalized or even romanticized.

Overall, Look Away is a thought-provoking drama that explores the complexities of human relationships, vulnerability, and the struggle to break free from patterns of self-destructive behavior.

documents.title: Made in Abyss: Journey's Dawn
documents.original_title: 劇場版総集編【前編】メイドインアビス 旅立ちの夜明け
documents.overview: First compilation movie of the TV series which covers episodes 1-8 with new scenes added for the introduction. It covers the period from when Riko descends into the Abyss with her robot companion Reg, reaching the second layer where they meet the White Whistle Ozen who reveals information about Riko's mother.
documents.plot:
Made in Abyss: Journey's Dawn is an anime film that delves into the complexities of human existence, particularly in the context of exploration and discovery. The story revolves around Riko, a young girl who embarks on a perilous journey to the bottom of a mysterious abyss with her friend Reg.

At its core, Made in Abyss: Journey's Dawn explores the theme of existentialism, where characters are forced to confront the meaninglessness of their existence and the impermanence of life. The abyss serves as a metaphor for the unknown, representing the vast and uncharted territories that lie beyond human understanding.

The film also touches on the idea of obsession and fixation, as Riko's determination to reach the bottom of the abyss becomes an all-consuming force in her life. This theme is intertwined with the concept of sacrifice, as characters are willing to risk everything for the sake of discovery and progress.

Furthermore, Made in Abyss: Journey's Dawn examines the complexities of human relationships and the bonds that form between individuals. Riko and Reg's friendship serves as a beacon of hope and comfort in an otherwise desolate world, highlighting the importance of emotional connections in the face of adversity.

Ultimately, the film presents a poignant exploration of the human condition, one that is marked by both beauty and brutality, wonder and despair. Through its thought-provoking narrative and stunning visuals, Made in Abyss: Journey's Dawn invites viewers to reflect on their own place within the world and the significance of their existence.

documents.title: Made in Abyss: Wandering Twilight
documents.original_title: 劇場版総集編【後編】メイドインアビス 放浪する黄昏
documents.overview: Second compilation movie of the TV series which covers episodes 9-13. Riko and Reg descend to the third and fourth layer where Riko has her first experience of the Curse.
documents.plot:
Made in Abyss: Wandering Twilight is an anime film that delves into the complexities of human existence, particularly in the context of exploration and discovery. The story follows Riko, a young girl who embarks on a perilous journey to the bottom of a mysterious abyss, accompanied by her companion Reg.

At its core, Made in Abyss: Wandering Twilight explores the theme of existentialism, where the protagonist's quest for answers about the nature of existence and the meaning of life becomes an all-consuming force. Riko's journey is not just about uncovering secrets but also about confronting the darkness within herself and the world around her.

The film also touches on the idea of loneliness and isolation, as Riko navigates the desolate landscape of the abyss, often finding herself disconnected from others and forced to rely solely on her own wits and determination. This sense of solitude serves as a catalyst for introspection, allowing Riko to grapple with her own emotions and the weight of her responsibilities.

Furthermore, Made in Abyss: Wandering Twilight examines the concept of sacrifice and the true cost of ambition. Reg's unwavering dedication to Riko and their shared quest raises questions about the nature of love, loyalty, and the sacrifices one is willing to make for others.

Throughout the film, the director weaves together these themes with a sense of wonder and awe, capturing the beauty and mystery of the abyss as a metaphor for the unknown and the unexplored aspects of human experience. Ultimately, Made in Abyss: Wandering Twilight presents a poignant and thought-provoking exploration of what it means to be human, to search for meaning, and to confront the darkness that lies within ourselves and the world around us.

documents.title: Black Beauty
documents.overview: Born free in the American West, Black Beauty is a horse rounded up and brought to Birtwick Stables, where she meets spirited teenager Jo Green. The two forge a bond that carries Beauty through the different chapters, challenges and adventures.
documents.plot:
Black Beauty is a 2020 family adventure drama film written, edited and directed by Ashley Avis, the sixth screen adaptation of Anna Sewell's 1877 novel. A co-production between the United States, the United Kingdom, South Africa, France and Germany, it recasts the title horse as a mare. Kate Winslet voices Black Beauty, with Mackenzie Foy as Jo Green, Iain Glen as her uncle John Manly, Calam Lynch as George Winthorp, Fern Deacon as his sister Georgina and Claire Forlani as their mother.

A wild mustang born in Utah's Onaqui Mountains narrates her life, remembering her mother's lesson that horses who die fly up to rest among the stars. Cowboys round up her herd, and she is bought by John Manly, a patient trainer who takes her to Birtwick, a horse sanctuary, where she befriends the horses Ginger and Merrylegs. When John's sister and her husband die in a car accident, he takes in his grieving teenage niece, Jo. Jo shuns her uncle but is drawn to the defiant mustang; recognizing each other's pain, the two bond, and Jo tames her and names her Black Beauty, learning to "partner" rather than "break" a horse. After a stable fire, with Birtwick losing money, Jo works extra hours to save up to buy Beauty. The wealthy Winthorps lease Beauty for their daughter Georgina, who treats her cruelly, while their kind son George, who rides Ginger, takes an interest in Jo. Georgina's reckless riding in a race injures Beauty, and the horse is returned, but Birtwick soon closes and Beauty is sold before Jo can say goodbye. Beauty passes from a ranger, Terry, to a farmer who works her hard and then to a kindly New York carriage driver, Jerry. She briefly reunites with Ginger, who dies soon afterwards. When Jerry falls ill, Beauty is sold to a cruel carriage company involved in illegal horse trading, and after glimpsing Ginger's body being carted away, she sits down in the road in grief, drawing media attention. A stable boy, Manuel, reports the company to the police, and Jo, who has searched for her all along, finds her. Jo has rebuilt Birtwick with John and George, now her husband, to rehabilitate horses, and Beauty spends the rest of her life there, reunited with Merrylegs.

Planned for cinemas, the film was acquired by Disney from Constantin Film and released on Disney+ on 27 November 2020. Reviews were mixed, with 48% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 52.

documents.title: Simple Passion
documents.overview: A man and a woman are brought together by chance for several months. He is younger than she is, married, Russian, officially a diplomat stationed in Paris. She is a beautiful teacher and researcher, with her feet firmly on the ground. The film follows the evolution of their love, from the beginning to end.
documents.plot:
Simple Passion is a 2021 French drama film directed by François Ozon, not Versus Production. 

The movie follows the story of Camille, a young woman who returns to her hometown in rural France after a long absence. She reconnects with her childhood friend and former flame, Pierre, and they rekindle their romance. However, as their relationship deepens, Camille's past and present begin to collide.

The main themes of Simple Passion include:

1. Unresolved emotions: The film explores the complexities of unrequited love, nostalgia, and the difficulty of moving on from past relationships.
2. Identity and belonging: Camille's journey is also one of self-discovery, as she navigates her place in the world and grapples with feelings of disconnection and longing for a sense of home.
3. The power of memories: The film highlights the significance of memories and experiences in shaping our identities and relationships, particularly those from childhood and adolescence.

Through Camille's story, Simple Passion offers a nuanced exploration of human emotions, relationships, and the complexities of growing up and finding one's place in the world.

documents.title: Morbius
documents.overview: Dangerously ill with a rare blood disorder, and determined to save others suffering his same fate, Dr. Michael Morbius attempts a desperate gamble. What at first appears to be a radical success soon reveals itself to be a remedy potentially worse than the disease.
documents.plot:
Morbius is a 2022 American superhero film based on the Marvel Comics character, produced by Columbia Pictures and distributed by Sony as the third film in Sony's Spider-Man Universe. Directed by Daniel Espinosa and written by Matt Sazama and Burk Sharpless, it stars Jared Leto as Dr. Michael Morbius, alongside Matt Smith as Milo, Adria Arjona as Martine Bancroft, Jared Harris as Dr. Emil Nicholas, Al Madrigal and Tyrese Gibson as FBI agents.

As a boy in a Greek hospital, Michael Morbius befriends another child, whom he names Milo; both suffer from a rare blood disease and dream of being normal. Their adoptive father, the hospital's director, sends the gifted Michael to study medicine in New York. Twenty-five years later, Michael is a renowned scientist who has declined a Nobel Prize for his work on artificial blood. Secretly, he has captured vampire bats in Costa Rica, hoping to splice their genes with his own to cure his condition.

With money from the wealthy Milo, Michael conducts his experiment aboard a ship in international waters. The treatment cures him but turns him into a vampire-like creature with superhuman strength, speed and echolocation, and he kills the ship's crew in a frenzy of bloodlust. Back in New York, he tries to control his hunger with artificial blood while FBI agents investigate the killings. When Milo discovers the cure, he takes it himself and embraces his new powers, killing without remorse. Michael, who refuses to give in to his thirst for human blood, develops an antibody to stop his brother, leading to a final confrontation after Milo kills those closest to him. In mid-credits scenes, the Spider-Man villain Adrian Toomes arrives in Michael's universe.

After being delayed several times from its original July 2020 date, mainly because of the COVID-19 pandemic, Morbius was released in the United States on April 1, 2022.

The film grossed 167.5 million dollars worldwide and suffered one of the steepest second-weekend drops ever for a superhero film. Critics panned its writing, visual effects and post-credits scenes, giving it 15 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 35. It became the subject of mocking internet memes, which led Sony to re-release it in June 2022, again with poor results. At the Golden Raspberry Awards, Leto won Worst Actor and Arjona Worst Supporting Actress.

documents.title: The Silence
