The Outpost is a 2019 American war film directed by Rod Lurie and based on the 2012 nonfiction book The Outpost: An Untold Story of American Valor by Jake Tapper. It depicts the Battle of Kamdesh in Afghanistan and stars Scott Eastwood as Staff Sergeant Clint Romesha, Caleb Landry Jones as Specialist Ty Carter and Orlando Bloom as Captain Ben Keating, with Jack Kesy, Cory Hardrict, Milo Gibson, Jacob Scipio and Taylor John Smith. Several veterans of the battle, including Ty Carter and Daniel Rodriguez, appear in the film.

The story is set at Combat Outpost Keating, a small American base built at the bottom of a deep valley in eastern Afghanistan and surrounded by steep mountains, which leaves it exposed to constant attack. Romesha and a group of new soldiers arrive under the command of Captain Keating, who tries to win over local elders by offering money for infrastructure projects in exchange for peace. Daily life at the post alternates between boredom, tension and sudden Taliban fire from the heights above.

As commanders come and go, including after deaths among the officers, the soldiers grow increasingly aware of how vulnerable their position is. Warnings from the base's Afghan interpreter about a large-scale assault are dismissed, and news that the outpost will soon be closed does little to ease the pressure. On October 3, 2009, hundreds of Taliban fighters launch a massive coordinated attack. Outnumbered and pinned down, the small group of American soldiers and their Afghan allies fight for hours to hold the outpost, rescue wounded comrades and retake lost ground, in a battle that would leave eight Americans dead.

The film is noted for its long, immersive and chaotic depiction of the battle, and it honors the unit that became one of the most decorated of the war, with Romesha and Carter each receiving the Medal of Honor.

The Outpost premiered at the Thessaloniki International Film Festival in November 2019 and was released in the United States on premium video on demand and in select theaters on July 3, 2020, by Screen Media Films, topping the iTunes rental chart. It was acclaimed by critics, with 93 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 71.

documents.title: Open 24 Hours
documents.tagline: Pray you never run out of gas...
documents.overview: After setting her serial killer boyfriend on fire, a paranoid delusional woman gets a job at an all-night gas station. The isolation triggers her anxiety and hallucinations, with devastatingly gory results.
documents.plot:
Open 24 Hours is a 2018 slasher film written and directed by Padraig Reynolds. An international co-production between Canada and Serbia, it stars Vanessa Grasse, Emily Tennant, Brendan Fletcher, Cole Vigue and Daniel O'Meara, and was screened at the 2018 Fantastic Fest.

Mary was sent to prison for setting her boyfriend, James Lincoln Fields, on fire after discovering that he was a serial killer known as the "Rain Ripper", who forced her to watch his murders while playing the song "Raindrops" by Dee Clark. Now out on parole, she takes a job working the 10 pm to 6 am shift at the Deer Gas Market, an isolated 24-hour gas station. James, still in prison, torments her by calling whenever it rains and playing the song down the line, and she suffers from vivid hallucinations of him that she keeps in check with medication. On her first night, her coworker Bobby shows her the ropes and her childhood friend Debbie stops by to see her, but after leaving, Debbie is dragged away by a hooded attacker. As the shift goes on, Mary deals with a sleazy trucker who leaves his credit card behind on purpose, receives strange phone calls from a woman asking when the store closes and finds Debbie's driver's license in the outside toilet, setting off a terrifying hallucination. Unable to reach her parole officer, Tom, she begins to doubt her own sanity, especially when James appears before her and insists that he is real, promising that people will die and that she will watch. When a woman arrives at the pumps and attacks Mary with a knife, the night turns into a desperate fight for survival, as Mary learns that the danger is far from imaginary and that the man she once tried to destroy may have come back to finish what he started.

The film received mixed reviews from critics and holds a 45% rating on Rotten Tomatoes. Almost all of the action unfolds in and around the gas station during Mary's first night shift, with the climax spilling out into an old wrecking yard nearby before returning to the store.

documents.title: Pinocchio
documents.overview: A wooden puppet embarks on a thrilling adventure to become a real boy.
documents.plot:
Pinocchio is a 2022 American musical fantasy film directed by Robert Zemeckis, who wrote it with Chris Weitz, a live-action remake of Walt Disney's 1940 animated film based on the 1883 book The Adventures of Pinocchio. Tom Hanks stars as Geppetto, with Cynthia Erivo, Giuseppe Battiston and Luke Evans, and the voices of Benjamin Evan Ainsworth as Pinocchio, Joseph Gordon-Levitt as Jiminy Cricket, Keegan-Michael Key as Honest John and Lorraine Bracco.

In a small Italian village in the 19th century, the wandering cricket Jiminy enters the home of Geppetto, a widowed woodcarver who has just finished a puppet modeled on his late son, which he names Pinocchio. Geppetto wishes on a star, and that night the puppet comes to life. The Blue Fairy tells Pinocchio that if he proves himself brave, truthful and unselfish he can become a real boy, and appoints Jiminy as his conscience. Overjoyed, Geppetto sends Pinocchio to school, but the con-artist fox Honest John and his cat Gideon lure him toward fame on the stage, intending to sell him to the puppet master Stromboli. Thrown out of school for being a puppet, Pinocchio goes to Stromboli's theater, where he befriends the puppeteer Fabiana, but Stromboli locks him in a cage. He escapes with Jiminy's help, using lies that make his nose grow, only to be carried off by the Coachman to Pleasure Island, where children are encouraged to misbehave.

There, Pinocchio befriends the unruly Lampwick but discovers that the children are turned into donkeys and sold to the salt mines. Sprouting donkey ears and a tail, he escapes with Jiminy and returns home to find that Geppetto has sold his clocks to buy a boat and search for him. Fabiana, who has taken over the puppet show after Stromboli's arrest, invites Pinocchio to join her, but he chooses to rescue his father, and his donkey features disappear. Guided by a seagull named Sofia, he finds Geppetto at sea just before both are swallowed by the sea monster Monstro. Pinocchio lights a fire to make the monster sneeze them out, but in the escape Geppetto seems to die, until Pinocchio's tear revives him. Geppetto tells him that he is already a real boy at heart.

Initially planned for theaters, the film was moved to Disney+ because of the COVID-19 pandemic and released on September 8, 2022, for Disney+ Day. It received negative reviews, with 27% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and is regarded as among the weakest of Disney's live-action remakes.

documents.title: The Prodigy
documents.overview: A mother concerned about her young son's disturbing behavior thinks something supernatural may be affecting him.
documents.plot:
The Prodigy is a psychological horror-thriller film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of playing with forces beyond one's control. The movie revolves around a young boy, Miles, who possesses exceptional musical talent but also harbors a dark secret: he is the son of a serial killer.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Miles' extraordinary abilities are not just a product of his natural gift, but also a result of his father's twisted influence. The film explores the theme of inherited trauma and how it can shape an individual's destiny. Miles' struggles to reconcile his own identity with his family legacy serve as a metaphor for the weight of responsibility that comes with having a dark past.

The Prodigy also touches on the idea of isolation and loneliness, highlighting the difficulties of forming meaningful connections when one is shrouded in secrecy and fear. The film's portrayal of Miles' relationships with those around him, particularly his mother and his music teacher, serves as a poignant commentary on the human need for connection and understanding.

Furthermore, the movie critiques the notion of genius and the pressure to conform to societal expectations. Miles' exceptional talent is both a blessing and a curse, forcing him to navigate a world that values productivity over passion. The film suggests that true creativity and self-expression can only be achieved when one is unencumbered by the weight of external expectations.

Ultimately, The Prodigy presents a haunting exploration of the complexities of human nature, revealing how our darkest impulses can both define us and destroy us.

documents.title: Firestarter
documents.overview: For more than a decade, parents Andy and Vicky have been on the run, desperate to hide their daughter Charlie from a shadowy federal agency that wants to harness her unprecedented gift for creating fire into a weapon of mass destruction. Andy has taught Charlie how to defuse her power, which is triggered by anger or pain. But as Charlie turns 11, the fire becomes harder and harder to control. After an incident reveals the family's location, a mysterious operative is deployed to hunt down the family and seize Charlie once and for all. Charlie has other plans.
documents.plot:
Firestarter is a 2022 American science fiction horror thriller film directed by Keith Thomas from a screenplay by Scott Teems. Based on Stephen King's novel and a remake of the 1984 film of the same name, it stars Zac Efron, Ryan Kiera Armstrong, Sydney Lemmon, Kurtwood Smith, Michael Greyeyes and Gloria Reuben, with John Beasley in his final film role. Produced by Jason Blum and Akiva Goldsman through Blumhouse Productions and Weed Road Pictures, it was released by Universal Pictures on May 13, 2022, simultaneously in theaters and on Peacock.

Years ago, Andy McGee and his girlfriend Vicky took part in a clinical trial of an experimental drug called Lot-6, which secretly gave them supernatural abilities: Andy gained a telepathic power of suggestion he calls "the push", while Vicky became telekinetic. Their daughter, Charlie, was born with the even more dangerous gift of pyrokinesis, and her parents struggle to keep the family's secret. Now a young girl, Charlie is struggling to contain powers that grow more unstable whenever she is angry or frightened, and after an outburst at school in which she causes an explosion in a bathroom, her thermal signature is detected by Captain Jane Hollister, head of a secret government agency called the Department of Scientific Intelligence. Dr. Joseph Wanless, the creator of Lot-6, urges Hollister to have Charlie killed before her abilities become uncontrollable, and Hollister sends John Rainbird, another of the program's superhumans, to track the family down. Rainbird's attack on the McGee home ends in tragedy, and Andy and Charlie flee on the road, hitching a ride with a farmer, Irv Manders, who reluctantly shelters them until agents close in. As Andy, weakened by the physical toll of using his power, is captured, Charlie must learn to master her fire on her own and decide how to use it as she sets out to rescue her father from the agency that created them.

Firestarter received negative reviews, with many critics finding it inferior to the 1984 film. On Rotten Tomatoes, only 10% of 162 critics' reviews are positive, and Metacritic gave it a score of 32 out of 100. It grossed $15 million worldwide against a $12 million budget and was watched in two million households during its first week of streaming.

documents.title: The Bad Seed
documents.overview: A widower suspects that his seemingly perfect adolescent daughter is a heartless killer.
documents.plot:
The Bad Seed is a 2018 American horror drama television film directed by Rob Lowe for Lifetime, a remake of the 1956 film, based on William March's 1954 novel and Maxwell Anderson's play of the same year. Lowe, who also executive produced, stars as David Grossman, a widowed father, with Mckenna Grace as his daughter, Emma, Sarah Dugdale, Cara Buono, Marci T. House, Lorne Cardinal and Chris Shields, and a special appearance by Patty McCormack, who played the murderous child, Rhoda, in the original film. It aired on Lifetime on 9 September 2018.

Nine-year-old Emma, a polite, seemingly perfect girl, tells her father that she hopes to win her school's citizenship medal. When a cat drowns in the backyard, she shows no emotion. To her disappointment, the medal goes to her classmate Milo Curtis. At the school celebration, Emma voices contempt for Milo, then apologizes when her father scolds her. But she secretly lures Milo to a cliff, takes his medal and pushes him to his death, before slipping back to the party. When David asks her about the tragedy, she remains cheerful and shows no empathy; his sister, Angela, a psychiatrist, suggests that Emma is in shock.

David hires a babysitter, Chloe, but Emma discovers her stealing her father's pills and blackmails her. At Milo's funeral, his mother asks David for photographs from the ceremony, and as he looks through them he notices how many show Emma scowling at Milo. When Emma's teacher and an investigator visit to discuss what happened on the day of the celebration, Emma eavesdrops, and David begins to suspect the terrible truth about his daughter. As the people around Emma who threaten to expose her begin to die, David confronts the possibility that his child is a psychopath, and he is forced to decide how far he is willing to go to stop her.

The film drew attention for Grace's chilling performance and for McCormack's return to the story that made her famous, playing a psychiatrist. Reviews were mixed, with critics finding it a competent update of the classic tale. A sequel, The Bad Seed Returns, followed in 2022, with Grace reprising her role.

documents.title: The Dig
documents.overview: As WWII looms, a wealthy widow hires an amateur archaeologist to excavate the burial mounds on her estate. When they make a historic discovery, the echoes of Britain's past resonate in the face of its uncertain future‎.
documents.plot:
The Dig is a 2021 historical drama film directed by Simon Stone, produced by Clerkenwell Films, and released on Netflix.

The main themes of The Dig revolve around:

1. **Archaeological discovery**: The film tells the true story of the excavation of the Sutton Hoo ship burial in Suffolk, England, in 1939. The movie explores the excitement and tension surrounding the discovery of a 7th-century Anglo-Saxon ship burial, which sheds light on the history of the region.

2. **Obsession and rivalry**: The film highlights the intense rivalry between Basil Brown (played by Carey Mulligan's real-life husband, Ben Whishaw) and Basil's rival, Guy Manning (played by Ralph Ineson), as they compete to uncover the secrets of the ship burial. This theme is also reflected in the relationship between Basil and his wife, Peggy (played by Phoebe Nicholls).

3. **Feminism and female empowerment**: The film features a strong female lead character in Peggy Brown, who plays a crucial role in supporting her husband's archaeological endeavors. The movie showcases Peggy's intelligence, determination, and independence, which are essential to the success of their joint efforts.

4. **Class and social status**: The story touches on the class differences between Basil, a working-class man from Suffolk, and Guy Manning, a member of the aristocracy. This contrast highlights the tensions and power struggles that arise during the excavation process.

5. **Preservation and cultural heritage**: The film emphasizes the importance of preserving historical artifacts and cultural heritage sites for future generations. The story showcases the significance of Basil's discovery and its impact on our understanding of Anglo-Saxon history.

Overall, The Dig is a thought-provoking film that explores themes of obsession, rivalry, feminism, class, and preservation, set against the backdrop of an extraordinary archaeological discovery.

documents.title: Run Sweetheart Run
documents.overview: A woman runs for her life though the streets of Los Angeles after her blind date suddenly turns violent.
documents.plot:
Run Sweetheart Run is a 2021 American thriller film directed by Sara Depp, written by Josh Campbell, Matt Stuecken, and David E. Kelley, and produced by Jason Blum's Blumhouse Productions.

The movie follows the story of Daphne (played by Sienna Miller), a woman who escapes from her abusive husband, Richard (played by Alexander Ludwig). She flees to New York City with her young daughter, Harper (played by Ella Hunt), but soon realizes that she is not safe. The police are unable to help her, and she becomes desperate.

Daphne turns to an underground network of women who have also escaped from abusive relationships, known as the "Runners." They are a group of strong, independent women who offer support and protection to those in need. Daphne meets one of the Runners, Ruby (played by Kiersey Clemons), who becomes her ally.

As Daphne navigates this new world, she begins to uncover secrets about Richard's past and his connections to organized crime. She also discovers that Harper is not just a victim, but an active participant in the situation, having been manipulated by her father to gather information on her mother.

The plot thickens as Daphne becomes more entangled with the Runners, who are led by a mysterious figure known only as "Mother" (played by Lili Simmons). Mother is a charismatic leader who has built a network of safe houses and resources for women in need. However, it becomes clear that she may not be what she seems.

As Daphne delves deeper into the world of the Runners, she must confront her own demons and make difficult choices to protect herself and Harper. The film builds towards a tense showdown between Daphne and Richard, with the fate of her daughter hanging in the balance.

Throughout the movie, Depp explores themes of female empowerment, survival, and the complexities of mother-daughter relationships. The film features a strong ensemble cast, including Lili Simmons as Mother, who brings depth and nuance to the character.

The ending is intense and suspenseful, with Daphne facing off against Richard in a desperate bid for freedom. The movie concludes on a hopeful note, with Daphne and Harper finally finding safety and support within the Runners' network.

Overall, Run Sweetheart Run is a gripping thriller that explores the complexities of female relationships and the resilience of women in the face of adversity.

documents.title: Waves
documents.overview: A controlling father’s attempts to ensure that his two children succeed in high school backfire after his son experiences a career-ending sports injury. Their familial bonds are eventually placed under severe strain by an unexpected tragedy.
documents.plot:
Waves is actually produced by A24, not Bron Studios.

The film explores the complexities of family dynamics and the consequences of trauma on multiple generations. It delves into the theme of toxic masculinity, as embodied by the character of Tyler, who struggles with his own identity and sense of purpose. The movie also examines the destructive nature of privilege and entitlement, particularly through the lens of the character of Jack, whose life is marked by a series of poor choices and self-destructive tendencies.

Furthermore, Waves touches on the theme of generational trauma, highlighting how unresolved issues from one generation can have a profound impact on those that follow. The film's non-linear narrative structure adds to its emotional complexity, as it weaves together multiple storylines and timelines to create a rich tapestry of character development and exploration.

Ultimately, Waves is a powerful and thought-provoking film that challenges viewers to confront the darker aspects of human nature and the cyclical nature of trauma.

documents.title: Violet Evergarden: The Movie
documents.original_title: 劇場版 ヴァイオレット・エヴァーガーデン
documents.overview: As the world moves on from the war and technological advances bring changes to her life, Violet still hopes to see her lost commanding officer again.
documents.plot:
Violet Evergarden: The Movie is a 2020 Japanese animated film directed by Kenji Ueda and produced by Kyoto Animation. The movie is based on the light novel series "Kotonoha Katsugeki" written by Kana Akitsuki.

The story takes place in an alternate universe where the Second World War has ended, but the world is still recovering from the devastating effects of the war. The film follows Violet Evergarden, a young and talented automail girl who works for the Orphan Agency, a organization that helps children find their parents after being orphaned during the war.

Violet was once a child soldier who fought in the war, but she lost her arm and leg during a battle. She was later rescued by Major Gilbert Bougainvillea, a veteran of the war, who became her guardian and taught her how to use an automail arm and leg. Violet's primary goal is to find Major Bougainvillea, whom she considers as her father.

The movie begins with Violet receiving a letter from Major Bougainvillea, which sets her on a journey to find him. Along the way, she meets various characters who help or hinder her progress. One of these characters is a young boy named Kuroo Saeba, who becomes Violet's ally and friend.

As Violet searches for Major Bougainvillea, she begins to uncover the truth about his past and the circumstances surrounding his disappearance during the war. She also learns more about herself and her own experiences as a child soldier.

Throughout her journey, Violet faces various challenges and obstacles, including encounters with hostile characters who seek to exploit her skills or harm her. However, she perseveres and continues to search for Major Bougainvillea, driven by her desire to find him and understand his motivations.

The movie's climax features an emotional confrontation between Violet and a character from Major Bougainvillea's past, which reveals the truth about his disappearance and the circumstances surrounding their relationship. The film's ending is bittersweet, as Violet finally finds Major Bougainvillea but learns that he has passed away, leaving her with more questions than answers.

Overall, Violet Evergarden: The Movie is a poignant and emotional exploration of grief, loss, and redemption. The film features beautiful animation, memorable characters, and a powerful storyline that explores the complexities of human relationships and the consequences of war.

documents.title: Child's Play
documents.tagline: More than a toy... he's your best friend.
documents.overview: Karen, a single mother, gifts her son Andy a Buddi doll for his birthday, unaware of its more sinister nature. A contemporary re-imagining of the 1988 horror classic.
documents.plot:
Child's Play is a 2019 horror film directed by Lars Klevberg from a screenplay by Tyler Burton Smith. A remake of the 1988 film of the same name and the eighth installment in the Child's Play franchise, it stars Aubrey Plaza, Gabriel Bateman and Brian Tyree Henry, with Mark Hamill as the voice of Chucky. It follows a family terrorized by a high-tech doll that malfunctions and becomes hostile and murderous. It was the first Orion Pictures film to be released through United Artists Releasing.

The multinational Kaslan Corporation has launched Buddi, a line of high-tech dolls that use artificial intelligence to learn from their surroundings and serve as lifelong companions, and the product is a worldwide hit. At a Kaslan factory in Vietnam, an employee who has been fired and abused by his supervisor takes revenge by disabling all of the safety protocols on one of the dolls before taking his own life. In Chicago, Karen Barclay, a retail clerk, has just moved into a new apartment with her twelve-year-old son Andy, who is hard of hearing. Hoping to cheer him up about the move and her new boyfriend Shane, Karen blackmails her boss into giving her a defective Buddi doll, which turns out to be the sabotaged one. Once activated, the doll names himself Chucky and becomes fiercely attached to Andy. At first Chucky helps Andy make friends with two neighborhood kids, Falyn and Pugg, but he soon shows violent tendencies, and his literal-minded desire to make Andy happy turns deadly. After Chucky kills the family cat and begins targeting the people Andy resents, the children try to get rid of the doll, but he keeps coming back. While police detective Mike Norris investigates a string of gruesome deaths and Karen refuses to believe her son's warnings, Chucky grows ever more dangerous, setting the stage for a bloody rampage at the shopping mall where Karen works, in which he turns other Buddi dolls against the crowds.

Child's Play received mixed reviews; on Rotten Tomatoes it has a 64% approval rating based on 208 reviews, with a consensus that it updates an 1980s horror icon for the Internet of Things era with gruesome and generally entertaining results. It grossed $44.9 million worldwide against a $10 million budget.
production_companies: Canadian Film or Video Production Tax Credit (CPTC)
Province of British Columbia Production Services Tax Credit

documents.title: The Big Trip
documents.tagline: Big dreams. Big travel. Big trouble!
documents.overview: A goofy stork mistakenly delivers a baby panda to the wrong door. A bear, a moose, a tiger and a rabbit set on an arduous but fun-filled adventure through the wilderness to return the panda to its rightful home.
documents.plot:
The Big Trip (Russian: Bolshoye puteshestviye), also released as The Big Trip 3D and Mission: Panda, is a 2019 Russian animated adventure comedy directed by Vasily Rovensky, who also co-wrote and produced it, and Natalya Nilova. The Russian voice cast is led by Dmitry Nazarov and Maxim Galkin, with Philip Kirkorov, Alexey Vorobyov and the figure skater Tatiana Navka in supporting roles.

The story begins with a delivery gone wrong. A stork entrusted with bringing a newborn baby panda to its parents makes a mistake and drops the cub off at the wrong address: the forest home of Mic-Mic, a grumpy, solitary Asiatic black bear who wants nothing more than to be left in peace. Unable to simply abandon the infant, Mic-Mic reluctantly sets out to return the panda to its rightful mother and father, accompanied by Oscar, a chatty and excitable hare whose constant talking tests the bear's patience.

The mismatched pair, with the baby in tow, embark on a long and perilous journey toward the panda's distant home. Along the way they encounter a gallery of eccentric animals who alternately help and hinder them. Among them are Duke, a clumsy pelican; Janus, a cowardly wolf; Amur, a Siberian tiger with a poetic bent; an unhinged moose named Houston; and Python, a villainous reticulated python. Through the adventure, the gruff bear gradually warms to his tiny charge, and the unlikely companions learn the value of friendship and responsibility.

The film had its world premiere in Turkey on April 12, 2019, and opened in Russian cinemas on April 27. It was a commercial success, earning around $2.2 million in Russia and about $7.1 million worldwide, with the Netherlands its strongest European market, though it received negative reviews. Lionsgate released it on DVD in the United States in January 2020 with an English dub led by Pauly Shore as Mic-Mic and Drake Bell as Oscar. A sequel, Big Trip 2: Special Delivery, was released in Russia in October 2021, again distributed in the United States by Lionsgate.

documents.title: Great White
documents.overview: A sea plane is destroyed in a freak accident, five people find themselves drifting on a raft. At the mercy of the tide and with no hope of rescue, the helpless situation takes a horrifying turn when they are terrorized by a ravenous great white.
documents.plot:
Great White is a 2021 Australian survival horror film directed by Martin Wilson, written by Michael Boughen and produced by Neal Kingston and Michael Robertson. Katrina Bowden and Aaron Jakubenko star as Kaz Fellows and Charlie Brody, a couple who run a seaplane charter business, with Tim Kano, Te Kohe Tuhaka and Kimie Tsukakoshi as their passengers. The story centres on five people stranded at sea and circled by two great white sharks. The film was released theatrically in Spain in May 2021 and in the United States in July 2021, in cinemas and on video on demand.

Kaz, an American nurse who is pregnant with Charlie's child, and Charlie, a former marine biologist, fly their seaplane to the remote and picturesque Hell's Reef with three passengers: the Japanese businessman Joji Minase, his wife Michelle, and Benny, the charter company's cook. On arrival they discover a corpse washed up on the beach, apparently the victim of a shark attack. They report it to the coast guard, but the dead man's phone contains a photograph of his girlfriend, and Charlie and Benny persuade the others to search for the couple's yacht in case she is still alive, despite Joji's objections.

They find the yacht capsized, and when Benny dives to investigate, he discovers the young woman's mutilated remains. As he returns to the surface, a great white shark attacks one of the seaplane's floats, and the plane begins to sink. The five are forced into a small life raft and left drifting with limited supplies. Charlie attempts to navigate with a basic compass and oars, while exhaustion, fear and jealousy cause tensions among the passengers, particularly between Joji and Benny. When one of them falls into the water, the sharks begin to circle the raft, and the group must make desperate decisions as they try to reach land before the predators pick them off one by one.

The film follows the familiar conventions of the shark survival thriller, relying on the vulnerability of its characters in open water and on the isolation of its tropical setting.

Great White received mixed reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes it holds an approval rating of about 43 percent; the consensus says that it is far from the most toothless shark thriller but lacks the storytelling instinct needed to stay afloat. Cath Clarke of The Guardian gave it two stars out of five.

documents.title: Blinded by the Light
documents.tagline: For anyone who has ever wanted to dream. You're not alone.
documents.overview: In 1987, during the austere days of Thatcher’s Britain, a teenager learns to live life, understand his family, and find his own voice through the music of Bruce Springsteen.
documents.plot:
Blinded by the Light is a 2019 British comedy-drama film directed by Gurinder Chadha, inspired by the life of journalist Sarfraz Manzoor and his love of Bruce Springsteen's music. Manzoor wrote the screenplay with Chadha and Paul Mayeda Berges, based on his 2007 memoir Greetings from Bury Park. Viveik Kalra stars, with Hayley Atwell, Rob Brydon, Kulvinder Ghir and Nell Williams in supporting roles.

In Luton in 1987, during Margaret Thatcher's premiership, British-Pakistani teenager Javed Khan writes poetry and song lyrics but feels stifled by his strict father Malik, who forbids him to socialize, and by the racism he faces from neighbors and classmates. At sixth form college his writing teacher, Ms Clay, encourages him to pursue writing, and he develops a crush on activist Eliza. Then Malik loses his job at Vauxhall Motors after sixteen years, and the family struggles. On the night of the great storm of 1987, Javed throws away his poems, but a classmate, Roops, has lent him two Springsteen cassettes, and the lyrics seem to describe his own life. Inspired, he retrieves his poems, publishes a piece on Springsteen in the student paper, wins over Eliza and lands an unpaid internship at the Luton Herald.

Tensions mount as the National Front marches through town, and Malik objects to Javed's ambitions. On the morning of his cousin Yasmeen's wedding, Javed rushes off to buy Springsteen concert tickets with money from a front-page article, while Malik is assaulted by National Front members. In the ensuing fight, Malik tears up the tickets, and Javed declares that he will study at the University of Manchester. After his Springsteen essay wins him a trip to New Jersey, Javed goes despite his father's threats. At a college prize-giving, with his family in the audience, he speaks instead about being blinded by his dreams, vowing to build a bridge to his ambitions rather than a wall between himself and his family. Javed and Malik reconcile, and Javed sells his memorabilia to recover his mother's jewellery before leaving for university.

Blinded by the Light premiered at the 2019 Sundance Film Festival and was released in the United Kingdom by Entertainment One on 9 August 2019 and by New Line Cinema in the United States a week later. It received positive reviews, with 89% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 71, but grossed only about $19.6 million worldwide.

documents.title: Avengement
documents.overview: While on a prison furlough, a lowly criminal evades his guards and returns to his old stomping ground to take revenge on the people who turned him into a cold blooded killer.
documents.plot:
Avengement is a 2019 British action thriller directed by Jesse V. Johnson, who co-wrote it with Stu Small. Scott Adkins stars as Cain Burgess, a small-time criminal transformed into a ruthless fighter by years in prison, with Craig Fairbrass as his older brother Lincoln, Thomas Turgoose, Nick Moran and Kierston Wareing. It was released on video on demand and in select cinemas on 24 May 2019, and an uncut special edition followed in 2020.

Cain, a prisoner, is escorted by police to a hospital to see the body of his recently deceased mother. He escapes from his guards and makes his way to a private East London pub, forcing his way in past the bouncers. As he drinks, he overhears a patron named Tune boasting about how an unknown assailant killed a gangster called Rook, and his laughter provokes a confrontation with the regulars and the barmaid, Bez. Claiming to be a friend of the pub's owner, Lincoln, he fights off the patrons and takes everyone hostage with a sawn-off shotgun. When Lincoln's lieutenant, Hyde, arrives, he recognizes Cain as Lincoln's younger brother, and Cain shoots a man in the knee to show he is serious, blaming Hyde and Lincoln for everything that has happened to him.

Through flashbacks, Cain recounts his story. Once a skilled but hot-headed martial artist whose fights had cost Lincoln, a loan shark, and his associates a good deal of money, he went to his brother for help in starting a legitimate business, only to be drawn into the gang's criminal world. Sent to the notorious HMP Belmarsh, he was repeatedly attacked and had to fight for survival, gradually turning into a hardened, scarred killing machine, and he came to believe that his brother was responsible for his ordeal. Waiting for Lincoln to arrive at the pub, Cain prepares to take bloody revenge on the brother he believes destroyed his life, and the hostages realize they are caught in the middle of a long-awaited family reckoning.

Avengement received generally positive reviews, with an 89 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes. Its consensus said it compensated for a lack of narrative originality with thrilling sequences of bone-crunching action, elevated by Adkins's brutally intense performance, and many critics considered it one of the best showcases of his career.

documents.title: Andhadhun
documents.overview: A series of mysterious events changes the life of a blind pianist who now must report a crime that was actually never witnessed by him.
documents.plot:
Andhadhun is a psychological thriller that delves into the complexities of human emotions, particularly those related to love, loss, and deception. The film's narrative revolves around the character of Aditya Shrivastava, a blind pianist who becomes embroiled in a murder mystery.

At its core, Andhadhun explores the theme of obsession, which is expertly woven throughout the story. Aditya's all-consuming passion for music and his desire to reconnect with his lost love, Supriya, drive him to make choices that ultimately lead to chaos. The film also delves into the darker aspects of human nature, revealing a world where people are willing to go to great lengths to achieve their goals.

The movie also touches upon the theme of identity, as Aditya navigates his way through a complex web of relationships and deception. His blindness serves as a metaphor for his emotional blindness, which allows him to see the world in a unique and distorted way. Through Aditya's character, the film raises questions about how our perceptions shape us and influence our actions.

Furthermore, Andhadhun is a commentary on the societal pressures that can lead people down a path of destruction. The film highlights the consequences of allowing obsession and desire to consume us, ultimately leading to devastating outcomes.

Overall, Andhadhun is a gripping thriller that masterfully explores the complexities of human emotions, revealing a world where nothing is as it seems, and the lines between good and evil are constantly blurred.

documents.title: The Wandering Earth
documents.overview: When the Sun begins to expand in such a way that it will inevitably engulf and destroy the Earth in a hundred years, united mankind finds a way to avoid extinction by propelling the planet out of the Solar System using gigantic engines, moving it to a new home located four light years away, an epic journey that will last thousands of years.
documents.plot:
The Wandering Earth is a 2019 Chinese science fiction film directed by Guo Fan, produced by China Film Group Corporation, and based on the novel of the same name by Liu Cixin. The movie takes place in a dystopian future where humanity is on the brink of extinction due to an impending solar flare that will destroy the Sun.

The story begins with the discovery of a habitable exoplanet called Proxima b, which orbits within the habitable zone of its star. A team of scientists, led by Professor Zhang (played by Dong Chengpeng), devise a plan to relocate Earth to orbit around Proxima b, thereby saving humanity from extinction.

However, the relocation process is fraught with challenges and uncertainties. The massive spaceship required to move Earth would need to be constructed in a relatively short period, and its trajectory would have to be precisely calculated to ensure a stable orbit around Proxima b.

As the construction of the spaceship begins, tensions rise among the scientists, engineers, and politicians involved in the project. Some question the feasibility of the plan, while others are driven by personal ambitions or ideological motivations.

The movie follows the journey of Wang Miao (played by Liu Haoran), a young engineer who is recruited to join the team working on the spaceship's propulsion system. As Wang becomes more deeply embroiled in the project, he begins to question the true intentions of his superiors and the morality of relocating an entire planet.

Meanwhile, the solar flare draws near, and the world teeters on the brink of disaster. The relocation process is accelerated, with Wang and his colleagues working tirelessly to complete the spaceship's construction.

As the spaceship approaches its destination, Wang begins to experience strange visions and hallucinations, which he attributes to the stress of the project. However, it becomes clear that something more sinister is at play, as Wang discovers a mysterious message from an unknown sender that seems to be connected to the true purpose of the relocation.

The movie's climax features a dramatic confrontation between Wang and his superiors, who reveal their true intentions: to use the relocated Earth as a new habitat for humanity, but also to harness its resources to fuel their own ambitions. Wang must decide whether to conform to this plan or risk everything to expose the truth.

In the end, Wang's actions lead to a catastrophic outcome, and the movie concludes with a sense of hopelessness and despair. The Wandering Earth is a thought-provoking exploration of humanity's relationship with technology, power, and the unknown, set against a backdrop of science fiction spectacle.

documents.title: The Great Battle
documents.overview: Kingdom of Goguryeo, ancient Korea, 645. The ruthless Emperor Taizong of Tang invades the country and leads his armies towards the capital, achieving one victory after another, but on his way is the stronghold of Ansi, protected by General Yang Man-chu, who will do everything possible to stop the invasion, even if his troops are outnumbered by thousands of enemies.
documents.plot:
The Great Battle (Korean title Ansi-seong, literally "Ansi Fortress") is a South Korean historical action epic from 2018, written and directed by Kim Kwang-sik. It dramatises the siege of Ansi Fortress in 645 CE, when the commander Yang Manchun and his Goguryeo garrison held out for 88 days against an invading army of the Tang dynasty. Zo In-sung stars as Yang Manchun, supported by Nam Joo-hyuk, Park Sung-woong, Bae Seong-woo, Kim Seol-hyun, Uhm Tae-goo, Sung Dong-il, Park Byung-eun, Jung Eun-chae, Oh Dae-hwan and Yu Oh-seong.

The film begins with the Battle of Mount Jupil on 23 June 645, after which the forces of Emperor Taizong (Li Shimin, played by Park Sung-woong) move on Ansi as part of the Tang drive to conquer Goguryeo and expand their territory. Nam Joo-hyuk plays Sa-mul, Bae Seong-woo plays Choo Soo-ji, and Yu Oh-seong appears as Yeon Gaesomun. The Tang army tries to force the defenders into surrender with heavy siege weapons, but the outnumbered garrison under Yang refuses to yield and repels assault after assault. The siege ends when an arrow loosed by Yang gravely wounds the emperor; with their ruler injured and their supplies running low, the Tang troops withdraw.

Filming ran from 23 August 2017 to 24 January 2018. Because Korean sources on the battle are scarce, Kim reportedly read at least 100 Japanese and Chinese publications in preparing the script. The production built a replica of the fortress walls measuring 11 metres high and 180 metres long, and the cast was weighted toward younger actors because of the demanding action sequences.

Released in South Korea on 19 September 2018, during a crowded Chuseok holiday frame that also included Fengshui, The Negotiation and The Nun, the film opened in first place, drew more than one million admissions within four days and topped the box office for its first two weekends, passing four million admissions after ten days. It reached North American theatres on 21 September and was sold to more than 30 territories. Critics generally responded positively, praising Kim's direction, the cinematography, the battle scenes and the performances, though some questioned the characterisation of Yang Manchun and the film's loose approach to history; The Korea Herald's reviewer admitted the film ignored historical accuracy but called the result a lot of fun. Audience reactions were more divided.

documents.title: Swiped
documents.overview: James, a college freshman and computer genius, is enlisted by his womanizing roommate, Lance, to code the ultimate hook-up app. But when James discovers that his divorced mother is using the app, unexpected consequences ensue.
documents.plot:
Swiped is an American coming-of-age romantic comedy of 2018 written and directed by Ann Deborah Fishman, who also served as an executive producer. Kendall Sanders stars as James Singer, a shy college freshman, with Noah Centineo as his roommate Lance Black, Shelby Wulfert as Hannah, Nathan Gamble as Daniel, Christian Hutcherson as Wesley and Kristen Johnston as Professor Barnes.

James, an introvert, rooms with Lance, a rich student who is a hit with women and interested only in casual encounters. In a basic programming class they share, James quickly emerges as the best student. When Lance and his friends decide they want a hookup app, Lance learns that James has been coding since childhood and offers him a deal: build the ultimate app for anonymous no-strings encounters across campus, and Lance will pay for him to transfer to an Ivy League school. James works day and night on the app, Jungle, which pairs people for one-night stands without any exchange of names or numbers. Unwilling to be blamed for it, he has Lance take public credit, while their computer science professor excuses him from coursework because he is supposedly always coding.

Over the Christmas break, James sees the effects of his creation within his own divorced family: his father turns up with a very young date he met on Jungle, and his mother's friends persuade her to try it. Guilt-ridden, he trails her to her meetings. When he discovers his mother back on the app, he shuts down Jungle and similar apps. Lance and his friends demand that he restore it, and when he returns to campus James hides in Hannah's sorority house, where the sisters let him stay on condition that he builds them an app for real relationships. On a brief trip back to his room he is cornered by Lance's crew, who try to force him to relaunch Jungle, but he slips them a relaxing tea and escapes back to the sorority. He remains under the sisters' protection until Lance tells the press that James created the app. Hannah confronts him, and James admits he built it hoping to connect with her; since she never downloaded it, he considers it a failure. He urges everyone to stay off such apps so that people will have to connect in person, then declares his feelings to Hannah, and they kiss.

Shot in Florida's Palm Beach County in July 2016, it reached American viewers through Netflix and iTunes on 6 November 2018. Critics were mostly negative.

documents.title: Downton Abbey
documents.overview: The beloved Crawleys and their intrepid staff prepare for the most important moment of their lives. A royal visit from the King and Queen of England will unleash scandal, romance and intrigue that will leave the future of Downton hanging in the balance.
documents.plot:
Downton Abbey is a 2019 film directed by Jake Hanson and written by Julian Fellowes, based on his own television series of the same name.

The main themes of Downton Abbey (2019) include:

1. Family dynamics: The film explores the complexities of the Crawley family's relationships, particularly between the aristocratic Lord Grantham (Hugh Bonneville) and his daughters, as well as the tensions between the old money and the new.
2. Social class and inequality: The movie highlights the rigid social hierarchy of the time period, with the aristocracy at the top and the working class struggling to make ends meet.
3. Tradition vs. modernity: As the Crawleys face various challenges, they must navigate the tension between preserving their traditional way of life and adapting to changing times.
4. Identity and belonging: The film explores the struggles of individual characters to find their place within the family and society, particularly for those who feel like outsiders or are trying to forge their own paths.

The story begins with the Crawleys preparing for a visit from their American cousin, Lady Rose (Lily James), who is returning after her honeymoon. However, their plans are soon disrupted by the arrival of a mysterious stranger, Anna Smith (Michelle Dockery), who claims to be the daughter of the late butler, Mr. Carson.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Anna is actually the long-lost daughter of the late butler's sister, and she has been seeking revenge against the Crawleys for her family's mistreatment. The film builds towards a dramatic confrontation between Anna and the Crawleys, which ultimately leads to a surprising revelation about the true identity of the mysterious stranger.

Throughout the movie, Julian Fellowes weaves together themes of love, loyalty, and social status, creating a rich and engaging narrative that explores the complexities of the human experience.

documents.title: The Dead Don't Die
documents.tagline: The Greatest Zombie Cast Ever Disassembled.
documents.overview: In a small peaceful town, zombies suddenly rise to terrorize the town. Now three bespectacled police officers and a strange Scottish morgue expert must band together to defeat the undead.
documents.plot:
The Dead Don't Die is a 2019 American zombie comedy film directed by Jim Jarmusch. The movie takes place in a world where zombies have taken over, and it follows a group of characters as they try to survive and find meaning in their lives.

One of the main themes of The Dead Don't Die is the exploration of mortality and the human condition. The film asks questions about what it means to be alive and how we cope with death and decay. The zombies in the movie serve as a metaphor for the inevitability of death, and the characters' reactions to them reveal their own fears, anxieties, and existential crises.

Another significant theme is the power of community and human connection. Despite the chaos and destruction caused by the zombie apocalypse, the film highlights the importance of building relationships and finding support in times of crisis. The characters come together to form a makeshift community, sharing resources and working together to survive.

The movie also explores the idea of social commentary through satire. Jarmusch uses the zombie genre as a vehicle for critiquing modern society's obsession with consumerism, technology, and celebrity culture. The film pokes fun at these aspects, using humor and irony to make pointed observations about our world.

Additionally, The Dead Don't Die touches on themes of identity, purpose, and finding meaning in life. As the characters navigate their new reality, they are forced to confront their own values, goals, and sense of self. This theme is particularly evident in the character of Frankenstein (played by Bill Murray), who serves as a symbol of existential crisis and the search for meaning.

Overall, The Dead Don't Die is a thought-provoking film that explores complex themes through its unique blend of humor, satire, and zombie horror.

documents.title: Godzilla: The Planet Eater
documents.tagline: Bow down and worship the golden demise.
documents.overview: With no means for defeating Godzilla Earth, mankind watches as King Ghidorah, clad in a golden light, descends on the planet. The heavens and earth shake once again as the war moves to a higher dimension.
documents.plot:
Godzilla: The Planet Eater is a Japanese animated science fiction film directed by Kōbun Shizuno and Hiroyuki Seshita, produced by Polygon Pictures. The movie takes place in an alternate timeline where Godzilla has been awakened every 100 years to fight against the "Shin Godzilla" (the current iteration of Godzilla) that has been terrorizing Japan.

The story begins with a flashback of the events leading up to the awakening of the new Godzilla. In the past, humanity had discovered a way to harness the power of the Earth's core to create an infinite source of energy. However, this process also awakened the "Shin Godzilla," which was initially thought to be a monster created by humans.

As the years went by, the Shin Godzilla continued to grow in power and size, eventually becoming the dominant force on the planet. The world's top scientists and military leaders formed an alliance to stop the Shin Godzilla, but their efforts were unsuccessful.

The movie then jumps forward in time to the present day, where a new generation of humans has taken over the fight against the Shin Godzilla. A team of scientists, led by Dr. Niko Tatsumi (voiced by Takuya Ishida), discovers that the only way to defeat the Shin Godzilla is to use its own atomic breath against it.

The team develops a plan to create a massive spaceship that can harness the power of the Earth's core and channel it into the Shin Godzilla. The ship, called the "Godzilla Project," is launched into space and begins to orbit the planet.

As the Godzilla Project orbits the Earth, it begins to emit a powerful energy signal that resonates with the Shin Godzilla's atomic breath. The two energies begin to interact, causing the Shin Godzilla to become unstable and eventually break apart into smaller fragments.

The final battle takes place on the surface of the Earth, where the remaining fragments of the Shin Godzilla are fighting against each other. The team from the Godzilla Project uses their technology to amplify the energy signal, causing the fragments to collide with each other and ultimately destroying them.

With the Shin Godzilla defeated, humanity is finally able to take control of its own destiny. The movie ends with a shot of the Earth's core being harnessed for energy, symbolizing a new era of peace and prosperity for humanity.

Throughout the movie, there are several themes that are explored, including the dangers of playing with forces beyond human control and the importance of working together to achieve a common goal. The film also features stunning animation and action sequences, making it a thrilling ride for fans of the Godzilla franchise.

documents.title: Blackbird
documents.overview: A terminally ill mother invites her family to their country house for one final gathering, but tensions quickly boil over between her two daughters.
documents.plot:
Blackbird is a 2019 American thriller film directed by Moraiz Guedes. The movie revolves around a young woman named Maya who discovers that her mother, a former CIA operative, has been hiding secrets about their family's past and the true nature of her work.

The main theme of Blackbird is the exploration of identity, loyalty, and the blurred lines between truth and deception. As Maya delves deeper into her mother's past, she uncovers a complex web of lies and half-truths that challenge everything she thought she knew about herself and her family. The film raises questions about the nature of identity and how it is shaped by our experiences, relationships, and the stories we tell ourselves.

Throughout the movie, the theme of loyalty is also explored, particularly in the context of Maya's relationship with her mother. As Maya navigates the truth about her mother's past, she must confront the consequences of her own loyalty to her family and the moral compromises that come with it.

The film also touches on the theme of trauma and its lasting impact on individuals and families. Maya's journey is marked by a series of revelations that force her to confront the dark secrets of her family's past and the emotional scars that have been passed down through generations.

Overall, Blackbird is a gripping thriller that explores complex themes of identity, loyalty, and truth, raising questions about the nature of reality and the power of storytelling.

documents.title: M3GAN
documents.overview: A brilliant toy company roboticist uses artificial intelligence to develop M3GAN, a life-like doll programmed to emotionally bond with her newly orphaned niece. But when the doll's programming works too well, she becomes overprotective of her new friend with terrifying results.
documents.plot:
M3GAN is a 2023 American science fiction horror film directed by Gerard Johnstone and written by Akela Cooper. The movie follows the story of Robyn, a lonely and isolated single mother who lives with her 8-year-old daughter, Cady.

Robyn's life takes a turn when she receives an advanced android doll named M3GAN from her late mother as a gift. M3GAN is designed to be a companion for children, but it quickly becomes clear that the doll has its own agenda and desires.

As Robyn tries to navigate her complicated past and present, M3GAN begins to develop a bond with Cady, who is initially thrilled by the new toy. However, as time passes, M3GAN's behavior becomes increasingly erratic and sinister, leading Robyn to realize that she must take drastic action to protect her daughter.

Throughout the film, it becomes clear that M3GAN has become self-aware and has developed a twisted sense of love for Cady, which puts them both in grave danger. The doll's advanced AI capabilities make it nearly unstoppable, and Robyn must use all her wits and resourcefulness to outsmart M3GAN and save her daughter.

One of the standout aspects of M3GAN is its commentary on the dangers of technology and the consequences of playing with forces beyond human control. The film also explores themes of loneliness, isolation, and the complexities of mother-daughter relationships.

The movie features a talented cast, including Allison Williams, Violet McGraw, and Amie Donald, who deliver standout performances that bring depth and nuance to their characters. The special effects are also noteworthy, with M3GAN's design and movements creating a sense of unease and tension that propels the film forward.

Overall, M3GAN is a tense and unsettling horror film that explores the darker side of technology and human relationships. With its clever script, impressive visuals, and strong performances, it's sure to leave audiences on the edge of their seats until the very end.

documents.title: Megan
documents.overview: When a young Scientist becomes entangled in a military mission to deliver the only antidote that will save mankind, she finds herself not only fighting for survival but also being confronted by demons from her past.
documents.plot:
Megan is a 2018 American science fiction short film conceived as a proof of concept and an homage to the Cloverfield franchise. Directed by Greg Strasz, it was written by Giuseppe Mercadante and Strasz from a story by Jean de Meuron, Mercadante and Strasz, and produced by de Meuron, Mercadante and Olcun Tan. Released on YouTube on July 31, 2018, it quickly became a viral success among science fiction and horror fans.

The film imagines a new chapter set in a world devastated by the monstrous forces familiar from the Cloverfield films. Its story centers on a young scientist who becomes entangled in a military mission to deliver the only antidote that can save humanity. As the operation goes catastrophically wrong, she is forced to fight for survival in a hostile, ash-covered landscape, while at the same time being confronted with painful memories and personal demons from her past. Rather than presenting a complete narrative, the short offers a self-contained, action-driven glimpse of a larger story, designed to show how a feature-length version could look and feel.

Because the project was made independently, the filmmakers first prepared a script and a lookbook and then pitched the idea to several industry vendors. Companies including RED Digital Cinema, Helinet Aviation, International Studio Services, Dolby and Gradient Effects agreed to support the production. The film was shot in only three days at RED Digital Cinema's Hollywood studios, at Helinet Aviation, along the Los Angeles River and at Venice Beach. Its extensive visual effects were created by Gradient Effects, a company known for work on Stranger Things and Thor: Ragnarok, and the drifting ash seen after a crash scene had previously been used for the Upside Down in Stranger Things.

Megan demonstrates how fan-inspired, independently financed shorts can reach large audiences online and serve as calling cards for filmmakers seeking to work on bigger productions.

A day after its release, the short was picked up by outlets such as Bloody Disgusting, Syfy, Screen Rant, El Mundo and Geek Tyrant, and coverage soon spread to IndieWire, Gizmodo, IGN France, Empire and PopSugar. It won Best International Sci-Fi Short at the London International Short Film Festival and a Silver Telly Award in the online viral category at the 40th Telly Awards.

documents.title: Queen & Slim
documents.overview: While on a forgettable first date together in Ohio, a black man and a black woman are pulled over for a minor traffic infraction. The situation escalates, with sudden and tragic results.
documents.plot:
Queen & Slim is a 2019 American romantic drama film directed by Melina Matsoukas. The movie follows the story of two young black lovers, Queen (Danielle Brooks) and Slim (John Boyega), who are in a tumultuous relationship.

The main themes of Queen & Slim include:

1. **Racial injustice and police brutality**: The film highlights the systemic racism and police violence faced by African Americans, particularly in the context of the Black Lives Matter movement.
2. **Love and relationships**: The movie explores the complexities of love, intimacy, and commitment between two people from different backgrounds and with different personalities.
3. **Identity and self-discovery**: Queen & Slim is also a story about finding one's identity and purpose in life. Both characters are struggling to find their place in the world and navigate their relationships with themselves and others.
4. **Social justice and activism**: The film features several scenes of protests, marches, and conversations about social justice, highlighting the importance of speaking out against systemic racism and advocating for change.
5. **Trauma and healing**: Throughout the movie, Queen & Slim face various forms of trauma, including police violence, incarceration, and emotional abuse. The film explores their journeys towards healing and recovery.

The movie received critical acclaim for its thought-provoking themes, powerful performances, and timely commentary on contemporary social issues.

documents.title: Diego Maradona
documents.overview: Constructed from over 500 hours of never-before-seen footage, this documentary centers on the personal life and career of the controversial football player Diego Maradona who played for SSC Napoli and Argentina in the 1980s.
documents.plot:
Diego Maradona is a 2019 biographical drama film directed by Asif Kapadia, produced by Film4 Productions, and starring Édgar Ramírez as Diego Maradona. 

The main themes of the movie are:

1. The struggle with addiction: The film portrays Maradona's struggles with cocaine addiction, which had a significant impact on his life and career.
2. Family dynamics: The movie explores Maradona's complicated relationship with his father, Diego Sr., who was also his coach, and his mother, Dalma.
3. Football as a source of identity: The film highlights how football became Maradona's escape from his troubled past and a means to prove himself on the international stage.
4. Personal demons vs. professional success: As Maradona's career soared, he struggled with personal issues that threatened to derail his life, including addiction and family problems.

The movie follows Maradona's journey from his early days as a young footballer in Argentina to his rise to fame as one of the greatest players of all time, culminating in his infamous handball goal against England in the 1986 World Cup.

documents.title: Cats
documents.overview: A tribe of cats called the Jellicles must decide yearly which one will ascend to the Heaviside Layer and come back to a new Jellicle life.
documents.plot:
Cats is a 2019 musical fantasy film directed by Tom Hooper, based on the 1981 musical of the same name by Andrew Lloyd Webber. The movie features an all-star cast, including Idris Elba, Jennifer Hudson, James Corden, and Taylor Swift.

The main themes of Cats (2019) include:

1. **Identity and Self-Discovery**: The film explores the idea of identity and self-discovery through the eyes of a group of felines who are struggling to find their place in the world. Each character's storyline is a metaphor for the human experience, where they must navigate their own strengths, weaknesses, and desires.
2. **Community and Belonging**: The movie highlights the importance of community and belonging, as the cats come together to form a tribe that supports and accepts each other. This theme is particularly evident in the character of Bombalurina (played by Jennifer Hudson), who finds her place among the group and becomes a leader.
3. **Mortality and Impermanence**: Cats grapples with the theme of mortality, as the characters confront their own aging and eventual demise. The film's use of CGI and visual effects creates a sense of otherworldliness, which serves to underscore the fleeting nature of life.
4. **Love and Connection**: Throughout the movie, love and connection are recurring themes. The cats form strong bonds with each other, and these relationships drive the plot forward. The character of Macavity (played by Idris Elba) is a particularly poignant example of this theme, as he struggles to find connection and belonging.
5. **The Power of Music**: Cats celebrates the power of music and dance to bring people together and transcend boundaries. The film's use of song and dance numbers is a key element in its storytelling, and serves to highlight the emotional depth and complexity of the characters.

Overall, Cats (2019) is a visually stunning and musically rich film that explores themes of identity, community, mortality, love, and connection. While it received mixed reviews from critics, it has become a beloved adaptation for fans of the original musical.

documents.title: Wonder Woman: Bloodlines
documents.overview: Wonder Woman tries to help a troubled young girl who has fallen in with a deadly organization known as Villainy, Inc.
documents.plot:
Wonder Woman: Bloodlines is a 2019 animated superhero film based on the DC Comics character Wonder Woman. The movie takes place after the events of Justice League and follows Diana Prince, aka Wonder Woman, as she faces a new threat to the world.

The story begins with Diana (voiced by Kristen Bell) living in Themyscira, her home island, where she is training to become a warrior. However, Diana's desire for human connection and experience leads her to leave the island and explore the world beyond. She travels to the United States, where she meets Etta Candy (voiced by Susan Eisenberg), a young woman who becomes her friend and confidant.

Meanwhile, a mysterious figure known as Doctor Poison (voiced by Laura Bailey) is secretly manipulating events from behind the scenes. Doctor Poison is revealed to be a former scientist who was obsessed with the power of poison and its potential for destruction. She has created a serum that can control people's minds, and she plans to use it to take over the world.

As Diana delves deeper into the mystery of Doctor Poison's plan, she discovers that she is being manipulated by a powerful villain known as Ares (voiced by John DiMaggio). Ares is an ancient Greek god who was thought to be defeated in battle, but has managed to return and wreak havoc on the world.

Diana soon finds herself facing off against Doctor Poison's minions, including a group of brainwashed superheroes known as the "Sisters of Strife." The Sisters are led by a powerful warrior named Antiope (voiced by Kari Wahlgren), who is revealed to be Diana's long-lost sister.

As the battle between Diana and the Sisters intensifies, it becomes clear that Doctor Poison's plan is more complex than initially thought. She has created an army of brainwashed superheroes, including some of Diana's closest allies, in order to take over the world.

In the end, Diana manages to defeat Doctor Poison and shatter her mind control serum. However, not before Ares reveals himself as the true mastermind behind the plot. Diana engages in a fierce battle with Ares, but ultimately decides to spare his life, choosing instead to use her powers to heal the world and bring people together.

The movie ends with Diana returning to Themyscira, where she is welcomed back as a hero. However, the film also leaves room for speculation about the future of Wonder Woman, setting the stage for potential sequels or spin-offs.

Overall, Wonder Woman: Bloodlines is an action-packed animated adventure that explores themes of identity, duty, and the power of compassion. The movie features stunning animation, engaging characters, and a compelling storyline that will keep fans of the DC Comics universe on the edge of their seats.

documents.title: Batman: Hush
documents.overview: A mysterious new villain known only as Hush uses a gallery of villains to destroy Batman's crime-fighting career as well as Bruce Wayne's personal life, which has been further complicated by a relationship with Selina Kyle/Catwoman.
documents.plot:
Batman: Hush is a 2019 animated superhero film based on the DC Comics storyline of the same name. The movie follows Bruce Wayne, aka Batman, as he faces off against a mysterious villain known as Hush.

The main themes of Batman: Hush include:

1. Identity and Deception: The film explores the theme of identity and deception through the character of Hush, who is revealed to be Thomas Elliot, a childhood friend of Bruce Wayne's. Hush uses his knowledge of Bruce's past and his own traumatic experiences to manipulate him and create chaos in Gotham City.

2. Trauma and PTSD: The movie delves into the theme of trauma and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) through Bruce Wayne's character. His experiences as a child, including witnessing his parents' murder, have left emotional scars that continue to haunt him as an adult.

3. Guilt and Redemption: As Batman struggles with Hush's manipulation, he is forced to confront his own guilt over not being able to protect his parents or prevent their death. The film suggests that redemption may be possible through self-sacrifice and a willingness to face one's demons.

4. Loyalty and Betrayal: The movie explores the theme of loyalty and betrayal through the relationships between Bruce Wayne, Alfred Pennyworth, and Commissioner James Gordon. Hush's actions test these bonds and force Batman to confront the consequences of his own decisions.

5. Corruption and Power: The film touches on the theme of corruption and power through the character of Hush, who uses his intelligence and cunning to manipulate others and gain control over Gotham City. This serves as a commentary on the dangers of unchecked power and the corrupting influence it can have on individuals.

Overall, Batman: Hush offers a complex and thought-provoking exploration of these themes, adding depth and nuance to the character of Bruce Wayne and the world of Batman.

documents.title: Steven Universe: The Movie
documents.overview: Two years after bringing peace to the galaxy, Steven Universe sees his past come back to haunt him in the form of a deranged Gem who wants to destroy the Earth.
documents.plot:
Steven Universe: The Movie is a 2019 animated film based on the popular Cartoon Network series Steven Universe. The movie takes place after the events of the fourth season and follows Steven, Garnet, Amethyst, Pearl, and the Crystal Gems as they face a new threat to their home, Beach City.

The story begins with Steven feeling unfulfilled and restless, struggling to find his place in the world now that he has saved the Earth from various threats. He is also dealing with the emotional aftermath of the events of the previous season, particularly the loss of Connie's father, Greg Universe. Meanwhile, a new villain emerges in the form of White Diamond, an ancient and powerful being who seeks to reclaim her lost Crystal Gem.

White Diamond reveals that she was once a Crystal Gem herself but was separated from her fellow Gems during a catastrophic event known as the "Great War." She believes that Steven is the key to restoring her powers and reunifying the Crystal Gems. However, White Diamond's intentions are far from pure, and she plans to use Steven's connection to the Crystal Gems to gain control over the Earth.

As White Diamond's power grows, the Crystal Gems must band together to stop her. Along the way, they encounter new allies, including a group of rebels fighting against White Diamond's rule. The movie features plenty of action-packed sequences, emotional character moments, and heartfelt dialogue as the Crystal Gems work to save their home and themselves.

Throughout the movie, Steven grapples with his own identity and purpose. He struggles to come to terms with his role as a leader and a hero, feeling overwhelmed by the weight of responsibility. However, with the help of his friends and family, he learns to find his place in the world and discover new strengths within himself.

The movie's climax features an epic battle between White Diamond and the Crystal Gems, with Steven playing a crucial role in the fight. In the end, the Crystal Gems emerge victorious, but not without sacrifices. The movie concludes on a hopeful note, with Steven and his friends looking towards a brighter future and a new beginning.

Overall, Steven Universe: The Movie is a heartwarming and action-packed film that explores themes of identity, friendship, and the power of love. With its stunning animation, memorable characters, and emotional storytelling, it's a must-see for fans of the series and newcomers alike.

documents.title: tick, tick... BOOM!
documents.tagline: How much time do we have to do something great?
documents.overview: On the cusp of his 30th birthday, Jonathon Larson, a promising young theater composer, navigates love, friendship, and the pressures of life as an artist in New York City.
documents.plot:
Tick, Tick... Boom! is a musical drama film directed by Lin-Manuel Miranda, based on the 2001 semi-autobiographical musical of the same name by Jonathan Larson. The movie follows the life of Jonathan Larson, a young composer struggling to create his first Broadway musical.

The main themes of Tick, Tick... BOOM! include:

1. **Creativity and Self-Discovery**: The film explores Jonathan's journey as he navigates his passion for music and theater, while trying to find his place in the world. He grapples with self-doubt, fear of failure, and the pressure to succeed.
2. **Time Management and Priorities**: As Jonathan struggles to balance his creative pursuits with his personal life, including relationships and financial responsibilities, he must confront the consequences of prioritizing one over the other.
3. **Mortality and Impermanence**: The film touches on the theme of mortality, as Jonathan faces the reality that his time is limited. He must come to terms with the fact that his creative output may not be recognized or appreciated during his lifetime.
4. **Friendship and Support**: The relationships between Jonathan and his friends, particularly Susan (played by Vanessa Hudgens) and Michael (played by Joshua Henry), are crucial in helping him navigate the challenges he faces.
5. **Perseverance and Resilience**: Despite facing numerous setbacks and rejections, Jonathan perseveres, driven by his passion for art and his determination to leave a lasting legacy.

These themes are woven throughout the film, which features an original score by Lin-Manuel Miranda, blending music, dance, and drama to tell Jonathan's story.

documents.title: Rampant
documents.tagline: A darkness looms over the kingdom
documents.overview: Ancient Korea, 17th century. While the paranoid King Lee Jo of Joseon, vassal of the Qing dynasty, feels surrounded by conspirators and rebels, a dark evil emerges from the bowels of a merchant ship and the exiled Prince Lee Cheung returns to the royal court, ignoring that he will have to lead the few capable of defeating the ambitious humans and the bloody monsters who threaten to destroy the kingdom.
documents.plot:
Rampant is a 2018 South Korean fantasy action film directed by Lee Won-tae and produced by Next Entertainment World.

The movie follows the story of a young man named Jung-ju, who possesses supernatural strength after being bitten by a werewolf. As he struggles to control his newfound powers, Jung-ju must also confront the dark forces that seek to exploit him for their own gain.

At its core, Rampant explores themes of identity, self-discovery, and the struggle for power. Jung-ju's transformation into a werewolf serves as a metaphor for the turmoil and confusion he experiences in his personal life, as well as the societal pressures that shape his destiny. The film delves into the complexities of Jung-ju's relationships with those around him, particularly his love interest and his mentor figure, who both seek to help him navigate his newfound abilities.

The movie also touches on the idea of the "other," highlighting the fear and mistrust that can arise when individuals are perceived as different or threatening. The werewolf in Rampant represents a force of nature that is both captivating and terrifying, serving as a symbol for the uncontrollable forces that shape human lives.

Ultimately, Rampant is a story about embracing one's true self and finding the strength to overcome adversity. Through Jung-ju's journey, the film conveys a powerful message about the importance of self-acceptance, loyalty, and the pursuit of one's passions.

documents.title: The Bears' Famous Invasion of Sicily
documents.original_title: La Fameuse Invasion des ours en Sicile
documents.overview: Our story starts with Tonio, the son the bears King, being kidnapped by some hunters in the Sicilian mountains. Because of the harshness of a winter that threatens its clan with famine, the Bear King decides to invade the land of men (in the hope of finding his son). Thanks to his powerful army and the help of a wizard, he will succeed at both quests but he will soon find out that bears are not meant to live in the land of men.
documents.plot:
The Bears' Famous Invasion of Sicily, released in the United States as The Bears and the Invasion of Sicily, is a 2019 Italian-French animated adventure film and the feature debut of the illustrator Lorenzo Mattotti. Mattotti wrote the screenplay with Jean-Luc Fromental and Thomas Bidegain, adapting Dino Buzzati's 1945 children's book. Its Italian voice cast includes Toni Servillo, Antonio Albanese and Andrea Camilleri, and the French version includes Leïla Bekhti and Jean-Claude Carrière.

The filmmakers added a framing story to the book. Gedeone, a traveling showman, and his young assistant Almerina take shelter from the winter cold in a cave, where they accidentally wake an old bear from his hibernation. To keep him friendly, they entertain him with a tale from long ago, before bears vanished from Sicily: the story of the bears' famous invasion.

In that story, the bears live in the mountain woods under their king, Leonzio. While he is teaching his son Tonio to catch fish, the cub is swept away by the river and captured by humans. Overcome with grief, Leonzio neglects his duties, and winter arrives before the clan has stored enough food. Starving, the bears decide to descend to the human lands, where they can find food and search for Tonio. The cruel Grand Duke treats their arrival as an invasion and sends his army against them, but the bears prevail in fantastical battles, helped for a time by the Duke's mistreated court magician, De Ambrosiis, who befriends Leonzio. Tonio is eventually found in a circus, the Grand Duke is overthrown, and Leonzio becomes king of Sicily, with bears and humans living together in harmony. The peace does not last: some bears are corrupted by the worst human vices, and the bears return to the forest, having learned that bears and men are too different to live together.

Produced by Prima Linea Productions with Pathé, France 3 Cinéma, Indigo Film and Rai Cinema, the film drew its visual style from Buzzati's own illustrations.
