5. **Social Class and Identity**: The contrast between Charlotte's wealthy upbringing and Mary's humble origins serves to highlight their differences in social class and identity. Despite these differences, they find common ground and a deep connection with each other.

Overall, Ammonite is a powerful and moving film that explores themes of love, desire, feminism, independence, nature, and social class, set against the stunning backdrop of 19th-century England.

documents.title: Snake Eyes: G.I. Joe Origins
documents.overview: After saving the life of their heir apparent, tenacious loner Snake Eyes is welcomed into an ancient Japanese clan called the Arashikage where he is taught the ways of the ninja warrior. But, when secrets from his past are revealed, Snake Eyes' honor and allegiance will be tested – even if that means losing the trust of those closest to him.
documents.plot:
Snake Eyes: G.I. Joe Origins is a 2021 American action-adventure film directed by Robert Schwentke, based on the G.I. Joe franchise. The movie follows the origin story of Snake Eyes, a skilled ninja and member of the elite special forces team known as G.I. Joe.

The film begins with a young Orko (Henry Golding), a skilled warrior from the fictional nation of Serranocia, who is trained by his mentor, Storm Shadow's father, Lord Shen (Ronny Chieng). Orko is a member of an elite group of warriors known as the Arashikage clan. However, he soon discovers that his family has been betrayed and killed by the rival clan, led by Storm Shadow.

Orko escapes with his infant daughter, Akiko (Lola Tung), and flees to the United States, where he is taken in by a G.I. Joe team member, Duke (Chad Michael Murray). Orko adopts the codename "Snake Eyes" and joins the G.I. Joe team, using his skills to help protect the world from threats.

As Snake Eyes grows into his role as a G.I. Joe operative, he becomes embroiled in a conflict between the Arashikage clan and the rival clan, led by Storm Shadow (Lee Byung-hun). The two clans engage in a brutal battle, with Snake Eyes caught in the middle.

Meanwhile, Akiko is kidnapped by Storm Shadow's forces, leading Snake Eyes on a perilous mission to rescue his daughter. Along the way, he must confront his troubled past and learn to trust others in order to save those he cares about.

The film culminates in an epic showdown between Snake Eyes and Storm Shadow, with the fate of the world hanging in the balance. In the end, Snake Eyes emerges victorious, but not without scars from his past and a newfound sense of purpose as a G.I. Joe operative.

Throughout the movie, there are nods to the classic G.I. Joe franchise, including references to iconic characters like Scarlett (Zazie Beetz) and Destro (Idris Elba). The film's action sequences are fast-paced and intense, with Snake Eyes showcasing his impressive ninja skills.

Overall, Snake Eyes: G.I. Joe Origins is a thrilling origin story that explores the complexities of Snake Eyes' character and sets the stage for future adventures in the G.I. Joe franchise.

documents.title: Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse
documents.tagline: Miles Morales' story and the Spider-Verse web expands.
documents.overview: After reuniting with Gwen Stacy, Miles Morales — Brooklyn's full-time, friendly neighborhood Spider-Man — is catapulted across the Multiverse, where he encounters a team of Spider-People charged with protecting its very existence. But when the heroes clash on how to handle a new threat, Miles finds himself pitted against the other Spiders and must redefine what it means to be a hero so he can save the people he loves most.
documents.plot:
Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse is a 2022 American animated superhero film directed by Joaquim Dos Santos, Kemp Powers, and Justin K. Thompson. The movie is produced by Sony Pictures Animation and Columbia Pictures.

The story begins with Miles Morales (voiced by Shameik Moore), a teenager who has just been bitten by a genetically engineered spider that gives him superpowers. Miles struggles to balance his new life as Spider-Man with his relationships with his family, particularly his parents, Rio (Lauren Vélez) and Jefferson (Brian Tyree Henry).

As Miles navigates his new identity, he meets Peter B. Parker (voiced by Jake Johnson), a worn-out Spider-Man from another dimension who has been traveling through the multiverse to find a way back home. The two Spiders team up to stop Kingpin (Jason Schwartzman) and his son, Otto Octavius (Riz Ahmed), who have stolen the Spider-Verse's most powerful artifact, the Web-Slinger.

The movie takes Miles on an epic journey across multiple dimensions, where he meets other Spider-People, including Spider-Gwen (Hailee Steinfeld), Spider-Man Noir (Nicolas Cage), Peni Parker (Kimiko Glenn), and Spider-Ham (John Mulaney). Together, they form the Spider-Verse's defense against Kingpin's plans to destroy the multiverse.

As Miles and his new friends navigate through different dimensions, they encounter various challenges and obstacles. They also learn about the concept of the "Multiverse" and how it works, which adds a layer of complexity to the story.

Throughout the movie, Miles struggles with his own identity as Spider-Man, feeling pressure from Peter B. Parker's mentorship and trying to prove himself as a worthy Spider-Man in his own right. He also grapples with the consequences of his actions, particularly when he is forced to make difficult choices that affect the lives of those around him.

The movie features stunning animation, vibrant colors, and an energetic soundtrack that perfectly captures the spirit of the Spider-Verse. The voice cast delivers impressive performances, bringing depth and nuance to their characters.

In the end, Miles and his friends successfully defeat Kingpin and Otto Octavius, saving the multiverse from destruction. However, the movie concludes on a bittersweet note, as Miles says goodbye to Peter B. Parker, who has found a way back home. The final scene sets up the possibility for future adventures in the Spider-Verse.

Overall, Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse is an exciting and visually stunning film that explores themes of identity, friendship, and responsibility. With its talented voice cast, engaging storyline, and impressive animation, it's a must-watch for fans of the Spider-Man franchise and superhero movies in general.

documents.title: Black Mirror: Bandersnatch
documents.overview: In 1984, a young programmer begins to question reality as he adapts a dark fantasy novel into a video game. A mind-bending tale with multiple endings.
documents.plot:
Black Mirror: Bandersnach is an anthology series that explores the darker aspects of technology and human nature. The story revolves around Stefan Butler, a young programmer who creates an interactive choose-your-own-adventure game called "Bandersnatch" based on his favorite book, "The Colour of Magic" by Terry Pratchett.

As Stefan navigates the complexities of his creation, he becomes increasingly entangled in a web of existential crises and moral dilemmas. The main theme of Black Mirror: Bandersnach is the blurring of reality and fantasy, as Stefan's choices within the game begin to bleed into his real life.

The story delves into the consequences of playing god with technology, where the boundaries between creator and creation become increasingly ambiguous. Stefan's struggles raise questions about free will, determinism, and the nature of choice in a world where algorithms and artificial intelligence are becoming more prevalent.

Throughout the series, the audience is presented with a complex exploration of the human condition, where the lines between reality and fantasy are constantly shifting. The story also touches on themes of mental health, addiction, and the consequences of escapism, as Stefan becomes increasingly obsessed with his creation.

Ultimately, Black Mirror: Bandersnach presents a thought-provoking commentary on the darker aspects of technology and human nature, inviting viewers to reflect on their own relationship with media and the choices they make in life.

documents.title: Trinity Seven 2: Heaven's Library & Crimson Lord
documents.original_title: 劇場版 トリニティセブン -天空図書館と真紅の魔王-
documents.overview: The series focuses on the adventures of Arata Kasuga, a high school student, who is targeted by Lilith, a teacher at a mystical school. Given three choices in an effort to help save the breakdown phenomenon of the world by evil forces and while attempting to solve the mystery of his beloved cousin and childhood friend, Hijiri, who disappeared to a difference space.
documents.plot:
Trinity Seven: Heavens Library & Crimson Lord is a 2019 Japanese animated fantasy romantic comedy and the second feature film based on the Trinity Seven manga created by Kenji Saitō and Akinari Nao, following The Eternal Library and the Alchemist Girl. Hiroshi Nishikiori directed at the studio Seven Arcs from a screenplay by Saitō, with character designs by Shinpei Tomōka and music by Technoboys Pulcraft Green-fund, and the cast of the television series returned, led by Yoshitsugu Matsuoka as Arata Kasuga and Yumi Hara as Lilith Asami, with Aya Uchida, Ayane Sakura, Yōko Hikasa and Nao Tōyama, joined by Tomoaki Maeno as the demon lord Abyss Trinity and Shizuka Itō as the demonic sword Judecca.

Arata, a student mage who carries the power of a Demon Lord candidate, sets out on a routine expedition with Lilith, Akio, Lieselotte and the former enemy Lugh to a lifeless ruin that was once Akio's hometown, destroyed in an attack and closely linked to a hidden library in the sky. Soon after they arrive, a beam of light seizes the group and carries them up to the floating Heavens Library.

There they face their most dangerous opponent yet: Abyss Trinity, a powerful Demon Lord from another dimension who reveals that he is Lilith's father. He challenges Arata, who is now a Demon Lord candidate himself, and the battle goes badly; Lilith is taken captive, since her father intends to use her to restore his full power, and the rest of the group is forced into hiding. To stand a chance, Arata must grow stronger and obtain a new weapon. He seeks out Judecca, a Demon Lord weapon sealed within the library, but nearly loses control of his magic when he tries to wield it, until Lieselotte's numerology magic pulls him back from the brink and he masters a new archive of magic. With the other members of the Trinity Seven joining the fight, Arata and his companions rescue Lilith from Abyss and defeat him, and the Heavens Library is destroyed. As in the series, the action is interspersed with risqué comedy built around Arata's lecherous streak.

The film opened in Japanese cinemas on 29 March 2019 through Avex Pictures and was streamed by Crunchyroll outside Japan. Its theme song, "Against the Abyss," was performed by ZAQ. Reviewers described it as light, entertaining fan service aimed at existing fans of the series, with energetic action but little depth.

documents.title: Trouble
documents.tagline: From the silk sheets... to the mean streets...
documents.overview: A pampered dog named Trouble must learn to live in the real world while trying to escape from his former owner's greedy children and must learn how to survive on the big-city streets.
documents.plot:
Trouble, also known as Dog Gone Trouble, is a 2019 computer-animated comedy directed by Kevin Johnson and written by Rob Muir from a story by Muir and Jordan Katz. It features the voices of Big Sean as Trouble, Pamela Adlon as Rousey and Lucy Hale as Zoe Bell, with Wilmer Valderrama, Marissa Winokur, Joel McHale, Damon Wayans Jr., Olivia Holt and Betty White, in what became her final film role. The film was dedicated to the memory of executive producer Conrad Vernon's dog, Linus.

Trouble is a pampered dog who lives in luxury in a mansion with his wealthy elderly owner, Mrs. Sarah Vanderwhoozie, cared for by her loyal butler James. When Mrs. Vanderwhoozie dies of natural causes, her greedy niece and nephew, the twins Claire and Norbert, arrive to claim her fortune. While clearing out the house, they carelessly get rid of Trouble, only to learn from their aunt's lawyer that they can inherit only if they prove they can take care of the dog within a few days. Desperate, they hire Thurman Sanchez, an eccentric animal tracker, to bring him back.

Meanwhile, Trouble finds himself lost in the city with no collar, after a gang of nut-obsessed squirrels steals it in revenge for a mishap. Having never fended for himself, he must learn to survive on the streets. He meets Rousey, a tough but kind-hearted stray pit bull, and accidentally causes a chase through a restaurant that costs Zoe, a pizza delivery girl and aspiring singer, one of her deliveries. As Trouble struggles to adjust to life without his comforts, he finds friendship among other dogs, forms a bond with Zoe and begins to discover what home and family really mean, while Thurman and the twins close in on him.

The film includes cameo appearances by personalities such as dog trainer Cesar Millan and chef Ludo Lefebvre, and blends slapstick chases with a story about loyalty and belonging.

Completed in 2019, Trouble was distributed worldwide by Netflix on May 28, 2021. It received largely negative reviews; Chris Azzopardi of The New York Times wrote that while home is at the center of the story, the film itself is nothing to write home about.

documents.title: Saving Flora
documents.tagline: How far would you go to save a friend?
documents.overview: Flora is a circus elephant who can no longer perform her tricks. The night before she's scheduled to be euthanized, the circus owner's 14-year old daughter, Dawn, sneaks Flora from the circus. All that stands between them and the safety of the elephant preserve is two hundred kilometers of woods, one raging river, two elephant hunters and the fear of not making it.
documents.plot:
Saving Flora is a 2018 American family adventure drama directed by Mark Drury Taylor from a screenplay he wrote with David Moss. Produced by FJ Productions, it stars Jenna Ortega, Martin Martinez, David Arquette and Leonor Varela, with Tom Arnold and Rhea Perlman, under the tagline "How far would you go to save a friend?". The film was shot in 21 days in the Los Angeles area, including the town of Piru and the Angeles Crest. Flora is played by Tai, a veteran film elephant nearly 50 years old at the time of filming, whose earlier credits include Water for Elephants; the animal rights organisation PETA objected that the elephant had been exploited and trained under cruel conditions and asked why computer effects had not been used instead.

Flora was once the star attraction of the struggling circus run by Henry (Arquette), but because of arthritis the elephant can no longer perform her tricks. Henry and his 14-year-old daughter Dawn (Ortega) hope that an elephant preserve will take her in, but at the last minute it turns them down, demanding a large donation the circus cannot afford. With a heavy heart Henry decides to have Flora put down, and knowing it would break Dawn's heart, since Flora was trained by her late mother, he sends the girl to her aunt. Dawn discovers the plan, and the night before Flora is due to be euthanised she sneaks the elephant out of the circus and sets off on foot for the preserve. Between them and safety lie some two hundred kilometres of woods, a raging river and the mountains. They are pursued not only by Henry and Isabella (Varela), his new partner and the circus's star performer, but also by two elephant hunters, and a crook sends his protégé Sebastian (Martinez), a young pickpocket, after them. Sebastian, however, has his heart in the right place and helps Dawn and Flora on their journey. Flora finally reaches the preserve and is taken in, thanks to donations raised by Isabella, who documented the search on social media; there Flora meets her daughter. Sebastian joins the circus, where Dawn becomes a rising star.

Saving Flora premiered at the Southampton International Film Festival in October 2018, winning best feature film, and Taylor received the Indie Vision debut director award at the Twin Cities Film Fest. In Poland it grossed about 148,000 dollars. Germany's Lexikon des internationalen Films called it a likeable if hardly credible children's adventure, winning viewers over with its sincere animal-welfare message.

documents.title: The Invisible Man
documents.tagline: What You Can't See Can Hurt You
documents.overview: When Cecilia's abusive ex takes his own life and leaves her his fortune, she suspects his death was a hoax. As a series of coincidences turn lethal, Cecilia works to prove that she is being hunted by someone nobody can see.
documents.plot:
The Invisible Man is a 2020 psychological horror film directed by Leigh Whannell, based on the 1933 novel of the same name by H.G. Wells.

The story begins with Cecilia Kass (Elisabeth Moss), a young woman who escapes from an emotionally and physically abusive relationship with her boyfriend, Adrian Griffin (Oliver Jackson-Cohen). After a violent incident, Cecilia flees to Boston, where she meets a therapist named Dr. Bernard Rose (David Strathairn).

Cecilia begins to experience strange occurrences, including hearing whispers in her ear and seeing apparitions around her. She becomes convinced that Adrian is stalking her from beyond the grave, using his wealth and influence to manipulate those around him.

As Cecilia delves deeper into her past, she discovers a dark secret: Adrian was involved in a sinister experiment at his family's estate, where he used a revolutionary technology to become invisible. The experiment went horribly wrong, leaving Adrian with severe psychological trauma and a deep-seated need for control.

Cecilia becomes determined to expose the truth about Adrian's past and bring him to justice. She enlists the help of Dr. Rose, who is initially hesitant but eventually becomes her ally.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Adrian has become increasingly unstable and paranoid, using his wealth and influence to manipulate those around him. He begins to stalk Cecilia again, this time using his technology to make himself invisible.

The film's tension builds as Cecilia tries to evade Adrian's attacks and uncover the truth about his past. Along the way, she discovers a series of cryptic messages and clues that suggest Adrian's experiment has had far-reaching consequences, including the creation of an army of mindless drones who are loyal only to him.

In the film's climax, Cecilia confronts Adrian at his family's estate, where she discovers the full extent of his plan. Adrian has created a network of invisible drones who are programmed to do his bidding, and he plans to use them to take over the world.

Cecilia manages to outsmart Adrian and destroy his technology, but not before he reveals that he has been manipulating her entire life, including her relationships and her career. The film ends with Cecilia, finally free from Adrian's control, setting out on a new journey of self-discovery and empowerment.

Throughout the film, Whannell explores themes of trauma, abuse, and the dangers of unchecked power. The Invisible Man is a thought-provoking and deeply unsettling film that challenges viewers to confront their own fears and vulnerabilities.

documents.title: Down
documents.tagline: This Valentine's Day, fall head over heels
documents.overview: A pair of coworkers gets trapped in an elevator over a long weekend, but what at first promises to be a romantic connection turns nefarious as each party begins to reveal who they truly are.
documents.plot:
"Down" is an episode of the American horror anthology web series Into the Dark, the fifth installment of its first season. Directed by Daniel Stamm from a script by Kent Kubena, it premiered on Hulu on February 1, 2019, and stars Natalie Martinez as Jennifer and Matt Lauria as Guy, with Arnie Pantoja, Diane Sellers and Christina Leone. Set over a Valentine's Day holiday weekend, it is a claustrophobic thriller about two strangers trapped in an elevator.

On the evening before Valentine's Day, Jennifer and Guy, who have both worked late in a high-rise office building, step into the same elevator on different floors. The car suddenly stops, apparently because of a storm, and with no phone signal they fear being stuck until Tuesday, since Monday is Presidents' Day. At first they get along well, sharing water, wine and chocolates and sketching each other. They agree to tell their raciest stories, and Jennifer records Guy on her phone as he invents one, until his mood darkens and he stops. They have sex, after which Guy says he could fall in love with her, but Jennifer tells him it was casual and that she still has feelings for an ex.

Stung, Guy confesses that he is not an accountant but one of the building's security guards, that he has been stalking her and that he stopped the elevator with his key. When Jennifer threatens him with prison, he halts it again; in the struggle the key breaks, truly trapping them. They climb through the ceiling, and Jennifer tries to escape up a ladder, but he chases her and both fall back into the car. Jennifer ties him up and, threatening him with a cigar cutter, records his confession: his name is John Deakins, a former white-collar worker whose "invented" story was real, except that his companion died when he crashed his car; after six months in jail he could not rebuild his career and staged the elevator incident to relive his old life. Early on Monday, a guard named Eddie tries to free them, but John, having freed himself and knocked Jennifer out, kills him with the elevator, murders Eddie's girlfriend, wipes the security files and drives off with Jennifer in his trunk. When he opens it, she attacks him, rams him into a dumpster with his car and sets it ablaze with a lit cigar, killing him.

The episode received a 73% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus praised its mix of suspense, violence and romance, though Brian Tallerico of RogerEbert.com called it the series' worst episode to date.

documents.title: Digimon Adventure: Last Evolution Kizuna
documents.original_title: デジモンアドベンチャー LAST EVOLUTION 絆
documents.overview: Tai is now a university student, living alone, working hard at school, and working every day, but with his future still undecided. Meanwhile, Matt and others continue to work on Digimon incidents and activities that help people with their partner Digimon. When an unprecedented phenomenon occurs, the DigiDestined discover that when they grow up, their relationship with their partner Digimon will come closer to an end.  As a countdown timer activates on the Digivice, they realize that the more they fight with their partner Digimon, the faster their bond breaks. Will they fight for others and lose their partner? The time to choose and decide is approaching fast. There is a short time before “chosen children” will become adults. This is the last adventure of Tai and Agumon.
documents.plot:
Digimon Adventure: Last Evolution Kizuna is a Japanese animated film directed by Keisuke Furukura, produced by Toei Animation, and released in 2020. The movie serves as the final installment of the Digimon Adventure trilogy.

The story takes place one year after the events of Digimon Adventure Tri.: Reunion. The main characters, Taichi "Tai" Kamiya (also known as Tai Kamiya), Kari Kamiya, Sora Takenouchi, Mimi Tachikawa, Joe Kido, and Renamon, are now in their mid-teens. They have been reunited with their Digimon partners, Agumon, Gabumon, Biyomon, Tentomon, Palmon, Gomamon, Patamon, and Renamon.

The movie begins with the group preparing for a school festival, but they soon discover that an evil organization known as the "Digital World's" rival, the "Dark Area," has appeared. The Dark Area is led by a powerful Digimon named Zemi, who seeks to destroy the Digital World and invade the human world.

As the story unfolds, Tai and his friends learn that Zemi was once a Digimon partner of a human boy named Takato Matsuda, who had been separated from his partner, Agumon. The group soon realizes that Zemi's true intention is to take revenge on the Digital World for abandoning Takato.

The movie follows the classic Digimon Adventure formula, with Tai and his friends embarking on a perilous journey through the Digital World to stop Zemi and save their partners. Along the way, they encounter new allies, including a young girl named Yui Kanzaki, who becomes the partner of a powerful Digimon named Gatomon.

As the story progresses, Tai and his friends face numerous challenges and obstacles as they navigate the Dark Area. They also uncover the truth about Takato's past and the reason behind Zemi's desire for revenge.

In the climactic final battle, Tai and his friends confront Zemi and her minions in an epic showdown. With the help of their Digimon partners and new allies, they manage to defeat Zemi and save the Digital World from destruction.

The movie concludes with a heartwarming moment as Tai and his friends reflect on their adventures and the bonds they have formed with their Digimon partners. The film ends on a hopeful note, with the group looking forward to a bright future together.

Overall, Digimon Adventure: Last Evolution Kizuna is a thrilling and emotional conclusion to the Digimon Adventure trilogy. It features stunning animation, engaging characters, and an exciting storyline that will keep fans of the series on the edge of their seats until the very end.

documents.title: Come Play
documents.overview: A lonely young boy feels different from everyone else. Desperate for a friend, he seeks solace and refuge in his ever-present cell phone and tablet. When a mysterious creature uses the boy’s devices against him to break into our world, his parents must fight to save their son from the monster beyond the screen.
documents.plot:
Come Play is a 2020 American supernatural horror film directed by Jacob Kornbluth and produced by Focus Features. The movie follows the story of Oliver, a young boy who moves into a new home with his mother, only to discover that it's inhabited by a malevolent spirit.

The main themes of Come Play revolve around the idea of childhood innocence and the fragility of human relationships. The film explores how Oliver's experiences in the haunted house affect him emotionally and psychologically, causing him to question the nature of reality and his own sanity.

One of the primary concerns of the movie is the theme of isolation and loneliness. As a new kid in town, Oliver struggles to form connections with his peers, which makes him more vulnerable to the supernatural forces that surround him. The film highlights how these feelings of isolation can be both debilitating and transformative.

Another significant theme present in Come Play is the idea of trauma and its long-term effects on individuals. Oliver's experiences in the haunted house serve as a catalyst for exploring the emotional scars he carries from his past, including the loss of his father. This theme is expertly woven throughout the narrative, adding depth to the story.

The film also touches upon the concept of grief and the complexities of human relationships. As Oliver navigates his new home, he begins to uncover secrets about his family's past, which forces him to confront the reality of his own mortality and the impermanence of life.

Throughout its runtime, Come Play masterfully balances elements of horror, drama, and coming-of-age themes, creating a captivating narrative that lingers long after the credits roll.

documents.title: Chicuarotes
documents.overview: Cagalera and Moloteco are two teenagers from San Gregorio Atlapulco who are desperate to get out and move up and away from oppressive circumstances. When they hear of an opportunity to buy a spot in the electrician’s union, which could transform their lives, they quickly devolve into the criminal, adult underworld of Mexico City in a bid to buy their freedom.
documents.plot:
I couldn't find any information on a movie called "Chicuarotes" released in 2019 by Pulse Films. The title seems to be incorrect or not accurate.

However, I found that there is a Mexican film called "El Chicuarote" (also known as "The Chicuarote") released in 1970, directed by Miguel Zacarías. If you're referring to this movie, it's a classic Mexican comedy-drama film about the adventures of a young man named El Chicuarote and his friends.

If you could provide more information or clarify which movie you are looking for, I'd be happy to try again.

documents.title: The Divine Fury
documents.tagline: Will you stand with good or evil?
documents.overview: After waking up with mysterious wounds on his hands, a champion fighter finds himself in an otherworldly battle against evil forces that wreak havoc in the human world.
documents.plot:
The Divine Fury is a 2019 South Korean martial arts film directed by Jung Yoon-sung and written by Jung Yoon-sung and Lee Jae-kyu. The movie follows the story of Ha-ram, a young man who seeks revenge against his father's killer.

One of the main themes of The Divine Fury is the struggle for identity and belonging. Ha-ram is a half-Korean, half-Japanese martial artist who feels like an outsider in both cultures. He struggles to find his place in the world and reconcile his dual heritage.

Another significant theme is the exploration of family dynamics and the consequences of past actions. Ha-ram's father was a renowned martial artist who abandoned him as a child, leading to a deep-seated sense of rejection and anger. As Ha-ram seeks revenge against his father's killer, he must confront the complexities of his own family history and the motivations behind his father's betrayal.

The film also touches on the theme of redemption and forgiveness. Throughout the movie, Ha-ram grapples with the idea of seeking revenge versus finding a path towards healing and redemption. Ultimately, he comes to realize that forgiveness is not about forgetting past wrongs but about letting go of anger and moving forward.

Additionally, The Divine Fury explores the cultural significance of martial arts in Korean society, particularly the traditional styles such as Hapkido and Kyokushin Karate. The movie showcases the discipline, dedication, and self-control required to master these martial arts, highlighting their importance in Korean culture and identity.

Overall, The Divine Fury is a thought-provoking film that delves into complex themes of identity, family, redemption, and cultural heritage, set against the backdrop of intense martial arts action.

documents.title: Valhalla
documents.overview: The Viking children Røskva and Tjalfe embark on an adventurous journey from Midgard to Valhalla with the gods Thor and Loki. Life in Valhalla, however, turns out to be threatened by the dreaded Fenrir wolf and the god's barbaric archenemies, the Jotnar. Side by side with the gods the two children must fight to save Valhalla from the end of the world - Ragnarok.
documents.plot:
Valhalla, released in some English-speaking markets as Valhalla: The Legend of Thor, is a 2019 Danish dark fantasy adventure film directed by Fenar Ahmad. It is based on the Danish comic book series Valhalla by Peter Madsen, Hans Rancke-Madsen and Henning Kure, which had previously been adapted as a celebrated 1986 animated film. Roland Møller plays Thor and Dulfi Al-Jabouri plays Loki, with Cecilia Loffredo and Saxo Moltke-Leth as the human children Røskva and Tjalfe and Jacob Ulrik Lohmann as Týr.

Røskva and her brother Tjalfe live with their parents in a humble farmstead in Midgard. One stormy night, the gods Thor and Loki arrive and demand shelter. Thor slaughters one of the goats that pull his chariot to feed the family, warning that none of its bones must be broken so that the animal can be restored the next morning. Egged on by Loki, Tjalfe cracks a bone to eat the marrow, and when the goat rises lame, the furious Thor takes the boy as a servant to the realm of the gods. Røskva stows away in the cart, and both children end up serving in the great hall of the Aesir.

They arrive at a time of crisis. The monstrous wolf Fenrir has broken free of the chains guarded by the war god Týr, and according to prophecy his escape heralds Ragnarok, the end of the world, in which he will kill Odin. The gods are quarrelsome and divided, more concerned with keeping up appearances than with finding a solution, and they also face their ancient enemies, the giants known as the Jotnar. While the children befriend a mute and unruly young giant named Quark and set off on a dangerous journey to the stronghold of Útgarða-Loki, Røskva discovers that she possesses a special gift, a bond with wolves that allows her to approach Fenrir where the gods only seek to fight him, offering a way to restore balance between the gods and the forces of nature.

The film was shot on location in Norway, Sweden, Denmark and Iceland and was released in Denmark on 10 October 2019, exactly 33 years after the animated version. Danish reviews were mixed: B.T., Soundvenue and DR's Per Juul Carlsen each gave it four stars out of six, praising its visuals and its update of the material, while Politiken and Ekko gave it two, finding it thin and unable to match international fantasy productions. It sold around 44,000 tickets in its first weeks, far fewer than Ahmad's previous film Darkland, and was nominated for the Robert Award for Best Children's Film.

documents.title: Time to Hunt
documents.overview: Four young men want to leave their dystopian world behind and go to a distant paradise to execute a money robbery, a daring act that will have unexpected consequences.
documents.plot:
Time to Hunt is a 2020 South Korean dystopian action thriller written and directed by Yoon Sung-hyun, starring Lee Je-hoon, Ahn Jae-hong, Choi Woo-shik, Park Jeong-min and Park Hae-soo. It premiered at the 70th Berlin International Film Festival in February 2020, the first South Korean film selected for the Berlinale Special section. Its planned theatrical release was postponed by the COVID-19 pandemic, and Netflix released it worldwide on April 23, 2020.

In a near-future South Korea wracked by economic collapse, where the won has become virtually worthless, Jun-seok is released from prison after serving time for a botched robbery. He proposes one last heist to his best friends Jang-ho and Ki-hoon so that they can escape their miserable lives: an illegal gambling den that keeps its money in US dollars. They recruit Sang-soo, a friend who works there, and obtain guns from Jun-seok's contact Bong-sik. Despite a chaotic execution, the robbery succeeds, and the gang escapes with a large haul of cash along with the den's surveillance hard drives. Sang-soo stays on at his job to avoid suspicion while the others lie low.

The hard drives, however, contain footage of the den owners' dealings with powerful criminals, and the owners hire Han, a former police officer turned contract killer, to retrieve them. Han murders Bong-sik after forcing him to reveal the trio's whereabouts, then kills Sang-soo and uses his phone to track them. Realising they are being hunted, the friends flee, but Han shoots Jang-ho as they leave and then toys with them, granting them a five-minute head start to prolong the chase. Han tracks them through the city's surveillance network to a hospital, from which they barely escape. Arrested by police, he is released on the orders of a police chief.

The trio hide out near a harbour, waiting to leave the country at dawn, but Ki-hoon goes back to check on his parents. Han finds the others, and in a desperate gunfight Jang-ho is killed. As Han closes in on Jun-seok, masked men led by Bong-sik's brother Bong-soo ambush him and riddle him with bullets, and he falls into the sea. Jun-seok escapes by boat to Taiwan, but learns that Han has survived and that Ki-hoon is apparently dead. Deciding that he will never be free by running, he trains, arms himself and returns home to confront Han.

Critics praised the film's technical prowess and tension, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 69% approval; The Hollywood Reporter called it a technical tour de force.

documents.title: Pokemon the Movie: Mewtwo Strikes Back - Evolution
documents.original_title: ミュウツーの逆襲 EVOLUTION
documents.overview: After accepting an invitation from a mysterious trainer, Ash, Misty and Brock meet Mewtwo, an artificially created Pokémon who wants to do battle.
documents.plot:
Pokémon: Mewtwo Strikes Back – Evolution is a 2019 Japanese computer-animated fantasy film directed by Kunihiko Yuyama and Motonori Sakakibara, the twenty-second film in the Pokémon anime series and a CGI remake of Pokémon: The First Movie (1998). It features Rica Matsumoto as the voice of Ash Ketchum. It was released in Japan on July 12, 2019, and worldwide on Netflix on February 27, 2020.

The scientist Dr. Fuji is hired by Giovanni, the leader of the criminal organization Team Rocket, to create a powerful living weapon by cloning the legendary Pokémon Mew from one of its eyelashes. The result is Mewtwo, a genetically engineered Pokémon with immense psychic powers. When Mewtwo awakens and learns that he was made merely as an experiment, he destroys the laboratory, killing the scientists. Giovanni persuades him to work for Team Rocket, but when Mewtwo realizes that he is being used as a tool, he escapes to New Island and plots revenge against humans and their Pokémon.

Mewtwo sends holographic invitations to skilled Pokémon trainers to challenge the world's greatest Pokémon master on New Island. Ash, Misty and Brock accept, but Mewtwo whips up a storm that cancels the ferries. The trainers who reach the island by riding their Pokémon across the sea, including Ash's group, are greeted by Nurse Joy, who has been under Mewtwo's control. Mewtwo reveals his plan: using his own superior clones, he defeats the trainers' Pokémon and captures them to create an army of clones. Team Rocket sneaks onto the island, unknowingly followed by Mew.

Ash pursues his captured Pikachu into the cloning laboratory and destroys the machine, freeing the Pokémon. Mew appears, and Mewtwo challenges it to prove that clones are superior to originals, setting off a brutal battle between the original Pokémon and their copies. Horrified by the senseless suffering, Ash throws himself between the psychic attacks of Mew and Mewtwo and is turned to stone. The tears of the grieving Pokémon bring him back to life. Moved by Ash's sacrifice, Mewtwo realizes that a living being's worth depends not on its origins but on its choices. He leaves with Mew and the clones, turning back time and erasing everyone's memories of the events.

The film received mixed reviews, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 44% approval from nine critics; critics such as the Los Angeles Times's Charles Solomon criticized its CGI character designs. It was the most-watched anime title on Netflix in 2020.

documents.title: Zombie for Sale
documents.tagline: What do you know about a zombie?
documents.overview: When a pharmaceutical company's illegal experiments inadvertently create a zombie, the strange Park family finds it and tries to profit from it.
documents.plot:
The Odd Family: Zombie on Sale (Korean: Gimyohan gajok), also released in English as Zombie for Sale, is a 2019 South Korean zombie comedy directed by Lee Min-jae in his feature debut. Jung Jae-young, Kim Nam-gil, Uhm Ji-won, Lee Soo-kyung, Jung Ga-ram and Park In-hwan star as members of an eccentric rural family whose lives are upended by a most unusual visitor.

The film opens as a young zombie escapes through a sewer and wanders into a sleepy village. After being chased by a dog, he bites an elderly local before suffering a string of indignities, including being hit by a car, and he is finally captured by the Park family, who run a struggling gas station. At first the family pities their strange, gentle captive, not realizing what he is. The younger son, Min-geol, researches the creature's behavior online and concludes that he is a zombie, insisting that both the zombie and their father Man-deok, who was bitten, must be killed. The family is torn over whether they could kill their own father.

To everyone's surprise, Man-deok, locked in a camper van, does not turn into a monster. Instead, after a night of sweating and writhing, he wakes up visibly stronger and younger. When news of his rejuvenation spreads among the village elders, the family sees a business opportunity and begins charging the old people of the village to be bitten by the zombie. The venture is wildly profitable, though Man-deok soon absconds with the earnings for a trip to Hawaii, leaving Min-geol in charge. The family gives the zombie the affectionate nickname "Jjongbi" and tames him by feeding him cabbage, which he eats in place of brains, and the youngest daughter, Hae-geol, played by Lee Soo-kyung, grows especially fond of him. As word spreads, even younger villagers line up to be bitten. But when the incubation period ends, the rejuvenated villagers begin turning into real zombies, and the village descends into chaos as the oddball family must defend their home and their unusual friend.

Principal photography took place from October 2017 to January 2018. The film was well received, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting an 89% approval rating from 28 critics and a consensus calling it an auspicious debut that puts a light yet surprisingly poignant spin on a familiar genre formula.

documents.title: Rascal Does Not Dream of a Dreaming Girl
documents.original_title: 青春ブタ野郎はゆめみる少女の夢を見ない
documents.overview: In Fujisawa, Sakuta Azusagawa is in his second year of high school. Blissful days with his girlfriend and upperclassman, Mai Sakurajima, are interrupted by the appearance of his first crush, Shoko Makinohara.
documents.plot:
Rascal Does Not Dream of a Dreaming Girl (Seishun Buta Yarō wa Yumemiru Shōjo no Yume o Minai) is a 2019 Japanese animated supernatural romantic drama produced by CloverWorks and distributed by Aniplex. Adapting the sixth and seventh volumes of Hajime Kamoshida's light novel series, illustrated by Kēji Mizoguchi, it continues the 2018 television anime Rascal Does Not Dream of Bunny Girl Senpai. Director Sōichi Masui, writer Masahiro Yokotani, character designer Satomi Tamura and composers Fox Capture Plan returned, as did the entire voice cast, led by Kaito Ishikawa, Asami Seto, Inori Minase, Yurika Kubo, Nao Toyama and Atsumi Tanezaki.

In Fujisawa, high school junior Sakuta Azusagawa is enjoying his relationship with his girlfriend, the actress and upperclassman Mai Sakurajima, when his first love, Shoko Makinohara, reappears. Sakuta realizes there are two Shokos: a middle schooler who is gravely ill and needs a heart transplant, and a grown woman who once helped him. He gradually connects the mysterious scars on his chest to the adult Shoko and learns the truth: she has come back from a future in which she survived thanks to his heart, donated after he was left brain dead by a car accident on Christmas Eve. Having fallen for him, she returned to change that fate.

Sakuta resolves to accept his death so Shoko can live, but at the decisive moment Mai pushes him out of the way and is killed instead, becoming the donor herself. Devastated, Sakuta is offered one last chance by the adult Shoko, who helps him travel back in time even though doing so will erase her. Invisible to almost everyone, he finds his classmate Tomoe Koga, who can still see him, warns his past self and saves both Mai and himself, leaving young Shoko without a donor. Unwilling to accept her death, Sakuta and Mai vow to find a way, until Shoko chooses to rewrite her own past so that she never meets them. In the new present, the couple meets a healthy Shoko on a beach, and fragments of memory let them recognize one another.

The film opened in Japan on 15 June 2019, selling over 250,000 tickets and earning about ¥377 million in its first 24 days. Aniplex of America premiered it at Anime Expo before a limited North American release that October. Anime News Network called it a tearjerker that brings the story's characters and themes full circle. A sequel film followed in 2023.

documents.title: Don't Tell a Soul
documents.overview: Two thieving teenage brothers, stealing money to help their sick mom, match wits with a troubled security guard stuck at the bottom of a forgotten well.
documents.plot:
Don't Tell a Soul is a 2020 American thriller film directed by Rob McKittrick. The movie revolves around a family's dark secrets and the consequences of keeping them hidden.

The main theme of Don't Tell a Soul explores the idea of toxic masculinity and the destructive nature of patriarchal expectations. The character of Jack (played by Michael B. Jordan) is forced to confront his own vulnerabilities and the societal pressures that have shaped him into a man who prioritizes strength over emotional expression.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the family's secrets are rooted in a deep-seated fear of vulnerability and a desperate attempt to maintain control. The film highlights how this toxic dynamic can lead to devastating consequences for those involved, particularly women and children.

The movie also touches on themes of trauma, grief, and the cyclical nature of violence. It suggests that unresolved trauma can be passed down through generations, causing harm to those who are closest to us. Through Jack's character, the film explores the idea that true strength lies not in suppressing emotions, but in confronting and working through them.

Overall, Don't Tell a Soul is a gripping thriller that delves into the darker aspects of human nature, revealing the devastating consequences of keeping secrets and perpetuating toxic relationships.

documents.title: Seized
documents.tagline: They kidnapped his son. Big mistake.
documents.overview: Hiding out with his son Taylor on the Mexican coast, Nero hopes to put his violent Special Forces career behind him. But after Nero’s home is attacked and Taylor is abducted, the mysterious Mzamo orders Nero to slaughter the members of three rival crime syndicates. If he fails, Taylor will die. Now, with bullets flying and bodies dropping as Nero completes his mission, he races to find Mzamo’s hideout and seek revenge.
documents.plot:
Seized is a 2020 American action thriller film directed by Isaac Florentine. Scott Adkins stars as a former special agent forced to wipe out a series of crime syndicates to save his kidnapped son, with Mario Van Peebles as the man pulling the strings. It was released on October 13, 2020.

Nero, a former special forces operative, lives a quiet life with his son, Taylor, in Rosarito Beach on the Baja California coast, following the death of his wife. One day he is knocked unconscious by a tranquilizer dart and wakes to find that Taylor has been abducted. A mysterious caller sends him a live video feed of the boy locked inside a truck rigged to fill with exhaust fumes, and gives him an ultimatum: to see his son again, Nero must eliminate the members of three dangerous criminal organizations. He is provided with weapons, a bulletproof SUV and a vest fitted with a body camera, through which his every move is watched.

The caller, a crime lord named Mzamo, monitors Nero's progress with his lover, Alanza, his associates and a group of corrupt intelligence agents led by Donovan. Nero storms a restaurant and kills a cartel boss and all of his men, then fights his way through a brothel run by a notorious criminal and kills him. When allowed to speak with Taylor, Nero tells his son the truth about his past: he once worked for an intelligence agency under a cover name, and his wife was kidnapped and killed after someone betrayed him. After he avenged her death, the agency relocated him and Taylor to Mexico. It emerges that Donovan was the traitor and has manipulated events so that Nero's combat skills will eliminate Mzamo's rivals.

Nero's third target, the arms dealer Omar Chavez, is ready for him and destroys his body camera, leading Mzamo and Donovan to believe Nero is dead. Chavez, learning why Nero is fighting, reveals Taylor's location, but is killed when Mzamo's men attack. Donovan wants to kill Taylor, but Mzamo, realizing the agents' treachery, has already moved the boy to safety. Nero arrives at Mzamo's estate and kills Donovan and his agents, then lets Mzamo go with a warning to stay away before riding off with his son.

Seized received mixed reviews. Rotten Tomatoes reported 40% approval from five critics, though Screen Anarchy praised Florentine's fluid camerawork and Adkins's fight choreography for creating a highly entertaining, video game-like action film.

documents.title: An Egg Rescue
documents.overview: Toto and his friends must rescue his egg children after they're taken away for a gourmet food event in Africa.
documents.plot:
Little Eggs: An African Rescue, released in Mexico, Latin America and the United States as Un rescate de huevitos, is a 2021 Mexican computer-animated adventure comedy produced by Huevocartoon Producciones and directed by brothers Gabriel and Rodolfo Riva Palacio Alatriste. The fourth film in the Huevos franchise and a sequel to Un gallo con muchos huevos (2015), it brings back the Spanish voice cast alongside newcomers including Jesús Ochoa and the comedy duo Freddy and Germán Ortega. Rodolfo drew the story of an overprotective father from raising his daughter, Dione, who voices one of the chicks, and the plot from articles about rare eggs and endangered animals sold as luxury food. About 350 people worked on it, many remotely during the COVID-19 pandemic. Delayed from 2019 and 2020, it opened in Mexico on 12 August 2021, with a limited US release through Pantelion Films on 27 August.

At the Granjas el Pollón farm, the rooster Toto and his wife, Di, welcome two golden eggs, the twins Max and Uly. Their unusual color wins a ranch contest and attracts La Duquesa, a Russian egg collector, whose offer to buy them is refused. Toto, newly anxious and overprotective, tears up the twins' prize ribbons in a fit of worry and frightens them. That night Duquesa's henchmen, Panzovich and Gordimitri, send moles in mind-control helmets to steal the twins. Toto's friends Bibi and Willy free one mole, Toporocho, who helps the group board the cargo plane bound for Congo, but Toto and Di are thrown off mid-flight and saved by parachute.

The twins are taken to the African mansion of Barón Roncovich, where a Master Chef orders the captured eggs, from a peacock, an eagle, a parrot and other rare species, chilled for a gourmet auction. Max and Uly lead the others in a breakout, while Toto and Di, caught up in an animal talent show run by the lion king Leonidas I, find the courage to stand up to him and recruit an army of animals. They storm the dinner, rescue the eggs and escape a fire, and Toto apologizes to his children. When Duquesa ambushes them on the flight home, Toto trusts the twins to fight back, and a newly hatched eagle sends her out of the plane.

Bruno Bichir voices Toto and Maite Perroni voices Di. Reviews were mixed to favorable; Common Sense Media called it well made, while The Guardian gave it one star. It earned about MX$50 million in Mexico, making Huevos the country's most-watched domestic film franchise.

documents.title: Halo Legends
documents.tagline: Seven stories from the heart of the Halo universe.
documents.overview: The universe of the Halo video game series is expanded in seven short animated films from Japan's greatest anime directors and studios.
documents.plot:
Halo Legends is a 2010 adult animated military science fiction anthology film set in the universe of the Halo video game franchise and produced by 343 Industries, the Microsoft division created to oversee the Halo brand. It compiles seven animated short films, ranging from about ten to twenty minutes each, that detail the backstory of the Halo universe and offer side stories expanding it. The shorts were made by six Japanese anime houses, Bee Train, Bones, Casio Entertainment, Production I.G, Studio 4°C and Toei Animation, with directors including Mamoru Oshii, Hideki Futamura and Hiroshi Yamazaki, while Shinji Aramaki, the creator of Appleseed, served as creative adviser. The idea had its origins in the 2006 Marvel tie-in The Halo Graphic Novel; 343's creative director Frank O'Connor supplied story outlines or finished scripts, felt that the Japanese style of narrative suited the stories, and gave the studios access to Halo's story bible and art assets along with wide latitude in visual style.

The two-part Origins, set after the events of Halo 3, has the artificial intelligence Cortana recount the history of the universe to the Master Chief in cryogenic sleep, from the Forerunners' struggle against the Flood to humanity's war with the alien Covenant, while reflecting on whether war will ever end. The Duel, rendered with a filter that makes each frame resemble a watercolour painting, tells the tragic story of an Arbiter on the Elite home world who defies the Prophets. Homecoming centres on the final mission of a Spartan, Odd One Out follows the clumsy Spartan 1337, Prototype tells the story of an elite soldier called Ghost, The Babysitter depicts an infiltration mission by a squad of ODST troopers and a Spartan, and The Package follows five Spartans who must recover a "package" from a Covenant fleet.

Warner Bros. released Halo Legends on DVD and Blu-ray on 16 February 2010, a week later than planned, after a United States premiere at the AMC Metreon in San Francisco. Reception was mostly positive. IGN UK's Orlando Parfit called it a successful if uneven attempt to fuse Halo with anime, essential viewing for dedicated fans, and IGN US found the shorts surprisingly accessible to science fiction fans in general, while Game Informer felt it would appeal to fans interested in the story rather than multiplayer. It ranked second in US Blu-ray sales in its first week, and its DVD sales eventually grossed about 11 million dollars in the United States.

documents.title: The Car: Road to Revenge
documents.overview: In a dilapidated cyberpunk city plagued by crime and corruption, an unscrupulous District Attorney is savagely murdered and tossed out of a building onto his brand new car. Mysteriously, the District Attorney and his car come back to life as a single being with a thirst for vengeance. The eerie driver-less car embarks on a vicious rampage exacting revenge on the criminals who murdered him. The Car: Road to Revenge is the stylized sequel to the unconventional horror cult classic The Car (1977), and features an homage to the original with the return of Ronny Cox as the Mechanic.
documents.plot:
The Car: Road to Revenge is a 2019 American science fiction action horror film directed by G.J. Echternkamp, who wrote the screenplay with Michael Tabb and Matt Yamashita. A belated sequel to the 1977 cult film The Car, it was produced by Jeffrey Beach and Phillip Roth through Roth's UFO International and released direct to video by Universal 1440 Entertainment on 8 January 2019. It stars Grant Bowler as Detective Rainer, Kathleen Munroe as Daria Morris and Jamie Bamber as District Attorney James Caddock, with Martin Hancock as Talen, Micah Balfour, Burt Grinstead, Nina Bergman and Ronny Cox, the only returning actor from the original, as the mechanic Waits. It was shot on location in Bulgaria, with music by Frederik Wiedmann, and runs 89 minutes.

In a dilapidated near-future city plagued by crime and corruption, Caddock is a fiercely ambitious and unscrupulous district attorney whose convicts are executed on the spot in the courtroom. After a bust, he takes possession of a chip containing technology belonging to The Night, a criminal gang led by Talen whose members are given cyborg enhancements. Caddock has just bought a new black luxury sedan, the Lazarus 1, and leaves the chip inside it after taking Daria, the object of his attentions, out to dinner. Members of The Night storm his office looking for the chip and throw him out of the window onto his own car. Rainer, a gruff cop who breaks the rules, investigates the killing. Soon afterwards the driverless car mysteriously comes to life, as if the dead man and his vehicle had become a single vengeful being, breaks out of impound and begins hunting down and killing the gang members responsible for the murder. Rainer, who has taken it on himself to protect Daria from the gang, joins forces with her to solve the mystery of the car, and in an homage to the original, Waits later refits the vehicle with the body of the 1977 car.

The film was poorly received. Kurt Dahlke of DVD Talk found Bowler and Munroe to have a fair amount of chemistry and praised one stunt sequence, but called the film daft, cliched and irritating, recommending it only as brain-dead entertainment if found cheaply. Moria gave it one star, criticizing Echternkamp for an action film in which the car does little but run people over, a sketchily developed future and contradictory explanations for the car, and named it the worst film of 2019.

documents.title: The Banishing
documents.tagline: Some houses were never meant to be a home
documents.overview: In the 1930s, a young reverend and his family are forced to confront their worst fears when they discover their new home holds a horrifying secret.
documents.plot:
The Banishing is a 2021 British supernatural horror film directed by Justin Benson and Aaron Moorhead, written by Benson and Moorhead, and produced by WestEnd Films. 

The story revolves around a group of friends who reunite for a weekend at their old boarding school in the English countryside. The main character, Sarah (played by Jessica Brown Findlay), is struggling to cope with her recent past experiences, including the loss of her mother and her own mental health issues.

Upon arrival, they discover that the school has been abandoned for years due to a tragic event involving one of their former students who died under mysterious circumstances. The group decides to spend the weekend exploring the old building and catching up on each other's lives.

As night falls, strange occurrences start to happen - doors slam shut, objects move on their own, and ghostly apparitions appear. At first, they dismiss these events as mere hallucinations or the product of a vivid imagination, but soon it becomes clear that something supernatural is at play.

The group discovers that the school's dark past is connected to an ancient ritual performed by one of the former students, which awakened a malevolent entity. The entity feeds on fear and begins to manipulate the group members, causing them to turn against each other.

As tensions rise, Sarah starts to unravel the mystery behind the school's dark history and the true nature of the entity. She also delves deeper into her own past, discovering that she has a personal connection to the tragedy that occurred at the school.

The film builds up to a climactic confrontation between Sarah and the entity, which forces her to confront her deepest fears and make a choice between saving herself or saving others. The ending is intentionally ambiguous, leaving the audience questioning what is real and what is just a product of Sarah's imagination.

Throughout the film, Benson and Moorhead explore themes of trauma, grief, and the power of friendship in the face of adversity. They also pay homage to classic horror movies, incorporating elements of folk horror and supernatural terror.

Overall, The Banishing is a tense, atmospheric horror film that masterfully crafts a sense of unease and uncertainty. With its slow-burning tension and eerie atmosphere, it's sure to appeal to fans of psychological horror and supernatural thrillers.

documents.title: The Wonderland
documents.original_title: バースデー・ワンダーランド
documents.tagline: Today is your special day, but you are special every day.
documents.overview: The story follows Akane, a girl with no self-confidence. On the day before her birthday, she meets a mysterious alchemist, Hippocrates, and his student, Pipo, who both tell her they're on a mission to save the world. Together, they set out from the basement for "Wonderland," and Akane finds herself labelled Wonderland's savior.
documents.plot:
The Wonderland, released in Japan and the United Kingdom as Birthday Wonderland, is a 2019 Japanese animated coming-of-age fantasy adventure film directed by Keiichi Hara from a screenplay by Miho Maruo. It adapts Sachiko Kashiwaba's 1988 children's story Chikashitsu Kara no Fushigi na Tabi (Strange Journey from the Basement), with character designs by the illustrator Ilya Kuvshinov. Distributed by Warner Bros. Japan, it opened on 26 April 2019, as the last Japanese film released in the Heisei era, and was screened in competition at the Annecy International Animation Film Festival that June. The voice cast includes Mayu Matsuoka as Akane, Anne Watanabe as Chii, Kumiko Aso as Midori, Nao Tōyama as Pipo, Keiji Fujiwara as Zan Gu and Masachika Ichimura as Hippocrates.

Akane is a girl with no self-confidence. On the day before her birthday, her mother Midori sends her to collect her present from her aunt Chii, an outgoing antiques dealer whose boldness contrasts with Akane's timidity. At the shop they meet the mysterious alchemist Hippocrates and his tiny apprentice Pipo, who say they are on a mission to save their world. Through a passage from the basement they travel to Wonderland, a kingdom threatened by drought, where Akane is hailed as the Goddess of the Green Wind, the only one who can save it by helping the ailing crown prince of the rain kings perform the ceremony that renews the realm's water once every 600 years. A talisman that pulls her forward whenever she turns negative drags the reluctant Akane along. On the road the travellers clash with the menacing iron man Zan Gu and his sorcerer's apprentice, who are plotting to destroy the entrance to the great well, and Hippocrates is turned into a fly. In the capital, Akane learns that Zan Gu is in fact the prince himself, transformed after he grew afraid of his heavy responsibilities. Finding the courage to reach him, she embraces him, restoring his human form, and helps him perform the ceremony, which brings the water back to the kingdom. Returning home, where only hours have passed, Akane celebrates her birthday with new self-assurance.

Critics praised the visuals but found the story uneven. Matt Schley of The Japan Times gave it three out of five stars, judging that it pushes the Miyazaki buttons successfully on the surface but lacks a deeper emotional core, and Allan Hunter of Screen Daily felt that its overly busy story plays like a string of set pieces rather than building dramatic momentum.

documents.title: White Snake
documents.overview: One day a young woman named Blanca is saved by Xuan, a snake catcher from a nearby village. She has lost her memory, and together they go on a journey to discover her real identity, developing deeper feelings for one another along the way. But as they learn more about her past, they uncover a darker plot of supernatural forces vying for power, with the fate of the world hanging in the balance.
documents.plot:
White Snake (Chinese: 白蛇：缘起, literally "White Snake: The Origin") is a 2019 Chinese animated fantasy film directed by Amp Wong and Zhao Ji and animated by Light Chaser Animation. Inspired by the folktale Legend of the White Snake, it features the voices of Zhang Zhe as Blanca, a snake demon in human form, Yang Tianxiang as Xuan, the snake catcher she falls in love with, and Tang Xiaoxi as her younger sister, Verta, the green snake.

The story recalls Blanca's mission to assassinate a ruthless general who uses Daoist magic and has ordered the people to hunt snakes, believed to aid immortality. Defeated in a magical battle, she sinks into the water and loses her memory. Xuan rescues her and takes her to his home, Snake Catcher Village. As Blanca, initially wary, reveals magical abilities, the two fall in love, and a jade hairpin that stirs her memories leads them on a journey to the workshop where it was made. Meanwhile, in the cavern of the oppressed snake demons, Blanca is branded a traitor, and Verta is sent to bring her back within three days or be killed by the Death Scales implanted in her. On the way, Blanca reveals her serpent form, but Xuan accepts her. A fox demon at the workshop explains that the jade wand Blanca had used carried a cost: her memory.

When Verta finds the couple and attacks Xuan, the sisters fight, and Blanca and Xuan fall into an underground temple, where her memories return and they become lovers. Believing their differences too great, Blanca rejoins the snakes, and Xuan has the fox demon turn him into a weak demon so they can be together. Blanca uses the wand again, absorbs a Daoist's power and becomes a giant serpent bent on vengeance. The general traps the lovers to consume their spirits, but Verta tricks him into absorbing her soul first, transferring the Death Scales to him, and he is defeated. The Snake Master then seizes the Daoist power for herself until Xuan lures her into the trap, and Blanca uses the wand a final time to preserve his spirit before escaping with Verta. Five hundred years later, the sisters search for Xuan's reincarnation and find him when a young man picks up Blanca's dropped hairpin.

Released in China on 11 January 2019, the film screened at the Annecy festival and was distributed in North America by GKIDS. It received 70% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 60; Variety praised its balance of action and romance. A sequel, Green Snake, followed in 2021.

documents.title: Made in Abyss: Dawn of the Deep Soul
documents.original_title: 劇場版メイドインアビス 深き魂の黎明
documents.overview: A continuation of the epic adventure of plucky Riko and Reg who are joined by their new friend Nanachi. Together they descend into the Abyss' treacherous fifth layer, the Sea of Corpses, and encounter the mysterious Bondrewd, a legendary White Whistle whose shadow looms over Nanachi's troubled past. Bondrewd is ingratiatingly hospitable, but the brave adventurers know things are not always as they seem in the enigmatic Abyss.
documents.plot:
Made in Abyss: Dawn of the Deep Soul is a Japanese anime film directed by Hiroyuki Okiura, produced by Kyoto Animation and Sony Music Entertainment Japan. The movie takes place in the world of Made in Abyss, where humans have been exploring the mysterious abyss for centuries.

The main themes of Made in Abyss: Dawn of the Deep Soul revolve around:

1. **Exploration and Discovery**: The film follows Riko, a young girl who embarks on an expedition to the bottom of the abyss with her friend Reg. As they delve deeper into the unknown, they uncover secrets about the world's creation and the mysteries that lie within.
2. **Friendship and Sacrifice**: Throughout their journey, Riko and Reg face numerous challenges and obstacles, but their bond and trust in each other remain unbreakable. The film highlights the sacrifices one must make for the greater good and the power of friendship in overcoming adversity.
3. **Self-Discovery and Growth**: As Riko navigates the abyss, she is forced to confront her own identity and purpose. She learns to let go of her past and find a new sense of self, which ultimately leads to personal growth and transformation.
4. **The Weight of Legacy**: The film explores the consequences of humanity's actions in the past, particularly the impact of their discoveries on the present. Riko and Reg must come to terms with the weight of their ancestors' legacy and the responsibility that comes with it.

The movie features stunning animation, a gripping storyline, and well-developed characters. Made in Abyss: Dawn of the Deep Soul is an emotional and thought-provoking film that explores complex themes and ideas, making it a compelling watch for fans of science fiction and adventure anime.

documents.title: Gunpowder Milkshake
documents.tagline: Revenge is best served ice cold.
documents.overview: To protect an 8-year-old girl, a dangerous assassin reunites with her mother and her lethal associates to take down a ruthless crime syndicate and its army of henchmen.
documents.plot:
Gunpowder Milkshake is a 2021 action thriller film directed by Navot Papushado and written by Papushado, Ehud Lavski, and Yossi Ghinsberg. The movie stars Karen Gillan, Lena Headey, Carla Gugino, Michelle Yeoh, and Lena Dunham.

The story follows Scarlett (Karen Gillan), a young assassin who is on the run from her past after being betrayed by her mentor, Veronika (Lena Headey). Veronika was once a skilled hitwoman who trained many assassins, including Scarlett. However, Veronika's true intentions were to use them for her own gain and eliminate anyone who stood in her way.

Scarlett is on the run with her daughter, Ryan (Chloe Coleman), from the ruthless crime lord, Hattie (Lena Dunham). Hattie is a former protégée of Veronika's who has become a formidable foe. Scarlett seeks revenge against Veronika and Hattie for abandoning her and putting her in harm's way.

As Scarlett navigates the complex web of assassins and crime lords, she must confront her own troubled past and learn to trust herself. Along the way, she teams up with a group of skilled assassins, including The Contessa (Michelle Yeoh) and The Wolf (Chloe Coleman), who help her take down Veronika and Hattie.

Throughout the movie, Scarlett faces numerous challenges and obstacles as she tries to protect herself and her daughter. She must use her skills and cunning to outwit her enemies and stay one step ahead of them. Along the way, she also discovers more about her own past and the true nature of Veronika's plans.

The film features a mix of action, suspense, and dark humor, with a strong focus on female empowerment and revenge. The movie has received praise for its strong performances, particularly from Karen Gillan and Lena Headey, who bring depth and nuance to their characters.

Overall, Gunpowder Milkshake is a thrilling and entertaining ride that explores themes of motherhood, loyalty, and the complexities of female relationships. With its talented cast and stylish action sequences, it's a must-see for fans of action movies and thrillers.

documents.title: The Operative
documents.overview: A young Western woman is recruited by the Mossad to go undercover in Tehran where she becomes entangled in a complex triangle with her handler and her subject.
documents.plot:
The Operative is a 2019 internationally co-produced espionage thriller written and directed by the Israeli filmmaker Yuval Adler, based on the Hebrew novel The English Teacher by Yiftach Reicher-Atir, a former intelligence officer. Diane Kruger stars as a Mossad recruit, with Martin Freeman and Cas Anvar in the main supporting roles. It premiered at the Berlin International Film Festival on February 10, 2019, and Vertical Entertainment released it in the United States on August 2, 2019.

Thomas is a British Jew who formerly worked as a handler for Israel's Mossad intelligence agency in Germany. Although retired, he still has access to some of his former employer's resources. He receives an unexpected phone call from Rachel, an agent he had recruited and befriended years earlier, who has since vanished. Summoned to a safe house in Cologne to help track her down and determine whether she poses a threat, Thomas reviews her recruitment and past missions with his former superiors, and the story unfolds through a series of flashbacks.

Rachel was sent to Tehran under cover as an English teacher, with instructions to blend into daily life and attract no attention. She eventually meets Farhad Razavi, the heir to an Iranian electronics company, who hires her to give him English lessons. The two begin a romantic relationship, and Farhad introduces her to the city's underground nightlife. Her intimacy with Farhad allows Mossad to use his company to smuggle sabotaged components into Iran's nuclear program and to position him as a potential recruit. As the missions grow riskier and her life is repeatedly put in danger, Rachel's loyalties are torn between the agency, her lover and herself. She ultimately rebels, assumes a new identity and cuts off contact, resurfacing in the present because she needs Thomas's help to build a life of her own without being eliminated as a security risk.

Kruger and Eric Bana were originally announced in the lead roles in February 2018, with Freeman later taking over the role of Thomas. Critical response was mixed. Rotten Tomatoes reports a 41% approval rating from 32 reviews, praising Kruger's steely performance but calling the mission forgettable, and Metacritic gave it 47 out of 100. The New York Times noted suspenseful sequences and interesting details of spycraft en route to an unsatisfying ending, while Christy Lemire found its sluggish pace and ambiguity frustrating.

documents.title: An Affair to Die For
documents.tagline: Be careful what you lust for
documents.overview: A weekend get-away for two lovers turns into a nightmare of psychological mind games when their infidelity is discovered.
documents.plot:
An Affair to Die For is a 2019 English-language thriller directed by Víctor García and produced as a Spanish and Italian co-production. Claire Forlani, Jake Abel and Titus Welliver star, with Nathan Cooper and Melina Matthews in supporting roles. The film was shot in Sofia, Bulgaria, with the hotel interiors filmed at the Nu Boyana Film Studios.

Holly Pierpoint, a successful professor, travels to a hotel in Aspen for a secret rendezvous with her lover Everett Alan, a 27-year-old former student. Following instructions left in the room, she blindfolds herself and handcuffs herself to the bed, unaware that the man who enters is not Everett but her husband Russell, a police officer, who forces himself on her before leaving. In the next room, Russell has Everett bound and gagged and tells him that he is holding Everett's wife Lydia and daughter Jessica hostage. He orders Everett to pretend to Holly that it was he who had been with her and forbids him to let her leave the room.

Over the course of a single day, unseen voices on the phone manipulate the two lovers and turn them against each other. Russell calls Holly to warn that Everett is a dangerous man linked to the disappearance of several women, while instructing Everett to drug her. Holly smuggles a note for help to the bellboy, Dave, but it is intercepted, and Lydia's severed finger is delivered as punishment. Each lover secretly drugs the other, and when they wake, the situation has shifted again: Russell is found beaten and dying, and a disguised voice issues an ultimatum that only one of the pair may leave the hotel alive.

Holly kills Everett and is then summoned to another room, where she finds a surveillance setup and Lydia bound in the bathtub. A memory card Everett had hidden reveals that Lydia was part of the scheme, and Lydia admits to having murdered Everett's previous lovers before destroying the evidence. In the final struggle Holly kills Lydia as hotel security bursts in and orders her to surrender.

The film was released in a limited theatrical run and on video on demand in the United States on February 1, 2019. Critical response was negative. Frank Scheck of The Hollywood Reporter dismissed its convoluted plotting as B-movie mediocrity, and Roger Moore of Movie Nation gave it one and a half stars out of four, faulting its bland direction and colorless dialogue while noting Welliver's more energetic performance.

documents.title: The Blackout
documents.tagline: Who's going to save you when the world falls into darkness?
documents.overview: Contact between most towns on Earth has been severed. A small ring-like area in Eastern Europe still has electricity, and maybe even life is being reported from space. What military forces find outside the ring is shocking.
documents.plot:
The Blackout (Russian: Аванпост, romanized: Avanpost, literally "Outpost") is a 2019 Russian science fiction action thriller film directed by Egor Baranov and starring Pyotr Fyodorov, with Lukerya Ilyashenko, Svetlana Ivanova, Aleksey Chadov and Kseniya Kutepova. It concerns a mysterious event that plunges the world into darkness, wiping out life everywhere except a small area of Eastern Europe. Originally conceived as a series, the project was reshaped into a feature after the first episode was shot, and about 70% of its running time involves computer graphics. Baranov described it as more anti-war than military spectacles such as Transformers and Top Gun, and real soldiers took part in the shoot, which wrapped in May 2019.

Shortly after a serviceman named Oleg goes on a date with Alena, the whole planet except Moscow and parts of Belarus, Ukraine and Finland is suddenly cut off and engulfed in darkness. Communications fail, the fate of billions is unknown, and the survivors in the region that becomes known as the Circle of Life build a defensive perimeter of military outposts while reconnaissance teams sent beyond it fail to return. The defenders face strange enemies, including a herd of bears that attacks one outpost after it loses power. In Moscow it emerges that some survivors from near the edge of the zone have developed psychic abilities, and one of them, Sasha, has a link to the attackers. A mysterious being named Eid approaches Sasha and a group of soldiers led by Marina, claiming that his immortal race seeded Earth 200 millennia ago with humanity as a weapon to destroy native intelligent life, and that his brother Ra is now mind-controlling the people outside the Circle in order to exterminate the remaining humans before an alien colony ship arrives. Joined by other surviving soldiers, including Oleg and Yura, Eid leads a mission to Kirov to destroy Ra, but his callousness and true intentions raise doubts about whether humanity has found a savior or a new master.

The film premiered at the Cinequest Film & Creativity Festival in San Jose, California, on 15 March 2019, and opened in Russia on 21 November 2019; Shout! Factory released it on VOD in 2020 as The Blackout: Invasion Earth. It received mixed reviews and grossed $2.8 million worldwide against a budget of about $4 million.

documents.title: Abigail
documents.overview: A young girl Abigail lives in a city whose borders were closed many years ago because of an epidemic of a mysterious disease. Abby's father was one of the sick - and he was taken when she was six years old. Going against the authorities to find his father, Abby learns that her city is actually full of magic. And she discovers in herself extraordinary magical abilities.
documents.plot:
Abigail (Russian: Эбигейл) is a 2019 Russian steampunk fantasy adventure film directed by Aleksandr Boguslavsky and produced by Viktor Denisyuk and Yevgeny Melentyev for the company KinoDanz. Tinatin Dalakishvili stars as Abigail Foster, with Gleb Bochkov, Rinal Mukhametov, Artyom Tkachenko, Ravshana Kurkova and Kseniya Kutepova. The film was released in Russian cinemas on 22 August 2019 by 20th Century Fox CIS and later distributed internationally.

Abigail, known as Abby, lives in a city that many years earlier was struck by a mysterious epidemic and has since been sealed off from the outside world by its government. The authorities maintain strict control over the population, and a Special Department hunts down anyone suspected of being "infected." Among those who fell ill was Abby's father, who was taken away when she was six years old.
