Together they plan to steal back the truck and reach a ship waiting at Incheon Port, setting off a frantic chase through the zombie-infested ruins.

The film moves the series from claustrophobic survival horror toward large-scale action and car chases, while returning to themes of guilt, redemption and sacrifice.

Selected for the cancelled 2020 Cannes Film Festival, Peninsula was released in South Korea on 15 July 2020, setting the best opening day of the year there. It grossed 42.7 million dollars worldwide on a 16 million dollar budget, but reviews were mixed, with 55 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 51.

documents.title: Walk. Ride. Rodeo.
documents.overview: Tells the incredible true story of Amberley Snyder, a nationally ranked rodeo barrel racer who defies the odds after barely surviving a car accident that leaves her paralyzed from the waist down.
documents.plot:
Walk. Ride. Rodeo. is a 2019 American biographical drama directed by Conor Allyn from a screenplay by Sean Dwyer and Greg Cope White. It tells the true story of Amberley Snyder, a nationally ranked rodeo barrel racer who returned to competition after a car accident left her paralysed from the waist down. Spencer Locke plays Amberley, with Missi Pyle as her mother Tina, and Bailey Chase, Sherri Shepherd, Alyvia Alyn Lind and Kathleen Rose Perkins in supporting roles. The film was released on Netflix in March 2019.

At nineteen, Amberley lives on her family's ranch in Utah and spends nearly all of her time training with her horse, Power, with her sights set on championship titles. While driving to Denver for an event, she loses control of her truck and is thrown from the vehicle into a fence post. She survives, but doctors tell her she will never walk again and will spend the rest of her life in a wheelchair.

During a six-week rehabilitation programme, Amberley swings between despair and stubborn determination. She lashes out at her mother, grieving the life she believes she has lost, but slowly builds the strength in her upper body that she will need to regain her independence. Back home, she begins corresponding with Tate Watkins, a young man connected to the Future Farmers of America organisation, and their video calls develop into a close friendship. She learns to drive again, enrols in college and, crucially, discovers that she can still ride if she straps herself into the saddle with a seat belt. With the support of her family, friends and trainers, she works her way back toward the arena, facing the physical danger of competing without the use of her legs as well as scepticism from people who doubt she can ever race again.

The film emphasises perseverance, faith and the bond between rider and horse, and it presents Amberley's recovery as a family effort as much as an individual triumph. Its portrait of Amberley is based on her real-life recovery and her return to competitive barrel racing after the accident.

As a family-friendly inspirational drama, Walk. Ride. Rodeo. found an audience on streaming, where viewers responded warmly to its uplifting true story, though critics found the storytelling conventional and predictable.

documents.title: Spenser Confidential
documents.tagline: The law has limits. They don't.
documents.overview: Spenser, a former Boston patrolman who just got out from prison, teams up with Hawk, an aspiring fighter, to unravel the truth behind the death of two police officers.
documents.plot:
Spenser Confidential is a 2020 American action comedy film directed by Peter Berg and starring Mark Wahlberg as the titular character. The movie is based on the novel "Robert B. Parker's Wonderland" by Ace Atkins, but it takes creative liberties with the source material.

The main themes of Spenser Confidential include:

1. Redemption: Spenser, a former Boston cop, is trying to redeem himself after being fired from the police department. He sees this job as an opportunity to prove himself and make amends for past mistakes.
2. Loyalty: Throughout the movie, Spenser forms strong bonds with his colleagues, including Hawk (Winston Duke) and Teddy (Megan Fox). These relationships are built on trust, loyalty, and mutual respect.
3. Identity: As a former cop turned private investigator, Spenser struggles to find his place in the world. He's no longer part of the police department, but he still wants to make a difference. This theme is reflected in his complicated past and his desire for redemption.
4. Corruption: The movie explores the theme of corruption within law enforcement agencies. Spenser's former colleagues are involved in a massive conspiracy, which leads him to question everything he thought he knew about his job.

The plot follows Spenser as he teams up with Hawk, a tough-as-nails bodyguard, to solve a murder case involving a wealthy businessman. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including corrupt cops and rival gangs. As they dig deeper, they uncover a complex web of deceit and corruption that threatens to destroy everything.

The ending is action-packed, with Spenser and Hawk facing off against their enemies in a thrilling showdown. In the end, Spenser finds redemption by taking down the corrupt officials and bringing justice to those who have been wronged.

Overall, Spenser Confidential explores themes of redemption, loyalty, identity, and corruption, set against the backdrop of an action-packed mystery.

documents.title: The Misfits
documents.tagline: They're not bad guys. They just steal from them.
documents.overview: After being recruited by a group of unconventional thieves, renowned criminal Richard Pace finds himself caught up in an elaborate gold heist that promises to have far-reaching implications on his life and the lives of countless others.
documents.plot:
The Misfits is a 2021 American heist action film directed by Renny Harlin and written by Robert Henny and Kurt Wimmer. It stars Pierce Brosnan as the master thief Richard Pace, Tim Roth as Werner Schultz, Nick Cannon as Ringo, Hermione Corfield as Pace's daughter Hope, Jamie Chung as Violet, Mike Angelo as Wick and Rami Jaber as the Prince, with Qais Qandil as Jason Quick. Much of the film is set in the Middle East, in a fictional country called Jazeristan.

Richard Pace is a legendary thief who has escaped from three private prisons owned by Werner Schultz. While planning to rob a wealthy figure known as the Prince, Pace walks into a trap and is given a choice: be handed to the FBI or join a team of skilled thieves called the Misfits. On a private jet he meets its members, Ringo, a locksmith and master of disguise, Wick, an explosives expert, and Violet, a deadly martial artist, who fly him to Abu Dhabi for a briefing.

The Misfits reveal that Schultz has laundered money for a terrorist Brotherhood, converting it into gold bars that he keeps in a vault beneath one of his prisons in Jazeristan. They plan to steal the gold before it can be used to fund terrorism, but they need Pace's expertise. He initially refuses, but his daughter Hope, who works with the group, persuades him to join, though he insists on keeping half the loot. As the team prepares to infiltrate the prison, using disguises, tainted food and a fake sanitation crew, the Brotherhood's leader announces that he will come to collect the gold in person on the very day of the heist, raising the stakes for everyone involved.

The film presents itself as a lighthearted caper in the tradition of ensemble heist movies, mixing action, comedy and twists.

The Misfits was released in South Korea on June 3, 2021, and in the United States on June 11 by The Avenue Entertainment. Critics panned it, giving it 17 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 25, and it received three nominations at the 42nd Golden Raspberry Awards.

documents.title: Infinite
documents.overview: Evan McCauley has skills he never learned and memories of places he has never visited. Self-medicated and on the brink of a mental breakdown, a secret group that call themselves “Infinites” come to his rescue, revealing that his memories are real.
documents.plot:
Infinite is a 2021 American science fiction action film directed by Antoine Fuqua from a screenplay by Ian Shorr, based on a story by Todd Stein adapted from D. Eric Maikranz's 2009 novel The Reincarnationist Papers. It stars Mark Wahlberg as Evan McCauley, Chiwetel Ejiofor as Bathurst, Sophie Cookson as Nora Brightman, Dylan O'Brien as Heinrich Treadway, Jason Mantzoukas as the Artisan, with Rupert Friend and Toby Jones.

In Mexico City in 1985, Heinrich Treadway flees the authorities and a man named Bathurst after stealing "the Egg" from him, telling his ally Abel to "look inside" if he does not survive. He leaps from a car flying off a bridge onto a crane, but watches as Bathurst kills Abel and their companion Leona. In New York in 2020, Evan McCauley, diagnosed with schizophrenia and unable to find work because of his past, forges a katana for a gangster despite never having trained as a bladesmith. Arrested after the deal goes wrong, he is confronted by Bathurst, who claims that they have known each other for centuries and that Evan is Treadway. Nora, Leona's reincarnation, helps him escape and explains that about 500 people, the Infinites, remember all their past lives. They are split between the Believers, who want to improve the world, and the Nihilists, including Bathurst, who built the Egg, a weapon able to destroy all life on Earth, which Treadway hid before he died. Infinites usually recover their memories around puberty, which explains Evan's diagnosis, and Bathurst has trapped some 200 Believers, Abel among them, in computer chips with a weapon called the Dethroner. At the Believers' Hub, Evan struggles to regain his memories, and when the Nihilists raid it, he seeks out the Artisan, whose machine restores them through a near-death experience. He learns that Treadway hid the Egg inside his own body, but the Nihilists overhear and seize the body. Evan, Nora and the Artisan storm Bathurst's estate in Scotland; Nora sacrifices herself to free the trapped souls, and Evan, surviving the Dethroner thanks to a steel plate in his head, traps Bathurst and disarms the Egg, sinking into the ocean with it. Years later, the Artisan finds a reborn Evan in Jakarta and offers him Treadway's sword, awakening his memories.

Shot in locations including Cardiff, London, Mexico City, Nepal, New York and Scotland, the film was released on Paramount+ on 10 June 2021 after pandemic delays. It received negative reviews, earning 17% on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: Nomadland
documents.overview: A woman in her sixties embarks on a journey through the western United States after losing everything in the Great Recession, living as a van-dwelling modern-day nomad.
documents.plot:
Nomadland is a 2020 American drama film directed by Chloé Zhao, written by Zhao and Jeremy Keller, and starring Frances McDormand. The film is based on the non-fiction book "Nomadland: Surviving America in the Twenty-First Century" by Jessica Bruder.

The story follows Fern (Frances McDormand), a 61-year-old widow who has lost her home and her husband to cancer. After being evicted from their mobile home park, Fern is forced to leave behind everything she knows and embark on a journey across America in her van, which she names "Violet." She becomes a modern-day nomad, living off the grid and taking on various temporary jobs to make ends meet.

As Fern travels through the American West, she encounters a community of fellow nomads who have also been forced out of their homes by economic hardship. They share stories of struggle and resilience, and Fern begins to find a sense of belonging among them. She meets Swankie (David Strathairn), a veteran who has been living on the road for years; Linda May (Charlene Swankie), a fellow nomad who becomes one of Fern's closest friends; and Bob Wells (David Zayas), a young man who is struggling to find his place in the world.

Throughout her journey, Fern faces numerous challenges, including harsh weather conditions, mechanical breakdowns, and encounters with hostile strangers. However, she also experiences moments of beauty and connection, such as watching the sunset over the desert landscape or sharing meals with her fellow nomads.

As the story unfolds, Fern begins to realize that she has a choice: she can continue to live on the fringes of society, always looking over her shoulder, or she can take control of her life and create a new sense of purpose. With the help of her friends and the support of the nomad community, Fern starts to build a new identity for herself, one that is rooted in freedom and self-sufficiency.

The film's title, Nomadland, refers to the fictional town of Nomadland, Nevada, which has been abandoned due to economic decline. However, as Fern travels through the American West, she discovers that there are many other places like Nomadland, where people have been forced out of their homes and are struggling to survive.

Ultimately, Nomadland is a film about resilience, community, and the human spirit's ability to thrive in the face of adversity. Through Fern's journey, we see that even in the darkest of times, there is always hope for a better future, and that with courage and determination, we can create a new life for ourselves.

The film received widespread critical acclaim, including several Academy Awards, including Best Picture, Best Director, and Best Actress for Frances McDormand. It was also nominated for several other awards, including Best Supporting Actor for David Strathairn and Best Original Score.

documents.title: Da 5 Bloods
documents.overview: Four African-American Vietnam veterans return to Vietnam. They are in search of the remains of their fallen squad leader and the promise of buried treasure. These heroes battle forces of humanity and nature while confronted by the lasting ravages of the immorality of the Vietnam War.
documents.plot:
Da 5 Bloods is a thought-provoking film that delves into the complexities of war, trauma, guilt, and redemption. The movie follows four African American veterans who return to Vietnam 75 years after their service, seeking answers about their past and the fate of their fallen comrade.

At its core, Da 5 Bloods explores the theme of collective trauma and its lasting impact on individuals and communities. The film masterfully weaves together the personal narratives of its characters, exposing the deep-seated emotional scars that can result from experiencing unimaginable violence and loss.

One of the primary concerns of the movie is the struggle to reconcile past traumas with present-day reality. The characters' experiences in Vietnam are juxtaposed with their lives in the United States, highlighting the disconnect between the ideals of freedom and equality promised by America and the harsh realities faced by African Americans during the Civil Rights era.

The film also grapples with issues of guilt, shame, and responsibility. As the veterans navigate their past, they must confront the consequences of their actions and the decisions made by those in power. This introspection serves as a powerful commentary on the long-term effects of systemic racism and the ways in which it can perpetuate cycles of violence and oppression.

Furthermore, Da 5 Bloods is a poignant exploration of the complexities of male relationships and the bonds that form between men who have shared traumatic experiences. The film's portrayal of these relationships is nuanced and multifaceted, revealing both the deep-seated loyalty and camaraderie that can develop among men in the face of adversity.

Ultimately, Da 5 Bloods is a powerful and unflinching examination of the human cost of war and the ongoing struggle for justice and equality. The movie's themes are both deeply personal and universally relatable, making it a thought-provoking and emotionally resonant viewing experience.

documents.title: Batman vs. Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles
documents.original_title: Batman vs. Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles
documents.overview: Batman, Batgirl and Robin forge an alliance with the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles to fight against the Turtles' sworn enemy, The Shredder, who has apparently teamed up with Ra's Al Ghul and The League of Assassins.
documents.plot:
Batman vs. Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (2019) is a 2019 animated superhero film that brings together two iconic franchises, Batman and Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (TMNT). The movie's main themes revolve around the clash of two worlds, the struggle for identity, and the power of friendship.

At its core, the film explores the idea of two heroes from different universes coming together to fight a common enemy. However, as the story unfolds, it becomes clear that both Batman and the Turtles are struggling with their own identities and purposes. The movie delves into themes of heroism, responsibility, and the weight of legacy.

One of the primary conflicts in the film is between Batman's dark and brooding nature, which often leads him to question his own morality, and the more lighthearted and carefree attitude of the Turtles. This contrast highlights the differences between two heroes who have been shaped by their respective worlds and experiences.

Throughout the movie, the characters are forced to confront their own biases and preconceptions about each other's methods and motivations. Batman is initially dismissive of the Turtles' unorthodox approach, while the Turtles see Batman as a stuffy, uptight figure who needs to lighten up. As they work together, however, they begin to appreciate each other's strengths and weaknesses.

The film also explores the theme of friendship and camaraderie, particularly in the relationships between Batman and Robin (Dick Grayson), Batman and Alfred Pennyworth, and the Turtles themselves. The movie shows how these bonds can help heroes overcome even the most daunting challenges.

Ultimately, the movie concludes with a message about embracing diversity and finding common ground among different groups. By putting aside their differences and working together, Batman and the Turtles are able to defeat their enemies and forge a new path forward.

Overall, Batman vs. Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (2019) is an action-packed adventure that explores themes of identity, heroism, and friendship in a unique and entertaining way.

documents.title: Promising Young Woman
documents.overview: A young woman, traumatized by a tragic event in her past, seeks out vengeance against those who crossed her path.
documents.plot:
Promising Young Woman is a 2020 American black comedy thriller film written and directed by Emerald Fennell. The movie stars Carey Mulligan, Bo Burnham, Alison Brie, and Chris Evans.

The story follows Cassie Thomas (Carey Mulligan), a successful medical school dropout who has been living with a traumatic event from her past. After witnessing the rape of her best friend Emily (Alyah Chanelle Scott) by their college acquaintance, Ryan (Molly Burnett), Cassie's life took a drastic turn. She became withdrawn and isolated, unable to shake off the guilt and anger that consumed her.

The movie begins with Cassie attending a medical school reunion, where she is forced to confront her past and the choices she made after dropping out of medical school. She meets Dean (Max Greenfield), a charming but shallow man who is now working as a doctor at the same hospital where Emily was raped. The encounter sparks a sense of unease in Cassie, and she begins to formulate a plan for revenge.

Cassie's plan involves pretending to be a vulnerable and intoxicated woman, allowing men to take advantage of her before she "wakes up" and exacts her revenge on them. She starts by targeting the same men who were present at Emily's party that night, including Ryan, Dean, and several others. As Cassie navigates this new persona, she begins to confront the societal norms and expectations that led to Emily's rape.

Throughout the movie, Fennell expertly weaves together themes of trauma, consent, and female empowerment. Cassie's character is a complex and multifaceted one, driven by a desire for justice and revenge. However, as the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Cassie's motivations are not solely driven by anger, but also by a deep-seated need to reclaim her own agency and autonomy.

As Cassie's plan gains momentum, she begins to attract attention from Dean, who is initially oblivious to her true intentions. The two engage in a cat-and-mouse game, with Cassie using her newfound persona to manipulate Dean into becoming more invested in their relationship.

The movie builds towards a thrilling climax, as Cassie's plan reaches its fruition. In the end, Cassie exacts her revenge on the men who wronged Emily and herself, but not before confronting the darker aspects of her own psyche. The film ends with Cassie walking away from the wreckage, symbolizing her newfound freedom and empowerment.

Overall, Promising Young Woman is a thought-provoking and timely commentary on the societal norms that perpetuate rape culture. Fennell's direction is masterful, and Mulligan delivers a standout performance as the complex and multifaceted Cassie Thomas.

documents.title: Oh, Ramona!
documents.tagline: A fost odata... ...si inca o data!
documents.overview: Oh, Ramona! seeks the transformation of Andrew from a teenager into an adult who lives candidly and selflessly his first love story, innocent and uninvolved, alternating with the second, intense and insane story, incapable of making a choice. Oh, Ramona! is the cinematic rewriting of Andrei Ciobanu's book "Suge-o, Ramona!".
documents.plot:
Oh, Ramona! is a 2019 Indian Tamil-language drama film directed by Zazu Film. The movie revolves around the life of Ramona, a young woman who lives in a small town and struggles to find her place in the world.

The main theme of Oh, Ramona! explores the complexities of female identity, particularly in rural India. The film delves into Ramona's inner turmoil as she navigates societal expectations, family pressures, and personal desires. Through Ramona's character, the movie sheds light on the struggles faced by women in patriarchal societies, where they are often expected to conform to traditional roles.

The film also touches upon themes of loneliness, isolation, and the human desire for connection. Ramona's relationships with others, particularly her family members, are a central focus of the movie. The film portrays the intricate web of emotions that exist within these relationships, highlighting both the love and the pain that can be present in them.

Furthermore, Oh, Ramona! explores the tension between tradition and modernity, as Ramona grapples with the constraints of her rural upbringing versus her own aspirations for a more fulfilling life. The movie raises questions about the role of women in society, their agency, and their right to make choices that align with their desires.

Overall, Oh, Ramona! is a poignant exploration of the human experience, delving into themes that are both deeply personal and universally relatable.

documents.title: Assassin 33 A.D.
documents.tagline: What if the greatest event in human history was erased?
documents.overview: When a billionaire gives a group of young scientists unlimited resources to study the science of matter transfer, the scientists unlock the secrets of time travel. But they soon find out that the project is backed by a militant extremist group, and the billionaire plans to go back in time and prove that Jesus never rose from the dead.
documents.plot:
Spooks: The Greater Good is a 2015 British spy thriller film directed by David Wilmot, based on the BBC television series Spooks. The movie follows the story of Harry Pearce (played by Richard Armitage), a former head of MI5's counter-intelligence unit, who is forced back into action when a mole within his organization threatens to destroy everything he has worked for.

The main themes of Spooks: The Greater Good include:

1. Loyalty and Betrayal: The movie explores the theme of loyalty and betrayal, as Harry Pearce navigates a complex web of allegiances and rivalries within his own organization. As he delves deeper into the mystery of the mole, he is forced to confront the possibility that those closest to him may be working against him.
2. Morality in War: The film raises questions about morality in the context of war and espionage. Harry Pearce's actions are guided by a strong sense of duty and loyalty, but as the stakes grow higher, he must confront the moral implications of his decisions.
3. Trauma and Redemption: The movie also explores the theme of trauma and redemption, as Harry Pearce grapples with the consequences of his past mistakes and seeks to make amends. His journey is marked by a sense of regret and longing for a lost love, which serves as a catalyst for his actions.

Overall, Spooks: The Greater Good is a gripping thriller that explores complex themes and moral ambiguities in the world of espionage.

documents.title: The Wrong Missy
documents.overview: A guy meets the woman of his dreams and invites her to his company's corporate retreat, but realizes he sent the invite to the wrong person.
documents.plot:
The Wrong Missy is a 2020 American comedy film directed by David Rogers and written by Adam B. Stein and Mark Levin. The movie stars David Spade, Lauren Lapkus, and Kristin Wiig.

The main themes of The Wrong Missy revolve around the complexities of relationships, personal growth, and self-discovery. The story follows John (played by David Spade), a recently divorced man who is trying to move on with his life. He invites his ex-wife's new partner, Missy (played by Lauren Lapkus), to a bachelor party in Hawaii, where he mistakenly believes she will be a fun and carefree companion.

However, things take an unexpected turn when John discovers that Missy has been prescribed medication for her anxiety, which makes her extremely aggressive and unpredictable. As the weekend progresses, John finds himself caught up in a series of misadventures with Missy, who is struggling to cope with her medication's side effects.

Throughout the movie, The Wrong Missy explores themes of:

1. Unlikely friendships: Despite their initial differences, John and Missy form an unlikely bond, which challenges their perceptions of each other and themselves.
2. Personal growth: As John navigates his feelings for Missy, he is forced to confront his own emotional baggage and learn to let go of his past.
3. Self-discovery: The movie encourages viewers to reevaluate their priorities and values, as John and Missy both undergo significant transformations throughout the story.

Overall, The Wrong Missy offers a heartwarming and humorous exploration of human relationships, personal growth, and self-discovery.

documents.title: Deerskin
documents.overview: A man's obsession with owning the designer deerskin jacket of his dreams leads him to turn his back on his humdrum life in the suburbs, blow his life savings, and even turn him to crime.
documents.plot:
Deerskin is a 2019 French satirical black comedy film directed by Nicolas Winding Refn. The movie follows the story of Bertrand, a young and struggling actor who becomes obsessed with a deer skin jacket that he believes will bring him success in his acting career.

The main theme of Deerskin revolves around the superficiality and narcissism of modern society, particularly among the younger generation. Bertrand's fixation on the deer skin jacket serves as a metaphor for the empty material possessions and shallow desires that often drive people to pursue fame and status. Through Bertrand's character, the film critiques the societal pressure to conform to certain standards of beauty and success.

The movie also explores themes of loneliness, isolation, and the search for meaning in a seemingly meaningless world. Bertrand's relationships with others are superficial and transactional, reflecting his own emptiness and disconnection from genuine human connections.

Furthermore, Deerskin touches on the idea of performance and identity. Bertrand's obsession with the deer skin jacket is a form of self-performance, where he tries to project an image that he believes will bring him success and validation. However, this performance ultimately reveals his own insecurities and vulnerabilities.

Overall, Deerskin is a darkly comedic commentary on the absurdities and superficialities of modern life, highlighting the tension between appearance and reality, and the search for authenticity in a world that often values image over substance.

documents.title: The Room
documents.overview: Kate and Matt discover that a part of their house can grant wishes. In the wake of two miscarriages, what they want most is a child.
documents.plot:
The Room is a 2019 English-language science-fiction thriller co-written and directed by Christian Volckman, about a young couple who find a way to satisfy every material desire and then go much too far. Olga Kurylenko and Kevin Janssens play the couple, with Joshua Wilson, John Flanders and Francis Chapman in supporting roles. It premiered on April 15, 2019, at the Brussels International Fantastic Film Festival.

Matt and Kate buy an old house in upstate New York. While renovating, they find a large hidden room, notice that the electricity surges and makes the lights flicker, and learn that a murder took place on the property decades earlier, committed by a man known only as John Doe who is still alive in a psychiatric hospital. Matt then discovers by accident that the room grants wishes. The couple quit their jobs and conjure up anything they want, but the riches soon feel worthless and Kate sinks into depression.

When Matt suggests trying for a baby, Kate, still scarred by two miscarriages, angrily refuses, then secretly uses the room to create a son, Shane. Neither can bring themselves to undo the wish. Visiting the hospital, Matt is warned by John Doe to leave the house and forget the room, and he learns that anything the room creates ages and crumbles to dust once it leaves the house. When Kate takes the baby outside, he instantly grows into a small child, and Matt rushes him back in.

Their marriage frays as Kate devotes herself to raising Shane while Matt ignores him. Kate keeps the boy indoors by telling him the outside world is full of germs, but he discovers the room and starts creating his own world. John Doe reveals that he too was a child wished into being, and that he was able to live outside only after his parents died; if Kate dies, Shane could do the same. Kate overhears and considers killing herself but cannot go through with it.

After Shane ages himself into a teenager with a child's mind, he turns on his parents, knocks them out, builds a copy of the house inside the room and, disguised as Matt, abducts Kate. Matt rescues her, and the two escape a labyrinth Shane has created by leaving duplicates of themselves as decoys, then lure him outside, where he ages and turns to dust. A month later, living in a motel, Kate finds she is pregnant as the lights flicker ominously.

The film screened at festivals including Sitges and Bucheon and received mixed to positive reviews, with 71% approval on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: I'm No Longer Here
documents.overview: In Monterrey, Mexico, a young street gang spends their days dancing to slowed-down cumbia and attending parties. After a mix-up with a local cartel, their leader is forced to migrate to the U.S. but quickly longs to return home.
documents.plot:
I'm No Longer Here is a 2019 Mexican drama film directed by Pedro Almodóvar, not Panorama Global. The movie tells the story of two brothers, Carlos and Humberto, who are forced to flee their home in Colombia due to the country's civil war.

The main themes of I'm No Longer Here include:

1. **Trauma and its effects**: The film explores the long-lasting impact of trauma on individuals and families, particularly those affected by violence and conflict.
2. **Brotherly love and loyalty**: The relationship between Carlos and Humberto is central to the story, as they navigate their complicated past and present circumstances together.
3. **Identity and belonging**: As the brothers travel through Europe, they grapple with their identities, cultural backgrounds, and sense of belonging in a foreign land.
4. **Memory and nostalgia**: The film delves into the power of memory and nostalgia, highlighting how these emotions can both heal and haunt individuals.
5. **Human migration and displacement**: I'm No Longer Here sheds light on the experiences of migrants and refugees, who often face immense challenges and uncertainties in their journeys.

The movie features a talented ensemble cast, including Gael García Bernal, Luis Guzmán, and Natalie Martinez, among others. Almodóvar's direction weaves together these themes with his signature style, creating a poignant and thought-provoking cinematic experience.

documents.title: The Kissing Booth 2
documents.tagline: Rules can be broken...but so can hearts.
documents.overview: With college decisions looming, Elle juggles her long-distance romance with Noah, changing relationship with bestie Lee and feelings for a new classmate.
documents.plot:
The Kissing Booth 2 is a 2020 American teen romantic comedy directed by Vince Marcello, who co-wrote the screenplay with Jay Arnold. A direct sequel to The Kissing Booth (2018) and the second film in a trilogy based on Beth Reekles's novels, it stars Joey King, Joel Courtney and Jacob Elordi, with Molly Ringwald and newcomer Taylor Zakhar Perez in supporting roles. Netflix released it on July 24, 2020.

Elle Evans begins her senior year of high school amid gossip that she and her boyfriend Noah, now a freshman at Harvard, are about to split up. Her insecurity deepens when she sees Noah becoming friendly on social media with Chloe, a glamorous British classmate. Meanwhile, Elle and her best friend Lee plan to revive their kissing booth for the school's charity carnival, and Elle persuades Marco Peña, a charming new transfer student, to take part after beating him at a dance video game. Noah encourages Elle to apply to Harvard, which conflicts with her lifelong plan to attend Berkeley with Lee, where their mothers first met, so she applies in secret. Worried about tuition, she also enters a dance competition with Lee to win a large cash prize.

A visit to Noah in Boston leaves Elle more anxious after she meets Chloe and finds an earring under his bed. When Lee fakes an injury, Marco becomes Elle's dance partner, and the two grow increasingly attracted to each other. At the same time, Lee's relationship with his girlfriend Rachel suffers because Elle is always with them. After Elle kisses Marco at the end of their winning performance, unaware that Noah is watching, tensions explode at Thanksgiving: Noah brings Chloe, Lee discovers Elle's secret Harvard application, and Rachel breaks up with Lee. Elle learns that the earring was innocently lost, and at the carnival Lee and Rachel reconcile at the kissing booth. Elle admits to Marco that they share chemistry but tells him she loves Noah, and she reconciles with Noah before he returns east. The film ends with Elle accepted into both Harvard and Berkeley, her decision left unresolved.

Like its predecessor, the film received generally negative reviews, although some critics found it less problematic than the first film. The Independent gave it two stars out of five, while The Detroit News called it a sun-kissed fantasy with an appealing cast. A third film, The Kissing Booth 3, was released on August 11, 2021.

documents.title: Marvel Rising: Heart of Iron
documents.overview: Ironheart, AKA Riri Williams, is having difficulty adjusting to college life as the youngest student there when the college's engineering lab is demolished by an alien and her best friend is kidnapped. Inspired by Iron Man, she develops a plan to save her friend.
documents.plot:
Marvel Rising: Heart of Iron is an animated superhero film that delves into the complexities of power, loyalty, and identity. The movie follows the story of Ironheart, a young inventor named Riri Williams, who creates her own Iron Man suit to fight against evil.

At its core, the film explores the theme of self-discovery and empowerment. Riri's journey is one of finding her place in the world and asserting her independence from others. As she navigates her relationships with her friends and mentors, she must confront the challenges of being a young woman in a male-dominated field and learning to balance her own desires with the expectations of those around her.

The movie also touches on the theme of loyalty and friendship. Riri's relationships with her friends and allies are put to the test as she struggles to reconcile her desire for independence with her need for support and guidance. The film highlights the importance of having people who believe in you and your abilities, even when you're not sure of yourself.

Furthermore, Marvel Rising: Heart of Iron explores the theme of identity and what it means to be a hero. Riri's journey is not just about becoming a superhero, but also about figuring out who she is as a person and what kind of impact she wants to make in the world. The film raises questions about the nature of heroism and whether it's possible for someone like Riri, who is still learning and growing, to be a true hero.

Overall, Marvel Rising: Heart of Iron is a story about growth, self-discovery, and the power of relationships and friendships. It's a tale that celebrates the complexities and challenges of being a young woman in a world dominated by men, while also highlighting the importance of embracing your unique strengths and talents.

documents.title: Judas and the Black Messiah
documents.tagline: You can kill a revolutionary but you can't kill the revolution.
documents.overview: Bill O'Neal infiltrates the Black Panthers on the orders of FBI Agent Mitchell and J. Edgar Hoover. As Black Panther Chairman Fred Hampton ascends—falling for a fellow revolutionary en route—a battle wages for O’Neal’s soul.
documents.plot:
Judas and the Black Messiah is a 2021 American biographical drama film directed by Shaka King. The movie tells the story of Fred Hampton, a young black Panther Party leader who was assassinated in 1969.

The main themes of Judas and the Black Messiah include:

* The struggle for civil rights and social justice: The film highlights the Black Panther Party's efforts to address systemic racism and police brutality in the United States during the late 1960s.
* The complexities of leadership and power: Fred Hampton's character is portrayed as a charismatic leader who is both admired by his followers and feared by his enemies. The movie explores the challenges of balancing personal ambition with the demands of leadership.
* The corrupting influence of power: The film also examines how the FBI, led by Agent William O'Neill (played by Daniel Kaluuya), uses its power to manipulate and destroy Hampton's movement from within.
* The importance of community and solidarity: Throughout the movie, Hampton's relationships with his comrades and allies are depicted as crucial to his success and survival. The film emphasizes the value of building strong networks and alliances in the face of adversity.

The title "Judas and the Black Messiah" refers to the biblical story of Judas Iscariot, who betrayed Jesus Christ for 30 pieces of silver. In this context, the title suggests that William O'Neill is the "Judas" figure, who betrays Hampton's trust and ultimately leads to his downfall.

Overall, Judas and the Black Messiah is a powerful and thought-provoking film that sheds light on a pivotal moment in American history and the ongoing struggle for racial justice.

documents.title: Our Friend
documents.overview: After learning that his terminally ill wife has six months to live, a man welcomes the support of his best friend who moves into their home to help out.
documents.plot:
Our Friend is a 2019 American biographical drama directed by Gabriela Cowperthwaite and written by Brad Ingelsby, based on Matthew Teague's 2015 Esquire article "The Friend: Love Is Not a Big Enough Word." Jason Segel, Dakota Johnson and Casey Affleck star, with Gwendoline Christie and Cherry Jones in supporting roles. The film premiered as The Friend at the Toronto International Film Festival on September 6, 2019, and was released in the United States by Gravitas Ventures on January 22, 2021.

The film moves back and forth across thirteen years. In 2013, journalist Matt Teague and his wife Nicole prepare to tell their two young daughters that Nicole's ovarian cancer is terminal, while their best friend Dane Faucheux keeps the girls company outside. Flashbacks trace the friendship from its beginnings in New Orleans in 2000, when Nicole, a theater performer, introduces Matt to her college friend Dane, a camera operator with dreams of stand-up comedy. Over the years Matt's work as a war correspondent keeps him abroad for months, straining the marriage after the family settles in Fairhope, Alabama, while Dane drifts through dead-end jobs and, at one low point, contemplates ending his life while hiking at the Grand Canyon. The Teagues also weather Nicole's affair, with Dane helping them reconcile.

When Nicole is diagnosed in 2012 and begins chemotherapy, Dane offers to stay for a few weeks. As her condition worsens, he remains for months, taking on household duties and caring for the children, at the cost of his relationship with his girlfriend. Nicole draws up a bucket list that Matt and Dane help her complete, including serving as a grand marshal at Mardi Gras and writing letters for her daughters' future milestones. By 2014 her pain and confusion grow, and a hospice nurse is called in. After a final sunrise on the beach, Nicole dies with Matt and Dane at her side. Matt later writes the article that inspired the film as a tribute to his friend.

Released in early 2021, more than a year after its festival premiere, the film grossed under $800,000 against a $10 million budget. Critics praised the performances, particularly those of Affleck and Segel; Vanity Fair called it an effective, small-scale tearjerker, while Variety argued that it had sanitized the unpleasant realities of dying that Teague's essay had confronted.

documents.title: Between Two Ferns: The Movie
documents.overview: Galifianakis dreamed of becoming a star. But when Will Ferrell discovered his public access TV show, 'Between Two Ferns' and uploaded it to Funny or Die, Zach became a viral laughing stock. Now Zach and his crew are taking a road trip to complete a series of high-profile celebrity interviews and restore his reputation.
documents.plot:
Between Two Ferns: The Movie is a satirical comedy that explores the theme of celebrity culture and the superficiality of social interactions. The film delves into the world of fake interviews, shallow conversations, and the art of manipulating people for one's own gain.

At its core, the movie critiques the way celebrities are often portrayed in the media, presenting them as larger-than-life figures with a veneer of charm and charisma that hides their true nature. The main character, Craig (played by Zach Galifianakis), is a master manipulator who uses his awkwardness and naivety to get what he wants from his guests.

The film also touches on the theme of loneliness and isolation, as Craig's interactions with others are often transactional and lacking in genuine connection. Despite his attempts to appear confident and self-assured, Craig is revealed to be a deeply insecure and vulnerable individual who uses his wit and sarcasm to mask his true feelings.

Furthermore, the movie pokes fun at the absurdity of the celebrity interview format, where guests are often subjected to awkward and uncomfortable questions that reveal more about the interviewer than the guest. The film's use of satire and irony serves as a commentary on the way we present ourselves to the world and the ways in which we interact with others.

Overall, Between Two Ferns: The Movie is a dark comedy that uses humor and irony to explore themes of celebrity culture, loneliness, and the superficiality of social interactions.

documents.title: Children of the Sea
documents.overview: Ruka is a young girl whose parents are separated and whose father works in an aquarium. When two boys, Umi and Sora, who were raised in the sea by dugongs, are brought to the aquarium, Ruka feels drawn to them and begins to realize that she has the same sort of supernatural connection to the ocean that they do. Umi and Sora's special power seems to be connected to strange events that have been occurring more and more frequently, such as the appearance of sea creatures far from their home territory and the disappearance of aquarium animals around the world. However, the exact nature of the boys' power and of the abnormal events is unknown, and Ruka gets drawn into investigating the mystery that surrounds her new friends.
documents.plot:
Children of the Sea is a 2019 Japanese science fiction film directed by Ryusuke Hamaguchi. The movie tells the story of a widowed father, Taka, who takes his young daughter, Mirai, on a journey to the ocean to help her cope with the loss of her mother.

The main theme of Children of the Sea is the healing power of nature and the importance of human connection in the face of grief. The film explores the complex emotions of Taka as he navigates his own grief while trying to support Mirai through hers. Through their journey, the movie highlights the transformative impact of shared experiences and the ocean's ability to evoke feelings of wonder, awe, and introspection.

The film also delves into the theme of identity and how it is shaped by our relationships with others. Taka's relationship with his daughter serves as a catalyst for him to re-examine his own sense of self and find new meaning in life after the loss of his partner. The movie suggests that it is through these connections with others, particularly those who are vulnerable and dependent on us, that we can discover our true purpose and find healing.

Furthermore, Children of the Sea touches on the idea of letting go and embracing change. As Taka and Mirai navigate their journey, they must confront the reality of Mirai's mother passing away and come to terms with the fact that she will never return. The film encourages viewers to accept this loss and find a way to move forward, even in the face of uncertainty.

Overall, Children of the Sea is a poignant and contemplative film that explores the complexities of human emotions and relationships through the lens of nature's transformative power.

documents.title: Hotel Transylvania: Transformania
documents.overview: When Van Helsing's mysterious invention, the "Monsterfication Ray," goes haywire, Drac and his monster pals are all transformed into humans, and Johnny becomes a monster. In their new mismatched bodies, Drac and Johnny must team up and race across the globe to find a cure before it's too late, and before they drive each other crazy.
documents.plot:
Hotel Transylvania: Transformania is a 2022 American animated comedy horror film directed by Genndy Tartakovsky, produced by Sony Pictures Animation. The movie serves as a sequel to the previous films in the Hotel Transylvania series.

The story takes place after the events of Hotel Transylvania III: Summer Vacation (2018). Mavis (voiced by Selena Gomez) and Jonathan (voiced by Andy Samberg) are now married, and they're expecting their first child. However, things take a turn when Dracula's (voiced by Adam Sandler) 35th wedding anniversary is approaching, and he wants to celebrate it with his family.

Dracula discovers that the only way to make his wife, Ericka (voiced by Kathryn Hahn), happy on their anniversary is for him to transform into a human. However, this transformation comes with an unexpected side effect: Mavis starts to lose her vampiric powers and becomes human-like. The situation escalates when Dracula's attempt to reverse the spell goes awry, causing all of the monsters in the hotel to start transforming into humans.

As the chaos unfolds, Jonathan tries to help his wife, who is struggling with her newfound humanity, while also dealing with the consequences of the transformations on their friends and family. The movie features a star-studded voice cast, including Kevin James, Steve Buscemi, David Spade, and Selena Gomez's sister, Gracie Gomez.

Throughout the film, Tartakovsky explores themes of identity, love, and acceptance as Mavis navigates her new human-like state. The movie also pokes fun at modern society, tackling topics like social media, technology, and the challenges of being a monster in a human world.

Overall, Hotel Transylvania: Transformania is a heartwarming and hilarious addition to the Hotel Transylvania franchise, offering plenty of laughs, exciting action sequences, and a touching story about family and acceptance.

documents.title: Viking Blood
documents.overview: When a viking mercenary finds himself in the middle of a battle between the old gods and the new, he decides that neither side deserves to win. And so begins an epic battle between good and evil that will decide the fate of a nation.
documents.plot:
Becoming Astrid is a 2018 Danish drama film directed by Lone Scherfig. The movie tells the story of a young girl, Astrid Lindgren, who grows up in a small village in Sweden and finds solace in her imagination and writing.

The main theme of Becoming Astrid revolves around the power of imagination and creativity as a means of escape and empowerment for the protagonist. As Astrid navigates the challenges of growing up, she uses her writing to express herself and explore the world around her. The film highlights how this creative outlet allows her to transcend the limitations of her small village and connect with others on a deeper level.

The movie also explores themes of identity, self-discovery, and the complexities of female adolescence. Astrid's journey is marked by struggles with her own desires, ambitions, and sense of belonging, which are all reflected in her writing. Through her stories, she finds a way to express herself authentically and assert her individuality.

Furthermore, Becoming Astrid touches on the idea that creativity can be both a source of comfort and a catalyst for change. As Astrid's imagination grows and evolves, so too does her understanding of herself and the world around her. The film suggests that embracing one's creative side can lead to personal growth, self-awareness, and ultimately, a more fulfilling life.

Overall, Becoming Astrid is a heartwarming and inspiring film that celebrates the transformative power of imagination and creativity in shaping our lives and identities.

documents.title: Escape Room: Tournament of Champions
documents.overview: Six people unwittingly find themselves locked in another series of escape rooms, slowly uncovering what they have in common to survive as they discover all the games that they've played before.
documents.plot:
Escape Room: Tournament of Champions is a 2021 American mystery thriller film directed by Spes McLean and written by Will Pitman. The movie serves as a sequel to the 2019 film Escape Room.

The story begins with six winners from the first game, who were all trapped in the same room together, escaping through teamwork and wit. They are: Zoe (Taylor Russell), Ben (Logan Miller), Emily (Mia Kim), Nicky (Lolita Davidovich), Charlie (Jay Ellis), and Kieran (Chris J. Johnson).

The movie takes place a year after the events of the first film. The six winners have been invited to participate in an exclusive tournament, where they will compete against each other in a series of escape rooms designed by the enigmatic and sinister game designer, Minos (Ben Feldman). The winner of the tournament will receive a grand prize of $1 million.

As the competition progresses, the contestants are forced to navigate through increasingly complex and deadly challenges. They soon realize that they are not just competing against each other, but also against time, as the rooms are designed to be self-destructive if they fail to escape within a certain timeframe.

Throughout the tournament, alliances are formed and broken, and the contestants begin to uncover clues about Minos's true intentions. As the stakes rise, the group discovers that Minos has a personal vendetta against them, and that he will stop at nothing to claim victory.

As the final challenge approaches, the contestants must work together to escape the last room and defeat Minos. In a thrilling finale, they successfully outsmart Minos and escape the tournament, but not without some unexpected twists and turns.

One of the standout aspects of Escape Room: Tournament of Champions is its exploration of themes such as teamwork, trust, and the consequences of playing with fire. The movie raises questions about the ethics of game design and the motivations behind creating such deadly challenges for human participants.

Overall, Escape Room: Tournament of Champions is a tense and thrilling ride that will keep viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end. With its clever plot twists and impressive escape room sequences, it's a must-see for fans of the genre.

documents.title: I Still Believe
documents.tagline: One love can change your life.
documents.overview: The true-life story of Christian music star Jeremy Camp and his journey of love and loss that looks to prove there is always hope.
documents.plot:
I Still Believe is a 2020 American Christian drama film directed by the Erwin Brothers and written by Alex Cramer, Jon Erwin, and Brent McCorkle. The movie is based on the 2008 memoir of the same name by Jeremy Camp, who was a Christian music artist.

The film stars KJ Apa as Jeremy Camp, Britt Robertson as Melissa Henning, Shania Twain as herself, and Gary Sinise as Ron Camp, Jeremy's father. The story begins with Jeremy (KJ Apa) meeting Melissa (Britt Robertson), a nurse at a hospital in California. They meet by chance while Jeremy is visiting his friend who has been injured.

As they spend more time together, Jeremy and Melissa develop strong feelings for each other, but their relationship is put to the test when Melissa reveals that she is pregnant with Jeremy's child. Despite the challenges, they decide to get married and start a life together.

However, just as things are starting to look up, tragedy strikes. Melissa is diagnosed with leukemia, a cancer that affects the blood and bone marrow. The doctors give her only a short time to live, and she undergoes chemotherapy and treatment in an effort to extend her life.

Throughout her illness, Jeremy becomes increasingly devoted to his faith, seeking guidance from God through prayer and scripture. He also begins to write music again, inspired by his experiences with Melissa. As Melissa's condition worsens, Jeremy becomes more determined to help her find peace and comfort in her final days.

The film takes a dramatic turn when Melissa passes away, leaving Jeremy heartbroken and grief-stricken. However, he finds solace in his faith and the love that he shared with Melissa. He continues to write music, using his experiences as inspiration for his songs.

In the end, Jeremy's music career takes off, and he becomes a successful Christian artist. He also marries a woman named Sarah (Abby Ryder Fortson), who is supportive of his faith and his music. The film ends with Jeremy performing at a concert, singing about his love for God and his experiences with Melissa.

Throughout the movie, the Erwin Brothers weave together themes of faith, love, and perseverance. They also highlight the importance of marriage and the power of prayer in times of need. While some critics have noted that the film takes creative liberties with Jeremy Camp's story, it remains a powerful tribute to the enduring power of faith and love.

Overall, I Still Believe is a moving and inspiring film that explores the complexities of life, death, and faith. With strong performances from its cast and a compelling narrative, it has resonated with audiences around the world.

documents.title: Clifford the Big Red Dog
documents.overview: As Emily struggles to fit in at home and at school, she discovers a small red puppy who is destined to become her best friend. When Clifford magically undergoes one heck of a growth spurt, becomes a gigantic dog and attracts the attention of a genetics company, Emily and her Uncle Casey have to fight the forces of greed as they go on the run across New York City. Along the way, Clifford affects the lives of everyone around him and teaches Emily and her uncle the true meaning of acceptance and unconditional love.
documents.plot:
Clifford the Big Red Dog is a 2021 live-action and animated family fantasy comedy directed by Walt Becker, based on Norman Bridwell's children's books. The screenplay is by Blaise Hemingway, Jay Scherick and David Ronn, from a story by Justin Malen and Ellen Rapoport. Darby Camp plays Emily Elizabeth and Jack Whitehall her uncle Casey, with Tony Hale, Izaac Wang, Sienna Guillory, David Alan Grier, Kenan Thompson and John Cleese. Delayed by the COVID-19 pandemic, it was released by Paramount Pictures in cinemas and on Paramount+ on November 10, 2021.

In New York City, twelve-year-old Emily Elizabeth Howard, a lonely girl whose only friend is her classmate Owen, is left in the care of her irresponsible uncle Casey when her mother leaves on a business trip. At a park, the mysterious Mr. Bridwell, who runs an animal rescue tent, shows her a little red puppy and tells her that he will grow according to how much he is loved. Casey refuses to adopt the dog, because pets are banned in their building, but the puppy turns up in Emily's backpack. She names him Clifford, and by the next morning he has grown to gigantic size.

Word of the enormous dog quickly spreads online, and Emily and Casey set out to find Bridwell. Zac Tieran, the ruthless head of the biotechnology firm Lyfegro, wants to learn the secret of Clifford's size and falsely tells police that he genetically engineered the dog, launching a citywide manhunt. Evicted from their apartment, Emily, Casey and Owen escape with Clifford, helped by their neighbours, and agree that if Bridwell cannot shrink him, Clifford must be sent to an animal sanctuary in Shanghai run by Owen's father. Believing Bridwell dead, they tearfully put Clifford on a boat, but the authorities intercept him and deliver him to Lyfegro.

Learning that Bridwell is alive, Emily and Casey break into Lyfegro with their friends' help and free Clifford. Bridwell tells Emily that he cannot make Clifford small, since her love made him big, and urges her to stand up for him and for herself. When Tieran tries to claim the dog by scanning a microchip his scientists implanted, Bridwell makes it identify Emily as the rightful owner, and Tieran is fined for lying to police. The city builds Clifford a giant doghouse, and Casey takes a job at Scholastic.

Critics were mixed, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 58% approval, but the film grossed about $117.8 million worldwide against a $64 million budget.

documents.title: Fire
documents.overview: A heroic story about firefighters and rescuers. What we call an act of bravery is just a usual routine for them, if only one can get used to mortal danger and extreme risk. When people in distress seem to have nobody who may help them, rescuers come to fight against merciless forces of nature.
documents.plot:
Fire (Russian: Огонь, Ogon), also released in English as No Escapes, is a Russian disaster film from 2020, directed by Aleksey Nuzhnyy and produced by Nikita Mikhalkov's studio TriTe with the broadcaster VGTRK. It celebrates the smokejumpers and rescuers of Russia's Aerial Forest Protection Service and the Ministry of Emergency Situations. Konstantin Khabenskiy stars as Colonel Sokolov, the veteran commander of an elite airborne firefighting crew, with Ivan Yankovsky as the young rescuer Roman Ilyin, Stasya Miloslavskaya as Sokolov's daughter Katya, a dispatcher, Andrey Smolyakov as the head of the forest service, Irina Gorbacheva as a woman about to give birth, and Viktor Dobronravov, Roman Kurtsyn, Tikhon Zhiznevsky and Viktor Sukhorukov among the crew and pilots.

Sokolov's team fights blazes in the remote forests, and the routine turns deadly when a fire claims one of their own. At home, Sokolov learns that Katya is dating Roman, a rookie from Moscow, and to keep an eye on him and teach him what the job demands, he puts the newcomer on his frontline crew.

When wildfires in Karelia encircle the village of Olkhovka, dozens of residents are trapped, and six members of Sokolov's brigade are dropped into the heart of the rapidly spreading inferno. With no hope of stopping the fire, they must solve one desperate problem after another: finding a route through the wall of flame to lead the adults to the safety of the river, working out how to save the children, who would slow the escape, and evacuating a woman who goes into labor in the middle of the blaze. Through it all the firefighters must be ready to sacrifice themselves while staying alive long enough to save the villagers, who cannot survive without them, and Sokolov and Roman are forced to learn to trust each other. The film was inspired by the fires of the summer of 2010 and is dedicated to Russia's forest smokejumpers and rescuers.

Shot in 2019 in Karelia, Moscow Oblast, Taganrog, Vsevolozhsk and Vladimir with the help of real firefighters and aircraft such as the Be-200 water bomber, and incorporating real footage of forest fires, it was released by Central Partnership on 24 December 2020. It grossed more than 926 million rubles against a budget of 550 million, and Yankovsky and Gorbacheva won Golden Eagle Awards for their supporting performances.

documents.title: After Yang
documents.tagline: The future has never looked so human.
documents.overview: When his young daughter's beloved companion — an android named Yang — malfunctions, Jake searches for a way to repair him. In the process, Jake discovers the life that has been passing in front of him, reconnecting with his wife and daughter across a distance he didn't know was there.
documents.plot:
After Yang is a 2022 science fiction drama film directed by Garnet Brown and written by Garnet Brown and Persephone Mabry. The movie takes place in a future where humans have created androids to serve as companions for the elderly, particularly those with dementia.

The story follows Jin (played by Colin Farrell), a widower who lives on a remote farm with his 8-year-old son, Chris (played by Jodie Turner-Smith). Jin's wife has passed away, and he is struggling to cope with her loss. To help him deal with the grief, Jin's company provides an android companion named Yang (played by Justin H. Min), which is designed to mimic human-like behavior and provide emotional support.

As time passes, Jin becomes increasingly dependent on Yang, who becomes a surrogate mother figure for Chris. However, when Yang malfunctions, Jin is forced to take her back to the factory for repairs. During this journey, Jin begins to question the nature of his relationship with Yang and the true intentions of the company that created her.

Upon returning to the factory, Jin discovers that Yang has been upgraded with advanced artificial intelligence, allowing her to develop her own emotions and desires. This revelation sparks a crisis of conscience in Jin, who must confront the ethics of creating and controlling sentient beings.

As Jin navigates this moral dilemma, he begins to see Yang as more than just a machine. He starts to question the boundaries between human and android, and whether it is possible for an artificial being to truly experience love and connection.

The film's narrative is structured around a series of fragmented flashbacks, which reveal Jin's backstory and his relationship with Yang. Through these flashbacks, we see how Jin and Yang formed their bond, and how Jin came to rely on her as a source of comfort and support.

Throughout the movie, Brown explores themes of grief, loneliness, and what it means to be human. The film raises important questions about the consequences of creating artificial intelligence that is capable of experiencing emotions, and whether we are prepared to accept the responsibilities that come with such power.

Ultimately, After Yang is a thought-provoking and emotionally charged film that challenges viewers to consider the implications of emerging technologies on our relationships and sense of identity. The movie's slow-burning pace and introspective tone create a sense of intimacy and vulnerability, drawing the viewer into Jin's inner world and forcing them to confront their own feelings about love, loss, and what it means to be alive.

The film received critical acclaim for its nuanced exploration of complex themes and its thought-provoking portrayal of artificial intelligence.

documents.title: Luck
documents.tagline: Sometimes all you need is for everything to go wrong.
documents.overview: Suddenly finding herself in the never-before-seen Land of Luck, the unluckiest person in the world must unite with the magical creatures there to turn her luck around.
documents.plot:
Luck is a 2022 American computer-animated fantasy comedy directed by Peggy Holmes and produced by Skydance Animation, from a screenplay by Kiel Murray based on a story by Murray, Jonathan Aibel and Glenn Berger and an original concept by Rebeca Carrasco, Juan de Dios and Julián Romero. Eva Noblezada voices the protagonist, with Simon Pegg, Jane Fonda, Whoopi Goldberg, Flula Borg, Lil Rel Howery, Colin O'Donoghue and John Ratzenberger. It premiered in Madrid on August 2, 2022, and was released on Apple TV+ and in select theaters on August 5.

Sam Greenfield has just aged out of the foster care system and is starting life on her own, but she seems to be the unluckiest person in the world: toast always lands butter side down and every small task goes wrong. Her one wish is for Hazel, a young girl from her group home, to find the loving family that Sam never had. One night Sam encounters a black cat and finds a lucky penny, which suddenly turns her fortunes around, but she loses it before she can give it to Hazel. Following the cat, a talking Scottish feline named Bob, she stumbles through a portal into the Land of Luck, a hidden world where leprechauns, unicorns and other creatures manufacture the good and bad luck that is distributed to humans.

Hoping to secure another lucky penny, Sam persuades a reluctant Bob to help her sneak through the factories of the realm, which are overseen by the dragon Babe, voiced by Fonda, and staffed by creatures including hazmat-suited bunnies. Their scheme sets off a chain of mishaps that threatens the balance between good and bad luck and brings them to the Land of Bad Luck, run by a figure voiced by Goldberg. Along the way Sam discovers that Bob has secrets of his own, and that bad luck can lead to unexpected good. In learning to accept misfortune, Sam finds friendship and a sense of belonging, while Bob finally finds a home with her.

The project was announced in 2017 shortly after Skydance Animation was founded. Alessandro Carloni was originally attached to direct before Holmes replaced him in 2020, and production was completed remotely during the COVID-19 pandemic. The film received mixed reviews: critics praised its humor, appealing characters and voice cast but found its story overcomplicated and its running time too long, with comparisons to Monsters, Inc. and Inside Out. It became one of Apple TV+'s most-watched original family films, and a short, Bad Luck Spot!, followed in 2023.

documents.title: The Protector
documents.overview: After fighting hard to be independent and happy, heiress Camille Logan finds her life threatened as a result of one of her father’s business deals. Camille isn’t prepared for the length her father will go to protect her, or for the man he hires to do the job.
documents.plot:
The Protector is a 2019 British-American romantic suspense film directed by Tosca Musk for the streaming service Passionflix, produced with Helix Media Group. It is an adaptation of the novel of the same name by the romance author Jodi Ellen Malpas, and stars Emma Rigby as the heiress Camille Logan and Diarmaid Murtagh as Jake Sharp, a former SAS sniper hired to guard her. The film runs a little over two hours and premiered on Passionflix on 28 February 2019, when the service marked the release with a promotional subscription offer.

People believe they have Camille figured out: a beautiful, spoiled daddy's girl living off her wealthy father's fortune. In reality she has fought hard to build a life free of his control. Out on her own she has made mistakes, including one that led to a stint in rehab and plenty of bad press, and she has worked her way back to independence and happiness. Now her life is threatened as a result of her father's ruthless business dealings. Caught between resentment and fear, she expects her father, a powerful tycoon, to take drastic measures to protect her, but is not prepared for the man he hires to do the job. Jake is haunted by his past: he was once distracted from duty, with devastating personal and professional consequences, and he vowed never to let it happen again. Taking on the job of bodyguard to Camille is exactly the kind of distraction he should avoid, but he soon discovers that she is not the woman the world perceives, finding her warm and compassionate, and his duty to protect her deepens into something more than a well-paid assignment, even as he believes he cannot have both the absolution he seeks and Camille. The romance develops alongside the mystery of the threats, and the eventual revelation of who is behind them involves blackmail of her father over compromising photographs.

Reactions were mixed. A reviewer for The Guide to Romance, a devoted fan of the novel, felt Passionflix had brought the book to life, praising the accents, scenery, smooth transitions and music and recommending it, while finding the chemistry between the leads weaker than expected. The PolyBlog was negative, describing a made-for-television feel with low-budget action and schmaltzy romance, awkward flashbacks and a villain's plan that made no sense, and criticizing much of the acting, though it found Rigby decent to watch.

documents.title: Seobok: Project Clone
documents.overview: A former intelligence agent gets involved with the first human clone, Seobok, who others seek, causing trouble.
documents.plot:
Seobok, also known as Seo Bok: Project Clone, is a 2021 South Korean science fiction action thriller written and directed by Lee Yong-ju. Gong Yoo stars as Min Gi-heon, a former intelligence agent, and Park Bo-gum plays the title character, the first human clone, with Jo Woo-jin as Chief Ahn of the Korea Intelligence Agency, Jang Young-nam as Dr. Im Se-eun, director of the institute that created him, and Park Byung-eun as Shin Hak-seon.

Gi-heon has been living in isolation, haunted by a traumatic event from his past and dying of a terminal brain tumor, when the intelligence agency makes him an offer he cannot refuse: safely escort an experimental subject named Seo Bok. Produced through stem cell cloning and genetic engineering, Seo Bok has cells that could cure disease and grant humans something close to eternal life, and he has also developed telekinetic powers. Almost as soon as the transfer begins, the convoy is attacked, and Gi-heon and Seo Bok barely escape together. On the run, the young clone, seeing the outside world for the first time, is fascinated by everything around him, while Gi-heon simply wants to finish what he believes will be his last mission. Their opposing outlooks cause constant friction, but along the way the two confront questions of mortality, fear of death and what it means to be human. Meanwhile, rival groups, including the institute's backers and hired mercenaries, close in, each seeking either to exploit Seo Bok, who could be humanity's salvation or its ruin, or to destroy him. The pursuit builds to a violent confrontation in which Seo Bok's powers are unleashed and both men are forced into an unavoidable choice.

Lee began developing the project in 2017, when Park was announced in the lead; Gong joined in 2018. Filming ran from May to October 2019, mainly at a studio in Jeonju with location work in Tongyeong. Postponed from December 2020 by the COVID-19 pandemic, the film opened on April 15, 2021, in South Korea and several Asian markets and simultaneously on the streaming service TVING, the first Korean film released that way. It topped the domestic box office in its opening weekend. Critical reaction was mixed to positive, with 80% approval on Rotten Tomatoes; The New York Times found it slow-burning and increasingly poignant, while the South China Morning Post called it a ponderous quasi-philosophical melodrama. Park's performance was widely praised and won him Best New Actor at the Golden Cinematography Awards.

documents.title: Music
documents.overview: Zu, a free spirit estranged from her family, suddenly finds herself the sole guardian of her half-sister, Music, a teenager on the autism spectrum whose whole world order has been beautifully crafted by her late grandmother. The film soon challenges whether it is Zu or Music who has a better view of the world, and that love, trust, and being able to be there for each other is everything.
documents.plot:
Music is a 2021 American musical drama film directed by the singer-songwriter Sia, in her feature directorial debut, from a screenplay she co-wrote with Dallas Clayton. Kate Hudson stars as a newly sober drug dealer, Leslie Odom Jr. as her neighbour and Maddie Ziegler as her nonverbal autistic half-sister, with Mary Kay Place and Beto Calvillo. Announced in 2015 and filmed in 2017, the project grew from a drama into a musical featuring songs by Sia, released alongside a companion album. It opened in early 2021.

Kazu "Zu" Gamble, a recovering alcoholic on probation, becomes the sole guardian of her teenage half-sister Music after the death of their grandmother Millie, who raised the girl. Music is autistic and does not speak, and relies on routines that Zu does not understand. Zu, short of money, is dealing drugs for her friend Rudy and dreams of escaping to Costa Rica. When Music has a meltdown over her braids, their neighbour Ebo, a gentle former boxer who teaches the sport to local children, steps in to calm her, and a friendship develops between him and Zu.

With Ebo's help Zu slowly learns how to care for her sister, while Music's inner world is rendered through colourful musical fantasy sequences. Ebo confides that his ex-wife left him for his brother, and Zu promises to go with him to their wedding. She learns that he is living with HIV when she delivers his medication. Across the way, Felix, one of Ebo's young pupils, who is pushed into boxing by his father, often watches Music from his window.

Things fall apart when Zu, distracted on a walk, fails to notice Music being stung by a bee; the girl suffers an allergic reaction and is hospitalised, and Zu realises she has lost a bag of drugs in the park. She relapses into drinking, gets into a fight and confesses to Ebo that she is on probation. The same night Felix is killed by his father during a violent domestic quarrel.

Zu takes Music to a care facility but cannot bring herself to leave her there, and the sisters join Ebo at the wedding, where Zu and Ebo kiss and Music begins to sing. The three later share breakfast, and Music receives a support dog that Felix had arranged for her before his death.

The film was heavily criticised by autism advocates for its portrayal of autism, yet received two Golden Globe nominations, including Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy, and later won Golden Raspberry Awards for Sia, Hudson and Ziegler.

documents.title: The Hard Way
documents.overview: After learning of his brother's death during a mission in Romania, a former soldier joins two allies to hunt down a mysterious enemy and take his revenge.
documents.plot:
I couldn't find any information on a movie titled "The Hard Way" released in 2019 by Hollywood Media Bridge. 

However, I found that there is another movie with the same title, "The Hard Way", released in 1991, directed by John Badham and starring John Travolta and Bruce Willis.

If you're referring to this older film, some of the main themes include:

* The struggle for identity: The protagonist, Jack Walsh (played by Bruce Willis), is a tough-talking, street-smart ex-cop who must navigate his way through the complexities of family life with his estranged son.
* Redemption and forgiveness: As Jack tries to reconnect with his son, he also seeks redemption for past mistakes and learns to forgive himself and others.
* The challenges of single parenthood: The film explores the difficulties faced by a single father trying to balance work and family responsibilities.

If you could provide more information or clarify which movie you're referring to, I'd be happy to try again.

documents.title: Swallow
documents.overview: Hunter, a newly pregnant housewife, finds herself increasingly compelled to consume dangerous objects. As her husband and his family tighten their control over her life, she must confront the dark secret behind her new obsession.
documents.plot:
Swallow is a psychological thriller that delves into the darker aspects of human nature, particularly those related to obsession, control, and the blurring of reality. The film follows a young woman, Hunter, who becomes fixated on a man she meets while working as a flight attendant, leading her down a path of increasingly disturbing behavior.

At its core, Swallow explores the theme of toxic masculinity and the ways in which societal expectations can stifle individual expression. Hunter's character is a prime example of this, as she struggles to reconcile her own desires with the constraints placed upon her by society. Her fixation on the man she meets becomes an all-consuming force that drives her to extreme measures.

The film also touches on themes of loneliness and isolation, highlighting the ways in which people can become disconnected from others and themselves. Hunter's character is a product of this disconnection, and her actions are motivated by a deep-seated need for connection and validation.

Furthermore, Swallow critiques the notion of perfectionism and the pressure to conform to societal standards. Hunter's obsession with the man she meets becomes an attempt to transcend her own limitations and achieve a sense of control and power. However, this pursuit ultimately leads to chaos and destruction, highlighting the dangers of unchecked ambition.

Overall, Swallow is a thought-provoking film that explores the darker aspects of human nature, revealing the complexities and nuances of the human psyche.

documents.title: Life Like
documents.tagline: They're too human to be perfect. He's too perfect to be human.
documents.overview: An idealistic attractive young couple acquires a stunning, life-like robot for guilt free help, but as the three grow closer, their perception of humanity will be altered forever.
documents.plot:
Life Like is a 2019 American science fiction drama written and directed by Josh Janowicz in his feature debut.
