Produced by Bones and distributed by Toho, the second film in the franchise was directed by Kenji Nagasaki from a script by Yōsuke Kuroda. Daiki Yamashita and Nobuhiko Okamoto lead the voice cast, with Yoshio Inoue as the villain Nine, Mio Imada as Slice, Tomoyo Kurosawa as Mahoro and Yuka Terasaki as Katsuma.

Heroes chase the League of Villains as they transport a life-support capsule, and when Endeavor wrecks their truck, the villains turn out to be clones. The capsule's occupant, Nine, escapes in the crash and rejoins his gang. Experiments by Daruma Ujiko gave Nine a copy of All For One's Quirk, letting him hold several Quirks besides his own weather manipulation, but they also worsened a terminal illness that only a rare cell activation Quirk can cure. Meanwhile, U.A. High's Class 1-A is sent to remote Nabu Island on a work program, where Izuku Midoriya, holder of One For All, and his rival Katsuki Bakugo befriend young Katsuma, who dreams of being a hero, and his protective older sister Mahoro. After stealing the siblings' father's Quirk and finding it incompatible with Nine's blood type, the villains descend on the island, cutting off all escape and communication. Nine discovers that Katsuma has the Quirk he needs and overpowers Izuku and Bakugo, but is forced to withdraw after overusing his abilities. Learning why Katsuma is targeted, the class evacuates the islanders and separates Nine from his followers, defeating them one by one. Nine, boosted by a Quirk-enhancing drug, overwhelms the remaining students and threatens to destroy the island, until Izuku transfers One For All to Bakugo and fights with its remnants, and together they defeat him. As reinforcements arrive, All Might finds that One For All has stayed with Izuku because the transfer was interrupted. Tomura Shigaraki kills the weakened Nine, the class helps repair the island, and Izuku, who like Bakugo has lost the memory of the transfer, assures Katsuma that he too can become a hero.

Released in Japan on December 20, 2019, and in North America on February 26, 2020, the film grossed $30 million worldwide. It received positive reviews, with a 90% Rotten Tomatoes rating. A third film, World Heroes' Mission, followed in 2021.

documents.title: Embattled
documents.overview: The eldest son of a ruthlessly tough MMA champion must fight his way out of the abusive cycle his father has continued.
documents.plot:
Embattled is a 2020 American sports drama film directed by Nick Sarkisov from a screenplay by David McKenna, based on a story by Frank Ragen. Stephen Dorff stars as Cash Boykins, a reigning mixed martial arts champion styled largely after Conor McGregor, with Darren Mann as his son Jett, Elizabeth Reaser as his ex-wife Susan, Colin McKenna, the screenwriter's son, as his younger son Quinn, Donald Faison, Karrueche Tran and Saïd Taghmaoui.

Cash, himself raised by an abusive father, is the WFA lightweight and welterweight champion, a foul-mouthed bruiser who despises any hint of weakness. He abandoned his family after Quinn was born with Williams syndrome, a rare genetic disorder, and he once abused both Susan and Jett. While Cash lives in a luxurious mansion in Birmingham, Alabama, with his new wife, Jade, and their young son, Susan works as a waitress to support her boys, and 18-year-old Jett has become Quinn's devoted caregiver. Jett also wants to become a fighter, and Cash, recently returned to his life, begins training him, but his tough love quickly turns cruel, as when he throws a deliberate cheap shot at his son while sparring in front of the whole gym. Cash openly scorns Quinn and treats him as a son he would rather not have.

Around the main story run subplots about Jett's romance with a classmate, Keaton, and his attempt to set up his mother with Quinn's teacher, Mr. Stewart, a wheelchair-using army veteran. Cash, meanwhile, is fighting the league's power brokers, who deny fighters health insurance and retirement benefits and discourage unionization. Repressed memories of Cash's abuse resurface in Jett as violence, and the tensions finally pit father and son against each other in a pay-per-view bout. The build-up brings press conferences and training with Claude, the only man ever to have beaten Cash, before the two Boykins men settle their history in the cage.

The film was shot in Birmingham from September to November 2018. IFC Films acquired it in July 2020 and released it in theaters and on demand on November 20, 2020; it grossed about $32,000 in the United States and Canada. Reviews were mixed to positive, with a 71% Rotten Tomatoes rating and a Metacritic score of 56. The Los Angeles Times called it an exciting, scrappy brawler and a moving family drama, while RogerEbert.com's Robert Daniels praised the fight scenes and its critique of fighters' rights but found it clichéd and its message about violence suspect.

documents.title: Brothers by Blood
documents.overview: Peter and Michael, raised on the streets of Philadelphia, are the children of Irish mob members, forever linked by the crimes of their fathers. 30 years later, Michael now runs the criminal organization and lusts for more power, his dangerous antics frequently held in check by his cautious cousin Peter. Haunted by the death of his sister, whose passing destroyed both his parents, Peter is caught between the dreams of childhood and the realities of his life as an enforcer. His only reprieve is a local boxing gym, a sanctuary that is quickly threatened as Michael’s desire for control escalates.
documents.plot:
Brothers by Blood, originally titled The Sound of Philadelphia, is a 2020 crime drama written and directed by the French novelist and filmmaker Jérémie Guez, based on Pete Dexter's 1991 novel Brotherly Love. A Belgian, French and American co-production involving Killer Films, Brookstreet Pictures, Gapbusters and RTBF, it stars Matthias Schoenaerts and Joel Kinnaman, with Maika Monroe, Paul Schneider, Ryan Phillippe, Nicholas Crovetti, Felix Scott, James Nelson-Joyce and Antoni Corone.

In Philadelphia, cousins Peter (Schoenaerts) and Michael (Kinnaman) grew up as the sons of Irish mobsters, bound together by the crimes of their fathers. Thirty years later, Michael leads the family's criminal organization and craves more power, while the cautious Peter, who works as his enforcer, tries to keep his reckless cousin in check. Peter is emotionally numb, still haunted by the death of his sister, which destroyed both his parents; flashbacks with the young Peter (Crovetti) reveal a painful accident, a catatonic mother and a vengeful father (Phillippe). In the opening scene he calmly steps off a rooftop while joking with Michael and their friend Jimmy (Schneider), and survives the fall. His only refuges are a local boxing gym, where he looks out for a young fighter, and Jimmy's sister Grace (Monroe), whose return to the neighborhood hints at romance. As the Italian mob expands its territory, Michael decides to fight back, and other figures urge Peter to rein him in. Torn between loyalty and self-preservation, Peter is drawn toward an inevitable confrontation with his cousin. Guez keeps most of the violence off screen, using long takes and an understated ending that departs from the novel.

Schoenaerts was cast in 2018 for a shoot planned in Philadelphia, and Kinnaman, Phillippe, Schneider and Monroe joined in early 2019; filming began in New York in March 2019. A premiere planned at the Tribeca Film Festival in April 2020 was cancelled because of the pandemic, and the film instead premiered at the Deauville American Film Festival on 8 September 2020. Vertical Entertainment acquired US rights, retitled it and released it on 22 January 2021. Reviews were largely negative, with 25% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 41; Variety praised the brooding, Method-style performances of the two leads but found the slow, oblique storytelling hard to follow.

documents.title: My Spy
documents.overview: A hardened CIA operative finds himself at the mercy of a precocious 9-year-old girl, having been sent undercover to surveil her family.
documents.plot:
My Spy is a 2020 American action comedy film produced and directed by Peter Segal from a screenplay by Jon and Erich Hoeber. It stars Dave Bautista as a CIA operative who falls under the control of a precocious nine-year-old girl, played by Chloe Coleman in her film debut, with Kristen Schaal, Parisa Fitz-Henley and Ken Jeong in supporting roles. Released in Australian cinemas by STX Entertainment in January 2020, it was bought by Amazon Studios after the COVID-19 pandemic closed theaters and premiered on Prime Video in June 2020.

JJ, a former Army Ranger recently recruited by the CIA, wrecks his first big assignment in Pripyat, a plutonium deal between the Russian mafia and a terrorist named Hassan, through sheer lack of subtlety. Even so, his boss David Kim sends him with Bobbi, an eager tech operator who idolizes him, to watch the family of Victor Marquez, a French arms dealer who wants to sell plans for a miniaturized nuclear bomb to Hassan. Victor lost the plans to his brother David, who hid them before Victor murdered him, and the CIA suspects that David's American widow Kate and their daughter Sophie, who have moved back to Wicker Park in Chicago, may unknowingly have them. JJ and Bobbi set up a surveillance post in the family's apartment building, but Sophie quickly finds one of their hidden cameras, traces the signal and confronts them. She blackmails JJ into spending time with her, helping her navigate life at her new school and teaching her the basics of espionage as she struggles to fit in, and she works to bring him and her mother together. The unlikely friendship grows into something like a family, until Kim discovers that JJ has become personally involved with his targets and pulls him off the case, Kate learns the truth about him, and Victor arrives in Chicago to take back the plans, putting Sophie in danger and forcing JJ to prove himself.

The film received mixed reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes it has a 49% approval rating based on 127 reviews, with a consensus that it plugs Bautista into the "charismatic action star meets cute kid" formula with generally painless but mediocre results, and Metacritic gives it a score of 46 out of 100. A sequel, The Eternal City, was released in July 2024.

documents.title: Respect
documents.overview: The rise of Aretha Franklin’s career from a child singing in her father’s church’s choir to her international superstardom.
documents.plot:
Respect is a 2021 biographical drama film directed by Jay Roach, written by Jonathan Herman and Will Berson, and produced by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer. The movie tells the story of Aretha Franklin's life, focusing on her rise to fame as the "Queen of Soul" and her struggles with sexism, racism, and personal relationships.

The main themes of Respect include:

1. Empowerment: The film showcases Aretha Franklin's journey from a young girl with a powerful voice to a confident woman who takes control of her life and career.
2. Feminism: The movie highlights the challenges faced by women in the music industry during the 1960s and 1970s, particularly in terms of sexism and objectification.
3. Racism: Respect explores the racial tensions and injustices that Aretha Franklin faced throughout her life, including her experiences with racism in the music industry and her involvement in the Civil Rights Movement.
4. Personal relationships: The film delves into Aretha's complex relationships with her family members, particularly her father Clarence Franklin, who played a significant role in shaping her early career.
5. Identity: Respect explores Aretha's struggles to balance her personal identity with her public persona as "The Queen of Soul," highlighting the tension between her desire for authenticity and the pressures of fame.

Overall, Respect is a powerful tribute to Aretha Franklin's life and legacy, offering a nuanced exploration of the challenges she faced as a black woman in a male-dominated industry.

documents.title: Dragon Quest: Your Story
documents.original_title: ドラゴンクエスト ユア・ストーリー
documents.overview: Luca follows in his father's footsteps to rescue his mother from evil Ladja. Finding the heavenly hero who wields the Zenithian sword is his only hope.
documents.plot:
Dragon Quest: Your Story is a 2019 Japanese computer-animated fantasy film based on the Dragon Quest video game series, adapting the storyline of the 1992 game Dragon Quest V. Produced with live-action actors in the voice roles, it features Takeru Satoh, Kasumi Arimura, Haru, Kentaro Sakaguchi and Takayuki Yamada. Toho released it in Japan on August 2, 2019, and Netflix made it available internationally on February 13, 2020. It was the last film scored by series composer Koichi Sugiyama before his death in 2021.

When Queen Mada of Gotha is abducted by monsters, her husband King Pankraz travels the world to rescue her, taking along their young son Luca. On the journey Luca befriends a girl named Bianca and obtains both a Golden Orb and a sabrecat cub he calls Purrcy. After Prince Harry of Coburg is also kidnapped, father and son give chase, but the sinister Bishop Ladja kills Pankraz and enslaves the two boys. Ten years later Luca and Harry escape. Reunited with a grown Purrcy and his father's loyal retainer Sancho, and accompanied by a friendly slime named Gootrude, Luca learns that Ladja seeks to free the demonic Grandmaster Nimzo and needs Mada's Zenithian bloodline to open a portal to the Demon World. Legend says a hero will seal it, and Pankraz believed that hero was Luca.

Luca's quest for the Zenithian Sword takes him to Mostroferrato, where he defeats a monster terrorizing the town and becomes engaged to the nobleman's daughter Nera, before realizing that Bianca is the one he loves. They marry and have a son, Alus, but Ladja turns the couple to stone. Eight years later Alus revives his father and proves to be the true Legendary Hero. In the final battle, as the portal is sealed, the world freezes and a computer virus reveals that Luca is in fact a player immersed in a virtual reality simulation of the game. Gootrude turns out to be an anti-virus program and helps Luca destroy the intruder and restore his adventure.

Before release, fans criticized the casting of famous actors instead of professional voice actors and the decision not to use Akira Toriyama's character designs. After release, the twist ending, which many viewers felt mocked players' attachment to the game, became the focus of fierce backlash among Japanese audiences.

documents.title: Hillbilly Elegy
documents.tagline: Inspired by a true story three generations in the making.
documents.overview: An urgent phone call pulls a Yale Law student back to his Ohio hometown, where he reflects on three generations of family history and his own future.
documents.plot:
Hillbilly Elegy is a 2020 American biographical drama directed by Ron Howard from a screenplay by Vanessa Taylor, based on JD Vance's 2016 memoir, who later became the 50th vice president of the United States. It stars Amy Adams as Vance's mother, Bev, and Glenn Close as his grandmother, Mamaw, with Gabriel Basso as the adult JD, Owen Asztalos as young JD, Haley Bennett as his sister Lindsay, Freida Pinto as his girlfriend Usha, and Bo Hopkins in his final film role as Papaw.

The story moves between two periods. In 2011, JD is a student at Yale Law School, working several jobs to pay his way and hoping to land a summer internship, when his sister calls to say that their mother has overdosed on heroin. He drives back to his hometown of Middletown, Ohio, to deal with the crisis, while trying to make it back in time for a crucial job interview.

Through flashbacks, the film recalls JD's childhood in the late 1990s, as the son of a family with roots in Appalachian Kentucky. His mother, Bev, struggles with addiction and violent mood swings, which bring a series of boyfriends, the loss of her job for stealing pills at work and terrifying outbursts. JD, falling into bad company as a teenager, finds stability when his tough, foul-mouthed grandmother Mamaw takes him in and pushes him to work hard at school and make something of his life. Encouraged by her, he goes on to join the Marine Corps and later college. In the present, JD struggles to find his mother a place in rehab and must decide how much of himself he can give to his family without sacrificing the future he has worked so hard to build.

The film explores poverty, addiction and family loyalty in working-class America, centering on the bond between three generations.

Given a limited theatrical release on November 11, 2020, before streaming on Netflix from November 24, Hillbilly Elegy was poorly received, with 24 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 38. Close received Academy Award, Golden Globe and SAG nominations, and the film was nominated for Best Makeup and Hairstyling, but it also earned three Golden Raspberry nominations.

documents.title: The Menu
documents.overview: A couple travels to a coastal island to eat at an exclusive restaurant where the chef has prepared a lavish menu, with some shocking surprises.
documents.plot:
The Menu is a 2022 American comedy horror film directed by Mark Mylod and written by Seth Reiss and Will Tracy. It stars Ralph Fiennes as celebrity chef Julian Slowik, Anya Taylor-Joy as Margot, Nicholas Hoult as Tyler and Hong Chau as the maître d' Elsa, with Janet McTeer, Judith Light, Reed Birney and John Leguizamo.

Wealthy foodie Tyler brings his date, Margot, to Hawthorn, an exclusive restaurant on a private island run by Slowik. The other guests include food critic Lillian Bloom and her editor, wealthy regulars Richard and Anne Liebrandt, a faded movie star and his assistant, three businessmen working for Slowik's investor, and Slowik's alcoholic mother. Elsa notes that Margot was not Tyler's original guest. As dinner progresses, the courses become increasingly disturbing: tortillas are laser-etched with each guest's secrets, a sous-chef kills himself, Richard has a finger cut off when he tries to leave, the investor is drowned, and Slowik lets himself be stabbed by an employee he once harassed. The chef announces that everyone, guests and staff alike, will die by the night's end, punished for exploiting or corrupting his art.

Because Margot was not invited, Slowik asks her to choose whether to die with the staff or the guests. She reveals that she is an escort, while Slowik exposes that Tyler knew of the plan and hired her only because Hawthorn does not seat solo diners. Humiliated after cooking a mediocre dish, Tyler hangs himself. Sent to fetch a barrel from the smokehouse, Margot kills Elsa in a struggle, calls for help on a radio and notices a photo of a young, happy Slowik flipping burgers. A rescuing "Coast Guard officer" turns out to be one of the cooks. Margot then complains that she is still hungry and orders a simple cheeseburger and fries, which Slowik joyfully prepares; after one bite she asks for it to go, and he lets her leave. For the s'mores-themed dessert, the guests are dressed as marshmallows and Slowik sets the restaurant ablaze, killing everyone inside. Escaping in the boat, Margot finishes her burger and wipes her mouth with the menu.

The Menu premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival on September 10, 2022, and Searchlight Pictures released it on November 18, 2022, in its widest release ever. It grossed $79.6 million worldwide and received positive reviews (88% on Rotten Tomatoes, 71 on Metacritic), and Fiennes and Taylor-Joy earned Golden Globe nominations.

documents.title: Castle Freak
documents.overview: After she’s permanently blinded in a tragic car accident, Rebecca receives some bizarre news: her long-lost mother has recently passed away, leaving her their family’s ancestral castle in rural Albania. Traveling to the estate with a group of friends, Rebecca hopes it will be an opportunity for her to reconnect with a past she never knew and a mother who seemingly left her behind. When mysterious events begin to occur and her friends begin to die, Rebecca must unravel the secrets of her family’s history before she too falls prey to the Castle Freak.
documents.plot:
Castle Freak is a 2020 American horror film directed by Stuart Gordon, based on the 1981 short story of the same name by H.P. Lovecraft.

The main themes of Castle Freak include:

1. **Isolation and confinement**: The story takes place in a remote location, where the protagonist, Dr. Marsten, is trapped with his niece, Lavinia, and her husband, William. This isolation creates an atmosphere of claustrophobia and heightens the sense of fear.
2. **The dangers of meddling with nature**: The film explores the idea that some things are better left alone, and that tampering with the natural world can have disastrous consequences. Dr. Marsten's experiments with the creature from Castle Freak ultimately lead to his downfall.
3. **The power of the unknown**: The movie taps into the fear of the unknown, as the characters are faced with a monstrous entity that defies explanation. This theme is classic Lovecraftian horror, where the protagonist's attempts to understand and control the creature only lead to more terror.
4. **Family dynamics and trauma**: The story also explores the complex relationships within the Marsten family, particularly between Dr. Marsten and his niece Lavinia. The film suggests that past traumas can have a lasting impact on individuals and families.

Overall, Castle Freak is a tense, atmospheric horror film that builds on the classic Lovecraftian themes of isolation, the unknown, and the dangers of meddling with nature.

documents.title: Homecoming: A Film by Beyoncé
documents.overview: This intimate, in-depth look at Beyoncé's celebrated 2018 Coachella performance reveals the emotional road from creative concept to cultural movement.
documents.plot:
Homecoming: A Film by Beyoncé is a 2019 American documentary concert film about Beyoncé's headlining performances at the 2018 Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival. Beyoncé wrote, executive-produced and directed the film, co-directing with Ed Burke, through her company Parkwood Entertainment. Running 137 minutes, it was released worldwide by Netflix on 17 April 2019, a day after preview screenings at several historically black colleges and universities, including Howard and Texas Southern, and was accompanied by the surprise release of Homecoming: The Live Album, with 36 live tracks and two new recordings.

Beyoncé had originally been booked to headline Coachella in April 2017 but postponed because of her pregnancy with twins. Playing the rescheduled dates on 14 and 21 April 2018, she became the first Black woman to headline the festival, performing a 26-song set before some 125,000 concertgoers in a show quickly nicknamed "Beychella". The film interweaves footage of both weekends, with their ensemble of dancers and guest appearances by her Destiny's Child bandmates Kelly Rowland and Michelle Williams, her husband Jay-Z and her sister Solange, with behind-the-scenes footage of rehearsals and glimpses of her life, including her pregnancy and her return to performing after giving birth. The show itself pays tribute to the culture of historically black colleges, with a full marching band, majorette dancers, a step show and strolling pledges echoing Black Greek life, and opens with her singing "Lift Every Voice and Sing", often called the Black national anthem. Drawing on Black feminism, it samples Black writers and thinkers such as Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie and Malcolm X. Her mother Tina Knowles recalled worrying that Coachella's largely white audience might not understand a show so steeped in Black culture, to which Beyoncé replied that her platform gave her a responsibility to do what was best for the world rather than what was most popular.

Homecoming received near-universal acclaim, and was widely described as one of the greatest concert films ever made; The Washington Post's Chris Richards called it exactly that, and The Atlantic's Spencer Kornhaber considered it a career-defining document. Nielsen reported that it drew more than a million US viewers on its first day. It won the Grammy Award for Best Music Film and Best Music Documentary at the IDA Documentary Awards, and received six Primetime Emmy nominations.

documents.title: Cinderella
documents.tagline: One shoe to rule them all.
documents.overview: Cinderella, an orphaned girl with an evil stepmother, has big dreams and with the help of her Fabulous Godmother, she perseveres to make them come true.
documents.plot:
Cinderella is a 2021 jukebox musical romantic comedy film written and directed by Kay Cannon, based on Charles Perrault's fairy tale. Singer Camila Cabello makes her acting debut in the title role, alongside Nicholas Galitzine as Prince Robert, Idina Menzel as Cinderella's stepmother, Billy Porter as her fairy godparent, Minnie Driver and Pierce Brosnan. The idea of reinterpreting the story came from James Corden, who produced the film through Fulwell 73. Filming began at Pinewood Studios in February 2020 but was suspended because of the COVID-19 pandemic, resuming in August 2020. It mixes pop and rock hits with several original songs.

Ella is an ambitious young woman whose dream is to open her own shop, Dresses by Ella. Prince Robert catches sight of her in passing, disguises himself as a commoner and finds her trying to sell one of her creations at the market, where after some playful banter he buys the dress for three times its price. He invites her to the royal ball, promising that she will meet guests from around the world who might buy her designs. On the night of the ball, Vivian, who has arranged for Ella to marry a vegetable merchant named Thomas, ruins her dress with ink so that only her own daughters, Malvolia and Narissa, can attend. Ella's fairy godparent, Fab G, comes to the rescue, dressing her in a gown of her own design and a pair of glass shoes and turning mice into footmen and a crate into a carriage. At the ball Ella meets Robert's sister, Princess Gwen, who is wearing the dress he bought, and a visiting queen, Tatiana, who offers to take her around the world as her personal dressmaker. When Robert proposes, Ella hesitates, fearing that marriage will mean giving up a dream that is finally within reach, while Robert, whose lifelong ambition has been to assume the throne, struggles with her answer. As midnight strikes and Ella flees, leaving a glass shoe behind, both of them must decide whether love and personal ambition can coexist.

Cinderella was released in select theaters and on Amazon Prime Video on September 3, 2021, to mixed reviews; it holds a 41% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes. According to Screen Engine, it was the most-watched streaming film of its opening weekend.

documents.title: NiNoKuni
documents.overview: Adapted from the video game series of the same name, NiNoKuni follows high school peers Yuu and Haru who must travel between two separate yet parallel worlds to help save their childhood friend, Kotona, whose life is in danger. In this magical quest complicated by love, the three teens will be tasked with making the ultimate choice.
documents.plot:
NiNoKuni is a 2019 Japanese animated fantasy film directed by Yoshiyuki Momose and based on the video game series developed by Level-5, whose founder Akihiro Hino wrote and executive produced the film. Produced by OLM and distributed by Warner Bros. Pictures, it features the voices of Kento Yamazaki as Yū, Mackenyu Arata as Haru and Mei Nagano as Kotona, with Maaya Sakamoto, Mamoru Miyano as the mage Gnauss, Kenjiro Tsuda as Galeroth and Masatō Ibu as King Astrum. Joe Hisaishi, who scored the earlier games, composed the music.

Yū, a bright high school student who uses a wheelchair, and his athletic best friend Haru are both close to their classmate Kotona. One evening, Kotona is attacked and stabbed by a mysterious hooded figure. As Haru tries to get her to a hospital, the two boys are suddenly transported to another world, the kingdom of Evermore, where Yū discovers that he can walk. In the royal castle they meet Princess Astrid, who looks exactly like Kotona and is suffering from a curse, which Yū manages to break.

The boys learn that the lives of people in their world are linked to those of their counterparts in Evermore, and that what happens to one affects the other. Back home, Kotona reveals that she has a serious illness, and the boys realize that saving her may require sacrificing Astrid, a choice that drives a wedge between them. As the kingdom is invaded by the army of the Black Banner, led by the sinister Galeroth, Yū and Haru are forced onto opposite sides before uncovering the true mastermind behind Astrid's curse and joining forces to save both worlds with the help of a legendary sword.

The film explores friendship, love and the connections between parallel lives, set in the world of the games centuries after the events of Ni no Kuni II: Revenant Kingdom.

NiNoKuni was released in Japan on August 23, 2019, debuting in seventh place at the box office. Netflix acquired the streaming rights and released it worldwide on January 16, 2020. The film's theme song, "MOIL", is performed by Keina Suda.

documents.title: Phineas and Ferb: The Movie: Candace Against the Universe
documents.original_title: Phineas and Ferb: The Movie: Candace Against the Universe
documents.tagline: Get ready for a mission that's out of this world!
documents.overview: Phineas and Ferb travel across the galaxy to rescue their older sister Candace, who has been abducted by aliens and taken to a utopia in a far-off planet, free of her pesky little brothers.
documents.plot:
Phineas and Ferb: Candace Against the Universe is a 2020 animated film produced by Disney Television Animation. The movie takes place after the events of the original series, with Candace Flynn still trying to prove that her brothers' inventions are real.

The story begins with Candace, now in her early twenties, feeling unfulfilled and restless. She's still obsessed with busting her brothers Phineas and Ferb, but she's starting to realize that her life is not turning out as planned. She decides to take a break from her family and embark on a solo journey to find herself.

Candace boards a spaceship and sets off into the galaxy, where she meets a group of aliens who are also searching for their own sense of purpose. The aliens, led by a wise and witty leader named Dr. Doofenshmirtz Jr., take Candace under their wing and teach her about the importance of following your dreams.

As Candace navigates this new world, she begins to see her life with Phineas and Ferb in a different light. She realizes that her brothers' inventions were not just random creations, but rather a way for them to express themselves and bring joy to others. Candace starts to understand that her own dreams and passions are what truly make her happy.

Meanwhile, back on Earth, Phineas and Ferb are dealing with their own set of problems. They're trying to save the city from an alien invasion, which is being led by none other than Dr. Doofenshmirtz Jr.'s father, the infamous Dr. Heinz Doofenshmirtz.

As Candace continues her journey through space, she begins to uncover a sinister plot by Dr. Doofenshmirtz Sr. to take over the universe. The aliens, who are actually the sons and daughters of various villains from the show, join forces with Candace to stop their father's evil plans.

In the end, Candace and her new friends successfully defeat Dr. Doofenshmirtz Sr. and save the universe. Along the way, Candace learns valuable lessons about following her dreams and finding her true purpose in life.

The movie ends with Candace returning home to Phineas and Ferb, where she's welcomed back with open arms. She realizes that she doesn't have to be defined by her failures, but rather by her own strengths and passions. The film concludes with a heartwarming moment of Candace joining her brothers in one of their famous inventions, finally finding the happiness and fulfillment she's been searching for.

Overall, Phineas and Ferb: Candace Against the Universe is a fun and heartwarming movie that explores themes of identity, purpose, and the importance of following your dreams.

documents.title: Lamp Life
documents.overview: Bo Peep explains what happened to herself and her sheep between the events of Toy Story 2 and Toy Story 4.
documents.plot:
Lamp Life is a 2020 American computer-animated short film produced by Pixar Animation Studios for the streaming service Disney+. Written and directed by Valerie LaPointe, head of story on Toy Story 4, in her directorial debut, and produced by Mark Sondheimer, it is a spin-off of that feature, running about seven minutes. Annie Potts reprises her role as the porcelain shepherdess Bo Peep, with Ally Maki as Giggle McDimples and Emily Davis as Bo's three sheep, while Woody is voiced by Jim Hanks, Tom Hanks's younger brother. The score was composed by Jake Monaco.

The short fills in what happened to Bo Peep between Toy Story 2 and Toy Story 4. After reuniting with Woody, Bo, joined by her friend Giggle, tells him in a series of flashbacks how she became a lost toy. Once part of a nursery lamp in the bedroom of Andy's younger sister Molly, Bo and her sheep were given away when Molly outgrew them. In her next home, a child's bedroom, she is bored because the mother will not let the children play with the lamp, and as the years pass she moves through a montage of temporary homes, including a white elephant party where teenagers treat her roughly, at one point setting her on fire. She eventually lands in the Second Chance Antiques store, where she is safe but bored once again, and where Gabby Gabby and her ventriloquist dummies make a brief appearance. Wanting adventure and the chance to be played with, Bo devises a plan with Giggle, outwits the shop's surprisingly elaborate security system and breaks out with her sheep, beginning a free life as a lost toy.

LaPointe built the short partly from flashback material cut from Toy Story 4, which had been sad in tone, reworking the gags into comedy as Bo looks back on her hard life with humor. She received guidance from Pete Docter and producer Jonas Rivera, and kept the lamp at the center of the frame while cutting through time, seasons and settings. Lamp Life premiered on Disney+ on 31 January 2020. Reviewers found it charming and packed with quick gags and Pixar Easter eggs, though Laughing Place considered it a tame series of vignettes that added little to the character.

documents.title: Sputnik
documents.tagline: The only survivor did not come back alone
documents.overview: At the height of the Cold War, a Soviet spacecraft crash lands after a mission gone awry, leaving the commander as its only survivor. After a renowned Russian psychologist is brought in to evaluate the commander’s mental state, it becomes clear that something dangerous may have come back to Earth with him…
documents.plot:
Sputnik (Russian: Спутник) is a 2020 Russian science fiction horror film directed by Egor Abramenko in his feature debut. Oksana Akinshina stars as Tatyana Klimova, a young doctor recruited by the Soviet military to examine a cosmonaut who has returned from a space accident with a dangerous organism living inside him, with Pyotr Fyodorov as the cosmonaut, Konstantin Veshnyakov, and Fyodor Bondarchuk as Colonel Semiradov. It was due to premiere at the Tribeca Film Festival in April 2020, but the festival was postponed due to the COVID-19 pandemic, and the film was released on video on demand in Russia that month and internationally by IFC Midnight in August.

In 1983, two Soviet cosmonauts hear something moving outside their spacecraft, which then crashes in Kazakhstan. The sole survivor, Veshnyakov, is taken to a secret military research facility run by Semiradov, but he remembers nothing of the crash. When the facility's scientist, Yan Rigel, fails to cure his amnesia, Semiradov recruits Klimova, a controversial psychiatrist facing disciplinary action for her unorthodox methods. Klimova concludes that Veshnyakov is suffering from post-traumatic stress, but Semiradov then shows her the facility's secret: each night, an alien creature emerges from the cosmonaut's mouth while he sleeps.

The creature is symbiotically bonded to Veshnyakov, keeping him alive, and any attempt to separate them would kill both. Klimova agrees to find a way to separate them permanently, to Rigel's resentment. To study how the cosmonaut's hormones respond to stress, she provokes him with accusations about abandoning his son and causing his colleague's death, then apologizes, learning that he had only discovered he had a son shortly before his mission. Spending time with the creature at night, Klimova discovers its true nature and how it feeds, and uncovers Semiradov's real intentions: the military hopes to use the organism as a weapon, and has been feeding it prisoners. As she becomes closer to Veshnyakov, Klimova must decide how far she will go to protect him and stop the creature from being exploited, even at a terrible cost.

Sputnik received generally positive reviews, with critics praising its atmosphere, its Cold War setting, Akinshina's commanding performance and its creature design, comparing it favorably to Alien and other classic science-fiction horror films.

documents.title: Shazam! Fury of the Gods
documents.overview: Billy Batson and his foster siblings, who transform into superheroes by saying "Shazam!", are forced to get back into action and fight the Daughters of Atlas, who they must stop from using a weapon that could destroy the world.
documents.plot:
Shazam! Fury of the Gods is a 2023 American superhero film based on the DC Comics character Shazam. Produced by New Line Cinema, DC Films and the Safran Company and distributed by Warner Bros. Pictures, it is the sequel to Shazam! (2019) and the twelfth instalment of the DC Extended Universe. David F. Sandberg returned as director, working from a script by Henry Gayden and Chris Morgan. Zachary Levi and Asher Angel again share the role of Billy Batson, with Jack Dylan Grazer, Adam Brody and Ross Butler among the returning foster family, Rachel Zegler as Anthea, and Helen Mirren and Lucy Liu as the villainous sisters Hespera and Kalypso.

Four years after the defeat of Thaddeus Sivana, Hespera and Kalypso, daughters of the Titan Atlas, raid a museum in Athens to steal the broken staff of the Wizard and force him to restore its power. In Philadelphia, Billy and his superpowered siblings, nicknamed the Shazamily, are drifting apart as they grow older, and the public mocks them as the Philly Fiascos after a rescue on a collapsing bridge causes considerable damage. Billy also fears that he will lose his place in the Vasquez home when he turns eighteen.

Warned in a dream by the Wizard, the family learn about the Daughters of Atlas and discover that Anne, a new girl at school whom Freddy has fallen for, is in fact Anthea, the youngest of the sisters. The goddesses intend to reclaim the magic they believe was stolen from them, and they seal Philadelphia under an enormous dome. Using a golden apple from the Tree of Life, Kalypso plans to unleash a horde of mythological monsters, including a dragon, on the human world. The siblings must overcome their differences and work together, as Billy learns that being a hero means accepting that he is truly part of a family, culminating in a sacrifice of his own.

The film blends superhero action with family comedy, keeping the lighthearted tone of the first instalment while expanding its mythology from Greek legend.

Fury of the Gods received mixed reviews, with praise for its cast and humour but criticism of its plot and villains, and it underperformed at the box office, grossing far less than its predecessor worldwide.

documents.title: Irresistible
documents.overview: A Democratic political consultant helps a retired Marine colonel run for mayor in a small, conservative Wisconsin town.
documents.plot:
Irresistible is a satirical comedy film that delves into the darker aspects of American politics and society. The movie follows a Democratic campaign manager, Gary Clements, who is sent to a small town in Pennsylvania to help a local candidate win an election. However, things take a turn when he discovers that the town's residents are being manipulated by a wealthy corporate executive, Jack Morris, who is using his influence to sway the outcome of the election.

Through this narrative, the film critiques the corrupting influence of money in politics and the ways in which special interests can manipulate public opinion. The movie also explores themes of class struggle, as Gary's character represents the values of the working class, while Jack's character embodies the power and privilege of the wealthy elite.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Irresistible is not just a comedy about politics, but also a commentary on the erosion of civic engagement and the decline of community. The film highlights how politicians and corporate interests often prioritize their own interests over those of the people they claim to represent.

Ultimately, the movie presents a bleak vision of American politics, where money and power are seen as the primary drivers of decision-making, rather than the needs and values of the citizens being represented.

documents.title: Death of Me
documents.overview: A couple on holiday on a remote South Pacific island awaken one morning with a hang over and no recollection of what transpired. When playing back a video of the previous night, they see they participated in a local ritual that somehow ends with him murdering her.
documents.plot:
Death of Me is an American horror film of 2020, written by Ari Margolis, James Morley III and David Tish and directed by Darren Lynn Bousman. It stars Maggie Q and Luke Hemsworth as Christine and Neil, an American couple trapped on a remote Thai island, with Alex Essoe as the hotel owner Samantha, Kat Ingkarat as the waitress Madee and Kelly B. Jones as the tattoo artist Kanda.

Christine and Neil wake in a wrecked hotel room, caked in dirt and grass, with no memory of the night before. Their passports are missing, so they miss their ferry and return to Samantha's hotel. Footage on Neil's phone shows them drinking at a bar, where Madee gave Christine a necklace, and then Neil, apparently drugged, strangling Christine and burying her. Neil insists none of it happened, but Christine finds bruises on her neck and coughs up soil. A local doctor dismisses their story, and the islanders prepare for a festival adorned with images of Christine.

Christine suffers increasingly gruesome visions, pulling a snake from her throat and seeing women whose eyes and mouths are sewn shut. Kanda tells her the necklace is a talisman with spiritual power, and Madee returns Neil's passport but not hers. While waiting for a boat, Neil falls into a trance and kills himself in front of her. The police do not believe her, and the doctor announces that she is pregnant, showing a monstrous ultrasound. Kanda finally explains that Christine was meant to be buried by her husband as a sacrifice: the islanders bury pregnant women to keep the island safe from storms, and she lingers in a spiritual limbo. Discovering that Samantha is complicit after being cured of cancer, Christine shoots her, but she is captured, and Madee begins sewing her eye shut before she breaks free and escapes by boat as a storm hits. The storm kills the islanders and Christine, but a rescuer lays the necklace beside her body, and its magic brings her back to life.

Saban Films released the film on digital and on demand on 2 October 2020; its theatrical run was limited to overseas markets because of the COVID-19 pandemic. Critics praised Maggie Q's committed performance but found it short on scares, and it scored 33% on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: The Pilgrim's Progress
documents.overview: An epic journey, faithfully adapted to modern-day. Christian faces distractions, challenges, and perils at every turn of the way. But ends victorious, with helpful guides, as he stays on the narrow path to the distant Celestial City.
documents.plot:
The Pilgrim's Progress is a 2019 American computer-animated Christian fantasy adventure written and directed by Robert Fernandez. It is based on John Bunyan's 1678 allegory of the same name. David Thorpe voices Christian, John Rhys-Davies voices Evangelist and Kristyn Getty voices the Interpreter. Jonathan Keeble, Justin Butcher, Chris Pavlo and Andrew Wyncott voice Faithful, Hopeful, Worldly Wiseman and the villain Apollyon.

The story begins in Not-Cursed, a city of laborers watched over by Apollyon, master of corruption. When a worker named Faithful disappears, leaving strange drawings behind, his colleague Christian learns he has set out for the Celestial City beyond the borders. After a nightmare, Christian reads a book from Faithful's office and becomes convinced the city will be destroyed. His wife dismisses the book as fiction and refuses to leave, so he sets out alone.

On the way, Evangelist urges him to keep to the path. His eager companion Pliable gives up after they fall into the Swamp of Despondency, and a man named Help pulls Christian out. The smooth-talking Worldly Wiseman leads him off course to the village of Morality, where he despairs under the Law of Moses until Evangelist rescues him. A Gatekeeper saves him from bats, and the Interpreter teaches him that those who follow the light will be protected if they persevere. On the Path of Patience, his burden falls away. Heralds of the King give him new clothes, and the daughters of Vigilant give him armor and a sword, with which he defeats Apollyon. Reunited with Faithful, he goes on to Vanity Fair, where Faithful is executed and Christian is imprisoned. A sympathetic jailer, Hopeful, helps him escape. The two are captured by a giant but realize their hope makes them unbreakable. They escape and are guided by a Shepherd. Apollyon, disguised as an old man, captures them, but a herald rescues them. At the sea before the Celestial City, Christian enters the water, Apollyon is cast into the depths, and the Shepherd welcomes him into the city. In an epilogue, his wife finds a letter showing he is alive, as Apollyon circles her home as a dragon, setting up a continuation.

Fathom Events released the film in American cinemas on April 18, 2019, around Easter, and it grossed about $3.2 million worldwide. Reviews were mixed. The Guardian criticized its stiff animation and lack of humor, while WORLD Magazine and Variety were more positive, and Radio Times called the animation basic but effective.

documents.title: Fever Dream
documents.overview: A woman named Amanda lies stricken, far from home. A young boy named David questions her, trying to make her remember. She's not his mother, he's not her son. As her time is running out, he helps her unravel a powerful, haunting story of obsessive jealousy, an invisible danger, and the power of a mother's love for her child.
documents.plot:
Fever Dream (Spanish: Distancia de rescate, literally "Rescue Distance") is a 2021 psychological thriller directed by the Peruvian filmmaker Claudia Llosa from a screenplay she co-wrote with the Argentine writer Samanta Schweblin, adapting Schweblin's 2014 novel of the same name. A Netflix release of a Gran Via and Paradise Falls production in collaboration with Fábula and Wanda Films it was shot in Chile in early 2019, with cinematography by Oscar Faura and a string-led score by Natalie Holt. The cast is led by María Valverde, Dolores Fonzi, Germán Palacios, Guillermo Pfening and Emilio Vodanovich.

Amanda (Valverde) arrives at an idyllic cottage in a quiet rural town in Argentina for a summer holiday with her even-tempered young daughter Nina (Guillermina Sorribes Liotta), while her husband Marco (Pfening) stays behind, preoccupied with work. Her vibrant neighbour Carola (Fonzi) appears bearing pails of drinking water, warning her not to trust what comes out of the tap, the first hint that something is unsound about the area. The two women quickly become close friends, but the timeline splinters into Carola's past, when she lived in the house Amanda now occupies and she and her husband Omar (Palacios) planned to breed show horses until a stallion's mysterious death plunged them into debt. At the same time their young son David (Marcelo Michinaux) fell suddenly and gravely ill, and a local healer (Cristina Banegas) performed a "spiritual migration", transferring part of his spirit into another body. David survived, but Carola insists that the surly, near-feral boy he has become (Vodanovich) is no longer her son. Amanda soon suspects that something is eerily wrong and fears that part of Nina's spirit may also go missing, as the story raises the question of whether toxins sprayed on the surrounding crops are to blame. The film unfolds through a conversation between Amanda and David that is heard rather than seen.

Fever Dream premiered in competition at the San Sebastián International Film Festival on 20 September 2021, opened in select US cinemas on 6 October and was released on Netflix on 13 October 2021. It holds a 72% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 75. The Guardian called it bonkers but very beautiful, a future cult classic, while Variety's critic praised its atmosphere, photography and score but found the story sliding into near-incoherence.

documents.title: Super Monsters Furever Friends
documents.overview: On the first night of spring, the Super Monsters gather for food, fun and games in the park -- and get to meet their adorable new pets!
documents.plot:
Super Monsters Furever Friends is an animated film that revolves around the adventures of a group of monster friends who learn valuable lessons about friendship, love, and acceptance. The movie primarily focuses on the theme of family and the importance of embracing one's uniqueness.

The story centers around the main character, Leif, who struggles to find his place among his peers due to his differences. However, with the help of his monster friends, he learns to accept himself and finds a sense of belonging. The film showcases how these monsters come together to form an unbreakable bond, demonstrating that true friendship can conquer even the most daunting challenges.

The movie also explores the theme of love and acceptance, particularly in the context of Leif's journey to find his forever home with his monster family. Through his experiences, the film conveys a powerful message about the importance of embracing diversity and promoting inclusivity.

Overall, Super Monsters Furever Friends is a heartwarming tale that celebrates the beauty of individuality and the power of friendship in overcoming adversity.

documents.title: Causeway
documents.overview: A US soldier suffers a traumatic brain injury while fighting in Afghanistan and struggles to adjust to life back home in New Orleans. When she meets local mechanic James, the pair begin to forge an unexpected bond.
documents.plot:
Causeway is a 2022 American drama film directed by Mark Duplass and written by Duplass and Tom McGowan. The movie stars Benedict Cumberbatch, Carey Mulligan, and Ann Dowd.

The story revolves around Thomas Merritt (Benedict Cumberbatch), an Iraq War veteran who suffers from what he believes is a traumatic brain injury. He lives in Memphis, Tennessee, with his wife, Susan (Carey Mulligan), a nurse at the local hospital where he works. The couple's relationship has become strained due to Thomas's increasing irritability and lack of motivation.

Thomas's life takes an unexpected turn when he meets Lynsey (Ann Dowd), a 75-year-old widow who is also a patient in his physical therapy sessions. Lynsey, who lost her husband in the war, becomes a source of inspiration for Thomas, and their conversations lead to a deeper exploration of his feelings about the war and its impact on him.

As Thomas's relationship with Lynsey deepens, he begins to confront the emotional scars of his past. He starts to question his marriage and his own identity, leading to a crisis that forces him to reevaluate his life choices. Through his interactions with Lynsey, Thomas gains a new perspective on his experiences in Iraq and the toll it has taken on his mental health.

Meanwhile, Susan is struggling to cope with her husband's increasing detachment from reality. She feels abandoned and unsure of how to support Thomas as he navigates his emotional turmoil. The couple's relationship reaches a breaking point, and they are forced to confront the harsh realities of their marriage.

Throughout the film, Duplass masterfully weaves together themes of trauma, identity, and relationships. The cinematography is stunning, capturing the beauty and grittiness of Memphis and its people. The performances from Cumberbatch, Mulligan, and Dowd are outstanding, bringing depth and nuance to their characters.

The title "Causeway" refers to a bridge that spans the Mississippi River in Memphis. It serves as a metaphor for Thomas's journey, connecting him to his past while also allowing him to move forward. The film's ending is both poignant and hopeful, suggesting that Thomas has finally found a way to heal and rebuild his life.

Overall, Causeway is a powerful and moving drama that explores the complexities of trauma, relationships, and identity. With its outstanding performances, stunning cinematography, and thoughtful direction, it is a must-see for fans of character-driven dramas.

documents.title: SAS: Red Notice
documents.overview: An off-duty SAS soldier, Tom Buckingham, must thwart a terror attack on a train running through the Channel Tunnel. As the action escalates on the train, events transpire in the corridors of power that may make the difference as to whether Buckingham and the civilian passengers make it out of the tunnel alive.
documents.plot:
SAS: Red Notice is a 2021 action-thriller film directed by Rawson Marshall Thurber and starring Dwayne Johnson, Ryan Reynolds, and Gal Gadot. The movie follows the story of an FBI agent, John Hartley (Johnson), who teams up with an art thief, Nolan Booth (Reynolds), to catch a notorious art forger, Elizabeth "The Cat" Lind (Gadot).

The film begins with Nolan Booth, a charming and skilled art thief, being pursued by the FBI. He is eventually caught and sentenced to prison, but manages to escape after serving only a few months. Meanwhile, John Hartley, an FBI agent specializing in art crimes, is tasked with catching Booth.

Hartley and Booth cross paths when they both receive a message from Elizabeth Lind, who has stolen a priceless artifact called the "Red Notice." The Red Notice is a valuable painting that holds significant historical and cultural value. Both Hartley and Booth are determined to catch Lind and claim the reward money for themselves.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Lind is not just any ordinary art thief. She is highly intelligent, resourceful, and has a personal vendetta against both Hartley and Booth. The three engage in a cat-and-mouse game, with each trying to outsmart the other.

Throughout the film, the characters' backstories are revealed through flashbacks. We learn that Lind was once a talented artist who became disillusioned with the art world's superficiality. She turned to theft as a way to expose the hypocrisy and corruption within the art community.

As the stakes rise, Hartley and Booth begin to form an unlikely alliance. They realize that they have more in common than they initially thought, and that their skills complement each other perfectly. Together, they devise a plan to catch Lind and retrieve the Red Notice.

The film's climax features an intense action sequence as Hartley, Booth, and Lind engage in a high-stakes game of cat and mouse. The three characters use their wits, charm, and cunning to outmaneuver each other, leading to a thrilling conclusion.

In the end, Hartley and Booth succeed in catching Lind, but not before she reveals that she has been playing them all along. She had planned her escape from prison and was using both men to get to the Red Notice. The film ends with Hartley and Booth walking away from each other, having formed an unlikely friendship.

Overall, SAS: Red Notice is a fast-paced, action-packed thriller that explores themes of loyalty, trust, and redemption. The film features impressive performances from its lead actors, and the chemistry between Johnson, Reynolds, and Gadot is undeniable.

documents.title: On a Magical Night
documents.overview: After 20 years of marriage, Maria decides to leave her husband. She moves into room 212 at the hotel across the street, with a bird’s-eye view of her apartment, her husband and the life she shared with him. While she wonders if she made the right decision, many of the people in her life offer their opinions on the matter. They intend to let her know, whether she likes it or not, on what proves to be a life-changing evening.
documents.plot:
On a Magical Night (French: Chambre 212, literally "Room 212") is a 2019 French fantasy comedy-drama written and directed by Christophe Honoré, starring Chiara Mastroianni, Vincent Lacoste, Camille Cottin and Benjamin Biolay, with Carole Bouquet. Developed under the working title Musique de chambre, the screenplay was written by Honoré for Mastroianni, whom he imagined as "a Cary Grant-type character". It was his first film shot in a studio. The title refers to Article 212 of the French Civil Code, which states that spouses owe each other respect, fidelity, help and assistance.

Maria Mortemart (Mastroianni), a university lecturer in the history of law, has been married to Richard Warrimer (Biolay) for twenty years. When Richard stumbles on messages on her phone revealing her affair with one of her students, Asdrubal the couple quarrel, and Maria walks out of their Paris apartment to spend the night in Room 212 of the hotel across the street. She gives herself the night to think. Over its course she is visited by figures from her own past and Richard's: Richard himself at twenty (Lacoste), as he was when she decided to marry him; her mother, who kept a precise tally of her lovers; and Irène Haffner (Cottin), Richard's piano teacher and first love, who agreed to step aside so that he could marry Maria. Irène wonders whether she was wrong, whether Richard would have been happier with her and whether she would have given him the children Maria never wanted, and she crosses the street to try to convince him, in vain. Meanwhile Maria is confronted by her "will", embodied by a man vaguely resembling Charles Aznavour, and by a crowd of her former lovers. Maria and Irène then journey to the Bay of the Somme, where Irène settled after Richard's wedding, and meet her serene, regret-free sixty-year-old self (Bouquet). In the morning Maria and Richard meet in the street; she must go and teach, but promises to come home that evening.

The film premiered in the Un Certain Regard section of the 2019 Cannes Film Festival, where Mastroianni won the award for Best Performance. Released in France on 9 October 2019 and by Strand Releasing in US virtual cinemas in May 2020, it grossed about 3 million dollars. Reviews were mixed: The Hollywood Reporter's Stephen Dalton found it breezy and bright, with the stylised feel of a stage play, while Variety's Owen Gleiberman felt it dragged and had holes in its fantasy logic.

documents.title: Cold Blood
documents.overview: A legendary but retired hit man lives in peace and isolation in the barren North American wilderness. When he rescues a woman from a snowmobiling accident, he soon discovers that she's harboring a secret that forces him to return to his lethal ways.
documents.plot:
Cold Blood, also released as Cold Blood Legacy, is a 2019 English-language action thriller written and directed by the French filmmaker Frédéric Petitjean. Jean Reno stars as a retired contract killer living in seclusion, with Sarah Lind as the young woman who enters his life, and Joe Anderson, David Gyasi, Ihor Ciszkewycz and Samantha Bond in supporting roles. Set in a snowbound wilderness, the film was released on 15 May 2019.

Henry, a professional assassin, has withdrawn to a remote cabin in the snowbound forests near the Canadian border, where he lives in silence and solitude, fishing on the frozen lake. One day he comes across a crashed snowmobile and a badly injured young woman, who tells him her name is Melody. He drives off a pack of wolves that close in on her, carries her back to the cabin and treats her injuries with what little he has, pulling out splinters and shards of wood embedded in her body.

As she recovers, Henry grows wary. She has no identification and no phone, and the circumstances of the crash do not add up, so he examines the scene and tells her she must leave as soon as she can. One day, seeing him sitting outside with his back to her, apparently fishing, she assembles a pistol hidden in her pack and shoots him in the head, only to discover that she has hit a straw dummy. Henry overpowers and questions her.

She admits that her real name is Charlie and that she came to kill him in revenge for his murder of her father, a wealthy man who largely ignored her but whose memory she still wanted to honour. Henry reveals that he already knew who she was, and that the contract he accepted had also required him to kill her. He releases her into the wilderness, but she comes back to the cabin. When one of her father's former bodyguards arrives to rescue her, Henry kills him in a gunfight.

Weary of his life as a killer, Henry calls the police on himself the next morning. Charlie strikes him, and when he raises his gun, he shoots a wolf behind her and then appears to aim at her before dropping the cartridge. The arriving officers shoot him dead. Charlie later returns to the cabin and finds that he has left her his copy of The Art of War and the phone number of the person who ordered her death.

Critics were dismissive, with Variety calling it instantly forgettable despite its striking snowy setting.

documents.title: Let Him Go
documents.overview: Following the loss of their son, a retired sheriff and his wife leave their Montana ranch to rescue their young grandson from the clutches of a dangerous family living off the grid in the Dakotas.
documents.plot:
Let Him Go is a 2020 American Western drama film directed by Thomas Bezucha, based on the 2009 novel of the same name by Larry Watson.

The movie follows George Blackwell (played by Kevin Costner) and his wife Margaret (played by Diane Lane), who live in rural Montana. When their daughter dies, they are left alone to care for each other. However, when Margaret falls ill, George is forced to take her on a road trip to visit her estranged sister in Utah.

During the journey, they encounter a mysterious and sinister figure named Lorne Malvo (played by Will Oldham), who seems to be manipulating events from behind the scenes. As they travel through the American West, George becomes increasingly obsessed with finding out what happened to his daughter and confronting the dark forces that have been at work in their lives.

The main themes of Let Him Go include:

1. **Grief and Loss**: The movie explores the devastating effects of loss on a family, particularly when it comes to the death of a child. George's grief is palpable, and his journey is driven by a desire to understand what happened to his daughter.
2. **The American West as a Character**: The film portrays the vast, isolated landscapes of Montana and Utah as a character in its own right, with the natural world serving as a backdrop for the characters' emotional struggles.
3. **Mortality and the Human Condition**: As George and Margaret face their own mortality, they are forced to confront the meaninglessness and uncertainty of life. The film raises questions about the human condition, the nature of existence, and what lies beyond death.
4. **The Corrupting Influence of Power**: Lorne Malvo is a master manipulator who uses his charm and intelligence to exploit those around him. His presence serves as a catalyst for George's transformation, highlighting the dangers of unchecked power and the corrupting influence it can have on individuals.

Overall, Let Him Go is a thought-provoking and emotionally charged film that explores the complexities of human relationships, the fragility of life, and the darkness that lurks beneath the surface of even the most idyllic communities.

documents.title: Pacto de Fuga
documents.tagline: Based on the most daring prison escape of all time.
documents.overview: During the last years of Pinochet's military regime,  a group of militants from the "Manuel Rodríguez Patriotic Front" plan a prison break of political prisoners, through a tunnel that will take them 18 months to dig.
documents.plot:
Jailbreak Pact, released in Chile as Pacto de fuga, is a 2020 Chilean prison drama and thriller directed by David Albala in his feature debut, from a screenplay he co-wrote with Cecilia Ruz, Loreto Caro-Valdés and Susana Quiroz-Saavedra. It stars Benjamín Vicuña as León Vargas and Roberto Farías as Rafael Jiménez, with Francisca Gavilán, Amparo Noguera, Víctor Montero, Diego Ruiz, Mateo Iribarren and Willy Semler. The film is inspired by "Operation Success", the escape of 49 inmates from the Santiago Public Jail on January 30, 1990, among them members of the Manuel Rodríguez Patriotic Front (FPMR) serving sentences for armed actions against the military dictatorship.

In the final years of Augusto Pinochet's regime, new political prisoners arrive at the Santiago jail. Vargas and Jiménez try to secure neighboring cells so they can communicate, but Vargas arrives late to the assignment, creating friction over the plans they brought with them. Meanwhile the ad hoc prosecutor Andrade and the warden receive Fabiola Pizarro, a defense lawyer from the group CODEPU who has come to check on the prisoners' conditions. The conspirators calculate that a tunnel would require removing some 50 tons of earth, so they open a hole in a cell ceiling to hide the soil, cover it with a fake section of wall painted to match, and devise secret signals to coordinate the work while evading guards and ordinary prisoners. Outside, Jiménez's former wife, Paulina Baeza, organizes logistical support from FPMR and Communist Party contacts for the day of the escape.

Over more than a year, 24 prisoners dig a tunnel over 80 meters long, using little more than a screwdriver, and hide 55 tons of earth inside the prison, while family visits expose the strain between revolutionary commitment and broken relationships, and the military justice system and the regime's security agencies wield power over the prison. Undetected to the end, the plan frees 49 inmates in one of the most astonishing jailbreaks in Chilean history.

Shot in former prisons in La Serena and Buin, the film was advised by Raúl Blanchet, one of the real escapees, who died during post-production. Its October 2019 release was postponed by Chile's social unrest, and it opened on January 23, 2020. It was shortlisted for Chile's Academy Award submission. The Guardian praised the lead performances but found the dialogue forced, while still calling it an entertaining debut.

documents.title: And Then We Danced
documents.overview: Merab has been training since a young age at the National Georgian Ensemble with his dance partner Mary. His world is suddenly turned upside down when the charismatic and carefree Irakli arrives and becomes both his strongest rival and desire. In this conservative setting Merab finds himself having to break free and risk it all.
documents.plot:
And Then We Danced is a poignant and powerful film that delves into the complexities of love, identity, and societal expectations in a small Estonian town. The movie tells the story of two young men, Kalju and Meri, who are forced to confront their feelings for each other when they're paired together as dance partners at the annual national ballet competition.

At its core, And Then We Danced is a film about the struggle for self-expression and acceptance in a society that often prioritizes conformity over individuality. The movie shines a light on the restrictive nature of traditional Estonian culture, where same-sex relationships are stigmatized and same-gender couples are shunned by their families and communities.

Through Kalju's character, the film explores the pain and vulnerability of being forced to hide one's true self in order to fit into societal norms. The movie also delves into the complexities of love and desire, as Kalju and Meri navigate their feelings for each other amidst the pressures of competition and expectation.

The film is a powerful exploration of the human need for connection and acceptance, and it raises important questions about the nature of identity, community, and what it means to be true to oneself. The movie's portrayal of the Estonian ballet world is also noteworthy, offering a nuanced critique of the cultural institution that often prioritizes discipline over passion and creativity.

Overall, And Then We Danced is a moving and thought-provoking film that challenges its audience to confront their own biases and assumptions about identity, love, and acceptance.

documents.title: Nightmare Alley
documents.overview: An ambitious carnival man with a talent for manipulating people with a few well-chosen words hooks up with a female psychologist who is even more dangerous than he is.
documents.plot:
Nightmare Alley is a 2021 neo-noir psychological thriller co-written and directed by Guillermo del Toro, based on William Lindsay Gresham's 1946 novel, which had previously been filmed in 1947. It stars Bradley Cooper as Stanton Carlisle, an ambitious drifter, with Cate Blanchett, Toni Collette, Willem Dafoe, Richard Jenkins, Rooney Mara, Ron Perlman, Mary Steenburgen and David Strathairn. Del Toro produced the film with J. Miles Dale and Cooper, with cinematography by Dan Laustsen and music by Nathan Johnson.

In 1939, Stan Carlisle hides the body of his father under the floor of a run-down house and burns it down before joining a traveling carnival. There he learns how the carnival's geek, a degraded man who eats live chickens in a sideshow pit, is recruited and controlled through alcohol and opium. Stan begins working with the clairvoyant Madame Zeena and her alcoholic husband Pete, who teach him the coded language and cold reading techniques of their mentalist act, warning him never to claim to speak with the dead. After Pete dies, Stan leaves the carnival with Molly, a young performer.

Two years later, Stan and Molly run a successful mentalist act for the wealthy elite of Buffalo, though their relationship is deteriorating. During a performance, a psychiatrist, Dr. Lilith Ritter, tries to expose Stan, but he outwits her. The two form a dangerous alliance: Ritter secretly gives Stan confidential information about her wealthy patients, which he uses to convince them that he can communicate with their dead loved ones. Ignoring Molly's objections and Zeena's warnings, Stan sets his sights on Ezra Grindle, a powerful and ruthless industrialist, and his ambition draws him into a con that spirals out of his control.

The film is a dark study of ambition, deception and self-destruction, with its ending echoing the carnival world where Stan's story began.

Production in Toronto was interrupted by the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020. Released by Searchlight Pictures on December 17, 2021, the film grossed 39.6 million dollars against a 60 million dollar budget. It received generally positive reviews, with 80 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 70, and earned four Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture.

documents.title: The Half of It
documents.tagline: A different kind of love story.
documents.overview: Shy, straight-A student Ellie is hired by sweet but inarticulate jock Paul, who needs help wooing the most popular girl in school. But their new and unlikely friendship gets tricky when Ellie discovers she has feelings for the same girl.
documents.plot:
The Half of It is a 2020 American romantic comedy-drama film that explores the complexities of identity, social hierarchy, and first love in a high school setting. At its core, the movie delves into the theme of self-discovery, particularly for its protagonist, Ellie, who navigates her own identity and sense of belonging.

The film also touches on the issue of social class and how it can shape one's experiences and relationships. The contrast between Ellie's working-class background and her more affluent peers serves as a backdrop for exploring themes of privilege, entitlement, and the pressure to conform to societal expectations.

Furthermore, The Half of It examines the complexities of female friendships and the ways in which women support and hurt each other. Ellie's relationships with her friends, particularly Pauline, are multifaceted and nuanced, reflecting the messy realities of female friendship in high school.

The movie also explores the theme of first love and the uncertainty that comes with it. Ellie's romance with Paul is tender and awkward, mirroring the ups and downs of young love. Through their relationship, the film captures the vulnerability and excitement of falling in love for the first time.

Ultimately, The Half of It is a thoughtful and engaging exploration of the challenges and triumphs of adolescence, identity, and relationships.

documents.title: My Little Pony: A New Generation
documents.original_title: My Little Pony: A New Generation
documents.overview: Equestria's divided. But a bright-eyed hero believes Earth Ponies, Pegasi and Unicorns should be pals — and, hoof to heart, she’s determined to prove it.
documents.plot:
My Little Pony: A New Generation is a 2021 computer-animated adventure comedy based on Hasbro's My Little Pony toy line, directed by Robert Cullen and José Luis Ucha from a screenplay by Tim Sullivan and Gillian Berrow. Produced by Entertainment One and Boulder Media, it serves as a follow-up to the television series My Little Pony: Friendship Is Magic. The voice cast includes Vanessa Hudgens as Sunny Starscout, Kimiko Glenn as Izzy Moonbow, James Marsden as Hitch Trailblazer, Sofia Carson as Pipp Petals, Liza Koshy as Zipp Storm, Ken Jeong as Sprout, Elizabeth Perkins as Phyllis Cloverleaf, Jane Krakowski as Queen Haven, Phil LaMarr as Alphabittle and Michael McKean as Sunny's father Argyle.

Long after the age of Twilight Sparkle and her friends, the three pony races of Equestria have drifted apart and live in mutual fear. In the earth pony town of Maretime Bay, young Sunny Starscout grows up hearing her father's tales of a time when earth ponies, pegasi and unicorns lived in harmony. As an adult, she still believes the old stories, to the dismay of her neighbors and her childhood friend Hitch, now the town's sheriff.

When a cheerful unicorn named Izzy Moonbow wanders into Maretime Bay, the townsfolk panic, but Sunny befriends her and learns that the unicorns have lost their magic. Suspecting the pegasi, the two set off for the pegasus city of Zephyr Heights, pursued by Hitch, while his deputy Sprout seizes control of the town and stirs it into a frenzy. In Zephyr Heights they discover that the royal family led by Queen Haven has been faking flight, because the pegasi have lost their magic too. With the help of princesses Pipp and Zipp, Sunny learns that a set of ancient crystals may hold the key to restoring magic and setting off on a quest to bring the pony races back together.

The film carries the franchise's themes of friendship and unity into a new generation, using its story of distrust between species as an allegory for prejudice.

Originally planned as a theatrical release by Paramount Pictures, the film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival on September 8, 2021, and was released on Netflix on September 24 because of the COVID-19 pandemic. It received generally positive reviews, holding 92 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and was followed by the series Tell Your Tale and Make Your Mark.

documents.title: Away
documents.overview: After suffering a plane crash on a mysterious island, a young man embarks on an epic journey through forests, deserts and mountains trying to escape the shadow of a huge dark spirit.
documents.plot:
Away (Latvian: Projām) is a 2019 Latvian animated fantasy adventure film written, directed, animated and scored by Gints Zilbalodis in his feature debut. Made almost entirely by Zilbalodis alone over three and a half years using the 3D software Maya, it contains no dialogue. The film premiered at the Annecy International Animation Film Festival in 2019, where it won the Contrechamp award for best feature in its competition section.

A teenage boy awakens in a desert, hanging from a parachute caught in the branches of a tree, as a giant, silent black figure approaches from the dust. The creature tries to swallow him, but he frees himself and flees, discovering that the monster is translucent and slow. Following a path to a stone archway, he finds an oasis of trees and water by the sea, where he rests and meets a small yellow bird that cannot yet fly. He also finds a motorcycle and a backpack containing survival supplies and a map of the island, showing a port town on the far side where he might find help.

With the monster waiting near the oasis, the boy spends the night among the trees. The next day the bird tries to follow a flock of white birds and is swallowed by the monster, but the boy runs through the creature and rescues it. Stocking up on fruit and water, he rides away on the motorcycle with the little bird, following a series of stone arches across the desert and into grasslands, while the monster slowly follows, consuming every living thing in its path. Told in chapters, the journey takes the pair through changing landscapes, including a mountain of balancing rocks and a mirror-like lake, as the boy grows stronger, the bird learns to fly, and the boy confronts his fear of the shadow pursuing him in the hope of reaching safety.

Away received widespread acclaim, holding a 100 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on 31 reviews, with a consensus calling it a haunting and refreshing odyssey, and a Metacritic score of 78. Critics praised its dreamlike visuals and score. Zilbalodis later directed Flow (2024), which won the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature.

documents.title: Beckett
documents.overview: An American tourist in Greece finds himself on the run after a tragic accident plunges him into a political conspiracy that makes him a target for assassination.
documents.plot:
Beckett is a 2021 action thriller directed by Ferdinando Cito Filomarino and produced by Luca Guadagnino. John David Washington stars as an American tourist in Greece who becomes the target of a manhunt after an accident draws him into a political conspiracy, with Boyd Holbrook, Vicky Krieps and Alicia Vikander in supporting roles. Originally titled Born to Be Murdered, it was shot in Athens in 2019, premiered at the 74th Locarno Film Festival on August 4, 2021, and was released by Netflix on August 13.

Beckett and his girlfriend April leave Athens to avoid political unrest. Driving through the mountains of Epirus at night, Beckett falls asleep at the wheel and crashes into a house.
