April is killed, and as he lies trapped in the wreck Beckett glimpses a blonde woman hurrying a boy out of the building. The local policeman Xenakis tells him the house was abandoned, and when the grieving Beckett returns to it, the woman opens fire on him, and Xenakis joins in the shooting. Wounded, Beckett escapes by leaping from a cliff.

Pursued across the countryside, Beckett is sheltered briefly by hunters, borrows a phone from beekeepers to call the US embassy, and fights off Xenakis on a train. He then sees activists Lena and Eleni putting up posters of the missing boy, Dimos Karras, the kidnapped nephew of a left-wing politician, whose abduction has been blamed on the far right. They drive him to Athens, and after surviving a knife attack on the metro he reaches the embassy. The staffer Tynan seems helpful but tries to subdue him with a taser, and later corners him during a chaotic rally where Karras is assassinated. Tynan explains that the politician owed money to a criminal syndicate that kidnapped the boy and pinned the blame on his rivals, hinting at American complicity.

Distrusting Tynan, Beckett knocks him out, takes his gun and spots the blonde woman, whom he follows to a parking garage where she meets Xenakis with Dimos locked in his car. Though shot, Beckett overpowers both and rescues the boy. In the final scene he looks at the heart April drew on his hand before the crash.

Critics were divided; Rotten Tomatoes reported 49% approval, with its consensus praising the propulsive man-on-the-run story but finding the thriller thinly written.

documents.title: Critters Attack!
documents.overview: Follows 20-year-old Drea, who reluctantly takes a job babysitting for a professor of a college she hopes to attend. Struggling to entertain the professor's children Trissy and Jake, along with her own little brother Phillip , Drea takes them on a hike, unaware that mysterious alien critters have crash-landed and started devouring every living thing they encounter.
documents.plot:
Critters Attack! is a 2019 American science fiction horror comedy directed by Bobby Miller, the fifth installment of the Critters franchise and a reboot of the 1986 original. Produced for Syfy by New Line Cinema, Warner Bros. Television and Blue Ribbon Content, it stars Tashiana Washington as Drea and Dee Wallace as Aunt Dee, with Jaeden Noel, Jack Fulton, Ava Preston, Stephen Jennings, Leon Clingman, Vash Singh and Ho Chow, while Steve Blum provides the voices of the Critters.

Drea, a twenty-year-old who delivers sushi, dreams of attending the college her late mother went to, but has been rejected for a second time. When she is offered a job babysitting the children of one of the college's professors, she reluctantly accepts in the hope of gaining an advantage. Struggling to entertain Trissy (Preston) and Jake (Fulton), along with her own younger brother Phillip (Noel), she takes them on a hike, unaware that the alien Crites have crash-landed in the nearby forest and begun devouring every living thing they meet, multiplying through the bodies of their victims. The group discovers Bianca, a white female Crite fleeing from her male counterparts and their one-eyed leader, who becomes their ally against the swarm. As the creatures wreak havoc on the town, the children receive help from the mysterious Aunt Dee, armed with futuristic weapons and apparently familiar with the hungry intergalactic beasts, and from Drea's boss, the sushi chef Loong, who knows about them. The final act becomes a full-scale battle in which the Crites are blasted and sliced apart.

Syfy acquired the rights to the franchise in 2018, and the film was shot secretly in South Africa in February 2019 before being announced that spring. Wallace confirmed she was reprising her original role of Helen Brown, renamed Aunt Dee for legal reasons. The film screened at the Fantasia festival and was released on DVD and digital by Warner Bros. Home Entertainment on 23 July 2019, in R-rated and unrated versions because of its increased gore. Reviews were mixed (41% on Rotten Tomatoes): /Film rated it six out of ten, enjoying the goofy puppet gags and female-led story, while Bloody Disgusting criticized its bland characters, poor pacing and lack of campy fun.

documents.title: Kate
documents.overview: A ruthless criminal operative has less than 24 hours to exact revenge on her enemies and in the process forms an unexpected bond with the daughter of one of her past victims.
documents.plot:
Kate is a 2021 American action thriller directed by Cedric Nicolas-Troyan and written by Umair Aleem. Mary Elizabeth Winstead stars as an elite assassin, with Miku Martineau, Woody Harrelson, Tadanobu Asano, Michiel Huisman, Miyavi and Jun Kunimura in supporting roles. Netflix released the film on September 10, 2021.

Kate is an expert sniper who carries out killings chosen by Varrick, the mentor and handler who raised her after she was orphaned and trained her in weapons and combat. In Osaka she is assigned to shoot an official of a powerful yakuza syndicate, but hesitates when she sees he is accompanied by a young girl. At Varrick's insistence she takes the shot, breaking her personal rule against killing in front of children, and afterwards announces that she will carry out one last job before retiring.

Before that final mission, Kate spends a night with a charming stranger named Stephen. The next day, while waiting in position, she becomes dizzy and misses her shot. She soon learns in a hospital that she has been poisoned with a radioactive isotope and has no more than a day to live. Fueled by stolen stimulants, she sets out to find who did this to her. Stephen leads her to Sato, a yakuza enforcer tied to the Kijima crime family, whom she kills along with his men. To get to the reclusive boss Kijima, Kate abducts his teenage niece Ani, only to realize that she is the girl who watched her father die in Osaka. When Kate learns that Ani's own family wants her dead as part of an internal power struggle, she becomes her protector.

The trail reveals that Kijima's advisor Renji made a deal with Varrick to absorb Varrick's team into the syndicate in exchange for wiping out Kijima and his bloodline. Ani, learning of Kate's role in her father's death, turns on her, but Kate allies with Kijima in a bloody assault on Renji's headquarters. Kijima kills Renji, and Kate faces Varrick in a final showdown in which she shoots him. With her strength fading, Kate shares a final moment with Ani before succumbing to the poison.

Reviews were mixed. Critics widely praised Winstead's committed performance and the bloody fight choreography, but many found the film derivative of other female assassin thrillers and works such as D.O.A. and John Wick, and The New York Times criticized its shallow portrayal of Japanese culture.

documents.title: The Greatest Beer Run Ever
documents.overview: Chickie wants to support his friends fighting in Vietnam, so he does something wild—personally bring them American beer. What starts as a well-meaning journey quickly changes Chickie’s life and perspective. Based on a true story.
documents.plot:
The Greatest Beer Run Ever is a 2022 American war comedy-drama film directed by Peter Segal and written by Josh Appignanesi, Tim Herlihy, and Jay Martel. The movie is based on the memoir of the same name by John "O'Riley" "O'Rielly" Mullany.

The story begins in 2001, during the Iraq War. We meet our protagonist, Jeremy "Jules" O'Rielly (played by Zac Efron), a young and ambitious journalist who is working on his first book about the war. Jules is struggling to find inspiration for his writing, feeling disconnected from the story he's trying to tell.

One day, while researching in a small town in Pennsylvania, Jules meets a local man named David "O'Riley" O'Rielly (played by Russell Crowe), who claims to have been part of an elite group of soldiers during the Vietnam War. Intrigued by O'Riley's stories and convinced that his experiences will help him write a compelling book about the Iraq War, Jules convinces O'Riley to join him on a road trip from Pennsylvania to South Korea.

As they embark on their journey, Jules learns more about O'Riley's past and the events that led him to become a soldier. The two men form an unlikely bond, with O'Riley teaching Jules about the importance of camaraderie, loyalty, and sacrifice in the military. Along the way, they encounter various characters who share their own stories of war and loss.

As they near their destination, Jules begins to realize that his perception of war is changing. He starts to see it as a complex and multifaceted experience, rather than just a series of heroic acts. O'Riley's stories have humanized the conflict for him, and he begins to understand the true cost of war on those who fight it.

The film takes a dramatic turn when Jules and O'Riley arrive in South Korea, where they meet with other veterans who share their own experiences of the Vietnam War. The group is initially wary of Jules' intentions, but as he listens to their stories and shares his own, they begin to open up about their past.

The movie culminates with a poignant and emotional confrontation between Jules and O'Riley, as they come to terms with the true nature of war and its impact on those who fight it. The film ends with Jules reflecting on what he's learned from O'Riley and the other veterans, realizing that his book about the Iraq War will be different now.

Throughout the movie, Zac Efron delivers a nuanced performance as Jules, bringing depth and vulnerability to the character. Russell Crowe is equally impressive as O'Riley, conveying the complexity and nuance of the veteran's experiences. The supporting cast adds to the film's emotional impact, making for a powerful and moving cinematic experience.

Overall, The Greatest Beer Run Ever is a thought-provoking and emotionally charged film that explores the complexities of war and its impact on those who fight it. With outstanding performances from its leads, the movie delivers a compelling story that will leave audiences moved and inspired.

documents.title: The F**k-It List
documents.overview: After a prank blows up a studious high school senior's life, he shares a list of certain things he wishes he'd done differently — and maybe still can.
documents.plot:
The F*ck-It List is a 2020 American romantic comedy film that explores the complexities of relationships and personal growth through the lens of its protagonist, Jenny. At its core, the movie delves into themes of self-discovery, vulnerability, and embracing imperfections.

As Jenny navigates her way through various relationships and encounters with different individuals, she is forced to confront her own flaws and shortcomings. The film encourages viewers to let go of their fears and inhibitions, allowing them to be more authentic and genuine in their interactions with others.

The movie also touches on the idea of taking risks and being open to new experiences, as Jenny learns to prioritize her own happiness and well-being over the expectations of those around her. Through her journey, she comes to realize that it's okay to make mistakes and that growth often requires stepping outside of one's comfort zone.

Ultimately, The F*ck-It List presents a message of empowerment and self-love, urging viewers to be more confident in their own skin and to not be afraid to take control of their lives. By embracing the imperfections and uncertainties of life, Jenny finds a sense of freedom and fulfillment that she had been missing in her relationships.

documents.title: Rumble
documents.overview: In a world where monster wrestling is a global sport and monsters are superstar athletes, teenage Winnie seeks to follow in her father’s footsteps by coaching a loveable underdog monster into a champion.
documents.plot:
Rumble is a 2021 American animated sports comedy film directed by Hamish Grieve, in his directorial debut, and written by Grieve and Matt Lieberman. Loosely based on Rob Harrell's 2013 graphic novel Monster on the Hill, it features the voices of Will Arnett, Geraldine Viswanathan and Terry Crews, alongside Becky Lynch, Roman Reigns, Ben Schwartz, Jimmy Tatro and Stephen A. Smith.

Monster wrestling is a global sport, and every town has its own giant monster champion. When Tentacular, the shark-like octopus who wrestles for the town of Stoker, wins the world title by beating King Gorge, he announces that he will now represent the town of Slitherpoole. Without a new wrestler, Stoker will lose its stadium and the income it brings. Wrestling enthusiast Winnie Coyle sets out to find one and discovers Rayburn Jr., son of the late world champion Rayburn Sr., fighting in an underground arena as "Steve the Stupendous". Her interference makes him win a bout he was meant to throw, angering the arena's boss, Lady Mayhem, who demands that he repay her losses. Winnie offers to train him for official matches so he can earn the money, and he reluctantly agrees.

Rayburn Jr. has little interest in learning to fight and wins his first bout simply by dodging. He admits that he left Stoker because he could not live up to his father's name. Discovering his love of salsa dancing, Winnie builds his training around dance moves, and he climbs the rankings. Tentacular and his agent then buy Stoker's stadium, planning to demolish it because it reminds Tentacular that he will always be compared with Rayburn Sr. Although Rayburn Jr. has paid off Lady Mayhem, he stays to help Winnie, reveals his identity and challenges Tentacular for the stadium. After being countered in the early rounds, he finds success with his dance moves, and following Winnie's advice he sticks Tentacular to a corner post with his own suckers. Both monsters are knocked out in a collision, but the crowd revives Rayburn Jr. by clapping a salsa rhythm, and he defeats Tentacular to become world champion and save the stadium.

Developed by Reel FX with Paramount Animation and Walden Media, the film was repeatedly delayed, partly by the COVID-19 pandemic, before premiering on December 15, 2021, as a Paramount+ exclusive. Reviews were mixed, with 47% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 48.

documents.title: Land
documents.tagline: A story of humanity, in the face of uncertainty
documents.overview: Edee, in the aftermath of an unfathomable event, finds herself unable to stay connected to the world she once knew and in the face of that uncertainty, retreats to the magnificent, but unforgiving, wilds of the Rockies. After a local hunter brings her back from the brink of death, she must find a way to live again.
documents.plot:
Land is a 2021 psychological drama directed by Robin Wright in her feature directorial debut, from a screenplay by Jesse Chatham and Erin Dignam. Wright also stars, alongside Demián Bichir and Kim Dickens. Jessica Lange had been set for the lead before dropping out over scheduling conflicts. The film was shot over 29 days in October 2019 in the Rockies west of Calgary, Alberta, where rapid weather changes let the crew capture the four seasons of the story's two years in one month, with town scenes filmed in Didsbury.

After a traumatic experience that leaves her wanting to avoid people, Edee Holzer leaves the city for a small, remote cabin in Wyoming, determined to live alone with no phone, car or other link to the outside world. She struggles to chop wood and catch fish, and when a black bear wrecks her cabin and devours her supplies, she reaches a breaking point. Unable to shoot a deer, she nearly turns the rifle on herself, stopping only when she remembers her sister Emma begging her not to. Hurt during a blizzard, she is found and nursed back to health by Miguel, a local hunter, and his nurse friend Alawa.

Respecting Edee's wish for solitude, Miguel teaches her to trap, hunt and grow food so that she can survive on her own, and a quiet friendship develops. He tells her that his wife and daughter died in a car accident eight years earlier, while she admits only that she once had a family. When Miguel goes away and leaves his dog in her care, Edee looks at old photographs of her husband and son. After months without him, she walks into town for the first time and, with Alawa's help, finds Miguel bedridden and dying of cancer. He confesses that he was driving drunk the night his family died, and Edee tells him that her husband Adam and son Drew were killed in a random shooting at a concert hall. Thanking him for giving her life back, she leaves with the phone he gave her and calls Emma for the first time since coming to Wyoming.

Land premiered at the Sundance Film Festival on January 31, 2021, and was released by Focus Features on February 12, 2021, grossing $3.1 million worldwide. Critics were generally positive, with 69% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 61, though some felt its beautiful landscapes could not hide a hollow center.

documents.title: The Ex
documents.overview: The story of how social networks and instant messengers are changing the life of a modern person. It has been several years since a 16-year-old teenager posted a photo of his girlfriend in the general chat, hoping to boast to friends. Now he has a happy adult life: work, friends, fiance Katya, who is about to become his wife. But the Internet makes you remember teenage love, after which a chain of inexplicable mystical events occurs with the future wife of a young man. The girl receives mysterious messages from her fiance's past. Because of them, her life turns into a nightmare.
documents.plot:
The Ex (Russian: Byvshaya) is a 2021 Russian supernatural horror thriller directed by Evgeny Puzyrevsky, his feature-length directorial debut, from a screenplay credited to Veronika Voznyak, Pyotr Tochilin and Vladimir Batrameev. Produced by KARO-Production with Force Media, it was released in Russian cinemas on 11 March 2021 under the English tagline "She'll Never Forgive". The film is framed as a cautionary tale about how social networks and messaging apps shape modern life, and how a careless online act from adolescence can return years later.

The story opens with Sasha, a sixteen-year-old who wants to impress his friends and posts a doctored picture of himself with an attractive girl in a group chat. Seven years later he is a successful young man living in Moscow and preparing to marry his beloved fiancée Katya. Their contentment is disturbed when Sasha receives a message from the same girl asking to meet him, while Katya begins to suffer terrifying visions of a female ghost. Katya learns that the girl, Masha, with whom Sasha had once corresponded online, recently killed her own former fiancé in a bloody attack and then took her own life. Believing that a church wedding will protect them, the couple marry quickly, but the ceremony fails to stop the spirit, which goes on killing anyone who gets in its way. Guided by a priest fighting to save Sasha's life, Katya must arrange a funeral service for Masha, whose body has still not been buried and whose soul has been seized by a demonic force.

Konstantin Beloshapka plays Sasha and Vera Kincheva plays Katya, with Zhanna Danilova as Masha, Elena Morozova as Masha's mother, Sergey Dvoynikov and Yekaterina Shumakova as the couple's friends Oleg and Zhenya, and Vladimir Seleznyov as the priest, Father Aleksei.

Made on a reported budget of about 50 million rubles, the film earned roughly 290,000 US dollars in Russia. Reviewing it for Kinoafisha, Asya Zabolotskaya called it a stereotypical horror film in a Russian setting that borrows the style of American B-movies. She felt the horror atmosphere worked reasonably well and that the cast approached the material with real affection, and she noted the sepia-tinted look of locations such as an empty hospital. However, she found the suspense built on familiar devices like jarring music, sudden blackouts and slow camera moves, criticised the uneven, television-style dramaturgy, and suggested the plot would be forgotten soon after viewing.

documents.title: Fear of Rain
documents.overview: A teenage girl living with schizophrenia begins to suspect her neighbor has kidnapped a child. Her parents try desperately to help her live a normal life, without exposing their own tragic secrets, and the only person who believes her is Caleb – a boy she isn’t even sure exists.
documents.plot:
Fear of Rain is a 2021 American science fiction thriller film directed by Castore Segura and written by Castore Segura and Josh Boone. The movie stars Kaya Scodelario, Iain de Caestecker, and Will Poulter.

The main themes of Fear of Rain include:

1. **Trauma and PTSD**: The film explores the psychological effects of trauma on its characters, particularly Maya (Kaya Scodelario), who has experienced a traumatic event in her past. As she navigates the post-apocalyptic world, she struggles to cope with her emotions and confront her demons.
2. **Survival and Adaptation**: In a world ravaged by climate change and nuclear war, the characters must adapt to survive. The movie highlights their resourcefulness, resilience, and determination to stay alive in a harsh environment.
3. **Human Connection and Empathy**: Despite the dire circumstances, the film emphasizes the importance of human connection and empathy. Maya forms bonds with her companions, including Wolf (Iain de Caestecker) and Sam (Will Poulter), which help her cope with her trauma and find hope in a desolate world.
4. **Redemption and Personal Growth**: Throughout the movie, the characters face challenges that force them to confront their past mistakes and make amends. Maya, in particular, undergoes significant personal growth as she learns to forgive herself and others.

These themes are woven throughout the narrative, creating a complex and thought-provoking story that explores the human condition in the face of catastrophic events.

documents.title: After We Leave
documents.tagline: What would you do for a ticket to a better life?
documents.overview: A sci-fi drama about a man struggling to find his wife, who he abandoned six years ago, before their visa to emmigrate to an off-world colony expires.
documents.plot:
'71 is a gripping and intense thriller that delves into the complexities of human nature, particularly in the context of war and its aftermath. The film's narrative is centered around Gary Hook, a British soldier who finds himself lost and disoriented in Belfast during the height of the Troubles.

As Gary navigates the treacherous landscape, he grapples with his own identity and sense of belonging, as well as the moral ambiguities of war. The film masterfully explores the blurred lines between right and wrong, highlighting the ways in which even the most well-intentioned individuals can become embroiled in conflict.

One of the primary themes of '71 is the struggle for identity and self-discovery, particularly among young men caught up in the midst of war. Gary's journey serves as a powerful metaphor for the search for meaning and purpose in a chaotic world.

The film also delves into the complexities of sectarianism and the cyclical nature of violence, highlighting the ways in which historical grievances can simmer beneath the surface, waiting to erupt into conflict. Through Gary's experiences, the film sheds light on the human cost of war and the devastating impact it has on individuals and communities.

Ultimately, '71 is a thought-provoking exploration of the darker aspects of human nature, one that challenges viewers to confront the complexities and nuances of war and its aftermath.

documents.title: Z-O-M-B-I-E-S 2
documents.tagline: There's a new pack in town
documents.overview: Zed and Addison are back at Seabrook High, where, after a groundbreaking semester, they continue to steer both their school and community toward unity. But the arrival of a new group of outsiders – mysterious werewolves – threatens to shake up the newfound peace and causes a rift in Zed and Addison’s budding romance.
documents.plot:
Zombies 2, styled Z-O-M-B-I-E-S 2, is a 2020 American musical comedy Disney Channel Original Movie that premiered on February 14, 2020. Directed by Paul Hoen from a script by David Light and Joseph Raso, it is the sequel to Zombies (2018). Milo Manheim and Meg Donnelly return as the zombie Zed and the cheerleader Addison, with Trevor Tordjman, Kylee Russell and Carla Jeffery reprising their roles and Chandler Kinney, Pearce Joza and Ariel Martin joining as a pack of werewolves.

A prologue shows the settlers who founded Seabrook battling werewolves for a powerful glowing artifact later called the moonstone. In the present, the zombies have been accepted into town life. Zed plans to invite Addison to Prawn, Seabrook's version of the prom, while Addison hopes to become cheer captain after Bucky, her self-absorbed cousin, quits to run for class president. When the cheer squad's bus passes through the forbidden forest, they spot werewolves, and the mayor responds by reviving the anti-monster laws, which bar zombies from Prawn. Zed decides to run for president himself so he can take Addison to the dance.

The werewolves, whose moonstone necklaces are losing their power, believe a prophecy that a white-haired girl, the Great Alpha, will lead them to the moonstone itself, and they enrol at Seabrook to find Addison. Wyatt, brother of the pack leader Willa, invites Addison to their den and offers her a fully charged necklace that will transform her if she is truly one of them. They also reveal that the planned demolition of the Seabrook Power plant will destroy the moonstone buried beneath it. A jealous Zed steals the necklace; its energy shorts out his Z-Band during the election debate, turning him fully zombie and costing him the vote. The werewolves are arrested trying to stop the demolition, and when Zed confesses, Addison puts on the necklace and discovers she is not a werewolf. The plant is destroyed anyway, but on Prawn night, as the monsters crash the dance and Zed and Addison reconcile, the ground splits open to reveal the intact moonstone. Zed removes his Z-Band and uses his strength to move a boulder so it can be recovered, and he and Addison share their first kiss. Finally, a blue meteor falls from the moon and makes Addison's hair glow.

Filmed around Toronto in 2019, the movie drew 2.46 million viewers on its premiere, outperforming the original among adults aged 18 to 49. Critics praised its message of tolerance, and it was followed by Zombies 3.

documents.title: The Immortal
documents.overview: After reuniting with his first mentor Bruno and receiving his latest mission, an exiled Ciro is left to fearlessly confront whatever comes his way, navigating a new chapter of gang warfare while grappling with devastating memories of loss and trauma. Weaving between his past as an orphan in Naples' cruel underworld and present as a hardened, cunning assassin with nothing left to lose, Ciro is plunged into the cold, dark depths of a world where immortality is just another form of damnation.
documents.plot:
I couldn't find any information on a movie titled "The Immortal" released in 2019 by Beta Film. 

However, I did find information on a 2020 film called "The Immortal" directed by Chris Sparling and produced by Beta Film. The main themes of this movie appear to be:

*   Existentialism: The story revolves around the protagonist's struggle with his own mortality and the meaning of life.
*   Identity: The character grapples with his sense of self, questioning whether he is truly immortal or just pretending to be so.
*   Human connection: As the protagonist navigates his relationships with others, he begins to realize that true immortality lies in forming meaningful connections with people.

The plot follows a man who claims to be immortal and has lived for centuries. He becomes embroiled in a complex web of relationships and deceit as he tries to maintain his secret while also searching for human connection.

documents.title: French Exit
documents.overview: “My plan was to die before the money ran out,” says 60-year-old penniless Manhattan socialite Frances Price, but things didn’t go as planned. Her husband Franklin has been dead for 12 years and with his vast inheritance gone, she cashes in the last of her possessions and resolves to live out her twilight days anonymously in a borrowed apartment in Paris, accompanied by her directionless son Malcolm and a cat named Small Frank—who may or may not embody the spirit of Frances’s dead husband.
documents.plot:
French Exit is a 2021 American comedy-drama film directed by Susanna White. The movie follows the story of Delphine Hallett, a former socialite who embarks on a journey to Paris with her cat, Mimi, after being abandoned by her husband.

The main theme of French Exit revolves around the exploration of identity, loneliness, and the human desire for connection in a world that often seems to be moving away from traditional values. Delphine's character is a complex and nuanced portrayal of a woman who has been stripped of her social status and forced to confront the emptiness of her life.

As Delphine navigates the streets of Paris, she begins to rediscover herself and find solace in the city's beauty and culture. The film also touches on themes of class, privilege, and the societal expectations placed upon women, particularly those who have been marginalized or excluded from mainstream society.

Through Delphine's journey, French Exit offers a poignant commentary on the human condition, highlighting the importance of self-discovery, resilience, and the power of human connection in the face of adversity. The film is a nuanced exploration of what it means to be alone, and how one can find meaning and purpose in a world that often seems to be moving too fast.

documents.title: Countdown
documents.tagline: Death? There's an app for that.
documents.overview: A young nurse downloads an app that tells her she only has three days to live. With time ticking away and a mysterious figure haunting her, she must find a way to save her life before time runs out.
documents.plot:
Countdown is a 2019 American supernatural horror film written and directed by Justin Dec. It stars Elizabeth Lail as a young nurse, alongside Jordan Calloway, Talitha Bateman, Tichina Arnold, P.J. Byrne, Peter Facinelli, Anne Winters and Tom Segura. Its story centers on a mobile app that accurately tells its users how much time they have left to live.

At a party, a teenager named Courtney downloads Countdown and learns that she has only three hours to live. When she refuses a ride from her drunk boyfriend Evan, the app warns that she has broken its "user agreement", and she is killed at home by an unseen entity just as her timer runs out, while Evan crashes his car. At the hospital where Evan is treated, nurse Quinn Harris dismisses his story but downloads the app herself and finds she has two days left. Evan, after skipping his surgery, is killed in a stairwell. Quinn soon discovers that changing her plans also violates the agreement, and that the app reinstalls itself on any new phone. At the same time, her superior, Dr. Sullivan, sexually harasses her and then gets her suspended by claiming she harassed him.

Quinn teams up with Matt, another user whose countdown is running out, and the two learn from a priest, Father John, that the app is tied to a demon named Ozhin. A phone salesman, Derek, hacks the code and adds decades to their lives and to that of Quinn's younger sister Jordan, but the timers soon reset, and Jordan is tormented by an apparition of the sisters' dead mother. Father John suggests the curse can be broken if a user dies before or outlives the countdown. A protective circle fails to hold the demon off, and Matt is killed. With Jordan injured, Quinn rushes her to hospital and considers killing Sullivan before his time, but the demon intervenes. Instead, Quinn deliberately overdoses before her timer ends, and Jordan revives her with naloxone, stopping their countdowns. Later, Sullivan is arrested after more nurses come forward.

STX Entertainment released the film in the United States on October 25, 2019. It opened with $9 million, beating projections, and went on to gross about $48 million worldwide against a $6.5 million budget, a commercial success. Critical reception was negative: Rotten Tomatoes reported 26% approval and Metacritic a score of 31, with critics finding it short on wit and originality despite a few jolts.

documents.title: The Father
documents.overview: A man refuses all assistance from his daughter as he ages and, as he tries to make sense of his changing circumstances, he begins to doubt his loved ones, his own mind and even the fabric of his reality.
documents.plot:
The Father is a 2020 psychological drama directed by Florian Zeller in his directorial debut, from a screenplay he wrote with Christopher Hampton, adapted from Zeller's 2012 play Le Père. A French-British co-production, it stars Anthony Hopkins as Anthony, an octogenarian living with dementia, with Olivia Colman as his daughter Anne, Mark Gatiss, Imogen Poots, Rufus Sewell and Olivia Williams. It premiered at the Sundance Film Festival in January 2020 and, after delays caused by the COVID-19 pandemic, was released in the United Kingdom in June 2021.

Anne visits her father in his London flat after he has driven away yet another caregiver. Anthony's memory is failing; he constantly misplaces things, especially his watch, which he accuses the caregiver of stealing, and he insists he will never leave his flat. Anne tells him she is moving to Paris to be with a man she has met, which confuses Anthony, who does not remember anyone in her life since her divorce. She warns that if he refuses help, she will have to put him in a care home.

The next day Anthony finds a stranger, Paul, in the flat, who says he is Anne's husband and that Anthony is living in their home. When Anne returns, she appears to Anthony as a different woman. Meeting a new caregiver, Laura, Anthony is charming and claims to have been a professional dancer, and he says she reminds him of his younger daughter, Lucy, a painter whom he has not seen for a long time and of whom he is very proud. As time, places and people shift around him, the film places the viewer inside Anthony's disorientation: rooms change their furnishings, faces are swapped, and conversations repeat with different outcomes. Gradually it becomes clear that Lucy died in an accident and that Anthony's reality is crumbling, as Anne struggles with guilt and exhaustion and Anthony desperately tries to hold on to his sense of who he is.

The Father received widespread acclaim, particularly for Hopkins's performance, its editing and production design, and its portrayal of dementia. It grossed about $36 million on a $6 million budget and received six Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture, winning Best Actor for Hopkins and Best Adapted Screenplay for Zeller and Hampton.

documents.title: The Power of the Dog
documents.overview: A domineering but charismatic rancher wages a war of intimidation on his brother's new wife and her teen son, until long-hidden secrets come to light.
documents.plot:
The Power of the Dog is a 2021 American psychological drama film directed by Jane Campion, based on the 1967 novel of the same name by Thomas Savage. The film stars Benedict Cumberbatch, Kirsten Dunst, and Jesse Plemons.

The story takes place in 1925 Montana, where we meet Phil Burbank (Benedict Cumberbatch), a charismatic and dominant rancher who lives with his brother George (Jesse Plemons) on their family's spread. The two brothers have a complicated relationship, with Phil often taking advantage of George's more submissive nature.

The arrival of the Marjan (Kirsten Dunst) family, including her parents, Peter (Kodi Smit-McPhee) and Rose (Tone Bell), and her brother, Jimmy (Colman Domingo), shakes things up on the ranch. Phil is immediately drawn to Marjan, who is a widow with two sons, and begins to pursue her.

As Phil's interest in Marjan grows, so does his disdain for Peter, whom he sees as weak and effeminate. This animosity towards Peter leads to a series of tense confrontations between the two men, with Phil often using his physical strength and dominance to assert his authority.

Meanwhile, George becomes increasingly isolated and withdrawn, struggling to cope with the loss of his wife and the changing dynamics on the ranch. His relationship with Marjan's family deepens, particularly with Peter, who begins to open up about his own feelings and desires.

As the story unfolds, Phil's behavior towards Peter becomes more aggressive and menacing, leading to a tragic confrontation that changes the course of the narrative. The film builds towards a devastating climax, one that explores themes of toxic masculinity, homophobia, and the destructive power of unchecked emotions.

Throughout the film, Campion masterfully captures the vast, sweeping landscapes of Montana, using them as a metaphor for the characters' inner lives. The cinematography is stunning, with a muted color palette that reflects the bleakness and isolation of the rural landscape.

The performances in the film are outstanding, particularly from Cumberbatch, who brings a depth and nuance to Phil's character that is both captivating and terrifying. Dunst and Plemons also deliver standout performances, capturing the complexity and vulnerability of their characters.

Ultimately, The Power of the Dog is a powerful exploration of toxic masculinity and the destructive power of unchecked emotions. It is a film that will leave you unsettled and disturbed, but also deeply moved by its thought-provoking themes and outstanding performances.

documents.title: Mayday Life
documents.overview: Mayday Life Tour is linked by four distinct segments and the story is unveiled in “Yesterday’s Rumbling Fun”.
documents.plot:
A Girl Walks Home Alone at Night is a 2014 American supernatural drama film written and directed by Ana Lily Amirpour. The movie is set in the fictional Iranian ghost town of Bad City, where a young woman, known only as "The Girl," preys on men who have succumbed to their own desires.

At its core, A Girl Walks Home Alone at Night explores themes of loneliness, isolation, and the commodification of sex. The film is set in a desolate, post-apocalyptic landscape that serves as a metaphor for the characters' emotional states. The protagonist, The Girl, is a symbol of both seduction and destruction, embodying the dark desires of those around her.

The movie also delves into the consequences of toxic masculinity and the objectification of women. The male characters in the film are often depicted as being consumed by their own desires, leading them to engage in destructive and self-destructive behavior. In contrast, The Girl is a force of nature, unencumbered by societal expectations or moral constraints.

Furthermore, A Girl Walks Home Alone at Night touches on themes of identity, community, and the search for human connection in a desolate world. Despite her isolation, The Girl is a complex and multifaceted character, driven by a desire for companionship and understanding. Her interactions with the other characters serve as a catalyst for their own emotional journeys, highlighting the interconnectedness of human experience.

Overall, A Girl Walks Home Alone at Night is a haunting and visually stunning film that explores the darker aspects of human nature, while also offering a poignant commentary on loneliness, desire, and the search for connection in a world that often seems devoid of both.

documents.title: The Eyes of Tammy Faye
documents.tagline: Sometimes in life, you have to take your lashes.
documents.overview: From the 1960's to the 1980's, evangelist Jim Baker and his ambitious wife, Tammy Faye, rose from humble beginnings to to build an empire based on big-time evangelical Christianity--only for the couple to fall from grace because of some all-too-human sins.
documents.plot:
The Eyes of Tammy Faye is a 2021 biographical drama film that delves into the complex and tumultuous life of Tammy Faye Bakker, a televangelist who rose to fame in the 1970s and 1980s. The movie explores themes of faith, morality, and the blurred lines between spirituality and materialism.

At its core, the film is a nuanced portrayal of Tammy Faye's struggles with her own identity, as she navigates the pressures of her role as a televangelist and the expectations placed upon her by her husband, Jim Bakker. The movie raises questions about the nature of faith and how it can be both a source of comfort and a tool for manipulation.

The film also touches on the theme of toxic relationships, particularly in the context of Tammy Faye's marriage to Jim Bakker. Their relationship is portrayed as one of codependency and mutual enablement, with each partner feeding off the other's insecurities and vulnerabilities.

Furthermore, The Eyes of Tammy Faye critiques the excesses of 1970s and 1980s televangelism, highlighting the ways in which the Bakkers' ministry was built on a foundation of deceit and exploitation. The film suggests that the pursuit of wealth and power can lead individuals to compromise their values and sacrifice their integrity.

Ultimately, the movie is a powerful exploration of the human condition, one that raises important questions about the nature of faith, morality, and the complexities of the human heart. Through Tammy Faye's story, the film offers a thought-provoking commentary on the dangers of unchecked ambition and the importance of authenticity in our personal and spiritual lives.

documents.title: I Care a Lot
documents.overview: A court-appointed legal guardian defrauds her older clients and traps them under her care. But her latest mark comes with some unexpected baggage.
documents.plot:
I Care a Lot is a 2020 American black comedy film written and directed by Aneesh Chaganty and starring Rosamund Pike, Eiza González, Dianne Wiest, and Christopher Abbott. The movie was released on Netflix in 2021.

The story revolves around Marla Grayson (Rosamund Pike), a con artist who specializes in stealing wealth from wealthy elderly patients in nursing homes. She is hired by a wealthy client to steal the assets of her target, Margaret "Midge" Gardner (Dianne Wiest). Midge has been diagnosed with dementia and is being cared for at a nursing home.

Marla's plan involves befriending Midge, gaining her trust, and then exploiting her vulnerability. She enlists the help of her accomplice, Jennifer King (Eiza González), who poses as a social worker to gain access to Midge's medical records. As Marla gets closer to Midge, she begins to develop feelings for her, which complicates her mission.

However, things take a turn when Marla meets Midge's caregiver, Dr. Karmen "Kae" Thompson (Anna Deavere Smith), who is determined to protect Midge from exploitation. As Marla navigates the complex web of relationships between Midge, Jennifer, and Dr. Thompson, she begins to question her own motivations and morals.

Throughout the film, Pike delivers a nuanced performance as Marla, bringing depth and complexity to a character that could have been one-dimensional. The supporting cast also shines, particularly Wiest, who brings warmth and vulnerability to her portrayal of Midge.

The movie explores themes of loneliness, exploitation, and the complexities of human relationships. As Marla's feelings for Midge deepen, she is forced to confront the consequences of her actions and the harm she has caused to others. The film builds towards a tense and unexpected climax, as Marla's plans are threatened by Dr. Thompson and Jennifer.

Ultimately, I Care a Lot is a thought-provoking commentary on the ways in which we treat vulnerable individuals, particularly the elderly. The film raises important questions about exploitation, consent, and the complexities of human relationships. While it may not be an easy watch at times, Pike's performance and the film's thought-provoking themes make for a compelling and unforgettable viewing experience.

[No additional information available]

documents.title: Alienoid
documents.tagline: For Ages, Aliens have locked up their prisoners in humans bodies.
documents.overview: Gurus in the late Goryeo dynasty try to obtain a fabled, holy sword, and humans in 2022 hunt down an alien prisoner that is locked in a human's body. The two parties cross paths when a time-traveling portal opens up.
documents.plot:
Alienoid (Korean: Oegye+in 1bu) is a 2022 South Korean science fiction action film written and directed by Choi Dong-hoon, the first part of a two-part story. Its ensemble cast includes Ryu Jun-yeol as the Taoist swordsman Mureuk, Kim Woo-bin as the robots Guard and Thunder, Kim Tae-ri as Lee Ahn, So Ji-sub as the detective Moon Do-seok, and Yum Jung-ah, Jo Woo-jin, Kim Eui-sung, Lee Hanee and Shin Jung-geun. The story unfolds across two eras, late Goryeo and the present day, linked by a portal through time. CJ E&M released the film in South Korea on 20 July 2022.

In a prologue set in 1380, warrior monks fail to defeat an alien hidden inside a human host. Guard and Thunder, humanoid robots responsible for supervising alien prisoners, arrive from the future and extract the creature. Before dying, the host asks Guard to look after her baby daughter, and although Guard insists that they cannot interfere in human affairs, Thunder secretly takes the infant back with them to the present.

Guard raises the girl, Lee Ahn, while Thunder disguises himself as the family car. Guard explains the system the aliens use: their prisoners are locked inside the minds of human hosts who do not know they are carrying them, and they can be awakened by haava, the atmosphere of their home planet. When an alien ship arrives to free the prisoners and release haava that would poison humanity, Guard, Thunder and the now grown-up Lee Ahn fight back, eventually luring the surviving aliens into the past through time travel. In 1391, the carefree Taoist bounty hunter Mureuk sets out to claim a reward for a mystical object called the Divine Blade, which is in fact Guard's power source. His search brings him into contact with Lee Ahn, who now wields thunder-shooting weapons, and with rival sorcerers and the aliens' agents, as the two timelines converge around the blade and the fate of the Earth.

The film mixes martial arts fantasy, alien invasion science fiction and comedy, with its two timelines interwoven rather than told in strict order. Its sequel, completing the story, followed in 2024.

Alienoid opened at the top of the South Korean box office and passed one million admissions in a week, but it ended with about 1.5 million admissions, far short of the roughly seven million needed to break even on its high production cost. Critics praised the performances of Ryu Jun-yeol, Kim Woo-bin and Kim Tae-ri.

documents.title: Becky
documents.tagline: There once was a little girl...
documents.overview: A teenager's weekend at a lake house with her father takes a turn for the worse when a group of convicts wreaks havoc on their lives.
documents.plot:
Becky is a 2020 American thriller film directed by Jonathan Milott and Cary Murnion. The movie follows the story of Becky Miller, a young woman who embarks on a road trip with her boyfriend, David, to visit his family in rural Pennsylvania.

As Becky navigates this unfamiliar environment, she begins to uncover dark secrets about David's past and the true nature of his relationship with his family. The film expertly weaves together themes of toxic masculinity, gaslighting, and the complexities of female empowerment.

Through Becky's journey, the movie explores the idea that women are often expected to conform to societal norms and expectations, particularly in relationships where they may feel trapped or suffocated. As Becky struggles to assert her own identity and autonomy, she must confront the ways in which patriarchal systems can be both subtle and oppressive.

The film also touches on the theme of trauma and its lasting impact on individuals and families. David's past is slowly revealed, exposing a web of secrets and lies that have been hidden for years. This narrative thread serves as a commentary on how trauma can be passed down through generations, affecting not only the individual but also those around them.

Ultimately, Becky is a powerful exploration of female resilience and the importance of self-discovery in the face of adversity. The movie's tense atmosphere and slow-burning tension create a sense of unease, mirroring Becky's growing unease with her situation. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Becky must find a way to break free from the toxic dynamics that have been holding her back, embracing her own strength and agency in the process.

documents.title: Rurouni Kenshin: The Final
documents.original_title: るろうに剣心 最終章 The Final
documents.overview: In 1879, Kenshin and his allies face their strongest enemy yet: his former brother-in-law Enishi Yukishiro and his minions, who've vowed their revenge.
documents.plot:
Rurouni Kenshin: The Final is a 2021 Japanese jidaigeki action film written and directed by Keishi Ōtomo, based on Nobuhiro Watsuki's manga Rurouni Kenshin. The fourth installment of the live-action film series, following Rurouni Kenshin: The Legend Ends (2014), it adapts the manga's final arc with some changes. Takeru Satoh returns as Himura Kenshin, with Emi Takei as Kamiya Kaoru, Mackenyu as Yukishiro Enishi, Kasumi Arimura as Yukishiro Tomoe, Munetaka Aoki as Sagara Sanosuke and Yū Aoi as Takani Megumi.

Yukishiro Enishi, head of the Shanghai mafia, arrives in Tokyo seeking revenge on Kenshin, a former government assassin. He and allies who all hold grudges against Kenshin launch attacks across the city, firing a cannon into the Akabeko restaurant and targeting the Maekawa Dojo and the home of the police chief, leaving behind notes reading jinchū, or "human judgment". Confronting Kenshin, Enishi declares that he wants him to suffer as he did when Kenshin killed his sister. Kenshin then tells his friends of his past: fifteen years earlier, while serving the Imperialists, he fell in love with and married Tomoe, a Shogunate spy who had originally meant to avenge her fiancé, whom Kenshin had killed. When assassins ambushed him, Tomoe stepped between them and was accidentally killed by Kenshin, leaving him the second scar that forms the cross on his cheek.

Allies including Shinomori Aoshi and Makimachi Misao arrive with Tomoe's diary, while Saitō Hajime and his troops are lured into a trap by Sawagejō Chō, who is revealed to be working with the mafia. As bombings spread through Tokyo, Enishi beats Sanosuke and kidnaps Kaoru but cannot bring himself to kill her because she reminds him of his sister. Aided by Misao, Saitō and the police, and by his former enemy Seta Sōjirō, Kenshin storms Enishi's mansion. In their duel he lets Enishi stab him and apologizes. When Woo Heishin fires at Kenshin, Enishi shields Kaoru and takes a bullet. Arrested, Enishi reads Tomoe's diary and understands that she gave her life to stop Kenshin from killing; Kenshin bids farewell to Tomoe at her grave.

Released in Japan by Warner Bros. Pictures Japan on April 23, 2021, and later internationally on Netflix, the film had the year's biggest opening weekend for a live-action film despite pandemic closures and grossed about 4.34 billion yen. Reviews were positive, praising its fight sequences and its conclusion to Kenshin's story.

documents.title: Inheritance
documents.overview: The patriarch of a wealthy and powerful family suddenly passes away, leaving his wife and daughter with a shocking secret inheritance that threatens to unravel and destroy their lives.
documents.plot:
Inheritance is a 2020 American thriller film directed by Vaughn Stein and written by Matthew Kennedy. It stars Lily Collins, Simon Pegg, Connie Nielsen, Chace Crawford and Patrick Warburton, and centers on the dark secret left behind when the patriarch of a wealthy and powerful family dies suddenly. Collins joined the cast in early 2019, replacing Kate Mara, and filming took place in Birmingham, Alabama.

After the sudden death of Archer Monroe, the patriarch of a powerful political family, his estate is divided among his wife, Catherine; his son, William, a politician running for reelection; and his daughter, Lauren, the Manhattan District Attorney. The family lawyer, Harold Thewlis, gives Lauren a private message from her father revealing a secret and directing her to an underground bunker on the family estate. Inside, she finds a man chained to the wall who calls himself Morgan Warner.

Morgan tells Lauren that he was Archer's friend and business partner, and that years ago the two of them, driving drunk, killed a pedestrian. To protect his career, Archer imprisoned Morgan rather than risk exposure, and over the years he used his captive as a confessor. Morgan's information leads Lauren to the victim's body, to Archer's longtime mistress and illegitimate son, and to evidence that Archer paid bribes to help his children win public office. Convinced, Lauren frees Morgan and has Harold arrange an offshore account and a private jet so he can disappear. But when his fingerprints are identified, Catherine recognizes the man in the photographs as Carson, calling him evil. Lauren discovers that his flight never left and that Harold has been murdered. At the house, Carson has taken Catherine to the bunker. He overpowers Lauren and reveals that 30 years earlier he drugged and raped Catherine; Archer had been taking him away to kill him when they struck the pedestrian, and imprisoned him instead. Archer died from the poison he had meant for Carson. As they fight, Carson claims to be Lauren's father, before Catherine shoots him dead. The women set the bunker on fire and leave.

Planned to premiere at the Tribeca Film Festival before its postponement due to COVID-19, the film was released on DirecTV Cinema on April 23, 2020, and by Vertical Entertainment on May 22. It received negative reviews, with 25% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 31.

documents.title: The Forever Purge
documents.overview: All the rules are broken as a sect of lawless marauders decides that the annual Purge does not stop at daybreak and instead should never end as they chase a group of immigrants who they want to punish because of their harsh historical past.
documents.plot:
The Forever Purge is a 2021 American horror film directed by Everardo Gout and written by Rafe Judkins. It is the fifth installment in The Purge franchise, which is based on the concept of James Wan's 2007 film The Conjuring.

The movie takes place four years after the events of The Forever Purge: Eternal Summer (2021). The story begins with a flashback to the aftermath of the previous purge, where we see the aftermath of the violence and destruction caused by the masked figures known as the "Purged." We also meet our protagonist, Naya (played by Ana de la Reguera), who is struggling to cope with the trauma she experienced during the previous purge.

The story then shifts to the present day, where we are introduced to a new family, the Garcias, who are preparing for their own home invasion. The family consists of parents, Alejandro and Marisol (played by Tenoch Huerta and Eva Longoria), and their two children, Carlos and Sofia (played by Jorge Lendeborg Jr. and Angélica Celaya). They are unaware that the government has announced a new policy: if you survive four purges, you will be granted immunity from future invasions.

As the family prepares for their own home invasion, they begin to realize that something is off. The Purged seem more organized and ruthless than ever before, and the Garcias soon find themselves trapped in their own home with no escape. As the night wears on, the family must fight for survival against the increasingly violent and relentless Purged.

Throughout the movie, we see flashbacks of Naya's past experiences during the previous purges, which serve as a reminder of the trauma that the characters are facing. We also see glimpses of the government's true intentions behind the new policy: they want to create a class system where those who survive multiple purges become the ruling elite.

As the night reaches its climax, the Garcias must confront their own demons and work together to take down the Purged. In a shocking twist, we discover that Naya is actually one of the leaders of the Purged, and she has been manipulating events from behind the scenes.

The movie ends with a sense of hopelessness and despair, as the Garcias are forced to confront the reality of their situation. The final shot is of Naya, standing alone in the darkness, her mask still on, as we realize that the cycle of violence and trauma will continue forever.

Overall, The Forever Purge is a thought-provoking and intense horror film that explores themes of class, privilege, and the cyclical nature of violence. With its strong performances, clever plot twists, and atmospheric tension, it's a must-see for fans of the franchise and horror enthusiasts alike.

documents.title: Harry & Meghan: Becoming Royal
documents.overview: The continuing love story of newlyweds Prince Harry and American actress Meghan Markle during their first year of marriage.
documents.plot:
Harry & Meghan: Becoming Royal is a 2019 American biographical romance television film that dramatizes the royal wedding of Prince Harry and Meghan Markle and the couple's first year of marriage. Directed by Menhaj Huda from a screenplay by Scarlett Lacey and executive produced by Merideth Finn and Michele Weiss, it was made for Lifetime as a sequel to Harry & Meghan: A Royal Romance (2018), whose leads were recast. Charlie Field plays Prince Harry and Tiffany Smith, in her first leading role, plays Meghan, with Charles Shaughnessy as Prince Charles, Deborah Ramsay as Camilla, Jordan Whalen as Prince William, Bonnie Soper as Diana, Clare Filipow as Stella, Marlie Collins as Annabella and James Dreyfus as Sir Leonard Briggs.

The film opens as Meghan shoots her final wedding scene on the legal drama Suits before moving to London, where Harry welcomes her to Kensington Palace with a homemade banner and champagne. As the wedding approaches, she struggles with royal protocol and a hostile press, embodied by a fictional morning show, Good Day UK, and its racist co-host. She attends her first royal Christmas, plans the guest list, supports victims of the Grenfell Tower fire and argues with palace staff over her white gown and tiara. When her father, Thomas Markle, is exposed for staging paparazzi photographs and then withdraws from the ceremony, Charles and Camilla reassure her, and Charles offers to escort her for part of the walk down the aisle. After the wedding the duchess promotes a charity cookbook created with women from a community kitchen formed after the fire, realizes she is pregnant as Harry gives her a puppy, and decides she will no longer suppress her own style, discarding the pantyhose palace aides expect her to wear. The film ends with a real photograph of the couple holding their newborn baby.

Lifetime announced the project in February 2019, and the film premiered on Memorial Day, 27 May 2019. It was followed by Harry & Meghan: Escaping the Palace. Reception was divided. Newsweek reported that viewers were split over the new cast and the gossip-driven plot, though Entertainment Tonight's Philiana Ng praised Smith's performance. Vanity Fair's Julie Miller described it as a budget-conscious attempt to theorize about what happened behind palace doors, and a recap by Martha Sorren and Lia Beck complained that the film skipped the wedding itself in favor of the cookbook storyline.

documents.title: The Little Things
documents.tagline: Some things never let us go.
documents.overview: Deputy Sheriff Joe "Deke" Deacon joins forces with Sgt. Jim Baxter to search for a serial killer who's terrorizing Los Angeles. As they track the culprit, Baxter is unaware that the investigation is dredging up echoes of Deke's past, uncovering disturbing secrets that could threaten more than his case.
documents.plot:
The Little Things is a crime thriller film directed by John Lee Hancock, released in 2021 by Warner Bros. Pictures. The movie stars Denzel Washington, Jared Leto, and Robert Forster.

The story begins with Joe Deacon (Denzel Washington), a detective from the Los Angeles Police Department who has just been transferred to the LAPD's Homicide Division after serving as a homicide detective in New Orleans for 20 years. Joe is struggling to adjust to his new surroundings and feeling disconnected from his colleagues.

The plot takes a turn when Joe meets Detective Jim Baxter (Jared Leto), a young and ambitious cop who is eager to prove himself. The two are tasked with solving the gruesome murder of a young woman, which has left the community shaken. As they delve deeper into the case, they discover that the victim was a sex worker who had been brutally murdered.

As Joe and Jim begin their investigation, they uncover a complex web of clues that lead them to suspect a serial killer. The killer is targeting women who are involved in prostitution, and the victims all have one thing in common: they were all seen with a man named Russell Ellis (Robert Forster) on the night of their murder.

Joe becomes increasingly obsessed with catching the killer, but his obsession also starts to affect his personal life. He begins to question his own morality and the true nature of justice. Meanwhile, Jim is struggling to balance his desire for success with his growing feelings for a woman named Wendy (Rami Malek's character was removed from the movie).

As the investigation unfolds, Joe and Jim discover that Russell Ellis is not just any ordinary man. He has a dark past and a twisted obsession with women who work in prostitution. The killer's motives are revealed to be rooted in a deep-seated hatred for women who engage in sex work.

The film builds up to a tense and suspenseful climax as Joe and Jim close in on the killer. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Russell Ellis was not the mastermind behind the murders, but rather a pawn in a larger game. The true culprit is revealed to be a woman who had been using Russell's identity to carry out her own twisted crimes.

The movie ends with Joe finally bringing justice to the victims and their families, but not before he has to confront his own demons and the true nature of evil. The film raises questions about morality, justice, and the complexities of human behavior.

Overall, The Little Things is a gripping and thought-provoking thriller that explores the darker side of human nature. With outstanding performances from Denzel Washington and Jared Leto, the movie delivers a tense and suspenseful ride that will keep viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end.

documents.title: Lego DC Batman: Family Matters
documents.overview: Suspicion is on high after Batman, Batgirl, Robin and other DC superheroes receive mysterious invitations. However, family values must remain strong when Batman and his team encounter the villainous Red Hood, who is obsessed with destroying the Bat-family and all of Gotham City.
documents.plot:
Lego DC Batman: Family Matters is an animated film that explores the complexities of family dynamics and relationships through the lens of the iconic superhero, Batman. The movie delves into the idea of what it means to be a good parent and how one's actions can have far-reaching consequences on those they care about.

At its core, the film is a heartwarming exploration of the importance of family bonds and the sacrifices that must be made for the greater good. Batman's struggles to balance his duties as a crime-fighter with his responsibilities as a father are expertly woven throughout the narrative, adding depth and nuance to the character.

The movie also touches on themes of identity and self-discovery, particularly in the context of Bruce Wayne's dual life as Batman and his role as a father. As he navigates the challenges of being a superhero and a parent, Bruce must confront the consequences of his choices and learn to prioritize what truly matters.

Furthermore, Lego DC Batman: Family Matters features a richly developed cast of characters, each with their own distinct personalities and motivations. The film's portrayal of these characters adds richness and depth to the narrative, making it easy for audiences to become invested in their stories and relationships.

Overall, the main themes of Lego DC Batman: Family Matters revolve around the complexities of family dynamics, the importance of self-sacrifice, and the challenges of balancing personal and professional responsibilities.

documents.title: Horizon Line
documents.overview: A couple flying on a small plane to attend a tropical island wedding must fight for their lives after their pilot suffers a heart attack.
documents.plot:
Horizon Line is a 2020 English-language Swedish adventure thriller film directed by Mikael Marcimain. Allison Williams stars as Sara Johnson and Alexander Dreymon as her former boyfriend Jackson Davisen, who must fight to survive aboard a small GippsAero GA8 Airvan over the Indian Ocean after their pilot, Freddy Wyman, played by Keith David, dies of a heart attack. Pearl Mackie appears as Pascale and Jumayn Hunter as the air traffic controller Samuel. With a budget of 200 million Swedish kronor, about US$22 million, it was among the most expensive Swedish films at the time, and it was shot in Mauritius, Dublin and at Pinewood Studios.

A year after slipping away from Jackson at an island bar without saying goodbye, Sara travels from London to Mauritius for a friend's wedding. There she spends the night with Jackson, misses the last boat to the wedding venue on Rodrigues and catches a ride on a small plane flown by her friend Freddy, only to discover that Jackson has booked the same flight. While Jackson sleeps, Freddy lets Sara take the co-pilot's seat, but he suffers a fatal heart attack and the plane plunges. The two regain control, yet with the autopilot damaged, Sara, who has learned a few basics from Freddy, must fly the aircraft. Reaching Samuel by radio, they try to follow his guidance but must first pass through a storm, which damages their compass, and the plane starts losing fuel rapidly. Jackson climbs outside to patch a fuel line, succeeding but badly breaking his arm. To save fuel they jettison weight, including Freddy's body, and Sara climbs out of the window to pour bottles of rum into the tank as makeshift fuel. When the radio falls silent and the fuel runs out, they glide toward a small island, but the plane crashes into the sea and flips over, and Sara frees the trapped Jackson before both swim ashore. The island proves to be a sandbar that soon vanishes beneath the rising tide. As they tread water, Jackson offers Sara his life vest, but she refuses, saying they are a team, and he declares his love for her just as a fishing boat that heard their radio calls arrives to rescue them.

SF Studios released Horizon Line in Swedish cinemas on 6 November 2020, and STXfilms released it on video on demand in the United States on 12 January 2021. It grossed about $916,000 internationally. It holds a 40% Rotten Tomatoes rating from a handful of reviews, with critics praising its pacing but finding it preposterous.

documents.title: Spiral: From the Book of Saw
documents.original_title: Spiral: From the Book of Saw
documents.overview: Working in the shadow of an esteemed police veteran, brash Detective Ezekiel “Zeke” Banks and his rookie partner take charge of a grisly investigation into murders that are eerily reminiscent of the city’s gruesome past.  Unwittingly entrapped in a deepening mystery, Zeke finds himself at the center of the killer’s morbid game.
documents.plot:
Spiral: From the Book of Saw is a 2021 American supernatural thriller film directed by Darren Lynn Bousman, written by Josh Stolberg and Peter Goldfinger, and produced by Lionsgate. The film serves as a sequel to the Saw franchise.

The story begins with Detective Ezekiel "Zeke" Banks (Chris Rock), a tough and seasoned detective from New York City, who is investigating a series of gruesome murders that seem to be connected to an old case from his past. As Zeke delves deeper into the investigation, he discovers that the murders are linked to Jigsaw's (Tobin Bell) legacy.

Zeke soon finds himself in the midst of a deadly game, where he must navigate through a series of puzzles and traps set by Jigsaw's successor, a mysterious figure known as "The Conductor" (Max Hogan). The Conductor is revealed to be a former apprentice of Jigsaw who has taken up his mantle and continues his twisted games.

As Zeke navigates the deadly game, he meets Amanda Young (Samantha Sloyan), a young woman with a troubled past who was once an apprentice of Jigsaw. Amanda becomes a key player in the game, as she is forced to confront her own dark past and the consequences of her actions.

Throughout the film, Zeke must use his wits and resourcefulness to survive the deadly traps and puzzles set by The Conductor. Along the way, he uncovers clues that suggest Jigsaw's legacy lives on through Amanda, who has become a complex and conflicted character in her own right.

As the game reaches its climax, Zeke discovers that The Conductor is actually a former cop who was obsessed with Jigsaw's philosophy and saw him as a twisted genius. The Conductor believes that by continuing Jigsaw's games, he can bring about a new era of enlightenment and self-discovery for humanity.

In the end, Zeke manages to outsmart The Conductor and escape the deadly game, but not before Amanda is forced to confront her own demons and make a choice between redemption and further descent into darkness. The film ends with a sense of closure for Zeke, but also raises questions about the legacy of Jigsaw's twisted games and whether they can ever be truly escaped.

Overall, Spiral: From the Book of Saw is a tense and thrilling ride that explores the darker themes of the Saw franchise while introducing new characters and plot twists. The film's use of puzzles and traps is clever and inventive, making for a fun and suspenseful viewing experience.
production_companies: Canadian Film or Video Production Tax Credit (CPTC)

documents.title: The Silencing
documents.overview: A reformed hunter becomes involved in a deadly game of cat and mouse when he and the local sheriff set out to track a vicious killer who may have kidnapped his daughter years ago.
documents.plot:
The Silencing is a 2020 action thriller directed by Robin Pront from a screenplay by Micah Ranum. It stars Nikolaj Coster-Waldau and Annabelle Wallis, with Hero Fiennes Tiffin, Zahn McClarnon and Melanie Scrofano in supporting roles. Saban Films released it through DirecTV Cinema in July 2020, followed by a theatrical and video-on-demand release in August 2020.

Coster-Waldau plays Rayburn Swanson, a former hunter and recovering alcoholic who now runs a wildlife sanctuary in the forests of northern Minnesota. He named it after his daughter Gwen, who disapproved of his trapping and who vanished five years earlier from his car while he stepped into a store to buy whiskey. The sanctuary is his form of penance, and he patrols it with surveillance cameras to keep hunters away. Wallis plays Alice Gustafson, the local sheriff, who also has to deal with her volatile younger brother Brooks.

When the body of a young girl is found near a lake, Alice notices a distinctive scar on the victim's throat and recovers the head of a spear from a nearby tree, a projectile launched with an atlatl, an ancient throwing device. Rayburn rushes to view the body, fearing it is Gwen, but it is not. Soon afterwards he spots a figure in a ghillie suit moving through the woods and is wounded by a thrown spear when he tries to intervene. Reviewing his camera footage, he discovers that the masked hunter has been using the sanctuary to stalk and kill abducted girls. He rescues one survivor, Molly, who has been left mute by the same throat injury, and the case draws him and Alice together as the investigation points closer to people they know.

The story becomes a cat-and-mouse thriller in the wilderness, in which Rayburn's tracking skills are pitted against a killer who knows the terrain just as well, while Alice wrestles with suspicions that touch her own family. The film combines a serial-killer mystery with a portrait of a grieving father who refuses to give up on finding his child.

Reviews were largely negative. On Rotten Tomatoes the film holds an approval rating of about 20 percent, with the consensus arguing that it mistakes mood for character development and delivers an undercooked mystery, although some critics praised Coster-Waldau's committed lead performance and the bleak, wintry atmosphere.

documents.title: Stars at Noon
documents.tagline: A sumptuous tale of romance and espionage.
documents.overview: In present-day Nicaragua, a headstrong American journalist and a mysterious English businessman strike up a romance as they become embroiled in a dangerous labyrinth of lies and conspiracies and are forced to try and escape the country.
documents.plot:
Stars at Noon is a 2022 film that explores the complexities of human relationships and the blurred lines between love, desire, and exploitation in a patriarchal society. The movie delves into the intricate dynamics of power and control, particularly in the context of colonialism and imperialism.

The story revolves around two characters, Hana and Jake, who form an intense connection in a small town in Africa. As their relationship deepens, it becomes increasingly complicated by the power imbalance between them, with Jake holding significant economic and social influence over Hana. The film raises questions about consent, agency, and the ways in which societal structures can both enable and constrain individual freedom.

Through its portrayal of this complex relationship, Stars at Noon critiques the ways in which colonialism and imperialism have shaped the lives of women in Africa, often leaving them vulnerable to exploitation and oppression. The movie also touches on themes of identity, culture, and belonging, highlighting the tensions that arise when individuals from different backgrounds and social classes interact.

Ultimately, Stars at Noon presents a nuanced and thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, one that challenges viewers to confront their own assumptions about power, desire, and relationships.

documents.title: The Hating Game
documents.tagline: He's the one she loves to hate.
documents.overview: Resolving to achieve professional success without compromising her ethics, Lucy embarks on a ruthless game of one-upmanship against cold and efficient nemesis Joshua, a rivalry that is complicated by her growing attraction to him.
documents.plot:
The Hating Game is a 2021 American romantic comedy directed by Peter Hutchings and adapted from Sally Thorne's 2016 novel. Lucy Hale and Austin Stowell star as two rival executive assistants at a publishing company, with Yasha Jackson, Sakina Jaffrey and Corbin Bernsen in supporting roles. Vertical Entertainment released it in limited cinemas and on video on demand on December 10, 2021.

After two publishing houses merge, Lucy Hutton and Joshua Templeman share an office as assistants to the company's two co-CEOs. They are opposites in every way. Lucy, who studied literature, is warm and accommodating, while Josh, a Harvard MBA, is cold, methodical and responsible for cutting a large share of the staff. Each loathes the other, and they wage a constant war of petty games, with Lucy disturbing the precise order of Josh's desk and Josh mocking her as a pushover. When a new senior position opens up, both apply and agree that whoever loses will resign.

Their rivalry reveals how closely they watch each other. After a vivid dream about Josh, Lucy wears a revealing dress to the office, and when he teases her about a supposed hot date, she invents one with the friendly colleague Danny. Leaving work, their bickering turns into a passionate kiss in the lift. Josh later sends flowers, which Lucy mistakes for Danny's. When she falls ill with a fever at a paintball team-building day, Josh takes her home and brings his doctor brother Patrick to treat her, and she offers to be his date at Patrick's wedding.

Their relationship deepens as Josh speaks of his strained ties with his parents, both doctors, who never forgave him for leaving medical school. At the wedding, held at an overbooked inn where they must share a room, they sleep together, and Lucy learns that the bride, Mindy, once left Josh for his brother. She defends Josh when his father belittles his career. Back home, Josh tells her he loves her and wants a real relationship. But Lucy overhears part of a conversation and wrongly concludes that he has used her to win the job. She throws herself into the final presentation and wins the promotion, only to discover that Josh has already accepted a better job elsewhere, and the two finally get together.

Reviews were generally positive, with 68% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, critics praising the chemistry between Hale and Stowell.

documents.title: John Wick: Chapter 4
documents.tagline: No way back, one way out.
documents.overview: With the price on his head ever increasing, John Wick uncovers a path to defeating The High Table. But before he can earn his freedom, Wick must face off against a new enemy with powerful alliances across the globe and forces that turn old friends into foes.
documents.plot:
John Wick: Chapter 4 is a 2023 American neo-noir action thriller directed by Chad Stahelski and written by Shay Hatten and Michael Finch, the fourth installment in the John Wick series and the sequel to Chapter 3 – Parabellum. Keanu Reeves returns as the legendary assassin John Wick, joined by Donnie Yen as Caine, Bill Skarsgård as the Marquis Vincent Bisset de Gramont, Laurence Fishburne as the Bowery King, Hiroyuki Sanada as Shimazu Koji, Shamier Anderson as Mr. Nobody, Rina Sawayama as Akira, Scott Adkins as Killa, Clancy Brown as the Harbinger, Lance Reddick as Charon and Ian McShane as Winston.

Recovering underground with the Bowery King after being shot off the roof of the Continental by Winston, John strikes back at the High Table by traveling to Morocco and killing the Elder, the one who sits above the Table. In response, the High Table gives the Marquis de Gramont unlimited resources to eliminate him. The Marquis strips Winston of his position, destroys the New York Continental, and coerces John's old friend Caine, a blind, retired assassin, into hunting him by threatening Caine's daughter.

John seeks shelter at the Osaka Continental run by his friend Koji, but the hotel is overrun by High Table enforcers, and a massive battle ensues in which Koji is killed by Caine, while a mercenary tracker known as Mr. Nobody waits for the bounty to rise. Back in New York, Winston suggests a way out: under an old High Table tradition, John can challenge the Marquis to a duel, which would free him from all obligations if he wins. To do so, John must first be readmitted to the Ruska Roma crime family in Berlin, a task that requires killing the brutal High Table member Killa. The duel is set for sunrise at the Sacré-Cœur in Paris, and as the Marquis puts a huge bounty on him, John must battle his way across the city to arrive on time.
