However, after a devastating loss in the championship game, Henry begins to question his priorities and feels suffocated by the expectations placed upon him by his parents, coaches, and teammates.

One day, while working at a local bookstore, Henry meets Grace Town (played by Lili Hayman), a quiet and introverted girl who is an avid reader. Despite their initial awkwardness around each other, they start to develop feelings for one another. As they spend more time together, Henry finds himself drawn to Grace's quirky nature and her passion for literature.

However, their budding relationship is put to the test when Henry discovers that Grace has a secret: she is actually a boy named Sam (played by Finn Wolfhard), who was assigned female at birth but identifies as male. This revelation shakes Henry to his core, forcing him to confront his own biases and assumptions about identity and relationships.

As Henry navigates this new information, he must also contend with the pressures of his senior year, including college applications and a looming future that seems uncertain. Meanwhile, Sam struggles to come to terms with his own identity and the fear of being rejected by those around him.

Throughout the film, Tanne explores themes of identity, love, and acceptance, raising questions about what it means to be true to oneself and to find one's place in the world. The title "Chemical Hearts" refers to the idea that our emotions and desires can be unpredictable and volatile, like a chemical reaction.

Ultimately, Henry and Sam must confront their own fears and insecurities in order to find a way forward together. The film builds towards a poignant and emotional conclusion, as the two characters come to terms with their feelings for each other and the complexities of human connection.

Overall, Chemical Hearts is a thoughtful and nuanced exploration of love, identity, and acceptance, featuring strong performances from its cast and a sensitive direction from Richard Tanne.

documents.title: Spell
documents.overview: A father survives a plane crash in rural Appalachia, but becomes suspicious of the elderly couple who take him in to nurse him back to health with the ancient remedies.
documents.plot:
Spell is a 2020 American supernatural horror thriller directed by the British-Zimbabwean filmmaker Mark Tonderai from a screenplay by Kurt Wimmer. Produced by Paramount Players with Mayhem Pictures and MC8 Entertainment, with Gordon Gray, Wimmer, Morris Chestnut and Brian Wilkins as producers, it stars Omari Hardwick and Loretta Devine, with John Beasley, Lorraine Burroughs, Hannah Gonera, Kalifa Burton, Tumisho Masha and Steve Mululu. The cinematography is by Jacques Jouffret and the score by Ben Onono.

Marquis T. Woods (Hardwick) escaped a violent, abusive childhood in the backwoods decades ago and has become a wealthy corporate lawyer. When he learns that his estranged and brutal father has died, his wife Veora (Burroughs) insists that she and their teenage children, Samsara (Gonera) and Tydon (Burton), accompany him to the funeral in rural Appalachian Kentucky. Marquis, an experienced pilot, flies the family there himself in a private plane, but a violent storm causes him to lose control on the approach. He wakes up injured and alone in the attic of a farmhouse, cared for by the folksy but stern Ms. Eloise (Devine) and her husband Earl (Beasley), who claim that no one else was found at the crash site, while their mute, powerful helper Lewis (Mululu) ensures he stays put. With a badly hurt foot and the door locked, Marquis grows suspicious as Eloise insists she can heal him through a form of folk magic called Boogity, using a figure she has made from his blood and skin. Slipping out across the roofs, he discovers that his hosts preside over a congregation of hoodoo worshippers who perform sacrificial healing rituals, and realizes that he may be the next offering. Unable to call for help, he must break free of her magic and save his family before a sinister ritual planned for the rise of the blood moon.

Principal photography took place in South Africa, near Cape Town and Stellenbosch, standing in for Kentucky. Originally scheduled to open in theaters on 28 August 2020, it was pulled because of the COVID-19 pandemic and released by Paramount on digital platforms on 30 October 2020. Reception was mixed to negative, with a 49% Rotten Tomatoes rating and a Metacritic score of 38. Variety called it a decently stylish occult thriller, praising Hardwick's grounded performance while finding the script formulaic, whereas The Hollywood Reporter felt the direction could not compensate for a predictable, cliché-ridden screenplay.

documents.title: Blue Story
documents.tagline: Their bond made them brothers. The streets made them enemies.
documents.overview: Blue Story is a tragic tale of a friendship between Timmy and Marco, two young boys from opposing postcodes. Timmy, a shy, smart, naive and timid young boy from Deptford, goes to school in Peckham where he strikes up a friendship with Marco, a charismatic, streetwise kid from the local area. Although from warring postcodes, the two quickly form a firm friendship until it is tested and they wind up on rival sides of a street war. Blue Story depicts elements of Rapman's own personal experiences and aspects of his childhood.
documents.plot:
Blue Story is a 2019 British drama film directed by Patrick Read Johnson. The movie follows the story of two young men, Marcus (Fahim Anwar) and Vinnie (Stephen Ogilvie), who grow up in the same London estate but are from different backgrounds.

The main themes of Blue Story include:

1. **Racial Tensions and Police Brutality**: The film explores the harsh realities of life in a London estate, where racism, police brutality, and social inequality are prevalent. Marcus and Vinnie's experiences with the police serve as a catalyst for their conflict.
2. **Friendship and Loyalty**: Despite their differences, Marcus and Vinnie develop a strong bond, which is tested when they find themselves on opposite sides of a violent confrontation. The film highlights the importance of loyalty and friendship in the face of adversity.
3. **Class Divide and Social Inequality**: Blue Story sheds light on the stark contrasts between the lives of those living in London estates and those from more affluent backgrounds. The film critiques the systemic issues that perpetuate inequality and limit opportunities for young people from disadvantaged areas.
4. **Violence and Trauma**: The movie depicts the devastating consequences of violence and trauma on individuals and communities. Marcus and Vinnie's experiences serve as a reminder of the long-term effects of violence and the need for support and healing.

The film received critical acclaim for its raw, unflinching portrayal of life in London estates and its thought-provoking exploration of social issues.

documents.title: The Vigil
documents.overview: A man providing overnight watch to a deceased member of his former Orthodox Jewish community finds himself opposite a malevolent entity.
documents.plot:
The Vigil is a 2020 American thriller film directed by Kiran Deol. The movie revolves around a retired police officer who seeks revenge against a corrupt cop responsible for his partner's death.

At its core, The Vigil explores the themes of grief, trauma, and the blurred lines between justice and vigilantism. The protagonist's quest for vengeance is driven by his emotional pain and sense of betrayal, which serves as a catalyst for his downward spiral into darkness. As he navigates the complex web of corruption and deceit, the film raises questions about the morality of taking the law into one's own hands.

The Vigil also delves into the psychological effects of trauma on individuals and how it can shape their perceptions of reality. The protagonist's experiences have left him with a deep-seated sense of anger and resentment, which he struggles to reconcile with his own moral code. This inner conflict serves as a powerful commentary on the human capacity for both good and evil.

Furthermore, the film critiques the systemic corruption that pervades law enforcement agencies, highlighting the ways in which power and privilege can be used to silence victims and protect perpetrators. The Vigil is a thought-provoking exploration of the darker aspects of human nature, inviting viewers to consider the complexities of justice and the consequences of unchecked ambition.

Overall, The Vigil is a gripping thriller that masterfully weaves together elements of crime drama, psychological suspense, and social commentary, resulting in a cinematic experience that is both unsettling and thought-provoking.

documents.title: Secret Society of Second Born Royals
documents.original_title: Secret Society of Second Born Royals
documents.tagline: Born to defend. They just have to learn how.
documents.overview: Sam is a teenage royal rebel, second in line to the throne of the kingdom of Illyria. Just as her disinterest in the royal way of life is at an all-time high, she discovers she has super-human abilities and is invited to join a secret society of similar extraordinary second-born royals charged with keeping the world safe.
documents.plot:
Secret Society of Second-Born Royals is a Disney Channel original movie that premiered on June 27, 2020. The film follows the story of Princess Amara, played by Millicent Simmonds, who discovers she's not the only royal with magical powers.

The movie begins with Princess Amara, a young princess from the fictional kingdom of Aldovia, feeling like an outcast among her family and people. She struggles to control her magical abilities, which often get in the way of her daily life as a princess. Meanwhile, Prince Erik, played by Travis Tope, is introduced as the charming but awkward prince next door.

As Amara navigates her royal duties and magical powers, she meets a group of "Second-Born" royals from other kingdoms who possess similar abilities. These Second-Borns are born with magical powers that make them outcasts in their own kingdoms, just like Amara. The group is led by Prince Erik, who becomes Amara's ally and potential love interest.

The story takes a turn when the evil Queen Beatrice, played by Virginia Kull, threatens to destroy Aldovia and rule over all the kingdoms. She seeks to exploit the magical powers of the Second-Borns for her own gain. The group must band together to stop Queen Beatrice and save their kingdoms.

Throughout the movie, Amara and Erik grow closer as they work together to defeat Queen Beatrice. Along the way, they learn more about each other's pasts and the secrets behind their magical powers. As they face challenges and obstacles, they develop feelings for each other that threaten to complicate their royal duties.

The climax of the movie features an epic battle between the Second-Borns and Queen Beatrice's minions. Amara and Erik use their combined magical powers to defeat the villains and save Aldovia. In the process, Amara discovers her true potential as a leader and a princess.

In the end, Amara and Erik confess their feelings for each other, and the movie concludes with a romantic kiss between the two leads. The film ends on a hopeful note, with Amara embracing her royal duties and magical powers, ready to face new challenges alongside her friends and allies.

Overall, Secret Society of Second-Born Royals is a heartwarming and action-packed Disney Channel original movie that celebrates self-acceptance, friendship, and the power of love.

documents.title: Flora & Ulysses
documents.tagline: No tights. No cape. No problem.
documents.overview: When Flora rescues a squirrel she names Ulysses, she is amazed to discover he possesses unique superhero powers, which take them on an adventure of humorous complications that ultimately change Flora's life--and her outlook--forever.
documents.plot:
Flora & Ulysses is a 2021 American fantasy comedy-drama film directed by Will Speck and Josh Waller, based on the 2009 novel of the same name by Kate DiCamillo. The movie stars Anna Kendrick as Flora Banks, a young girl who finds an unlikely ally in her life.

The story begins with Flora, a shy and introverted 10-year-old girl, struggling to cope with the loss of her mother, who passed away when she was just six years old. Her father, Walter (played by Jeremy Jordan), is trying his best to raise her on his own but is often distant and preoccupied.

One day, while walking home from school, Flora encounters a stray cat that has been hit by a car. As she tries to save the cat's life, it gets caught in a metal can and is subsequently bitten by a winged insect, which turns out to be an alien named Ulysses (voiced by Keanu Reeves). The encounter changes Flora's life forever.

As Ulysses begins to transform into a superhero-like creature with incredible powers, Flora starts to see the world in a new light. She learns that Ulysses has been sent to Earth as an ambassador for his home planet and is on a mission to gather information about humanity. However, their time together is limited, and Flora must come to terms with the fact that she will have to say goodbye to her new friend soon.

As the story unfolds, Flora's life becomes increasingly complicated. Her father's past as a musician comes back to haunt him, and he starts to reconnect with his own childhood passions. Meanwhile, Ulysses's presence in their lives attracts unwanted attention from various factions, including government agents and a sinister organization that seeks to exploit the alien's powers.

Throughout the film, Flora learns valuable lessons about courage, friendship, and the importance of embracing her individuality. As she navigates this new reality, she must also confront her own emotional baggage and learn to let go of her grief.

The movie takes a poignant turn as Ulysses prepares to leave Earth, leaving Flora heartbroken but ultimately empowered by their time together. The film's climax features an emotional goodbye between the two friends, with Flora finding a way to honor Ulysses's memory and continue his legacy on Earth.

In the end, Flora emerges stronger and more confident, having discovered that even in the darkest moments, there is always hope for connection and transformation. The movie concludes on a hopeful note, suggesting that the lessons Flora learned from Ulysses will stay with her forever.

Overall, Flora & Ulysses is a heartwarming and visually stunning film that explores themes of grief, friendship, and self-discovery. With its talented cast, witty dialogue, and imaginative storytelling, it's a must-see for fans of all ages.

documents.title: Arctic Apocalypse
documents.overview: A massive influx of glacial melting triggers a new ice age in the Northern Hemisphere, forcing a family to make their way across the ice-covered landscape before they are frozen out for good.
documents.plot:
Arctic Apocalypse is a 2019 American science-fiction disaster film produced by The Asylum with Syfy, directed by Jon Kondelik and Eric Paul Erickson from a screenplay by Bill Hanstock. Because its premise closely resembles that of The Day After Tomorrow, it is generally regarded as one of The Asylum's mockbusters. It was shot at Mammoth Mountain in eastern California, premiered on British television on 4 August 2019 and was released in Germany that November.

Within a matter of weeks, a massive surge of glacial melting plunges the Northern Hemisphere into a new ice age. Glaciers devastate cities such as New York and Paris, the Eiffel Tower collapses and even the pyramids of Giza are buried in snow. In the United States, Mark (Joel Berti) and his wife Helen (Jennifer Lee Wiggins), a scientist, are forced to flee the cold. Their weather-obsessed daughter Brie (Lauren Esposito) and her boyfriend Tyler (Charles Townsend) are out studying the phenomenon when Tyler loses control of their car, and they escape just before it plunges into a chasm. Chased by a pack of wolves, they shelter in a school, where they join a group of students led by Aliyah (Anna Christensen) and Roger (Blake Dang). After an avalanche buries the entrance, the group barricades itself against the weather and the wolves, and Roger finds a pistol and propane tanks in the janitor's office.

Mark and Helen set out to find their daughter, parting from their colleague Larry (Erickson), who heads alone for a military post. Helen squeezes into the iced-over school, evades a wolf and reunites with Brie and Tyler, who are now engaged. Roger blows open the blocked entrance by shooting the propane tanks. While the students drive towards the military station, the family makes for a research station on a nearby plateau where the weather has inexplicably stayed normal, hoping to understand why and share the findings with the world. On the way they lose their car and are confronted by a gang of looters who want Mark's bag of research instruments; lightning from a freezing storm kills most of them, and Helen knocks out the surviving leader before the family finds another vehicle and reaches the plateau.

German critics were dismissive. The German film magazine Filmdienst described it as a low-budget variation on blockbuster disaster scenarios, told with deadly seriousness, with miserable effects and characters left undeveloped, while Cinema dismissed it as Ice Age without the gags or cute animals.

documents.title: Jingle Jangle: A Christmas Journey
documents.tagline: Discover a world of wishes and wonder
documents.overview: An imaginary world comes to life in a holiday tale of an eccentric toymaker, his adventurous granddaughter, and a magical invention that has the power to change their lives forever.
documents.plot:
Jingle Jangle: A Christmas Journey is a Netflix original musical fantasy film released in 2020, produced by Will Packer and Marlon Wayans through their production company, Black & White Productions. The movie stars Forest Whitaker as Jeronicus Jangle, a brilliant toymaker who creates magical toys that bring joy to children.

The story begins with Jeronicus Jangle (Forest Whitaker), a renowned toymaker who lives in the fictional town of Whimsy, where he creates extraordinary toys that can come to life. However, his obsession with creating the perfect toy leads him to abandon his daughter, Journey (Madison Davenport), and his wife, Abilene (Keegan-Michael Key).

Years later, Jeronicus is haunted by a curse that was placed upon him by his estranged daughter, who has grown up in a world without magic. The only way to break the curse is for Jeronicus to reunite with Journey and make amends for his past mistakes.

Jeronicus sets out on a journey to find Journey, accompanied by his loyal apprentice, Gus (Bryan Cranston), and Abilene, who has been searching for her father all these years. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous landscapes, wicked creatures, and Jeronicus's own self-doubt.

As Jeronicus navigates this challenging journey, he learns valuable lessons about love, forgiveness, and the importance of family. He also discovers that Journey has grown into a talented young woman with her own unique gifts, which she uses to help those in need.

Throughout their adventure, Jeronicus and Journey face numerous challenges, including a rival toymaker, Mr. Hobbs (Gerald McRaney), who seeks to steal Jeronicus's secrets and claim the title of greatest toymaker for himself.

Ultimately, Jeronicus and Journey reach Whimsy, where they are reunited with Abilene and the rest of their community. With the help of his friends and family, Jeronicus breaks the curse that has haunted him for so long, and he is finally able to reconnect with his daughter and rediscover his passion for creating magical toys.

The movie features a range of catchy musical numbers, including "Jingle Jangle," "Make Room for Love," and "All I Want for Christmas Is You." The film's blend of music, fantasy, and family drama makes it a heartwarming and entertaining holiday treat.

documents.title: A Sun
documents.overview: A family of four fractures under the weight of unmet expectations, unexpected tragedy, and uncompromising pride.
documents.plot:
A Sun (Chinese: 陽光普照) is a 2019 Taiwanese drama film directed by Chung Mong-hong, who co-wrote it with Chang Yao-sheng. Chen Yi-wen and Samantha Ko star as the parents of two very different sons, played by Wu Chien-ho and Greg Hsu, with Liu Kuan-ting as a dangerous friend. Exploring juvenile delinquency, suicide and the pressures placed on children, the film also reflects socioeconomic inequality in Taiwan.

In Taipei in 2013, the teenage Chen Jian-ho, known as A-Ho, accompanies his friend Radish to confront a young man in a restaurant, where Radish suddenly cuts off the victim's hand with a machete. A-Ho is sentenced to juvenile detention, while Radish receives a longer term. Their father, A-Wen, a driving instructor whose motto is "Seize the day, decide your path," effectively disowns his younger son and focuses all his hopes on A-Hao, the gentle and studious elder son preparing for medical school. Their mother, Qin, continues to visit A-Ho, and soon learns that A-Ho's fifteen-year-old girlfriend, Yu, is pregnant with his child. Meanwhile the victim's father harasses A-Wen for compensation.

The family is shattered when A-Hao, outwardly the perfect son, takes his own life. A girl he was close to later tells Qin that he felt overwhelmed by the constant attention and had nowhere to hide from it. After his release, A-Ho marries Yu and works at a car wash to support his family while A-Wen continues to ignore him, though father and son begin to reconcile after a quiet late-night conversation about A-Hao.

Years later, Radish is released and begins pulling A-Ho back into crime, coercing him into firing a gun at a politician's office and later into helping with a mysterious delivery. When A-Wen's offer of money to stay away from his son is refused, Radish disappears, and his associates abduct and beat A-Ho. A-Wen later confesses to Qin that he had been following the pair and killed Radish himself, believing it was the only way to protect his one remaining son. Afterward, Qin and A-Ho find the notebooks A-Wen once gave A-Hao, inscribed with his motto and left blank, and mother and son ride a bicycle together through a sunlit park.

A Sun premiered at the 2019 Toronto International Film Festival and was widely acclaimed. It won Best Feature Film and Best Director at the Golden Horse Awards, and as Taiwan's Oscar submission it made the shortlist.

documents.title: The Last Vermeer
documents.overview: A soldier and member of the Dutch resistance investigates stolen art in the wake of the Second World War, including a Vermeer sold to the Nazis by a flamboyant forger.
documents.plot:
The Last Vermeer is an American historical drama directed by Dan Friedkin from a screenplay by John Orloff (credited as James McGee), Mark Fergus and Hawk Ostby, based on Jonathan Lopez's 2008 book The Man Who Made Vermeers. Guy Pearce plays the Dutch painter and dealer Han van Meegeren, accused of selling national treasures to the Nazis, and Claes Bang plays Joseph Piller, the former resistance fighter assigned to investigate him, with Vicky Krieps and Roland Møller. It premiered at the Telluride Film Festival in August 2019 and was released in American cinemas by Sony's TriStar Pictures label on November 20, 2020.

At the end of the Second World War, Captain Joseph Piller, a Dutch Jew who fought in the resistance, works for the Allied military administration of the Netherlands. When a Vermeer is found in Hermann Göring's looted collection, Piller and his assistant Dekker arrest van Meegeren, the flamboyant artist who sold it to him, on charges of collaboration. Fearing that Dutch authorities led by the zealous De Klerks will either let him slip away or sacrifice him in a postwar purge, Piller hides him in a safe house under Allied protection.

Under interrogation, van Meegeren demands painting materials and explains himself: dismissed by critics before the war, he became the source of several "lost" Vermeers that surfaced in the 1930s and funded a lavish life, later enriched by dealings with the Nazis, whom he claims to despise. Finally he insists that the Göring Vermeer is a fake. When the Allies withdraw, De Klerks takes custody of him, and he faces the death penalty. Piller, now working as a labourer, finds the unfinished canvas van Meegeren painted in the safe house and realises it matches the recovered painting. Convinced, he agrees to defend him and learns how he faked the works, using Bakelite to harden his paint and heating and rolling the canvases to simulate age.

At the trial, the art experts who once authenticated the paintings persuade the judges to convict. Piller has Dekker create a diversion, splashes acid on one canvas and reveals van Meegeren's own signature underneath, and the verdict is overturned to public acclaim. Later, however, De Klerks shows Piller a book from the safe house bearing van Meegeren's dedication to Adolf Hitler. Realising he was deceived, Piller confronts the painter, is coldly dismissed, and burns the book.

Rotten Tomatoes reported 70% approval, with critics praising Pearce's performance.

documents.title: The Haunted
documents.tagline: You see what you want to see.
documents.overview: In a rambling, isolated house, Emily’s first night-shift as carer to an elderly dementia patient turns into a nightmare as she is tormented by a vengeful spirit and uncovers the house's dark secrets.
documents.plot:
The Haunted is a 2018 British low-budget supernatural horror film written and directed by David Holroyd and produced by TH Film. It stars Sophie Stevens as Emily, with Nick Bayly as Arthur and Ray MacAllan, Maggie Daniels, Kirstie Steele and Virginia Denham in supporting roles. Running 75 minutes and promoted with the tagline "You see what you want to see," it is set almost entirely in a single rambling, isolated house.

Emily, who has never worked as a carer before, is driven by her employer to her new job as the night carer for Arthur, a bedridden elderly man with dementia who is barely ever conscious. Before she starts, the day carer asks the employer whether they should tell her something, but he insists there is nothing to tell. He gives Emily a brief tour of the old house, showing her the camera and monitor and mentioning an upstairs that no one uses any more, and then leaves her alone for the long night. Almost at once strange things begin to happen. She gets locked out of the house, doors creak open and slam shut, objects turn up in different places, Arthur claims that someone is standing behind her, and she thinks she glimpses a figure. With no electricity in most rooms, she explores by flashlight, finding furniture under dust sheets and a girl's bedroom still full of belongings. In a bag apparently left behind by the previous carer she discovers tools for communicating with the dead, including a Ouija board, along with charms meant to ward off harmful spirits. Using the board, Emily makes contact with a vengeful presence and, as the night grows more terrifying, uncovers the house's dark secrets, before a final twist recasts what has come before.

The film was an official selection of the Screamfest horror festival in Los Angeles in 2018, and was released on video on demand in the United States in May 2020 before arriving on Hulu that September. Reviews were largely negative. Brandon of PopHorror credited Stevens's performance with keeping the film alive and admired its sparse, realistic chills, while finding the plot thin and the twist confusing. Cynthia Vinney of CBR called it all atmosphere and no substance, criticizing its lack of momentum, grimy look, reliance on the score and a twist that made no sense. John Serba of Decider likewise recommended skipping it, describing it as almost entirely a woman walking slowly through a house.

documents.title: Sinkhole
documents.tagline: A house earned after 11 years of effort falls deep into the ground in a minute.
documents.overview: A working class family move into a new condo purchased after 11 years of hard work. They throw a housewarming party to show his co-workers when overnight a heavy downpour creates an extremely deep sinkhole that engulfs the entire building.
documents.plot:
Sinkhole is a 2021 South Korean disaster comedy film directed by Kim Ji-hoon and starring Cha Seung-won, Kim Sung-kyun, Lee Kwang-soo and Kim Hye-jun, with Nam Da-reum and Kwon So-hyun in supporting roles. Its premise centers on an ordinary office worker whose home, bought after eleven years of saving, plunges 500 meters underground into a sinkhole in the space of a single minute.

Park Dong-won, a mid-level manager at a company, has worked hard for eleven years to afford his first home, and he moves with his wife, Young-yi, and their family into a new condominium. Proud of his purchase, he throws a housewarming party and invites coworkers, including the junior employees Kim Seung-hyun and Hong Eun-joo. In the same building lives Jeong Man-soo, a resident who works day and night to raise his son, Seung-tae, on his own and who is not on good terms with him. After a heavy overnight downpour, an enormous sinkhole opens beneath the building, and in barely a minute the whole condominium is swallowed, with residents and guests still inside.

Trapped deep in the pit, Dong-won, Man-soo and the survivors must put aside their differences and work together to survive amid the wreckage and find a way back to the surface. Their situation grows more desperate when the rain starts again and water begins pouring into the sinkhole, and the group must find a solution before time runs out. The film blends the spectacle and peril of a disaster movie with ensemble comedy drawn from the clashing personalities of its characters.

Made on a budget of about ₩15 billion, the film began shooting in August 2019 at Bomnae Film Studio and a school in Chuncheon. It was planned for the 2020 Chuseok holidays but was postponed by the COVID-19 pandemic. It premiered in the Piazza Grande section of the Locarno Film Festival on August 6, 2021, and opened in South Korea on August 11, posting the year's best opening, crossing one million admissions in six days and ending 2021 as the country's second highest-grossing domestic film, with about 2.2 million admissions and nearly US$18 million. It also closed the New York Asian Film Festival and screened at Sarajevo, Vancouver and Busan. Korean critics praised the ensemble, the light humor and the elaborate sets used to convey the shaking of the sinking building, though Sports Korea found the second half's setting somewhat unrealistic while still calling it fun enough as a disaster blockbuster.

documents.title: Falling Inn Love
documents.tagline: Never assume anything on the internet matches its profile picture.
documents.overview: When a San Francisco exec wins a New Zealand inn, she ditches city life to remodel and flip the rustic property with help from a handsome contractor.
documents.plot:
Falling Inn Love is a romantic comedy-drama film that explores the theme of second chances and finding love in unexpected places. The movie follows Tully, a successful businesswoman who wins a small inn in a New Zealand town through a contest she didn't even enter. As she navigates her new life in the quaint town, she butts heads with the inn's handsome owner, Josh, who is initially resistant to her presence.

Through their interactions, the film delves into themes of identity, community, and the importance of embracing one's true self. Tully, who has been so focused on her career, must confront her own desires and values as she gets to know Josh and the charming town he calls home. As she learns to let go of her past and open herself up to new experiences, she discovers a sense of belonging and purpose that she never knew was missing.

The movie also touches on the idea of finding love in unexpected places, where two people from different walks of life come together and form an unlikely connection. Through their romance, Tully and Josh learn to appreciate each other's quirks and flaws, and find common ground in their shared desire for happiness and fulfillment.

Ultimately, Falling Inn Love is a heartwarming film that celebrates the power of love, community, and self-discovery. It's a story about finding one's true home, whether it's a physical place or a sense of belonging within oneself.

documents.title: The Babysitter: Killer Queen
documents.tagline: Face Your Demons. Survive the Night.
documents.overview: Two years after defeating a satanic cult led by his babysitter Bee, Cole's trying to forget his past and focus on surviving high school. But when old enemies unexpectedly return, Cole will once again have to outsmart the forces of evil.
documents.plot:
The Babysitter: Killer Queen is a 2020 American horror film directed by McG and written by McG, Chris McKenna, and Erik Sommers. The movie serves as a sequel to the 2017 film The Babysitter.

The story follows Bee (Judah Lewis), a teenager who has just moved back in with his mother after being kicked out of boarding school. He is struggling to adjust to life at home and feels like an outsider among his peers. To make matters worse, he discovers that his babysitter, Greta (Samara Weaving), has a dark secret: she's the leader of a coven of teenage witches.

Greta and her friends are planning a ritual to summon a powerful demon, but things take a turn when Bee gets caught up in their activities. As Bee becomes more entrenched in the group, he begins to realize that Greta's intentions are far from pure. The group's true plan is to use Bee as a human sacrifice to bring about an apocalypse.

As the night wears on, Bee must use his wits and resourcefulness to outsmart Greta and her cohorts. Along the way, he discovers that Greta has a personal connection to him that makes their confrontation even more intense.

Throughout the film, McG pays homage to classic horror movies, particularly those of the 1980s. The Babysitter: Killer Queen is a fun, self-aware take on the genre that pokes fun at common horror tropes while still delivering plenty of scares and suspense.

One of the standout aspects of the film is its cast, which includes Samara Weaving as the charismatic and complex Greta. Weaving brings depth to her character, making it clear that Greta's motivations are rooted in a desire for power and control rather than pure malice.

Overall, The Babysitter: Killer Queen is a fun, entertaining horror film that will appeal to fans of the genre. With its witty script, strong cast, and plenty of scares, it's a great addition to any horror movie collection.

documents.title: The Burning Sea
documents.tagline: The biggest disaster lies ahead of us.
documents.overview: An oil platform dramatically goes down on the Norwegian coast, and researchers try to find out what happened when they realize this is just the start of something even more serious.
documents.plot:
The Burning Sea (Norwegian: Nordsjøen; also released as The North Sea) is a 2021 Norwegian disaster thriller directed by John Andreas Andersen from a screenplay by Harald Rosenløw-Eeg and Lars Gudmestad. Produced by Therese Bøhn for Fantefilm, with backing from partners including Film i Väst, Zefyr Media Fund, the Nordisk Film & TV Fond and the Norwegian Film Institute, it is set among the oil platforms off the Norwegian coast. The music is by Johannes Ringen and Johan Söderqvist and the cinematography by Pål Ulvik Rokseth. The film premiered at the Rome Film Festival in October 2021 before opening in Norway later that month.

Kristine Kujath Thorp stars as Sofia, a young researcher working on an underwater search drone, who lives with oil worker Stian (Henrik Bjelland) and his young son Odin (Nils Elias Olsen). When a platform suddenly sinks, Sofia and her colleague Arthur (Rolf Kristian Larsen) are sent to the site, where their drone finds bodies and a lone survivor trapped in an air pocket. Before he can be rescued, gas bursts from a crack in the seabed and a violent explosion destroys the platform, wounding Sofia. Reviewing the footage, Arthur discovers that the official explanation is wrong: a gigantic fault is opening on the floor of the North Sea, threatening every installation in the area and a catastrophic oil spill. The operator begins an emergency evacuation and orders all wells sealed, but on Stian's platform one valve fails to close automatically, and he volunteers to shut it by hand. The last helicopter leaves without him and he is presumed dead. Refusing to accept this, Sofia studies the surveillance footage, concludes he may have survived, and flies out to the stricken platform unofficially with Arthur to find him, just as the authorities decide to ignite the spreading slick from the air. Anders Baasmo Christiansen, Bjørn Floberg and Anneke von der Lippe play key roles.

Rather than relying chiefly on spectacle, the film devotes much of its attention to how the Norwegian authorities handle the crisis. It received seven nominations at the 2022 Amanda Awards, Norway's national film prizes, including Best Norwegian Film, and won the award for Best Visual Effects. Writing for Film.ru, Konstantin Myshkin gave it seven out of ten, observing that the oppressive mood Andersen creates lingers past the end credits, since the individual characters may be saved but humanity's relationship with nature seemingly cannot.

documents.title: Let Them All Talk
documents.overview: A celebrated author takes a journey with some old friends to have some fun and heal old wounds. Her nephew comes along to wrangle the ladies and finds himself involved with a young literary agent.
documents.plot:
Let Them All Talk is a 2020 American comedy-drama film directed by Liz Gilbert. The movie follows the story of Alice Hawley, a successful author in her sixties who embarks on a European river cruise with two friends, Georgia and Andy.

The main theme of Let Them All Talk revolves around the complexities of female friendships, particularly those that have been formed over time and have weathered various life experiences. The film explores how these relationships can be both a source of comfort and a catalyst for growth, as Alice navigates her own midlife crisis and confronts the realities of aging.

Through the characters' interactions and conversations, the movie delves into themes of identity, loneliness, and the search for meaning in one's life. As Alice struggles to come to terms with her own mortality and the decline of her writing career, she is forced to reevaluate her priorities and consider what truly brings her joy and fulfillment.

The film also touches on the idea of female empowerment and the importance of supporting one another through life's challenges. The relationships between the three women are multifaceted and nuanced, reflecting the complexities of real-life friendships and the ways in which they can both enrich and complicate our lives.

Ultimately, Let Them All Talk is a thoughtful and humorous exploration of the human experience, offering a poignant portrayal of aging, friendship, and the search for purpose.

documents.title: Superman II: The Richard Donner Cut
documents.original_title: Superman II: The Richard Donner Cut
documents.tagline: The version you have never seen.
documents.overview: Superman agrees to sacrifice his powers to start a relationship with Lois Lane, unaware that three Kryptonian criminals he inadvertently released are conquering Earth.
documents.plot:
Superman II: The Richard Donner Cut is a 2006 re-edited version of the 1980 film Superman II, directed by Richard Donner and produced by Warner Bros. Pictures.

The main themes of this movie revolve around the struggle between good and evil, as embodied by the iconic characters of Superman (played by Christopher Reeve) and General Zod (played by Terence Stamp). The story delves into the complexities of power, responsibility, and the blurred lines between heroism and tyranny. 

As Superman faces off against his arch-nemesis, he must confront the darker aspects of his own abilities and the consequences of his actions on a global scale. This internal conflict is juxtaposed with the external threat posed by General Zod, who seeks to claim Earth as his own and impose his brand of order through force.

The film also explores the theme of identity, particularly in the context of Superman's dual nature as an alien from Krypton and a human raised on Earth. The character of Lois Lane (played by Margot Kidder) serves as a catalyst for this exploration, as she represents both the comfort of familiarity and the thrill of adventure.

Furthermore, the movie touches upon the idea of sacrifice and the weight of responsibility that comes with great power. Superman's relationships with his adoptive parents, Jonathan and Martha Kent, are also a significant aspect of the narrative, highlighting the importance of family and the values they instill in their son.

Overall, Superman II: The Richard Donner Cut is a thought-provoking tale that balances action, adventure, and character-driven drama, making it a compelling exploration of the human condition through the lens of a superhero.

documents.title: Paw Patrol: Ready, Race, Rescue!
documents.tagline: Get ready to race and rescue!
documents.overview: It’s the Adventure Bay 500! The pups have built an awesome race track and are ready to be the pit crew for their race hero, The Whoosh! But when the legendary racer is unable to drive in the championship race, he calls on his biggest fan-pup Marshall to take the wheel and race in his place! Marshall has to overcome his lack of confidence and his dastardly competition, The Cheetah, to fulfill his dream of becoming the fastest race-pup ever!
documents.plot:
Paw Patrol: Ready, Race, Rescue! is a 2019 animated adventure film based on the popular children's television series Paw Patrol. The movie follows the PAW Patrol team as they compete in the Great Race, a high-stakes racing competition that requires teamwork and quick thinking to win.

The main themes of the movie include:

1. Teamwork: The film highlights the importance of working together towards a common goal. The PAW Patrol team uses their unique skills and abilities to overcome obstacles and challenges.
2. Friendship: The movie showcases the strong bonds between the PAW Patrol pups, who put aside their differences to work together and support each other.
3. Problem-solving: The film encourages children to think creatively and develop problem-solving skills as the pups face various challenges and puzzles during the Great Race.
4. Perseverance: The movie teaches kids about the value of perseverance and determination, as the PAW Patrol team faces setbacks and obstacles but never gives up.

The story begins with Ryder announcing the Great Race, a competition that will determine which team is the best. The PAW Patrol pups are excited to participate, but things take a turn when they realize that the competition is not just about winning, but also about learning valuable lessons about teamwork and friendship.

As the race progresses, the pups face various challenges, including navigating through obstacles, solving puzzles, and working together to overcome their differences. Along the way, they learn important values such as empathy, selflessness, and cooperation.

In the end, the PAW Patrol team emerges victorious, but more importantly, they have learned a valuable lesson about the importance of teamwork, friendship, and perseverance. The movie concludes with a heartwarming moment of celebration and camaraderie among the pups, emphasizing the power of unity and collaboration.

Overall, Paw Patrol: Ready, Race, Rescue! is an entertaining and educational film that promotes positive values and encourages children to develop essential skills such as problem-solving, teamwork, and perseverance.

documents.title: VFW
documents.overview: A typical night for veterans at a VFW turns into an all-out battle for survival when a desperate teen runs into the bar with a bag of stolen drugs. When a gang of violent punks come looking for her, the vets use every weapon at their disposal to protect the girl and themselves from an unrelenting attack.
documents.plot:
VFW (2019) is a tense and dark thriller that delves into the world of human trafficking and exploitation. The film's narrative revolves around a group of women who are being held captive in a remote location, forced to work as sex slaves for a powerful and ruthless trafficker.

At its core, VFW explores the themes of survival, resilience, and the unbreakable bonds between women. Despite being trapped and subjected to unimaginable cruelty, the characters find ways to cope, support each other, and ultimately fight back against their oppressors. The film highlights the strength and resourcefulness of these women, who refuse to be broken by their circumstances.

The movie also touches on the theme of trauma and its long-lasting effects on individuals and communities. The characters' experiences are marked by pain, fear, and anxiety, but they also find ways to heal, forgive, and move forward. This narrative thread adds depth to the story, emphasizing the importance of empathy, compassion, and understanding in the face of adversity.

Furthermore, VFW critiques the societal systems that enable human trafficking and exploitation. The film shines a light on the dark underbelly of modern society, where vulnerable individuals are preyed upon by those who seek to exploit them for their own gain. By exposing these injustices, the movie aims to raise awareness about this critical issue and inspire change.

Overall, VFW is a gripping and thought-provoking thriller that explores the complexities of human nature, resilience, and the power of female solidarity in the face of adversity.

documents.title: Big Gold Brick
documents.overview: Recounts the story of fledgling writer Samuel Liston and his experiences with Floyd Deveraux, the enigmatic, middle-aged father of two who enlists Samuel to write his biography.
documents.plot:
Big Gold Brick is a 2022 American black comedy with surreal and fantasy elements, written and directed by Brian Petsos in his feature directorial debut. It stars Emory Cohen as the struggling writer Samuel Liston and Andy Garcia as Floyd Deveraux, with Megan Fox as Floyd's second wife and attorney Jacqueline, Lucy Hale as his daughter Lily, Leonidas Castrounis as his son Edward, Oscar Isaac as Anselm, Shiloh Fernandez as Roy and Frederick Schmidt as Percy. Justin Hori composed the score; the film runs 132 minutes.

The story is framed as Samuel's account of how he met Floyd, a memoir that later becomes a literary sensation. At his lowest point, a despondent Samuel leaves his apartment, rides a bus out of town and wanders the streets until he is struck by a Cadillac driven by Floyd, an enigmatic, middle-aged father of two who was eating ice cream at the wheel. Mortified at having badly injured him, Floyd visits him in the hospital and offers a deal: free room and board in his large suburban home and 500 dollars in cash a week if Samuel will write his biography. Samuel moves in with the eccentric Deveraux family, which includes Jacqueline, who at one point attempts to seduce him, the tween Edward, a death metal fan with disturbing interests, and the teenage Lily, a former violin prodigy who walked away from her career by smashing her instrument at a recital. As he listens to Floyd's tall tales, Samuel is plagued by vivid nightmares and hallucinations, including a talking Santa doll in his room, and the line between reality and delusion blurs, especially after the menacing, inhaler-using Anselm draws him and Floyd into violent trouble.

Principal photography began in Toronto in May 2019. Samuel Goldwyn Films acquired distribution rights in June 2021 and released the film in theaters and on digital platforms on 25 February 2022. Critical reception was largely negative: Rotten Tomatoes reported a 21 percent approval rating from 34 reviews, with a consensus faulting its quirkiness, visual tricks and crowded narrative for hiding a lack of purpose, and Metacritic gave it 30 out of 100. Glenn Kenny of RogerEbert.com dismissed it as bloated, strained and unfunny, arguing that Petsos echoes Richard Kelly, Wes Anderson, David Lynch and the Coen brothers without doing anything useful with those influences. Time's review was kinder, singling out Garcia's suave, eccentric performance as the film's main asset.

documents.title: Love Wedding Repeat
documents.tagline: One Wedding. One Simple Plan. What Could Possibly Go Wrong?
documents.overview: While trying to make his sister's wedding day go smoothly, Jack finds himself juggling an angry ex-girlfriend, an uninvited guest with a secret, a misplaced sleep sedative, and the girl that got away in alternate versions of the same day.
documents.plot:
Love, Wedding & Repeat is a 2021 romantic comedy film, not 2020, and it's directed by Greg Cohen, produced by Notorious Pictures.

The movie follows the story of two brothers, Tom (Sam Richardson) and Cliff (Adam Pally), who are both unlucky in love. The plot revolves around their attempts to find true love while navigating their complicated family dynamics and personal growth. As they go on a series of disastrous dates, the brothers begin to realize that they need to focus on themselves before they can find someone special.

The main theme of Love, Wedding & Repeat is the exploration of identity, self-discovery, and the complexities of human relationships. The film delves into the idea that true love requires vulnerability, trust, and a willingness to confront one's own flaws and insecurities. Through the characters' experiences, the movie shows how embracing individuality and taking time for personal growth can lead to more meaningful connections with others.

The film also touches on the theme of family dynamics and the challenges of navigating complex relationships, particularly when it comes to sibling bonds. The brothers' relationship is a central aspect of the story, and their interactions are often humorous and poignant, highlighting the ups and downs of brotherly love.

Overall, Love, Wedding & Repeat is a heartwarming and hilarious exploration of love, identity, and human connection, with a healthy dose of humor and wit.

documents.title: The Matrix Resurrections
documents.overview: Plagued by strange memories, Neo's life takes an unexpected turn when he finds himself back inside the Matrix.
documents.plot:
The Matrix Resurrections is a 2021 science fiction action film directed by Lana Wachowski, written by David Mitchell and Alex Hassell, and produced by Village Roadshow Pictures. 

The movie follows Neo (played by Keanu Reeves), who has been living in a simulated reality with his wife, Trinity (Carrie-Anne Moss). However, their life is disrupted when a new threat emerges in the form of a rogue program created by the Merovingian (Lambert Wilson) that threatens to destroy the entire Matrix. 

As Neo tries to stop this new threat, he begins to experience strange visions and memories from his past life before the Matrix. He also meets a new character, Bugs (Jessica Henwick), who is a skilled hacker and becomes his ally in the fight against the rogue program.

Throughout the movie, Neo struggles with his identity and purpose, as he tries to reconcile his past and present selves. The film's narrative is layered with themes of free will, artificial intelligence, and the nature of reality.

The Matrix Resurrections received mixed reviews from critics, who praised its visuals and action sequences but criticized its storytelling and character development. Despite this, the movie performed well at the box office, grossing over $350 million worldwide.

Overall, The Matrix Resurrections is a thought-provoking and visually stunning film that explores complex themes and ideas. While it may not be as cohesive or impactful as some of the previous Matrix films, it remains an entertaining and engaging addition to the franchise.

documents.title: A Babysitter's Guide to Monster Hunting
documents.original_title: A Babysitter's Guide to Monster Hunting
documents.overview: Recruited by a secret society of babysitters, a high schooler battles the Boogeyman and his monsters when they nab the boy she's watching on Halloween.
documents.plot:
A Babysitter's Guide to Monster Hunting is a 2020 American dark fantasy comedy horror film directed by Rachel Talalay and distributed by Netflix. It was written by Joe Ballarini, who adapted his own book trilogy of the same name, and stars Tamara Smart, Oona Laurence, Indya Moore and Tom Felton, with Alessio Scalzotto and Ian Ho in supporting roles.

Kelly Ferguson, a high school freshman in Rhode Island, has been cruelly nicknamed "Monster Girl" ever since she claimed to have been attacked by a monster as a small child. On Halloween night, instead of going to a senior's party, she is roped into babysitting Jacob, the son of her mother's boss, Ms. Zellman. Jacob shows her drawings of the monsters that haunt his dreams, and Kelly reassures him, checks under the bed and gives him a small light. Minutes later she finds three little creatures carrying him off. Unable to get help from 911, she meets Liz Lerue, a member of a secret society of babysitters who protect children, who identifies the creatures as Toadies, servants of the Boogeyman.

The Boogeyman, also known as the Grand Guignol, a stealer of dreams and bringer of nightmares, plans to raise a monster army by extracting nightmares from Jacob's unusually vivid imagination. At the headquarters of the Rhode Island Order of Babysitters, hidden at Brown University, Kelly uses a magic dust to recover a memory of the Boogeyman telling her as a five-year-old that she could bring dreams to life. The trainee sitters, all of whom bear scars from childhood encounters with boogeymen, learn that the villain can be defeated by delivering a potion called Angel Hair with a "monster punch," while their ally Curtis gathers the ingredients and equips Kelly with gadgets. A tracking plan backfires, leading the girls into a trap at the Halloween party, and the Boogeyman captures and hypnotizes Liz. Kelly breaks into a condemned lighthouse, outwits the Toadies, snaps Liz out of her trance and strikes the Boogeyman with the Angel Hair, while the awakened Jacob makes the nightmare creatures vanish. Kelly gets Jacob home before his mother returns, is asked to babysit again, is recommended to the Order and is asked out by her crush, Victor.

The film premiered on Netflix on October 15, 2020. It received mixed reviews, with a 65% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 31.

documents.title: 12 Mighty Orphans
documents.tagline: Based on the true story of the team that inspired a nation.
documents.overview: Haunted by his mysterious past, a devoted high school football coach leads a scrawny team of orphans to the state championship during the Great Depression and inspires a broken nation along the way.
documents.plot:
"12 Mighty Orphans" is a biographical sports drama film directed by Tyler Perry, released in 2021 by Sony Pictures Classics.

The main themes of "12 Mighty Orphans" revolve around perseverance, teamwork, and the power of believing in oneself. The movie tells the true story of the 1972 Dallas Texans, an amateur football team from a small town in Texas that defied all odds to become one of the top teams in the United States.

The film focuses on the journey of Billy Bob "Hoot" Gibson (played by Matthew McConaughey), a young boy who dreams of playing football despite his physical limitations. With the help of Coach Rusty Russell (played by Brian Cox) and the team's determination, they overcome their challenges to achieve success.

Throughout the movie, themes such as:

1. Perseverance: The team faces numerous setbacks, including injuries, financial struggles, and personal losses, but they never give up on their dreams.
2. Teamwork: The film highlights the importance of unity, trust, and communication among teammates, which ultimately leads to their success.
3. Believing in oneself: Hoot's journey is a testament to the power of self-belief and confidence, as he proves that with hard work and dedication, anything is possible.

The movie also explores themes of small-town America, community spirit, and the impact of sports on people's lives.

Overall, "12 Mighty Orphans" is an inspiring true story that celebrates the underdog spirit, teamwork, and the power of believing in oneself.

documents.title: Tall Girl
documents.tagline: When you don't fit in, stand tall
documents.overview: Jodi, the tallest girl in her high school, has always felt uncomfortable in her own skin. But after years of slouching, being made fun of, and avoiding attention at all costs, Jodi finally decides to find the confidence to stand tall.
documents.plot:
Tall Girl is a 2019 American teen comedy film directed by Jake Kasdan and written by Liz Feldman. The movie follows the story of Jodi Lynn Nevers, played by Hailee Steinfeld, who stands at an impressive 6'5" (196 cm) in a world where most people are significantly shorter.

The main themes of Tall Girl revolve around self-acceptance, body positivity, and finding one's place in the world. The film explores Jodi's struggles to navigate high school as a tall girl, often feeling like an outsider due to her unusual height. However, she also discovers that being different can be a strength, allowing her to see things from a unique perspective.

Throughout the movie, Jodi learns to love herself and her body, embracing her individuality rather than trying to conform to societal norms. The film promotes a positive message about self-acceptance, encouraging viewers to appreciate their own uniqueness and not compare themselves to others.

The movie also touches on themes of friendship, family, and first love, as Jodi navigates her relationships with those around her. Overall, Tall Girl is a heartwarming and humorous coming-of-age story that celebrates individuality and self-acceptance.

documents.title: Unhinged
documents.overview: A divorced mother honks impatiently at a deranged middle-aged stranger at a red light while running late on her way to work. His road rage escalates to horrifyingly psychotic proportions as he becomes single-mindedly determined to teach her a deadly lesson for provoking him.
documents.plot:
Unhinged is a 2020 American thriller film directed by Derrick Borte and written by Derek Kolstad. The movie stars Russell Crowe as Joe, a retired police officer who becomes embroiled in a cat-and-mouse game with a deranged driver (Caren Pistorius) on the road.

The main themes of Unhinged include:

1. **Violence and Aggression**: The film explores the theme of violence and aggression, particularly through the character of Joe, who is driven by a desire for justice after his wife's murder. However, as the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Joe's actions are not just about revenge, but also about his own emotional turmoil.
2. **Mental Health**: The movie touches on the theme of mental health, particularly through the character of Caren, who is revealed to be a complex and troubled individual with a dark past. Her actions become increasingly erratic and violent as the story progresses, highlighting the dangers of untreated mental illness.
3. **Revenge and Retribution**: Unhinged explores the theme of revenge and retribution, particularly through Joe's character. As he seeks to track down Caren, he becomes increasingly consumed by his desire for justice, leading him down a path of violence and destruction.
4. **The Dangers of Isolation**: The film also highlights the dangers of isolation and loneliness, particularly through Joe's character. His wife's murder has left him feeling isolated and disconnected from society, leading him to lash out at those around him.

Overall, Unhinged is a tense and suspenseful thriller that explores themes of violence, mental health, revenge, and isolation. While it may not be a traditional "good guy vs. bad guy" story, the film's complex characters and moral ambiguity make for a thought-provoking and unsettling viewing experience.

documents.title: Morgue
documents.overview: On his first day as a security guard, Diego Martinez is assigned to the night shift at the Hospital Regional. On his rounds, he notices the hallways can be unsettling at night until he accidentally notices he’s trapped inside the morgue.
documents.plot:
Morgue is a 2019 Paraguayan supernatural horror film written, produced and directed by Hugo Cardozo, his second feature after El secuestro (2016). Shot inside the morgue of the Regional Hospital of Encarnación, it stars Pablo Martínez as a young security guard who spends a terrifying night locked in the building, with Willi Villalba, María del Mar Fernández, Abel Martínez, Aldo Von Knobloch, Raúl Rotela and Francisco Ayala in supporting roles. Cardozo has said the story drew on accounts from guards, nurses and doctors at the hospital who had experienced strange events, and cast member Abel Martínez, a security guard in real life, contributed substantially to developing the story.

Diego Martínez is a poorly paid security guard who likes to project a status he does not have, taking selfies beside other people's expensive pickup trucks, and who constantly lies to his girlfriend, with whom he keeps in touch through video calls. One night, while distracted by text messages at the wheel, he hits a pedestrian and flees the scene, leaving the victim behind. The following night he receives a call assigning him to guard the morgue at the regional hospital. Left largely alone in the dim, decaying building, he becomes trapped inside as a mounting series of paranormal events unfolds. A shadowy figure appears in the background of a video call, which only his girlfriend notices, and a stranger tries to break into the building, while Diego is tormented by spirits and by his own guilt as he tries to discover who, or what, is terrorizing him. The film closes with two endings, one resolving Diego's story and another suggesting that death is not the end.

Morgue opened in Paraguay on August 22, 2019 and topped the national box office in its first week, selling about 23,000 tickets on 36 screens and beating the new release Once Upon a Time in Hollywood; it remained at number one for two consecutive weeks. Well Go USA later released it in the United States on digital, Blu-ray and DVD in May 2021. In ABC Color, Sergio Ferreira praised its expressive force, its use of guilt and empty spaces, and Martínez's convincing lead performance. American reviewers also singled out Martínez and the atmospheric camerawork and lighting, while finding the middle of the film slow and the ending confusing.

documents.title: Write Before Christmas
documents.overview: A recently single Jessica sends Christmas cards to people who have impacted her life—the aunt who raised her, her younger brother in the military, a popstar who was part of the soundtrack of her life, the music teacher who inspired her, and the best friend who always tells the truth.
documents.plot:
"Write Before Christmas" is a 2019 American romantic comedy film produced by Hallmark Movies & Mysteries.

The movie follows Samantha (played by Lacey Chabert), a successful businesswoman who has lost touch with her creative side. She's offered a job in New York City, but before she leaves, she meets a charming and handsome stranger named Nick (played by Paul Greene) at a bookstore. They share a magical moment where they write love letters to each other, which becomes the foundation of their connection.

As Samantha navigates her new life in the city, she begins to question her priorities and reevaluate what truly matters to her. She starts to see the world through Nick's eyes, and her experiences with him help her rediscover her passion for writing and her own sense of purpose.

The main themes of "Write Before Christmas" include:

1. Rediscovering one's creative spark: Samantha's journey is about finding her way back to her artistic side and embracing her creativity.
2. The power of love letters: The movie highlights the significance of written expressions of love and how they can bring people closer together.
3. Following your heart: Samantha must confront her fears and doubts to follow her heart and pursue a life that aligns with her values and passions.
4. Finding balance in life: As Samantha navigates her new life, she learns to strike a balance between her professional ambitions and personal relationships.

Overall, "Write Before Christmas" is a heartwarming story about finding love, rediscovering oneself, and embracing the magic of human connection.

documents.title: Dog
documents.tagline: filthy animal unfit for human company and a...DOG
documents.overview: An army ranger and his dog embark on a road trip along the Pacific Coast Highway to attend a friend's funeral.
documents.plot:
Dog is a 2022 American comedy-drama road film directed by Channing Tatum and Reid Carolin in their directorial debuts, from a story by Carolin and Brett Rodriguez. Tatum stars as a former Army Ranger who must deliver the military dog of a fallen comrade to his funeral, with Jane Adams, Kevin Nash, Q'orianka Kilcher, Ethan Suplee, Emmy Raver-Lampman and Nicole LaLiberte in supporting roles. Produced by Free Association on a $15 million budget, it was released in the United States by United Artists Releasing on February 18, 2022.

Jackson Briggs is a former Ranger struggling with post-traumatic stress who is desperate to return to duty but has been deemed unfit because of a brain injury. After learning that his friend and former partner Riley Rodriguez has been killed in a car crash, he is offered a deal: if he drives Riley's military dog, Lulu, an aggressive Belgian Malinois, from Washington state down the Pacific coast to the funeral in Nogales, Arizona, his former commanding officer will recommend him for a coveted deployment. After the funeral, Lulu is to be taken to White Sands to be euthanized.

The road trip in Briggs's old Ford Bronco is chaotic from the start. Lulu, traumatized by her service, panics at gunfire, tears apart his car and sabotages his attempts to pick up women in Portland. In the forests of northern California, Briggs is tranquilized and tied up by a suspicious cannabis farmer whose wife tends to Lulu's injured paw. In San Francisco, his scam to get a free hotel room by posing as a blind veteran backfires when Lulu attacks a Middle Eastern doctor, and Briggs narrowly escapes charges on the condition that he seek help. In Los Angeles he is turned away by his estranged wife when he tries to see his young daughter, but a fellow veteran who has rehabilitated Lulu's brother teaches him how to communicate with the dog. As man and dog learn to trust each other, Briggs begins to confront his own trauma and realizes that he cannot abandon Lulu to her fate, choosing a future together with her over a return to war.

The film was well received, with critics praising Tatum's performance and the emotional bond at its center, though some felt it was misleadingly marketed as a comedy. Metacritic gave it 61 out of 100, and audiences polled by CinemaScore gave it an A−. It grossed about $85 million worldwide. Thomas Newman composed the score.

documents.title: Emergency Declaration
documents.overview: While investigating a terroristic threat that goes viral online, Korean authorities discover that a suspect has recently boarded an international flight bound for the United States. When a healthy passenger on the same flight suddenly dies a gruesome death of unknown cause, panic erupts both in-flight and on the ground. With steadily decreasing fuel and international refusals to offer aid, the captain and crew will be forced to take unprecedented emergency measures in an attempt to save the lives of their passengers.
documents.plot:
Emergency Declaration is a 2022 South Korean thriller film directed by Lee Jeong-ho, produced by Showbox.

The movie follows the story of Kang Min-kyu (played by Song Kang), a young doctor who works as an emergency room physician at a hospital in Seoul. One day, while reviewing patient records, he discovers that one of his patients, a 17-year-old girl named Kim Ji-soo (played by Cho Yeo-jeong), has been declared dead by the hospital's system.

Min-kyu is shocked and decides to investigate further, as he believes that the death was not due to natural causes. He starts questioning the patient records and discovers that there are several other patients who have also been incorrectly declared dead. Min-kyu becomes obsessed with uncovering the truth behind these deaths and sets out on a mission to expose the hospital's errors.

As Min-kyu delves deeper into the mystery, he faces resistance from his colleagues and superiors at the hospital, who are more concerned with maintaining their reputation than with revealing the truth. Despite this, Min-kyu remains determined to uncover the truth and bring justice to the families of the deceased patients.

Throughout the movie, Min-kyu's investigation takes him on a journey through the dark underbelly of the Korean healthcare system, where corruption and incompetence are rampant. Along the way, he encounters a cast of characters who are equally flawed and complex, including his colleagues, his superiors, and even some of the patients' families.

As the story unfolds, Min-kyu's obsession with uncovering the truth becomes increasingly all-consuming, leading him to question his own identity and purpose. The movie builds towards a tense and suspenseful climax as Min-kyu confronts the hospital administrators and demands answers about the deaths.

Overall, Emergency Declaration is a gripping thriller that explores themes of mortality, morality, and the human condition. With its tight script, strong performances, and thought-provoking subject matter, it's no wonder that this movie has resonated with audiences worldwide.

documents.title: Antebellum
documents.tagline: If it chooses you, nothing can save you.
documents.overview: Successful author Veronica finds herself trapped in a horrifying reality and must uncover the mind-bending mystery before it's too late.
documents.plot:
Antebellum is a 2020 American horror film written and directed by Gerard Bush and Christopher Renz. The movie stars Janelle Monáe, Eric Lange, and Jena Malone.

The main themes of Antebellum revolve around the horrors of slavery, racism, and the cyclical nature of oppression. The film's narrative is presented in a non-linear fashion, jumping between two timelines: 1903, where the story takes place during the Jim Crow era, and 2020, where the protagonist, Veronica Henley (Janelle Monáe), finds herself trapped in a nightmarish world that mirrors her own reality.

Throughout the film, Bush and Renz explore themes of systemic racism, oppression, and the ways in which historical trauma continues to affect marginalized communities. The movie also delves into the concept of "double consciousness," coined by W.E.B. Du Bois, which refers to the experience of living with two conflicting identities: one that is imposed upon you by society, and another that is authentic and true to yourself.

The film's use of horror elements serves as a metaphor for the terror and trauma experienced by enslaved people and those who continue to face systemic racism today. By presenting these themes in a thought-provoking and unsettling manner, Antebellum encourages viewers to confront the dark history of America and its ongoing impact on contemporary society.

Ultimately, the film's ending suggests that true freedom and liberation can only be achieved through self-awareness, resistance, and collective action. The movie serves as a powerful commentary on the need for ongoing dialogue and activism in the face of systemic oppression, and it challenges viewers to consider their own complicity in perpetuating or challenging these systems.

Overall, Antebellum is a thought-provoking and unsettling film that explores some of the most pressing issues facing America today. Its non-linear narrative and use of horror elements make for a compelling and unforgettable viewing experience.

documents.title: The Assistant
documents.overview: A searing look at a day in the life of an assistant to a powerful executive. As Jane follows her daily routine, she grows increasingly aware of the insidious abuse that threatens every aspect of her position.
documents.plot:
The Assistant (2020) is a thought-provoking drama that delves into the darker aspects of power dynamics and the consequences of unchecked ambition. The film follows Jane, a young and ambitious assistant who becomes embroiled in a toxic work environment at a prestigious law firm.

At its core, The Assistant explores the theme of gaslighting and emotional manipulation, as embodied by the firm's ruthless and cunning leader, Martha. This character serves as a symbol of the ways in which women can be silenced, belittled, and exploited in the workplace. As Jane navigates this treacherous landscape, she must confront the ways in which her own self-worth has been eroded by her boss's constant belittling and manipulation.

The film also touches on the theme of identity and how it is shaped by our relationships with others. Jane's struggle to assert herself and find her place in the world serves as a powerful metaphor for the ways in which we often seek validation from those around us. As she grapples with her own desires and ambitions, Jane must confront the tension between her need for recognition and her desire to maintain a sense of self-worth.

Furthermore, The Assistant critiques the patriarchal norms that perpetuate inequality and sexism in the workplace. The film's portrayal of a male-dominated industry where women are often relegated to secondary roles serves as a scathing commentary on the ways in which systemic power structures can perpetuate oppression.

Ultimately, The Assistant is a powerful exploration of the human cost of ambition and the importance of self-care and emotional intelligence. Through Jane's journey, the film offers a nuanced and thought-provoking examination of the ways in which we navigate complex relationships and confront our own vulnerabilities.

documents.title: Cranston Academy: Monster Zone
documents.overview: An intelligent 15-year-old high school student is unexpectedly transferred to a boarding school where he opens a portal of monsters from another dimension.
documents.plot:
I couldn't find any information on "Cranston Academy: Monster Zone" released in 2020 or produced by Ánima Estudios. 

However, I found that there is a Netflix animated series called "Cranston Academy: Monster Combat" (not "Monster Zone") released in 2021, also produced by Ánima Estudios. If you're referring to this series, it's an action-comedy anime that follows the story of a group of students at Cranston Academy who discover they have supernatural abilities and must learn to control them.

The main themes of "Cranston Academy: Monster Combat" include:

* Self-discovery and empowerment: The characters must navigate their newfound powers and learn to work together to overcome challenges.
* Friendship and teamwork: The series highlights the importance of building strong relationships and working together as a team to achieve common goals.
* Balancing individuality with conformity: The characters often struggle with balancing their unique abilities with the expectations of their peers and the school's rules.

If you're referring to a different movie or series, please provide more information so I can try to assist you further.

documents.title: The Banker
documents.tagline: Don’t pay the man. Be the man.
documents.overview: In the 1960s, two entrepreneurs hatch an ingenious business plan to fight for housing integration—and equal access to the American Dream.
documents.plot:
The Banker is a 2020 biographical drama film directed by George Tillman Jr., not Mad Hatter Entertainment.

The main themes of The Banker include:

1. **Racism and Prejudice**: The film explores the experiences of Bernard Garrett, an African American entrepreneur who faced racism and prejudice in his pursuit of success.
2. **Perseverance and Determination**: Despite facing numerous obstacles, Garrett persevered and worked tirelessly to achieve his goals, ultimately becoming one of the most successful African American entrepreneurs of his time.
3. **Identity and Self-Discovery**: The film delves into Garrett's journey of self-discovery, as he navigates between his humble beginnings and his rise to success in the business world.
4. **The Power of Mentorship**: The relationship between Bernard Garrett and his mentor, George Washington Williams, is a pivotal aspect of the film, highlighting the importance of guidance and support in achieving one's goals.

These themes are woven throughout the narrative, which follows Garrett's life from his childhood to his rise as a successful businessman.

documents.title: Wild Mountain Thyme
documents.tagline: There's nothing more dangerous... than an Irish woman in love.
documents.overview: Headstrong farmer Rosemary Muldoon has her heart set on winning her neighbour Anthony Reilly's love. The problem is, Anthony seems to have inherited a family curse, and remains oblivious to his beautiful admirer. Stung by his father's plans to sell the family farm to his American nephew, Anthony is jolted into pursuing his dreams.
documents.plot:
Wild Mountain Thyme is a romantic comedy of 2020 written and directed by John Patrick Shanley, who adapted it from his own play Outside Mullingar. Emily Blunt and Jamie Dornan star as Rosemary Muldoon and Anthony Reilly, neighbouring farmers in rural Ireland, with Jon Hamm as Anthony's American cousin Adam Kelly, Christopher Walken as Anthony's father Tony and Dearbhla Molloy, reprising her stage role, as Rosemary's mother Aoife.

In County Mayo, two introverted misfits approaching forty have spent their whole lives on adjoining farms. Rosemary has long loved Anthony, who seems oblivious; a childhood memory shows him pushing her down after she defended him from a girl who mocked him. Anthony hears a voice in the fields telling him to "go", though he will not say where. Convinced that his reclusive son will never marry and continue the family line, Tony plans to disinherit him and sell the farm to his nephew Adam, a New York banker. Anthony resolves to propose to Rosemary with his late mother's ring, only to lose it in a field, and spends weeks combing the ground with a metal detector.

Adam arrives for Tony's 75th birthday, charms Rosemary with his directness and invites her to New York. After Rosemary's mother dies, Tony abandons the sale so as not to spoil the young couple's chances, then reconciles with Anthony on his deathbed. Left alone on their farms, Rosemary reaches out, but Anthony pushes her away and urges her to leave Ireland. She visits Adam, who takes her to Swan Lake, kisses her and tells her that pining for Anthony is making her miserable, yet she refuses to give up. Back home she confronts Anthony, who finally admits the secret that has wrecked his past romances: he believes he is a honeybee. Rosemary produces the ring she found, he proposes, and he realises the voice had been telling him to go to her all along. The film ends in the pub, where the whole village, joined by the couple's late parents, sings "Wild Mountain Thyme".
