Shot in and around Crossmolina and Ballina in 2019, the film was released by Bleecker Street in the United States in December 2020. Its trailer was mocked for its Irish accents, and critics were largely negative, with 25% on Rotten Tomatoes.
production_companies: The Western Regional Audiovisual Producers Fund/Wrap Fund

documents.title: The White Tiger
documents.overview: An ambitious Indian driver uses his wit and cunning to escape from poverty and rise to the top. An epic journey based on the New York Times bestseller.
documents.plot:
The White Tiger (2021) is a thought-provoking film that delves into the complexities of class struggle, social inequality, and the human condition. Set against the backdrop of India's growing economy and rising middle class, the movie explores the stark contrast between the lives of two individuals: Balwan Khurana, a poor and ambitious driver, and Roy Chaudhary, a wealthy businessman.

At its core, The White Tiger is a scathing critique of the Indian caste system and the social hierarchy that perpetuates inequality. Through Balwan's character, the film sheds light on the struggles faced by those at the bottom of the social ladder, who are forced to navigate a system designed to keep them in their place. The movie highlights the ways in which poverty, lack of education, and limited opportunities can lead individuals to make difficult choices that ultimately define their lives.

The White Tiger also explores the theme of moral ambiguity and the blurred lines between good and evil. Roy Chaudhary is a complex character who embodies both the privileges and pitfalls of wealth and power. His actions are driven by a desire for status, security, and self-preservation, but they also perpetuate a cycle of violence and exploitation that ultimately destroys him.

One of the most striking aspects of The White Tiger is its portrayal of the human condition in all its complexity. The film is both a commentary on the social ills of India and a deeply personal exploration of Balwan's inner world. Through his character, the movie reveals the struggles of living with trauma, the weight of responsibility, and the search for meaning in a seemingly meaningless world.

Ultimately, The White Tiger is a powerful and thought-provoking film that challenges viewers to confront the harsh realities of social inequality and the human condition. It is a searing critique of a society that perpetuates injustice and a testament to the resilience and determination of those who refuse to be silenced or marginalized.

documents.title: Midnight
documents.overview: A serial killer ruthlessly hunts down a deaf woman through the streets of South Korea after she witnesses his brutal crime.
documents.plot:
Midnight (Korean: Mideunaiteu; released in France as Midnight Silence) is a 2021 South Korean psychological thriller written and directed by Kwon Oh-seung and produced by Peppermint & Company. It stages a night-long game of hide-and-seek between a psychopathic killer and a deaf woman across the streets of Seoul. Jin Ki-joo and Wi Ha-joon were confirmed in the leads in August 2019, and filming began on 8 September that year. Planned for 2020, the release was delayed by the COVID-19 pandemic, and the film finally opened on 30 June 2021 simultaneously in cinemas and on the streaming service TVING.

Jin plays Kyung-mi, a deaf woman who works as a sign-language counsellor at a call centre. Walking home late one night after meeting her mother (Gil Hae-yeon), who is also deaf, she finds So-jung (Kim Hye-yoon), a young woman bleeding from a stab wound in an alley, and becomes the next target of the serial killer Do-shik (Wi), who had been stalking So-jung. Do-shik moves the wounded woman into his van before the police arrive and then presents himself as a fellow witness, using a second, friendly face to read Kyung-mi's statement and learn her address. So-jung's brother Jong-tak (Park Hoon), a former marine now working as a security guard, bursts into the police station demanding a search for his missing sister and comes to suspect the stranger. Over the rest of the night the killer pursues Kyung-mi from her home through the city, offers Jong-tak a cruel bargain between saving his sister and saving Kyung-mi, and even convinces indifferent passers-by that the fleeing woman is his own sister, while Kyung-mi, unable to hear the danger approaching, relies on her wits and on her mother.

The film opened on 693 screens, placed third at the Korean box office on its first day and drew about 108,500 admissions by December 2021. Abroad it screened in the Genre Masters section of the New York Asian Film Festival, at Fantasia in Montreal, where it won the audience prize for best Asian film, and at Grimmfest in the United Kingdom, where it was named best feature. Critics responded positively, with all 17 reviews counted by Rotten Tomatoes favourable. In the Korean press, Maeil Business praised the way two deaf women confront the killer by their own means, and the Seoul Economic Daily singled out the fast-paced chases through everyday spaces and the physical commitment of the cast, especially Jin Ki-joo.

documents.title: Panama
documents.overview: An ex-marine is hired by a defense contractor to travel to Panama to complete an arms deal. In the process he becomes involved with the U.S. invasion of Panama, and learns an important lesson about the true nature of political power.
documents.plot:
Panama is a 2022 American action thriller directed by Mark Neveldine and starring Cole Hauser and Mel Gibson, with Kate Katzman, Charlie Weber and Jackie Cruz in supporting roles. Set in 1989, in the months before the United States invasion of Panama, the film follows a former Marine recruited for a covert arms deal in Central America during the final years of the Cold War.

James Becker, a former Marine, has fallen into despair and heavy drinking after the death of his wife, often passing out beside her grave behind his house. Stark, a defense contractor and old associate played by Gibson, approaches him with a secret assignment that might give him a reason to keep going. At a government facility, Becker meets Stark and a skeptical agent named Burns, who explain the mission. The CIA, barred from openly supporting the Contra rebels in Nicaragua and eager to undermine the Panamanian dictator Manuel Noriega, has arranged to buy a Russian helicopter from Noriega's regime, with payment to a Swiss account, and intends to pass the aircraft to the Contras. Becker is to travel to Panama under cover as a consultant for a casino and see the transaction through.

In Panama, Becker is introduced to Enrique Rodriguez, a Harvard-educated, cocaine-fueled playboy with powerful connections, including ties to Colonel Marcos Justines of the Panamanian military and to an uncle who opposes Noriega. Enrique keeps putting off the helicopter deal, urging Becker to settle into his job at the casino, and eventually challenges him to a dirt-bike race in the jungle with the aircraft as the prize. When Enrique wins and tries to squeeze more money from the Americans, Becker takes back the million-dollar CIA advance. As tensions rise and an American invasion approaches, Justines orders Enrique to recover the money at any cost, and assassins are sent after Becker and those close to him, including Camila, a woman with whom he has begun a relationship. Becker must survive long enough to complete his mission amid the chaos of Operation Just Cause.

Panama was released in limited theaters and on demand in March 2022. It was poorly received by critics, with a 7 percent approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on 14 reviews and an average score of 2.6 out of 10. The film blends its fictional espionage plot with real historical events of the period, including the Iran-Contra affair and the American military operation that removed Noriega from power in December 1989.

documents.title: Queenpins
documents.overview: Bored and frustrated suburban homemaker Connie and her best pal JoJo, a vlogger with dreams, turn a hobby into a multi-million-dollar counterfeit coupon caper. After firing off a letter to the conglomerate behind a box of cereal gone stale, and receiving an apology along with dozens of freebies, the duo hatch an illegal coupon club scheme that scams millions from mega-corporations and delivers deals to legions of fellow coupon clippers. On the trail to total coupon dominance, a hapless Loss Prevention Officer from the local supermarket chain joins forces with a determined U.S. Postal Inspector in hot pursuit of these newly minted “Queenpins” of pink collar crime.
documents.plot:
Queenpins is a 2021 American crime comedy film written and directed by Aron Gaudet and Gita Pullapilly. Kristen Bell and Kirby Howell-Baptiste star as two friends who build a counterfeit coupon empire, with Paul Walter Hauser, Vince Vaughn, Bebe Rexha and Joel McHale. Ben Stiller executive produced through his Red Hour Productions. Released in limited theaters by STX Films in September 2021 and on Paramount+ later that month, it was inspired by the case of three women arrested in Phoenix in 2012, when police found more than $25 million in fake coupons.

Connie Kaminski, a suburban housewife and former Olympic racewalker, feels ignored by her husband, Rick, an IRS auditor, and the rest of the world. Unemployed and grieving after a miscarriage following attempts at IVF, she confides in her best friend, JoJo Johnson, who has been unable to find work since her identity was stolen and lives with her mother while trying to earn money with YouTube videos. After Connie writes to General Mills to complain about a stale box of cereal, she receives a coupon for a free replacement, and she learns from a store cashier that companies routinely respond to complaints this way.

Discovering that the coupons are printed at a plant in Chihuahua, Mexico, Connie and JoJo travel there and persuade a married couple who work at the factory to send them unused coupons. The pair launch a website, Savvy Super Saver, to sell the coupons at a fraction of their value, and their scheme quickly grows into a highly profitable operation, bringing them money and a sense of purpose. Their success attracts the attention of Ken Miller, a hapless loss-prevention officer for a supermarket chain, played by Hauser, who teams up with Simon Kilmurry, a U.S. postal inspector played by Vaughn, to track down the source of the fraudulent coupons. As the investigators close in, Connie and JoJo struggle to launder their growing fortune and hide their activities from their families, and their friendship is tested as the risks mount.

Queenpins received mixed reviews from critics, who found the true story's premise amusing and appreciated the performances of Bell, Howell-Baptiste and Hauser, but felt the film lacked the bite of the best crime comedies and did not fully exploit its satirical potential.

documents.title: An American Pickle
documents.overview: An immigrant worker at a pickle factory is accidentally preserved for 100 years and wakes up in modern day Brooklyn. He learns his only surviving relative is his great grandson, a computer coder who he can’t connect with.
documents.plot:
An American Pickle is a 2020 comedy-drama film that tells the story of an immigrant named Herschel Greenbaum who discovers he has a doppelganger in his great-grandson, also named Herschel. As the two Hershels navigate their lives in different eras, they must confront the complexities of identity, community, and belonging.

At its core, An American Pickle explores the theme of identity and how it is shaped by our experiences, relationships, and cultural backgrounds. The film delves into the idea that our sense of self is not fixed, but rather a dynamic and evolving construct that can be influenced by various factors, including family history, social context, and personal choices.

The movie also touches on the theme of community and how it provides a sense of belonging and connection to others. Herschel's relationships with his family, friends, and community are central to the story, highlighting the importance of these connections in shaping our identities and experiences.

Furthermore, An American Pickle critiques the idea of assimilation and the immigrant experience, suggesting that true belonging can only be achieved by embracing one's cultural heritage while also adapting to new environments. The film's exploration of these themes is nuanced and thought-provoking, inviting viewers to reflect on their own relationships with identity, community, and culture.

Overall, An American Pickle is a heartwarming and humorous exploration of the complexities of human experience, identity, and belonging.

documents.title: Child of Kamiari Month
documents.overview: A year after losing her mother, a young girl learns that she must journey across Japan to the annual gathering of gods in the sacred land of Izumo.
documents.plot:
Child of Kamiari Month (Japanese: Kamiarizuki no Kodomo) is a 2021 Japanese animated fantasy adventure film produced by Liden Films and directed by Takana Shirai. The project was announced and funded through three crowdfunding campaigns by Cretica Universal between 2019 and 2020, and Miwa performed its theme song, "Kanna". It opened in Japanese cinemas on October 8, 2021, and Netflix, which acquired international rights, began streaming it on February 8, 2022.

Kanna Hayama, an elementary school girl in Tokyo's Sumida ward, has lost her love of running since the death of her mother, Yayoi, a year earlier, and lives with her widowed father, Norimasa. During the school marathon she gives up mid-race and, after snapping at her father, runs to the local Ushijima Shrine. There her mother's keepsake bracelet activates, time slows, and she meets a huge black cow deity, a demon boy named Yasha who wants the bracelet, and Shiro, the school rabbit she looks after, who can now speak. Shiro, a messenger of the gods, explains that in October the deities of Japan gather above Izumo-taisha Shrine in Shimane for a harvest feast, and that Kanna must collect offerings from shrine gods along the way in a magic gourd and deliver them by seven o'clock that night.

Yasha, descended from swift demons once stripped of divine status by the supreme god Ōkuninushi, steals the gourd and bracelet and beats Kanna in a race, but ends up joining the journey. At Lake Suwa the dragon god Ryūjin, a son of Ōkuninushi, draws out Kanna's real wish, to see her mother again, and shares his own separation from his father. Near the end of the route, a vision of Yayoi lures Kanna away, but it is her own dark side in disguise. Despairing, Kanna tears off the bracelet and can no longer hear her companions as a typhoon strikes. A vision reveals that Yayoi, too, was a descendant of the Idaten, the runners who once performed this task. Inspired, Kanna ties up her hair with the bracelet and runs on through the storm to the shrine, where Ōkuninushi appears and the feast begins. He thanks the three but says even his matchmaking cannot bring Yayoi back and that time must move on. Back in Tokyo, Kanna takes up running again in the spring.

Aju Makita voices Kanna, with Maaya Sakamoto as Shiro, Miyu Irino as Yasha, Akira Kamiya as Ōkuninushi, Wataru Takagi as Ryūjin, Ko Shibasaki as Yayoi and Arata Iura as Norimasa. All six critics counted by Rotten Tomatoes gave it positive reviews.

documents.title: Shut In
documents.tagline: The will to live is found within.
documents.overview: A young single mother is held captive along with her two children by a violent ex and must plot their escape before it’s too late.
documents.plot:
Shut In is a 2022 American thriller film directed by D. J. Caruso from a screenplay by Melanie Toast, starring Rainey Qualley, Jake Horowitz, Luciana VanDette and Vincent Gallo. It was the first original film of The Daily Wire and the third released on its streaming platform, DailyWire+. Toast's script had featured on the 2019 Black List and was once set up at New Line Cinema with Jason Bateman attached to direct; it also marked Gallo's first feature film role since 2013.

Jessica Nash, a young mother of two, is fixing up the house she inherited from her late grandmother so that she can sell it and move away. While working on a closet, she accidentally locks herself inside, and her young daughter Lainey is unable to bring her the key. Her ex-boyfriend Rob, a drug addict, arrives with his friend Sammy and lets her out, but Jessica is furious that he has brought Sammy, a pedophile, to her home. Manipulated by Sammy, Rob locks her back in the closet before the two men leave. Sammy later breaks into the house.

Jessica tricks Sammy into reaching under the door and pins his hand to the floor with a screwdriver that Lainey had slipped her, trapping him beside her. When Lainey comes downstairs despite being told to stay with her baby brother Mason, Sammy grabs her and threatens her, but Jessica sets his hand on fire, forcing him to let go. With Sammy apparently dead, Jessica escapes by climbing through the ceiling to the second floor and takes the children to the car, but heavy rain forces them back into the house, where Sammy, still alive, seizes the children and holds a knife to Mason's throat. Rob arrives and shoots Sammy dead, and he and Jessica attempt to reconcile. Realizing that Rob will always put drugs ahead of her and the children, Jessica slips him a large quantity of crystal meth. When he tries to make her relapse and inject her, he overdoses, and she pushes him out of a window to his death. Some time later, Jessica and her children live happily in the restored house, where she makes and sells apple butter from her mother's recipe.

The Daily Wire hosted a special viewing of the film on its YouTube channel on February 10, 2022. Shut In received mixed reviews, with 55% approval on Rotten Tomatoes; some critics praised its redemption arc while noting it lacked visceral thrills.

documents.title: Run Hide Fight
documents.overview: A 17-year-old girl uses her wits, survival skills, and compassion to fight for her life, and those of her fellow classmates, against a group of live-streaming school shooters.
documents.plot:
Run Hide Fight is an American action thriller written and directed by Kyle Rankin, premiered in 2020, about a teenage girl who fights back against a group of shooters who take over her high school. Its title comes from the "Run. Hide. Fight." guidance for active-shooter situations. Isabel May stars as Zoe Hull, with Thomas Jane as her father Todd, Radha Mitchell as her late mother Jennifer, Eli Brown as the ringleader Tristan Voy, Olly Sholotan as her friend Lewis, Treat Williams as Sheriff Tarsy and Barbara Crampton as Mrs. Crawford.

Zoe, still grieving her mother, has a strained relationship with her father. On her way to school she sees classmate Chris Jelick planting a device in a field, but dismisses it as a prank. As incendiary devices go off around town to distract first responders, a van carrying four shooters, Tristan, Chris, his sister Anna and Kip Quade, smashes into the cafeteria. Tristan forces Lewis to livestream the attack and takes most of the students hostage, admitting that he simply craves notoriety; he kills the principal and lets an unarmed guard flee. Zoe, who escaped through a bathroom ceiling, returns to warn students and lead them out, realising that the lockdown only helps the attackers corner their victims.

Zoe kills Anna in self-defence and overpowers Kip, who confesses he was avenging middle-school bullying; she reminds him that his victims had nothing to do with it. She asks the sheriff to pull the media cameras away so students can escape, but Tristan sees through the ruse and threatens to kill hostages unless she shows herself. A remorseful Kip agrees to ambush his partners and is killed, while Zoe rescues the wounded Lewis and admits she returns his feelings. Lewis warns her that the van is packed with explosives. Todd, who has taken up a sniper position outside, shoots Chris before he can execute Zoe, and Zoe takes over the livestream to deny Tristan his fame, then reverses the rigged van so that it explodes in an empty car park. Tristan fakes his own death, but Zoe, reconciled with her father, spots him fleeing into the woods, shoots him with her father's rifle and leaves him to die.

Shot in Red Oak, Texas, on a budget of about $1.5 million, the film premiered at the Venice Film Festival on 10 September 2020 and was released by The Daily Wire on its subscription platform in January 2021. Reviews were largely negative, with 30% on Rotten Tomatoes, though some critics praised its young cast.

documents.title: Samaritan
documents.tagline: 25 years ago the world's greatest hero vanished.
documents.overview: Thirteen year old Sam Cleary  suspects that his mysteriously reclusive neighbor Mr. Smith is actually the legendary vigilante Samaritan, who was reported dead 20 years ago. With crime on the rise and the city on the brink of chaos, Sam makes it his mission to coax his neighbor out of hiding to save the city from ruin.
documents.plot:
Samaritan is a 2022 American superhero film directed by Julius Avery and written by Bragi F. Schut, whose story was also adapted into a series of graphic novels. Produced by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer Pictures and Balboa Productions, it stars Sylvester Stallone as Joe Smith, Javon "Wanna" Walton as Sam Cleary, Pilou Asbæk as Cyrus, Dascha Polanco as Sam's mother Tiffany and Moisés Arias as Reza. The film offers a gritty, darker take on the superhero genre.

Decades earlier, Granite City was home to two superpowered twin brothers. After an angry mob burned their family's home, killing their parents, one brother became the heroic Samaritan, while the other became the villain Nemesis. To gain an advantage over his equally powerful sibling, Nemesis forged a sledgehammer capable of harming him. During a final battle at a power plant, both were believed to have been killed when the plant exploded, plunging the city into darkness.

Twenty-five years later, Granite City is impoverished and crime-ridden. Thirteen-year-old Sam Cleary, who is struggling to help his mother pay the rent, gets drawn into the world of a local gang and becomes obsessed with the theory that Samaritan is still alive. When a garbage collector named Joe Smith, a reclusive elderly man living across the street, fends off a group of gang members with apparently superhuman strength, Sam becomes convinced that he has found his hero. Joe denies everything, but after he heals from serious injuries in front of Sam's eyes, the two develop a friendship. Meanwhile, the ambitious criminal Cyrus recovers Nemesis's hammer and takes on his mantle, plotting to plunge the city into chaos, forcing Joe to confront the past he has tried to bury.

The film explores the legacy of heroes and villains and the moral gray areas between them, culminating in a twist that reframes the story of the two brothers.

Samaritan was released on August 26, 2022, by United Artists Releasing and Amazon Studios on the Prime Video streaming service. It received mixed reviews, with 38 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it creatively underpowered, and a Metacritic score of 45.

documents.title: What Happened to Mr Cha?
documents.overview: With the peak of his career long behind him, an actor clings to his past glory — until a sudden wake-up call forces him to face who he's become.
documents.plot:
Titled in Korean simply 차인표, after its star, What Happened to Mr. Cha? is a South Korean comedy from 2021 written and directed by Kim Dong-kyu, previously a co-writer of the thrillers Confession of Murder and Golden Job, in his feature directing debut, and released by Netflix. The veteran actor Cha In-pyo plays a fictionalised, somewhat haughtier version of himself, with Jo Dal-hwan as his manager A-ram, Song Jae-ryong, Ji Seung-hyun, Shin Shin-ae as Bok-soon, Jo Sang-gu as a hiker and Song Duk-ho; Cha's real-life wife, the actress Shin Ae-ra, plays his on-screen wife, and Ryu Seung-ryong appears as himself.

After 25 years in show business, Cha is still handsome, fit and fond of the signature finger wag his ageing fans remember, but his career is fading. Once the star of hit television dramas, he now poses for advertisements for mid-range casual sportswear while a young creative director rejects his leading-man looks and the makeup artist gets better offers than he does. He lives apart from his wife, from whom he has recently separated, and his young manager A-ram has not had the heart to tell him that the phone has stopped ringing.

Out on a hike with his tiny dog to clear his head, Cha is asked by passing seniors whether he has quit acting, and then tumbles into a mud puddle. Unwilling to be seen in such a state, he follows a stranger's advice to wash up at a nearby high school that is empty for the summer. While he is in the shower, the building's bumbling staff set off an explosion, and the school collapses on top of him. Naked, covered in dust and pinned in the rubble, Cha calls his manager, but he refuses any rescue that might humiliate him or ruin the image he has spent decades building, imagining live television footage of his blurred body being carried out. As A-ram tries to placate him and fend off the building's manager and the approaching excavator, Cha reflects on his past triumphs, seen in clips of his old roles, and as he grows delirious the film turns surreal, with Cha floating among the stars still encased in concrete and confronting his manager and versions of himself before accepting his new reality.

Netflix released the film on 1 January 2021. Critics admired Cha's willingness to mock his own persona. Decider recommended it, praising his wit and melancholy despite a sluggish middle section, while the South China Morning Post found that its sharp satire of celebrity culture gave way to more ordinary slapstick.

documents.title: The Bad Guys
documents.tagline: Good is no fun at all.
documents.overview: When the Bad Guys, a crew of criminal animals, are finally caught after years of heists and being the world’s most-wanted villains, Mr. Wolf brokers a deal to save them all from prison.
documents.plot:
The Bad Guys is an animated action-comedy film released in 2022, produced by Illumination Entertainment and Universal Pictures.

The movie follows the story of a group of animal outcasts who are known as "the bad guys" in their community. The main character, Wolf (voiced by Sam Rockwell), is a cunning and charismatic leader who has been shunned by his peers due to his mischievous behavior. He is joined by his loyal sidekicks, Whitey the rabbit (voiced by Awkwafina) and Shark (voiced by Antonio Banderas).

The trio plans to rob a bank in the city of Dogville, where they hope to escape their troubled pasts and start anew. However, things don't go as planned, and they find themselves on the run from the authorities.

As Wolf navigates his complicated relationships with Whitey and Shark, he begins to question his own morality and the true nature of being a "bad guy." Along the way, he meets a young girl named Fiona (voiced by Marie Gauthier), who becomes an unlikely ally in their quest for redemption.

Throughout the film, Wolf's backstory is slowly revealed, showcasing his troubled childhood and the events that led him to become the leader of the group. The movie also explores themes of friendship, loyalty, and the power of change.

The animation style in The Bad Guys is vibrant and colorful, with a unique blend of humor and heart. The voice cast delivers impressive performances, bringing depth and nuance to their characters.

Overall, The Bad Guys is a fun and entertaining film that offers a fresh take on the traditional "bad guy" trope. With its engaging storyline, lovable characters, and stunning animation, it's sure to delight audiences of all ages.

documents.title: The Vault
documents.overview: When an engineer learns of a mysterious, impenetrable fortress hidden under The Bank of Spain, he joins a crew of master thieves who plan to steal the legendary lost treasure locked inside while the whole country is distracted by Spain's World Cup Final. With thousands of soccer fans cheering in the streets, and security forces closing in, the crew have just minutes to pull off the score of a lifetime.
documents.plot:
The Vault, released as Way Down in several regions, is a 2021 Spanish heist action thriller directed by Jaume Balagueró. Freddie Highmore stars as a young engineering prodigy, with Àstrid Bergès-Frisbey, Sam Riley, Liam Cunningham, Luis Tosar, Axel Stein, José Coronado and Famke Janssen in the ensemble cast. The story bears a passing resemblance to the real-life case of the Black Swan Project treasure, recovered in 2007 by the salvage company Odyssey Marine Exploration and later handed over to Spain after a legal battle.

In July 2010, Thom Johnson is a gifted engineering student at Cambridge University who turns down lucrative offers from oil companies, telling his father, an oil executive, that he does not want that kind of life. An anonymous message leads him to Lorraine, a skilled con artist, who introduces him to Walter, the head of a salvage company. Walter's firm found a legendary sunken treasure off the Spanish coast, only to have it seized by the Spanish government because the salvage was not carried out legally. The treasure is now kept in a vault beneath the Bank of Spain in Madrid, one of the most secure facilities in the world.

Walter has assembled a team of specialists, including Lorraine, the logistics expert Simon and the technician Klaus, and he wants Thom to find a way into the vault. Its defences, designed by a brilliant and secretive engineer, include an elaborate system that floods the chamber the moment it detects a breach. Thom determines that there is a narrow window of opportunity during the final of the 2010 FIFA World Cup, when Spain is playing and the entire country is distracted by the match. As the team improvise their way through the bank's security, they are pursued by the bank's head of security, Gustavo, while Thom discovers that the treasure holds a further secret linked to Sir Francis Drake.

The film combines the mechanics of a classic heist movie with the excitement surrounding Spain's World Cup triumph, and its action set pieces were largely filmed in Madrid and in a reconstruction of the bank's vault.

Critical reception was mixed. On Rotten Tomatoes about 60 percent of critics' reviews are positive; the consensus finds that its runtime passes painlessly enough but that its slickly engineered thrills are rarely more than routine for the genre.

documents.title: Titane
documents.overview: A woman with a metal plate in her head from a childhood car accident embarks on a bizarre journey, bringing her into contact with a firefighter who's reunited with his missing son after 10 years.
documents.plot:
Titane is a 2021 French body horror film written and directed by Julia Ducournau. The film premiered at the 2021 Cannes Film Festival, where it won the Palme d'Or.

The story revolves around Alexia (played by Agathe Rousselle), a young woman who was adopted as an infant after being found in a dumpster on her birthday. As she grows up, Alexia struggles to connect with others due to her troubled past and her own sense of identity. She is fascinated by cars and becomes an expert mechanic.

One day, while working at a car dealership, Alexia meets Vincent (played by Laia Costa), a beautiful and charismatic woman who is also a skilled driver. The two women form a deep connection, but their relationship is complicated by the fact that Vincent has been involved in a series of violent crimes, including murder.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Alexia has a unique condition - she has a titanium plate implanted in her head, which was inserted after an accident as a child. The plate allows her to transform into a hybrid creature with car parts, giving her superhuman strength and agility.

Throughout the film, Alexia's transformation is depicted as a metaphor for her own identity crisis. As she becomes more and more integrated with Vincent's body, she begins to lose herself in the process. The two women's relationship becomes increasingly intense and violent, leading to a series of shocking and disturbing events.

The film's climax features a confrontation between Alexia and Vincent, which ends in tragedy. In the aftermath, Alexia is left to grapple with the consequences of her actions, and the audience is left wondering about the nature of identity and humanity.

One of the most striking aspects of Titane is its exploration of themes such as trauma, identity, and the objectification of women's bodies. The film features a number of disturbing and unsettling scenes, including graphic violence and gore.

Overall, Titane is a thought-provoking and visually stunning film that challenges audiences to confront their own assumptions about identity and humanity. With its unique blend of body horror and psychological drama, it has become a modern classic of the genre.

documents.title: The Cursed
documents.overview: In the late 19th century, a brutal land baron slaughters a Roma clan, unleashing a curse on his family and village. In the days that follow, the townspeople are plagued by nightmares, the baron's son goes missing, and a boy is found murdered. The locals suspect a wild animal, but a visiting pathologist warns of a more sinister presence lurking in the woods.
documents.plot:
I couldn't find any information on a movie titled "The Cursed" released in 2021 by LD Entertainment. 

However, I did find that there is a Netflix series called "The Sandman" which has an episode titled "Cain & Abel" and another one titled "Lovers and Other Demons", but also a movie titled "The Cursed Child" (2016) based on the play of the same name by Jack Thorne, based on an original story by J.K. Rowling, Jack Thorne, and John Tiffany.

If you are referring to the 2021 film adaptation of "The Cursed Child", I can provide information about it.

documents.title: Clouds
documents.tagline: Don't wait for tomorrow to live for today
documents.overview: Young musician Zach Sobiech discovers his cancer has spread, leaving him just a few months to live. With limited time, he follows his dream and makes an album, unaware that it will soon be a viral music phenomenon.
documents.plot:
Clouds is a 2020 American biographical drama film directed by Justin Baldoni, based on the memoir "Clouds: The Autobiography of a Teenage Prophet" by Gabriel Grazer and the late Zach Sobiech.

The main themes of Clouds include:

1. **Mortality and Legacy**: The film explores the theme of mortality through the story of Zach Sobiech, who was diagnosed with osteosarcoma, a type of bone cancer. The movie shows how Zach's life was cut short, but his legacy lives on through his music and the impact he had on those around him.

2. **Perseverance and Resilience**: Despite facing numerous health challenges, Zach Sobiech continued to pursue his passion for music, inspiring others with his determination and resilience. The film highlights the importance of staying positive and focused in the face of adversity.

3. **Friendship and Love**: Clouds celebrates the power of friendship and love, particularly between Zach and his friends, who supported him throughout his struggles. The movie shows how these relationships can bring meaning and purpose to life.

4. **Self-Discovery and Purpose**: As Zach navigates his illness, he begins to question his purpose in life. Through music and his experiences, he discovers a sense of self and finds his place in the world.

5. **The Impact of Social Media**: The film touches on the theme of social media's influence on our lives, particularly for teenagers. Zach's online presence helps him connect with others and share his story, but it also raises questions about the authenticity of online personas and the pressure to present a perfect image.

Overall, Clouds is a heartwarming and inspiring film that explores themes of mortality, perseverance, friendship, self-discovery, and purpose, all set against the backdrop of Zach Sobiech's remarkable life.

documents.title: Wrong Turn
documents.overview: Jen and a group of friends set out to hike the Appalachian Trail. Despite warnings to stick to the trail, the hikers stray off course—and cross into land inhabited by The Foundation, a hidden community of mountain dwellers who use deadly means to protect their way of life.
documents.plot:
Wrong Turn, also known as Wrong Turn: The Foundation, is a 2021 folk horror film directed by Mike P. Nelson and written by Alan B. McElroy, who wrote the 2003 original. The seventh entry in the series, it drops the cannibalism of earlier films. Charlotte Vega stars as Jen Shaw, with Adain Bradley as Darius, Bill Sage as Venable, Emma Dumont as Milla, Dylan McTee as Adam, Daisy Head as Edith and Matthew Modine as Jen's father, Scott.

Jen, her boyfriend Darius and their friends Adam, Milla, Gary and Luis arrive in a small Virginia town to hike the Appalachian Trail, meeting hostile locals, a strange woman named Edith and a mute girl, Ruthie. Leaving the trail to find an old fort, they lose Gary to a rolling tree trunk. Lost, they find a plaque from 1859 commemorating the "Foundation", settlers who believed the United States was about to collapse. Adam is caught in a trap and carried off by two men in animal-skull masks, and when his friends confront them, he breaks free and beats one to death. Milla is later impaled in a pit and killed with an arrow, and the others are captured and brought to the Foundation's hidden settlement. Its leader, Venable, holds a trial, sentences Adam to death for killing a man named Samuel and condemns the others to "darkness" for lying to save him. After Ruthie stabs Adam with a hidden blade when he takes her hostage, Venable beats him to death with the same log, and Luis is blinded with a hot poker. Jen saves herself and Darius by offering their usefulness to the community, and she becomes the wife of the widowed Venable. Six weeks later, Scott arrives searching for her, and after his guide dies in a trap he is captured. Jen frees him at night, but Darius refuses to leave. Helped by Ruthie, father and daughter find the blinded prisoners, including Luis, whom Jen mercy kills, and fight their way out with the help of armed townsmen, killing Edith among others. Months later, Jen finds her stepmother welcoming Venable and Ruthie to the neighborhood, and Venable, seeing that Jen is pregnant with his child, asks her to return; she agrees if he leaves her family alone. As the credits roll, she crashes their RV, stabs Venable and the driver to death and walks Ruthie back to her family's house.

Shot in Felicity, Ohio, in late 2019, the film was released in theaters for one night on 26 January 2021 by Saban Films. It received positive reviews, with 64% on Rotten Tomatoes, and grossed $4.8 million at the box office.

documents.title: If I Were a Rich Man
documents.overview: A man which wife is filing to divorce him wins 25 million EUR in the lotto, hiding her to prevent sharing the half of the prize.
documents.plot:
If I Were Rich (Spanish: Si yo fuera rico) is a 2019 Spanish comedy directed by Álvaro Fernández Armero, who wrote the screenplay with Ángela Armero and Tom Fernández. It is a remake of the 2002 French comedy Ah! Si j'étais riche. Álex García and Alexandra Jiménez star as the separating couple Santi and Maite, with Jordi Sánchez as a scheming bank manager, Adrián Lastra and Franky Martín as Santi's friends Marcos and Pedro, and Diego Martín, Paula Echevarría and Antonio Resines in supporting roles. Telecinco Cinema, the company behind the hit comedy Spanish Affair, produced it with Si yo fuera AIE, Think Studio and Ciskul, with the participation of Mediaset España and Movistar+.

Santi is a hapless man to whom every possible misfortune seems to happen. He loses his job, takes on unpleasant odd jobs to earn a little money and, with his marriage to Maite collapsing and a divorce under way, ends up sleeping in his camper van, collecting a stream of parking fines from a local officer who seems fixated on him. To make matters worse, a former high school classmate, once mocked for his weight, returns to town slim and flush with success and begins a relationship with Maite.

His luck turns when he gambles the last of his money on a lottery jackpot and wins 25 million euros. On the advice of the branch manager at his bank, he decides to keep the windfall secret, since revealing it while the divorce is still pending would oblige him to hand half of the prize to the wife he is leaving. Keeping the secret proves difficult. His new habits and spending do not go unnoticed by Marcos and Pedro, and the effort to conceal the fortune from Maite and everyone around him leads to a chain of lies, misunderstandings and farcical situations.

The film was shot in Asturias, including Gijón and the beaches of Salinas, Xagó and Verdicio, and in Madrid. Distributed by Paramount Pictures, it opened in Spain on 15 November 2019 and became a surprise box-office success, taking in about 12 million euros by February 2020. Critical reception was mixed. Fotogramas praised the lead couple and the scene-stealing supporting cast while finding the film formulaic, and Cinemanía felt it kept its honesty despite commercial tics and heavy product placement. El País called it uneven but watchable, while eCartelera and HobbyConsolas criticized its stale, often crude gags and forced Asturian accents, though several reviewers singled out Resines and Isabel Ordaz.

documents.title: Nostalgic Christmas
documents.overview: When Anne helps her father close the family's toy store, what she finds will help inspire an entire town that is need of some Christmas cheer.
documents.plot:
Nostalgic Christmas is a heartwarming film that explores the complexities of love, loss, and redemption during the holiday season. The movie delves into the theme of nostalgia, as its protagonist, Emma, returns to her small hometown after many years away, only to find herself reconnecting with old friends and rekindling past relationships.

At its core, Nostalgic Christmas is a story about the power of love and forgiveness to heal emotional wounds. Emma's journey is marked by a deep sense of longing and regret, as she grapples with the choices she made in the past and the opportunities she may have missed. Through her interactions with those around her, particularly a kind-hearted local baker, Emma begins to confront her own vulnerabilities and learn to let go of past hurts.

The film also touches on the theme of community and the importance of finding one's place within it. Emma's return to her hometown serves as a catalyst for her reconnection with old friends and acquaintances, who welcome her back with open arms. As she becomes more involved in the local community, Emma begins to feel a sense of belonging and purpose that she had been lacking.

Ultimately, Nostalgic Christmas is a story about the transformative power of love, forgiveness, and second chances. Through its exploration of nostalgia, community, and personal growth, the film offers a poignant reminder that it's never too late to rediscover ourselves and find happiness again.

documents.title: Things Heard & Seen
documents.overview: Catherine Clare reluctantly trades life in 1980 Manhattan for a remote home in the tiny hamlet of Chosen, New York, after her husband George lands a job teaching art history at a small Hudson Valley college. Even as she does her best to transform the old dairy farm into a place where young daughter Franny will be happy, Catherine increasingly finds herself isolated and alone. She soon comes to sense a sinister darkness lurking both in the walls of the ramshackle property—and in her marriage to George.
documents.plot:
I couldn't find any information on a movie titled "Things Heard & Seen" released in 2021 by Likely Story. 

However, I found that there is a movie titled "Things Heard & Seen" released in 2022, directed by Shari Springer Berman and Robert Pulcini, not Likely Story.

The movie "Things Heard & Seen" (2022) is a psychological thriller starring Amanda Seyfried as Catherine, a young woman who moves to the countryside with her husband, but discovers that their new home has a dark history. 

As for the main themes of the movie, it explores several ideas such as:

1. The power of secrets and hidden histories: The movie delves into the idea that the past can be both fascinating and terrifying, and how secrets can shape our present.
2. Isolation and loneliness: Catherine's move to the countryside is meant to bring her closer to nature and her husband, but she finds herself increasingly isolated and alone, highlighting the difficulties of building a new life in a remote area.
3. The blurring of reality and fantasy: As Catherine becomes more entrenched in the history of their home, she begins to question what is real and what is just her imagination, leading to a sense of disorientation and unease.

These themes are woven throughout the movie, creating a complex and suspenseful narrative that keeps the viewer engaged until the very end.

documents.title: Goblin Slayer: Goblin's Crown
documents.original_title: ゴブリンスレイヤー -GOBLIN'S CROWN-
documents.tagline: He does not let anyone roll the dice
documents.overview: Goblin Slayer and his party head up to the snowy mountains in the north after receiving that request from the Sword Maiden to find any information on the Noble Fencer that disappeared after leaving to slay some goblins. A small village gets attacked, they encounter a mysterious chapel, and something about how these goblins are acting bothers the Goblin slayer.  In order to save the captured Noble Fencer, the Goblin Slayer and his party head to an ancient fortress covered in snow to face off with a powerful foe and a horde of goblins!
documents.plot:
Goblin Slayer: Goblin's Crown is a 2020 Japanese animated dark fantasy film based on Kumo Kagyu's light novel series Goblin Slayer, illustrated by Noboru Kannatsuki. Produced by White Fox with the returning staff and cast of the 2018 television anime, it was directed by Takaharu Ozaki from a screenplay by Hideyuki Kurata, with music by Kenichirō Suehiro, and adapts the fifth volume of the novels. Yūichirō Umehara voices the title character, with Yui Ogura as Priestess, Nao Tōyama as High Elf Archer, Yuichi Nakamura as Dwarf Shaman, Tomokazu Sugita as Lizard Priest, Maaya Uchida as Guild Girl and Yuka Iguchi as Cow Girl.

In a fantasy world where adventurers take contracts from the Guild, the nameless Goblin Slayer is a silver-ranked warrior devoted solely to exterminating goblins, having survived as a child the goblin raid that destroyed his village. The Sword Maiden asks him and his party to travel to the snowy mountains of the north to learn what became of the Noble Fencer, a young noblewoman whose party of novice adventurers vanished after setting out to hunt goblins. Along the way they find a small village under attack and a mysterious chapel, and Goblin Slayer is troubled by the unusual way these goblins behave. They rescue the Noble Fencer, who has survived horrific abuse at the hands of her captors but refuses to abandon the fight, determined to recover the sword they stole from her and take revenge. The trail leads to an ancient fortress buried in snow, which the goblins defend like an army, and there the party must face a goblin leader able to wield magic, an ability previously believed to belong only to the human-like races. The Noble Fencer finds strength in her bond with Priestess and High Elf Archer as the battle unfolds.

Goblin's Crown premiered in Japanese theaters on 1 February 2020 and was licensed by Crunchyroll. Its main story runs about an hour, preceded by a recap of the television series. Reviews were mostly unfavorable. Kim Morrissy of Anime News Network gave it a D, arguing that condensing an entire novel into roughly sixty minutes left its emotional moments without weight and made the Noble Fencer's recovery abrupt; she also criticized the goblins' convenient intelligence, the stilted animation and the decision to make the creatures increasingly human-like, though she praised the music and ending theme. Other reviewers enjoyed the snowy setting and the action but also noted the long recap and rushed character development.

documents.title: Knock at the Cabin
documents.tagline: Save your family or save humanity. Make the choice.
documents.overview: While vacationing at a remote cabin, a young girl and her parents are taken hostage by four armed strangers who demand that the family make an unthinkable choice to avert the apocalypse. With limited access to the outside world, the family must decide what they believe before all is lost.
documents.plot:
Knock at the Cabin is a thought-provoking thriller that delves into the complexities of human nature, morality, and the true meaning of sacrifice. The film's narrative revolves around a group of four strangers who are held hostage by a mysterious figure known as Lev (played by Jonathan Groff), who demands that they make an impossible choice: save a young family or face certain death.

At its core, Knock at the Cabin is a movie about the human condition, exploring the depths of our capacity for empathy, compassion, and selflessness. The story raises questions about what it means to be a good person, and whether the ends justify the means. As the characters navigate this moral dilemma, they are forced to confront their own dark pasts, personal demons, and the true nature of their relationships with one another.

The film also touches on themes of faith, free will, and the consequences of our choices. Lev's character, in particular, serves as a catalyst for exploring these ideas, as he embodies a twisted sense of morality that challenges the characters to reevaluate their own values and principles.

Ultimately, Knock at the Cabin is a movie about the power of human connection and the resilience of the human spirit. Despite the darkness and intensity of the story, it ultimately offers a message of hope and redemption, suggesting that even in the most desperate of circumstances, there is always a way forward, and that the choices we make can shape us into better versions of ourselves.

documents.title: Old
documents.tagline: It's only a matter of time.
documents.overview: A group of families on a tropical holiday discover that the secluded beach where they are staying is somehow causing them to age rapidly – reducing their entire lives into a single day.
documents.plot:
Old is a 2021 American supernatural horror film directed by Mimi Leder and written by Goekpinar Gökce. The movie stars Gael García Bernal, Vicky Krieps, and Rufus Sewell.

The story begins with an elderly couple, Charles (Rufus Sewell) and Amelia (Vicky Krieps), who are struggling to cope with the loss of their daughter, Martha, in a tragic accident when they were young. They have been married for over 40 years and are now facing the reality of their own mortality.

The movie takes a dramatic turn when Charles and Amelia find themselves on a beach in Greece, where they meet two strangers, Mau (Gael García Bernal) and Abigail (Elle Fanning). The four characters form an unlikely bond as they spend the day together, sharing stories and laughter. However, things take a dark turn when Mau reveals that he has been searching for something on the beach, which leads to a series of eerie events.

As the day progresses, it becomes clear that time is not passing normally for these four characters. They are stuck in a time loop, reliving the same day over and over again. The characters try to make the most of their situation, but they soon realize that something sinister is at play.

Throughout the movie, the characters' pasts are slowly revealed through flashbacks and conversations. We learn about Martha's tragic accident, Charles and Amelia's struggles with grief, and Mau's motivations for searching for something on the beach. The story becomes increasingly complex as the characters try to unravel the mystery behind their time loop.

As the day repeats itself, the characters begin to experience strange and terrifying events. They are stalked by a mysterious figure, and they start to question their own sanity. The tension builds as the characters try to find a way out of the time loop and uncover the truth about what is happening to them.

The movie's climax features a dramatic confrontation between the characters and the sinister force behind the time loop. In the end, Charles and Amelia are able to break free from the loop, but not before they have to confront their own mortality and the consequences of their actions.

Overall, Old is a thought-provoking and suspenseful horror movie that explores themes of grief, loss, and the human condition. The film's unique premise and complex characters make it a compelling watch, even if it doesn't always follow traditional horror tropes.

documents.title: The Legion
documents.overview: Noreno, a half-Roman, is entrusted with the mission of crossing the snowy mountains of Armenia, swarming with Parthian patrols, to seek help for his slowly dying men.
documents.plot:
The Legion is a 2020 Spanish-American historical action adventure film and the directorial debut of the veteran Spanish producer José Magán, from a screenplay by Pedro Santamaria and Carmen Ballesteros. Inspired by the war between Rome and the Parthian Empire over Armenia in the years 58 to 63 AD, it stars Lee Partridge as Noreno, a half-Roman soldier, with Mickey Rourke as General Corbulo, Bai Ling as Amirah, Joaquim de Almeida as General Paetus and Vladimir Kulich as Marcus.

Opening titles set the story in Syria in 62 AD. Two Roman legions have become trapped in the snowy mountains of Armenia during the campaign against Parthia; surrounded by enemy patrols, the soldiers are slowly dying of cold and hunger. The main Roman army in Syria is still two weeks away on foot, and the passes between are infested with hostile forces. Noreno is chosen for a perilous mission across the frozen mountains, carrying an urgent message on which the fate of his besieged comrades depends, because he is an expert runner, even though he deeply resents Rome and everything its empire stands for. Meanwhile, Corbulo frets over the crisis in front of a bust of the Emperor Nero, and Amirah, in a single scene, urges him to accept martyrdom.

Noreno, who also narrates the film, sets off alone and spends much of his journey running through the wintry landscape, periodically stopping to fight Parthian soldiers who cross his path. Along the way he faces harsh weather and his own inner conflicts, rescues a young woman from being raped, is briefly captured by a bounty hunter, and is saved by an older man, an early Christian, with whom he has a long philosophical discussion. By the end of the mission the trek has become a journey of personal growth for Noreno, who finds that he has felt free for the first time.

Produced by Magol Films, Carbara Films and Equo Entertainment, the film was released in the United States by Saban Films on May 8, 2020, on video on demand and digital platforms. Reviews were negative. Tara McNamara of Common Sense Media gave it one star out of five. Frank Scheck of The Hollywood Reporter compared its premise to 1917, noted that the billed stars Rourke and Bai Ling have only brief roles, found the repeated running scenes monotonous, and wrote that Magán showed no flair for action, partly owing to budget limits, nor for drama, singling out an anguished monologue by Rourke that nearly erased memories of his work in Diner and The Wrestler.

documents.title: The Legend of La Llorona
documents.overview: While vacationing in Mexico, a couple discovers their son's disappearance is tied to a supernatural curse.
documents.plot:
The Legend of La Llorona is a 2022 American supernatural horror film directed by Michael Chaves and produced by Blumhouse Productions, not Saban Films. 

The movie revolves around the legend of La Llorona, a vengeful spirit who haunts rivers and lakes in Mexico, searching for her drowned children. The main theme of the film is the devastating consequences of grief and the destructive power of maternal love turned to madness.

La Llorona's character embodies the tragic tale of a mother driven by guilt and despair after losing her children due to her own actions. Her relentless pursuit of revenge against those who she believes wronged her serves as a cautionary tale about the dangers of unchecked emotions, particularly in women.

The film also explores the theme of cultural heritage and the importance of honoring one's ancestors and traditions. La Llorona's character is deeply rooted in Mexican folklore, and the movie delves into the rich history behind this legend, highlighting its significance in Mexican culture.

Furthermore, The Legend of La Llorona touches on the idea that trauma can be passed down through generations, affecting not only the individual but also their loved ones. This theme is skillfully woven throughout the narrative, adding depth and complexity to the story.

Overall, The Legend of La Llorona is a haunting tale that masterfully weaves together elements of horror, drama, and cultural heritage, creating a compelling narrative that explores the darker aspects of human nature.

documents.title: The Forest of Love
documents.tagline: Is it love or is it a lie?
documents.overview: A con man and a would-be filmmaking crew force themselves into the lives of two grief-scarred young women. But nothing is as it seems.
documents.plot:
The Forest of Love (Japanese: 愛なき森で叫べ, Ainaki Mori de Sakebe) is a Japanese crime thriller written and directed by Sion Sono, inspired by the murders, torture and extortion carried out in Kyushu from the mid-1990s by the serial killer Futoshi Matsunaga. It stars Kippei Shiina as the con man Joe Murata, Shinnosuke Mitsushima as Shin, Eri Kamataki as Mitsuko, Kyoko Hinami as Taeko, Young Dais as Jay and Yuzuka Nakaya as Mitsuko's sister Ami.

Two aspiring filmmakers, Jay and Fukami, befriend the shy Shin and introduce him to Taeko, who sets him up with her sheltered classmate Mitsuko. Years earlier the two women had been part of a group of schoolgirls who, after a friend named Eiko died in a car accident, jumped from their school roof; Mitsuko alone held back, while Taeko survived with a limp and a scar. Murata now resurfaces in Mitsuko's life, claiming he wants to repay fifty yen she once lent him, and woos her with a sports car. Mitsuko and Taeko recognise him as a swindler who once deceived Mitsuko's sister and Taeko's mother, yet he seduces Mitsuko, Ami and Taeko alike and leaves them scarred and burned.

Pretending to be rich, Murata offers to back the young men's film about his cons and then seizes control of it, revelling in cruelty. He coaches Mitsuko into strangling Jay on camera and has the body destroyed, and Taeko is shot dead by an unseen gunman while trying to escape. Using Jay's death, Murata blackmails and tortures Mitsuko's parents while Ami eagerly joins in, and a series of deaths engulfs the family. In a forest, Mitsuko confesses that she secretly hoped Murata and Shin would kill her sister, parents and Taeko. Shin shoots Mitsuko and Ami and reveals himself as the serial killer in the news; Murata escapes in a car driven by a woman resembling Eiko, while Shin pursues a vision of Eiko into the trees.

First screened in Tokyo in June 2019, the film was released on Netflix on 11 October 2019, followed in 2020 by a seven-episode extended cut, The Forest of Love: Deep Cut. Critics found it excessive and overlong but compelling; IndieWire's David Ehrlich praised Sono's feral energy, and Rotten Tomatoes reviews were positive.

documents.title: All My Life
documents.tagline: Based on a true love story.
documents.overview: It was a chance meeting started by one of Sol’s friends trying to chat up Jennifer. However, in the end, it was those two who hit it off. Sol enjoyed Jen’s smile, her effort, and how silly she could be. Jen enjoyed Sol’s cooking, his athleticism, and that he would join her in fun moments. As you can imagine, love bloomed, and things got serious. Jen’s investment in Sol led to her pushing him to follow his dreams and even move in to save money. Sol’s investment in Jen well, it led to him proposing. But what started as a liver tumor grew into full-on cancer, so with a diagnosis of 6 months to live, Sol and Jennifer try to make the best of it.
documents.plot:
All My Life is a 2020 American romantic drama film directed by Chris Collett and written by David Iserson. The movie follows the story of a young couple, Charlie (played by Charlie Plummer) and Liz (played by Zoe Kravitz), who are deeply in love but face an unexpected challenge when Charlie is diagnosed with a terminal illness.

The main theme of All My Life revolves around the complexities of love, mortality, and the human experience. The film explores the ways in which love can both bring people together and tear them apart, as Charlie and Liz navigate their relationship amidst the uncertainty of Charlie's impending death. Through their story, the movie delves into the emotional depths of grief, loss, and the search for meaning in the face of mortality.

The film also touches on the theme of acceptance and the importance of living in the present moment. As Charlie's condition worsens, he and Liz are forced to confront the reality of their situation and make difficult choices about how to spend their remaining time together. The movie ultimately becomes a poignant exploration of the human spirit, highlighting the resilience of love and the power of human connection in the face of adversity.

Overall, All My Life is a heart-wrenching and thought-provoking film that explores the complexities of love, mortality, and the human experience with sensitivity and nuance.

documents.title: C'mon C'mon
documents.overview: Johnny and his young nephew forge a tenuous but transformational relationship when they embark on a cross-country trip to see life away from Los Angeles.
documents.plot:
"C'mon C'mon" is a 2021 American comedy-drama film written and directed by Mike Mills. The movie follows the story of Walter, a recently widowed father who embarks on a road trip with his young daughter to find her estranged mother.

The main themes of "C'mon C'mon" include:

1. Grief and Healing: The film explores Walter's journey as he navigates the loss of his wife and finds ways to heal and move forward. Through his interactions with his daughter, he begins to confront his emotions and find a new sense of purpose.
2. Parenting and Nurturing: As Walter spends more time with his daughter, he learns to let go of his own emotional baggage and focus on nurturing her. This theme highlights the importance of parental love and support in helping children heal from trauma.
3. Identity and Self-Discovery: Throughout the trip, Walter's daughter encourages him to explore new places and try new things. As a result, Walter begins to rediscover himself and find his own identity outside of his role as a husband and father.
4. Human Connection and Community: The film showcases the importance of human connection and community in helping us heal and grow. Walter forms connections with various characters he meets on his journey, including a kind-hearted woman who becomes a source of support for him.

The movie features a nuanced exploration of these themes, often through subtle humor and poignant moments. Overall, "C'mon C'mon" is a heartwarming and thought-provoking film that celebrates the complexities of human relationships and the power of love and connection to heal and transform us.

documents.title: Texas Chainsaw Massacre
documents.overview: After nearly 50 years of hiding, Leatherface returns to terrorize a group of idealistic influencers who accidentally disrupt his carefully shielded world in a remote Texas town.
documents.plot:
Texas Chainsaw Massacre is a 2022 American slasher film directed by David Blue Garcia from a screenplay by Chris Thomas Devlin, based on a story by Fede Álvarez and Rodo Sayagues. The ninth installment of the franchise and a direct sequel to the 1974 original, it stars Sarah Yarkin, Elsie Fisher, Mark Burnham as Leatherface, Jacob Latimore, Alice Krige and Olwen Fouéré as Sally Hardesty. Filmed in Bulgaria in 2020, it was released on Netflix on February 18, 2022.

Nearly fifty years after the 1973 massacre, whose sole survivor, Sally Hardesty, never spoke publicly about it again, a group of young entrepreneurs arrives in the decaying Texas town of Harlow, hoping to auction its old buildings to investors and turn it into a fashionable community. They are Melody, her younger sister Lila, Melody's business partner Dante and his girlfriend Ruth. Lila is a survivor of a school shooting and is still haunted by the trauma. At a derelict orphanage they find an elderly woman, Ginny, still living there with a silent, hulking man. When they insist she has been evicted, Ginny collapses with a heart attack and dies on the way to hospital, and the man, Leatherface, murders the officers in the ambulance, kills Ruth and, wearing Ginny's face as a mask, returns to Harlow.

As a busload of potential buyers arrives for the auction, Melody and Dante return to the orphanage to retrieve their car keys, taken by a suspicious local mechanic, Richter, and discover that Ginny had in fact been wrongfully evicted. Leatherface attacks, killing Dante and Richter, and when a storm drives the buyers into their bus, he slaughters everyone aboard in a frenzy. Meanwhile Sally, now a hardened Texas Ranger, arrives in town to confront him at last. Leatherface ignores her demands that he remember what he did, and in the ensuing struggle Sally is fatally wounded, though she saves the sisters and urges Lila to stand and fight rather than spend her life running.

Lila and Melody finally manage to escape, but in a final shock, Leatherface pulls Melody from their car as they drive away and kills her, leaving Lila alone.

The film was developed after Legendary acquired the franchise rights from Lionsgate. The original directors, Ryan and Andy Tohill, were replaced by Garcia during production because of creative differences. The film received generally negative reviews; Rotten Tomatoes reported 30% approval, and Metacritic gave it 34 out of 100.

documents.title: Spirited
documents.tagline: Start your holidays on a high note.
documents.overview: Each Christmas Eve, the Ghost of Christmas Present selects one dark soul to be reformed by a visit from three spirits. But this season, he picked the wrong Scrooge. Clint Briggs turns the tables on his ghostly host until Present finds himself reexamining his own past, present and future.
documents.plot:
Spirited is a musical comedy film released on Apple TV+ in 2022, directed by Marc Silverstein and Sean Anders, and written by Will Ferrell and John Morris. The movie is an adaptation of Charles Dickens' classic novel "A Christmas Carol," with a modern twist.

The story follows William "Will" Ferrell's character, George Bailey, who is a successful businessman in New York City. However, his life takes a drastic turn when he meets a mysterious and charismatic stranger named Henry Cratchit (played by Ryan Reynolds), who claims to be the ghost of Charles Dickens himself.

As the story unfolds, Will begins to experience strange and supernatural events that make him question his own existence and the true meaning of Christmas. He is visited by three ghosts - Jacob Marley (played by Lin-Manuel Miranda), the Ghost of Christmas Past (played by Octavia Spencer), the Ghost of Christmas Present (played by Kate McKinnon), and the Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come (played by Will Ferrell in a dual role) - who guide him on a journey of self-discovery and redemption.

Throughout the film, Will's character undergoes significant development as he confronts his own flaws and shortcomings. He learns valuable lessons about the importance of kindness, generosity, and compassion, which ultimately lead to a transformation that changes his life forever.

The movie features a blend of humor, music, and drama, with a talented ensemble cast that brings the characters to life. The film's visuals are also noteworthy, with a unique blend of live-action and animation that adds to the overall sense of wonder and magic.

Overall, Spirited is a heartwarming and entertaining adaptation of "A Christmas Carol" that offers a fresh take on the classic tale. With its talented cast, witty script, and catchy musical numbers, it's sure to delight audiences of all ages.

documents.title: The Forgotten Battle
documents.overview: November 1944. On the flooded isle of Walcheren, Zeeland, thousands of Allied soldiers are battling the German army. Three young lives become inextricably connected. A Dutch boy fighting for the Germans, an English glider pilot and a girl from Zeeland connected to the resistance against her will, are forced to make crucial choices that impact both their own freedom and the freedom of others.
documents.plot:
I couldn't find any information on a movie titled "The Forgotten Battle" released in 2021 or any other year, directed by EO. 

However, I found that there is a documentary film called "The Forgotten Battle" released in 2021, directed by EO (Eduardo Ortiz). The film is about the Battle of La Loma, which took place on December 8, 1945, during the Philippine-American War.

If you're referring to this specific movie, I couldn't find any information on its themes. However, based on my research, it appears that the documentary explores the historical significance and cultural impact of the Battle of La Loma, as well as the experiences of Filipino soldiers who fought in the battle.

Unfortunately, without more information about the specific movie you're referring to, I couldn't provide a detailed analysis of its themes.

documents.title: Yummy
documents.overview: A young couple travels to a shabby Eastern European hospital for plastic surgery. The young woman wants a breast reduction. Her mother comes along for yet another face-lift. Wandering through an abandoned ward the boyfriend stumbles upon a young woman, gagged and strapped to an operating table; she is the result of an experimental rejuvenation treatment. He frees her, but does not realize he just caused the outbreak of a virus that will change doctors, patients and his mother-in-law into bloodthirsty zombies.
documents.plot:
Yummy is a 2019 Belgian comedy horror film directed by Lars Damoiseaux, who co-wrote the screenplay with Eveline Hagenbeek. Widely described as the first Belgian zombie film, it stars Maaike Neuville as Alison, Bart Hollanders as her boyfriend Michael, Benjamin Ramon as the orderly Daniel and Clara Cleymans as the hospital administrator Janja, with Annick Christiaens and Eric Godon in supporting roles. The story satirises the cosmetic surgery industry through a gory zombie outbreak in a shabby clinic.

Alison travels with Michael and her mother Sylvia to a cut-price cosmetic surgery hospital somewhere in Eastern Europe, where the renowned surgeon Dr. K is to operate on both women. Michael, a squeamish and anxious young man, is uneasy about the clinic's lax standards. He is given a tour by Daniel, a staff member who abandons him midway to steal drugs. Wandering alone, Michael discovers a restrained and muzzled woman in a back room and removes her muzzle just as Daniel returns.

The woman is a zombie, the result of a secret experimental treatment carried out in the facility. She frees herself and starts attacking patients and staff, and the infection rapidly spreads throughout the hospital. Michael interrupts Alison's surgery so that they can escape, but they become separated, and Alison goes in search of her mother, who is bitten while Alison tries to wheel her to safety. As the small group of survivors, including Daniel, attempt to escape through the infected corridors, they learn from Dr. K that the clinic accidentally created the virus during experiments, before he is killed by Janja, who is hiding secrets of her own. The night descends into increasingly grotesque set pieces involving liposuction machines, surgical tools and mutilated patients.

The film combines slapstick humour, splatter effects and social satire about vanity and the pursuit of youthful beauty, and it presents Michael's growth from a timid boyfriend to a reluctant survivor.

On Rotten Tomatoes it holds an approval rating of about 69 percent, with critics enjoying its gleefully gory practical effects while finding its humour crude and uneven.

documents.title: Dark Spell
documents.overview: Terror strikes when a heartbroken woman uses black magic to get her husband back.
documents.plot:
Dark Spell (Russian: Приворот. Чёрное венчание, Privorot. Chyornoe venchanie, literally "Love Spell: The Black Wedding") is a 2021 Russian supernatural horror film directed by Svyatoslav Podgaevsky, who co-wrote the screenplay with Natalya Dubovaya and Ivan Kapitonov. Podgaevsky, a leading figure in Russia's horror revival, had previously made Queen of Spades, The Bride, Mermaid: Lake of the Dead and Baba Yaga: Terror of the Dark Forest. Produced by Central Partnership, QS Films and Iney Productions, it stars Yana Enzhaeva and Konstantin Beloshapka, with Ilya Ermolov, Varvara Borodina, Sabina Akhmedova, Nikita Yuranov and Larisa Domaskina. It was released in English-speaking markets as Dark Spell.

Zhenya (Enzhaeva), a dressmaker, is devastated when she finds her boyfriend Kir (Beloshapka), an artist and the father of their baby daughter Polina, having sex with one of his models, and he pushes her away. Told that only a love spell can bring him back, she visits a Romani fortune-teller, Aza (Akhmedova), who instructs her to perform a ritual during the wedding of someone she knows. Zhenya chooses the wedding of her client Sonya (Borodina) and the doctor Viktor (Ermolov), and hides on the church balcony during the service to carry out the rite with candles and scraps of cloth, even eating raw meat. Afterwards she collapses on the church steps and is rushed to Viktor's hospital, while Viktor soon finds his new wife with another man, though Sonya protests she does not know what came over her. Kir does return to Zhenya, but his renewed love turns into frightening obsession and jealousy: he attacks her friends, chases her in a car, tries to encase her body in plaster and cuts off his own mother's finger at the dinner table to take a family ring for his proposal. Even after Kir's death the spell keeps its hold, turning Zhenya's life into a nightmare as his spirit pursues anyone standing between him and his beloved, and at one point she is trapped in a mortuary cabinet with his corpse. The story culminates in a ceremony in the church to break the spell.

Reviews were mixed. Gulnaz Davletshina of Kinoafisha praised its dramatic exploration of how an exhausted relationship can drive someone into a dark corner but felt the idea was underdeveloped, with too many demons and too little humanity. Moria awarded it three stars for heading into pleasingly dark places, while Brian Orndorf found it bland and lacking real menace.

documents.title: The Deer King
documents.original_title: 鹿の王 ユナと約束の旅
documents.overview: Following a brutal war, former soldier Van toils in a mine controlled by the ruling empire. One day, his solitary existence is upended when a pack of wild dogs carrying a deadly and incurable disease attack, leaving only Van and a young girl named Yuna as survivors. Finally free, the pair seek out a simple existence in the countryside but are pursued by nefarious forces. Intent on protecting Yuna at all costs, Van must uncover the true cause of the plague ravaging the kingdom—and its possible cure.
documents.plot:
The Deer King (Shika no Ō: Yuna to Yakusoku no Tabi) is a 2021 Japanese animated fantasy film directed by Masashi Andō and Masayuki Miyaji and produced by Production I.G, adapted from Nahoko Uehashi's novel, which won both the 2015 Japan Booksellers' Award and the Japan Medical Novel Award. Andō, an acclaimed animator on Princess Mononoke, Spirited Away and Your Name, made his directing debut and also handled the character designs and animation direction, while Miyaji had served as Hayao Miyazaki's assistant on Spirited Away. Taku Kishimoto wrote the screenplay. Shinichi Tsutsumi voices Van, with Ryoma Takeuchi as Hossal, Anne as Sae and Hisui Kimura as Yuna.

Van, once the leader of the Dokkaku, a fabled band of warriors, has been defeated by the mighty Tsuol Empire and enslaved in a salt mine. One night a pack of strange wild dogs attacks the mine, spreading a deadly illness known as Black Wolf Fever. Everyone dies except Van, who survives despite being bitten, and Yuna, a little girl he rescues. The pair escape and find refuge in the countryside, where Van comes to love Yuna like a daughter. The plague, however, has been deliberately unleashed by the king of Akafa, a vassal state that hopes to weaken the empire and regain its power.

Hossal, a brilliant physician of the empire, deduces that Van carries antibodies to the disease and sets out to find him in order to make a cure from his blood, while the assassin Sae is sent to hunt him down. The dogs are controlled by Kenoi, an aging man known as the King of Dogs, who has Yuna abducted to force Van to become his successor. Van follows her to a hidden village where survivors of Akafa, led by the warrior Ohfan, plot a rebellion against the Tsuol emperor with the help of the dogs. Hossal reaches the village and succeeds in making a serum from Van's blood. Van refuses Kenoi's legacy, but Yuna shares the same power and, in a trance, leads the pack toward the emperor. Van stops her just in time, breaks the spell and departs alone with the dogs, choosing to become their king so that Yuna can live in peace. Hossal uncovers why the people of Akafa had been protected from the fever, the rebellion is abandoned, and years later the grown Yuna glimpses the Deer King leading the pack in the mountains.

The film competed at the Annecy International Animation Film Festival in June 2021. Its Japanese release, delayed twice by the COVID-19 pandemic, finally took place on 4 February 2022 through Toho.

documents.title: The Guide to the Perfect Family
documents.original_title: Le guide de la famille parfaite
documents.overview: A couple in Québec deals with the pitfalls, pressure and high expectations of raising kids in a society obsessed with success and social media image.
documents.plot:
The Guide to the Perfect Family (French: Le Guide de la famille parfaite) is a 2021 Canadian comedy-drama film directed by Ricardo Trogi. Louis Morissette and Catherine Chabot star as Martin Dubois and Marie-Soleil Blouin, a married couple with a tendency toward helicopter parenting, with Émilie Bierre as Martin's teenage daughter Rose, from his previous marriage to Caroline, played by Isabelle Guérard. Xavier Lebel also appears. The story centres on the pressure that a father's ambitions place on his daughter.

At work, the middle-aged Martin hires a young man named Pier-Luc only because he is the son of a colleague. The new employee refuses to work under pressure, resents a heavy workload and will not accept criticism from his superiors, and when a major contract under his responsibility is lost, Martin misses out on an important promotion.
