documents.plot:
How I Became a Super Hero (Comment je suis devenu super-héros) is a 2020 French superhero film co-written and directed by Douglas Attal, adapted from Gérald Bronner's 2007 novel. Produced by Artémis Productions, Trésor Films and Shelter Prod with Warner Bros. France, it stars Pio Marmaï, Vimala Pons, Benoît Poelvoorde, Leïla Bekhti and Swann Arlaud, with Léonie Souchaud, Camille Japy, Gilles Cohen and Clovis Cornillac.

In a version of Paris where people with superpowers are part of everyday life, Lieutenant Gary Moreau (Marmaï), once the police liaison to the disbanded hero team the Royal Pack, investigates super-crimes. Paired with Cécile Schaltzmann (Pons), a newcomer from the financial brigade, he looks into a wave of incidents caused by a drug that grants temporary powers to ordinary people, such as a bullied teenager who takes revenge using fire. Moreau's friend Monte Carlo (Poelvoorde), a retired Royal Pack hero living with Parkinson's disease, points him toward an old villain, who turns out to have been killed and drained of blood to make the drug. Moreau also notices Lily (Souchaud), a schoolgirl whose electrical powers are just emerging.

The trail leads to Naja (Arlaud), the leader of a gang that kidnaps people with powers and turns their blood into narcotics. After the gang frees one of its dealers from a police station, it abducts Lily and her mother. Callista (Bekhti), a former Royal Pack heroine with precognitive visions who now runs a rehab program, reluctantly joins the investigation after two of her young patients die of overdoses. Moreau, who has hidden his own telekinetic powers for years, is captured and shot but survives. His friends then reveal his secret: while using his powers on a mission, he accidentally caused the explosion that killed Gigaman, Lily's father, and the guilt led him to give them up. Tracing Naja to a disgraced psychiatrist who once erased his childhood mind-control powers, the team storms his hideout. Moreau defeats the overdosing Naja and rescues Lily, and he emerges as a new hero, nicknamed Titan.

First announced at Comic Con Paris in 2015, the film closed the 2020 Deauville American Film Festival. It was subsequently sold to Netflix, which released it worldwide on 9 July 2021. Reviews were mixed: critics praised Poelvoorde's comic turn and some fresh ideas but felt the premise was underdeveloped.

documents.title: Pieces of a Woman
documents.overview: When a young mother's home birth ends in unfathomable tragedy, she begins a year-long odyssey of mourning that fractures relationships with loved ones in this deeply personal story of a woman learning to live alongside her loss.
documents.plot:
Pieces of a Woman is a 2020 drama directed by Kornél Mundruczó from a screenplay by Kata Wéber, partly based on their stage play. Vanessa Kirby stars as Martha, a woman who loses her baby during a home birth, with Shia LaBeouf as her partner Sean, Ellen Burstyn as her mother Elizabeth, Molly Parker as the midwife Eva, Sarah Snook, Iliza Shlesinger, Benny Safdie and Jimmie Fails. Martin Scorsese and Sam Levinson served as executive producers, and Howard Shore composed the score. It premiered at the Venice Film Festival in September 2020, where Kirby won the Volpi Cup for Best Actress, and was released by Netflix in January 2021.

Martha and Sean, a Boston couple, are expecting their first child. Sean, a construction worker helping to build a bridge across a river, resents Martha's mother, Elizabeth, a wealthy and domineering Holocaust survivor who has bought them a minivan. When Martha goes into labor at home, their regular midwife is unavailable and sends a colleague, Eva. The birth, filmed in a single continuous take of about twenty minutes, is long and painful. When the baby's heart rate drops, Eva tells Sean to call an ambulance. Martha gives birth to a girl who at first seems healthy, but the baby soon turns blue and dies despite Eva's attempts to revive her.

In the following months, the couple's grief drives them apart. At the coroner's office, Sean is desperate to know what went wrong, while Martha is reluctant to learn the details. They are told the cause of death has not been determined but that the baby suffered from a lack of oxygen, and Eva is charged with criminal negligence. Martha withdraws into silence, returns to work and refuses to talk about her loss, while Sean, a recovering alcoholic, relapses and begins an affair with Martha's cousin Suzanne, the lawyer handling the case. Elizabeth pressures her daughter to testify against Eva to secure justice. As the months pass and the bridge Sean is building nears completion, Martha must decide how to face the trial, her mother's expectations and her own grief.

Pieces of a Woman received generally positive reviews, with particular acclaim for Kirby's performance and the virtuoso birth sequence, although some critics found the rest of the film less compelling. Kirby was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Actress.

documents.title: Seance
documents.overview: At an elite boarding school for girls, six friends jokingly engage in a late night ritual, calling forth the spirit of a dead former student who reportedly haunts their halls. Before morning, one of the girls is dead, leaving the others wondering what they may have awakened.
documents.plot:
Seance is a 2021 supernatural horror slasher film written and directed by Simon Barrett, known as the screenwriter of You're Next and The Guest, in his feature directorial debut. It stars Suki Waterhouse as Camille Meadows, with Madisen Beaty, Inanna Sarkis, Ella-Rae Smith, Stephanie Sy, Djouliet Amara, Jade Michael, Seamus Patterson and Marina Stephenson Kerr. Set in an exclusive boarding school, the film blends ghost story and murder mystery.

One night at the Edelvine Academy for Girls, a clique led by the cruel and popular Alice plays a prank on their classmate Kerrie by staging an appearance of the Edelvine Ghost, the legend of a student who once took her own life at the school. Shaken, Kerrie returns to her room, where she glimpses a figure watching her; moments later the girls hear her scream and find that she has fallen to her death from her window.

Soon afterward, a new student, Camille Meadows, arrives to take Kerrie's place and is assigned her old room, where strange things begin to happen. After a fight with Alice and her friends, Bethany, Yvonne, Rosalind and Lenora, Camille and her roommate Helina are given detention with the group in the library, where Alice persuades them to hold a séance to contact Kerrie. To everyone's surprise, a spirit answers and warns them that they will be murdered. That same night Lenora vanishes, and the school assumes she has run away, but a blood-drawn symbol in her room suggests otherwise. As more girls die in apparent accidents, Camille, Helina and the remaining members of the clique must determine whether they are being hunted by a vengeful ghost or by a very human killer, while Camille hides secrets of her own.

Barrett plays with the conventions of the boarding-school ghost story before turning the film into a slasher mystery with an unexpected climax.

Seance was released by RLJE Films on May 21, 2021. Reviews were mixed: it holds 47 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus said Barrett has filmmaking flair but not enough to lift a somewhat pedestrian story, while IndieWire's Kate Erbland noted that it grows more convoluted as it goes on.

documents.title: Trauma Center
documents.tagline: The enemy is closer than you think
documents.overview: Lt. Wakes is a vengeful police detective determined to solve the murders of his partner and an informant, and joins forces with a witness injured during the shootings. After the killers pursue the witness across the abandoned floor of a hospital, she confirms Wakes's worst fears.
documents.plot:
Trauma Center is a 2019 American action thriller directed by Matt Eskandari from a screenplay by Paul Da Silva. Nicky Whelan stars as Madison Taylor, a young woman hunted through a hospital by two corrupt police officers, with Bruce Willis as the police lieutenant assigned to protect her. The supporting cast includes Tito Ortiz, Texas Battle, Catherine Davis, Tyler Jon Olson, Lala Kent and Steve Guttenberg. The film was produced by Randall Emmett and George Furla's Emmett/Furla Oasis Films, among others, and released by Lionsgate's Grindstone Entertainment Group.

The story is set in San Juan, Puerto Rico. Detective Pierce and Sergeant Tull, two crooked cops, murder an accomplice in a warehouse because his phone holds evidence against them. Madison, who has moved to Puerto Rico and works long hours to support her teenage sister Emily after their mother's death, finishes a shift at the coffee shop where she works and stumbles on the body of Tony Martin, the partner of Lieutenant Steve Wakes, who had been investigating the warehouse killing. Caught in the crossfire, she is wounded, and the bullet that remains lodged in her leg becomes the only piece of evidence that can tie the two killers to the murder.

Madison wakes up in hospital, where Wakes asks her to help his investigation and, for her own safety, has her moved to an isolation ward in an empty wing of the building. Pierce and Tull realize she is the key to tracing the crime back to them and come to finish the job. Trapped overnight in the locked-down ward, Madison desperately calls Wakes for help, but with the lieutenant mostly failing to keep her safe she must use the meagre resources of the under-stocked unit to evade and fight off the two men in a long game of cat and mouse if she is to get out of the hospital alive.

Trauma Center received a limited theatrical release in the United States on December 6, 2019. Reviews were largely negative. Writing in the Los Angeles Times, Noel Murray described it as essentially Die Hard in a hospital and praised Whelan's Willis-worthy performance, but felt that Willis's few scenes were a distraction and that the confined setting was a cost-saving measure rather than a creative opportunity. Blu-ray.com called it short but hopelessly bland, while Film Threat considered it an undemanding piece of fun for fans of the star. On Rotten Tomatoes, only a small minority of critics' reviews are positive.

documents.title: Four Good Days
documents.overview: A mother helps her daughter work through four crucial days of recovery from substance abuse.
documents.plot:
Four Good Days is a 2021 American drama film directed by Abby Kohn and Mary Marc. The movie stars Mila Kunis as Hannah, a mother struggling to cope with her daughter's opioid addiction.

The main themes of the movie Four Good Days revolve around:

1. **Motherly love and sacrifice**: The film showcases the unconditional love and devotion of a mother for her child, even in the face of adversity. Hannah's journey is driven by her desire to save her daughter from the clutches of addiction.
2. **Addiction and recovery**: The movie sheds light on the complexities of opioid addiction, highlighting the struggles of withdrawal, cravings, and the long road to recovery. It also explores the emotional toll of addiction on families and loved ones.
3. **Guilt, shame, and redemption**: Hannah's guilt and shame over her daughter's addiction serve as a catalyst for her journey. As she navigates the challenges of sobriety, she begins to find redemption and a sense of purpose.
4. **The complexities of mother-daughter relationships**: The film delves into the intricate dynamics between mothers and daughters, particularly in situations where addiction is involved. It raises questions about the responsibilities that come with parenthood and the blurred lines between love and enabling.

Throughout the movie, these themes are woven together to create a narrative that is both heart-wrenching and hopeful. Ultimately, Four Good Days is a powerful exploration of the human spirit's capacity for resilience, forgiveness, and transformation.

documents.title: The Stranger by the Shore
documents.overview: Abandoned after coming out, Shun befriends Mio just before he has to move. Years later, Mio returns with a confession. How will Shun feel?
documents.plot:
The Stranger by the Shore (Japanese: Umibe no Étranger) is a 2020 Japanese animated romantic drama directed by Akiyo Ohashi and animated by Studio Hibari, adapted from L'étranger de la Plage, the debut boys' love manga by Kanna Kii, published in English as Seaside Stranger. Fuji TV produced the film as part of its Blue Lynx label for boys' love anime. Kii, a former animator, supervised the production and designed the characters and Mina Kubota composed the music. Taishi Murata voices Shun Hashimoto and Yoshitsugu Matsuoka voices Mio Chibana, reprising their roles from an earlier drama CD, with Yū Shimamura as Sakurako and Kanae Itō and Sayaka Nakaya as the couple Eri and Suzu.

Shun is a gay novelist who has settled on a small island in Okinawa after being cut off by his family in Hokkaido when they learned of his sexuality. There he meets Mio, a high school student who has lost his mother and lives with relatives. When Shun reaches out to him, the boy's prickly reaction stirs painful memories of Shun's estrangement from his parents, yet the two gradually become close. Before anything can develop, Mio reveals that he must move away to the city, promising to keep in touch.

Three years later Mio, now an adult, suddenly returns to the island and declares that he is in love with Shun. Shun is attracted to him but holds back, wracked with guilt at the idea of depriving the younger man of a so-called normal life and doubting that Mio understands what being gay will mean. Complications arrive with Sakurako, Shun's childhood friend and former fiancée, whose arranged wedding ended when Shun came out to his parents during the ceremony and who still loves him. She comes to the island to persuade him to return to Hokkaido because his father is in poor health. Shun is determined to stay with Mio, but Mio urges him to go home and make peace with his family. Realizing that Mio's feelings are sincere and his advice is right, Shun decides to return to Hokkaido and asks Mio to go with him.

The film opened in Japanese cinemas on 11 September 2020, and Funimation began streaming it in North America and other territories in July 2021. Reviews were mixed to positive. Anime News Network gave it a B-minus, feeling that it needed more time to develop its characters, especially Mio, but offered tantalizing glimpses of a satisfying love story, while The Japan Times rated it 2.5 out of 5, arguing that the adaptation lost some of the strength of the excellent manga.

documents.title: Supernova
documents.overview: Sam and Tusker, partners of 20 years, are traveling across England in their old RV visiting friends, family and places from their past. Since Tusker was diagnosed with early-onset dementia two years ago, their time together is the most important thing they have.  As the trip progresses, however, their ideas for the future clash, secrets come out, and their love for each other is tested as never before. Ultimately, they must confront the question of what it means to love one another in the face of Tusker’s illness.
documents.plot:
Supernova is a 2020 British romantic drama written and directed by Harry Macqueen. It stars Colin Firth as Sam and Stanley Tucci as Tusker, a couple who have been together for two decades, with Pippa Haywood, Peter MacQueen and James Dreyfus in supporting roles. The film is an intimate two-hander about love, memory and the approach of loss.

Sam, a concert pianist, and Tusker, a writer, are long-term partners and amateur astronomers who set off in their old campervan across England toward the Lake District. The trip is meant to revisit places that have mattered to them, to reconnect with friends and family, and to bring Sam to what he says will be his final concert. The journey carries a heavy undercurrent, however: Tusker has been diagnosed with early-onset dementia, and his condition is steadily worsening. He is struggling to finish a new book and refuses to let Sam read it.

Along the way the couple bicker and tease each other with the ease of people who have shared a life, but the strain of the illness keeps breaking through. When Tusker wanders off with their dog and becomes disoriented, Sam is badly shaken, though he tries to hide his fear. They camp beside a lake they first visited at the beginning of their relationship and then stay with Sam's sister Lilly, who gently urges him to consider professional care. During the visit, a surprise gathering of friends brings both joy and sorrow, and Sam stumbles upon a discovery that reveals how Tusker has been privately planning to face the future on his own terms. The two men are forced into a painful confrontation about choice, dignity and what it means to care for someone you love.

Macqueen keeps the drama understated, relying on long conversations, landscapes and the quiet chemistry between the two leads rather than on melodrama.

The film premiered in competition at the San Sebastián International Film Festival in September 2020 and was released in the United States by Bleecker Street in January 2021 and in the United Kingdom by StudioCanal in June 2021. It was well received, with about 90 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 73, and the performances of Firth and Tucci were especially praised.

documents.title: Hocus Pocus 2
documents.tagline: Back and more glorious than ever.
documents.overview: 29 years since the Black Flame Candle was last lit, the 17th-century Sanderson sisters are resurrected, and they are looking for revenge. Now it's up to three high school students to stop the ravenous witches from wreaking a new kind of havoc on Salem before dawn on All Hallow's Eve.
documents.plot:
I have information on Hocus Pocus 2.

Hocus Pocus 2 is a 2022 American fantasy comedy film directed by Anne Fletcher and written by Jen D'Angelo. The movie serves as a sequel to the 1993 film Hocus Pocus, which was also produced by Walt Disney Pictures.

The story takes place 29 years after the events of the first film. Becca (Whitney Peak), the daughter of Max Dennison (Omri Katz), is now a teenager who has grown up hearing stories about her father's encounter with the Sanderson sisters, Winifred (Bette Midler), Mary (Kathy Najimy), and Sarah (Sarah Jessica Parker). The three witches were resurrected by Max's teenage sister Dani (Thora Birch) in an attempt to scare him away from his girlfriend.

The movie follows Becca as she discovers that the Sanderson sisters are still alive and living in Salem, Massachusetts. Winifred, Mary, and Sarah have been waiting for their next victim, which they believe will be a young girl with magical powers. However, when they discover that Becca is not only a witch but also the chosen one to defeat them, they become determined to kill her.

As Becca navigates her newfound identity as a witch, she must also confront the Sanderson sisters and their evil plans. Along the way, she meets a group of young witches who help her on her quest to stop the sisters and save Salem from their wrath.

Throughout the movie, there are plenty of nods to the original film, including cameos from some of the original characters. The movie also explores themes of identity, family, and the power of friendship and love.

Overall, Hocus Pocus 2 is a fun and lighthearted sequel that is sure to delight fans of the original film. With its blend of magic, humor, and adventure, it's a great addition to the Hocus Pocus franchise.

documents.title: The Card Counter
documents.tagline: He's Playing the Hand He Was Dealt.
documents.overview: William Tell just wants to play cards. His spartan existence on the casino trail is shattered when he is approached by Cirk, a vulnerable and angry young man seeking help to execute his plan for revenge on a military colonel. Tell sees a chance at redemption through his relationship with Cirk. But keeping Cirk on the straight-and-narrow proves impossible, dragging Tell back into the darkness of his past.
documents.plot:
The Card Counter is a 2021 American neo-noir thriller film written and directed by Paul Schrader. The movie stars Oscar Isaac, Willem Dafoe, and Tiffany Haddish.

The story follows the protagonist, Henry McCardel (Oscar Isaac), a professional gambler who suffers from PTSD after witnessing the murder of his family in a small town. He is haunted by the memories of that fateful night and struggles to form connections with others due to his emotional scars.

Henry's life takes a turn when he meets Catherine Clifton (Tiffany Haddish), a woman who claims to be a victim of a similar traumatic event. She convinces him to join her on a road trip, where they visit various towns and gamble at card tables. As they travel together, Henry begins to open up about his past, sharing the story of how he lost his family.

However, their journey is disrupted by the presence of LaGraine (Willem Dafoe), a ruthless and cunning gambler who seeks revenge against Henry for winning from him in a previous game. LaGraine's true intentions are shrouded in mystery, but it becomes clear that he has a personal vendetta against Henry.

As the story unfolds, Henry's past begins to catch up with him. He is forced to confront his demons and make amends with those who were wronged by him. The film builds towards a tense showdown between Henry and LaGraine, which ultimately leads to a dramatic confrontation that changes the course of their lives forever.

Throughout the movie, Schrader explores themes of trauma, guilt, and redemption. Henry's character is complex and multifaceted, struggling to find peace and forgiveness in a world that seems determined to hurt him. The film's use of long takes and atmospheric sound design adds to the overall sense of unease and tension, drawing the viewer into Henry's dark and troubled world.

The Card Counter received critical acclaim for its performances, direction, and writing. Oscar Isaac delivers a nuanced and emotionally charged performance as Henry McCardel, while Willem Dafoe brings his signature intensity to the role of LaGraine. The film's exploration of complex themes and moral ambiguity has been praised by critics, who have noted that it is both a gripping thriller and a thought-provoking drama.

Overall, The Card Counter is a gripping and unsettling film that explores the darker aspects of human nature. With its tense plot, atmospheric sound design, and outstanding performances, it is a must-see for fans of neo-noir thrillers and those who appreciate complex, thought-provoking cinema.

documents.title: Willy's Wonderland
documents.tagline: Their idea of fun is killer!
documents.overview: When his car breaks down, a quiet loner agrees to clean an abandoned family fun center in exchange for repairs. He soon finds himself waging war against possessed animatronic mascots while trapped inside Willy's Wonderland.
documents.plot:
Willy's Wonderland is a 2021 American horror comedy film directed by Zach Cregger and written by Cregger and Matthew Berkowitz. The movie stars Nicholas Hoult, Jay Baruchel, and Ryan Hansen.

The story begins with Arkin (Nicholas Hoult), a former convict who has just been released from prison after serving five years for a crime he didn't commit. He is hired to work at Willy's Wonderland, a struggling family-friendly restaurant in the middle of nowhere. The owner, Phil (Jay Baruchel), is desperate to save his business and offers Arkin a job with a promise that he will be able to spend time with his estranged father.

Upon arrival, Arkin discovers that the restaurant has been taken over by a group of violent and sadistic animatronic animals, including a giant bear, a rabbit, and a snake. The animatronics were created by Willy (Ryan Hansen), the former owner's son, who was obsessed with revenge against his father for abandoning him.

As Arkin tries to navigate his new job and reconnect with his father, he soon realizes that the animatronics are not just malfunctioning machines, but are actually alive and determined to kill anyone who enters the restaurant. The animatronics begin to hunt down and murder the employees, including Phil's daughter, making it clear that Willy has a personal vendetta against them.

Arkin teams up with a janitor named Delilah (Krysta Rodriguez) to survive the night and uncover the truth behind the animatronics' creation. Along the way, they discover that Willy was driven mad by his father's abandonment and created the animatronics as a twisted form of revenge.

As the night wears on, Arkin and Delilah face off against the animatronics in a series of gruesome and hilarious battles. The movie builds up to a climactic showdown between Arkin and Willy, who is revealed to be the mastermind behind the animatronic killings.

In the end, Arkin emerges victorious, but not without scars. He manages to defeat Willy and destroy the animatronics, saving the restaurant and its employees. The movie ends with Arkin reflecting on his experience and realizing that he has found a new sense of purpose in life.

Overall, Willy's Wonderland is a fun and entertaining horror-comedy that pays homage to classic '80s movies like Friday the 13th and Child's Play. With its over-the-top violence, witty humor, and memorable characters, it's sure to delight fans of the genre.

documents.title: I'm Your Woman
documents.overview: A woman is forced to go on the run after her husband betrays his partners, sending her and her baby on a dangerous journey.
documents.plot:
I'm Your Woman is a 2020 American comedy-drama film directed by Maria Pulera. The movie revolves around Marisa Wemstead, a suburban mom who pretends to be her husband's girlfriend in order to impress his wealthy and influential family.

The main theme of I'm Your Woman explores the complexities of identity, class, and social status. Marisa, as she navigates this new persona, must confront her own insecurities and desires, which are deeply rooted in her suburban upbringing. As she becomes more entrenched in this role, she begins to question what it truly means to be a woman, a partner, and an individual.

Throughout the film, the tension between Marisa's authentic self and her fabricated persona serves as a metaphor for the societal expectations placed on women, particularly those from lower socioeconomic backgrounds who are expected to conform to certain standards of behavior. The movie also touches on themes of loneliness, intimacy, and the performance of relationships in order to achieve social acceptance.

Ultimately, I'm Your Woman is a nuanced exploration of the human desire for connection and belonging, as well as the difficulties that arise when we try to fit into predetermined roles or expectations.

documents.title: The Princess Switch: Switched Again
documents.overview: When Duchess Margaret unexpectedly inherits the throne & hits a rough patch with Kevin, it’s up to Stacy to save the day before a new lookalike — party girl Fiona — foils their plans.
documents.plot:
The Princess Switch: Switched Again is a 2020 American Christmas romantic comedy film directed by Mike Rohl and produced by Brad Krevoy, the second installment in The Princess Switch trilogy. Vanessa Hudgens plays three look-alike roles: Stacy, now Princess of Belgravia; Margaret Delacourt, who is about to become Queen of Montenaro; and Margaret's scheming cousin, Lady Fiona Pembroke. Sam Palladio plays Stacy's husband, Prince Edward, Nick Sagar plays Stacy's best friend Kevin, Suanne Braun plays Margaret's assistant Mrs. Donatelli, Mia Lloyd plays Kevin's daughter Olivia and Lachlan Nieboer plays Count Antonio Rossi.

Two years after the events of the first film, Margaret unexpectedly inherits the throne of Montenaro after the king's death and his son's abdication. Overwhelmed by her new responsibilities, she has ended her relationship with Kevin, who now runs his Chicago bakery with his daughter Olivia. Stopping in Chicago on her way to the Christmas coronation, Stacy finds Kevin miserable and persuades him to come to Montenaro, even as her own marriage to Edward is strained by her devotion to royal duty. Kevin and Margaret reunite while decorating the palace for Christmas, but she remains preoccupied with royal affairs, and her charming chief of staff, Count Antonio, courts her and plants doubts in Kevin's mind about whether a commoner could ever be worthy of a queen. Meanwhile Margaret's cousin Fiona, an immature and greedy aristocrat who has squandered her family's fortune, hatches a plan to impersonate Margaret, be crowned queen and loot the royal treasury, with the help of her servants Reggie and Mindy. To give Margaret and Kevin time together, Stacy and Margaret switch places once more, and while the couple spend an afternoon at a Christmas park, Fiona's accomplices kidnap Stacy, believing her to be Margaret, and Fiona takes her place at the palace. With three identical women now in play, Margaret and Edward race to rescue Stacy and unmask the impostor before the coronation, while Antonio pursues schemes of his own.

The film was released on Netflix on November 19, 2020, and received mixed reviews, holding a 56% rating on Rotten Tomatoes; Variety's Dennis Harvey wrote that what it was really selling was Yuletide. The trilogy concluded with The Princess Switch 3: Romancing the Star.

documents.title: Blue Bayou
documents.tagline: It's not where you're from. It's where you belong.
documents.overview: As a Korean-American man raised in the Louisiana bayou works hard to make a life for his family, he must confront the ghosts of his past as he discovers that he could be deported from the only country he has ever called home.
documents.plot:
Blue Bayou is a 2021 American drama film directed by Justin Chadwick. The movie follows the story of Louis, a young man who was separated from his mother at a young age and grows up in foster care. He sets out to find her, only to discover that she has been living under an assumed identity in Louisiana.

The main theme of Blue Bayou is the search for identity and belonging. Louis's journey is driven by his desire to reconnect with his past and understand where he comes from. As he navigates this complex web of family secrets and lies, he must confront the reality that his mother's life has been built on a foundation of deception.

The film also explores the theme of trauma and its lasting impact on individuals. Louis's experiences in foster care have left emotional scars, and his quest to find his mother forces him to confront the pain and vulnerability he has carried with him for so long.

Furthermore, Blue Bayou touches on the idea of identity formation and the complexities of human relationships. The movie raises questions about the nature of family, love, and loyalty, highlighting the ways in which our experiences shape us and define who we are.

The film's narrative is also marked by a sense of longing and nostalgia, as Louis struggles to reconcile his past with his present. Through Louis's story, Blue Bayou offers a poignant exploration of the human condition, inviting viewers to reflect on their own experiences of identity, belonging, and the search for connection.

documents.title: Finding ʻOhana
documents.overview: Two Brooklyn siblings' summer in a rural Oahu town takes an exciting turn when a journal pointing to long-lost treasure sets them on an adventure, leading them to reconnect with their Hawaiian heritage.
documents.plot:
Finding ʻOhana is a 2021 American family adventure film directed by Jude Weng in her feature debut and written by Christina Strain. It stars Kea Peahu as Pili, a young geocaching enthusiast, and Alex Aiono as her older brother Ioane, with Lindsay Watson, Owen Vaccaro, Kelly Hu as their mother Leilani, Branscombe Richmond and Ke Huy Quan, whose appearance marked his return to acting. Described during development as an adventure in the spirit of The Goonies, it was produced by Ian Bryce after Netflix acquired the project in 2019.

Pili and her brother Ioane, known as E, are Hawaiian siblings raised in Brooklyn. Pili, an avid geocacher, wins a place at a summer camp, but instead the family travels to the island of Oʻahu with their mother to help her father, Kimo, who is struggling with health and financial problems. Bored and homesick, Pili discovers an old diary in her grandfather's studio, kept by the quartermaster of a ship whose crew mutinied and hid a treasure on the island centuries earlier.

Together with Casper, a nerdy local boy, Pili decides to follow the clues in the journal to find the treasure, which could save her grandfather's home. E, who has been dismissive of his Hawaiian heritage, joins the search along with Hana, a local girl he likes. The four venture into a network of caves, facing collapsing tunnels, flooded passages and dangerous traps. When they finally reach the treasure, Hana realizes that it is a sacred offering protected by the Night Marchers, the ghosts of ancient warriors, and the siblings' quest becomes a journey of reconnection with their family, culture and the meaning of ʻohana. An encounter with the spirits brings the family a final moment with the children's late father, and they decide to make Hawaiʻi their home.

The film celebrates Hawaiian culture, family and heritage, combining adventure with themes of identity and belonging.

Finding ʻOhana premiered on Netflix on January 29, 2021. It received generally favorable reviews, with 81 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 69.

documents.title: The Mauritanian
documents.overview: The true story of the Mauritanian Mohamedou Ould Slahi, who was held at the U.S military's Guantanamo Bay detention center without charges for over a decade and sought help from a defense attorney for his release.
documents.plot:
The Mauritanian is a 2021 American drama film directed by Kevin Macdonald, based on the book "Guantánamo Diary" by Mohamedou Ould Slahi. The movie stars Tahar Rahim as Mohamedou Ould Slahi, a Mauritanian citizen who was detained at Guantánamo Bay for over 14 years without charge.

The main themes of The Mauritanian include:

1. **Detention and Torture**: The film highlights the inhumane treatment of detainees at Guantánamo Bay, particularly Mohamedou Ould Slahi, who was subjected to physical and psychological torture.
2. **Human Rights and Justice**: The movie explores the struggles of Mohamedou Ould Slahi as he fights for his freedom and justice, highlighting the flaws in the US detention system and the importance of upholding human rights.
3. **Identity and Belonging**: Through Mohamedou's story, the film delves into themes of identity, culture, and belonging, showcasing the complexities of being a Muslim man from Mauritania in a foreign land.
4. **The War on Terror and National Security**: The Mauritanian critiques the US government's policies and actions during the War on Terror, questioning the morality and effectiveness of these measures.
5. **Redemption and Forgiveness**: As Mohamedou navigates his journey towards freedom, he must confront his past mistakes and seek redemption, highlighting the importance of forgiveness and personal growth.

The film received critical acclaim for its thought-provoking portrayal of these themes, with many praising Tahar Rahim's performance as a powerful representation of Mohamedou Ould Slahi.

documents.title: The Legend of Tomiris
documents.tagline: The queen born to magnify the steppe.
documents.overview: This is the story of the life of the great queen of the steppe - legendary Tomiris. She is destined to become a skillful warrior, survive the loss of close people and unite the Scythian/Saka tribes under her authority.
documents.plot:
The Legend of Tomiris is an epic historical drama that tells the story of Tomiris, the queen of Massagetae, who played a crucial role in the ancient world. 

At its core, the film explores themes of power, identity, and the struggle for independence. The movie delves into the complexities of being a woman in a patriarchal society, where Tomiris must navigate the treacherous landscape of politics and war to assert her authority and protect her people.

The film also touches on the theme of cultural heritage and the clash of civilizations. As a member of the Massagetae tribe, Tomiris is caught between her loyalty to her people and her duty to forge alliances with neighboring nations. This tension highlights the challenges faced by indigenous cultures in the face of external influences and conquests.

Furthermore, The Legend of Tomiris examines the human cost of war and the impact it has on individuals and communities. Through Tomiris's journey, the film conveys a sense of empathy and understanding for those affected by conflict, inviting viewers to consider the complexities of war and its consequences.

Overall, the movie offers a rich tapestry of themes that are both historically grounded and universally relatable, making it a compelling watch for audiences interested in epic historical dramas.

documents.title: Blithe Spirit
documents.overview: A spiritualist medium holds a seance for a writer suffering from writers block but accidentally summons the spirit of his deceased first wife which leads to an increasingly complex love triangle with his current wife of five years.
documents.plot:
Blithe Spirit is a 2020 romantic comedy film directed by Edward Simpson and written by Simon Elkhun and Paul Whitehouse. The movie is an adaptation of Noël Coward's 1941 play of the same name.

The main themes of Blithe Spirit (2020) include:

1. Love and relationships: The film explores the complexities of love, relationships, and marriage through the story of Charles Condomine, a writer who becomes involved with two women from different worlds.
2. Identity and self-discovery: As Charles navigates his relationships with Madame Arcati and Ruth, he is forced to confront his own identity and sense of purpose.
3. Class and social status: The film pokes fun at the class differences between the characters, particularly the contrast between Charles's humble background and that of his two love interests.
4. Ghostly encounters: The supernatural element of the story allows for commentary on the human experience, including the idea that our past experiences shape us in ways we may not even realize.

The plot follows Charles Condomine (played by Dan Stevens), a writer who is struggling to find inspiration after the death of his first wife. He becomes involved with Madame Arcati (Lesley Manville), a medium who helps him contact the ghost of his first wife, Elvira (Dakota Fanning). As Charles navigates his relationships with both women, he must confront the consequences of his actions and decide which path to take.

The film features a talented cast, including Lesley Manville, Dan Stevens, and Olivia Colman. Overall, Blithe Spirit is a charming and witty romantic comedy that explores themes of love, identity, and class in a unique and entertaining way.

documents.title: The Voyeurs
documents.tagline: How far will you go for one more look?
documents.overview: When Pippa and Thomas move into their dream apartment, they notice that their windows look directly into the apartment opposite – inviting them to witness the volatile relationship of the attractive couple across the street. But what starts as a simple curiosity turns into full-blown obsession with increasingly dangerous consequences.
documents.plot:
The Voyeurs is a 2021 American erotic thriller film written and directed by Michael Mohan. Shot and set in Montreal, it stars Sydney Sweeney and Justice Smith as a young couple who become obsessed with the lives of the neighbors they can see across the street, played by Ben Hardy and Natasha Liu Bordizzo. It was produced by Greg Gilreath and Adam Hendricks through their Divide/Conquer banner and was released by Amazon Studios on Prime Video in September 2021.

Pippa and Thomas move into their first apartment together and discover that their windows look straight into the loft opposite, where a photographer works and lives with a woman. Half joking, they nickname the pair Brent and Margot. Pippa, a trainee optometrist who feels neglected by Thomas, buys binoculars and starts watching the neighbors closely, seeing "Brent" bring models home while "Margot" is away. Thomas knows a trick for eavesdropping with a laser and a reflective surface, so the couple slip into the neighbors' Halloween party and Pippa leaves a mirror behind. They overhear a fight in which the woman accuses the man of cheating and he turns violent. Soon afterwards the woman, whose real name is Julia, turns up at Pippa's optical shop, and the two become friendly; Pippa learns that the husband is a well-known photographer named Seb. Unable to stop herself, Pippa uses Julia's wireless printer to expose his affairs, which leads Thomas to accuse her of being far too invested in strangers' lives. When the couple later appear to witness a death in the apartment across the way, guilt drives Pippa and Thomas apart, yet Pippa keeps watching Seb and eventually lets herself be drawn into his world, only to find that the game of watching and being watched is far more calculated than she had assumed.

The film received mixed reviews. Critics frequently compared it, mostly unfavorably, to earlier voyeuristic thrillers such as Rear Window and Body Double; it holds a 45% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 54 out of 100, indicating "mixed or average reviews". Its viewership on the streaming service nevertheless exceeded Amazon Studios' expectations.

documents.title: The Protégé
documents.overview: Rescued as a child by the legendary assassin Moody and trained in the family business, Anna is the world’s most skilled contract killer. When Moody, the man who was like a father to her and taught her everything she needs to know about trust and survival, is brutally killed, Anna vows revenge. As she becomes entangled with an enigmatic killer whose attraction to her goes way beyond cat and mouse, their confrontation turns deadly and the loose ends of a life spent killing will weave themselves ever tighter.
documents.plot:
The Protégé is a 2021 action-thriller film directed by Martin Campbell and written by Michael Finch, Miles Chapman, and Daniel Casey. The movie stars Michael Fassbender, Maggie Q, Abbie Cornish, and Jeremy Irons.

The story follows a legendary assassin named John (Michael Fassbender), who is known for his exceptional skills in the art of killing. He has been working alone for years, taking on high-paying jobs from wealthy clients. However, when he discovers that one of his targets is actually a young woman named Kukulkan (Abbie Cornish) who is being hunted by a ruthless crime lord named Boss (Jeremy Irons), John decides to take her under his wing and teach her the ways of the assassin.

As they embark on their mission together, John and Kukulkan form an unlikely bond, with John becoming a mentor to Kukulkan. However, as they delve deeper into the world of espionage, they realize that Boss is not just any ordinary crime lord, but a highly skilled and ruthless adversary who will stop at nothing to achieve his goals.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Boss has a personal vendetta against John, who had previously thwarted one of his plans. The stakes are raised when Kukulkan's past comes back to haunt her, and she is forced to confront her own demons in order to survive.

Throughout the film, the action sequences are intense and well-choreographed, with Fassbender delivering a performance that showcases his impressive physicality and acting range. Maggie Q also shines as the tough-as-nails Sarah, who becomes embroiled in John's world and finds herself drawn into the conflict between him and Boss.

The film's climax features an epic showdown between John and Boss, with Kukulkan playing a crucial role in the outcome. In the end, John emerges victorious, but not without scars, both physical and emotional. As he looks out over the city, it is clear that his work as an assassin is far from over.

Overall, The Protégé is a gripping action-thriller that explores themes of mentorship, loyalty, and redemption. With its talented cast, slick action sequences, and intricate plot, it's a must-see for fans of the genre.

documents.title: The Unforgivable
documents.tagline: No one walks free of their past
documents.overview: A woman is released from prison after serving a sentence for a violent crime and re-enters a society that refuses to forgive her past.
documents.plot:
The Unforgivable is a 2021 American crime drama film directed by Nora Fingscheidt and written by Sarah Burgess. The movie stars Sandra Bullock, Jon Bernthal, and Viola Davis.

The story revolves around Ruth Slater (Sandra Bullock), a woman who has just been released from prison after serving 18 years for the murder of her husband's mistress. Ruth is determined to rebuild her life and reconnect with her estranged daughter, Faith (Julia Long). However, she faces numerous challenges as she tries to reintegrate into society.

Ruth lands a job at a local nursing home, where she meets a new colleague, Nona (Viola Davis), who becomes a source of support and guidance. As Ruth navigates her new life, she also encounters a series of obstacles, including a hostile landlord, a difficult boss, and a complicated relationship with Faith.

Throughout the film, Ruth's character is revealed through a series of flashbacks that show her past mistakes and the events leading up to her imprisonment. The film also explores themes of redemption, forgiveness, and personal growth as Ruth tries to make amends for her past wrongdoings.

As the story unfolds, Ruth faces a series of challenges that test her resolve and force her to confront her demons. Along the way, she meets a new love interest, John (Jon Bernthal), who becomes a source of comfort and support.

The film's title, The Unforgivable, refers to Ruth's past crime, which is considered unforgivable by many people. However, as the story progresses, it becomes clear that forgiveness is not always easy or straightforward. Ultimately, the film suggests that true forgiveness requires effort, understanding, and a willingness to confront one's own flaws and mistakes.

The Unforgivable received widespread critical acclaim for its performances, particularly from Sandra Bullock and Viola Davis. The film was praised for its nuanced exploration of complex themes and its thoughtful portrayal of a flawed but ultimately redeemable protagonist.

documents.title: The Ice Road
documents.tagline: This mission is on thin ice.
documents.overview: After a remote diamond mine collapses in far northern Canada, an ice road driver must lead an impossible rescue mission over a frozen ocean to save the trapped miners.
documents.plot:
The Ice Road is a 2021 American action thriller written and directed by Jonathan Hensleigh. Liam Neeson stars alongside Laurence Fishburne, Benjamin Walker, Amber Midthunder, Marcus Thomas, Holt McCallany, Martin Sensmeier, Matt McCoy and Matt Salinger. Influenced by Henri-Georges Clouzot's 1953 film The Wages of Fear, it follows a team of truck drivers hauling vital equipment across frozen lakes to save workers trapped in a collapsed mine.

When an explosion at a diamond mine in northern Manitoba traps 26 miners, the clock starts ticking on any rescue. In North Dakota, trucker Mike McCann and his younger brother Gurty, an Iraq War veteran living with PTSD and aphasia, lose their jobs after Mike punches a co-worker for mocking Gurty. They travel to Winnipeg and join a rescue convoy led by veteran driver Jim Goldenrod, who has been hired to deliver heavy wellheads needed to reach the miners. The team also includes Tantoo, a young Indigenous driver whose brother is among the trapped men, and Varnay, an insurance actuary representing the mining company, Katka.

The journey across the thawing ice road proves deadly. Goldenrod's truck breaks down and he is lost when the ice gives way, and the survivors soon discover that the accident was no misfortune: Varnay has been sabotaging the convoy on behalf of Katka's general manager, who wants to avoid the company being held responsible for the disaster. After Varnay leaves Mike and Gurty for dead and abducts Tantoo, the brothers fight their way back through avalanches, cracking ice and armed contractors. Mike eventually kills Varnay, but Gurty dies saving the last truck on a collapsing bridge. Mike and Tantoo reach the mine in time to free the miners, and the corrupt manager is fired and arrested.

The film was shot in and around Winnipeg, including Gimli and Île-des-Chênes, in February 2020. Netflix acquired the US rights for $18 million and released it on June 25, 2021, when it became the most-streamed film on the service in its debut weekend; Amazon Prime Video released it in the United Kingdom. Reviews were mixed, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting a 44% approval rating from 89 critics and a consensus describing it as a predictable downhill trundle despite Neeson's continued appeal as an action hero. A sequel, Ice Road: Vengeance, was released in June 2025.

documents.title: Don't Look Up
documents.overview: Two American astronomers attempt to warn humankind about an approaching comet that will wipe out life on planet Earth.
documents.plot:
Don't Look Up is a 2021 American satirical science fiction film directed by Adam McKay from a screenplay by McKay and David Sirota, based on the 2018 novel of the same name by Diamond Ken Smith. The movie stars Leonardo DiCaprio and Jennifer Lawrence as two astronomers trying to warn the world about an impending comet impact.

The story begins with Dr. Randall Mindy (DiCaprio), a low-level astronomer at South Boston University, who discovers that a massive comet is on a collision course with Earth. He shares his findings with his colleague, Dr. Kate Dibiasky (Lawrence), and together they try to alert the government and the media about the impending disaster.

However, their warnings fall on deaf ears as politicians and media outlets are more interested in sensationalizing the story for ratings and clicks than taking it seriously. The comet's impact is predicted to be catastrophic, causing widespread destruction and potentially wiping out humanity.

As the comet draws closer, Mindy and Dibiasky try to find a way to get their message heard by the world. They enlist the help of a washed-up talk show host, Brie Evantee (Meryl Streep), who agrees to broadcast their warnings to her audience. However, even this plan is hijacked by the media's desire for ratings, and Dibiasky becomes a reluctant celebrity.

Meanwhile, Mindy's relationship with his girlfriend, Dr. Rachel Drayton (Cate Blanchett), begins to fray as she tries to balance her own career ambitions with her growing concern about the comet. The couple eventually breaks up, leaving Mindy feeling isolated and disconnected from the world around him.

As the comet hurtles towards Earth, Mindy and Dibiasky's warnings become increasingly desperate and urgent. They try to find a way to deflect or destroy the comet, but their efforts are met with bureaucratic red tape and corporate interests that prioritize profits over people.

The film builds towards a climactic finale as the comet makes its final approach. In a last-ditch effort, Mindy and Dibiasky team up with a group of eccentric billionaires, including Captain Dick Todd (Rob Morgan), to launch a private rocket into space in an attempt to deflect the comet.

In the end, the plan succeeds, but not without significant collateral damage and loss of life. The film ends on a bleak note, with Mindy and Dibiasky reflecting on the futility of their efforts and the world's continued apathy towards the dangers of climate change and existential threats.

Throughout the film, McKay uses satire to critique the media's role in shaping public opinion, the failures of government bureaucracy, and the complacency of wealthy elites. The movie is a scathing commentary on our society's inability to confront the harsh realities of climate change and its devastating consequences.

documents.title: Scream
documents.overview: Twenty-five years after a streak of brutal murders shocked the quiet town of Woodsboro, a new killer has donned the Ghostface mask and begins targeting a group of teenagers to resurrect secrets from the town’s deadly past.
documents.plot:
Scream is a 2022 American slasher film written by James Vanderbilt and Guy Busick, with Matt Bettinelli-Olpin and Tyler Gillett directing. The fifth instalment of the Scream series and a sequel to Scream 4 (2011), it is the first not directed by Wes Craven, who died in 2015 and to whom it is dedicated. Melissa Barrera and Jenna Ortega play the sisters Sam and Tara Carpenter, alongside Jack Quaid, Mikey Madison and Dylan Minnette, with Neve Campbell, Courteney Cox and David Arquette returning as Sidney Prescott, Gale Weathers and Dewey Riley.

Twenty-five years after the original Woodsboro murders, teenager Tara Carpenter is attacked by a new Ghostface and hospitalised. Her estranged older sister Sam returns from Modesto with her boyfriend Richie and meets Tara's friends Wes, Liv, Amber and the twins Chad and Mindy Meeks-Martin. After Vince, the nephew of original killer Stu Macher, is murdered, Sam confides to Tara that she has been haunted by visions of Billy Loomis, who she learned as a teenager was her biological father, a discovery that broke up their parents' marriage and drove her away from home. Sam and Richie turn to Dewey, now divorced from Gale, who warns Gale and Sidney. Mindy reasons that the killer is staging a "requel", targeting a new generation while using Sam's link to Billy to draw in the survivors of the past.

Ghostface murders Wes and his mother, Sheriff Judy Hicks, and attacks Tara and Richie at the hospital; the sisters escape, but Dewey is killed trying to finish off the masked killer. Sidney and Gale arrive and follow Sam to a party at Amber's house, Stu's old home and the scene of the first massacre. There Amber shoots Liv and is unmasked as Ghostface, and Richie, revealed as her accomplice, stabs Sam. The pair, fans of the Stab movies who met online, explain that they were disgusted by the latest instalment and set out to inspire a new one based on real killings, with Sam as their scapegoat. In the fight that follows, Gale shoots Amber, who falls onto a lit stove, and Sam, guided by a vision of Billy, kills Richie. When the burned Amber attacks again, Tara shoots her dead. Gale opts to write a tribute to Dewey instead of a book about the killers.

Released by Paramount Pictures on January 14, 2022, the film grossed $138 million worldwide on a $24 million budget. Reviews were generally positive (76% on Rotten Tomatoes), praising its direction, cast and tribute to Craven. A sequel, Scream VI, followed in 2023.

documents.title: Plane
documents.tagline: The crash was only the beginning.
documents.overview: After a heroic job of successfully landing his storm-damaged aircraft in a war zone, a fearless pilot finds himself between the agendas of multiple militias planning to take the plane and its passengers hostage.
documents.plot:
Plane is a 2023 American action thriller written by Charles Cumming and J. P. Davis and directed by Jean-François Richet. Gerard Butler stars as a commercial pilot who must team up with a suspected murderer after an emergency landing in hostile territory, with Mike Colter, Yoson An, Tony Goldwyn and Daniella Pineda in supporting roles.

Brodie Torrance, a Scottish former RAF pilot, captains Trailblazer Airlines Flight 119 from Singapore to Honolulu by way of Tokyo. Among the fourteen passengers is Louis Gaspare, a fugitive wanted for homicide who is being extradited to Canada in the custody of an RCMP officer. Told by a superior not to change course over the South China Sea despite a severe storm, Brodie flies on until lightning knocks out the avionics, and turbulence kills a flight attendant and the officer. Brodie and his co-pilot, Samuel Dele, manage to put the aircraft down on a road on Jolo, a remote island in the southern Philippines controlled by rebels. In New York, the airline's crisis manager, David Scarsdale, learns that local authorities will need a full day to respond and hires a team of private mercenaries to go in.

Brodie heads into the jungle with Louis, a former French Foreign Legionnaire. At a deserted warehouse he reaches the airline and his daughter by phone before killing a rebel who attacks him, and Louis dispatches the others; the pair learn that the militants kidnap foreigners for ransom. By the time they return, the rebel leader Datu Junmar has seized the passengers and crew, executing a couple who tried to run. Brodie and Louis capture two looters, force them to reveal where the base is, and leave a note for rescuers. They break into the camp and get the hostages onto a bus, but when more rebels close in, Brodie stays behind as a diversion and is about to be executed when the mercenaries arrive. Everyone retreats to the plane; while the pilots restart the aircraft, Louis and the mercenaries hold off the attackers. Louis stays behind and disappears into the jungle with a bag of ransom money, and Junmar is killed by the landing gear as the plane takes off. Brodie lands the crippled plane on nearby Siasi and calls his daughter to say he is coming home.

Shot in Puerto Rico after passing from Lionsgate to Solstice Studios and back, Plane was released by Lionsgate on January 13, 2023. It grossed $74.5 million worldwide and received generally favourable reviews, with 78% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 62.

documents.title: Dear Zoe
documents.overview: Tess enlists her biological father - a lovable slacker from the wrong side of the tracks - and the charming juvenile delinquent next door to help her come to grips with the death of her little sister.
documents.plot:
Dear Zoe is an American drama of 2022 directed by Gren Wells from a screenplay by Marc Lhormer and Melissa Martin, adapted from Philip Beard's novel of 2005. Sadie Sink stars as Tess DeNunzio, a grieving teenager in Pittsburgh, with Theo Rossi as her father Nick, Kweku Collins as her neighbour Jimmy Freeze, Jessica Capshaw as her mother Elly, Justin Bartha as her stepfather David and Vivien Lyra Blair as her younger half-sister Em.

Sixteen-year-old Tess lives with her mother, stepfather and Em. Her three-year-old half-sister Zoe was killed by a hit-and-run driver on the day of the September 11 attacks, while Tess was meant to be watching her. Since then she has helped David look after Em while Elly battles depression, and in family therapy she feels shut out of her parents' grief. When she learns that her mother has been carrying on an emotional affair with a much younger grocery clerk, Tess breaks down and moves in with her biological father, a German Shepherd breeder living in poorer Braddock, though she feels guilty about leaving Em behind.

Tess cares for one of Nick's puppies and he drives Em home from school so the sisters can still meet, but a hymn at church brings back 9/11 and sends her fleeing in tears. She is drawn to Jimmy, a neighbour Nick warns her to avoid, and realises that her father sells drugs from his truck. Jimmy starts climbing through her window at night; he talks of his mother's death and his time in a correctional facility, and they fall in love while working summer jobs at the Kennywood amusement park. Weekly calls with Elly help mother and daughter heal. On Tess's seventeenth birthday, Nick and Jimmy are both arrested, revealing that Jimmy deals with her father. That night Tess finally tells Jimmy the truth: she missed the bus, ran indoors to watch the news of the attacks, and came back to see Zoe step off the curb into the path of a car. Jimmy still loves her. Tess returns home, weeps on the spot where Zoe fell and reconciles with her mother, David and Em.

Shot in Pittsburgh with a mostly local crew in late 2019, after the novel had been optioned since 2010, the film was released in select cinemas and on demand on 4 November 2022. It holds 71% on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: Wander
documents.overview: After getting hired to probe a suspicious death in the small town of Wander, a mentally unstable private investigator becomes convinced the case is linked to the same 'conspiracy cover up' that caused the death of his daughter.
documents.plot:
Wander is an American thriller of 2020 directed by April Mullen from a script by Tim Doiron, following two conspiracy theorists drawn into a murder investigation in the desert Southwest. Aaron Eckhart stars as Arthur Bretnik, with Tommy Lee Jones as his friend Jimmy Cleats, Katheryn Winnick as the mysterious Elsa Viceroy, Heather Graham as his lawyer Shelly Luscomb, Raymond Cruz as Sheriff Luis Santiago and Brendan Fehr as FBI agent Nick Cassidy.

Bretnik, a mentally fragile former detective turned private investigator, has never recovered from the death of his daughter in a car crash. As a detective he once examined a corpse whose chest seemed to have burst open from within, a body later stolen from the morgue. Now he and Cleats host a conspiracy podcast. A listener, Elena Guzman, hires him to look into her daughter Zoe's death in the small New Mexico town of Wander, which she is convinced was murder disguised by a cover-up. Convinced he is being followed, Bretnik tails two men in an old Jeep, discovers they are moving a woman's body, and finds an underground laboratory where captives are implanted with microchips. With Cleats, he learns that his clients' names were false; the woman who hired him attacks him, then dies when her chip explodes, and the two bury her in the desert. Before raiding the lab to film evidence, Bretnik mails an envelope.

The story jumps ahead to Bretnik being arrested by Cassidy after a shoot-out. Under questioning he recounts how Cleats was shot in the lab, how Elsa, apparently a CIA operative, and Santiago enlisted him to assassinate the chips' inventor, Victor Canton, and how Elsa gunned down the others, including Santiago, before letting Bretnik kill Canton. Shelly then tells him that his medication can cause delusions, that the garage was empty and derelict, and that Cleats's decapitated body was found in his car. Awaiting commitment, Bretnik is visited by Elsa and a living Cleats, who reveal that he was used all along to tie up loose ends and take the blame. In the institution he digs into his chest with a stolen pen and pulls out a microchip, laughing, while his envelope of photographs reaches Shelly.

Shot in Carrizozo and Ruidoso, New Mexico, in 2019, the film was released by Saban Films in December 2020. Critics praised Eckhart but not the twisting story, giving it 32% on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: Benny Loves You
documents.overview: Jack, a man desperate to improve his life, throws away his beloved childhood plush, Benny. It’s a move that has disastrous consequences when Benny springs to life with deadly intentions!
documents.plot:
Benny Loves You is a 2019 British horror comedy written, directed, edited and produced by Karl Holt, who also plays the lead role. The cast includes Claire Cartwright, George Collie, James Parsons, David Wayman and Lydia Hourihan. A low-budget entry in the killer-toy subgenre, the film premiered at the Buenos Aires Rojo Sangre festival in November 2019 before playing other genre festivals and reaching wider release.

After a brief prologue in which a discarded teddy bear takes violent revenge on the spoiled girl who replaced it, the story turns to Jack, a toy designer in his mid-thirties who still lives with his parents and relies on them for nearly everything. On his 35th birthday they die in a freak accident, and months later Jack is struggling to cope with the bills, the upkeep of the house and an estate agent pressing him to sell. At work he is overshadowed by Richard, a smug rival who has won the Designer of the Year award, and after a string of failed ideas his boss Ron demotes him to a lower-paid job.

Resolving to finally grow up, Jack decides to sell the house and packs away his childhood toys, reluctantly throwing out Benny, the plush bear he loved as a boy. Benny, however, has other plans. The bear destroys Jack's other toys and begins killing anyone he sees as a threat to his friend, leaving Jack to clean up the gory aftermath and dodge two bumbling police officers. Jack strikes a bargain with Benny to stop the killings, and the toy's presence unexpectedly inspires new designs that impress Ron. At the same time Jack begins a romance with Dawn, a technology consultant at his company. Benny's jealousy and enthusiasm for violence keep escalating, however, and Jack is forced to decide how far he will go to protect the people in his new life from his old best friend.

The film was well received for a micro-budget production. It holds a favorable score on Rotten Tomatoes, whose critics' consensus described it as a zany, enjoyably macabre and clever horror comedy with a lovable villain. Anton Bitel of Sight and Sound highlighted its comic treatment of a hero who has to put childish things behind him.

documents.title: The Unbearable Weight of Massive Talent
documents.original_title: The Unbearable Weight of Massive Talent
documents.overview: Creatively unfulfilled and facing financial ruin, Nick Cage must accept a $1 million offer to attend the birthday of a dangerous superfan. Things take a wildly unexpected turn when Cage is recruited by a CIA operative and forced to live up to his own legend, channeling his most iconic and beloved on-screen characters in order to save himself and his loved ones.
documents.plot:
The Unbearable Weight of Massive Talent is a 2022 American action comedy directed by Tom Gormican, who co-wrote it with Kevin Etten. Nicolas Cage stars as a fictionalized version of himself, alongside Pedro Pascal as Javi Gutiérrez, Sharon Horgan, Lily Mo Sheen, Tiffany Haddish, Ike Barinholtz and Neil Patrick Harris.

Nick Cage's career is stalling after he misses out on several major roles, and he is plagued by visions of "Nicky", his younger, more successful self, while years of neglect have strained his bond with his ex-wife, Olivia, and daughter, Addy. After losing a coveted part and embarrassing himself at Addy's birthday party, he announces his retirement and accepts his agent's offer of $1 million to attend the birthday of Javi, a billionaire fan in Mallorca. Though irritated at first by Javi's neediness, Nick warms to him over a shared love of movies such as The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari and Paddington 2. CIA agents Vivian and Martin then tell Nick that Javi, who they say is an arms dealer, has kidnapped María Delgado, the daughter of a Catalan politician, to force her father out of an election. Doubtful but willing, Nick plants cameras in Javi's compound and announces their film partnership as a pretext to stay and search for María. After an LSD-fueled misadventure, they decide their movie should be about their friendship. When Javi brings Nick's family to the villa, they rebuff Nick's apology.

Javi's cousin Lucas is revealed as the real arms dealer and María's kidnapper; he warns Javi that Nick is working with the CIA and demands that he kill him. Neither man can go through with it, and when Lucas's men attack, they discover Addy has been abducted too. At the CIA safe house, Martin is found dead and Vivian dies holding off Lucas's men. Nick and Olivia pose as a criminal couple to approach Lucas and, though he sees through it, escape with Addy and María, racing for the American embassy as Javi stays behind to delay him. When Lucas corners Nick, Addy throws him a knife and he kills Lucas, a moment that becomes a scene in the film Nick and Javi later complete. At its premiere, Nick congratulates Javi and goes home with his family to watch Paddington 2.

The film premiered at South by Southwest on March 12, 2022, and Lionsgate released it on April 22. It grossed $29.1 million against a $30 million budget. Reviews were positive, with 87% on Rotten Tomatoes and 68 on Metacritic, praising Cage and Pascal's chemistry.

documents.title: La Casa
documents.overview: Responding to an urgent call for help, a police officer becomes trapped by the evil spirits of a cursed house.
documents.plot:
La Casa (The House) is a 2020 Chilean horror film directed by Jorge Olguín, the Chilean filmmaker who has devoted more of his career to horror and fantasy than any other in his country, known for films such as Ángel Negro (2000) and Caleuche: el llamado del mar (2012). It was his sixth feature. The film stars Gabriel Cañas as Corporal Arriagada, a carabinero, with Camila Carreño, Carol Campos, Carlos Cortez and Felipe Silva Rodríguez in the cast. It runs about 73 minutes and opened in Chilean cinemas on 30 January 2020.

The film is inspired by the urban legend surrounding the Casona Dubois in the Santiago district of Quinta Normal, now a cultural centre, where most of it was shot. According to the legend, a French engineer and his wife who settled there in the early twentieth century turned to witchcraft to conceive a child; the baby was born deformed, the father killed it and the mother took her own life, and the house has been considered cursed ever since. Title cards at the start inform the audience of this history. The story is set in 1986, during the military dictatorship. In the middle of the night Arriagada receives an urgent call: neighbours report someone inside the old mansion, crying for help. Arriagada, who that same day has committed an atrocity of his own by beating a woman labelled a subversive to death, goes to investigate, calling for reinforcements that will take time to arrive. Once inside he cannot find his way out, and the violent spirits of the family begin to torment him, including a bloodied woman who appears and vanishes, until a final twist ties the haunting to his own guilt and to the repression of the regime. Olguín shot the film quickly as an apparent single real-time take, following Cañas through the dark, labyrinthine house lit largely by his flashlight, with only a handful of actors inside the mansion.

Olguín described the film as "a great lie to tell a great truth." Reception was mixed. Patricia Reyes of La Tercera highlighted its sound design and its blend of the political context with horror, and Edgardo Viereck Salinas of Cine y Literatura considered it the director's best work, a powerful portrait of guilt under Pinochet. Reid Ramsey of Cinematary praised Cañas's physically demanding performance and the practical effects but found the scares repetitive and the concept better suited to a short film.

documents.title: Red Dot
documents.overview: On a hiking trip to rekindle their marriage, a couple find themselves fleeing for their lives in the unforgiving wilderness from an unknown shooter.
documents.plot:
Red Dot is a 2021 Swedish drama film directed by Anna Odell, produced by Film i Dalarna, and released on Netflix.

The main theme of Red Dot revolves around the story of a young woman named Maja, who becomes involved in an online relationship with a man she meets through a dating app. As their connection deepens, Maja begins to share intimate details about her life, including her struggles with anxiety and depression. However, it soon becomes apparent that this person is not who they claim to be.

The film explores the darker side of online relationships, where people can hide behind masks and manipulate others for their own gain. The title "Red Dot" refers to a dating app feature that allows users to see when someone has been active on the site, creating a sense of urgency and encouraging users to engage with each other more frequently.

Throughout the film, Maja's relationship becomes increasingly toxic, as she becomes trapped in a cycle of emotional manipulation. The film raises questions about the nature of intimacy, trust, and vulnerability in online relationships, highlighting the risks and consequences of becoming too deeply invested in someone you've never met in person.

The film also touches on themes of loneliness, social isolation, and the human desire for connection in a world where technology can both unite and isolate us. Ultimately, Red Dot is a thought-provoking exploration of the complexities of online relationships and the importance of maintaining healthy boundaries in our digital interactions.

documents.title: Worth
documents.tagline: Our national tragedy. Their personal suffering. His impossible task.
documents.overview: Kenneth Feinberg, a powerful D.C. lawyer appointed Special Master of the 9/11 Fund, fights off the cynicism, bureaucracy, and politics associated with administering government funds and, in doing so, discovers what life is worth.
documents.plot:
Worth is a 2021 American drama film directed by Darin Moiselle and written by Steven Conrad. The movie tells the story of Dean Whiting, a lawyer who represents a group of 9/11 first responders who are struggling to receive fair compensation for their medical expenses.

The main theme of Worth revolves around the struggle for justice and the human cost of war. The film highlights the plight of these brave men and women who risked their lives to save others on that fateful day, only to be left with severe health problems as a result. The movie showcases the emotional toll of watching loved ones suffer due to the government's failure to provide adequate support.

The film also explores the theme of sacrifice and the true meaning of patriotism. Dean Whiting's character is driven by a sense of duty and responsibility to his clients, who have made the ultimate sacrifice for their country. As he navigates the complex web of bureaucracy and politics, he must confront the harsh realities of war and its impact on those who serve.

Furthermore, Worth touches on the theme of systemic injustice and the need for accountability. The film sheds light on the government's failure to provide adequate support to its own citizens, particularly those who have made the ultimate sacrifice in service to their country. This theme is woven throughout the narrative, highlighting the importance of standing up for what is right and fighting for justice.

Overall, Worth is a powerful and emotional drama that explores the complexities of war, sacrifice, and justice. The film serves as a tribute to the brave men and women who have served our country, and it sheds light on the need for accountability and support for those who have made the ultimate sacrifice.

documents.title: No Sudden Move
documents.overview: A group of criminals are brought together under mysterious circumstances and have to work together to uncover what's really going on when their simple job goes completely sideways.
documents.plot:
No Sudden Move is a 2021 American neo-noir crime thriller film directed by Steven Soderbergh and written by David Koepp, based on the novel of the same name by Daniel Mainwaring.

The story revolves around a group of wealthy businessmen who are brought together for a weekend retreat in Detroit. The guests include:

* Vincent McMurty (Don Cheadle), a successful businessman with a troubled past
* Lester Nygaard (Jeff Bridges), a retired insurance salesman struggling to cope with his wife's infidelity and his own feelings of inadequacy
* Lester's wife, Catherine (Julianne Moore), who is having an affair with Vincent
* Richard Stark (Benicio del Toro), a ruthless and cunning businessman with ties to organized crime
* Frank Grusadinsky (David Harbour), a former hitman trying to leave his past behind

The weekend begins with a series of tense and awkward interactions among the guests, as they try to navigate their personal demons and business dealings. However, things take a deadly turn when Richard Stark is found dead in his hotel room.

As the group tries to figure out who killed Richard, they realize that each of them had a motive for the murder. The investigation unfolds over the course of several days, with the guests using their wealth and influence to try to cover their tracks and avoid suspicion.

Throughout the film, Soderbergh uses his signature non-linear storytelling style, jumping back and forth in time to reveal clues and piece together the events leading up to Richard's murder. The film also explores themes of class, privilege, and the corrupting influence of wealth.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that each of the guests has a dark secret to hide, and that they are all connected to Richard Stark in some way. In the end, the killer is revealed, but not before Soderbergh subverts expectations and sets up a twist ending that leaves the audience guessing until the very end.

Overall, No Sudden Move is a gripping and suspenseful thriller that explores the darker side of human nature. With its talented ensemble cast and Soderbergh's masterful direction, it's a must-see for fans of crime dramas and neo-noir thrillers.

documents.title: My Best Friend's Christmas
documents.overview: When Ashley Seever returns home for the holidays hoping to reconnect with her high school sweetheart Grant, she soon meets his new girlfriend. In an attempt to escape the embarrassment, she and her best friend Liam fake their own holiday romance…but when her fake feelings for Liam start to turn real, Ashley will have to choose what her heart really wants this Christmas.
documents.plot:
My Best Friend's Christmas is a 2019 American Christmas romantic comedy television film written and directed by Jake Helgren, who co-wrote the screenplay with Blaine Chiappetta, and produced by his company Ninth House Films. It stars Breanne Hill, Colton Little and Tanner Novlan, with Masiela Lusha, Beth Broderick and Trevor Eve in supporting roles. Acquired by Showtime as one of the network's first original Christmas films, it was released in December 2019 and premiered on the Showtime Women channel on 3 December. It runs about 90 minutes.

Ashley Seever (Hill), a cheerful party planner, travels back to her hometown for the holidays, hoping to rekindle her romance with her high school sweetheart, Grant Hines (Novlan). Her plans fall apart when she discovers that Grant is now dating Bella Vega (Lusha), a famous social media influencer. Embarrassed and unwilling to admit defeat, Ashley persuades her colleague and best friend, Liam Marsh (Little), to pose as her boyfriend for the season, and the pair stage a holiday romance in front of Grant and Bella, while Ashley's parents, Sheila (Broderick) and Winston (Eve), look on. As the pretence continues through the festivities, Ashley and Liam begin to realise that their feelings for each other may be more than an act, and Ashley has to decide whether she still wants the man she came home for or the friend who has been beside her all along.

In an interview with Gas Mask Magazine ahead of the premiere, the Texas-born Helgren described the film as a fun Christmas spin on My Best Friend's Wedding, built around a sweet party planner who returns home to revive an old flame and asks her best friend to play her fake boyfriend to avoid embarrassment. He said the team was excited that Showtime had liked the film enough to make it one of its first original Christmas acquisitions.

The film received little professional critical attention. Audience reviews on IMDb were largely negative, calling the story predictable and criticising the dialogue, the leads' chemistry and a soundtrack that some found loud enough to drown out the dialogue; Colton Little's performance was among the few elements viewers singled out for praise, while one reviewer was surprised to find the veteran British actor Trevor Eve in the cast.
